laws.title: Authority of department of finance
laws.content:
The department of finance shall collect all permit fees, delinquent fees and penalties and supervise and enforce the collection of all excise or license taxes, penalties, and delinquent fees that may be due under the provisions of this chapter.

(Code 1956, § 5-94)

*State law reference—Secretary to collect taxes, R.S. 26:451.*

laws.title: Collection by state department of revenue and taxation of excise tax on malt beverages
laws.content:
(a) The excise tax of $1.50 per standard barrel of 31 gallons on malt beverages shall be collected by the secretary of the department of revenue and taxation, and the amount thereof collected and remitted by him to the department of finance in accordance with the provisions of R.S. 26:492.

(b) If a dealer in beverages of low alcoholic content fails to file a return and pay the tax due on the beverages within the time provided in R.S. 26:346, he shall be subject to a penalty of five percent on the amount of the tax if the period of delinquency is ten days or less or 20 percent on the amount of the tax if the period of delinquency is greater than ten days. If an attorney is called on to assist in collection, there shall be an additional sum due equal to ten percent of both the amount of the penalties and tax due.

(Code 1956, § 5-95)

laws.title: How tax on beverages of low alcoholic content collected
laws.content:
The excise or license tax on beverages with a low alcoholic content shall be collected by direct payment monthly from bonded dealers, importers, and manufacturers.

(Code 1956, § 5-96)

*State law reference—Collection of taxes, R.S. 26:451 et seq.*

laws.title: Rules and regulations for collection
laws.content:
The department of finance may make and promulgate rules and regulations to provide for the collection of the excise or license taxes due on all alcoholic beverages taxable under the provisions of this chapter, so as to prevent any alcoholic beverages being sold, handled, used, imported, stored, distributed or consumed within the city without the tax prescribed in this chapter having been paid.

(Code 1956, § 5-97)

*State law reference—Similar provisions, R.S. 26:453.*

laws.title: Price of stamps; quantity discount
laws.content:
The director of the department of finance shall redeem all unaffixed tax stamps purchased by manufacturers and wholesalers purchased by such manufacturers and wholesalers in order to comply with the former provisions of this section requiring such purchases by making a refund in the amount of the face value of the stamps less any discount received at the time of the purchase of such stamps. The inventory of stamps now held by the manufacturers and wholesalers shall be refunded or applied as a credit to taxes due by them in ten equal monthly installments.

(Code 1956, § 5-101)

*State law reference—Refunds, R.S. 26:347.*

laws.title: Original containers not to be refilled
laws.content:
It shall be a violation of this chapter for any person to refill an original container with an alcoholic beverage or to have in his possession any original container that has been refilled with a beverage of high alcoholic content, taxable under this chapter.

(Code 1956, § 5-104)

*State law reference—Standards of fill, R.S. 26:351.*

laws.title: Inspection of records to determine whether tax paid
laws.content:
The department of finance may inspect any or all books, records and memoranda of any person including any common, public or contract carrier for the purpose of determining whether or not the taxes prescribed by this chapter have been paid.

(Code 1956, § 5-105)

laws.title: Annual reports and remittances
laws.content:
(a) Every wholesale dealer that delivers alcoholic beverages to retail dealers within the city shall submit to the department of finance an annual summary report by March 1st detailing the preceding year’s sales. The annual summary report shall provide the following information:

1. The corporate/business name and address of each retail dealer sold alcoholic beverages by the wholesale dealer; and

2. A monthly breakdown of total alcohol sales, both high-alcohol and low-alcohol, sold to the retail dealer by category (for example: liquor, beer, wine).

The report shall be submitted in a form and manner prescribed by the department of finance. Failure to submit such report within 30 days from March 1st shall result in a penalty of $100.00 per day when such records are not produced for the first 90 days after March 1st, and $200.00 per day for each day between 91—180 days. For any wholesale dealer who fails to produce such records after 181 days, the penalty shall be $500.00 per day.

(b) The taxes levied in this article shall be due and paid by every wholesaler, manufacturer or dealer with the gallonage tax report referred to in subsection (a) of this section and shall be computed upon the basis of the number of gallons sold, or otherwise disposed of by every wholesaler, manufacturer or dealer during the preceding calendar month. Gallons sold or disposed of shall be deemed conclusively to be gallons on hand at the beginning of the calendar month plus purchases during the calendar month less gallons on hand at the end of the calendar month, less any exempt sales.

(c) The monthly gallonage tax report required by this section shall be made on forms prescribed and furnished by the director of the department of finance and shall include such information as the director of the department of finance may by rule require. Reports shall be accompanied by the taxpayer’s remittance in full of the correct amount of taxes due and owing for the period covered by the report.

(d) For accurately reporting and timely remitting the taxes all taxpayers shall be allowed a discount of six percent of the amount of the tax otherwise due. One-sixth of the discount shall be paid by the dealer to the director of the department of finance and shall be retained by the director to defray the cost of administration. When a check or other instrument given in payment of taxes is returned unpaid, the discount is forfeited.

(Code 1956, § 5-105.1; M.C.S., Ord. No. 27065, § 2, 9-8-16)

*State law reference—Payment and reporting of taxes, R.S. 26:354—26:360.*

laws.title: Examination of records to determine imports, exports, etc
laws.content:
The department of finance may examine at all reasonable hours the books, records and other documents of all such persons, including dealers, transportation companies, agencies or firms operating in the city, whether such companies, agencies or firms conduct their business by rail, water or otherwise, in order to determine what persons or dealers are importing or exporting, or otherwise shipping alcoholic beverages which are liable for the tax hereby imposed. If any such person shall refuse to permit such examination of its books, records or other documents, the city, through the department of finance or the council, may proceed by rule and require such person to show cause why the department should not be permitted to examine its books, records or other documents.

(Code 1956, § 5-106)

*State law reference—Payment and reporting of taxes, R.S. 26:354—26:360.*

laws.title: Authority to search for violations
laws.content:
The department of safety and permits may search and examine any warehouse, boat, store, storeroom, automobile, truck, conveyance, vehicle or other place of storage, except a private residence which may be searched only in the manner provided for by law, and any means of transportation, whenever there is probable cause to believe that the terms of this chapter have been or are being violated.

(Code 1956, § 5-107; M.C.S., Ord. No. 27737, § 1, 4-19-18)

*State law reference—Authority to search, R.S. 26:371(C).

laws.title: Limitations on authority
laws.content:
(a) Notwithstanding the provisions of section 10-566 no place, other than such as is open to the public, shall be invaded and searched except by an officer named in a search warrant issued by a competent court having the power of a committing magistrate, upon the filing with such court of an affidavit reciting that affiant has reason to believe and believes that the named place is being utilized as a site for the violation of the provisions of this chapter, together with such additional evidence as the court may require to make a prima facie case. No house, room or apartment used as, or which apparently is, a bona fide residence, shall be subject to invasion and search except by an officer designated in a search warrant issued by a competent court having the powers of a committing magistrate, upon the filing in such court of an affidavit by two reliable persons reciting that they have reason to believe and do believe that such place of residence is being used as a cloak or cover for a violation of the provisions of this chapter, and setting forth the specific violations being committed therein, together with such additional corroborating evidence as the court may, in its

*State law reference—Forfeitures and penalties, R.S. 26:354 et seq.

discretion, require to establish the probable existence of the alleged violation of this chapter.

(b) The court shall preserve in its records, subject to inspection at any time by the public, the affidavit hereinabove referred to.

(Code 1956, § 5-108)

*State law reference—Similar provisions, R.S. 26:371(B), (D).

laws.title: When operator lives on premises
laws.content:
Under the terms and conditions of this chapter, and the agreement under which permits are granted for such places of business, where the operator resides in or on the same premises and where the permit allows the storage or sale of alcoholic beverages anywhere on such premises, such premises are hereby declared to be entirely and completely commercial, so far as the agreement for the search of the entire premises is concerned (though this provision does not affect the zoning laws) and, as such, shall, notwithstanding the provisions of section 10-567 be subject to invasion and search without a search warrant, unless the holder of such permit specifically defines and limits the area in which such alcoholic beverages are to be stored or sold, in which case the area so defined shall not have any opening into any portion or part of the property used as residential, either through an adjoining room, hallway, stairs, yard or otherwise, but the commercial and residential parts of the premises must be completely separate and distinct from each other and divided and separated from each other by a solid partition from floor to ceiling without any openings whatever therein in order that such person or dealer may claim or demand a search warrant or for the term "bona fide residence" to apply to such case.

(Code 1956, § 5-109)

*State law reference—Similar provisions, R.S. 26:371(B).

laws.title: Execution of search warrant
laws.content:
Any warrant issued under this division shall be directed to a duly authorized peace officer and the premises described in the warrant shall be searched and all alcoholic beverages or any property used or designed or intended to be used in the keeping for sale or sale of any alcoholic

beverages on such premises shall be seized by such officer and the keeper of such place and such other persons as may be involved in such violation or the person to whom such alcoholic beverages or property belongs shall be apprehended and brought before the court issuing the warrant, to abide the further orders of the court. The officer to whom the search warrant is directed shall make proper return thereon of the action taken thereunder, describing the alcoholic beverages or property so seized, if any. **Sec. 10-570. Seizure of vehicle used in transportation.**

Any automobile, truck, boat, conveyance, vehicle or other means of transportation, other than a common carrier, caught or detected transporting any of the articles taxed by this chapter, without the proper permit or the required tax having been paid may be seized by the department of finance in order to secure it as evidence in a trial brought under this chapter.

(Code 1956, § 5-111)

*State law reference—Similar provisions, R.S. 26:371(A).*

**Sec. 10-571. Disposition of property seized.**

The alcoholic beverages or property seized under the provisions of sections 10-569 and 10-570 shall be held by the officer, without the right of having them released upon writ or claim, except alcoholic beverages seized in a bona fide dwelling house, which shall be released to their owner upon his giving bond, with good and solvent surety, for the value of such alcoholic beverages, conditioned for the return of such alcoholic beverages to the officer upon the order of the court. The court, after the trial of the accused, shall order all alcoholic beverages and property illegally held by the accused at the time of seizure to be immediately and publicly sold or destroyed by the sheriff or peace officer designated by the court.

(Code 1956, § 5-112)

*State law reference—Similar provisions, R.S. 26:371(C).*

**Sec. 10-572. Claim by innocent owner or holder of lien.**

Any person who:

(1) Claims title to any alcoholic beverage seized under the provisions of this chapter, or claims to be entitled to any lien existing thereon prior to the date of seizure; and

(2) Did not in any respect participate in the violation of this chapter for which such beverage was seized;

may file with the department of finance, under oath, a detailed statement of his claim, with a sworn declaration that the claimant did not in any way participate in such violation of this chapter.

(Code 1956, § 5-113)

*State law reference—Similar provisions, R.S. 26:373.*

**Sec. 10-573. Release of property under bond.**

Upon the filing of the statement referred to in the preceding section the property may be released by the department of finance and delivered to the claimant if claimant shall furnish to the department of finance a good and solvent surety bond with a surety company qualified to do business in the state as surety on the bond in a penal sum of not less than double the appraised value of the goods seized, and in no event less than $50.00, which bond shall be conditioned to pay the department of finance the appraised tax value of the goods, and all costs if the claimant does not prosecute his claim to successful judgment.

(Code 1956, § 5-114)

*State law reference—Similar provisions, R.S. 26:373.*

**Sec. 10-574. Further proceedings to establish rights of claimant.**

If it is not practical to make service upon the claimant to the seized property or in case the claimant is a nonresident, the procedure outlined by the state laws and in this chapter may be used in order that the issue may be presented in a court of competent jurisdiction, thereby affording the claimant a fair opportunity to be heard.

If a bond has been furnished by the claimant and the property has been released to him, the judgment of the court, if the contention of the department of finance is sustained, shall be directed against both the claimant and the surety on the bond and shall include all costs from the beginning of the seizure up to the final disposition of the case.

(Code 1956, § 5-115)

*State law reference—Similar provisions, R.S. 26:373.*

**Sec. 10-575. Waiver of forfeiture when violation unintentional.**

The department of finance may waive any proceedings for the forfeiture of the seized taxable articles or any part thereof if it is found that the violation of the law, for which the goods were seized, was unintentional or without intention to defraud the city of its tax, but only if the offender shall pay to the city double the amount of the necessary tax.

(Code 1956, § 5-116)

*State law reference—Waiver of forfeiture of beverages of high alcoholic content, R.S. 26:374.*

**Sec. 10-576. Compromises.**

The department of finance may make a compromise with any claimant, before or after the claim is filed in court.

(Code 1956, § 5-117)

*State law reference—Similar provisions, R.S. 26:458.*

**Sec. 10-577. Record of compromises and waivers.**

A record of all compromises and waivers of forfeiture shall be kept by the department of finance and shall be open to public inspection.

(Code 1956, § 5-118)

*State law references—Waiver of forfeiture of beverages of high alcoholic content, R.S. 26:374; compromises, R.S. 26:458.*

**Sec. 10-578. Destruction of certain seized liquors.**

The department of finance may, after it has held for a period of not less than six months any seized liquors which are damaged, opened, unsaleable or unfit for human consumption and which have not been claimed by the person from whom they were seized, destroy such articles which are damaged, opened, unsaleable or unfit for human consumption without the necessity of court proceedings, and such articles shall be destroyed in the presence of the director of the department of finance, and two other witnesses. The department of finance shall prepare a proces-verbal describing all such articles to be destroyed, to whom such articles belong and the address of the place where seized, and such proces-verbal shall be signed by the director and the two other witnesses and shall be preserved among the records of the department for a period of not less than three years from the date upon which such damaged, opened, unsaleable or unfit for human consumption articles are so destroyed.

(Code 1956, § 5-119)

*State law references—Penalty for keeping blind tiger; destruction or sale of beverages, R.S. 26:712.*

**Sec. 10-579. Failure to pay tax ground for attachment.**

Failure to pay any tax, penalty, delinquent fee or costs accruing under this chapter, or failure to furnish the sworn statements as required by this section shall be construed as an attempt to avoid the payment of such tax, penalty, delinquent fee or costs and shall be sufficient grounds for attachment of any alcoholic beverage belonging to such person, wherever they may be found, whether such delinquent taxpayer be a resident or nonresident of the city, and whether such alcoholic beverage is in the possession of such delinquent taxpayer or in the possession of some other person.

(Code 1956, § 5-120)

*State law reference—Similar provisions, R.S. 26:348(B)(1).*

**Sec. 10-580. Procedure.**

Failure to pay the tax, penalty, delinquent fees or costs referred to in section 10-579 shall, ipso facto, without demand or putting in default, cause the tax, penalties, delinquent fee or fees or costs to become immediately delinquent and the department of finance and the council through that department may on motion in a court of competent jurisdiction take a rule on such person without deposit or advance in costs, to show cause why such person should not be ordered to

laws.title: How alcoholic beverages brought into city
laws.content:
It shall be a violation of this chapter for any person to receive any shipment of alcoholic beverages from without the city other than by common authorized license carriers, under the jurisdiction of the Interstate Commerce Commission, by steamship or as otherwise provided in this chapter. The department of finance may grant a special permit under special circumstances to any wholesale dealer to transfer merchandise from one bonded wholesale dealer to another within the state and to any wholesale dealer to import merchandise into the city in vehicles or conveyances owned by such wholesale dealer.

(Code 1956, § 5-122)

*State law reference—Transportation of alcoholic beverages, R.S. 26:361, 26:362.*

laws.title: Dealers to be bonded
laws.content:
Every dealer producing, manufacturing, importing or holding any alcoholic beverage within the city for any purpose shall be bonded to the city to collect and pay the taxes levied by this article.

(Code 1956, § 5-123)

*State law reference—Similar provisions, R.S. 26:348.*

laws.title: Dealers not to be in possession of unstamped liquor
laws.content:
No manufacturer or wholesale dealer in the city shall have in his possession any alcoholic beverages outside of his bonded interparish or interstate stockroom, unless such alcoholic beverages be in containers of no greater capacity than a gallon. No retail dealer shall have in his possession at any time any alcoholic liquors in containers of not more than one-gallon capacity. But the department of finance may authorize the sale and handling of wines in containers of a content greater than one gallon.

(Code 1956, § 5-124)

*State law reference—Similar provisions, R.S. 26:351.*

laws.title: Permit required for music or other entertainment
laws.content:
Except as otherwise provided in this chapter, it shall be unlawful to keep any piano, organ or other musical instrument whatsoever for the purpose of performing upon it or having it performed upon in any public park or place of public resort or recreation or in any regularly licensed theatre or restaurant or having any other character of entertainment in such places, unless and until the applicant shall have first applied for and obtained from the director of the department of safety and permits a permit authorizing music or other form of entertainment in such place and location, and subject to any conditions imposed by law.

(Code 1956, § 63-1; M.C.S., Ord. No. 29257, § 1, 11-17-22)

laws.title: Amusement games in outdoor amusement parks
laws.content:
(a) Amusement games of skill or amusement games where skill predominates or where the player has the dominant control of the outcome, whether mechanical or manual, whether the contestants participate against each other or not, and which through the outcome of such amusement game or contest do not return to the player or contestant thereof anything but additional free games or awards of merchandise prizes are hereby sanctioned; provided, that the aforesaid games are conducted and operated at outdoor amusement parks, as defined in R.S. 47:354, and licensed to operate in accordance with the provisions of such section.

(b) The provisions of this section shall not apply to any game or games requiring a federal coin-operated gaming device stamp or gaming stamp as presently provided for under existing federal laws.

(Code 1956, § 63-1.1)

*State law reference—Regulation of amusement rides and attractions by city, authorized, R.S. 4:7.*

laws.title: Bungee jumping prohibited
laws.content:
(a) *Definitions.* The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this section, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this subsection, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:

*Bungee catapulting or reverse bungee jumping* means the sport, activity or practice whereby a person is attached to a bungee cord which is stretched and then released, thus catapulting or otherwise launching the jumper into the air from a fixed position, ultimately intending to bring the person to a stop at a point above the surface.

*Bungee cord* means the elastic rope made by rubber, latex or other elastic type materials, whether natural or synthetic, to which the jumper is attached. It lengthens and shortens and thus produces a bouncing action.

*Bungee jumping* means the sport, activity, or other practice of jumping, diving, stepping out, dropping or otherwise being released into the air while attached to a bungee cord, whereby the cord stops the fall, lengthens and shortens, allows the person to bounce up and down, and is intended to finally bring the person to a stop at a point above the surface.

(b) *Prohibition.* It shall be unlawful for any person to engage in the act, sport, or practice of bungee jumping or bungee catapulting or to conduct bungee operations whether mobile or stationary, permanent or temporary, on property owned or leased by the city.

(1) No person shall place equipment utilized in bungee jump operations including cranes, platforms or towers, etc., on property owned or leased by the city.

(2) No person shall use air-space above property owned or leased by the city, such that, should an accident occur, a person would fall on property owned or leased by the city.

(c) Violations. Whoever violates the provisions of this section shall be subject to a mandatory sentence of six months incarceration and/or a fine of not less than $500.00.

laws.title: Places reserved for mayor and police
laws.content:
Managers of places of amusement shall reserve, free of charge, places for the mayor, the judges of the municipal court and the superintendent of police and such other of the police as may be necessary to preserve order.

(Code 1956, § 63-2)

laws.title: Duties of policemen on guard at theatres, etc
laws.content:
The police officers on guard at theatres, shows, balls or exhibitions of any kind shall be and remain within such balls, theatres or other places of amusement or at or about the entrance thereto and any person connected with such entertainment as owner, agent or employee who shall refuse permission or attempt to interfere with such police officers in the performance of such duty shall be liable to a fine and imprisonment.

(Code 1956, § 63-3)

laws.title: Officers may enter theatres, etc
laws.content:
The mayor, the judges of the municipal court and the superintendent of police or any corporal, sergeant or other officer of the police force, specially designated by the superintendent of police, may at any time and at all times enter during performances, theatres, balls and other public entertainments to inspect them and receive reports of police officers on duty.

(Code 1956, § 63-4)

laws.title: Closing permanently place of public resort
laws.content:
The mayor shall cause to be closed any place of public resort whenever the maintenance of order and the public safety or tranquility may require it.

(Code 1956, § 63-6)

laws.title: Prohibition against selling unassigned seating admission tickets
laws.content:
It shall be unlawful for any promotion corporation, management firm, entrepreneur or sponsoring organization to sell admission tickets to any concerts, programs, plays or events that do not specify a particular reserved seat in any assembly center, auditorium, stadium, theatre or any other place of assembly in the city when the seating capacity of the facility is 2,000 or more.

(Code 1956, § 63-6.1)

State law reference—Regulation of shows and concerts by city, authorized, R.S. 4:7.

laws.title: Exemptions from unassigned seating prohibition
laws.content:
The prohibition in section 14-9 shall not apply to high school and college athletic events, including club sponsored athletic events; nor to religious events sponsored by bona fide religious organizations; nor to events where the sponsor has applied for and received a specific exemption from the superintendent of police or his designated agent.

(Code 1956, § 63-6.2)

laws.title: Criteria for granting exemptions to the unassigned seating prohibition
laws.content:
In determining whether an event shall be exempt from the prohibition in section 14-9, the superintendent of police, or his designated agent, shall consider the following factors: The facility where the event is to be scheduled; the size, age and anticipated conduct of the audience; and the hazard to the health, safety and welfare of participants, spectators and the community associ-

For crowd control purposes inside or outside of assembly centers, auditoriums, stadiums, theatres and other places of assembly in the city, the police

laws.title: Liabilities of the events management and sponsors
laws.content:
Nothing in sections 14-1 through 14-12 shall be construed in any way to lessen in any fashion the liability of those responsible for the management and operation of the event. Those responsible for the management and operation of an event shall employ enough personnel to ensure adequate levels of security, safety, health and sanitation.

laws.title: Obscene, etc., entertainments
laws.content:
No person shall, as owner, manager, director, agent or in any other capacity, prepare, advertise, give, present or participate in any obscene, indecent, immoral or impure show or entertainment or in any show or entertainment manifestly tending to corrupt morals.

(Code 1956, § 63-16)

laws.title: Showing obscene pictures prohibited
laws.content:
It shall be unlawful for any person, whether as owner, agent, lessee, employer or employee, to operate or exhibit at any moving picture show, theaterium, nickelodeon, theatre or other similar place of amusement in the city any obscene, lewd or vulgar picture, film, slide, view or other representation.

(Code 1956, § 63-17)

Cross reference—Offenses affecting morality, § 54-231 et seq.

laws.title: Conduct of spectators
laws.content:
All persons attending any public spectacle are forbidden to commit, either at the doors or in the theatre, lobbies, galleries or corridors, any disorderly acts, to behave riotously, to make any noise, to use violence, insult, indecency or to offer any kind of aggression, to have their hats on while the curtain is raised or to smoke in the theatre, the galleries, lobbies or corridors. Every person who, on being thereto required by any police officer on duty at the public spectacle shall neglect or refuse to observe what is prescribed in this section shall be guilty of an offense.

(Code 1956, § 63-19)

Secs. 14-17–14-35. Reserved.

laws.title: Monthly inspection of wiring, quarterly report
laws.content:
The department of safety and permits shall supervise and inspect the electric wiring of all theatres, buildings used for public entertainment and places of public amusement at least once a month and furnish the mayor and council with a quarterly report of the condition of such wiring and installation.

(Code 1956, § 63-7)

laws.title: Failure to comply forfeits license
laws.content:
Any failure on the part of any owner, agent or manager of any theatre, building used for public entertainment or place of amusement to comply

(Code 1956, § 63-9)

**Sec. 14-39. Obstruction of aisles, etc., of motion picture theatres.**

No owner, lessee, proprietor or manager of any theatre, theatorium, nickelodeon, hall, place, opera house or building in the city where theatrical or other performances or exhibitions of moving pictures are given and an admission fee is charged shall permit or suffer any person to congregate, gather, stand or be seated in the aisles, lobbies, entrances or exits of any such building at any time when such theatrical or other performances or exhibition of moving pictures is to take place.

(Code 1956, § 63-10)

**Sec. 14-40. Examination of places of public resort; prevention of accidents.**

The mayor and the department of safety and permits, as often as they may deem it necessary, shall examine whether theatres and places of public resort are constructed with the requisite solidity and carefully kept in repair, so that the public may assemble there without danger. They shall adopt suitable measures to prevent accidents that might occur from any negligence in that respect on the part of the proprietors, tenants or other persons having the management or direction of such theatres or places of public resort.

(Code 1956, § 63-11)

**Sec. 14-41. Registration with the department of health.**

Any person operating any theatre, moving picture show or other place of public amusement within the city shall register in the office of the department of health the name of such theatre, moving picture show or other place of amusement, its location and the name of the owner, if an individual, if a firm, the name of its members, and if a corporation, the name of the president.

(Code 1956, § 63-12)

**Sec. 14-42. Cleaning and disinfecting.**

Every theatre, moving picture show or other place of public amusement or recreation where the public congregate shall be cleansed daily and disinfected at least once each week and at such other time as may be required, with a disinfectant and in a manner to be approved by the department of health or such officer or inspector as may be designated by it.

(Code 1956, § 63-13)

**Sec. 14-43. Fire alarm boxes on stages.**

A city fire alarm box shall be placed on the stage of every theatre in the city for the purpose of communicating fire alarms direct to headquarters at the city hall, thus avoiding delays in case of emergency.

(Code 1956, § 63-20)

Cross reference—Fire alarms, § 74-46 et seq.

**Sec. 14-44. Marking and diagram of exits.**

The owner, lessee, manager or other person having charge or control of any theatre in the city shall cause each door and means of exit to be used in the case of fire or panic to be conspicuously numbered so as to be visible to the audience by whom it is to be used and shall have printed in conspicuous type a plan or diagram and explanation showing each of such exits thereon and referring to the numbers aforesaid.

(Code 1956, § 63-21)

**Sec. 14-45. Department to enforce; inspections.**

The department of health shall enforce the provisions of this article and prosecute all persons charged with violating it and to that end its officers, members, agents, employees, inspectors and appointees may enter any premises or place in the city for the purpose of inspection for violations thereof.

(Code 1956, § 63-14)

**Sec. 14-46. Responsibility of members, partners, etc.**

(a) When an association of individuals is charged with the violation of any provision of this article, each individual of such association of in-

laws.title: Permit required
laws.content:
Every operator of an itinerant circus shall, before conducting his circus in the city, obtain from

the director of the department of safety and permits a permit to do so.

(Code 1956, § 63-22)

laws.title: Bond required of operator
laws.content:
The permit required by this article shall be issued only after the operator shall have filed with the director of the department of safety and permits, a bond payable to the city, in the sum of $1,000.00 to indemnify the city for any damages it may sustain during the time such circus shall be conducted in the city as a result of the fault of the operator of such circus or of his agents, servants or employees. Such bond shall contain a stipulation that such operator and his surety consent and yield to the jurisdiction of the civil courts of the state for the parish and waive any plea to the jurisdiction of the court on account of their residence elsewhere upon suit for damages such as are referred to in this section.

(Code 1956, § 63-24)

laws.title: Cash deposit in lieu of bond
laws.content:
In lieu of filing the bond required by this article with the director of the department of safety and permits any operator may deposit with the director of the department of finance the sum of $1,000.00 in cash as security to the city against such damages as are mentioned in section 14-68 and upon presentation to the director of the department of safety and permits of the receipt of the director of the department of finance for such deposit the permit required by this article shall be issued.

laws.title: Classification of public dance halls
laws.content:
Public dance halls are hereby designated and rated as follows:

(1) Class A, cabarets and nightclubs.

(2) Class B, places or buildings owned, rented or operated by clubs and used for dancing by members or rented to others for such purposes.

(3) Class C, all dance halls under the terms of this article not otherwise specifically classified.

(4) Class D, dance schools and studios.

(5) Class E, teen clubs.

(Code 1956, § 63-26.2)

laws.title: Prohibited acts
Taxi dance halls
laws.content:
(a) It shall be unlawful for any person to operate, manage, or direct the operation of any taxi dance hall, as defined in section 14-121, or to employ or permit any person to dance therein.

(b) No person shall be permitted to be employed on a salary, contract or commission basis in any dance hall for the purpose of dancing with the patrons of such dance hall.

(c) No person shall be permitted to frequent a taxi dance hall.

(Code 1956, § 63-28B)

laws.title: Permission and license tax required for giving ball
laws.content:
It shall be unlawful for any person to give, within the limits of the city, any public balls of any description unless permission in writing is previously obtained from the director of the department of finance to give such ball and after payment of the license tax.

(1) *Closing balls illegally held.* Whenever the provisions of this section shall be violated the mayor shall cause the ball to be closed immediately by the police.

(2) *Prolongation of ball beyond permit hours.*  
No public ball shall be prolonged beyond the hour fixed by the permit of the director of the department of finance.  
(Code 1956, § 63-29)  
Cross reference—Carnival, Mardi Gras, ch. 34.

laws.title: Premises to be open for inspection at all times
laws.content:
All portions of the establishment or premises under this article shall at all times be open for inspection by the police department or other city departments for the purpose of enforcing any of the provisions of this article or other ordinances of the city relating to the health, safety, and welfare of the public.  
(Code 1956, § 63-26.8)  
State law reference—Similar provisions, R.S. 4:363.

Secs. 14-127–14-135. Reserved.

laws.title: Permit required
laws.content:
It shall be unlawful for any person, as owner, or operator or lessee or their authorized agents and/or representatives to operate within the city limits any public dance hall, without a permit issued by the department of finance.  
(Code 1956, § 63-26)

laws.title: Permit application
laws.content:
(a) Persons desiring to obtain a public dance hall permit required by this article shall file a written application with the department of finance, bureau of revenue. The applications shall include the following information:

(1) The name, address and telephone number of the applicant and/or his agent who shall be the operator of the public dance hall.

(2) The location and the name of the owner of the property on which the establishment is to be located.

(3) The business name (assumed name) to be used by the applicant.

(4) The number of persons projected to be on the premises at any one time.

(5) The name and address of the licensed security agency which services the establishment.

(6) Certification that the premises is adequate for the purpose, and conforms with existing health, safety, fire and zoning ordinances.

(b) A permit shall not be issued until the applicant is in full compliance with the provisions of this article as well as the pertinent rules and regulations of the department of safety and permits, the department of health, the fire department, and the city planning commission.  
(Code 1956, § 63-26.1)

laws.title: Application and license fees
laws.content:
A fee shall be charged for the processing and issuance of a permit under this division in addition to a fee for the permit.

(1) A fee schedule shall be established by the director of the department of finance and posted at the bureau of revenue.

(2) An application fee shall be charged for each new applicant and any existing permittee seeking to move his business to a new location or to open up any new additional public dance hall or expand any existing public dance hall premises where a city building permit is required.

(3) Owners and operators shall be required to pay an annual application fee for a permit renewal upon the expiration of the current permit.

(4) Upon payment of the application fee and approval of the permit application by the director of the department of finance an annual permit will be issued.  
(Code 1956, § 63-26.3)

*State law reference—Department of police of New Orleans authorized to place matrons or policewomen in dance halls, R.S. 4:361 et seq.

(b) All fees for applications and permits collected under this division shall be paid in advance and placed in a special revolving fund. If no permit is issued, the application fee shall be applied to cover the cost of processing such application. The first period permit fee shall be refunded. (c) If a permit is revoked, suspended, or terminated or the operation of the establishment is discontinued, no refund of any portion of any of the fees paid for the application or permit shall be made. (d) Permits issued pursuant to the provisions of this division shall not be transferable between persons or locations. (e) A penalty of ten percent of the application fee shall be assessed for all renewal applications filed after January 15. (f) Any permit lost or destroyed or defaced shall be replaced with a duplicate for a fee of $10.00. (Code 1956, § 63-26.4(a)—(e), (g))

laws.title: Display of permit
laws.content: All permits issued under this division shall be posted or displayed in a prominent place on the premises for which the permit is issued. (Code 1956, § 63-26.4(f))

laws.title: Suspension, revocation, and/or termination
laws.content:
(a) Any permit issued pursuant to the provisions of this division shall be revoked or suspended upon any one or more of the following grounds:

(1) The permittee, his employee, agent, or any person connected or associated with the permit as a partner, director, officer, stockholder or manager, or any person financially interested has violated any of the rules and regulations promulgated for or ordinances pertinent to the establishment and operation of a dance hall as required by the fire department, the department of safety and permits, the department of finance, and/or the city planning commission or any state or federal law in conducting or operating a dance hall.

(2) False, misleading or fraudulent statement of material fact in the application.

(3) There exists a clear and present danger of serious damage or danger to the public if the permit is not suspended or revoked.

(4) The permittee has been convicted of a crime which is either a felony or a crime involving moral turpitude and which is related to the operation of a dance hall.

(5) The permittee is a corporation and is no longer qualified to transact business in the state.

(b) To suspend or revoke a permit, the director of the department of finance shall notify the owner/operator in writing by hand delivery or registered mail. The notice shall state the reasons for such action and that the permit shall be surrendered to the bureau of revenue on demand.

(c) Permits issued pursuant to this division shall terminate upon failure of the permittee to pay any license fee not paid by January 15 of the new license period.

(d) Appeals from the suspension, revocation or termination of a permit shall be filed with the director of the department of finance or tendered and processed in accordance with the appropriate administrative or civil adjudication procedures designated by the director. (Code 1956, § 63-26.5)

laws.title: Exceptions
laws.content:
(a) A permit shall not be required for any municipal dance hall under the authority of the city, the parish school board, any political subdivision

of the city, or any state or federal government department or agency.

(b) A permit shall not be required of any hotel, motel, cafe, restaurant, banquet hall or catering facility where no charge or admission is imposed for the privilege of entry or dancing.

(Code 1956, § 63-26.6)

laws.title: Public dances for minors, permit
laws.content:
(a) Owners or operators of public dance halls other than teen clubs who wish to conduct a public dance or municipal dance to be attended exclusively by minors shall be required to obtain a special public dance for minors permit from the department of finance, bureau of revenue. Such permit shall be issued for a duration of 24 hours. The applicant shall provide proof that the premises where the dance is to be held holds a current public dance hall permit or is exempt from the requirements for same as reflected in section 14-142.

(b) Public dance for minors permits shall be issued only under the following conditions:

(1) The general adult public shall not be permitted admission to the premises while the special permit is in effect.

(2) The owner or operator or applicant must agree to comply with the provisions of sections 14-160 through 14-170 for teen clubs.

(3) Any establishment holding a special permit for minors shall require all minors to vacate the premises and shall close its operations for at least one hour prior to reopening the establishment to adults.

(Code 1956, § 63-26.11)

laws.title: Dressing rooms for entertainers
laws.content:
Owners and operators of public dance halls shall provide separate and adequate dressing rooms for male and female entertainers where live entertainment is provided.

(Code 1956, § 63-26.9)

laws.title: Employment of minors
laws.content:
It shall be unlawful for any person under the age of 18 to act as a cashier, door keeper, or to work or be employed in any capacity whatever in or about any public dance hall, or assist in any way whatsoever in conducting same. The provisions of this section shall not be applicable to teen clubs, dance studios, or dance schools.

(Code 1956, § 63-26.10)

laws.title: Dance halls required to have telephone
laws.content:
It shall be unlawful for any owners or proprietors of any hall where public balls or theatre or other similar public entertainment is held to rent them for any such purpose unless such hall shall be connected by telephone with the head office and various precinct stations of the department of police.

(Code 1956, § 63-26.12)

Secs. 14-147–14-154. Reserved.

laws.title: Definition
laws.content:
The term “teen club” includes teenage dance halls, discotheques, nonalcoholic bars for teenagers, dry cabarets, juice bars, milk bars, teenage cabarets or other public resorts to be frequented exclusively by teenagers for entertainment or amusement, including but not limited to music, music videos, and dancing. Such establishments shall not be licensed to sell alcoholic beverages.

(Code 1956, § 63-27)

Cross reference—Definitions generally, § 1-2.

laws.title: Permit required
laws.content:
It shall be unlawful for any person to operate within the city any teen club without having been issued a permit by the department of finance.

(Code 1956, § 63-27.1)

CD14:14

laws.title: Application for permit
laws.content:
(a) The application for a teen club permit shall be filed with the department of finance, bureau of revenue in a format as prescribed by same and shall include the following information:

(1) Full name and any name by which the person or applicant is or has been known.

(2) Date and place of birth.

(3) Driver’s license number if available.

(4) Fingerprints.

(5) A current photograph.

(6) Any prior felony or misdemeanor convictions except minor traffic violations.

(7) Home and business address and telephone number.

(8) Any revocation or suspension of a license issued pursuant to this division.

(9) The name of any local, authorized agent who will be managing or operating the establishment at the indicated location and proof of their authority to act on behalf of the owner.

(10) If the owner/operator is a corporation or a person financially interested in the applicant business is a corporation, the owner shall provide a list of the names and addresses of all persons financially interested in that corporation.

(11) Certification that the premises where the teen club is to be located is adequate for the purpose and that the premises conforms with the existing health, safety, fire and zoning ordinances of the city.

(12) The name and address of the licensed security agency which will provide the security officers for the establishment.

(13) A copy of the neighborhood petition, as required by section 14-159, which was circulated for the approval of persons owning property, living, or doing business within 300 feet of the proposed location.

(14) The size of the premises, room, space or building proposed to be used for such purposes.

(15) Certification of the maximum number of persons that may be accommodated on the premises.

(b) Any change in the information required to be provided above concerning the applicant or agent shall be reported to the bureau of revenue within ten days of the change. All other information must be updated at the time of permit renewal.

(Code 1956, § 63-27.1(a), (b))

laws.title: Exemptions
laws.content:
The provisions of this division shall not apply to any of the following:

(1) Private dances given at private homes.

(2) Dances or balls held in the city auditorium or coliseum.

(3) Dances for school children held in the auditorium or gymnasium of any public school under the supervision of the school authorities.

(Code 1956, § 63-27.7)

laws.title: Neighborhood petition
laws.content:
(a) No permit to operate a teen club under this division shall be issued until the applicant for such permit has filed a petition signed by a minimum of 65 percent of the residents within a radius of 300 feet of the proposed location, indicating their approval of the establishment of a teen club.

(b) The director of the department of finance shall adopt rules and regulations governing the procedure for securing the petition of consent provided for in this section. The rules shall provide that the circulator of the petition requesting a waiver shall subscribe to an affidavit attesting to the fact that the petition was circulated in accordance with the rules of the department and that the circulator personally witnessed the signatures on the petition and that the same were affixed to the petition by the person whose name appeared thereon.

(c) An official petition form shall be prepared by the department and shall state in boldfaced type the official definition of a public dance hall, including its allowed hours of operation and the fact that the consent of 65 percent of the residents within 300 feet of the subject establishment is required. The petition form to be circulated for a public dance hall shall be the official form prepared by the department. No other form shall be used or will be accepted as a valid petition.

(Code 1956, § 63-27.5)

laws.title: Supervision
laws.content:
A sufficient number of adult supervisors who are employees of the teen club shall be provided to ensure compliance with the provisions of this division. For the purposes of this section, a sufficient number shall constitute, at a minimum, a ratio of one adult to every 35 teenagers on the premises. All employees shall be considered supervisory staff.

(Code 1956, § 63-27.2(a))

laws.title: Lighting of premises
laws.content:
The premises of the teen club shall be adequately lighted at all times when in operation. For the purposes of this section, the volume of illumination shall at no time be less than one footcandle in any part of the building or premises accessible to participants.

(Code 1956, § 63-27.2(b))

laws.title: Parking facilities
laws.content:
All off-street parking facilities for a teen club, under the direct or indirect control of the permittee, shall be adequately lighted and supervised to ensure compliance with this section and any other laws of the city. Required off-street parking shall be determined at no less than a rate of one space per 200 feet of floor area.

(Code 1956, § 63-27.2(c))

laws.title: Hours of operation
laws.content:
A teen club shall not operate during regular elementary or high school hours. All applicable curfew hours shall be enforced by the operator of the facility. The hours during which teen clubs shall not be allowed to operate are as follows:

(1) Fridays and Saturdays, between the hours of 11:30 p.m. and 12:00 noon.

(2) Sundays through Thursdays, between the hours of 10:30 p.m. and 12:00 noon.

(3) New Year’s Day, between the hours of 1:00 a.m. and 12:00 noon.

(Code 1956, § 63-27.2(d))

laws.title: Admissions
laws.content:
(a) It shall be the responsibility of the operator or permittee of a teen club to ascertain the correct legal age of all persons seeking admission and such persons who do not meet the age requirement of this subsection shall be excluded.

(1) On nights preceding a regular school attendance day no person under the age of 17 shall be permitted to attend after 9:00 p.m. unless accompanied by a parent or legal guardian.

(2) On nights preceding a school holiday or during vacation periods no person under the age of 15 shall be permitted to attend after 9:00 p.m. unless accompanied by a parent or legal guardian.

(3) All persons over the age of 20 shall be denied admission unless such person is a parent or legal guardian.

(4) All persons under the age of 13 shall be denied admission.

(5) Teenagers under the age of 15 shall not be admitted unless accompanied by a parent or legal guardian or unless a parent or legal guardian has signed and filed with the operator, agent, or owner of the establishment a consent form for such minor to be there unaccompanied by such parent or guardian. Such form must be signed by the parent or guardian in the presence of the owner, operator or agent. The form shall contain the parent or guardian’s telephone number and address. In addition to the con-

sent form such teenager shall also be required to provide proper identification before being admitted.

(6) Teenagers between the ages of 15 and 18 shall be admitted upon providing proof of age.

Proof of age shall be required of all persons entering teen clubs. Such proof may be established by identification issued by a governmental agency, the patron’s school, or the department of motor vehicles, and must contain the patron’s name, date of birth, and picture that has been taken within the preceding two years.

(b) Admission shall be denied to any person showing evidence of drinking any alcoholic beverages or showing evidence or symptoms of being intoxicated as a result of the ingestion of any chemical substance.

(Code 1956, § 63-27.2(e))

laws.title: Attendance
laws.content:
Except in emergency situations, no patron shall be permitted to leave the premises of a teen club and thereafter reenter prior to closing. No pass or other identification permitting reentry shall be issued.

(Code 1956, § 63-27.2(f))

laws.title: Denial of entry on request of the parent or legal guardian
laws.content:
No person having charge or control of any premises regulated under this division shall allow any teenager to enter or remain on or at the premises after having received a written notice signed by the parent or legal guardian of such teenager.

(Code 1956, § 63-27.2(g))

laws.title: Alcoholic beverages
laws.content:
No alcoholic beverages are to be possessed, sold, served, or consumed on the premises for which a permit was issued under this division.

(Code 1956, § 63-27.2(h))

laws.title: Location
laws.content:
(a) The teen club shall not be located within a 300-foot radius of a cocktail lounge or barroom or other establishment where alcoholic beverages are sold or consumed.

(b) The establishment shall not be located within a 300-foot radius of any residential district.

(Code 1956, § 63-27.2(i))

laws.title: Smoking
laws.content:
There shall be no smoking on the premises of a teen club. The sale of tobacco products to minors is prohibited.

(Code 1956, § 63-27.2(j))

laws.title: Occupancy
laws.content:
The maximum number of persons allowed on the premises of a teen club, as required by the fire codes of the city, shall be posted.

(Code 1956, § 63-27.2(k))

laws.title: Criminal history of supervisory staff
laws.content:
(a) No person, as the owner or operator or agent of a teen club, shall employ any person as a supervisory employee who has been convicted of a misdemeanor or a felony in the last five years or any person who has been arrested and is out on bond or bail or out on his own recognizance pending trial.

(b) No person shall be employed who has been convicted of a crime involving moral turpitude. Upon a showing of just cause a licensee may petition the director of the department of finance for a waiver of this provision. Just cause shall include but is not limited to a demonstration that the prior conviction or arrest would not have an adverse effect on the employee’s ability to supervise teenagers.

(Code 1956, § 63-27.3)

laws.title: Security
laws.content:
The owner, operator or agent of a teen club shall provide security at least one hour prior to opening and one hour after closing both on the

premises and in the parking facility serving the establishment. The number of licensed security officers which shall be required is as follows:

(1) For any number of persons from one to 75, two security officers.

(2) For any number of persons from 75 to 150, three security officers.

(3) For each additional 50 persons, one additional security officer.

(Code 1956, § 63-27.4)

laws.title: Operation after 1:00 a.m
laws.content:
(a) If the teen club intends to operate after the closing time set forth in this division the premises must first be vacated by all customers, and thereafter only those persons 18 years of age or older who present valid identification containing proof of age as set forth in this section may be permitted to enter the premises.

(b) Any establishment holding a teen club permit shall require all minors to vacate the premises and shall close its operation for at least one hour prior to reopening the establishment to adults.

(Code 1956, § 63-27.6)

laws.title: Lighting and drinking fountains
laws.content:
(a) Each permittee shall provide, at all times, adequate lighting in every part of the establishment, at one footcandle throughout the establishment.

(b) There shall be at least one sanitary drinking fountain for each 2,500 square feet of floorspace or fraction thereof.

(Code 1956, § 63-27.8)

Secs. 14-175–14-185. Reserved.

laws.title: Permit required
laws.content:
Owners, operators or agents of dance studios or dance schools shall be required to obtain a permit for such establishments in accordance with the requirements of section 14-136 et seq.

(Code 1956, § 63-28)

laws.title: Sanitation of premises
laws.content:
Owners and operators of dance studios and schools shall at all times maintain the premises in a clean and sanitary condition and shall provide proper drinking facilities.

(Code 1956, § 63-28A(a))

laws.title: Minors
laws.content:
Owners and operators of dance studios and schools shall be responsible for the protection and safety of minor children while such minors are students or patrons on the premises.

(Code 1956, § 63-28A(b))

laws.title: Minimum age of teachers
laws.content:
(a) Owners and operators of dance studios and schools shall employ dancing teachers 18 years of age or over; except that minor students, 16 and 17 years of age, acting in the capacity of teacher as part of their study of dancing, shall in all instances be supervised by an employee over 18 years of age. Classes taught by such minors shall be restricted to children under the age of 16.

(b) All minors 16 and 17 years of age, employed in any capacity by a dance studio, shall secure work permits from the state department of labor. Such employment and classes shall be terminated not later than 10:00 p.m.

(Code 1956, § 63-28A(c))

laws.title: Dance fee
laws.content:
Owners and operators of dance studios and schools shall not employ or permit any persons as dance partners on a fee per dance basis.

(Code 1956, § 63-28A(d))

laws.title: General prohibition
laws.content:
(a) Gambling is the intentional conducting, or directly assisting in the conducting, as a business, of any game, contest, lottery, or contrivance whereby a person risks the loss of anything of value in order to realize a profit. Whoever commits the crime of gambling shall be fined not more than $500.00, or imprisoned for not more than six months, or both.

(b) The conducting, or directly assisting in the conducting, as a business, of any game, contest, lottery, or contrivance on board a commercial cruiseship used for the international carriage of passengers whereby a person risks the loss of anything of value in order to realize a profit is not gambling and shall not be suppressed by any law enforcement officer. This subsection shall apply only to commercial cruiseships for the carriage of passengers which are sailing from a port outside the continental limits of the United States to a port in any parish of this state having a population of more than 475,000 or any such ship which is sailing from a port in such a parish to a port outside the continental limits of the United States, provided that the ship is not docked or anchored but is navigating en route between such ports.

(c) The conducting or assisting in the conducting of authorized lottery activities or operations in accordance with provisions of R.S. 47:9000 through 47:9081 shall not be considered gambling for purposes of this section.

(d) The intentional conducting or assisting in the conducting of gaming activities upon a riverboat as defined and authorized in R.S. 4:501 through 4:562, whereby a person risks the loss of anything of value in order to realize a profit is not gambling and shall not be suppressed by any law enforcement officer.

(e) The intentional conducting or assisting in the conducting of gaming operations at the official gaming establishment as defined and authorized in R.S. 4:601 et seq. shall not constitute gambling. (Code 1956, §§ 27-1—27-2.3)

*State law reference—Similar provisions, R.S. 14:90.*

laws.title: Exclusion
laws.content: No act or activity shall be prohibited by this article if it has been excluded by the legislature from the definition of gambling; and no penalty shall be imposed for any violation of this article which would exceed the maximum penalty which may be imposed for the offense of committing the same act or engaging in the same activity under laws adopted by the legislature for the suppression of gambling.

laws.title: Persons under the age of twenty-one entering gaming area—Prohibition
laws.content:
(a) A person under the age of 21 shall not play any licensed gaming device or slot machine in or about a gaming area.

(b) A person under the age of 21 shall not enter into or be present in or about a gaming area.

(c) For the purposes of this section, a "gaming area" is defined as follows: That portion of a gaming riverboat or land-based casino in which gaming activities may be conducted. For purposes of this section, gaming activities means "any activity involving any banking or percentage game which is played with cards, dice, or any electronic, electrical or mechanical device or machine for money, property, or anything of value, but does not include video poker, a lottery, bingo, pull-tabs, raffles, electronic video bingo, cable television bingo, or race horse wagering."

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 18,701, § 1, 4-16-98)

laws.title: Same—Penalties for violators
laws.content:
Any person who violates any of the provisions of section 14-213 may be imprisoned for not more than six months or fined not more than $500.00 dollars or both.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 18,701, § 2, 4-16-98)

*Cross reference—Criminal code, ch. 54.*

*State law reference—Gambling, R.S. 14:90 et seq.*

laws.title: License fees generally
laws.content:
(a) There is hereby levied, for general municipal purposes, a license fee of 2.26 percent on the total daily betting pool, on each person, association, corporation, or other entity conducting a race meeting within the parish.

(b) The license fee imposed under this section shall become the property of the city upon the placing of a wager on a race meeting within this parish.

(c) The license fee levied under this section shall be due and payable monthly on the 20th day of each month.

(d) For the purpose of ascertaining the amount of the license fee payable under this section, all persons, associations, corporations, or other entities conducting race meetings within the parish on or before the 20th day of each month, shall transmit to the director of the department of finance, upon forms prescribed and furnished by him, returns showing the gross amounts wagered during the preceding calendar month. Such returns shall show such further information as the director may require to enable him to correctly compute and collect the fee herein levied. Each return shall be signed by the race conductor filing it and his signature thereon shall constitute a warranty on his part that, to the best of his knowledge and belief, it is true and correct. Every race conductor, at the time of making the return required hereunder, shall compute and remit to the director the required fees due for the proceeding calendar month and failure to do so shall cause such fee to become delinquent. Should any return be prepared by a person other than the race conductor, such person shall also affix his signature thereto and warrant the correctness thereof.

(Code 1956, § 27-19(a)—(d))

*State law reference—Parish license fees for conducting race meetings, R.S. 4:163.1.

laws.title: False returns
laws.content:
Any race conductor and/or other person on behalf of such race conductor signing and filing a return under this division subsequently found to be grossly incorrect, false or fraudulent shall be guilty of a misdemeanor and, upon conviction thereof, shall be subject to a fine of not more than $300.00 or imprisonment for not more than 149 days or both, in the discretion of the court.

(Code 1956, § 27-19(e))

laws.title: Records, reports—Required
laws.content:
Every race conductor required to make a report and pay any fee under this division shall keep and preserve suitable records of the daily gross wager receipts upon which the fee is imposed under this division and such other books of accounts, ledgers or other information as may be required by the director. These records are to be preserved for a period of three years. All books of account, ledgers and other records of the gross wager receipts shall be open to the inspection, examination and photocopying at all reasonable hours, by the director or any of his duly authorized agents.

(Code 1956, § 27-19(f))

laws.title: Same—Penalty for violation
laws.content:
The failure of any race conductor to keep records required by this division or permit the inspection, examination and photocopying thereof by the director or his duly authorized agents, shall be a misdemeanor punishable, upon conviction, by a fine of not more than $ 300.00 or imprisonment for not more than 149 days or both.

(Code 1956, § 27-19(f))

laws.title: Penalty for delinquency
laws.content:
When any license fee payor under this division fails to pay the license fee or any portion thereof on or before the date prescribed for its payment, interest at the rate of $1\frac{1}{4}$ percent per month shall be added to the amount of the fee due from the due date until paid. In addition to the interest that may be so due, there shall also be collected a penalty of five percent of the fee if the failure to pay is not more than 30 days, with an additional five percent for each 30 days or fraction thereof during which the failure to pay continues. **ARTICLE VI. RIVERBOAT GAMING***

**Sec. 14-276. Fee levied.**

(a) In accordance with Louisiana Revised Statute 27:93 (2000), there is hereby levied an admission fee of $2.50 for each passenger boarding or embarking upon a riverboat operating on a river, lake, or other waterway with a licensed berth in the city and which is authorized to originate its excursions in the city by the state riverboat gaming commission.

(b) In the alternative, the city may calculate the $2.50 admission fee based upon a monthly percentage of the adjusted gross revenues of the

*Cross references—Businesses, ch. 30; finance, ch. 70. State law references—Riverboat economic development and gaming control act, R.S. 4:501 et seq.; power of local governing authority, restricted, R.S. 4:552(B).

riverboat. The percentage shall accurately reflect an amount equal to the total monthly admission fees charged at $2.50 per passenger

(c) Pursuant to paragraph (b) of this section, the alternative calculation of the $2.50 admission fee for the Belle of Orleans, L.L.C., shall be 5.47 percent of the adjusted gross revenues collected per month by Belle of Orleans, L.L.C.

(d) Adjusted gross revenue means the revenue figure as currently reported by Belle Orleans, L.L.C. to the office of state police, as audited by that office, and used in the computation of state tax. It is the amount as currently defined in Louisiana Revised Statute 27:44(15) (2000), Louisiana Register sections 42 L.R. § 2723(V)(3)(d), 42 L.R § 2735(A), 42 L.R. 2735(C), 42 L.R. § 2736(A), 42 L.R. § 2736(B), 42 L.R. § 2736(C), less the increases in the Caribbean Stud Poker Progressives, as currently authorized by the office of state police. (Code 1956, § 55A-1; Ord. No. 19,967, § 1, 12-14-00)

**Sec. 14-277. When due and payable.**

The fee levied by this article shall be due and payable at the time when the passenger boards a riverboat subject to the provisions of this article. The riverboat operator is hereby charged with the duty and obligation to collect and remit the fee to the department of finance. For the purposes of this article, the term "passenger" shall not include an employee of the riverboat operators during his working hours; a contractor or supplier of the riverboat operator performing work or providing goods or services in connection with the riverboat’s operation, or a person employed by or acting on behalf of the federal, state or local government while on official government business on the riverboat. (Code 1956, § 55A-2)

**Sec. 14-278. Collection by operator.**

The fee authorized in this article may be assumed by the riverboat operator. (Code 1956, § 55A-3)

**Sec. 14-279. Collection of excess fee prohibited.**

Whoever advertises or collects in the guise of a riverboat gaming admission fee in excess of the fee actually due is guilty of a misdemeanor.  
(Code 1956, § 55A-4)

**Sec. 14-280. Report and remittance.**

Every riverboat operator subject to the terms of this division shall make reports of the previous month’s business on or before the 20th day of the following month, such reports to be accompanied by a certified check, money order or cash for the amount of the fee due as indicated by the report. The monthly report submitted to the department of finance shall be on forms prescribed by the department and shall be signed by the person or riverboat operator remitting the fee, or his duly authorized representative. Such signature shall constitute a warrant on the part of the riverboat operator and the person signing the report that he has read and examined it and that, to the best of his knowledge and belief, the statement and figures therein contained are true, correct and complete.  
(Code 1956, § 55A-5)

**Sec. 14-281. Inspections.**

In order that the department of finance may have additional means of checking and verifying the accuracy of such reports, all the records, books and other documents of riverboat operators and those making such reports as required by the preceding section shall be open for inspection by the department of finance agent at all reasonable hours for a period of four years, commencing with the calendar year in which the fee becomes due and continuing for a period of the three subsequent consecutive calendar years thereafter.  
(Code 1956, § 55A-6)

**Sec. 14-282. Penalties—Civil.**

To further enforce the collection of the fees due under this article, independent of and in addition to the enforcement of the criminal penalties herein provided for under this section, the department of finance and/or the department of law are hereby vested with authority, on motion in a court of competent jurisdiction, to invoke and include in a rule or summary proceeding against a riverboat operator and/or the person responsible for remittance of the fee requiring them to show cause in not less than two nor more than ten days after service thereof, exclusive of holidays, which matter may be tried out of term and in chambers, and shall always be tried by preference, why such riverboat operator should not be enjoined and restrained from further pursuit of the business. In case such rule is made absolute, the order thereon rendered shall be considered a judgment in favor of the city, prohibiting, restraining and enjoining such riverboat operator from further pursuit of the business until such time as he has paid the delinquent fee, penalties, interest, attorney’s fees and costs due, and every violation of the injunction shall be considered as a contempt of court and punishable as such according to law.  
(Code 1956, § 55A-7)

**Sec. 14-283. Same—Additional.**

(a) If any fee due under this article is not collected and remitted within the time prescribed herein it shall become delinquent and the riverboat operator, in addition to being liable for the fee plus interest, shall be subject to penalties of 20 percent of the amount of the fee and interest or $500.00, whichever is greater, and attorney’s fees of ten percent of the sum of the fee, interest and penalty in all cases where an attorney is required to assist in the collection.

(b) Any person signing and filing a daily or monthly report subsequently found to be grossly incorrect, false or fraudulent or violating any of the other provisions of this article shall, upon conviction, be guilty of a misdemeanor.  
(Code 1956, § 55A-8)

laws.title: Permit duration and renewal
laws.content:
(1) Permits shall be valid from the date of issuance through March 31 of each calendar year. Renewal applications and fees shall be due and payable on April 1 for the ensuing year. Failure to pay permit fees shall result in the imposition of delinquency penalties, as provided in subpart (2).

(2) The delinquency penalty shall be 25 percent over and above the regular fee, beginning five days after April 1, if the failure to pay is for not more than 30 days. There shall be an additional five percent penalty for each additional 30 days or fraction thereof during which the failure continues.

laws.title: Permits to be displayed
laws.content:
All permits issued under the provisions of this article shall be displayed in a conspicuous place on the premises at all times. If the establishment’s ability to host live entertainment is granted by conditional use ordinance from the city council, the operating provisos relative to that use shall also be displayed. Failure to comply with this section shall constitute a violation of this article.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 29257, § 2, 11-17-22)

laws.title: Enforcement
laws.content:
(1) Any violation of this article, or applicable provisions of the comprehensive zoning ordinance, or any conditional use pertaining to live entertainment, or any other applicable law is prohibited, and shall subject the permittee to penalties, which may include revocation or suspension of the live entertainment permit, fines or fees, and any other remedy allowed by law.

(2) Notice and hearing requirements for determining violation(s) shall be in accordance with the administrative procedures provided in chapter 6, article II of this Code.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 29257, § 2, 11-17-22)

laws.title: Denial or rescission
laws.content:
Any misstatement or suppression of facts in any application for a permit under this article shall be grounds for refusal of the permit or rescission thereof if already issued.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 29257, § 2, 11-17-22)

laws.title: Approval required of plans
laws.content:
Any person intending or desiring to construct and operate for public amusement any device, contrivance or structure of any kind or nature whatsoever, such as a loop-the-loop, chute-the-chute, scenic railway or roller coaster in any park, vacant lot, building or other place of public resort in the city shall, before attempting to construct such, submit the plans to the department of safety and permits and obtain from it a certificate that the proposed device, contrivance or structure is safe and free from any elements of danger to persons who may use or come in contact therewith.

(Code 1956, § 63-35)

laws.title: Certificate required as prerequisite to operation
laws.content:
Before any device, contrivance or structure under this article is permitted to operate and before the public is permitted to use or come in contact therewith, the person that proposes to operate such shall first obtain a certificate from the director of the department of safety and permits that the structure is safe in all respects and that it has been constructed with the requisite solidity and that all of the materials used in the construction are sound and free from defect. Such certificate must show that the inspection contemplated by this section was actually made by the director of the department of safety and permits or one of his duly qualified assistants.

(Code 1956, § 63-36)

laws.title: Frequency of inspection
laws.content:
The director of the department of safety and permits shall inspect all structures of the character set forth in section 14-331 as often as he may deem necessary; but such inspection shall be made at least once in every 30 days. If any such structure is found to be unsafe or in bad repair the director shall notify the owner or operator thereof. If the operator fails to stop the operation of such device, contrivance or structure immediately he shall be punished in the manner provided in section 1-13.

(Code 1956, § 63-37)

laws.title: Consent required; enclosure
laws.content:
It shall not be lawful for any person to erect or in any manner establish or continue any pistol or shooting gallery within the limits of the city without having first obtained the consent of two-thirds of the persons residing within one square [sic] of the place where any pistol or shooting gallery is intended to be established and the permission of the council. Any person establishing such shooting gallery shall have it enclosed as to prevent the report of firearms being heard in the streets on which it may be located.

(Code 1956, § 63-38)
