*Subdivision IV. Telephone Operator Permit*

laws.title: Required
laws.content:
No person shall answer the business telephone of an escort service without a valid permit issued pursuant to the provisions of this article.  
(Code 1956, § 22A-5)

laws.title: Application fee
laws.content:
Any person desiring to obtain a permit to act as a telephone operator for an escort service shall make application to the director of the department of finance for a telephone operator permit. A fee of $250.00 made payable to the director of the department of finance shall accompany the submission of the application to defray the costs of investigation and administration before and after the issuance of a permit.  
(Code 1956, § 22A-5(1)(a))

laws.title: Grant
laws.content:
Within 60 days of receipt of the application, the director of the department of finance shall grant or deny it. The director shall grant a telephone operator permit only if he finds that:

(1) The required fee has been paid.

(2) The applicant has not knowingly made a material misstatement in the application for a permit.

(3) The applicant has fully cooperated in the investigation of his application.

(4) The applicant has not been convicted of or has currently pending against that person any violation of the law of any state of the United States which would be a felony under the law of the state or any violation of any law of any jurisdiction for the unlawful practice of massage, prostitution, pandering, pimping, promoting prostitution,

inciting prostitution, lewd conduct or sexual misconduct within five years of the application.

(5) The applicant has not previously had a telephone operator permit, escort permit or escort service license denied or revoked for cause by this city or by any other jurisdiction in this or any other state within two years of the date of application.

(6) The applicant is at least 17 years of age.  
(Code 1956, § 22A-5(3))

Secs. 30-561–30-585. Reserved.

laws.title: Authorized, procedure
laws.content:
No license or permit may be revoked until after due notice and hearing before the director of the department of finance or his duly authorized representative to determine if grounds for revocation exist. Notice of such hearing shall be in writing and served at least ten days prior to the date of hearing by registered mail or personal service or, in the case of the escort establishment, by posting on the interior of the escort establishment. The notice shall state the grounds of the complaint against the permittee or licensee and shall designate the time and place where the hearing will be held. The licensee or permittee shall have the right to appear at such hearing and to produce evidence. After holding the hearing, the director of the department of finance shall suspend or permanently revoke the license or permit if it has been charged and proved that the licensee or permittee has been guilty of violating one or more of the grounds for revocation specified in section 30-587 or that the circumstances exist that would warrant the denial of issuance of such license or permit in the first place.  
(Code 1956, § 22A-6)

laws.title: Grounds
laws.content:
The following acts or omissions are declared to be in violation of this article and, when committed by an escort service, escort or telephone operator employed by the escort service, constitute grounds for suspension or revocation of a license or permit issued under this subdivision to the escort service which employs the violator or to the violator:

(1) The committing or solicitation to commit any lewd acts, sexual misconduct, sexual perversion or unlawful homosexual acts engaged in by escorts, including but not limited to the following: Exposing, touching, caressing or fondling of genitals, anus, vulva, pubic hair or nipples of female breasts; masturbation; oral copulation, cunnilingus or fellatio; sodomy; bestiality; sadomasochistic abuse; flagellation or torture in the context of sexual relationship; any unnatural carnal copulation by a human being with another of the same or opposite sex.

(2) Prostitution, pandering or solicitation to perform a natural or unnatural sex act by escorts.

(3) Making false statements in writing on the application for a license issued under this article.

(4) Allowing persons below the age of 17 years to be on the premises of an escort service establishment or to be employed by an escort service.

(5) Any act of disturbance of the peace at the escort service premises or at the location of any escort appointment. For purposes of this section, disturbing the peace is defined as the performance of any of the following acts:

a. To communicate to another person a threat, either verbally, in writing or through any other form of communication, to kill or murder him or to do him great bodily harm or threatening to kill, murder or do great bodily harm to members of his family or to any other person to whom the threat is communicated.

b. To address any words to any person who is lawfully in a public place where such words, which, by their very utterance, inflict injury and have a direct tendency to cause acts of violence by the

CD30:35
§ 30-587

NEW ORLEANS CODE

person to whom individually the remark is addressed.

c. To address language to any person that makes reference to the person addressed as having sexual intercourse with himself or with another where such language inflicts injury, insults or causes acts of violence by the person to whom the language is addressed or is intended to inflict injury, insult or cause acts of violence.

(6) Violation of any of the provisions of this article.

(7) The presence of a person at the escort service establishment premises who engages in escort appointments and does not have a valid escort permit.

(8) The presence of a person on the escort service premises who answers the business telephone of the escort service and does not have a valid telephone operator permit.

(9) The negotiation of any escort service appointment by a telephone operator with a customer that alludes to, suggests or in any way discusses services described in subsection (1) or (2) of this section.

(10) The sending of an escort who does not possess a valid permit on an escort appointment.

(11) Failure to obtain a valid occupational license.

(Code 1956, § 22A-7)

Secs. 30-588–30-610. Reserved.

laws.title: Maintenance of license on premises
laws.content:
Escort services shall maintain their licenses at the location at which their business telephones are answered.

(Code 1956, § 22A-2(1))

laws.title: Possession of permits
laws.content:
Escorts and telephone operators shall maintain their permits on their person at all times while employed.

(Code 1956, § 22A-2(2))

laws.title: Records
laws.content:
Escort services shall keep a written record of the date and hour of each escort appointment, the name and address of the customer and the location of the escort appointment. Such record shall be open to inspection by officials charged with the enforcement of this article, including representatives of the departments of finance and police.

(Code 1956, § 22A-2(3))

laws.title: Prohibited acts
laws.content:
Escorts shall not engage in any acts of sexual intercourse for compensation, nor shall escorts engage in any activities which would be in violation of any laws of the city or state.

(Code 1956, § 22A-2(4))

laws.title: Right of entry on premises
laws.content:
The police department shall have the right of entry on the premises of any escort service located within the parish during the hours such establishment is operating. The escort service establishment premises shall be construed to be the location at which the business telephones of such service are being answered.

(Code 1956, § 22A-2(5))

laws.title: Work performed on premises
laws.content:
(a) The owner or telephone operator shall be at the premises of the escort service establishment at all times during working hours.

(b) The business telephone of the escort service shall only be answered at the location listed on the escort service license.

(Code 1956, § 22A-2(6), (7))

laws.title: Minimum age of employees
laws.content:
The owner shall not employ any escort or telephone operator who is under the age of 17 years.

(Code 1956, § 22A-2(8))

§ 30-651

laws.title: List of employees
laws.content:
The owner shall maintain at all times at the escort service establishment premises a list of all employees, including current home addresses and telephone numbers.

(Code 1956, § 22A-2(9))

Secs. 30-619—30-650. Reserved.

laws.title: Enforcement
laws.content:
The department of health shall enforce the provisions of this article and prosecute all persons charged with violating it and to that end its officers, members, agents, employees, inspectors and appointees shall have the right to enter any place, car, conveyance or other vehicle in the city for the purpose of inspection for violations thereof.

(Code 1956, § 26-2)

laws.title: Establishments outside jurisdiction of city
laws.content:
Food from food service establishments outside the jurisdiction of the department of health may be sold within the city if such food service

establishments conform to the provisions of this article or to substantially equivalent provisions. To determine the extent of compliance with such provisions, the health authority may accept reports from responsible authorities in other parishes or jurisdictions where such food service establishments are located.

(Code 1956, § 26-41.8(4))

laws.title: Temporary food service establishments
laws.content:
A temporary food service establishment shall comply with all provisions of this article which are applicable to its operation; provided, that the health authority may augment such requirements when needed to assure the service of safe food, may prohibit the sale of certain potentially hazardous food and may modify specific requirements for physical facilities when in his opinion no imminent health hazard will result.

(Code 1956, § 26-41.7)

laws.title: Plan review of future construction
laws.content:
When a food service establishment is constructed or extensively remodeled, or when an existing structure is converted for use as a food service establishment, properly prepared plans and specifications for such construction, remodeling, or alteration, showing layout, arrangement, and construction materials of work areas, and the location, size, and type of fixed equipment and facilities, shall be submitted to the health authority for approval before such work is begun.

(Code 1956, § 26-41.8(5))

laws.title: Price lists required
laws.content:
Every keeper or owner of a restaurant, eating house or other place where wines and dishes of food are sold shall provide his customers in such restaurant or eating house with a plainly written or printed list of the wines and dishes of food he has for sale and the price he charges for each bottle of wine and dish of food.

(Code 1956, § 26-37)

laws.title: Charging more than list price prohibited
laws.content:
It shall not be lawful for any keeper, owner or employee of any restaurant or eating house to

(Code 1956, § 26-38)

**Sec. 30-660. Posting copies of law; penalty.**

All keepers or owners of restaurants and eating houses to whom sections 30-658 and 30-659 may extend shall have a copy of sections 30-658 and 30-659 conspicuously posted in their restaurants or eating houses.

(Code 1956, § 26-39)

**Sec. 30-661. Failure to pay for food or drink obtained.**

Any person who shall go into any drugstore, hotel, inn, boardinghouse, restaurant, barroom, saloon, cabaret, night club, fountain or other public eating or drinking house and obtain food, beverages, alcoholic or nonalcoholic, and fail or refuse to pay for such food or beverages, except when credit is given by express agreement, at the prices regularly charged by such public eating or drinking house or place shall be guilty of an offense.

(Code 1956, § 26-36)

*State law reference—Fraudulent acts, R.S. 21:21, 21:22.*

**Sec. 30-662. Responsibility of members, officers, etc.**

When an association of individuals is charged with the violation of any provision of this article, each individual of such association or, if a foreign association, the local agent or person locally in charge thereof shall be deemed to represent such association of individuals for the purpose of enforcing this article and shall be held responsible and punishable for each violation thereof. When a firm is charged with such violation each member thereof and, if a foreign firm, the local agent or person locally in charge of such firm shall be deemed to represent such firm for the purpose of enforcing this article and shall be held responsible and punishable for each violation thereof. When a corporation shall be charged with such violation, the president or, in his absence, the vice-president or, in the absence of both, the officer or individual in charge of such corporation or, if a foreign corporation, the local agent or person

locally in charge thereof shall be deemed to represent such corporation for the purpose of enforcing this article and shall be held responsible and punishable for each violation thereof.

(Code 1956, § 26-3)

**Sec. 30-663. Penalties.**

Any person who shall violate any of the provisions of this article shall be guilty of a misdemeanor and, upon conviction thereof, shall be punished by a fine of not less than $50.00 nor more than $100.00. In addition thereto, such persons may be enjoined from continuing such violations. Each day upon which such a violation occurs shall constitute a separate violation.

(Code 1956, § 26-41.8(8))

**Secs. 30-664—30-690. Reserved.**

(a) It shall be unlawful for any person to operate a food service establishment within the city who does not possess a valid permit issued to him by the department of health. Only a person who complies with the requirements of this article shall be entitled to receive and retain such a permit.

(b) Permits shall be posted conspicuously in every food service establishment.

(c) Except as otherwise provided in this code, permits for temporary food service establishments shall be issued for a period of time not to exceed 14 days.

laws.title: Issuance
laws.content:
When inspection reveals that the applicable requirements of this article have been met, a permit required by this division shall be issued to the applicant by the department of health after payment of any established permit fees. If the initial permit is purchased at a time other than the regular licensing period the cost of the permit shall be prorated except that itinerant food operations shall pay the stated permit fee regardless of the date of licensing. When it is necessary to prorate a permit fee, any part of a month shall be considered a whole month to facilitate calculating the permit fee.  
(Code 1956, § 26-41.8(1)(a))

laws.title: Renewals
laws.content:
Once a permit has been issued under this division, subsequent permits will be issued automatically upon paying of the permit fee; however, such food service establishments are subject to regulatory inspections and such permit is subject to suspension or revocation for cause.  
(Code 1956, § 26-41.8(1)(a))

laws.title: Suspension
laws.content:
(a) Permits issued under this division may be suspended temporarily by the department of health for failure of the holder to comply with the requirements of this article.

(b) Whenever a permit holder or operator has failed to comply with any notice issued under the provisions of this division, the permit holder or operator shall be notified in writing that the permit is, upon service of the notice, immediately suspended and that an opportunity for a hearing will be provided if a written request for a hearing is filed with the department of health by the permit holder.

(c) Notwithstanding the other provisions of this article, whenever the department of health finds unsanitary or other conditions in the operation of a food service establishment which, in its judgment, constitute a substantial hazard to the public health, it may without warning, notice or hearing, issue a written notice to the permit holder or operator citing such condition, specifying the corrective action to be taken, and specifying the time period within which such action shall be taken; and, if deemed necessary, such order shall state that the permit is immediately suspended, and all food service operations are to be immediately discontinued. Any person to whom such an order is issued shall comply immediately therewith, but upon written petition to the department of health, shall be afforded a hearing as soon as possible.  
(Code 1956, § 26-41.8(1)(b))

laws.title: Revocation
laws.content:
For serious or repeated violations of any of the requirements of this article, or for interference with the department of health in the performance of its duties, the permit may be permanently re-

CD30:41
§ 30-698

NEW ORLEANS CODE

voked after an opportunity for a hearing has been provided by the department of health. Prior to such action, the department shall notify the permit holder in writing, stating the reasons for which the permit is subject to revocation and advising that the permit shall be permanently revoked at the end of five days following service of such notice, unless a request for a hearing is filed with the department of health, by the permit holder, within such five-day period. A permit may be suspended for cause pending its revocation or a hearing relative thereto.

(Code 1956, § 26-41.8(1)(d))

laws.title: Misuse of permits
laws.content:
(a) No person, individual, or corporation shall copy, reproduce, or counterfeit, or cause to be copied, reproduced or counterfeited, any permit issued pursuant to this division by any form or process, or to otherwise represent something to be a valid permit when it is not.

(b) Whosoever violates the prohibition of this section shall be punished in accordance with the penalty provided for in section 1-13.

(Code 1956, § 26-42)

Secs. 30-701–30-725. Reserved.

laws.title: Inspection of food service establishments
laws.content:
At least twice yearly, the department of health shall inspect each food service establishment located in the parish and shall make as many additional inspections and reinspections as are necessary for the enforcement of this article.

(Code 1956, § 26-41.8(2))

laws.title: Access to establishments
laws.content:
The department of health, after proper identification, shall be permitted to enter, at any reasonable time, any food service establishment within the parish for the purpose of making inspections to determine compliance with this article. Department personnel shall be permitted to examine the records of the establishment to obtain pertinent information pertaining to food and supplies purchased, received, or used, and persons employed.

(Code 1956, § 26-41.8(2)(a))

laws.title: Inspection records
laws.content:
Whenever the department of health makes an inspection of a food service establishment, the inspector shall record his findings on an inspection report form provided for this purpose, and shall furnish the original of such inspection report form to the permit holder or operator.

(Code 1956, § 26-41.8(2)(b))

laws.title: Issuance of notices
laws.content:
Whenever the department of health makes an inspection of a food service establishment and discovers that any of the requirements of sections 30-656, 30-732, 30-733, 30-735, 30-737, 30-738, 30-656 have been violated, the director of the department of health shall notify the permit holder or operator of such violations by means of an in-

*Cross reference—Health regulations regarding food, § 82-36 et seq.

CD30:42
BUSINESSES

§ 30-732

spection report form or other written notice. In such notification, the director shall:

(1) Set forth the specific violations found.

(2) Establish a specific and reasonable period of time for the correction of the violations found. In the case of temporary food service establishments, violations must be corrected within a specified period of time not to exceed 24 hours. Failure to comply with such notice shall result in immediate suspension of the permit by the director of the department of health.

(3) Failure to comply with any notice issued in accordance with the provisions of this article may result in immediate suspension of the permit.

(4) An opportunity for appeal from any notice or inspection findings will be provided if a written request for a hearing is filed with the department of health within the period of time established in the notice for correction.

(Code 1956, § 26-41.8(2)(c))

laws.title: Service of notices
laws.content:
(a) Notices provided for under this division shall be deemed to have been properly served when the original of the inspection report form or other notice has been delivered personally to the permit holder or person in charge, or such notice has been sent by registered or certified mail, return receipt requested, to the last known address of the permit holder. A copy of such notice shall be filed with the records of the department of health.

(b) The police department shall be notified of and shall enforce revocations and suspensions.

(Code 1956, § 26-41.8(2)(d))

laws.title: Examination and condemnation of food
laws.content:
Food may be examined or sampled by the department of health without charge as often as may be necessary to determine freedom from adulteration or misbranding. The department may, upon written notice to the owner or person in charge, place a hold order on any food which it determines or has probable cause to believe to be unwholesome or otherwise adulterated, or misbranded. Under a hold order, food shall be permitted to be suitably stored. It shall be unlawful for any person to remove or alter a hold order, notice or tag placed on food by the department of health, and neither such food nor the containers thereof shall be relabeled, repacked, reprocessed, altered, disposed of, or destroyed without permission of the department. On the basis of his examination the director of the department of health may vacate the hold order, or may by written order direct the owner or person in charge of the food which was placed under the hold order to denature or destroy such food or to bring it into compliance with the provisions of this article.

(Code 1956, § 26-41.8(3))

laws.title: Food
laws.content:
(a) Food supplies. All food in food service establishments shall be from sources approved or considered satisfactory by the department of health, and shall be clean, wholesome, free from spoilage, free from adulteration and misbranding, and safe for human consumption. No hermetically sealed, nonacid and low acid food which has been processed in a place other than a commercial food processing establishment shall be used.

(b) Food protection. All food while being stored, prepared, displayed, served, or sold at food service establishments, or during transportation between such establishments, shall be protected from contamination. All perishable food shall be stored at such temperatures as will protect against spoilage. All potentially hazardous food shall be maintained at safe temperatures (45 degrees Fahrenheit or below, or 145 degrees Fahrenheit or above), except during necessary periods of preparation and service. Raw fruits and vegetables shall be washed before use. Poultry stuffing, stuffed meats and poultry, and pork and pork products shall be thoroughly cooked before being served. Portions of food once served to the customer shall not be served again.

(c) Poisonous, toxic materials. Only such poisonous and toxic materials as are required to maintain sanitary conditions and for sanitization purposes may be used or stored in food service

CD30:43
§ 30-732

NEW ORLEANS CODE

establishments. Poisonous and toxic materials shall be identified, and shall be used only in such manner and under such conditions as will not contaminate food or constitute a hazard to employees or customers.

(Code 1956, § 26-41.2)

laws.title: Personnel
laws.content:
(a) *Health and disease control.* Notice shall be sent to the duly authorized representative of the director of the department of health immediately by the manager of the public eating and/or drinking place or by the employee concerned, if he or any employee contracts any infectious, contagious or communicable disease, or has a fever, a skin eruption, a cough lasting more than three weeks, or any other suspicious symptoms of a communicable disease. It shall be the duty of any employee to notify the manager immediately when and if said conditions occur, and if neither the manager nor the employee concerned notifies the duly authorized representative of the director of the department of health immediately when any of such conditions occur, they shall be held jointly and severally to have violated this regulation.

(b) *Cleanliness.* All employees shall wear clean outer garments, maintain a high degree of personal cleanliness, and conform to hygienic practices while on duty. They shall wash their hands thoroughly in an approved hand washing facility before starting work, and as often as may be necessary to remove soil and contamination. No employee shall resume work after visiting the toilet room without first washing his hands. Employees shall wear hair restraints approved by the health authority.

(Code 1956, § 26-41.3)

laws.title: Procedure when infection is suspected
Food equipment and utensils
laws.content:
(a) *Sanitary design, construction and installation of equipment and utensils.* All equipment and utensils shall be so designed and of such material and workmanship as to be smooth, easily cleanable and durable, and shall be in good repair; and the food contact surfaces of such equipment and utensils shall, in addition, be easily accessible for cleaning, nontoxic, corrosion resistant and relatively nonabsorbent. When approved by the department of health, exceptions may be made to the above materials requirements. Single service articles shall be made from nontoxic materials.

(b) *Cleanliness of equipment and utensils.* All eating and drinking utensils shall be thoroughly cleaned and sanitized after each usage. Sanitization shall be by a method approved by the department of health.

(1) All kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment, exclusive of cooking surfaces of equipment, used in the preparation or serving of food or drink, and all food storage utensils, shall be thoroughly cleaned after each use. Cooking surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned at least once a day. All utensils and food contact surfaces of equipment used in the preparation, service, display, or storage of potentially hazardous food shall be thoroughly cleaned and sani-

CD30:44
BUSINESSES

§ 30-737

tized prior to such use. Nonfood contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned at such intervals as to keep them in a clean and sanitary condition.

(2) After cleaning and until use, all food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils shall be so stored and handled as to be protected from contamination.

(3) All single-service articles shall be stored, handled, and dispensed in a sanitary manner, and shall be used only once.

(Code 1956, § 26-41.4)

laws.title: Inspections, order to discontinue use of utensils and materials
laws.content:
The department of health is hereby authorized to inspect, through its proper officers, all public places, licensed under state laws or city ordinances, in which foods or liquids are prepared or sold for human consumption, and to inspect and examine the utensils and apparatus used therein, and in case that any practices are ascertained, or utensils or materials are used therein deleterious to human health, to order the discontinuance thereof.

(Code 1956, § 26-40)

laws.title: Sanitary facilities and controls
laws.content:
(a) Water supply. The water supply shall be adequate, of a safe, sanitary quality and from an approved source. Hot and cold running water under pressure shall be provided in all areas where food is prepared, or equipment, utensils, or containers are washed. Ice used for any purpose shall be made from water which comes from an approved source, and shall be used only if it has been manufactured, stored, transported, and handled in an approved sanitary manner.

(b) Sewage disposal. All sewage shall be disposed of in a public sewerage system or, in the absence thereof, in a manner approved by the department of health.

(c) Plumbing. Plumbing shall be so sized, installed, and maintained as to carry adequate quantities of water to required locations throughout the establishment; as to prevent contamination of the water supply; as to properly convey sewage and liquid wastes from the establishment to the sewerage or sewerage disposal system; and so that it does not constitute a source of contamination of food, equipment, or utensils, or create an unsanitary condition or nuisance.

(d) Toilet facilities. Each food service establishment shall be provided with conveniently located toilet facilities for its employees. These facilities shall consist of a minimum of one commode and one lavatory, properly plumbed, for each 15 employees on the premises at one time. Those establishments employing in excess of 15 persons including both males and females shall provide separate facilities. Toilet fixtures shall be of sanitary design and readily cleanable. Toilet facilities, including rooms and fixtures, shall be kept in a clean condition and in good repair. The doors of all toilet rooms shall be self-closing. Toilet tissue shall be provided. Easily cleanable receptacles shall be provided for waste materials, and such receptacles in toilet rooms for women shall be covered. Where the use of nonwater-carried sewage disposal facilities have been approved by the health authority, such facilities shall be separate from the establishment. When toilet facilities are provided for patrons, such facilities shall meet the requirements of this subsection. Toilet rooms shall be ventilated by positive means to the outside air.

(e) Hand washing facilities. Each food service establishment shall be provided with adequate, conveniently located hand washing facilities for its employees, including a lavatory or lavatories equipped with hot and cold running water, a mixing faucet, hand cleansing soap or detergent, and approved sanitary towels or other approved hand drying devices in food preparation areas. Such facilities shall be kept clean and in good repair.

(f) Garbage and rubbish disposal. All garbage and rubbish containing food wastes shall, prior to disposal, be kept in leakproof, nonabsorbent containers which shall be kept covered with tightfitting lids when filled or stored, or not in continuous use; provided, that such containers need not be covered in a special insect and rodent proofed room or enclosure, or in a food waste refrigerator. All other rubbish shall be stored in containers, rooms or areas in an approved manner. The rooms,

CD30:45
§ 30-737

NEW ORLEANS CODE

enclosures, areas and containers used shall be adequate for the storage of all food waste and rubbish accumulating on the premises. Adequate cleaning facilities shall be provided, and each container, room or area shall be thoroughly cleaned after the emptying or removal of garbage and rubbish. Food waste grinders, if used, shall be installed in compliance with state and local standards and shall be of suitable construction. All garbage and rubbish shall be disposed of with sufficient frequency and in such a manner as to prevent a nuisance.

(g) Insect and rodent control. Effective measures shall be taken to protect against the entrance into the establishment and the breeding or presence on the premises of insects and rodents. All openings into the outer air shall be effectively screened, unless other accepted effective means of fly control are provided. Doors and screen doors shall be self-closing and open outward.

(Code 1956, § 26-41.5)

laws.title: Other facilities and operations
laws.content:
(a) Floors, walls, and ceilings. The floor surfaces in kitchens, in all other rooms and areas in which food is stored or prepared and in which utensils are washed, and in walk-in refrigerators, dressing or locker rooms and toilet rooms, shall be of nonabsorbent materials, and so constructed as to be easily cleanable; provided, that the floors of nonrefrigerated, dry food storage areas need not be nonabsorbent. All floors shall be kept clean and in good repair. Floor drains shall be provided in all rooms where floors are subjected to flooding type cleaning or where normal operations release or discharge water or other liquid waste on the floor. All exterior areas where food is served shall be kept clean and properly drained, and surfaces in such areas shall be finished so as to facilitate maintenance and minimize dust.

(1) The walls and ceilings of all rooms shall be kept clean and in good repair.

(2) All walls of rooms or areas in which food is prepared, or utensils or hands are washed, shall be easily cleanable.

(b) Lighting. All areas in which food is prepared or stored or utensils are washed, hand washing areas, dressing or locker rooms, toilet rooms, and garbage and rubbish storage areas shall be well lighted. During all cleanup activities, adequate light shall be provided in the area being cleaned, and upon or around equipment being cleaned.

(c) Ventilation. All rooms in which food is prepared or served or utensils are washed, dressing or locker rooms, toilet rooms, and garbage and rubbish storage areas shall be well ventilated. Ventilation hoods and devices shall be designed to prevent grease or condensate from dripping into food or onto food preparation surfaces. Filters, where used, shall be readily removable for cleaning or replacement. Ventilation systems shall comply with applicable state and local fire prevention requirements and shall, when vented to the outside air, discharge in such a manner as not to create a nuisance.

(d) Dressing rooms and lockers. Adequate facilities shall be provided for the orderly storage of employees’ clothing and personal belongings. Where employees routinely change clothes within the establishment, one or more dressing rooms or designated areas shall be provided for this purpose. Such designated areas shall be located outside of the food preparation, storage, and serving areas, and the utensil washing and storage areas; provided, that, when approved by the health authority, such an area may be located in a storage room where only completely packaged food is stored. Designated areas shall be equipped with adequate lockers, and lockers or other suitable facilities shall be provided in dressing rooms. Dressing rooms and lockers shall be kept clean.

(e) Housekeeping. All parts of the establishment and its premises shall be kept neat, clean, and free of litter and rubbish. Cleaning operations shall be conducted in such a manner as to minimize contamination of food and food contact surfaces. None of the operations connected with a food service establishment shall be conducted in any room used as living or sleeping quarters nor shall there be a direct opening between such areas. Soiled linens, coats, and aprons shall be kept in suitable containers until removed for laundering. No live birds or animals shall be allowed in any enclosed area used for the conduct of food service establishment operations; provided, that guide

dogs accompanying blind persons may be permitted in dining areas.  
(Code 1956, § 26-41.6)

Secs. 30-739—30-770. Reserved.

laws.title: Floor and drains
laws.content:
The whole floor of the room in which the market is situated shall be properly ratproofed and shall be paved with concrete, stone or tile pavement, with ice drains and a cleanout or drain connected to the city’s subsewer main if artificial ice refrigeration is used. If mechanical refrigeration is used such ice drain and cleanout to sewer will not be required.

(Code 1956, § 35-4)

laws.title: Ceilings and walls; wainscot
laws.content:
The entire inside surfaces of ceilings and walls down to the wainscot shall be finished with smooth gypsum plaster, wallboard or mill-dressed, clear-face tongue and grooved wood ceiling boards. There shall be a wainscot built to grounds around all inside walls, five feet high from the floor up, in three-coat work plaster, the last coat to be in hard, smooth putty or some cement finish, or the wainscot may be of glazed tile, salt-glazed brick or wall tile.

(Code 1956, § 35-5)

laws.title: Paint
laws.content:
The interior woodwork and plaster wainscot shall receive three coats of inside oil paint; the plaster wainscot shall receive an additional coat of high gloss enamel paint.

(Code 1956, § 35-6)

laws.title: Light and ventilation; screens
laws.content:
Ample light and ventilation shall be provided and all openings shall be properly screened with a standard mesh screen wire.

(Code 1956, § 35-7)

laws.title: Doors
laws.content:
All entrances to private markets shall be equipped with glass or wire screen doors which shall be provided with self-closing springs of sufficient strength to ensure the doors being tightly closed at all times when not in use.

(Code 1956, § 35-8)

laws.title: Ceiling fan
laws.content:
There shall be an adequate approved ceiling fan installed at each door affording entrance to the market.

(Code 1956, § 35-9)

laws.title: Artificial illumination
laws.content:
Adequate artificial illumination shall be provided for all parts of the market.

(Code 1956, § 35-10)

laws.title: Water, sinks, toilet facilities
laws.content:
There shall be provided a wash sink or sinks and an ample supply of both hot and cold water. There shall also be provided ample toilet facilities in accordance with the rules of the department of health and the sewerage and water board of the city.

(Code 1956, § 35-11)

laws.title: Refrigeration
laws.content:
All compartments, boxes or space intended for the storage or display of foods shall be properly and adequately refrigerated with ice or by mechanical means with drains to the main drain.

(Code 1956, § 35-12)

laws.title: Requirements when less than whole room used for market
laws.content:
A private market may occupy the whole or any part of a building but, when a market occupies only a part of a room, the whole room shall conform entirely to the provisions of this article, irrespective of what use is made of the other portions of the room. This requirement shall not apply to existing markets or alterations for which a building permit was acquired prior to May 28, 1932.

(Code 1956, § 35-13)

**ARTICLE XII. MASSAGE THERAPISTS AND MASSAGE ESTABLISHMENTS***

**DIVISION 1. GENERALLY**

**Sec. 30-931. Definitions.**

The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:

*Massage* shall mean any process or procedure upon the external parts of the body of a patron consisting of rubbing, stroking, pressing, kneading, or tapping by any means.

*Massage establishment* means any establishment or business wherein massage is practiced as a major use occupying more than 25 percent of the floor areas of the subject establishment or business, including establishments commonly known as massage studios or massage parlors.

*Massage therapist* means any person who gives or administers a massage.

*Patron* means any person 18 years or older who receives a massage under such circumstances that it is reasonably expected that he will pay money or give any consideration therefor.

(Code 1956, § 35A-1-4)

Cross reference—Definitions generally, § 1-2.

State law reference—Definitions, R.S. 37:3552.

*Cross reference—Performing massage on person of the opposite sex prohibited, § 54-485.*

**Sec. 30-932. Purpose.**

It is hereby found and determined that the practice of massage therapy is a professional skill which offers significant therapeutic benefits to many persons. It is further found and determined that the practice of massage therapy by unqualified persons may pose a danger to the public health, safety and welfare. It is the purpose of this article, in the absence of uniform state regulation of massage therapy, to ensure that persons performing massage therapy in the city have a proper knowledge of the practice of the profession and that the public is protected from unqualified practitioners.

(Code 1956, § 35A-1-1)

**Sec. 30-933. Rules and regulations.**

The director of the department of health shall, with the consent of the mayor, submit to the council for its approval such reasonable regulations necessary to the performance of the functions assigned by this article in accordance with section 4-107 of the home rule charter. Any such regulation may be rescinded or amended either by the same process as when originally submitted or by the council at any time. All regulations shall be subordinate to the ordinance of the council.

(Code 1956, § 35A-1-3)

**Sec. 30-934. Exemptions.**

This article shall not apply to the following:

(1) Hospitals, nursing homes, sanitariums or other healthcare facilities licensed under the state; and physicians, surgeons, chiropractors, osteopaths or physical therapists licensed or registered to practice their respective professions under the laws of the state or nurses registered under the laws of the state acting under their direction and control.

(2) Barbershops and beauty parlors, barbers and beauticians licensed under the laws of the state provided that such massage as is practiced is limited to the head, neck and scalp.

(3) Accredited high schools and colleges and coaches and trainers therein while acting within the scope of their employment.

(4) Trainers of any amateur, semiprofessional or professional athlete or athletic team.

(5) Clubs organized for pleasure, recreation and other nonprofitable purposes, who shall furnish proof of tax-exempt status under the provisions of 26 USC 501(c)(3) and (7) to the director of the department of health.

(Code 1956, § 35A-1-14)

laws.title: Expiration of licenses and permits
laws.content:
All licenses or permits issued pursuant to the provisions of this article shall expire one calendar year from the date of issuance unless previously revoked. All practicing massage therapists or operators of massage establishments on the effective date of the ordinance from which this article was derived shall immediately be subject to all of the provisions of this article.

(Code 1956, § 35A-1-13)

State law reference—License or registration renewal, R.S. 37:3561.

laws.title: Penalty
laws.content:
Violation by any person of any of the provisions of this article is hereby declared to be a misdemeanor.

(Code 1956, § 35A-1-11)

State law reference—Penalties, R.S. 37:3565.

Secs. 30-937–30-955. Reserved.

laws.title: License required
laws.content:
No person shall carry on the business of operating a massage establishment at any place within the city unless he has a valid license issued pursuant to the provisions of this division for each and every place of business.

(Code 1956, § 35A-1-7)

*State law references—Registration of massage establishments, R.S. 37:3558 et seq.; effect on local regulations, R.S. 37:3567.

laws.title: Application
laws.content:
(a) Any person desiring a massage establishment license shall file a written application with the director of the department of health on a form to be provided by the director. If the applicant is a corporation, the name of the corporation shall be set forth exactly as set forth in its articles of incorporation, together with the names and addresses of each of its officers, directors and each stockholder of the corporation; and the application shall be verified by an officer of the corporation. If the applicant is a partnership, the application shall set forth the name and residence address of each of the partners, including limited partners; and the application shall be verified by each partner. If one or more of the partners is a corporation, the provisions of this section pertaining to a corporate applicant shall apply to the corporate partner. If the applicant is neither a corporation nor a partnership, the application shall set forth the full name and address of the applicant and be verified by the applicant.

(b) The application for a massage establishment license shall set forth the proposed place of business and the facilities therefor, together with a detailed description of the nature and scope of the proposed business operation. In addition to the foregoing, the following information shall be furnished concerning the applicant if an individual; and officer and director if the applicant is a corporation; and concerning the partners, including limited partners, if the applicant is a partnership:

(1) The previous addresses, if any, for a period of three years, immediately prior to the date of application and the dates of such residence.

(2) The date of birth.

(3) Four passport-size photographs, one inch by one inch, taken within 60 days of the date of application.

(4) The business, occupation or employment history for three years immediately preceding the date of application, including but not limited to whether such person previ-

NEW ORLEANS CODE

ously operating under a permit or license in another city in this or another state had such license suspended or revoked.

(5) All convictions, including ordinance violations, exclusive of traffic violations, with a brief statement of the nature of the convictions and the jurisdiction in which the convictions occurred.

(6) A physical description, including height, weight, sex, color of eyes, color of hair, birthmarks and scars.

(7) Proof of property damage and bodily injury liability insurance coverage in an amount of not less than $1,000,000.00.

(8) Proof that the applicant holds a valid occupational license.

(9) A complete set of fingerprints taken by the department of health.

(Code 1956, § 35A-1-7(1)(b))

**Sec. 30-958. Application fee.**

Any person desiring to obtain a license to operate a massage establishment shall make application to the director of the department of health. A fee of $ 100.50 made payable to the city shall accompany the submission of the application to defray the cost of administration and investigation. If the applicant is not granted a license under the provisions of this chapter, $50.00 of the application fee shall be returned to the applicant.

(Code 1956, § 35A-1-7(1)(a))

**Sec. 30-959. Investigation.**

Applications for licenses under this division shall be referred to the superintendent of police and the director of the department of safety and permits within 48 hours of the application being filed, who shall cause an investigation to be made and report their findings to the director of the department of health. Applicants shall cooperate with any investigation conducted pursuant to the provisions of this article and shall permit access to the proposed place of business and facilities therefor in conjunction with any such investigation.

(Code 1956, § 35A-1-7(2))

**Sec. 30-960. Issuance.**

Within 60 days of the receipt of an application, the director of the department of health shall either grant or deny a massage license. The departments of police, safety and permits, and state sanitarian services shall be notified within 48 hours of the denial or acceptance of the application by the department of health. The director of the department of health shall grant a massage license only if he finds that:

(1) The required fee has been paid.

(2) The application conforms in all respects to the provisions of this article.

(3) The applicant has not knowingly made a material misstatement in the application for a license.

(4) The applicant has fully cooperated in the investigation of his application.

(5) The massage establishment as proposed by the applicant would comply with all applicable laws, including but not limited to the city’s building, zoning and health regulations.

(6) The applicant if an individual, or any of the stockholders of the corporation, any officers or directors if the applicant is a corporation, or any of the partners, including limited partners, if the applicant is a partnership, have not been convicted of a felony or pleaded guilty to or have currently pending against that person or forfeited bail or been convicted of violation of any law of any jurisdiction for prostitution, pandering, pimping, lewd conduct or sexual misconduct within five years of the application.

(7) The applicant has not had a massage establishment license or a massage therapist permit or other similar license or permit denied or revoked for cause by this city or any other city located in or out of this state within the two years prior to the date of the application.

(8) The applicant if an individual, or any of the officers and directors if the applicant is a

corporation, or any of the partners, including limited partners, if the applicant is a partnership, is at least 18 years of age.

(9) The applicant, if a corporation, is licensed to do business in good standing in the state.

(10) The massage establishment as proposed by the applicant would comply with the requirements of this article.

(Code 1956, § 35A-1-7(3))

laws.title: Sale or transfer
laws.content:
Upon the sale or transfer of any interest in a massage establishment, the license therefor shall be null and void. Any person desiring to continue to operate such massage establishment following sale or transfer shall make application therefor pursuant to this division.

(Code 1956, § 35A-1-12)

laws.title: Qualifications
laws.content:
Any person is qualified for licensure as a massage therapist under this division who:

(1) Is at least 18 years of age and has received a high school diploma or graduate equivalency diploma;

(2) Has submitted a sworn affidavit completed before a notary and two witnesses indicating that the applicant for a massage therapist license has completed a resident course of study of not less than 200 hours given in not less than three calendar months at a school or schools which have for their purpose the teaching of the theory, method and profession of massage therapy. Additionally, the applicant shall provide the name and address of the school or schools and such other information relating to the school or schools as may be required by the director of the department of health; and

(3) Has received a passing grade on an examination administered by the department of health.

(Code 1956, § 35A-1-8(a))

laws.title: Contents of application
laws.content:
Any person desiring a massage therapist permit shall file a written application with the department of health. The application shall be verified by the applicant. Any applicant for a massage therapist permit shall furnish all the information required by section 30-957. In addition, the applicant shall furnish the following:

(1) Certificate from a medical doctor, licensed to practice in the state, stating that the applicant has, within 30 days immediately preceding the date of application, been examined and found to be free of any contagious or communicable diseases.

(2) A diploma or certificate of graduation from a school of massage.

(3) The massage establishment, if any, at which the applicant expects to be employed.

(Code 1956, § 35A-1-8(d)(2))

plication to defray the cost of investigation and administration.

laws.title: Granting of permit
laws.content:
Within 60 days of receipt of the application, the director of the department of health shall grant a massage therapist permit only if he finds that:

(1) The applicant has passed the examination as required in section 30-982.

(2) The required fee has been paid.

(3) The application conforms in all respects to the provisions of this article.

(4) The applicant has not knowingly made a material misstatement in the application for a permit.

(5) The applicant has fully cooperated in the investigation of his application.

(6) The applicant has not been convicted of a felony or pleaded guilty to or has currently pending against that person or forfeited bail or been convicted of violation of any law of any jurisdiction for prostitution, pandering, pimping, lewd conduct or sexual misconduct within five years of the application.

(7) The applicant has furnished an acceptable medical certificate in compliance with the rules and regulations of the department of health.

(8) The applicant has furnished to the director of the department of health an acceptable diploma or certificate of graduation from a school of massage therapy.

(9) The applicant has not previously had a massage therapist permit or other similar

permit or license denied or revoked for cause by this city or by any other state within two years of the date of the application.

(10) The applicant is at least 18 years of age.

(Code 1956, $\S 35A-1-8(e), (f)$ )

State law reference—Issuance of licenses, R.S. 37:3559.

Secs. 30-987–30-1010. Reserved.

laws.title: Grounds for suspension and revocation
laws.content:
The following acts or omissions are declared to be in violation of this article and constitute grounds for suspension or revocation of a license or permit issued under this article. Prohibited acts include:

(1) Any lewd acts, sexual misconduct, sexual perversion or homosexual acts within such establishment. The following acts are in violation: Exposing, touching, caressing or fondling of genitals, anus, vulva, pubic hair or nipples of the female breast; masturbation; oral copulation, cunnilingus or fellatio; sexual intercourse, vaginal or anal; urination or defecation except in provided facilities; sodomy; bestiality; sadomasochistic abuse, flagellation or torture in the context of sexual relationship; any unnatural carnal copulation by a human being with another of the same or opposite sex.

(2) Prostitution, pandering or solicitation to perform a natural or unnatural sex act within such establishment.

(3) Making false statements in writing on the application for license issued under this article.

(4) The drinking or consuming of intoxicants or use of illegal drugs at such establishment.

*State law reference—Suspension or revocation of license, R.S. 37:3563.

(5) Allowing persons below the age of 18 years to be on the premises of a massage establishment unless the person is accompanied by his parent or legal guardian.

(6) Any act of disturbance of the peace at such establishment, defined as the performance of any of the following acts:

a. To communicate to another person a threat, either verbally, in writing or through any other form of communication, to kill or murder him or to do him great bodily harm or threatening to kill, murder or do great bodily harm to members of his family or to any other person when that person is in the immediate company of the person to whom the threat is communicated.

b. To address any words to any person who is lawfully in a public place where such words, which by their very utterance, inflict injury or have a direct tendency to cause acts of violence by the person to whom, individually, the remark is addressed.

c. To address language to any person that makes reference to the person addressed as having sexual intercourse with himself or with another where such language inflicts injury, insults or causes acts of violence by the person to whom the language is addressed or is intended to inflict injury, insult or cause acts of violence.

(7) Violation of any of the provisions of this article.

(8) The presence of a person on the massage establishment premises who administers massages and does not have a valid massage therapist permit.

(9) The practice of colon irrigation on the premises by any person who is not a medical doctor licensed to practice in the state.

(Code 1956, § 35A-1-10)

State law reference—Causes for suspension or revocation, R.S. 37:3563.

laws.title: Notice of hearing
laws.content:
(a) No license or permit issued under this article may be suspended or revoked until after due notice and hearing before the director of the department of health or his duly authorized representative to determine if grounds for such revocation exist. Notice of such hearing shall be in writing and served at least ten days prior to the date of hearing by registered mail or personal service or, in the case of a massage establishment, by posting on the interior of the massage establishment.

(b) The notice shall state the ground of the complaint against the permittee or licensee and shall designate the time and place where the hearing will be held. The licensee or permittee shall have the right to appear at such hearing and to produce evidence.

(Code 1956, § 35A-1-9)

laws.title: Discretionary action by director
laws.content:
If, after holding the hearing, the director of the department of health shall determine that the massage establishment was being operated as charged in the complaint or that the massage therapist has violated the provisions of this article, then the director shall either:

(1) Suspend the license or permit for a period not to exceed 90 days if it is charged and proved that the licensee or permittee has been guilty of violating sections 30-1011(4), 30-1011(6), or 30-1011(7); or

(2) Permanently revoke the license or permit if it is charged and proved that the licensee or permittee has been guilty of violating sections 30-1011(1), 30-1011(2), 30-1011(3), 30-1011(5), or 30-1011(8) or for any grounds that would warrant the denial of issuance of such license or permit in the first place.

(Code 1956, § 35A-1-9)

Secs. 30-1014–30-1035. Reserved.

laws.title: Compliance, public notice
laws.content:
Every massage establishment and every massage therapist shall comply with the following op-

*State law reference—Rules and regulations, R.S. 37:3555, 37:3567.

erating requirements as set out in this division. These requirements shall be prominently and publicly displayed in a conspicuous place upon every premises licensed under the provisions of this article.

(Code 1956, $\S 35A-1-6$ )

**Sec. 30-1037. Hours of operation.**

Massage establishments shall commence operations no earlier than 6:00 a.m., and the hours of operation shall extend no later than 10:00 p.m. Massage therapists shall not practice or administer massage at a massage establishment at any time outside of the hours of operation.

(Code 1956, $\S 35A-1-6(1)$ )

**Sec. 30-1038. Display of license, permit.**

Massage establishments and massage therapists therein shall prominently and publicly display on the premises their licenses and permits during all hours of operation.

(Code 1956, $\S 35A-1-6(2)$ )

**Sec. 30-1039. Business records.**

Massage establishments shall keep a record of the date and hour of each massage, the name and address of the patron receiving the massage and the name of the therapist practicing or administering the massage. Such record shall be maintained for a period of five working days and shall be open to inspection by officials charged with the enforcement of this article. Information furnished or secured as a result of such inspection by authorized officials shall be confidential.

(Code 1956, $\S 35A-1-6(3)$ )

**Sec. 30-1040. Linen supplies.**

Massage establishments shall at all times be equipped with an adequate supply of clean, sanitary towels, covering and linens. Clean towels, coverings and linens shall be stored in cabinets. Towels and linens shall not be used on more than one patron unless they have first been laundered and disinfected. Disposable coverings and towels shall not be used on more than one patron. Soiled linens and paper towels shall be deposited in approved receptacles.

(Code 1956, $\S 35A-1-6(4)$ )

**Sec. 30-1041. Sanitary maintenance of equipment, supplies.**

Instruments utilized in performing massage shall not be used on more than one patron unless they have first been disinfected, using disinfecting agents or sterilizing equipment approved by the director of the department of health. Massage table pads and reusable table coverings shall be disinfected between each massage with approved chemicals. Chemicals used during massage shall be stored separately in containers clearly labeled as to contents. All chemical containers shall be stored in cabinets reserved solely for such purpose.

(Code 1956, $\S 35A-1-6(5)$ )

**Sec. 30-1042. Attire of patrons, therapists.**

Massages shall not be given unless patrons are wearing clothing fully covering their genitals and female patrons are, in addition, wearing clothing fully covering their breasts. Where such clothing is furnished patrons by the massage establishment, it shall not be used by more than one patron unless it has first been laundered and disinfected. Massage therapists shall be fully clothed from the knee to the neck in clean, opaque, light-colored clothing.

(Code 1956, $\S 35A-1-6(6)$ )

**Sec. 30-1043. Health of patrons.**

Massages shall not be given to patrons who have open sores or other visual signs of contagion or communicable disease.

(Code 1956, $\S 35A-1-6(7)$ )

**Sec. 30-1044. Right of entry, inspections.**

For purposes of ascertaining violations of this article and conducting routine inspections, police officers, health inspectors, fire inspectors and building inspectors of the city shall have the right of entry onto the premises of any massage establishment during the hours such establishment is open for business. If health officers observe that any massage therapist has open sores or, otherwise, have reasonable grounds to believe that any massage therapist is infected with a contagious or communicable disease, they shall have the right to suspend such massage therapist from practicing or administering massage until such time

BUSINESSES

§ 30-1047

as he furnishes a doctor's certificate showing him to be free of any contagious or communicable disease.

(Code 1956, § 35A-1-6(8))

**Sec. 30-1045. Attendance by licensee.**

The owner or licensee or his duly authorized manager shall be on duty at all times during working hours in the massage establishment.

(Code 1956, § 35A-1-6(9))

**Sec. 30-1046. Proof of issuance of license, permit.**

Proof of issuance of the license required by this article for the establishment and for each massage therapist employed by the establishment shall be available for inspection on the premises of the establishment.

(Code 1956, § 35A-1-6(10))

**Sec. 30-1047. Massage establishment facilities.**

Every massage establishment shall maintain facilities meeting the following requirements:

(1) Every massage establishment shall be equipped with security deposit facilities capable of being locked by the patron. Sufficient safety deposit facilities shall be furnished so that each patron will have a separate compartment available for storage of clothing and valuables. Disposable containers shall be provided for storage of articles of clothing. Such containers are to be used only by one patron and then discarded.

(2) Each massage establishment shall have a minimum of one water closet and one handwashing facility for every 15 employees and patrons. Such handwashing facility shall be located in the same room as the water closet or immediately adjacent thereto and shall have hot and cold water supplied through a mixer faucet and be equipped with soap and towels. Bar soap is not allowed, and the use of reusable towels by more than one person is prohibited.

(3) If male and female patrons are to be served simultaneously, such massage rooms, dressing facilities, toilet facilities, steam rooms and sauna rooms as are provided shall be separate for male and female patrons; and such separate facility or room shall be clearly marked as such.

(4) Rooms in which massage is to be practiced or administered shall have at least 50 square feet of clear floor area and shall maintain lighting provided by an incandescent bulb of not less than 100 watts or a fluorescent bulb of not less than 25 watts. Lighting in colors other than white shall be prohibited. Such room shall be equipped with cabinets having doors for the storage of clean linen and chemicals. Such cabinet doors are to remain closed at all times except for removal and placement of items. Soiled linen shall be stored in approved receptacles. Each massage room is to contain two solid waste containers constructed of metal or heavy plastic, that are in good condition and provided with tightfitting covers. Each container is to be lined with a plastic liner to prevent soiling. One container is to be used to store soiled linen and towels that are reusable. The other container is for the storage of used single use items that are to be discarded. Such rooms shall contain a door incapable of being locked from the exterior or interior. Such door shall contain a transparent windowpane no less than 12 inches wide and 12 inches long such that an unobstructed view of the room is provided from a hallway or other common access area which is immediately adjacent to the room.

(5) No stuffed or upholstered furniture or beds and mattresses shall be permitted in rooms in which massage is to be practiced or administered. Such room shall be equipped with massage tables having a hard surface impervious to liquids with a width of no more than three feet and a length of no more than

eight feet. The surface of such tables shall be positioned at least two feet from the surface of the floor so as to allow for free access to the floor beneath. Such tables may be equipped with either non-disposable pads or coverings or disposable coverings not more than $2\frac{1}{2}$ inches thick. Nondisposable pads or coverings shall be removable, impervious and cleanable and maintained in a clean condition and good repair.

(6) Each massage establishment shall maintain handwashing facilities inside the establishment and within 20 feet of the massage table as measured along passageways. Such handwashing facilities shall have hot and cold running water provided through a mixer faucet and soap and towels available. Bar soap is not allowed, and the use of reusable towels by more than one person is prohibited.

(7) All walls, floors and ceilings shall be maintained in a clean condition and good repair.

laws.title: Definitions
laws.content:
For the purposes of this article, the following terms shall have the following meanings:

*Annual operating license* shall mean the license required by the City of New Orleans to authorize the operation of a nursing home within the corporate boundaries of the City of New Orleans.

*Critical facility system(s)* shall mean medical life support systems, any heating, ventilation,

*Editor’s note—M.C.S., Ord. No. 28150, § 1, adopted July 25, 2019, amended Art. XIII in its entirety to read as herein set out. Former Art. XIII, §§ 30-1081—30-1089, pertained to similar subject matter, and derived from Code 1956, §§ 41-1—41-9.*

*State law references—Rules and regulations; nursing homes, R.S. 40:2009.1 et seq.*

and/or air-conditioning equipment in patient rooms or care areas, elevator service, illumination of means of egress, alarms and alerting systems, communications systems, sufficient lighting to provide illumination to exit ways from dining and recreation areas, and task illumination in the generator set location.

*Nursing home* shall mean a private home, institution, building, residence or other place, serving two or more persons who are not related by blood or marriage to the operator, whether operated for profit or not, and including those places operated by a political subdivision of the State of Louisiana, which undertakes, through its ownership or management, to provide maintenance, personal care, or nursing for persons who, by reason of illness or physical infirmity or age, are unable to properly care for themselves. The term does not include the following:

(1) A home, institution, or other place operated by the federal government or agency thereof, or by the State of Louisiana.

(2) A hospital, sanitarium or other institution whose principal activity or business is the care and treatment of persons suffering from tuberculosis or from mental diseases.

(3) A hospital, sanitarium or other medical institution whose principal activity or business is the diagnosis, care and treatment of human illness through the maintenance and operation of organized facilities therefor.

(4) Any municipal, parish or private child welfare agency, maternity hospital or lying-in home required by law to be licensed by some other department or agency.

(5) Any sanitarium or institution conducted by and for Christian Scientists who rely on the practice of Christian Science for treatment and healing.

(6) Any nonprofit congregate housing program which promotes independent living by providing assistance with daily living activities such as cooking, eating, dressing, getting out of bed, and the like to

§ 30-1085

persons living in a shared group environment who do not require the medical supervision and nursing assistance provided by nursing homes. No congregate housing program, except those licensed or operated by the State of Louisiana, shall: (1) use the term "nursing home" or any other term implying that it is a licensed health care facility; or (2) administer medications or otherwise provide any other nursing or medical service.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 28150, § 1, 7-25-19)

**Sec. 30-1082. Nursing home license required.**

(a) It shall be unlawful to engage in the operation of a nursing home in the City of New Orleans without having first obtained from the director of safety and permits an annual operating license authorizing such activity.

(1) The director is authorized to promulgate such rules as may be required to carry out the purpose and intent of this article.

(b) Licenses shall be issued on an annual basis, and shall expire on May 31. Renewal shall be completed prior to June 1.

(c) Annual operating licenses are non-transferrable and may not be assigned or granted to any other person or business which may occupy the premises to which a license has been previously approved.

(d) An annual operating license is a privilege, not a right, and may be revoked, suspended, or not renewed based on non-compliance with the requirements of the comprehensive zoning ordinance or the requirements of this article.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 28150, § 1, 7-25-19)

**Sec. 30-1083. Application for license.**

(a) Any person desiring to operate a nursing home shall file an application for license with the department of safety and permits.

(b) The application shall be in a form prescribed by the department and, together with such other information as the department shall require, shall provide:

(1) The name and address of the applicant.

a. If the applicant is a partnership, association, or corporation, the application shall state the names and addresses of all the partners or officers, as the case may be.

(2) The name of the person managing the daily operations of such facility.

(3) The location of the nursing home.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 28150, § 1, 7-25-19)

**Sec. 30-1084. Issuance of annual operating license.**

When satisfied that the applicant for a nursing home annual operating license has met all requirements of this article, the comprehensive zoning ordinance, and any regulations regarding preparing for and operating during an emergency which may be established, the director of the department of safety and permits shall approve and issue the license.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 28150, § 1, 7-25-19)

**Sec. 30-1085. Inspections.**

The director of the department of safety and permits may inspect any nursing home that is required to have a license under this article. The director of the department of safety and permits, or his duly authorized representatives, shall have free and full access to the grounds, premises, and building used as a nursing home to ensure compliance with the standards of this article, the Code, and the Comprehensive Zoning Ordinance of the City of New Orleans, and any regulations which may be established. All persons connected with any such facility as officers or employees charged with the management thereof shall cooperate with any inspection or investigation of the director in the administration of this article.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 28150, § 1, 7-25-19)

laws.title: Fees
laws.content:
(a) Fees shall be assessed in accordance with the following fee schedule:

(1) Annual operating license application fee: $250.00.

(2) Delinquency fee for failure to renew by June 1: $50.00/month.

(b) All fees collected under this article shall be deposited into the general fund of the city. (M.C.S., Ord. No. 28150, § 1, 7-25-19)

laws.title: Minimum standards for nursing homes
laws.content:
(a) All nursing homes shall comply with the standards of the Louisiana Administrative Code applicable to their specific occupancy classification or grouping in addition to the provisions of this article. Failure to maintain compliance with the Louisiana Administrative Code shall be considered a violation of this article.

(b) All nursing homes shall:

(1) Comply with the Fire Code of New Orleans as determined by the New Orleans Fire Department and confirmed by annual facility inspections.

(2) Provide sufficient generator capacity and fuel reserve to ensure that nursing homes sustain critical facility systems for not less than 96 hours in the event of the loss of electrical power. Generator capacity shall be adequate to maintain an ambient indoor air temperature of 81 degrees Fahrenheit or less in the warmest weather and 71 in the coldest weather in all patient areas for the duration of the 96-hour backup period.

(3) Demonstrate compliance with the requirements of this article prior to issuance of the annual operating license, including a quarterly testing report verifying functional condition and capacity of the required generator(s).

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 28150, § 1, 7-25-19)

laws.title: Facilities required to coordinate with the city for emergency planning
laws.content:
(a) All nursing homes operating in the city shall provide to the mayor's office of homeland security and emergency preparedness an emergency operations and evacuation plan, to be updated on an annual basis.

(1) The mayor's office of homeland security and emergency preparedness is authorized to promulgate regulations for content of the emergency operations and evacuation plan to adequately meet the needs of the population to be served by the facility.

(b) An annual operating license shall not be issued by the director of the department of safety and permits unless an acceptable emergency operations and evacuation plan has been filed with the mayor's office of homeland security and emergency preparedness.

(c) All nursing homes operating in the city shall provide situational updates every 24 hours to the mayor's office of homeland security and emergency preparedness during all declared emergencies or disasters.

(1) All nursing homes operating in the city shall provide immediate notification by email or phone to the mayor's office of homeland security and emergency preparedness, or authorized representative, if the facility evacuates, temporarily relocates, or temporarily ceases operation.

(2) If a nursing home requires the city's assistance to evacuate or shelter patients, the city may bill the nursing home for all incurred costs and administrative fees.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 28150, § 1, 7-25-19)

laws.title: Enforcement
laws.content:
Failure of any person, business, or entity to comply with any of the provisions of this article shall be in violation of this Code and may result in suspension or revocation of license.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 28150, § 1, 7-25-19)

**Sec. 30-1150. Bond.**

No permit shall be issued under this division until the applicant has executed, delivered and filed in the department of police a bond, with one or more good and solvent sureties in the sum of $10,000.00, conditioned for the faithful and honest conduct of such business by the applicant, which bond as to its form, manner of execution and sufficiency of security, shall be approved by the department of police.
