laws.title: Facilities required to coordinate with the city for emergency planning
laws.content:
(a) All residential facilities for seniors or persons with disabilities operating in the City of New Orleans shall provide to the department of safety and permits an emergency operations and evacuation plan, to be updated on an annual basis.

(1) The Mayor’s Office of Homeland Security and Emergency Preparedness and the New Orleans Health Department are authorized to establish additional standards for content of the emergency operations and evacuation plan to adequately meet the needs of the population to be served by the facility.

(2) The emergency operations and evacuation plan shall be posted in a conspicuous place at the residential facility. In addition, a copy of the plan shall be provided to each resident of the facility.

(b) An annual operating license shall not be issued by the director of the department of safety and permits unless an acceptable emergency operations and evacuation plan has been filed with the department of safety and permits and approved by the Mayor’s Office of Homeland Security and Emergency Preparedness and the New Orleans Health Department.

(c) All residential facilities in the city shall provide situational updates, at least every 24 hours to the Mayor’s Office of Homeland Security and Emergency Preparedness, or their designee, during all declared emergencies and disasters, unless directed by the Mayor’s Office of Homeland Security and Emergency Preparedness or the New Orleans Health Department to report situ-

ational updates on a different cadence. During a declared emergency or disaster, all residential facilities must also comply with the following:

(1) The point of contact must be on site at the residential facility and available to the city at all times, until deemed no longer necessary by the Mayor’s Office of Homeland Security and Emergency Preparedness or the New Orleans Health Department, or until the facility evacuates or temporarily relocates. The point of contact may designate an authorized representative for a 24-hour period by providing such person’s name and mobile phone number on the preceding situational update.

(2) The current point of contact and mobile phone number must be posted on site at the residential facility in a location visible to the public.

(3) All residential facilities in the city shall provide immediate notification by email or phone to the Mayor’s Office of Homeland Security and Emergency Preparedness or the New Orleans Health Department, if the facility evacuates, temporarily relocates, or temporarily ceases operation.

(4) If a residential facility requires the city’s assistance to evacuate or shelter residents or patients, the city may bill the residential facility for all incurred costs and administrative fees.  
(M.C.S., Ord. No. 28801, § 1, 10-21-21; M.C.S., Ord. No. 29908, § 1, 5-2-24)

laws.title: Inspections
laws.content:
(a) *Power to inspect.* The director of the department of health or his duly authorized representative is hereby empowered, in the administration and enforcement of this article, to make inspections of the premises of any roominghouse, boardinghouse or lodginghouse for the purpose of determining whether or not it is in compliance with this article, at any time and upon showing proper identification as a representative of the department in the following instances:

(1) Whenever a complaint is filed which gives the director of the department of health the reasonable belief that there is probable cause to believe that the premises is in violation of any of the provisions of this article.

(2) Whenever an agent or employee of the city submits a written report to the director which gives facts that there is probable cause to believe that any portion of the premises are in violation of any of the provisions of this article.

(3) Whenever the administrator believes with cause, that such inspection is necessary or desirable, or is in accordance with a legislative or administrative plan.

(b) *Cause.* Cause shall be deemed to exist if either reasonable legislative or administrative standards for conducting routine or area inspections are satisfied with respect to the particular place, structure, premises or operation; or there is reason to believe that a condition of nonconformity exists with respect to the particular place, structure, premises or operation.

(c) *Warrant for inspection.* If the owner of the premises refuses admittance thereto to the director of the department of health or his duly authorized representative for the purpose of making an inspection or examination of the premises the director or his representative may present an affidavit to any judge of the municipal court stating that he has cause to believe that an inspection of the designated premises will reveal designated violations of this article, or that the proposed search is pursuant to a reasonable legislative or administrative plan. If the proposed search is based on an affidavit alleging probable cause to believe that an inspection of the designated premises will reveal designated violations of this article, the affidavit shall identify the factual basis for any opinions the affiant may hold, or any conclusions the affiant may reach. If the proposed search is to be based on an affidavit alleging that it is pursuant to reasonable legislative or administrative plan, the affidavit shall briefly describe that plan, and describe the characteristics of the premises to be searched which bring it within the scope of that plan. Upon receiving this affidavit the judge may issue a warrant authorizing the director or his representative to search the premises. If the proposed search is based on an affidavit alleging probable cause to believe that an inspection of the designated premises will reveal designated violations of this article, the scope of the search authorized by the warrant shall be limited to a search for those designated violations. If the proposed search is based on an affidavit alleging that it is pursuant to a reasonable legislative or administrative plan, the scope of the search may encompass the entire premises, but if the plan may be complied with by a more limited search, the warrant shall limit the search so that its scope will not extend beyond what is necessary to ensure compliance with the plan.  
(Code 1956, § 29-163)

laws.title: Required
laws.content:
It shall be unlawful for any person to establish, maintain or operate a roominghouse, boardinghouse or lodginghouse without first having obtained a permit from the department of health. Permits issued under the authority of this division shall be nontransferable to any other person or location. Every roominghouse, boardinghouse or lodginghouse permit shall expire at the end of one year following its date of issuance, unless sooner suspended or revoked.

(Code 1956, § 29-156)

laws.title: Application
laws.content:
Any person desiring to establish, maintain or operate a roominghouse, boardinghouse or lodginghouse shall make application for a permit to the department of health on application forms furnished by the department. Such application shall set forth the name and residence of the applicant if an individual, and the names and residences of all members if a firm or partnership, or the president, vice-president and secretary if a company or corporation, and indicate the location of the place for which such permit is desired. Any person having a mailing address located outside of the parish shall have a designated representative or agent having a business or residence address upon whom legal documents may be served located within the parish. Such application shall also state the number of sleeping rooms, the maximum number of occupants and any other facts concerning the proposed use which the department of health may deem necessary.

(Code 1956, § 29-158)

**Sec. 30-1356. Fee.**

A fee of $200.00 shall accompany the application and if a permit is not granted, $100.00 shall be returned to the applicant.

**Sec. 30-1357. Revocation or suspension.**

Failure to comply with any of the provisions of this division shall be deemed grounds for suspension or revocation of a permit, however, no permit may be suspended or revoked until after the owner, permittee, designated agent or operator is notified and afforded a hearing before the director of the department of health. The permittee, designated agent or operator may be represented by an attorney for the purpose of this hearing.

laws.title: Regulations
laws.content:
**Sec. 30-1376. Minimum size of room, occupancy.**

Each sleeping room shall contain a minimum of 120 square feet and be limited to two occupants unless the sleeping room contains 70 square feet of floor area per occupant or bed. In no instance shall there be more than six occupants or beds per sleeping room.

(Code 1956, § 29-162(1))

**Sec. 30-1377. Sanitary facilities.**

(a) Sanitary facilities shall be provided on the basis of one per ten occupants or beds. Such sanitary facilities shall include a lavatory, bathtub or shower and a toilet all properly connected in accordance with the standards of the sewerage and water board and in working order. Sanitary facilities shall be located in rooms provided especially for that purpose. Sanitary facility rooms shall not be less than seven feet in any dimension; shall have a solid self-closing door and positive ventilation; and be supplied at all times with toilet tissue, single hand use towels and soap contained in a dispenser. Sanitary facility rooms shall contain a minimum of 50 square feet per sanitary facility combination. Additional space shall be provided on the basis of 16 square feet for a toilet, 12 square feet for a lavatory and 22 square feet for a bathtub or shower.

(b) Sanitary facilities shall be located on the same floor or not more than one story away from any of the occupants it is intended to serve. In no case shall it be necessary for an occupant of one bedroom to pass through another bedroom to reach any sanitary facilities, nor to pass through a room containing such sanitary facilities to reach a sleeping room.

(Code 1956, § 29-162(2), (3))

**Sec. 30-1378. Storage for occupants.**

Closet or locker accommodations shall be provided for each occupant for storage of personal effects. Each closet or locker shall be capable of being locked and shall measure at least 12 inches wide, 18 inches deep and 60 inches in height.

(Code 1956, § 29-162(4))

**Sec. 30-1379. Bed facilities.**

(a) Each sleeping room shall contain separate bed facilities for each unrelated occupant. A bed facility shall consist of at least a standard single-size bed frame, spring and mattress. Mattresses placed on the floor are prohibited.

(b) Beds shall be spaced at least three feet apart.

(Code 1956, § 29-162(5), (6))

**Sec. 30-1380. Common area.**

An area for the common use and enjoyment of all occupants, such as a television room, recreation room or dining hall shall be provided. Such common area shall have a minimum floor area of 120 square feet or five square feet per occupant, whichever is greater; but such common area need not exceed 300 square feet.

(Code 1956, § 29-162(7))

**Sec. 30-1381. Doors, windows, etc.**

(a) Walls, ceilings, floors, windows, fixtures and furnishings throughout the establishment shall be maintained in a clean condition at all times and shall be in good repair.

(b) All outside openings shall be screened with 18 mesh wire.

(Code 1956, § 29-162(8), (9))

**Sec. 30-1382. Lighting, ventilation.**

All rooms shall be adequately lighted and properly ventilated by natural or artificial means or both, and shall be provided with adequate heating facilities capable of maintaining 68 degrees Fahrenheit for the comfort of the occupants. All natural gas fired heaters shall be vented to the outside atmosphere.

(Code 1956, § 29-162(10))

**Sec. 30-1383. Food handling.**

All food handling, storage and preparation must be in accordance with the health, sanitation and permit code of the city and the state sanitary code. The use of common kitchens by occupants is prohibited.

(Code 1956, § 29-162(11))

**Sec. 30-1384. Linen.**

Each occupant shall be furnished with clean towels, washcloths and bed linen that is changed at least weekly, before the letting of any bed to an occupant and more frequently if necessary. Sheets must be of sufficient width and length to completely cover the mattress and be turned under the mattress so as to properly secure the sheet. The use of common towels and soap is prohibited.

(Code 1956, § 29-162(12))

**Sec. 30-1385. Garbage, solid wastes.**

Garbage shall be deposited and/or stored in conveniently located watertight containers provided with tightly fitted covers. A minimum of two containers shall be provided on each floor and each shall have a plastic inner liner that will reduce soiling of the container. The inner liner and contents shall be removed as often as necessary to prevent the creation of nuisances.

(Code 1956, § 29-162(13))

**Sec. 30-1386. Register of occupants.**

All roominghouses, boardinghouses and lodginghouses shall maintain a register of occupants which includes the occupant’s name, signature, room assignment in the facility and arrival and departure date. The register shall be retained for three years following the departure of a tenant.

(Code 1956, § 29-162(14))

**Sec. 30-1387. Other provisions.**

Every roominghouse, boardinghouse and lodginghouse shall also comply with the minimum standards set forth in sections 26-282 through 26-285, 26-287 through 26-291, 26-293, 26-294, and 26-297 through 26-303.

(Code 1956, § 29-162(15))

**ARTICLE XIX. SLAUGHTERHOUSES***

**Sec. 30-1411. Daily cleaning.**

The floors and walls or other partitions of the slaughtering pens of any abattoir or slaughterhouse shall be flushed, washed and thoroughly cleansed each day, except that in special cases, when in the opinion of the meat inspector the circumstances or necessities warrant it, such officer may grant special permits to dispense with the observance of the provisions of this section. No person shall slaughter for human food and offer for sale in this city, until previously inspected, any cattle, hogs or sheep.

**Sec. 30-1460. Obscenity laws to be provided to certain applicants.**

The department of finance shall provide a copy of R.S. 14:91.11 relative to sale, exhibition or distribution of material harmful to minors and R.S. 14:106 relative to obscenity to each applicant for a permit under this chapter to conduct live entertainment and to the owner of the premises upon which the live entertainment is proposed to be conducted.

(Code 1956, § 46-2.1)

**Sec. 30-1461. Mayoralty permits penalties and interest.**

All mayoralty permits must be obtained prior to the occasion for which it is issued. Should applicant fail to secure the permit prior to the occasion, the following penalties and interest shall apply:

(1) Mayoralty permits acquired on a regular yearly basis shall become delinquent February 1 of that year. If the regular yearly permit is not obtained by February 1 of that year, there shall be interest added to the fee at the rate of eight percent per annum from the due date until paid. In addition to the interest that may be so added, a penalty shall be imposed at the rate of 20 percent of the fee if the failure to obtain said permit is for not more than 30 days and with an additional 20 percent for each additional 30 days or fraction thereof during which the failure continues, not to exceed 60 percent of the amount of the fee.

(2) Mayoralty permits acquired on other than a regular yearly basis shall become delinquent at the start of the occasion. If the permit has not been obtained prior to the occasion, there shall be interest added to the fee at the rate of eight percent per annum from due date until paid. In addition to the interest that may be so added, a penalty shall be imposed at the rate of 50 percent of the fee.

(3) The director of the department of finance may, at his discretion, for good cause, waive, in whole or in part, any of the penalties provided in this section.

(Code 1956, § 46-15)

**Sec. 30-1462. Permits nontransferable.**

Permits issued under the authority of this chapter shall be nontransferable and nontransferable either as to individuals, location or item.

(Code 1956, § 46-3)

**Sec. 30-1463. Permits valid in the central business district.**

The permits shall not be valid in that area of the city bounded by the Mississippi River on the east, Rampart Street on the west, Esplanade Avenue on the north and Canal Street on the south; provided, however, that vendors who have continuously operated the same business within that area under the authorization of this chapter for eight or more years prior to January 1, 1972 may obtain the same number of permits to operate such businesses within that area as the vendor possessed as of January 1, 1972.

(Code 1956, § 46-1.1)

**Sec. 30-1464. Penalty.**

Persons who fail to obtain a permit or to comply with any of the other regulations contained in this chapter, shall be guilty of a misdemeanor and upon conviction thereof shall be subject to the punishment prescribed in section 1-13. A permittee so convicted shall forfeit such permit and not be entitled to a refund of the fees paid therefor.

(Code 1956, § 46-16)

laws.title: Required, scope
laws.content:
Pursuant to the requirements below, tour planners are required to obtain a tour planner license from the department of public works, which shall expire on September 30 of each year and must be renewed in the month following expiration subject to the same standards as initial issuance.

(1) **Category 1**: All parties, except CPNC holders, contracting to provide transportation services within the parish in for-hire vehicles through CPNC companies must be licensed by the department of public works as tour planners. A tour planner license does not give the licensee any right to sell sightseeing tours on a per-capita basis unless the permit holder has been granted by written contract the exclusive right to sell per capita tours to a particular convention or conference group, in which case the license holder is authorized to sell sightseeing tours on a per capita basis only to members of that group to whom the party is granted this exclusive right by contract.

(2) **Category 2**: Any person or entity marketing, selling, scheduling, arranging, or organizing tours to be conducted on the public right of way, regardless of whether such tours are conducted by employees, independent contractors, or any other person representing said person or entity, must be licensed by the department of public works as tour planners. Such person or entity is responsible for maintaining compliance with all regulations of this article. Issuance of a tour planner permit does not convey any legal authorization to obstruct pedestrian or vehicular traffic on the streets, sidewalks, banquets, or other publicly owned right-of-way. Tour planners holding a license under this category are considered a "tour company" for the purposes of this article.

(Code 1956, § 12-234; M.C.S., Ord. No. 21480, § 1, 4-1-04; M.C.S., Ord. No. 27526, § 2, 9-14-17; M.C.S., Ord. No. 28624, § 1, 3-11-21)

(4) In addition to identification of the tour guide, as proscribed in section 30-1490 and in subpart (3), above, tour companies are required to provide all tour participants with an identifiable indicator of the company from whom they have secured tour services. This identification may be in the form of a sticker, decal, wristband, or other device, subject to the review and approval of the director of the department of public works.

(5) In addition to the standards explicitly provided in this article, tour companies are required to make all reasonable effort to ensure customers, patrons, employees, independent contractors, and any other individual conducting business with the company do not damage public or private property while conducting or patronizing tours. This standard shall include placement of group identification stickers or decals on any public or private property encountered during or subsequent to a tour.

(6) Failure to maintain compliance with the standards of this section is subject to issuance of an administrative citation by the department of public works, levying of fines by administrative hearing, or the suspension or revocation of the tour planner license, pursuant to division 4 of this article.

laws.title: Enforcement
laws.content:
(a) Failure of any person to comply with any of the provisions of this article, or of the terms and conditions of any permit granted, constitutes a violation.

(b) When the department of health determines that a violation of this article, or the terms and conditions of any permit issued under this article, has occurred, it shall initiate suspension or revocation proceedings.

(c) The department of health may also impose fines and/or hearing costs in addition to the suspension and revocation procedures established in this article.

(d) The following are grounds for the suspension or revocation of the permits and/or the fining of the permittee:

(1) Illegal disposal of any of the substances delineated in section 30-1636 will automatically result in revocation of a permit.

(2) Lack of a covering for noncontainerized or open-bodied vehicles as required by section 30-1676.

(3) Failure to maintain a leak-resistant body for enclosed or containerized vehicles as required by section 30-1676.

(4) Failure to have a required manifest.

(5) Transporting any of the substances delineated in section 30-1636 in violation of state law or this article.

(6) Unsanitary conditions of vehicles.

laws.title: Types of permits
laws.content:
There shall be two types of permits issued:

(1) *Temporary permits.* Permits issued by the department of health to applicants and which allow transportation of solid waste or any other substances delineated in section 30-1636 only for a limited period while a standard permit application is being processed.

(2) *Standard permits.* Permits issued by the department of health to applicants that have successfully completed the standard permit application and inspection process and which grant permission for the transportation of solid waste or any other substances delineated in section 30-1636.

a. With capacity of three-quarter-ton capacity or less, $50.00 per vehicle;

b. Over three-quarter-ton capacity, $75.00 per vehicle.

**Sec. 30-1644. Denial, appeal.**

Any applicant who has been denied a permit under this division shall be notified in writing of such denial and the reasons therefor. Within ten days of the mailing of the notice of denial, such denied applicant may appeal the denial by submitting a written request for appeal to the director of the department of health or his designated representative. Within 30 days of the receipt of the request for appeal, a hearing on such appeal shall be held. The written decision of the director of the department of health, or his designated representative, is final unless appealed to the civil district court for the parish within 30 days of the director's or his designated representatives written decision.

(Code 1956, § 29-206(F))

**Sec. 30-1645. Suspension or revocation.**

(a) The department of health may review a permit at any time. If the department determines that the permittee has violated any provisions of this article it may initiate proceedings to fine the permittee and/or to suspend or revoke the permits issued under this division. Such hearings shall be held in accordance with chapter 6.

(b) The decision of the administrative hearing officer shall be final unless appealed to the civil district court for the parish, pursuant to section 6-40 and within 30 days of the hearing officer's order.

(Code 1956, § 29-205)

**Sec. 30-1646. Duration.**

A temporary permit shall be valid for 90 days. A standard permit shall be valid for one year from the date of issuance unless revoked. Applications for renewals shall be submitted at least 30 days prior to the date of expiration or upon request by the department of health.

(Code 1956, § 29-204(A))

**Sec. 30-1647. Transfer.**

Permits issued pursuant to this division are assigned only to the permittee and cannot be transferred, sublet, leased, or assigned to another person, without prior written approval of the department of health.

(Code 1956, § 29-204(B))

**Sec. 30-1648. Decals.**

Decals shall be issued for each vehicle represented by the permittee to be used for the transportation of solid waste and any other substances delineated in section 30-1636.

(Code 1956, § 29-204(C))

**Sec. 30-1649. Changes.**

It shall be the duty of each permittee to notify in writing the department of health of any changes in the information contained in the application for the permit issued under this division, or any information which may be relevant to the conduct of business under such permit.

(Code 1956, § 29-204(D))

laws.title: Operating Requirements

**Sec. 30-1676. Vehicle requirements.**

(a) The type and size of vehicles operated under this article shall comply with the regulations and licensing of the department of transportation and development and with other applicable local ordinances governing weight and size for the streets that must be traveled.

(b) The bodies of vehicles used to transport septic waste, solid waste, recovered materials, recyclable materials, waste tires and white goods shall be covered at all times, except during loading and unloading, in a manner that prevents rain from reaching waste, inhibits access by rodents and insects, prevents waste from spilling, leaking, falling or blowing from the vehicle, minimizes escape of odors and does not create a nuisance.

(d) The bodies of all vehicles used to transport solid waste that produces leachate shall be equipped with a collection and containment system to ensure that leachate from the waste is not discharged in violation of state regulations.

(e) The interior and exterior of the body of all vehicles regulated in this section shall be maintained in a sanitary condition.

laws.title: Definitions
laws.content:
Except as otherwise expressly provided in this article, the following terms and their variant forms shall mean the following:

*Applicant* means the individual applying for a permit who must be legally authorized to bind the producer.

*Film location* means a specific place where filming will occur.

*Film location permit* means a permit issued by the film office that authorizes filming and specified associated activities at a specified film location.

*Film office* means the division of the Mayor's Office of Cultural Economy, or its successor, or the city office otherwise in charge of reviewing and issuing permits and regulating filming in the City of New Orleans.

*Film permit* means the master permit issued by the film office that authorizes a production or individuals to film in the city pursuant to a film location permit or a small film project permit.

*Film project* means an overall endeavor that involves filming at a variety of locations within the City of New Orleans.

*Filming* means creating motion picture images, including the on-site or on-location pre- and post-production activities associated therewith.
BUSINESSES

§ 30-1705

Filming does not include activities performed as part of documenting current affairs or producing news broadcasts.

*Filming permits* means film permits, film location permits, and small film project permits.

*Neighborhood filming notification* means the notice proposed by the applicant and approved by the film office which meets the requirements of this article.

*Producer* means an individual, organization, corporation or other entity that is ultimately responsible for the filming that is the subject of the application and the permit.

*Production preparation* means on-site or on-location pre-production activities.

*Small film project permit* means a permit issued by the film office to authorize filming under certain specified conditions.

*Vieux Carré* is the area bounded by Iberville Street, North Rampart Street, Esplanade Avenue, and the Mississippi River.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 29899, § 1, 5-2-24, eff. 6-1-24)

**Sec. 30-1703. Authority of the film office.**

(a) The film office is authorized to approve the following activities for filming purposes in accordance with this article, notwithstanding any requirements contained elsewhere in this Code, and after consultation with and approval by the department of public works:

(1) The use of parking lanes;

(2) The closure of a city street or other public right-of-way;

(3) Intermittent traffic control; and

(4) Simulated gunfire or explosions.

(b) The film office is authorized to permit signage regarding temporary parking or right-of-way restrictions in accordance with this article, notwithstanding any requirements contained elsewhere in this Code or in the comprehensive zoning ordinance.

(c) All filming permits required under the provisions of this article are issued at the discretion of the film office. When determining whether to issue filming permits the film office shall prioritize the health, welfare and safety of the public but shall not consider the content of the film project. The film office may require changes to a film locations, or approve or deny alternate arrangements for parking, parking lane clearance, sidewalk or street closures, intermittent traffic control, or condor or equipment placement in order to preserve the quality of life, health, safety, or welfare of the affected community and the public at-large.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 29899, § 1, 5-2-24, eff. 6-1-24)

**Sec. 30-1704. Film permit required.**

(a) A film permit is the master permit that defines the film project plan and instructs what additional permits or permissions are required in accordance with this Code. A film permit is required to obtain any film location permit, or other permit or permission required by this article.

(b) No film project shall conduct filming or otherwise engage in film production preparation or similar business on public property without a film permit.

(c) A film permit is a regulated privilege, not a right, and can be revoked or suspended by the city in accordance with law.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 29899, § 1, 5-2-24, eff. 6-1-24)

**Sec. 30-1705. Film location permits required; other location requirements.**

(a) A film location permit is required for any filming that involves:

(1) Reserving parking on the public right-of-way;

(2) Controlling the public right-of-way;

(3) Filming in public parks or greenspaces;

(4) Filming on any other city property; or

(5) Simulating gunfire or explosions.

(b) A film location permit shall not be issued unless a film permit for the film project has been issued.

(c) A separate film location permit is required for each film location. Whether a film location is a separate film location for purposes of this section shall be determined by the film office, in accordance with its rules and regulations.

(d) A concession agreement or other legal permission may be required for the use of certain city property, as established by the film office in its rules and regulations in consultation with the department of property management.

(e) Parking meter rentals or parking space reservations as specified herein may be required in addition to a film location permit.

(f) A film location permit is a regulated privilege, not a right, and can be revoked or suspended by the city in accordance with law. (M.C.S., Ord. No. 29899, § 1, 5-2-24, eff. 6-1-24)

laws.title: Film permit application requirements
laws.content:
(a) The film permit application shall be on forms created by the film office, and shall, at a minimum, require the following information:

(1) Name, address, phone number, and email address of each of the applicant and producer.

(2) Name of studio or production company and local production office address.

(3) Title of film project and type of production.

(4) Production preparation and filming start and end dates, and wrap date.

(5) A signed attestation that each of the applicant and the producer has read, understands, and agrees to comply with the provisions of this article, including section 30-1719, and all applicable laws.

(6) A signed attestation that the producer agrees to defend, indemnify, and hold harmless the city from all actions, claims, costs, damages, and expense to which the city may be subject by reason of any injury or alleged injury to any persons and property resulting or alleged to result from any activity, condition, or event arising out of the filming.

(b) At the time of the application for, and prior to issuance of any film permit pursuant to this article, the applicant shall provide a certificate of insurance certifying commercial general liability insurance coverage. At the time of the application for, and throughout the period of validity of the film permit, the insurance coverage must be in full force and effect. Such insurance coverage shall provide liability coverage of not less than $1,000,000 per occurrence. The certificate of insurance must name the City of New Orleans as an additional insured and specifically list "the City of New Orleans and all of its agents and departments" as the certificate holder; and must show the city's address as 1300 Perdido St., New Orleans, LA 70112. The producer shall notify the film office in writing at least 30 days before coverage is substantially changed, cancelled, or not renewed.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 29899, § 1, 5-2-24, eff. 6-1-24)

[Sec. 30-1709. Reserved.]

laws.title: Film location permit application requirements
laws.content:
(a) The film location permit application shall be on forms created by the film office, and shall, at a minimum, require the following information from applicants:

(1) Number of the film permit issued per section 30-1704 for the film project that is associated with the film location permit application.

(2) Name, address, phone number, and email address of the applicant.

(3) Location that is the subject of the application, including cross streets and municipal addresses, as applicable.

(4) Start and end dates and total number of days required at this location.

(5) Whether the applicant requests the reservation of parking spaces, street or sidewalk closures, intermittent traffic control, or use of simulated gunfire or explosives, including cross streets and municipal addresses, and description of traffic control needs, as applicable.

(b) At the time of the application for, and prior to the issuance of any film location permit, the applicant shall provide the following documentation to the film office:

(1) A schematic depicting the requested parking, cleared parking lanes, sidewalk

closures, street closures, intermittent traffic control, and placement of any condors or other equipment.

(2) A copy of the proposed neighborhood notification required pursuant to section 30-1712.

(3) Any location specific checklist as required by the film office in accordance with its rules and regulations, including but not limited to, the Jackson Square Filming Checklist, if applicable.

(4) Noise variance waiver, per section 30-1715, if applicable.

Permit Effective Period Permit Application Deadline
Five or fewer days No later than four business days before the date of the first day of the permit effective period.

laws.title: Neighborhood filming notification required
laws.content:
(a) Prior to obtaining a film location permit, the applicant shall distribute a neighborhood filming notification approved in advance by the film office. Failure to distribute this notification in accordance with this section may result in revocation or suspension of the film location permit or the film permit, and other enforcement action permissible by law.

(b) The neighborhood filming notification must include the name, email address, and telephone number of the location manager(s), or similar personnel, and contact information for the film office.

(c) The producer shall ensure the neighborhood filming notification is provided to each business and residence immediately adjacent to the permitted location (e.g., the reserved parking or the closed street), and within one additional block in each direction of the permitted location at least 72 hours in advance of any production preparation at the location.

(d) The neighborhood filming notification shall be hand delivered, or secured to a door, mailbox, fence, or front porch; it shall not be placed in mailboxes.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 29899, § 1, 5-2-24, eff. 6-1-24)

laws.title: No parking signage required
laws.content:
The producer shall ensure official City of New Orleans "No Parking" signs are posted in the parking area subject to the film location permit at least 48 hours in advance of any production preparation at the location, and include the following:

(1) A statement that "Parking is restricted by Sec. 154-979 of the Code of the City of New Orleans;"

(2) The dates and times of the restricted parking per the film location permit.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 29899, § 1, 5-2-24, eff. 6-1-24)

laws.title: Signage removal
laws.content:
The producer shall ensure all signage required by this article or otherwise used in filming is removed upon the earlier of the completion of filming activities at the location or expiration of the film location permit. Any signage remaining within ten days of the expiration of the film location permit shall be deemed in violation of section 134-121 of this Code and subject to any applicable penalties.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 29899, § 1, 5-2-24, eff. 6-1-24)

Supp. No. 108

CD30:86

laws.title: Simulated gunfire and explosions
laws.content:
(a) Simulated gunfire or explosions related to filming may not take place except in accordance with an issued film location permit.

(b) Approval for simulated gunfire or explosions is granted at the discretion of the film office in accordance with its rules and regulations, and with approval of the fire department.

(c) The film office shall permit only one-quarter rounds of simulated gunfire.

(d) If the use of simulated gunfire or explosions will occur after 10:00 p.m. or before 7:00 a.m., the applicant shall obtain a noise variance waiver from the health department, in accordance with section 66-177 of this Code, prior to the issuance of a film location permit.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 29899, § 1, 5-2-24, eff. 6-1-24)

laws.title: Condors, scissor lifts, and other large equipment use
laws.content:
(a) Condors, lifts, or other large equipment may not be used in the public right-of-way except in accordance with an issued film location permit.

(b) Condors, lifts, or other large equipment used in the public right-of-way may not exceed 14 feet in width, including supporting extensions, and 80 feet in height.

(c) Use in the public right-of-way of condors, lifts, or other large equipment which exceed the foregoing dimensions may be as permitted at the discretion of the film office, provided, however that closure of the street including related fees, shall be required as part of such film location permit.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 29899, § 1, 5-2-24, eff. 6-1-24)

laws.title: Parking restrictions and requirements
laws.content:
(a) The producer shall ensure parking associated with the film project is permitted pursuant to one or more film location permits and adheres to the following provisions:

(1) Personal vehicles of crew members or production personnel, etc. are parked a minimum of three blocks from the area permitted by a film location permit, or in a lot secured for the purpose of parking these vehicles.

(2) Adjacent businesses are notified of the film project's use of loading, passenger, or taxicab zones.

(b) The film office may require, in accordance with its rules and regulations, the film location permit include one block of parking adjacent to the permitted parking area for resident vehicles. The producer shall ensure that signage reading "No Crew Parking / Resident Parking Only" is posted in these areas.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 29899, § 1, 5-2-24, eff. 6-1-24)

laws.title: Vieux Carré filming restrictions and requirements
laws.content:
(a) Vehicles and trucks larger than 36 feet in length are strictly prohibited in the Vieux Carré, except that the film office may allow larger vehicles on Esplanade Avenue, North Rampart Street, or Decatur Street provided the use is included in a film location permit.

(b) Mardi Gras or carnival floats are prohibited in the Vieux Carré, except that the film office may allow floats to be staged for filming on Esplanade Avenue, North Rampart Street, or Decatur Street included in the film location permit, provided that such floats have all inspections and fire safety certificates required under chapter 34 of this Code.

(c) The film office may issue a film location permit for a maximum of two blocks in the Vieux Carré for parking equipment or vehicles less than 36 feet in length, and two blocks of clearance for filming. If additional parking is required for a catering truck, or similar vehicle, only one additional half of a block may be permitted at the discretion of the film office.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 29899, § 1, 5-2-24, eff. 6-1-24)

laws.title: Acknowledgement in film credits
laws.content:
Permitted film projects must include an acknowledgement of the cooperation and support

of the City of New Orleans and the film office, including the official logos for both the city and the film office, in the final credits of the film.  
(M.C.S., Ord. No. 29899, § 1, 5-2-24, eff. 6-1-24)

**Sec. 30-1720. Regulations.**

Pursuant to section 2-1000 of this Code, the film office shall promulgate rules and regulations in accordance with the provisions contained in this article and such other rules and regulations as may be necessary for the purpose of implementing the provisions contained herein.  
(M.C.S., Ord. No. 29899, § 1, 5-2-24, eff. 6-1-24)

**Sec. 30-1721. City participation in programs featuring first responders.**

(a) The city shall not enter into any agreement authorizing or related to the filming or production of a motion picture, documentary, television program, reality show, or other media production that features first responders engaged in the course and scope of their official duties. For the purposes of this section, first responder means any full or part-time city employee whose duties include responding rapidly to an emergency and includes the following: peace officers, fire protection personnel, emergency medical services personnel, or an emergency response operator or services dispatcher who provides communication support services for an agency by responding to requests for assistance in emergencies. No first responder may be compelled to participate in a film or production subject to the prohibition in this section.

(b) Nothing herein shall be deemed to prohibit or restrict journalistic coverage of emergency situations or other constitutionally protected expressive activities occurring in public areas.  
(M.C.S., Ord. No. 30508, § 1, 11-6-25, eff. 1-1-26)

laws.title: Parade position, route, date and time
laws.content:
(a) Unless and except as otherwise provided in a motion adopted pursuant to paragraph (d) of this section, parade permits issued under this chapter shall be for the same position, route, date and time as the parade permit issued to the carnival organization in the previous year. Parade permits issued to a carnival organization which paraded in the previous year on a rescheduled date under section 34-23 shall be for the original position, route, date and time.

Supp. No. 114

CD34:7
§ 34-6

(b) Truck parades shall only be conducted on Mardi Gras Day.

(c) A carnival organization may request a change in a parade route or time by applying for and obtaining an authorization from the superintendent of police, who shall have sole and final discretion whether to approve the parade route and time; provided, however, that any request for a change in a parade route or time shall be submitted prior to December 15 of the calendar year immediately preceding the year in which the carnival parade is to be presented.

(d) Parade position, route, date, and start time shall be determined by city council motion.

(e) If a conflict exists as to parade position, route, date or time, the city council shall resolve the conflict by motion and may consider the rule of parade seniority, together with other pertinent factors, to determine which organization shall have the right to the contested position, route, date or time. Parade seniority is determined by the number of consecutive years that a carnival organization has paraded. If two or more parade organizations have paraded for the same number of years, seniority shall be determined by the city council. A carnival organization shall, for the purposes of determining seniority, be deemed to have paraded if the parade is cancelled for reasons beyond the control of the permit holder, such as weather, fire or national emergency.

(f) No more than three permits for a night parade shall be issued for the same date, except when a parade is rescheduled per section 34-5 or paragraph (g) of this section.

(g) The superintendent of police is authorized to adjust a carnival organization’s parade position, date, route, and start time as necessary to respond to issues of public safety or other emergent circumstances.

**ARTICLE III. GENERAL REGULATIONS FOR PARADES***

**Sec. 34-7. Commercial nature prohibited.**

(a) No parade shall be of a commercial nature or convey or contain a commercial message, corporate or commercial sign, logo or symbol, or commercial signs, identifications or decorations except as expressly provided for herein.

(b) No advertising of any kind shall be displayed or used in any parade.

(c) Notwithstanding any other provisions of this chapter, only the following vehicles may contain commercial signs or messages, only as expressly provided by this section:

(1) Property trucks, truck tractors and float tractors may identify the designer and/or builder of the floats in a parade;

(2) Convertible automobiles used to carry designated krewe officials, grand marshal, guest celebrities, maids, dukes or lieutenants may identify such persons as well as both the manufacturer of the vehicles and the donor furnishing the vehicles, provided the donor is a private individual or an entity whose principal business is the manufacture or retail sale of automobiles;

(3) News media vehicles which are actively transmitting parade progress reports to the general public during the pendency of a parade may identify their radio or television affiliation;

(4) Horse or mule drawn vehicles which have paraded in carnival parades prior to 1984 may identify only the owner or operator of such vehicles; for such vehicles, the provisions of paragraphs (a) and (b) of this section shall otherwise apply.

(d) No participants in any parade shall display in any manner in such parade any endorsement of candidates for elective public office, nor any endorsement of any issues to be voted on in an election. However, nothing contained in this

The use of the United States mails is specifically exempted from this provision.

laws.title: Parade routes generally
laws.content:
(a) *Length.* The maximum length of any carnival parade route shall not exceed seven miles, exclusive of formation and disbanding areas.

(b) *Special conditions.* The following special conditions shall apply:

(1) No parade route shall cross the Industrial Canal.

(2) No parade route shall include any of the streets bounded by Canal Street, Esplanade Avenue, Rampart Street and the Mississippi River, except that parade routes may include Canal Street and Rampart Street.

(c) *Excessive stoppage prohibited.* Carnival organizations shall be limited to no more than three stops along the designated parade route for a ceremonial toast, including but not limited to stops for ceremonial toasts with public officials or other dignitaries. The three floats conducting the ceremonial toast and the location of the toast must be provided to the department of police pursuant to section 34-3.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 19,314, § 1, 7-15-99; M.C.S., Ord. No. 25813, § 6, 4-14-14; M.C.S., Ord. No. 29637, § 1, 9-7-23)

laws.title: Failure to start on time
laws.content:
The failure of any float provider and/or parading organization to commence the float or truck parade within 30 minutes of the scheduled starting time shall subject the float or truck parade to cancellation and/or subject the float provider and/or parading organization to a $300.00 fine per violation.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 19,314, § 1, 7-15-99)

laws.title: Drivers
laws.content:
All drivers of self-propelled floats and drivers of tractors or other prime movers shall possess a current valid class "D" chauffeur's license issued by the state department of public safety. It shall be unlawful for any person to drive a self-propelled float or minifloat or drive a tractor or other prime mover pulling any float or minifloat without a current valid class "D" chauffeur's license.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 19,314, § 1, 7-15-99)

laws.title: Pre-parade parties
laws.content:
Any parading carnival organization may request permission to conduct a pre-parade party provided that such request is made in the initial application to the department of police. Proof of insurance shall include the pre-parade party. Security shall be provided at the carnival organization's cost as determined to be neces- Supp. No. 110 CD34:9 $\S 34-12$ NEW ORLEANS CODE sary by the New Orleans Police Department. Portolets shall be provided and removed within 24 hours of the party. (M.C.S., Ord. No. 19,314, § 1, 7-15-99) **Sec. 34-13. Disbanding of night parades.** Night carnival parades may not be disbanded in the area bounded by Iberville Street, North Claiborne Avenue, Esplanade Avenue and the Lake Pontchartrain side of North Rampart Street unless the organization sponsoring the parade is having a ball at the Morris FX Jeff Auditorium on the same date of the parade. Basin Street between Canal Street and St. Louis Street shall be exempt from the provisions of this section. (M.C.S., Ord. No. 19,314, § 1, 7-15-99) **Sec. 34-14. Float parades.** All float parades conducted during carnival parade season shall be subject to the following additional requirements: (1) Each parade shall consist of no less than 14 and no more than 45 pull units. Each pull unit shall bear a unique, sequential arabic number corresponding to the order in which the pull unit appears on the parade route, beginning with the number "1". (2) A tandem float shall be considered a single float for the purposes of this section. (3) The number of automobiles and/or mini-floats or any combination thereof shall not exceed 14 or a number equal to 75 percent of the number of floats in a parade, whichever is the greater. Each automobile shall be limited to the driver, three maskers, and one escort riding therein. (4) The number of marching bands participating in a parade shall be based on the total number of pull units in the parade, as follows:
14 to 27 pull units A minimum of seven marching bands
28 to 36 pull units A minimum of ten marching bands
37 to 45 pull units A minimum of 14 marching bands
Parades which are rescheduled because of inclement weather shall not be required to comply with the minimum number of marching bands. Any element that contains at least one person under the age of 18 shall provide a minimum of one adult chaperone per every 15 participants, regardless of age. Such adult chaperones shall also be required to have affixed to their clothes, within clear, unobstructed and plain view, while the parade is in progress, placards, badges, or similar identification associating them with the band or parade that individual is chaperoning. (5) Only members of the military band and their supervisors may participate in military bands marching or riding in carnival parades. All persons participating in military bands shall be in uniform. (6) Each Mardi Gras float that uses 120-volt fixed electrical wiring must register annually with the electrical division of the department of safety and permits and have an official annual electrical inspection sticker. (7) The annual fee for an inspection sticker is $10.00 per float. For purposes of this section only, tandem floats are considered one float. (8) The annual registration fee is $ 40.00 per carnival organization. (9) Inspection stickers will be issued after a licensed electrician has completed an official inspection form which states that the relevant floats have been examined by the electrician who certifies that the electrical systems conform to the requirements of this section. (10) The inspection sticker must be installed on the tongue of the float and must be visible for inspection. Supp. No. 110 CD34:10 CARNIVAL, MARDI GRAS § 34-15 (11) The fire department will inspect each float for the presence of the electrical inspection sticker during the formation area inspection immediately prior to the start of the parade. Any float that does not have a valid sticker will be withdrawn from the parade. (12) Every float and minifloat must conform to the following electrical requirements: (a) All wiring must be over-current protected with circuit breakers meeting the minimum requirements of NFPA 70, Article 240: National Electrical Code. Example: 15-amp circuit breakers for 14-gauge wiring or 20-amp circuit breakers for 12-gauge wiring. (b) The electrical distribution panel must be located in an accessible location. (c) All electrical connections must utilize wire nuts or insulated butt splices. (d) All electrical connections must be housed within covered junction boxes, except for butt splices. (e) All staples used to secure wiring must have nonmetallic insulation. (f) All electrical work must be inspected by and signed off by an Orleans Parish class A licensed electrician. (g) A manual shutoff device for the generator must be within ten feet of the tractor driver or conspicuously marked for easy identification. (h) All pin socket light fixtures must be installed using the correct polarity. (i) Any float which uses electrical energy for anything other than lighting, i.e. disc jockey, musical equipment, animation etc., shall provide a minimum of one 20-amp circuit which may be placed anywhere on the float. Each circuit may have no more than two weatherproof duplex receptacles or one weatherproof quad receptacle. Extension cords shall not be used. The float shall also have a current inspection sticker for this year's parade on the tongue of the float. (13) Each float shall be pulled by either a tractor or traditional equine team. (14) Each parade shall consist of no more than 12 elements before the first float and no more than one element between each float. (M.C.S., Ord. No. 19,314, § 1, 7-15-99; Ord. No. 29637, § 1, 9-7-23)

laws.title: Truck parades
laws.content:
All truck parades shall be subject to the following additional requirements:

(1) No truck shall be more than 13 feet, six inches high, from ground at highest spot, nor wider than ten feet. No truck shall be longer than 70 feet.

(2) No truck shall be more than 13 feet, six inches high, from ground at highest spot, nor wider than ten feet. Each truck shall be equipped with such safety equipment as required by state law.

(3) They shall follow a route to be prescribed by the superintendent of police, which shall include a requirement that they proceed as directed by him and disband in the area or vicinity designated.

(4) The interval between each truck shall be not less than 30 feet. No unauthorized vehicle shall be allowed to parade between the trucks.

(5) The maximum number of trucks which may participate in the parade sponsored by the Elks Krewe of Orleanians shall be not more than 120 trucks. The maximum number of trucks which may participate in the parade sponsored by the Truck Parade of Crescent City shall not be more than 60 trucks.

Supp. No. 110

CD34:11
§ 34-15

NEW ORLEANS CODE

(6) Effective January 1, 2016, no generators will be allowed on truck floats. All electrical needs will be supplied by the use of extension cords connected to the power inverter in the cab pulling the truck float. Every truck float that uses extension cords to provide electrical service must meet the requirements of Chapter 6, sections 605.5, 605.6 and 605.9 of the International Fire Code.

(7) Every truck float that uses permanent branch circuit wiring for 120-volt or 240-volt electrical source must comply with section 34-14 of this chapter.

(8) All truck floats shall have sides or skirts built down on 12 inches from the street. Truck floats shall have attached fringe to block any view under the truck float.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 19,314, § 1, 7-15-99; M.C.S., Ord. No. 21578, § 1, 6-3-04; M.C.S., Ord. No. 25813, § 8, 4-14-14; M.C.S., Ord. No. 25988, § 4, 8-14-14)

laws.title: Mandatory video documentation of parades
laws.content:
The city shall document the entirety of each permitted carnival parade by video and be responsible for custody of the recording. A copy of the recording shall be provided to the mayor’s Mardi Gras advisory council upon its request.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 25813, § 9, 4-14-14)

laws.title: Age of parade participants
laws.content:
(a) The minimum age of persons participating in any carnival parade made up of floats and/or vehicles, whether as riders of floats or members of bands or marching units, or otherwise, shall be 12 years. This restriction shall not apply to pages, attendants, grand marshals, or special guest celebrities riding floats or vehicles therein or to persons participating in truck parades.

(b) Persons employed as operators of animation on floats shall be at least 15 years of age and shall have the necessary work permits required by law.

(c) Persons employed or engaged to carry a liquid fuel flambeaux or compressed gas flambeaux shall be at least 18 years of age. Government approved identification will be required.

(d) The minimum age of persons participating in truck parades shall be three years.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 19,314, § 1, 7-15-99; M.C.S., Ord. No. 25988, § 5, 8-14-14)

laws.title: Riders
laws.content:
No person shall ride on the exterior of an automobile during a parade, except that one person may ride on the back of a convertible automobile.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 19,314, § 1, 7-15-99; M.C.S., Ord. No. 25661, § 1, 1-23-14)

laws.title: Smoking prohibited
laws.content:
It shall be unlawful for any person to smoke while participating in a carnival parade or truck parade. A "no smoking" sign shall be securely attached and plainly visible to all occupants of a float, minifloat or tandem float.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 19,314, § 1, 7-15-99)

Cross reference—Fire prevention and protection, ch. 74.

laws.title: Obstructing parades
laws.content:
(a) During and two hours prior or subsequent to the publicized start of a passage of any parade of the carnival krewes, organizations and/or societies of the city and on Mardi Gras Day between the hours of 7:00 a.m. and 10:00 p.m., it shall be unlawful for any person in control or charge of a horse or vehicle, including a motor vehicle:

(1) To park, loiter or stop on or upon any street, roadway or boulevard of the parade route, on the line of route from sidewalk curb to sidewalk curb;

(2) To park, loiter or stop on or upon the sidewalk of any street, roadway or boulevard of the parade route, or on or upon the neutral ground of any boulevard of the parade route; or

Supp. No. 110

CARNIVAL, MARDI GRAS

§ 34-22.1

(3) To obstruct the passage of traffic on any intersecting or adjacent street to the parade route.

(b) Where the offending vehicle is unoccupied, the police are authorized to have the vehicle towed. The provisions of this section shall not apply to authorized emergency vehicles; to horses ridden by the police department; to mass transit vehicles; to vehicles used by public utilities for any necessary installation, maintenance or repair of public utility facilities or to any vehicle or horse forming a part of the parade authorized by its permit.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 19,314, § 1, 7-15-99)

laws.title: Obstructing sanitation
laws.content:
After the passage of parades of carnival societies of the city during the Mardi Gras season, it shall be unlawful for any person in charge of a vehicle, horse, or vending contrivance to personally park, stop or loiter in such a manner as to obstruct the passage of movement of sanitation vehicles or street sweepers of the city on the line of route from curb to curb.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 19,314, § 1, 7-15-99)

laws.title: Animals prohibited
laws.content:
Horses not participating in a carnival parade and all reptiles are prohibited within 200 yards of a carnival parade route during a carnival parade or the pendency of a parade. This section shall not apply to any animal used by a law enforcement agency.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 19,314, § 1, 7-15-99; M.C.S., Ord. No. 30002, § 1, 7-25-24)

laws.title: Southern Decadence Festival; Bourbon Street; use of amplification equipment
laws.content:
(a) Beginning on the Wednesday of or prior to the Southern Decadence Festival, until Monday, the last day of the Southern Decadence Festival,

on Bourbon Street, between Iberville Street and Esplanade Avenue, it shall be unlawful to operate or allow the operation, for personal use, of any personal sound-amplification equipment, megaphones, bullhorns or any device or apparatus for the reproduction or amplification of the human voice or other sounds (hereinafter collectively referred to as "sound-amplification equipment"), in the public right-of-way, including streets or sidewalks, producing sounds registering more than 85 db(A).

(b) The limitations on the operation of sound amplification equipment in subsection (a) of this section shall not apply to the operation of horns, sirens, or other emergency warning devices actually being used in emergency circumstance.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 21676, § 1, 9-9-04; M.C.S., Ord. No. 23668, § 1, 8-6-09)

laws.title: Physical requirements
laws.content:
(a) Any float which is greater than 130 feet in length, including pull unit and generator, shall obtain prior, written approval by the New Orleans Police Department, Department of Public Works, and Safety and Permits to ensure maneuverability on the parade route, except floats that paraded in the prior carnival parade season without causing delays shall not be subject to this inspection.

(b) All floats and minifloats shall be in theme, color, design and overall composition in accord with the traditional manner in which Mardi Gras or carnival floats have been in the past.

(c) Should a casualty or accident destroy or damage a nonstructural, decorative portion of any float or floats within such period of time before a parade such that repair or replacement by the exercise of due diligence is not feasible or practical, the float or floats, if no unsafe or unsightly condition exists, may be used in the parade for which it is scheduled.

(d) No minifloat shall carry more than nine maskers.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 19,314, § 1, 7-15-99; M.C.S., Ord. No. 25813, § 19, 4-14-14)

Supp. No. 113

CD34:14

laws.title: Safety precautions
laws.content:
In all parades there shall be:

(1) *Fire extinguishers.* Each float, each section of a tandem float, and each deck of a multideck float shall have at least one dry chemical powder extinguisher with a minimum of a 4A-40BC rating or at least two dry chemical powder extinguishers with a minimum of a 2A-10BC rating. Fire extinguishers shall be securely mounted and readily accessible. Fire extinguishers may be mounted on either the tractor or the float; however, they must be situated so that the distance between the fire extinguisher and the tractor driver and all riders is no greater than 50 feet from a 4A-40BC extinguisher, or 30 feet from a 2A-10BC extinguisher.

(2) *Exits.* Each float, or section of a tandem float, shall have two methods of safely entering or exiting each level of each float. The two methods may include ladders, rope ladders, built in stairs or any combination thereof. For double-decker (two-level floats), each float shall have two methods of safely entering or exiting each level of each float. The two methods may include ladders, rope ladders, built in stairs or any combination thereof. Minifloats which have main platforms three feet or less above the ground shall be exempt from this requirement.

(3) *Safety chains.* There shall be a sufficient number of safety chains of adequate
CARNIVAL, MARDI GRAS

§ 34-24

tensile strength on all tractor hitches which shall be firmly attached to the float.

(4) Safety positioning devices.

a. All float riders and truck parade riders, ages six to 12 years old shall be equipped with a safety positioning device which consists of the following components:

i. Nylon safety belt or harness with a minimum width of one and three-quarter’s inches seat-belt grade flat webbing material.

ii. Nylon tether rope with a minimum diameter of one-quarter-inch and of enough length to restrict a rider’s fall over the side of a float to no more than two feet.

iii. Anchor point eye bolts, steel welded O rings, steel safety hook with Grommets, or any other similar devices shall be metal with a corrosion-resistant finish.

iv. Minimum diameter of anchor point eye bolts will be three-eighths of an inch and will be threaded to use nuts and washers.

v. Minimum diameter of steel welded O rings will be 6 mm and two inches round.

vi. Minimum diameter of the steel safety hook with grommets will be 10 mm or three-eighths inches.

vii. The anchor point eye bolt shall be securely fastened to the body or framework of the float.

b. Any safety positioning device utilized by riders must be submitted to the NOFD for approval a minimum of 30 days prior to the date of the parade. In addition to any other penalties specified in this chapter,

violations of this section shall subject the offending float rider to removal from the float.

(5) Animated float. Operators of animation shall be provided solid platforms, not below rider level, upon which to operate, together with a means of exhausting the air therefrom and such other safety requirements as may be necessary.

(6) Self-propelled floats. Self-propelled floats shall comply with state brake test provisions for an equivalent class and weight of motor vehicles and shall each have affixed thereto a current motor vehicle inspection certificate issued by the state. Self-propelled floats shall contain double the amount of fire extinguishers as provided for in subsection (1) of this section. Additionally, self-propelled floats shall comply with such safety standards and criteria established for that class of floats that may be developed and promulgated by the city. Each self-propelled float shall also have the means of being towed in case of breakdown. Each such self-propelled float shall be designed to allow the driver thereof peripheral vision of at least 180 degrees.

(7) Tandem floats. The ends and corners of each unit of a tandem float immediately adjacent to the connecting hitch shall be completely enclosed. The skin, barrier, or other enclosure shall completely enclose the area immediately adjacent to the connecting hitch from the bottom of the float up to the handrail height for riders occupying the lower level of the float.

(8) Generators. All electrical generators utilized to provide power for floats shall be mounted on the tractor. Generators utilized to provide power for truck floats may be mounted on the truck float provided that there is adequate ventilation and sufficient separation of the generator from the riders. Effective January 1, 2016, generators shall not be allowed to provide electrical power to truck floats. Truck floats shall use power

Supp. No. 110

CD34:15
§ 34-24

NEW ORLEANS CODE

inverters provided by the cab pulling the truck float. There shall be no refilling generators for floats or truck floats once the parade has started.

(9) Flambeaux. All flambeaux are subject to the following requirements:

a. Equipment. Parade lighting may be provided or supplemented with flambeaux carried along the route. The carrying of highway flares, railway fuses, night marine distress signal flares, or similar lighting devices in a parade is prohibited.

b. Fuels. Flambeaux fuel may be either a Class II combustible liquid or a compressible gas such as propane or butane. Class I flammable liquids having a flashpoint below 100°F, such as gasoline or alcohol based fuels, shall be prohibited

c. Flambeaux which use liquid fuel. Flambeaux of the traditional old-line "vapor burner" type, utilizing liquid fuel shall be permitted with the following stipulations:

i. All liquid fueled flambeaux shall be fueled by Class II combustible liquids having a flash point at or above 100 degrees Fahrenheit, such as kerosene (fuel oil) or mineral spirits.

ii. Class I flammable liquids having a flash point below 100 degrees Fahrenheit, such as gasoline or alcohol based fuels, shall be prohibited.

iii. Each liquid-fuel flambeaux shall be comprised of a single non-pressurized fuel can which is vented at the top and has a maximum capacity of approximately two gallons, no more than four burners and a carrying stick.

iv. A reflector of sheet metal or other suitable material may be attached near the burners.

v. Each burner shall be a vapor burner suitable for use in open air.

vi. Each burner shall be connected to an appropriate wick tube. The wick tube shall be a pipe made of iron, steel, stainless steel, copper, or other suitable flame-resistant heat-conducting material.

vii. The wick tube(s) shall be connected to the fuel can with black iron pipe or galvanized iron pipe or other suitable piping and appropriate elbow and tee fittings.

viii. The fuel can, shall be mounted on a vertical length of pipe of sufficient height so that gravity will cause adequate fuel pressure to be supplied to the wick tubes. Such vertical length of pipe shall incorporate a hand-operated fuel shutoff valve which can be opened and closed with a wrench or an attached handle. Any flambeaux constructed or fabricated at any time after December 1, 2013, shall use a fuel shutoff valve that can be operated using only the hand and would not require a wrench or tool to turn the valve. In operation, the burner/wick-tube system shall cause a Class II combustible liquid fuel to generate fuel vapor which is then mixed with ambient air for ignition.

d. Flambeaux which use compressible gas fuel. Flambeaux utilizing compressed propane gas, butane, or the like fuel shall be permitted with the following stipulations:

i. A backpack support for the user, operator or carrier shall be provided to hold the gas containment tank and first regulator stage components.

Supp. No. 110

CD34:16
CARNIVAL, MARDI GRAS

§ 34-24

ii. A torch frame carrying a single or multiple numbers of burners is connected to the tank by means of a quick disconnect hose.

iii. The torch frame is designed such that an internal passageway is formed by the hollow, closed ended, tubular members that make up the torch frame.

iv. A hand manipulated, quick release kill switch is in place which must be held down by the operator to allow the gas to continuously flow to the burners during use. (welding, taping, rigging, or other means to circumvent the kill switch is prohibited)

v. The burner chambers are formed by concentric cylindrical members.

e. Flambeaux fueling operations.

i. Flambeaux fueling may only take place prior to or at the formation area. No refueling will be allowed along the parade route.

ii. At the parade disbanding location, all flambeaux shall be extinguished under the supervision of the flambeaux contractor.

f. Placement of flambeaux. No flambeaux shall be within 15 feet of the front, back, and/or sides of a float, parade element or parade participant not involved in the carrying or supervision of flambeaux. Flambeaux shall not be placed or flanked along the sides of a float or parade element, except for king’s, queen’s, duke’s, or maid’s floats with a maximum of five riders aboard such float, having no throws aboard the float, which are preceded by crowd chaperones on each side of the float who will carry rope to create a barrier between the flambeaux and the parade spectators, and keep the flambeaux at least three feet from the side of such floats and the flambeaux are facing forward and with the reflector to the rear, and which have a fire watch in close proximity for immediate response.

g. Group supervision.

i. Each flambeaux group shall be composed of one stick man for every 15 flambeaux carriers.

ii. Stick man duties include ensuring that the flambeaux safety guidelines are being adhered to.

h. Safety briefing. A safety briefing shall be conducted prior to each parade by the NOFD Flambeaux Detail Officer with mandatory participation from the krewe’s parade marshall or his/her designee, the flambeaux contractor and all stick men. All flambeaux safety guidelines established in this chapter will be reviewed at such safety briefing.

i. Flambeaux carrier behavior.

i. Flambeaux carriers shall carry flambeaux in manner that prevents flambeaux from coming in contact with floats or parade elements, parade participants not involved in the carrying or supervision of flambeaux, parade spectators, trees/vegetation, and any public utility elements.

ii. All flambeaux carriers shall carry their flambeaux in a safe manner, utilizing a pole belt or harness, back support, or similar device to distribute the weight of the flambeaux to provide a stable means of carrying the flambeaux for the

Supp. No. 110

CD34:17
§ 34-24

NEW ORLEANS CODE

duration of the parade route. Spinning, dipping of the flambeaux or any other activity which may cause the fuel to spill is prohibited.

iii. Flambeaux carriers shall not exit the designated parade route with active (lit) flambeaux unless so directed by NOPD, NOFD, or parade official.

j. Enforcement. Any flambeaux carrier who fails to comply with the requirements set forth in the flambeaux safety guidelines, and/or any other applicable law shall be removed from the parade. The resulting unmanned flambeaux shall be extinguished by the flambeaux contractor and placed in the parade property truck for the rest of the parade.

(10) Safety seats.

a. All truck parade riders, age three to five years old, shall be placed in safety seats according to the following specifications:

i. Seats shall be made of wood. The height of the safety seat shall be adjusted for each child so that the top of the side railing of the truck is no lower than the child’s underarms.

ii. The safety seat shall include safety belts that attach across the waist and through the legs of the child placed in the seat.

iii. The safety seat shall be bolted into the floor of the truck.

iv. Three to five year olds shall be seated and strapped in safety seats whenever the truck is in motion.

b. Any safety seat utilized by riders must be submitted to NOFD for approval a minimum of 30 days prior to the date of the parade.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 19,314, § 1, 7-15-99; Ord. No. 19,908, § 1, 11-16-00; M.C.S., Ord. No. 25988, § 6, 8-14-14; M.C.S., Ord. No. 28789, § 1, 9-23-21)
