laws.title: Inspections generally
laws.content:
Timing, issues and city agency responsibilities. Representatives of the fire and/or police department shall inspect each parade for which a permit has been issued to see that the provisions of this chapter have been complied with. The inspection shall take place immediately prior to the beginning of the parade of the particular organization being inspected and shall be recorded on a float inspection report. If any violation of the provisions of this chapter are found during these inspections, the particular float, minifloat, piece of equipment or other apparatus shall be immediately removed from the parade. Additionally, if at any time during the parade the fire department or police department determines that the physical or safety requirements of this chapter are not being complied with, the particular float, minifloat, piece of equipment or other apparatus may be immediately removed from the parade.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 19,314, § 1, 7-15-99)

laws.title: Consultation with department of safety and permits
laws.content:
If, at any time during the inspection or thereafter, a question arises as to whether a particular float, minifloat, piece of equipment or other apparatus is structurally sound, the police and/or fire department may consult the department of safety and permits or its designated agent. If the department of safety and permits or its designated agent determines that a particular float, minifloat, piece of equipment or other apparatus is not structurally sound, the particular float, minifloat, piece of equipment or other apparatus may be immediately removed from the parade by the police department.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 19,314, § 1, 7-15-99)

laws.title: Throwers restricted
laws.content:
(a) Riders or maskers are prohibited from tossing throws or favors to the rear and/or front of their floats or trucks and in the parade formation and disbanding areas.
CARNIVAL, MARDI GRAS

§ 34-28

(b) No parade participant other than the members or float riders in the parade of the carnival organization and its special guest celebrities shall toss or hand out throws during the parade without first obtaining written permission and approval of throws from the organization.

(c) No member in a marching unit nor persons riding a news media vehicle shall toss, hand out, or otherwise distribute doubloons, trinkets, or other throws. In addition to any other penalties specified in this chapter, violation of this subsection shall subject the band or news media vehicle to immediate removal from the parade.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 19,314, § 1, 7-15-99)

laws.title: Prohibited throws
laws.content:
(a) No carnival parade may include nor shall any carnival parade participant, while participating in a parade on the parade route, in a parade staging area or in a parade disbanding area, possess or have in the participant’s custody or control any of the following:

(1) Any life-threatening objects or safety-threatening objects, including, but not limited to "bomb bags";

(2) Any noxious substance or any liquid intended to be poured, tossed, handed out or otherwise distributed;

(3) Any throw containing sharp points, including but not limited to plastic spears or plastic, paper or silk flowers with wire stems;

(4) Any insects, marine life, rodents, fowl or other animals, dead or alive;

(5) Any "silly string" or other such item which, when used, emits an adhesive string-like or adhesive streamer-like substance that is shot or expelled from a pressurized container; or

(6) Confetti or confetti cannons, whether mechanical or handheld.

(b) Except as provided in this subsection, no carnival parade participant may throw toilet paper, bathroom tissue, paper streamers or any other similar paper product customarily shipped and stored in a rolled condition and capable of being unrolled to a length of more than 36 inches. A member of the Krewe of Tucks may, during the Tucks parade, dispense the krewe’s traditional toilet paper throw, provided that the paper is fully biodegradable, marine grade, and made of most readily degradable form of paper commercially available. Paper cannons or any other mechanical device intended to launch or disburse paper products is strictly prohibited.

(c) No carnival parade participant shall knowingly throw any doubloon, trinket or other throw which would be redeemable for or entitle the bearer to a prize or a discount on the price of any food, beverage, merchandise, service or admission to any event or which displays, conveys or communicates any commercial, political or religious message.

(d) No carnival parade participant, while participating in a parade on the parade route, shall hand out, throw, toss, or in any way discard boxes, corrugated boxes, paper steamers or other paper products exceeding 36 inches in length regardless of whether the paper biodegrades when wet, or empty single-use plastic bags. Any package containing bulk throws, including but not limited to doubloons, beads, cups, trinkets, or toys shall be handed to parade attendees and shall not be thrown or tossed. Bulk throws shall be removed from any plastic packaging before being thrown or tossed.

(e) No carnival parade participant, while participating in a parade on the parade route, in a parade staging area, or in a parade disbanding area, shall hand out, throw, or distribute in any way, any condom or prophylactic or any sexually-oriented device. Sexually-oriented device shall include but not be limited to any paraphernalia that is designed in whole or part for specified sexual activities as defined in the comprehensive zoning ordinance.

(f) No carnival parade participant shall knowingly throw beads that contain words or images that are unrelated to the carnival organization’s parade, the parade theme, or the theme of the float on which the parade participant is riding. Beads must either be plain and unadorned or contain the carnival organization’s logo, name,

Supp. No. 110

CD34:19
§ 34-28

NEW ORLEANS CODE

or other identifying feature specific to that carnival organization. Elements may throw beads if the designs have been individually pre-approved and documented by the permitted carnival organization.

(g) Any carnival organization that allows or permits a violation of this section shall be subject to the penalties set out in section 34-49 of this chapter. Each violation shall be considered a separate incident.

(h) Any carnival parade participant who violates this section shall be subject to immediate removal from the parade in addition to the penalties set out in section 34-49 of this chapter. No. 30002, § 1, 7-25-24)

laws.title: Throwbacks
laws.content: It shall be unlawful for a person to throw any object at a float or at any participant in a carnival parade. Any person who violates this provision shall be fined $250.00 per violation. (M.C.S., Ord. No. 19,314, § 1, 7-15-99; M.C.S., Ord. No. 25661, § 2, 1-23-14)

laws.title: Stands and structures location
laws.content:
(a) Outside of central business district. No stands or structures will be erected or maintained during the carnival parade season by any individual, firm or corporation on the streets, sidewalks or neutral grounds of the city except such stands or structures as are specifically requested for use by carnival organizations that stage carnival parades and the various news media organizations. Such stands and structures may be erected only with the permission of the director of safety and permits and must be located on the carnival organization’s parade route. No more than one reviewing stand per carnival organization shall be permitted, and all reviewing stands requested by news media organizations must be approved by the office of communications. The leasing of streets, sidewalks or neutral grounds or any agreement or arrangement that is intended to permit the erection of stands or structures on the streets, sidewalks or neutral grounds of the city during the carnival parade season, except those erected by a parading carnival organization as specified above, shall be prohibited.

(b) Within central business district. The above prohibition does not apply to stands and structures erected adjacent to buildings which abut the sidewalk in the central business district area bounded by Howard and South Claiborne Avenues, Canal Street, and Convention Center Boulevard. The director of the department of safety and permits and the director of the department of public works may issue written permission and approve carnival parade stands and structures within the central business district not adjacent to buildings which abut the sidewalk, subject to these stands and structures meeting the criteria established by the city.

(c) Pre-parade parties. Any parading carnival organization may request permission to construct a stand or platform for purposes of sponsoring a pre-parade party, provided that the intention to conduct such a party was stated in their initial parade permit application to the department of police. No stand shall be constructed less than five feet from the curb of the neutral ground after securing a noise permit from the director of health, approval from the director of parkways and parks, and approval from the director of safety and permits and the department of fire.

(d) Outside of central business district. The department of property management may erect up to 12 parade stands or platforms outside of the central business district as the availability of materials permit. Fees for the erection of parade stands or platforms shall be in accordance with a fee schedule established by ordinance of the city council unless waived by ordinance of the city council.

(e) Obstructions. Except for stands or structures erected by the department of property management, no stands or structure shall obstruct the usage or access to a fire hydrant.

Supp. No. 110

CD34:20
CARNIVAL, MARDI GRAS

§ 34-33

(f) Department of public works approval. The approval of the department of public works shall be obtained before any attachment, connection, or temporary removal of any part of a city-owned street lighting standard or fixture is made.

(g) Except for the department of property management, every person or entity that erects a stand, structure, or platform shall apply for a permit from the director of safety and permits no later than 15 days before the first parade on that route. Each stand, structure, or platform erected on the public right-of-way by persons or entities other than the department of property management, shall provide for passage on the sidewalk and shall be approved by the department of public work as to size and location prior to erection.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 19,314, § 1, 7-15-99; M.C.S., Ord. No. 19,397, § 1, 10-7-99; Ord. No. 19,515, § 1, 1-6-00; M.C.S., Ord. No. 20404, § 1, 10-4-01; M.C.S., Ord. No. 28304, § 1, 1-30-20)

laws.title: News media coverage
laws.content:
Notwithstanding any provisions of this chapter to the contrary, coverage of any activities of the parade and most particularly of those activities in front of the reviewing stands by television or other news media shall not unreasonably block the view of the crowds or prevent them from seeing such activities.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 19,314, § 1, 7-15-99)

laws.title: Fencing of public property prohibited
laws.content:
It shall be unlawful for any individual, organization, or legal entity to fence, rope off, or stake out any area of public property along a parade route, including the neutral ground, except when necessary to protect plants, shrubbery, trees, and other landscaping materials with the approval of the department of parks and parkways. Each private property owner shall apply in writing for approval from the department of parks and parkways at least 30 days prior to the beginning of the Carnival parade season, and shall submit a detailed drawing of the planned protective enclosure device. Any approval issued by the department of parks and parkways shall be issued at least ten days prior to the beginning of the Carnival parade season. Any changes to the proposed protective enclosure device mandated by the department of parks and parkways shall be complied with.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 19,314, § 1, 7-15-99; M.C.S., Ord. No. 28304, § 1, 1-30-20)

laws.title: Ladders, tents, grills, personal items, and portable toilets
laws.content:
(a) Prohibited items. Upholstered furniture, including, for example, chaise lounges, and sofas or couches; scaffolding; platforms; open flames; and gas or diesel generators shall not be placed in any public space including, but not limited to, public rights-of-way, neutral grounds, sidewalks, and intersections during the carnival season.

(b) Ladders and chairs. All ladders used by parade spectators shall be structurally sound and the top cap of the ladder shall not exceed six feet in height. Ladders, chairs, and other personal effects shall be placed at least six feet back from the street curb. Additionally, the practice of fastening two or more ladders together shall be prohibited. Ladders must be free-standing and not connected, permanently or temporarily, to any other ladder or object, provided that a small seat box capable of accommodating small children may be affixed to the top of any ladder.

(c) Enclosures prohibited. Any item used to enclose a public area, including, but not limited to, tents, canopies, shelters, screens, awnings, ropes, spray paint, or any other type of barricade, is prohibited. The use of any object that obstructs foot traffic or line of sight is prohibited.

(d) Removal of items. All ladders, chairs, ice chests, and other personal items placed on the public right-of-way, including the neutral ground, four hours or more before the start of a parade, may be removed and discarded. Items left unattended on the public right-of-way upon the conclusion of the final parade for that day may be removed and discarded. Items prohibited by this section are subject to removal from the parade route at any time during the carnival season.

Supp. No. 110

CD34:21
§ 34-33

NEW ORLEANS CODE

(e) Portable toilets. Portable toilets are prohibited during the carnival season on all public rights-of-way, neutral grounds, sidewalks, and intersections within a three-block radius of a parade route, unless authorized by the department of safety and permits. A fine of $250.00 per day shall be assessed against the individual, organization, or legal entity responsible for the placement of any portable toilet in violation of this section. A fine of $250.00 per day shall be assessed against the owner of any portable toilet found to be in violation of this section.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 19,314, § 1, 7-15-99; M.C.S., Ord. No. 25661, § 3, 1-23-14; M.C.S., Ord. No. 28304, § 1, 1-30-20; M.C.S., Ord. No. 30002, § 1, 7-25-24)

laws.title: Mayoralty permits required for various callings or occasions
laws.content:
Every person who shall desire to use the public streets, sidewalks, or other public places or private places of business establishments for the conduct of any of the businesses or callings set forth in this article shall first apply to and obtain from the department of finance a permit. Such permit shall in each instance state the occasion for which it is issued and the date upon which it will expire and shall be in addition to any other tax or license to which permittee may be liable. Except as otherwise provided, annual permits expire on December 31. Such permits, however, are not valid within the central business district area bounded by the river on the east, Claiborne Avenue on the west, Esplanade Avenue on the north and Howard Avenue on the south, except as provided in section 34-45.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 19,314, § 1, 7-15-99; M.C.S., Ord. No. 21426, § 1, 2-20-04)

laws.title: Vendors in a fixed location; permit requirements and regulations
laws.content:
(a) There shall be a $1,000.00 deposit on each permit to guarantee payment of sales tax at the end of the Mardi Gras season. This deposit will be forfeited 30 days after Mardi Gras if the taxpayer has not filed his sales tax return. This provision shall not restrict the authority of the director of finance to assess and collect sales tax and use tax in accordance with section 150-441 et seq.

(b) A specific location can be assigned but not guaranteed by the city.

(c) Vendors at fixed locations on public streets may set up their vehicles during "parade time" only.

(d) When the use of fixed location would interfere with a parade along a particular route or interfere with public safety, the city shall have the option to deny the use of such location for such period of time as may be necessary.

(e) Vendors selling from fixed locations shall comply with all provisions of chapter 154 relative to traffic regulations, especially, but not exclusively with regard to distances from fire hydrants and intersections.

(f) The trailer, van and any appendant thereto from which a vendor sells shall not exceed 30 feet in length, inclusive of any auxiliary or ancillary equipment, or nine feet in width. Vendors must sell and display from a "vehicle"; no stands, card tables or the like shall be allowed on public streets, sidewalks, alleys, parks, squares, neutral grounds or rights-of-way for the sale or display of goods.

(g) All vendors selling from fixed locations shall have the mayoralty permit as provided for in section 34-35 publicly displayed at his place of business and failure to do so shall constitute a violation of this article.

(h) No Mardi Gras mayoralty permit shall be issued for vendors from fixed locations on public streets, sidewalks, alleys, parks or squares in the Vieux Carré as defined in chapter 166.

(i) All applicants for Mardi Gras mayoralty permits to sell food and/or drinks on public or private property must show proof of compliance with all regulations and requirements of the state department of health and the department of fire, fire prevention bureau, before a permit can be issued by the department of finance.

(j) Vendors selling from fixed locations shall provide containers sufficient for the storage, in a sanitary manner, of all trash, garbage, or any other refuse generated by their business activities at each authorized location during "parade time" as defined in section 34-34 of this Code. The contained refuse shall be deposited upon the curb nearest each vendor's authorized fixed location upon the departure of said vendor.

(k) Vendors selling from fixed locations shall not conduct sales from the side of his location that faces the street or on the immediate street side of his location.

(l) Every fixed location vendor utilizing a flammable gas cooking apparatus must have a permit from the fire department.

(m) Vendors in a fixed location shall be prohibited from selling silly string. For the purposes of this section, "silly string", regardless of its brand name, shall be defined as an item purchased from a vendor during Mardi Gras season and when used, emits a string-like or streamer-like substance that is shot or expelled from a pressurized container.

(n) Vendors in a fixed location shall be prohibited from selling stink bombs. For the purposes of this section, a "stink bomb", regardless of its actual brand name, shall be defined as a device purchased from a vendor during Mardi Gras season for the purpose of emitting an odorous substance when used.

Vendors in a fixed location shall be prohibited from selling snap pops. For the purposes of this section, a "snap pop," regardless of its actual brand name, shall be defined as a device purchased from a vendor during Mardi Gras season which contains high explosives.

(o) Any person or entity possessing an alcoholic beverage permit who permits or allows the sale or consumption of alcoholic beverages on the parking or driveway area of a fixed location, pursuant to section 10-404 of this Code, shall pay the following additional fees:

laws.title: Vendors not in a fixed location; permit requirements and regulations
laws.content:
(a) There shall be a $200.00 deposit on each permit to guarantee payment of sales tax at the end of the Mardi Gras season. This deposit will be forfeited 30 days after Mardi Gras, if the taxpayer has not filed the sales tax return. This provision shall not restrict the authority of the director of finance to assess and collect sales and use tax in accordance with section 150-441 et seq.

(b) All moving vendors must keep moving except when making a sale. No stands, card tables or the like, except hand-carried displays, shall be allowed on public streets, sidewalks, alleys, parks, squares, neutral grounds or rights-of-way for the sale or display of goods.

(c) For each permit issued, one Mardi Gras mayoralty badge with a corresponding number shall be purchased by the permittee from the department of finance, which badge must be publicly displayed on their person at all times and failure to do so shall constitute a violation of this chapter.

(d) Mardi Gras mayoralty permits for moving locations shall be invalid in the 100 block of Bourbon Street, Chartres Street and the 100 block of Royal Street and in the Vieux Carré as defined in chapter 166.

(e) Mardi Gras mayoralty permits for moving locations shall only be valid during "parade time" along designated "parade routes."

(f) All moving vendors shall be prohibited from selling silly string. For the purposes of this section, "silly string," regardless of its brand name, shall be defined as an item purchased from a moving vendor during Mardi Gras season and when used emits a string-like or streamer-like substance that is shot or expelled from a pressurized container.

(g) All moving vendors shall be prohibited from selling stink bombs. For the purposes of this section, a "stink bomb," regardless of its actual brand name, shall be defined as a device purchased from a moving vendor during Mardi Gras season for the purpose of emitting an odorous substance when used.

(h) All moving vendors shall be prohibited from selling snap pops. For the purposes of this section, a "snap pop," regardless of its actual

**Sec. 34-39. Mayoralty permits, penalties and interest.**

All mayoralty permits must be obtained prior to the occasion for which it is issued. Should applicant fail to secure the permit prior to the occasion, the following penalties and interest shall apply:

(1) Mayoralty permits acquired on a regular yearly basis shall become delinquent February 1 of that year. If the regular yearly permit is not obtained by February 1 of that year, there shall be interest added to the fee at the rate of eight percent per annum from the due date until paid. In addition to the interest that may be so added, a penalty shall be imposed at the rate of 20 percent of the fee if the failure to obtain such permit is for not more than 30 days and with an additional 20 percent for each additional 30 days or fraction thereof during which the failure continues, not to exceed 60 percent of the amount of the fee.

(2) Mayoralty permits acquired on other than a regular yearly basis shall become delinquent at the start of the occasion. If the permit has not been obtained prior to the occasion, there shall be interest added to the fee at the rate of eight percent per annum from due date until paid. In addition to the interest that may be so added, a penalty shall be imposed at the rate of 50 percent of the fee.

(3) The director of the department of finance may, at his discretion, for good cause, waive, in whole or in part, any of the penalties provided in this section.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 19,314, § 1, 7-15-99)

**Sec. 34-40. Rules and regulations.**

The director of finance shall prescribe such other rules and regulations as to the form of the application for permits and their issuance as may be required to carry out the full intent and purpose of this article.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 19,314, § 1, 7-15-99)

**Sec. 34-41. Fees to go to general fund.**

The collector of revenue shall transmit, day by day, as collected by him, to the bureau of the treasury all moneys and fees received for the issuance of the permits required by this chapter. The bureau of the treasury upon the receipt of such moneys and fees shall immediately deposit them in the general fund.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 19,314, § 1, 7-15-99)

**Sec. 34-42. Additional charges for police pension fund.**

In addition to the charges shown in the fee schedule for each permit, each applicant shall be required to pay the sum of $0.25 for the account of the police pension fund, which additional sum shall be transmitted by the collector of revenue, day by day, as collected by him, to the chief of bureau of the treasury. At the end of each month the chief of the bureau of the treasury shall remit all such sums so collected for account of the police pension fund to the board of trustees, police pension fund.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 19,314, § 1, 7-15-99)

**Sec. 34-43. Obscenity laws to be provided to certain applicants.**

The department of finance shall provide a copy of R.S. 14:91.11 relative to sale, exhibition or distribution of material harmful to minors and R.S. 14:106 relative to obscenity to each applicant for a permit under this chapter to conduct live entertainment and to the owner of the premises upon which the live entertainment is proposed to be conducted.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 19,314, § 1, 7-15-99)

**Sec. 34-44. Permits nontransferable.**

Permits issued under the authority of this chapter shall be nontransferable and nontransferable either as to individuals, location or item as specified in sections 34-36 through 34-38.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 19,314, § 1, 7-15-99)

**Sec. 34-45. Permits valid in the central business district.**

Permits designated in sections 34-37 and 34-38 are valid within that area of the city bounded by the Mississippi River on the east, Rampart Street on the west, Esplanade Avenue on the north and Canal Street on the south.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 19,314, § 1, 7-15-99)

**Sec. 34-46. Peddling novelties, souvenirs and foods; prohibited near schools.**

It shall be unlawful to sell novelties, souvenirs, candies, nuts, confections, ice cream, ice cream bars, hot tamales, hot dogs, sandwiches, soft drinks, cakes, pies, fruits and vegetables on the city streets within two blocks of any elementary or secondary school when such school is in session.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 19,314, § 1, 7-15-99)

**Sec. 34-47. Offense for misuse of permits.**

(a) No person, individual, or corporation shall copy, reproduce, or counterfeit, or cause to be copied, reproduced or counterfeited, any permit issued pursuant to this article by any form or process, or to otherwise represent something to be a valid permit when it is not.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 19,314, § 1, 7-15-99)

**ARTICLE VIII. ENFORCEMENT AND PENALTIES**

**Sec. 34-48. Enforcement.**

(a) The department of police, the fire department, and department of safety and permits shall issue citations for the violation of any of the provisions of this chapter.

(b) The department of police, the fire department, and the department of safety and permits shall be authorized to remove any person, element, float, or vehicle of any sort from a carnival parade if the person, element, float or vehicle is in violation of the provisions of this chapter.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 19,314, § 1, 7-15-99; M.C.S., Ord. No. 29637, § 1, 9-7-23)

**Sec. 34-49. Penalties.**

(a) Failure of any carnival organization to comply with any provisions of this chapter may subject the carnival organization to revocation of its parade permit, and/or may be punishable up to the maximum limit provided by law.

(b) If any carnival organization, its member, or any individual riding on its float, willfully violates or permits a violation of any of the provisions of this chapter, the carnival organization may be subject to a $500.00 fine per violation and to other sanctions which may be imposed by the city council, including revocation of the carnival organization’s permit for the following and subsequent years.

(c) If any individual willfully violates a provision of this chapter, the individual shall be punished by a fine of $ 500.00, such fine and/or by imprisonment as are allowable by law, or as otherwise provided in this chapter.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 19,314, § 1, 7-15-99; M.C.S., Ord. No. 25813, § 11, 4-14-14; M.C.S., Ord. No. 29637, § 1, 9-7-23)

**Sec. 34-50. Reserved.**

*Editor’s note—M.C.S., Ord. No. 29637, § 1, adopted Sept. 7, 2023, repealed § 34-50, which pertained to permit revocation and derived from M.C.S., Ord. No. 19,314, § 1, adopted July 15, 1999.*

**Sec. 34-51. Mayoralty permit violations.**

Persons who fail to obtain a permit or fail to comply with any of the other regulations contained in this chapter relative to mayoralty permits shall be punished by such fine and/or by such imprisonment as are allowable by law. A permittee so convicted shall forfeit such permit and not be entitled to a refund of the fees paid therefor.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 19,314, § 1, 7-15-99)

laws.title: Permission required for establishment
laws.content:
There shall not be established within the city any cemetery or depository of the dead without the approval of a conditional use by the city council in accordance with the comprehensive zoning ordinance having first been obtained.  
(Code 1956, § 13-1)

laws.title: Regulations for use of cemeteries not owned by city
laws.content:
The various churches and associations owning cemeteries may use them under such regulations made by them from time to time as may not conflict with city ordinances and state laws.  
(Code 1956, § 13-2)

laws.title: No person to be buried except in public cemetery
laws.content:
It shall be unlawful for any person to bury any human body within the limits of the city anywhere outside of a duly authorized public, private, religious or fraternal cemetery.  
(Code 1956, § 13-3)

laws.title: State laws—Compliance
laws.content:
The keepers of the several cemeteries in the city shall, before receiving for interment within their respective cemeteries any body of any deceased person, see that the requirements imposed by the existing laws of the state have been complied with.  
(Code 1956, § 13-4)

laws.title: Same—Exceptions
laws.content:
From the effect of section 38-4 is excepted the body of any person who shall have died in the charity or marine hospital or in the army or navy or who shall be ordered to be interred upon the production of the certificate of the coroner.  
(Code 1956, § 13-5)

laws.title: Same—Endorsement of local registrar as to compliance with state law
laws.content:
Every burial certificate shall bear the endorsement of the registrar of vital statistics of the parish that such requirements of existing state laws have been fully complied with.  
(Code 1956, § 13-7)  
*State law reference—Death certificate, R.S. 40:34(B)(2) et seq.*

laws.title: Same—Physicians to advise people of necessity for compliance with state law
laws.content:
The physicians of the city shall inform all persons applying for burial certificates that they will not be received by the keepers of the several cemeteries of the city unless they shall have been endorsed by the registrar of vital statistics of the parish in accordance with section 38-7.  
(Code 1956, § 13-8)

laws.title: No more burials in certain cemetery
laws.content:
No person shall be buried in the ground of the cemetery or the square comprised within Washington, Sixth, Prytania and Coliseum Streets, of the Fourth District and in the future no interments shall be made therein except by persons owning lots, vaults or tombs and except further that the St. Joseph Asylum, of the Fourth District, may use square nos. 311 and 312 for burial purposes.  
(Code 1956, § 13-9)

**Sec. 38-11. Punishment for damaging graves, etc.**

Any person who shall wantonly damage or destroy the enclosures of any grave, tomb, or monument or damage a tomb or fence in any cemetery shall be liable to punishment in accordance with state law or with section 54-377 of the City Code.

(Code 1956, § 13-12; M.C.S., Ord. No. 18,751, § 2, 6-4-98)

*State law reference—Desecration of graves, R.S. 14:101.*

**Sec. 38-12. Disturbing cemeteries.**

Any person who shall enter a cemetery and break the trees or shrubbery therein or deface the tombs or commit any other depredation, use any profane or improper language while on the premises, or sell or offer for sale any refreshment or fruit of any kind within such cemetery shall be liable to a fine in accordance with state law or to penalties as contained in section 54-377 of the City Code.

(Code 1956, § 13-13; M.C.S., Ord. No. 18,751, § 3, 6-4-98)

*State law reference—Criminal mischief, R.S. 14:59.*

**Sec. 38-13. Unlawful to play music in commercial establishments near cemeteries.**

It shall be unlawful for any person to play or permit the playing of any radio, phonograph or other sound-producing instrument in any commercial establishment located within 1,000 feet of the outer boundary line of any cemetery or burial ground between the hours of 9:00 a.m. and 6:00 p.m.

(Code 1956, § 13-14)

**Sec. 38-14. Printed copy of article to be posted in cemeteries.**

A printed copy of this article shall be placed for reference in a conspicuous position at each entrance of all cemeteries within the incorporated limits of the city, at the expense of the sexton of each cemetery.

(Code 1956, § 13-16)

Secs. 38-15—38-50. Reserved.

**ARTICLE II. CITY-OWNED CEMETERIES***

**DIVISION 1. IN GENERAL**

**Sec. 38-51. Maintained by the department of property management.**

The cemeteries owned by the city shall be operated, managed, and maintained by the division of city cemeteries within the department of property management.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 28518, § 1, 10-15-20)

**Sec. 38-52. Deposit of funds.**

All fees, charges, and revenues received by the city for the use of any city-owned cemetery or for cemetery services rendered or related goods sold or provided by the division of cemeteries or the department of property management shall be deposited into a newly created cemetery repair and maintenance fund, created pursuant to Ordinance No. 28519 M.C.S. and codified at section 70-415.298 et seq. of the Code of the City of New Orleans.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 28518, § 1, 10-15-20)

**Sec. 38-53. Superintendent of city cemeteries; duties.**

The city cemeteries shall be under the control of a superintendent of city cemeteries who shall exercise immediate supervision of necessary

**Sec. 38-54. Regulations; suspension.**

The superintendent of city cemeteries may make and enforce such other regulations governing the operation of the city cemeteries which are not inconsistent with this article or state law.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 28518, § 1, 10-15-20)

**Sec. 38-55. Record of burials.**

The superintendent of cemeteries shall keep a permanent record of each interment in the city cemeteries under his supervision, which record shall include a copy of the certificate of death of the individual interred and the plot number, square, and location of the place of interment. Such records shall be maintained in perpetuity in the superintendent of cemeteries office.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 28518, § 1, 10-15-20)

**Sec. 38-56. Personnel to perform cemetery work.**

No person other than cemetery personnel under the supervision of the superintendent of cemeteries shall inter, disinter, or reinter any human remains within the confines of any city cemeteries, provided that the superintendent of city cemeteries may permit the performance of such work by noncity parties, so long as said work is performed to the standards set by the superintendent.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 28518, § 1, 10-15-20)

**Sec. 38-57. Depth and spacing of graves.**

Any cemetery sexton or other person digging graves for underground interments shall dig sufficiently deep to allow for at least two feet of soil to cover the entire area of the casket, unless the said interment is in a burial vault, coping or lawn crypt. Spacing shall be adjacent, but not overlapping, the grave shafts on either side.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 28518, § 1, 10-15-20)

**Sec. 38-58. Plot, space, or structure to be kept orderly.**

All persons having an interest in plots, spaces, or structures within city cemeteries shall keep the same in good repair and free from vegetative overgrowth at all times.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 28518, § 1, 10-15-20)

**Sec. 38-59. Maintenance of cemetery tombs and/or spaces more than 50 years old; sale of repaired abandoned cemetery spaces.**

(a) The cemeteries division may renovate and repair but not demolish, at its own cost and/or in conjunction with any private, state, or federal grant or fund, titled cemetery spaces within any city cemetery that are more than 50 years old and which have deteriorated, when the record owner or his spouse or heirs, assigns, or successors have neglected to do such repair or renovation within one year after written notice mailed by registered or certified mail to the last known address of the last record owner on the records of the city, the posting of notice on each of such cemetery spaces and/or tombs, and advertising in the official journal of the parish or municipality notifying the owner thereof that such renovation and/or repair will be made, unless the owner thereof objects by written notice to the office of the cemetery authority before the end of the one year period. Upon failing to receive any objections, after due notice has been given, the city may proceed with the repairs or renovations with impunity.

(b) The cemetery superintendent shall require the payment by the record owner, heirs, or assigns of all documented repair and/or renovation costs before any such renovated or repaired interment space and/or tomb may thereafter be used.

(c) The repaired space and/or tomb shall revert to the ownership of the city if the cemetery superintendent has been unable to locate, after diligent efforts, any of the owners or their successors, assigns, or heirs for a period of three years following the repair or renovation, and the city shall take possession of such interment

laws.title: Cemeteries; maintenance of vaults and wall vaults more than 50 years old; reclamation by authority
laws.content:
(a) The cemeteries division may renovate, repair, and/or maintain vaults, at its own cost and/or in conjunction with any private, state, or federal grant or fund, vaults and/or wall vaults that are more than 50 years old located in city cemeteries, which have deteriorated or are in a ruinous state under the following conditions:

(1) In the event that the cemetery superintendent has no evidence of ownership or interments in the vault and/or wall vault in question, it may immediately make the repairs, renovations, and maintenance and after same have been completed, publish as part of a general notice in the official journal of the parish or municipality a notice notifying all persons that if no one comes forward to the office of the cemetery superintendent with written evidence of ownership of the vault and/or wall vault in question within 60 days of the date of publication then the cemetery authority shall have the right to reclaim the ownership of the vault and/or wall vault in question and resell same.

(2) In the event that there is evidence of an interment or interments in the vault and/or wall vault in question, and the cemetery superintendent has no evidence of ownership, the remains may be immediately removed and temporarily reinterred at another location, and the city shall then have the power to immediately make the renovations,

repairs, and maintenance necessary, and the same notice procedure set forth in paragraph (1) shall be followed, except that all persons shall have six months to come forward to the office of the cemetery superintendent and present written evidence of ownership in the vault and/or wall vault in question, and in the event that anyone fails to do so within the time prescribed, then the vault and/or wall vault may be reclaimed by the city and resold. If the vault is resold by the city, the existing remains shall remain as a servitude burdening the new ownership of the vault.

(3) In the event that records of the cemetery superintendent indicate that there is a record owner of the vault and/or wall vault in question, the remains, if any, may be immediately removed and temporarily reinterred at another location, and the cemetery superintendent shall have the right and power to immediately make the necessary renovations, repairs, and maintenance; then the cemetery authority shall attempt to contact the owner by registered or certified mail at his last known address, and also publish as part of a general notice in the official journal of the parish or municipality in question a notice stating that in the event the owner or his heirs, assigns, or successors fail to come forward to the office of the cemetery superintendent within six months of the date of the notice and submit written proof of ownership, then the vault and/or wall vault in question may be reclaimed and resold by the city. If the vault is resold by the city, the existing remains shall remain as a servitude burdening the new ownership of the vault.

(4) In addition to the notifications called for in paragraphs (1), (2), and (3) hereinabove, the cemetery superintendent shall also post a common or general sign or notice in a conspicuous place in the cemetery informing the public of the above so that

claimants may come forward in the manner prescribed herein to assert their rights.

(5) Under no circumstances shall the city be prevented from doing repairs, renovations, and maintenance to vaults and/or wall vaults if same are necessary for the preservation of the section of vaults and/or wall vaults in question and/or the beautification of the cemetery. If it becomes necessary to remove remains therefrom, the cemetery authority shall have this right and power as set forth above, but the remains must be kept separate and returned to their original location after work is complete

(6) After the renovations, repairs, and maintenance have been completed and the prescribed time period has lapsed, and the city has reclaimed the ownership of the vault and/or wall vault in question, then all of the remains removed in accordance with the provisions of this Paragraph, shall be reinterred, and the cemetery superintendent shall retain records, tablets, stones, and other information regarding which vaults and/or wall vaults the remains were removed from and the interments therein, and the names of the deceased persons in question, if they are available.

(7) Under no circumstances shall any of the above be construed in such a fashion as to prevent the city from immediately making repairs, renovations, and/or maintenance of wall vaults in the event that same are deemed necessary for the protection of the health, safety, and welfare of the general public.

(8) If a person comes forward to the cemetery superintendent within the time periods prescribed in paragraphs (1) through (3) hereof with satisfactory written evidence of ownership or title to the vault and/or wall vault in question, the cemetery superintendent may require that they pay their pro rata share, to be reasonably determined by the cemetery superintendent, of all actual costs and expenses of repairs, renovations, and maintenance before the said vault and/or wall vault may thereafter be used by them and their title thereto confirmed. If there is some other impediment or objection to reuse of the vault and/or wall vault in question, they must still pay their pro rata share of all costs as set forth hereinabove to confirm their title to same, otherwise ownership or title may be reclaimed by the city and the space resold. Under no circumstances shall the owner of the vault and/or wall vault in question be able to object to the repairs, renovations, and maintenance done or to be done if it is necessary for the preservation of the section of vaults, and/or wall vaults in question, or the protection of the health, safety, and welfare of the general public.

laws.title: Fees
laws.content:
Fees for cemetery services and use shall be set annually by the superintendent of cemeteries. The fees shall be re-evaluated annually and based on the fair market value of the service or use. Said fees shall annually be posted in a public location.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 28518, § 1, 10-15-20)

laws.title: Interment days and hours of operation
laws.content:
The director of the department of property management shall establish the hours of operation for city cemeteries provided however, that all cemeteries shall be open for visitation for an eight-hour period on All Saint’s Day, Father’s Day and Mother’s Day of each year.

The superintendent of cemeteries may determine specific days for interments in each of the city cemeteries.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 28518, § 1, 10-15-20)

laws.title: Servitudes: Right of use of city cemetery space
laws.content:
On/in specified areas of city cemeteries, there shall be granted by the city only the servitude of the right of use of space, and no one shall be granted, nor shall the city alienate for the purpose of the interment of human remains, the full ownership of any space or plot.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 28518, § 1, 10-15-20)

laws.title: Application for right of use of space
laws.content:
(a) Any person desiring to purchase a servitude of the right of use of a space or plot within a city cemetery shall make application for same to the superintendent of cemeteries. The application shall be nontransferable and shall be accompanied by a nonrefundable application fee as provided for in this chapter. No person shall have more than one application pending for a space or plot within a city cemetery at any time.

(b) Applicants shall be granted a right of use for a space or plot within a city cemetery on a first-come, first-served basis. The superintendent of the division of city cemeteries may establish, for each city cemetery, a waiting list, or lists, of applicants for the use of spaces or plots within that cemetery based upon the size or type of space or plot desired or such other criteria as may be deemed desirable.

(c) Upon approval of the application or a grant of servitude of right of use and acceptance by the applicant of the space or plot available, the superintendent of city cemeteries shall cause the right of use of space within a city cemetery to be granted by the execution by the applicant of a written act of grant of servitude of the right of use in a form approved by the city attorney and the director of the department of property management.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 28518, § 1, 10-15-20)

Supp. No. 96

CD38:8

laws.title: Restrictions upon right of use
laws.content:
Every servitude of right of use granted by the city shall contain the following restrictions:

(1) Transferability. The servitude of right of use granted pursuant to this division shall not be transferable except upon the written approval of the director of the department of property management in a form approved by the city attorney. No person granted a servitude of right of use pursuant to this article shall demand or receive from the transferee of such servitude any remuneration whatsoever, provided, however, that the transferor of such servitude may demand, as a condition of the transfer, that the transferee pay a pro-rata amount of the fee for the right of use charged by the city. Nothing in this section shall be construed to deny to co-owners in indivision a right to seek partition by licitation of their jointly held right of use.

(2) Extent of right of use. The servitude of right of use granted by this article may be exercised by, and at the exclusive discretion of, the person in whose name the servitude of right of use is granted, his heirs, assigns, or successors in interest, solely for the interment of human remains and subject to the restrictions provided by this chapter, applicable law and the regulations of the department of property management. In no event shall the person in whose name the servitude of right of use is granted, his heirs, assigns, or successors in interest, impose any fee or charge for the interment of human remains in such city cemetery space or plot.

(3) Term. All servitudes of right of use granted pursuant to this article shall terminate on the tenth anniversary of the date of grant thereof.

(4) Renewal of servitude.

a. Every person granted a servitude of right of use pursuant to this article, or granted a renewal of such

servitude, his heirs, assigns, or successors in interest, shall have the right to renew, for a succeeding ten-year period, the servitude of the right of use granted to him. The right of renewal granted by this subsection shall be exercised by:

1. Written notice of the intention to renew the servitude filed with the superintendent of the division of city cemeteries not sooner than one year, nor later than 30 days, prior to the expiration of the then-current term of such servitude, and accompanied by;

2. The applicable renewal fee; and

3. In the case of renewal by an heir, assign, or successor in interest, a judgment of possession of a court of competent jurisdiction, an act translative of title or an affidavit which meets the requirements of section 38-92(a)(1)

b. The renewal of any servitude of right of use shall be conditioned upon the payment by the renewing grantee of the then-current fee for the grant of the servitude of right of use.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 28518, § 1, 10-15-20)

laws.title: Extinguishment of servitude of right of use
laws.content:
Absent renewal of the servitude as set out in section 38-88 above, the servitude for a right of use shall extinguish at the end of ten years without any required notice or action by the city or the superintendent of cemeteries.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 28518, § 1, 10-15-20)

laws.title: Construction pursuant to servitude of right of use
laws.content:
Markers, copings, boxes, railings, and other enclosures:

(1) must not exceed 3.5' × 8' in dimension on the outside of the form and

(2) must not interfere with the long-term use of the grave shaft or site.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 28518, § 1, 10-15-20)

laws.title: Title transfers; judgment of possession, act translative of title
laws.content:
(a) Any person claiming to be the successor in interest of any person in whose name title to a space or plot within a city cemetery is held, and who desires that the title to such space or plot be transferred to claimant's name shall make written application, in a form approved by the department of property management, to the superintendent of city cemeteries for a transfer of title, and shall present to the director together with such application either:

(1) A judgment of a court of competent jurisdiction recognizing the person requesting such transfer as the rightful heir or legatee of the title holder of record and placing them in possession of the space or plot in question, or,

(2) An act translative of title and in authentic form, showing the person requesting such transfer to be the successor in interest of the title holder of record to the space or plot in question.

(b) The superintendent of the division of city cemeteries shall present the application and the documents required under this division to the city attorney for approval as to form and legality, and, if so approved by the city attorney, shall issue a new title in the name or names of the persons requesting the transfer.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 28518, § 1, 10-15-20)

laws.title: Title transfer requests without judgment of possession, act translative of title
laws.content:
(a) Any person claiming to be the successor in interest of any person in whose name title to a space or plot within a city cemetery is held, and who desires that the title to such space or plot be

laws.title: Characteristics of tombs; repairs, etc
laws.content:
All tombs must be built of high-quality components approved by the superintendent of cemeteries. All the tombs must be kept in good order by the owners.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 28518, § 1, 10-15-20)

laws.title: Construction and alteration permit required
laws.content:
(a) No contractor, builder, monument dealer, gardener or other person shall place or construct any tomb, coping, vault of any description,

headstone, marker, tablet, statue, trees or shrubbery, make any repairs, redesign or alter, or demolish in whole or part, any existing structure within a city cemetery without first obtaining the approval of the superintendent of city cemeteries, who, upon approving such work to be in accordance with the provisions of this article, will issue a construction and alteration permit.

(b) The provisions of this article shall not be deemed to apply to routine maintenance or the routine trimming of grass, trees or shrubbery, the inscribing of names upon tablets or headstones already in place or other work incidental, as a matter of course, to interment, disinterment or reinterment.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 28518, § 1, 10-15-20)

laws.title: Permit application; fees; criteria
laws.content:
The superintendent of city cemeteries shall prescribe the procedure and forms for making application for a construction and alteration permit and fees for such permit shall be charged in accordance with fair market value as determined annually. The superintendent of city cemeteries shall issue such permit provided that the quality and grade of materials used in the construction or alteration and the general design and general arrangement meet criteria which the superintendent deems appropriate.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 28518, § 1, 10-15-20)

laws.title: Historic cemeteries—Designation; certificate required
laws.content:
(a) Any city cemetery designated a National Historic Site or Landmark, entered upon the National Register of Historic Places, accorded historic site status by the state department of culture, recreation and tourism or which is bounded by or falls within any historic district shall be considered a historic cemetery. No contractor, builder, monument dealer, gardener or other person shall place or construct any tomb, coping, vault of any description, headstone, marker, tablet, statue, tree or shrubbery, make any repairs, redesign or alter or demolish in whole or part, any existing structure within a city cemetery, without first obtaining the approval of the

(b) Such certificate shall be in lieu of a construction and alteration permit provided, however, that the fees established by section 38-61 shall be applicable to the application and receipt of the certificate.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 28518, § 1, 10-15-20)

laws.title: Same—Criteria
Certificate of appropriateness—Posting; expiration
laws.content:
(a) The certificate of appropriateness shall be posted where plainly visible on or near the exterior of the structure to be constructed, altered or demolished during the period of such construction, alteration or demolition.

(b) All certificates of appropriateness shall expire 90 days after the date of issuance if the work approved has not commenced.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 28518, § 1, 10-15-20)

laws.title: Same—Denial; appeal
laws.content:
(a) The superintendent of city cemeteries shall notify by certified mail every applicant who is denied a certificate of appropriateness.

(b) Any applicant denied a certificate of appropriateness may appeal the finding of the superintendent of city cemeteries by filing a written request for review of the superintendent's determination with the director of the department of property management within 15 days of the applicant's receipt of the notice of denial.

(c) The director of the department of property management shall afford the applicant reasonable opportunity to present testimony or documentary evidence regarding the construction, alteration or demolition proposed by the applicant and may solicit expert testimony regarding the architectural or historic importance or significance of the structure in question. In reviewing the denial of an application for a certificate of appropriateness, the director of the department of property management shall consider the quality and grade of materials to be used in the construction or alteration, the general design and general arrangement, the architectural

style, the scale, the historic or architectural significance of the structure in question and such other criteria as the director may deem appropriate.

(d) The director of the department of property management shall either affirm or overrule the denial of the superintendent of city cemeteries and shall notify the applicant of his decision by certified mail.

(e) Any applicant denied a certificate of appropriateness by decision of the director of property management may appeal the finding of the director of property management by filing a written request for review of the director's determination with the clerk of council within 15 days of the applicant's receipt of the property management director's notice of denial.

(f) The council shall consider the applicant's request for review at its next regular meeting, or at any regular meeting within 60 days of the applicant's filing of appeal with the clerk of council, and the council may affirm or overrule the denial of a certificate of appropriateness by an affirmative vote of a majority of all of its members, failing which the decision of the director of the department of property management shall stand as final.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 28518, § 1, 10-15-20)

laws.title: Sanctions
laws.content:
Whoever shall place or construct any tomb, coping, vault of any description, headstone, marker, tablet, statue, trees or shrubbery or make any repairs, redesign, alter or demolish any existing structure within a city cemetery without first securing a certificate of appropriateness in accordance with the provisions of this article shall be guilty of a misdemeanor, which shall be punishable by a fine not to exceed $300.00 and/or 90 days in jail. Each day upon which a violation of this section shall occur shall be deemed a separate offense.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 28518, § 1, 10-15-20)

laws.title: Temporary or emergency constructions
laws.content:
Nothing contained in this division shall prevent the making of a temporary construction, altera-

tion or demolition of any structure within a city cemetery when such construction, alteration or demolition is undertaken under or by the order of any court or governmental agency for the purpose of remedying emergency conditions determined to be dangerous to life, health or property.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 28518, § 1, 10-15-20)

laws.content: Secs. 42-204–42-225. Reserved.

laws.title: Raffles, bingo, video bingo, keno, and pull tabs prohibited
laws.content:
It shall be unlawful for any person to hold, conduct, or operate the game or games of chance commonly known as raffles, bingo, electronic video bingo, keno, or pull tabs unless licensed to do so under the provisions of this article.

(Code 1956, § 14-41)

laws.title: Charitable raffles, bingo and keno authorized
laws.content:
It shall be lawful for any bona fide nonprofit veteran’s, charitable, educational, religious or fraternal organizations, or civic and service clubs licensed under this article, to hold and operate the specific kind of game of chance commonly known as a raffle played by drawing for prizes or the allotment of prizes by chance by the selling of shares or tickets or rights to participate in such game and by conducting the game accordingly; and the game of chance commonly known as bingo or keno played for prizes with cards bearing numbers or other designations, five or more in one line, the holder covering numbers, as objects, similarly numbered, are drawn from a receptacle, and the game being won by the person who first covers a previously designated arrangement of numbers on such a card, by selling shares or tickets or rights to participate in such games and by conducting the games accordingly when the entire net proceeds of such games of chance are to be devoted to educational, charitable, patriotic, religious or public spirited uses and the department of finance may issue a license to any such organization or club above specified in accordance with the provisions of this article.

(Code 1956, § 14-42)

*State law references—Definition, R.S. 33:4861.2(1); requirement for state license, R.S. 33:4861.4.*

laws.title: Pull tabs authorized
laws.content:
It shall be lawful for any bona fide nonprofit veterans, charitable, educational, religious or fraternal organizations, or civic and service clubs licensed under this article to hold the specific game known as pull tabs. The term “pull tabs” shall mean single or banded tickets or cards each with its face covered to conceal one or more numbers or symbols, where one or more card or ticket in each set has been designated in advance as a “winner.” Funds from all pull tab sales, after deduction of necessary expenses, shall be dedicated for use by bona fide nonprofit veterans, charitable, educational, religious or fraternal organizations, or civic and service clubs in accordance with R.S. 33:4861.1 et seq.

(Code 1956, § 14-42.1)

*State law reference—Definition, R.S. 33:4861.2.*

laws.title: Gambling; immunity
laws.content:
No person shall be liable to prosecution or conviction for violation of section 54-276 for any of the following:

(1) Possessing, selling or in any manner disposing of, in the city, any shares, tickets or rights to participate in any game of chance conducted or to be conducted under any license lawfully issued pursuant to this article;

(2) Lawfully conducting or participating in the conduct of any such game of chance; or

(3) Permitting the conduct of any such game of chance upon premises owned by him or it of

*State law reference—Charitable raffles, bingo and keno, generally, R.S. 33:4861.1 et seq., 40:1485.1 et seq.*

any game of chance conducted or to be conducted under any license lawfully issued pursuant to this article.

This immunity shall not extend to any person or corporation knowingly conducting or participating in the conduct of any game of chance under any license obtained by any false pretense or statement in any application for such license or otherwise, or possessing, selling or disposing of shares, tickets, or rights to participate in, or permitting the conduct upon any premises owned by him or it of any game of chance conducted under any license known to him or it to have been ordained by any such false or fraudulent pretense or statement.

(Code 1956, § 14-56)

laws.title: Application requirements for certain organizations
laws.content:
Notwithstanding the provisions of subsections (b) and (c) of section 42-66 with regard to the requirement that applicants for a license to conduct charitable raffles, bingo, or keno be domiciliaries and residents of the parish, and that applicants do not conduct charitable games of chance in other parishes, an organization which operates within the parish as a unit of an organization domiciled elsewhere in the state may be issued a license under this division under the following conditions:

(1) The applicant shall submit applicable articles of incorporation and by-laws describing the status of the organization to the department of finance.

(2) The director of the department of finance or his designated representative shall review the material submitted and make a recommendation as to whether or not the organization operates independently as a unit of an organization domiciled elsewhere in the state and devotes the proceeds of its activities to educational, charitable, patriotic, religious, or public spirited uses within the parish.

(3) An initial application for a license pursuant to this section shall not be issued unless the director of the department of finance or his designated representative has reviewed the application and made a recommendation concerning issuance of the license to the council and the council has approved the issuance of the license by resolution. The council may act contrary to the recommendation of the director of the department of finance or his designated representative. Renewals of licenses previously approved by council resolution shall not require subsequent council approval.

(4) Failure of an organization holding a license under this section to devote proceeds from the conduct of charitable games of chance to activities in the parish shall be cause for suspension or revocation of the license.

(5) All other provisions of this division shall be applicable to an organization granted a license pursuant to this section.

(Code 1956, § 14-43.01)

State law references—Definition, R.S. 33:4861.2(1); application for license, R.S. 33:4861.5.

laws.title: Games conducted in other parishes
laws.content:
Notwithstanding the provisions of subsection (c) of section 42-66, a license to conduct charitable games of chance under this division may be issued to a nonprofit, nonstock corporation that provides professional education, public education, community and patient services, and research to improve the care and treatment of those afflicted with diseases of the kidney provided that the applicant is a domiciliary of the parish and meets all other requirements of this division even if the organization conducts charitable games of chance in another parish. An organization granted a license pursuant to this section may conduct charitable games of chance in another parish. All other

(Code 1956, § 14-43.02)

laws.title: Senior citizens clubs
laws.content:
(a) Notwithstanding any provision of this division to the contrary, the department of finance may issue a license for the conduct of raffles, bingo or keno to nonprofit civic clubs for senior citizens, which clubs are hereby found to constitute a class which tends to promote the general welfare by affording recreational opportunities and companionship for older citizens. For the purposes of this section, a club is a club for senior citizens if at least 75 percent of its members are 55 years of age or older.

(b) A license issued pursuant to this section shall be subject to the following restrictions:

(1) Games of chance shall not be conducted more often than twice each month.

(2) The total value of prizes awarded for bingo and keno shall not exceed $300.00 per occasion on which the games of chance are conducted.

(3) The games of chance conducted shall be held only as an activity on a program including the serving of meals.

(c) A club applying for a license to conduct games of chance pursuant to this section shall not be required to furnish proof of tax exempt status under title 26 of the United States Code.

(d) All other provisions and requirements of this division shall apply to civic clubs for senior citizens licensed pursuant to this section.

(Code 1956, § 14-43.1)

State law reference—Authorization to license certain organizations, R.S. 33:4861.4(D).

laws.title: Special licenses
laws.content:
(a) It is hereby lawful for any charitable organization licensed by the state and city for the conduct of charitable bingo to apply for a special license for the conduct of no more than two bingo sessions annually at which the total amount of prizes which may be awarded on any one calendar day under such a license shall not exceed $25,000.00 in cash or other thing or things of value in accordance with applicable state law. Except as otherwise provided by this article and applicable state law, all other provisions of this article shall apply to the issuance of such special licenses.

(b) The council may by motion authorize the waiver of limits on expenditures for janitorial service, security service and space rental imposed by section 42-126 for charitable bingos conducted in accordance with subsection (a) of this section. The motion authorizing the waiver shall specify a maximum amount which may be expended for janitorial and security service and space rental, and such a motion shall be required for each separate occasion. Each such motion shall be forwarded by the clerk of council to the department of finance.

(Code 1956, § 14-52.2)

laws.title: Issuance, fee
laws.content:
If satisfied from its investigation that the applicant for a license under this division is qualified to conduct charitable games of chance, the department of finance shall issue a license for the conduct of bingo, keno, and raffles upon payment CD42:6 CHARITIES § 42-101 of an annual fee in accordance with the following schedule:
License Annual Fee
(1) Bingo, keno and raffles……… $100.00
(2) Pull tabs:
a. At leased bingo hall facilities………………… 250.00
b. Other locations…………… 50.00
c. One occasion…………… 15.00
(3) Electronic video bingo……… 100.00
(4) One annual raffle…………… 10.00
(Code 1956, § 14-45)

laws.title: Term
laws.content:
Licenses under this division shall be valid beginning on April 1, 1978. All licenses under this division shall be valid from time of issuance until March 31 next following, unless sooner suspended or revoked in accordance with this division.

(Code 1956, § 14-46)

laws.title: Form
Display
laws.content:
All licenses issued under the provisions of this division shall be publicly displayed by the licensee at the place where any game is conducted thereunder at all times during the conduct thereof, so as to be easily seen by the public and the department of finance or its authorized agents.

(Code 1956, § 14-49)

Secs. 42-76–42-100. Reserved.

laws.title: Refusal to issue license; appeal
laws.content:
(a) If the department of finance finds that the applicant for the license is not in compliance with the provisions of this article, it shall deny the application for the license or renewal thereof. This denial shall be communicated to the applicant by registered or certified mail, giving specific reasons for such denial.

(b) In order to afford every person a full opportunity to be heard, it is hereby provided that when an application for a license or renewal thereof is denied, the applicant, within ten days from the date of notification of such denial, may petition in writing the department of finance for a hearing. Such hearing shall be held by the chief administrative officer or his designated representative, the city attorney or his designated representative, and the director of the department of finance or his designated representative after due notice of the hearing to the applicant.

(c) If, following such hearing, the parties representing the city find that the application for the license is not in compliance with this division, or that the applicant does not meet the qualifications required by this division, then the department of finance shall be instructed to confirm the denial of the application for a license. This denial shall be communicated to the applicant by registered or certified mail, giving the specific reason for such denial and shall constitute the final action of the city in connection with such application.

(Code 1956, § 14-47)

laws.title: Grounds for revocation
laws.content:
(a) Any person who shall make any false statement in any application for a license under this article, or shall fail to keep such books and records and shall fully and truly record all transactions connected with the holding, operating or conducting of games of chance under any such license, or shall falsify or make any false entry in any books or records so far as they relate to any transaction connected with the holding, operating and conducting of any game of chance under any such license, or shall fail to submit in a timely manner any reports required under the provisions of this article, or conduct any game of chance not authorized by this article, or shall violate any of the provisions of this article, or of any term of such license, shall, in addition to suffering any other penalties which may be imposed by law, forfeit his current license upon a determination to revoke the same, and shall be ineligible to apply for a license under this article for one year after the date of such revocation.

(b) No license shall be issued to any applicant for the use of the same physical location or premises whereon the license of the previous licensee has been revoked for six months after the date of such revocation.

(c) Notwithstanding any provision of this section to the contrary, a violation of this article committed during the term of a previous license shall also constitute cause or grounds for revocation of a current license held under this article.

(Code 1956, § 14-57)

*State law reference—Charitable Raffles, Bingo and Keno Licensing Law, R.S. 33:4861.1 et seq.*

laws.title: Suspension pending hearing
laws.content:
(a) Whenever any person licensed under this article is found to be in violation of any provision of this article by the department of finance through its officers, employees, or authorized agents or the department of police, then such licensee shall be issued a written citation which shall set forth the facts and circumstances of the violation and command such licensee to appear before the director of the department of finance at a date, time and place therein specified to show cause why his license should not be suspended pending the filing of a petition for revocation and a hearing thereon.

(b) Upon receipt of evidence satisfactory to the director of the department of finance at such hearing that any person licensed under this article has violated the provisions of this article, the director of the department of finance shall forthwith suspend the license of such licensee pending the filing of a petition to revoke the license. This suspension shall remain in effect for a period of 30 days unless extended by the chief administrative officer because of a delay in the revocation hearing date initiated by the licensee or his representative or the director of the department of finance. This suspension may be withdrawn at any time by the director of the department of finance upon his determination not to file a petition for revocation or for other good cause. Any licensee who has his license suspended under this section may appeal to the chief administrative officer for a review of the decision by the director of the department of finance.

(Code 1956, § 14-57.1)

*State law reference—Charitable Raffles, Bingo and Keno Licensing Law, R.S. 33:4861.1 et seq.*

laws.title: Regulation and inspections
laws.content:
The department of finance through its officers, employees, or authorized agents and the department of police shall have and exercise control and supervision over all games of chance held, operated and conducted under such license to the end that the same are fairly held, operated and conducted in accordance with the provisions of such license and this article. The department of finance through its officers and agents, and the department of police, shall have the right of entry at all times onto any premises where any such games of chance are being held, operated and conducted or where it is intended that any such game of chance shall be held, operated and conducted, or where any equipment being used or intended to be used in the conduct thereof is found, for the purpose of inspecting the same.

(Code 1956, § 14-50)

laws.title: Frequency of games
laws.content:
(a) Except as provided in article IV of this chapter, no session of a charitable game of chance shall be held, operated or conducted under any license issued under this article more than 15 days in any one calendar month, or shall any session of a charitable game of chance be held in any one building more than twice in any one week from Sunday to Saturday. A licensed, leased bingo facility permitted under article IV of this chapter shall not be subject to the restriction limiting the conduct of charitable games of chance to two sessions per week.

(b) For the purposes of this section, a session of a charitable game of chance is a four-hour period of time during which one or more permitted games of chance are played.

(c) No charitable games of chance shall be conducted at leased bingo hall facilities licensed in accordance with article IV of this chapter on Sundays from 12:01 a.m. until 1:00 p.m. nor shall such charitable games of chance be conducted at any location at times which are prohibited by the comprehensive zoning ordinance.

(Code 1956, § 14-51)

laws.title: Operation and conduct of games
laws.content:
No person shall hold, operate or conduct, or assist in holding, operating or conducting, any game or games of chance under any license issued under this article except an active member of the organization or association to which the license is issued. No such game of chance shall be conducted with any equipment, except such as shall be owned absolutely or used without payment of any compensation therefor by licensee. No item of expense shall be incurred or paid in connection with the holding, operating or conducting of any game of chance held, operated or conducted pursuant to any license issued under this article, except such as are bona fide items of expense for goods, wares and merchandise furnished which are reasonably necessary to be purchased or furnished for the holding, operating or conducting of such game. No commission, salary, compensation, reward or recompense whatever shall be paid or given, directly or indirectly, to any person holding, operating or conducting, or assisting in the holding, operation or conduct of any game of chance so held, operated or conducted provided that any association or corporation licensed to hold, operate, or
