conduct any games of chance under any license issued pursuant to this article may compensate for services rendered, any 15 employees who assist in the holding, operating, or conducting of such games. The rate of compensation shall be no more than $15.00 per hour and in any event shall not exceed $90.00 per session for any employee. Each employee or volunteer worker may also be provided meals and beverages to be eaten on the premises not to exceed a total value of $15.00 per person. Compensation provided for in this section shall not constitute a violation of the prohibition against the payment or giving of any person holding, operating, or conducting any such game.

(Code 1956, § 14-52; M.C.S., Ord. No. 28762, § 1, 8-5-21)

State law reference—Commissions or salaries, R.S. 33:4861.12.

laws.title: Prize limits
laws.content:
On any one day on which bingo or keno games are staged by a licensee, the total amount of prizes or possible prizes available to patrons of the bingo or keno games shall not exceed the amount of $3,500.00. All prizes, cash or otherwise, shall be provided by the individual licensee.

(Code 1956, § 14-52.1)

State law reference—Similar provisions, R.S. 33:4861.11(B).

laws.title: Reports by licensee
laws.content:
Not later than 20 days after January 1, April 1, July 1 and October 1 of each year, each licensee under this article shall furnish to the department of finance a duly verified statement showing the amount of the gross receipts derived from activities licensed under this article for the quarter preceding the reporting dates established hereinabove, which shall include receipts from the sale of shares, tickets or rights in any manner connected with participation in such activities or the right to participate therein, each item of expense incurred, or paid, and each item of expenditure made or to be made, name and address of each person to whom each such item has been, or is to be paid, with a detailed description of the merchandise purchased or the services rendered therefor, the net profit derived from each game of chance, and the uses to which such net profit has been or is to be applied and a list of prizes offered or given, with the respective values thereof. It shall be the duty of each licensee to maintain and keep such books and records as may be necessary to substantiate the particulars of each such report. Reports furnished under this section shall be subject to the provisions of the Public Records Act.

(Code 1956, § 14-53)

laws.title: Payment of expenses; bookkeeping
laws.content:
(a) Payment of expenses by a licensee under this article shall be made only by checks signed by a duly authorized person and made payable to a specific person, and at no time shall a check be made payable to cash. Permitted expenses shall only be for one or more of the following purposes:

(1) Payment of necessary expenses incurred in connection with the conduct of charitable games of chance. For the purposes of this section, promotion or advertising shall not be considered a necessary expense.

(2) Raffles, bingo, and keno supplies, equipment.

(3) Bookkeeping or accounting.

(4) Janitorial service and security service, not to exceed a total of $170.00 per occasion.

(5) License fees.

(6) Disbursement of net proceeds derived from the charitable raffles, bingo, and keno for educational, charitable, patriotic, religious or public spirited uses.

(7) The transfer of net proceeds derived from the conduct of charitable raffles, bingo, or keno into one or more interest bearing accounts.

(8) Space rental not to exceed $400.00 per occasion.

(9) Payment of employees in accordance with section 42-123.

Supp. No. 97

CD42:10
CHARITIES

§ 42-126

(b) Each licensee shall maintain a bookkeeping system for the purpose of recording all receipts and expenditures in connection with the conduct of charitable games of chance and the disbursement of net proceeds derived therefrom. The books of account shall be kept up to date. Bookkeeping records, deposit books, savings account passbooks, cancelled checks, checkbooks, deposit slips, bank statements and copies of statements required

CHARITIES

§ 42-128

under this article and all other books of account shall be available for examination by the department of finance or their representatives at all reasonable times, and shall be maintained by the licensee for three years following the expiration of each year’s license.

(c) The provisions of subsections (4) and (8) of subsection (a) of this section shall not apply to any charitable bingo game or other charitable game of chance which is conducted by an organization which has been duly licensed as of January 1, 1981, and is held in a facility that is owned by the Louisiana Stadium and Exhibition District and which is held at a maximum frequency of two events per calendar year.

(Code 1956, § 14-54)

State law reference—Expenses, R.S. 33:4861.12(A)(5).

laws.title: Examination of books and records
laws.content:
The department of finance or its authorized agents shall have power to examine or to cause to be examined the books and records of any organization or association to which such license is issued so far as they may relate to any transactions connected with the holding and conducting of any game of chance thereunder, and to examine any manager, officer, director, agent, member or employee thereof under oath in relation to the conduct of any such game of chance under any such license, but any information so received shall not be disclosed except so far as may be necessary for the purpose of carrying out the provisions of this article.

(Code 1956, § 14-55)

laws.title: Electronic video bingo
laws.content:
(a) Any organization licensed to conduct bingo games under this article may apply to conduct electronic video bingo at its bingo games provided that all requirements of this article not in conflict with the provisions of this section are met.

(b) Any electronic bingo machine used in the conduct of electronic video bingo shall be subject to the following requirements and restrictions concerning its operation and use:

(1) The cost of each game play shall be not less than $0.25 nor more than $1.00.

(2) Payout shall be not less than 80 percent and not more than 90 percent of the total amount wagered.

(3) The maximum prize awarded shall be not more than $1,000.00.

(4) The machine shall dispense only tickets verified as valid, indicating the prize amount. No machine shall dispense cash.

(5) The machine shall allow only a linear based payout in which the amount of the payout follows a straight line progression in direct proportion to the amount wagered.

(6) The machine shall allow the player a choice of cards on which to play and must show a “BINGO” at the end of play.

(7) The machine shall provide for an electronic readout giving, at a minimum, a summary of total wagers, total plays, total payout, and the current prize allotment since the last date of summary or the last date of reset of the machine.

(c) Only cash prizes may be awarded to winners of games on electronic video machines.

(d) Bingo licensees may lease electronic video bingo machines provided that no lease agreement shall authorize the lessor to receive a percentage of the receipts from the machine.

(e) At least 45 percent of the net win from the machine must be paid to the licensee leasing the machine. The term “net win” means the total gross receipts of the machine reduced only by the actual prizes paid.

(f) In addition to the requirements of this section, all bingo licensees using electronic video bingo machines and all manufacturers, distributors, suppliers or lessors of electronic video bingo machines are subject to the rules, regulations, and licensing requirements of the state.

(g) Lessors licensed by the state to lease electronic video bingo machines shall submit to the department of finance duplicate copies of all documents and reports submitted to the state regarding machines leased for play in the city.

CD42:11
$\S$ 42-128

NEW ORLEANS CODE

(h) Lessors licensed by the state to lease electronic video bingo machines shall submit a sworn affidavit to the department of finance stating they are familiar with and shall comply with the provisions of this article.

(i) Organizations licensed to conduct games of chance in the city which purchase electronic video bingo machines shall comply with all provisions of this section.

(j) Compensation to a licensed bingo lessor for allowing video bingo machines to be used on its premises may be paid only by the actual owner of the machines. Any such compensation paid by a licensed charitable organization which owns machines may not exceed a reasonable amount established by rules of the department of finance which have been approved by resolution of the council.

(Code 1956, § 14-59.1)

State law reference—Use of electronic or video bingo games, R.S. 33:4861.17.

Secs. 42-129–42-160. Reserved.

laws.title: Regulation and inspections
laws.content:
The department of finance and the department of police through their officers, employees or authorized agents shall have authority to investigate and supervise the operation of cable television bingo operators to the end that the same are fairly operated and conducted in accordance with the provisions of the license and of this article. The department of finance and the department of police, through their officers, employees and authorized agents, shall have the right of entry upon the premises of any cable television bingo operations at any time during which games of chance are being conducted.

(Code 1956, § 14-77)

CD42:12
CHARITIES

§ 42-192

laws.title: Waiver of pot limits and maximum expenses
laws.content:
Notwithstanding the provisions of article II of this chapter, pot limits, expense ceilings and other necessary expense restrictions are hereby waived for cable television bingo operators.

(Code 1956, § 14-65)

laws.title: Gambling; immunity
laws.content:
No person shall be liable to prosecution or conviction for violation of section 54-276 for the following:

(1) Possessing, selling or in any manner disposing of in the city any shares, tickets or rights to participate in any game or games of chance conducted or to be conducted under any license lawfully issued pursuant to this article;

(2) Lawfully conducting or participating in the conduct of any such game of chance; or

(3) Permitting the conduct of any such game of chance upon premises owned by him or it of any game of chance conducted or to be conducted under any license lawfully issued pursuant to this article.

This immunity shall not extend to any person or corporation knowingly conducting or participating in the conduct of any game of chance under any license obtained by any false pretense or statement in any application for such license or otherwise, or possessing, selling or disposing of shares, tickets or rights to participate in, or permitting the conduct upon any premises owned by him or it, of any game of chance conducted under any license known to him or it to have been ordained by any such false or fraudulent pretense or statement.

(Code 1956, § 14-81)

laws.title: Violations
laws.content:
(a) Any person who shall make any false statement in an application for a license under this article, or shall fail to keep such books and records that shall fully and truly record all transactions connected with the holding, operating or conducting of cable television games of chance under any such license, or shall falsify or make any false entry in any books or records so far as they relate to any transaction connected with the holding, operating and conducting of any cable television game of chance under any such license, or shall violate any provision of this article of any term of such license, shall be a disorderly person and if convicted as such shall, in addition to suffering any other penalties which may be imposed, forfeit any license issued to it under this article and shall be ineligible to apply for a license under this article for one year thereafter.

(b) Whoever commits a violation of the provisions of this article shall be fined in an amount not more than $300.00 or imprisoned for a term of not more than 150 days in jail, or both.

(Code 1956, § 14-83)

laws.title: Criminal penalties
laws.content:
It shall be unlawful and a misdemeanor for any person to do any act prohibited by or to fail to do any act required by this article.

(Code 1956, § 14-80)

Secs. 42-167–42-190. Reserved.

laws.title: Required
laws.content:
No person shall use a cable television channel for the transmission of cable television games unless a cable television bingo operator’s license has been obtained from the department of finance.

(Code 1956, § 14-61)

laws.title: Operations and procedures manual—Required
laws.content:
The department of finance shall not issue a license to any cable television bingo operator pursuant to this division unless such cable television bingo operator has obtained approval from the city council for a comprehensive operations and procedures manual. Such manual must outline in exact detail all relevant information concerning the funding, administration, production, packaging, organization and other operational procedures of the proposed cable television bingo game. The city council shall approve this operations and procedures manual, as well as any changes

CD42:13
§ 42-192

NEW ORLEANS CODE

thereto, by resolution in accordance with the procedures established by this division.  
(Code 1956, § 14-64(a))

laws.title: Same—Criteria for approval
laws.content:
In evaluating whether or not an operations and procedures manual proposed by a cable television bingo operator should be approved, the council shall consider all relevant information including but not limited to the following to ensure that cable television bingo operations are conducted honestly and in a manner which will promote the interests of charitable organizations in the city:

(1) Provisions for monthly operating and financial reviews of the licensee’s operations during the first six months of operation and quarterly thereafter and provisions for an annual audit of the licensee’s operations. Such reviews and audits shall be at the expense of the licensee and performed by a qualified certified public accountant (C.P.A.) chosen by the city council. Such certified public accountant shall use generally accepted industry rates and standards for the auditing of nonprofit charitable games of chance if such standards exist.

(2) Provisions for the maintenance of detailed monthly accounts showing each day’s activities regarding pot prizes, weekly activities regarding revenues from the sales of bingo cards, monthly activities regarding production facility expenditures, payrolls, office expenses, studio rentals, retention and carry over of all unclaimed or unwon prizes and other necessary expenses, all in accordance with the provisions of applicable state law.

(3) Provisions that sales of cards to charitable sales outlets shall be made in accordance with applicable state regulations.

(4) Provisions for the resolution of any disagreements between the licensee and charitable sales outlets.

(5) Provisions for the maintenance and storage of old program video and audio tape dating back two years and means for the general public and regulatory authorities to replay such tapes.

(6) Provision of detailed statements showing that sufficient funds are available to cover all start up costs, pot prizes, city fee, production expenses, office expenses and other overhead items for at least two months.

(7) Provisions that all telecasts by the licensee shall be live or shall contain a live segment broadcasting the selection of the bingo numbers called.

(8) Location of offices within the city in a location with reasonable access to ample parking and public transit lines.

(9) Provisions for the maintenance of all monetary accounts in financial institutions headquartered in the city.

(10) Provisions for detailed description of the broadcast format including, but not limited to, production personnel and other similar production needs. If any production entity is retained, a listing of the firm, its directors and officers shall also be provided. If such details are not available at the time of application, the cable television bingo operator applicant shall submit them to the city council at the earliest possible date.

(11) Provisions for a sworn statement that the entire proceeds will be devoted to educational, charitable, patriotic, religious or public spirited uses in the parish except for contractor expenses, production expenses, applicable city fees, payments of prizes, and other expenses permitted by law or ordinance.

(12) Provisions to ensure that the cable television bingo operator shall provide copies of its contract with the city cable franchisee for the cablecast of cable television bingo.

(13) Provisions to ensure that the cable television bingo operator shall provide separate interest-bearing bank accounts established for the receipt of monies from the sale of bingo cards and that all such receipts and

CD42:14
CHARITIES

§ 42-194

accrued interest will be credited to the proper accounts as provided in section 42-194.

(14) Provisions to ensure that the cable television bingo operator shall post a bond to ensure payment of all amounts due the city, charitable organizations, and prize winners.

(15) Provisions to ensure that no charitable sales outlet shall be excluded from contracting with the cable television bingo operator under the same terms as other charitable sales outlets except for exclusion based on reasonable and objective criteria approved by resolution of the council.

(16) If the cable television bingo operator is not a nonprofit organization, provisions for affirmative action by the operator for minorities, women, small businesses, and residents of the parish in employment, subcontracting, and ownership of the partnership or corporation.

(17) Provisions for council approval for all contracts or subcontracts for computer hardware, software, or data processing services prior to execution by the cable television bingo operator or a contractor of the cable television bingo operator.

(18) Provisions providing for articles of incorporation or partnership and any amendments thereto to be provided to the director of the department of finance and the city council.

(19) Provisions to ensure that the director of the department of finance and the city council receive copies of all contracts or subcontracts with the cable TV bingo operator in connection with cable television bingo.

(20) Provisions to ensure that the director of the department of finance and the city council are provided with the names and addresses of all persons with an economic interest in the operation of the cable television bingo operator including but not limited to persons receiving franchise fees, royalties, commissions, or anything of economic value from the cable television bingo operator in connection with cable television bingo.

(21) Provisions to ensure that revenues generated by the cable television bingo operator from the sale of advertising is used for enhancement of prizes awarded to the extent that revenues from the sale of advertising exceed the cable television bingo operator’s expenses for advertising, promoting, and marketing cable television bingo games and printing of cable television bingo cards.

(22) Provisions for approval of the council for any changes to the operations and procedures manual.

(Code 1956, § 14-64(b))

laws.title: Bank accounts, distribution of receipts, interest
laws.content:
Cable television bingo operators shall provide separate interest-bearing accounts for the receipt of monies from the sale of bingo cards. All such receipts and accrued interest will be credited to the proper accounts as follows:

(1) If the cable television bingo operator is a nonprofit entity, the following schedule shall be applicable:

a. City regulatory expenses as imposed by sections 42-202 and 42-236.

b. State regulatory expenses as imposed by state law.

c. Prize money, contributions to charitable and nonprofit organizations and public spirited uses, and contract fees in such percentages as detailed in the operations and procedures manual.

(2) If the cable television bingo operator is not a nonprofit entity, the following schedule shall be applicable:

a. City regulatory expenses as imposed by sections 42-202 and 42-236.

b. State regulatory expenses as imposed by state law.

c. New Orleans Public Benefit Fund, 20 percent of revenues from the sale of shares, tickets, or rights to participate in cable television bingo games after deductions for regulatory costs imposed by the city and the state.

CD42:15
$\S 42-194$

NEW ORLEANS CODE

d. Prize money, 50 percent of revenues from the sale of shares, tickets, or rights, to participate in cable television bingo games after deductions for regulatory costs imposed by the city and the state.

e. Contract fees, not more than ten percent of revenues from the sale of shares, rights to participate in cable television bingo games after deductions for regulatory costs imposed by the city and the state.

f. Charitable organizations, 20 percent of revenues from the sale of shares, tickets, or rights to participate in cable television bingo games after deductions for regulatory costs imposed by the city and the state.

(Code 1956, § 14-64(b)(13))

laws.title: Bond required
laws.content:
The cable television bingo operator shall post a bond to ensure the payment of all amounts due to the city, charitable organizations, and prize winners. The initial amount of the bond shall be $50,000.00 and shall be in a form approved by the city attorney for a term approved by the director of the department of finance. The director may, with the approval of the council by resolution, require a bond in a greater amount than $ 50,000.00 if necessary in the judgement of the director to protect the interests of the city, charitable organizations, and prize winners.

(Code 1956, § 14-64(b)(14))

laws.title: Affirmative action
laws.content:
(a) If the cable television bingo operator is not a nonprofit organization licensed under this division, it shall establish and follow provisions for affirmative action by the cable television bingo operator for minorities, women, small businesses, and residents of the parish in employment, subcontracting, and ownership of the partnership or corporation. Such affirmative action plans shall establish goals and describe in detail the methods by which the goals are to be achieved. As a minimum, the following goals should be established:

(1) Ownership, 25 percent minorities, five percent women.

(2) Employment, 50 percent parish residents, 50 percent minorities, 50 percent women.

(3) The operator shall submit full information demonstrating the manner in which the services or purchases of minority business enterprises will be obtained to accomplish a minimum procurement level of at least 25 percent of the value of equipment, supplies, materials, and services purchased by the cable bingo operator and minimum of five percent of the value of equipment, supplies, materials, and services purchased by the cable bingo operator from businesses owned by women.

(b) For the purposes of this section, a minority person is any individual who is a citizen or lawful permanent resident of the United States and a member of one of the following groups:

(1) Black (a person having origin in any of the black racial groups of Africa);

(2) Hispanic (person of Spanish or Portuguese culture with origins in Mexico, South or Central America, or the Caribbean Islands, regardless of race);

(3) Asian American (a person having origins in any of the original peoples of the Far East, Southeast Asia, the Indian subcontinent or the Pacific Islands);

(4) American Indian and Alaska Native (a person having origins in any of the original people of North America).

(c) For the purposes of this section, a minority business enterprise is a person or business, whether it is company or a corporation, at least 51 percent of which is owned and controlled by one or more minority persons.

(d) For the purposes of this section, a business owned by women means a business that is at least 51 percent owned by a woman or women, which woman or women also control and operate such business. The term “control” in this context means being actively involved in the day-to-day management. In determining whether a business is 51 percent owned by a woman or women, the percentage of ownership of the woman or women shall not be diminished because any such woman de-

CD42:16

§ 42-226

rives her ownership interest through the community property regime, provided that any such woman is the sole manager of the community enterprise or business.

(Code 1956, § 14-64(b)(16))

**Sec. 42-197. Grounds for revocation.**

The failure to comply with any provision of an operations and procedures manual approved in accordance with this division shall be grounds for the suspension or revocation of the cable television bingo operator’s license.

(Code 1956, § 14-64(c))

**Sec. 42-198. Investigation of applicants.**

The department of finance shall make or cause to be made an investigation of the qualifications of each applicant for a license under this division and the merits of the application, with due expedition after the filing of the application; and it shall determine whether or not the applicant is qualified to obtain a cable television bingo operator’s license. The applicant and all persons listed on the application must be of good moral character and have never been convicted of any felony or of a misdemeanor involving gambling or related offenses. Lack of good moral character or conviction of any felony or of a misdemeanor involving gambling or related offenses shall be cause for denial, suspension or revocation of a cable TV bingo operator’s license.

(Code 1956, § 14-76)

**Sec. 42-199. Display.**

All licenses under the provisions of this division shall be publicly displayed by the licensee at the place where any game of chance is conducted at all times during the conduct thereof, and shall be so placed as to be easily seen by the public and the authorized agents of the department of finance. Additionally, any charitable sales outlet or legally authorized representatives thereof shall publicly display a license, permit, or other official identification issued by the department of finance at any place where shares, tickets, or rights to participate in a charitable game of chance trans-

mitted by a cable television operator are sold or distributed.

(Code 1956, § 14-75)

**Sec. 42-200. Issuance, fee; renewal.**

Licenses, permits, or other official identification shall be issued under this division upon submission of an application in a form prescribed by the department, approval of the department of finance, and payment of a fee of $10.00 per license, permit, or other identification. Such licenses shall be renewable on March 31 of each year in accordance with renewal procedures prescribed by the department of finance.

(Code 1956, § 14-75)

**Sec. 42-201. Duration.**

A license issued pursuant to this division shall be valid for five years from the date of issuance.

(Code 1956, § 14-70)

**Sec. 42-202. Bingo fees.**

In addition to fee imposed by section 42-72 relative to the payment for a license to conduct bingo, keno, or other charitable games of chance, any cable television bingo operator shall pay an annual fee in the amount of $5,000.00 to the city.

(Code 1956, § 14-71(a))

**Sec. 42-203. Denial, suspension or revocation of license.**

The rules specified in article II of this chapter relative to the denial, suspension or revocation of charitable games of chance licenses shall govern the denial, suspension or revocation of cable television bingo operations licenses applied for or issued under this division, except as otherwise provided in this article.

(Code 1956, § 14-74)

**Secs. 42-204–42-225. Reserved.**

laws.title: Regulations
laws.content:
**Sec. 42-226. Private contractors.**

Notwithstanding any provision of this article to the contrary, a cable television bingo operator li-

CD42:17
$\S 42-226$

NEW ORLEANS CODE

censed to conduct cable television bingo may enter into a contract with a private contractor possessing demonstrated skills in the conduct and administration of charitable games of chance to provide for the operation and management of its games. Any such contract shall stipulate that payment to the contractor for professional services shall be in accordance with an estimated fee schedule based upon the number of cards sold and shall require the use of volunteer members of charitable organizations in the actual conduct of and assisting in the conduct of such games.

(Code 1956, § 14-67)

**Sec. 42-227. Necessary transmission equipment and services ownership exemption.**

The provisions of section 42-123, relative to the requirement for the ownership of equipment for the conduct of charitable games of chance, shall not be applicable to bona fide items and reasonable amounts of goods, wares and merchandise furnished or services rendered which are reasonably necessary to be purchased or furnished for the cable television transmission of charitable games of chance permitted by this article.

(Code 1956, § 14-82)

**Sec. 42-228. Charitable sales outlet purchases.**

No nonprofit charitable organization shall sell shares, tickets or right to participate in a charitable game of chance transmitted by a cable television bingo operator unless such shares, tickets or rights to participate in a charitable game of chance are sold by an authorized charitable sales outlet or a legally authorized representative thereto. Such charitable sales outlet shall possess, at the time of sale, a valid city license for the conduct of bingo, keno or other charitable game of chance as provided for in article II of this chapter.

(Code 1956, § 14-66)

**Sec. 42-229. Parading carnival krewes; charitable sales outlet licenses.**

(a) Notwithstanding any provision of this article to the contrary, a parading carnival krewe may obtain a valid city license for the conduct of bingo for the purposes specified in this section possessing an appropriate nonprofit designation issued by the Federal Internal Revenue Service. A license issued to a parading carnival krewe pursuant to this section shall allow the organization to sell shares, tickets, or rights to participate in a charitable game of chance transmitted by a cable television bingo operator but shall not permit the organization to conduct any other games of bingo, keno, or raffles.

(b) Proceeds derived by a parading carnival krewe from the sale of shares, tickets, or rights to participate in cable television bingo may be used for carnival parade staging costs but may not be used for costs associated with the staging of balls or the purchase of carnival throws or any other personal expense of the individual members of the parading carnival organization. All other provisions of this article applicable to city licenses for the conduct of bingo, keno, or other charitable games of chance or cable television bingo shall be applicable to an organization receiving a license pursuant to this section.

(c) For the purposes of this section, parading carnival krewes means those chartered bona fide, nonprofit organizations existing under the laws of the state that are domiciled in the parish and conducting lawfully permitted Mardi Gras parades pursuant to chapter 34 during the official Mardi Gras season.

(Code 1956, § 14-66.1)

*State law references—Definition, R.S. 33:4861.2(1); application for license, R.S. 33:4861.5.*

**Sec. 42-230. Channel use.**

All cablecasts of charitable games of chance by a cable television bingo operator pursuant to this article shall only be on a leased access channel and shall not be part of the organization broadcasting programs of the cable television franchise holder whose system is being used for broadcast of such charitable games of chance.

(Code 1956, § 14-69)

**Sec. 42-231. Frequency limits and game times.**

(a) No cable television bingo operator shall transmit charitable games of chance by means of a cable television channel on more than two days per week.

(b) No cable television bingo operator shall transmit by means of cable television channel more than 20 charitable games of chance per night.

(c) No cable television bingo operator shall transmit any charitable games of chance by means of a cable television channel prior to 10:30 p.m. (Code 1956, § 14-63)

laws.title: Operator restricted
laws.content:
All bingo, keno or other charitable games of chance transmitted by a licensed cable television bingo operator must be conducted and operated by a nonprofit partnership, corporation or other legal entity possessing a valid license for the conduct of such games as required by applicable state law. (Code 1956, § 14-63.1)

State law reference—Restrictions, R.S. 33:4861.21.

laws.title: Pot prize payments
laws.content: Pot prizes payable under this article shall be distributed to eligible winners on a weekly basis. (Code 1956, § 14-72)

laws.title: Reports by licensee; payment of fees
laws.content:
(a) Not later than 20 days after January 1, April 1, July 1 and October 1 of each year, each licensee under this article shall furnish to the department of finance a duly verified statement showing the amount of the gross receipts derived from activities licensed under this article for the quarter preceding the reporting dates established hereinabove. The reports shall specify the amounts charged for the use of television channels, or for any other purpose, the gross receipts of each and every game of chance, costs, utility charges, concession revenues and any other information deemed necessary by the department of finance. In addition, any fees payable shall be remitted to the department of finance with this report.

(b) Each licensee shall maintain and keep such books and records as may be necessary to substantiate the particulars of each such report. Reports furnished under this section shall be subject to the provisions of the Public Records Act.

(c) Each licensee shall maintain a bookkeeping system for the purpose of recording all receipts and expenditures in connection with the conduct of charitable games of chance and the disbursement of gross revenues derived therefrom. The books of account shall be kept up to date. Bookkeeping records, deposit books, savings account, passbooks, canceled checks, checkbooks, deposit slips and bank statements and all other records and books of account shall be available for examination by the department of finance or its representative at all reasonable times, and shall be maintained by the licensee from three years following the expiration of each year’s license. (Code 1956, § 14-78)

laws.title: Examination of books and records
laws.content:
(a) The department of finance or its authorized agents shall have power to examine or to cause to be examined the books and records of any person to whom a cable television bingo operator of charitable games of chance license is issued so far as such books or records may relate to any transaction connected with the holding and conducting of any game of chance under any such license, but any information received shall not be disclosed except as otherwise provided by this article or except so far as may be necessary for the purpose of administration, implementation and enforcement of the provisions of this article.

(b) Any person who shall make any false statement in any application for a license under this article, or shall fail to keep such books and records as shall fully and truly record all transactions connected with the operation of cable television bingo operations or the holding, operating or conducting of games of chance under any such license, or shall falsify or make any false entry in any books or records so far as they relate to any transaction connection with the ownership or operation of a cable television bingo operation or the holding, operating and conducting of any game of chance under any such license, or shall violate any of the provisions of this article or of any term of such license shall, in addition to suffering any other penalties which may be imposed, forfeit any license issued to it under this article and shall be

ineligible to apply for a license under this article for five years thereafter.

laws.title: Percentage of gross receipts
laws.content:
(a) Any cable television bingo operator and any charitable sales outlet shall remit the amount of $2\frac{1}{2}$ percent of all quarterly gross revenues from the sale only of shares, tickets, or rights to participate in cable television bingo games received by the cable television bingo operator and/or charitable sales outlets to the city for regulatory expenses and, if the operator is not a nonprofit entity, to the New Orleans Public Benefit Fund, 20 percent of all quarterly gross revenues from the sale only of shares, tickets, or rights to participate in cable television bingo games received by the cable television bingo operator and/or charitable sales outlets less and except the amount paid to the city for regulatory expenses and the amount paid or to be paid to other regulatory agencies including but not limited to the state police charitable gaming division for the quarter for regulation of cable television operations. The gross revenues of a combination of charitable sales outlets associated with any cable television bingo operator shall be combined for the purposes of determining gross revenues. Each charitable sales outlet shall remit an amount proportionate to the gross revenues derived by the individual charitable sales outlet as that amount relates to the total gross revenue of all charitable sales outlets associated with a cable television bingo operator.

(b) The $2\frac{1}{2}$ percent regulatory costs imposed by subsection (a) of this section shall not exceed $125,000.00 annually. The percentage imposed by subsection (a) of this section for the New Orleans Public Benefit Fund shall be deposited in a special fund which, pursuant to the provisions of section 6-215 of the charter, is hereby created and shall be known as “The New Orleans Public Benefit Fund” and such fund is established for the purpose of lessening the burdens of government on the city in planning, renovating, constructing, leasing, subleasing, managing and promoting such properties as may be owned, leased, subleased or controlled by the city for the benefit of the general public.

(c) The fund mentioned in this section is authorized to receive donations from private individuals, corporations and other institutions and entities in the private sector as well as grants from the state or from the federal government or any branch thereof. Upon the availability of grants designed for the purposes expressed herein, the city is authorized to make application for same and to take such other actions as may be necessary and appropriate to obtain such grant.

(1) The fund hereby created shall be administered by the director of the department of finance and shall be kept in an interest bearing account to the benefit of and to become a part of the fund.

(2) The fund shall be utilized to finance the operations and activities of a public benefit corporation created and chartered by the mayor pursuant to R.S. 41:1212(G) and (H), R.S. 41:1215(B) and R.S. 12:201–12:269, particularly R.S. 12:202.1(D) thereof, and which shall be known as New Orleans Public Benefit Corporation (NOPBC).

(3) The NOPBC shall annually submit a budget to the director of the department of finance setting forth its needs for the ensuing year at the same time as the various departments of the city. The initial budget, subject to the approval of the chief administrative officer, shall be exempted from the foregoing requirement.

(4) After the approval of the NOPBC budget by the chief administrative officer, the director of the department of finance shall be authorized to remit funds to NOPBC in accordance with the approved budget upon the warrant of the treasurer of NOPBC. Upon a need to amend the approved budget, such amendment shall be subject to the approval of the chief administrative officer.

(5) Such fund shall be subject to an annual audit by an independent certified accountant.

(Code 1956, § 14-71(b), (c))

§ 42-291

laws.title: Bingo lessor’s license; application procedures, requirements
laws.content:
An applicant granted a license pursuant to this section may allow the conduct of charitable raffles, bingo, keno, and pull tabs in a building as often as seven days per week notwithstanding the provisions of section 42-122. A bingo lessor’s license shall be subject to the following application procedures and the requirements contained in this article:

(1) An applicant applying for a bingo lessor’s license shall file with the department of finance a written application in the form provided by the department, duly executed and verified, which must include:

a. Proof of the applicant’s tax exempt status under section 501 C.(3), (4), (8), or (19) of the United States Internal Revenue Code.

b. The address of the premises to be offered for lease.

c. A copy of the applicant’s title to or lease for the property. If this applicant is leasing the premises from another person, the applicant’s lease must give the applicant complete control of the entire area where charitable games of chance are to be conducted, any area where any coin operated amusement or gambling devices are located, and any concession areas where food, drinks, or other refreshments are to be sold within the building or on the premises. The holder of a bingo lessor’s license must operate all charitable gaming areas and all concessions or coin-operated amusement or gambling devices on the premises and shall not lease, sublease, or assign the right to operate charitable gaming areas, coin-operated devices or concessions on the premises to any other person or entity; provided that the council, by motion, may approve the assignment of such rights to an entity related to the holder of the bingo lessor’s license. In addition to a copy of the applicant’s title to or lease for the property, the applicant shall provide copies of any and all other legal documents in connection with the sale or lease of the property including but not limited to, any counter letters, contracts or agreements with the owner, lessor, third party, real estate agents or brokers. If the property is leased by the applicant, no license pursuant to this article shall be issued to the applicant until the lease has been approved by resolution of the city council as to the amount paid to the lessor as compensation for the lease of the property. The director of the department of finance shall provide a report to the council concerning the terms and conditions of the applicant’s lease and may contract with a professional property appraiser, real estate consultant, or other appropriate parties to obtain recommendations as to whether or not the compensation paid for the lease of the property and the terms and conditions of the lease are fair and equitable in terms of the local real estate market. Prior to consideration of a lease agreement under this subsection, the council may provide for a hearing on the matter by a hearing examiner, a council committee, or a panel which may be composed of representatives of the council staff, administrative office, department

CD42:21
$\S$ 42-291

NEW ORLEANS CODE

of property management, or other departments and agencies of the city as deemed appropriate by the council.

d. A duly executed affidavit by the applicant or its authorized representative, attesting to the fact that the applicant is familiar with and shall comply with all ordinances of the city pertaining to charitable games of chance as authorized by this chapter, additionally, the applicant shall provide any other documents in connection with the transaction requested by the director of the department of finance and, that neither the applicant nor any agent, employee or member of the applicant organization has given or received or will give or receive any compensation, commission, payment or any other thing of value in connection with the granting of a license hereunder; the purchase or lease of a leased bingo hall facility or the subleasing of its leased bingo hall facility to any person licensed by the city to conduct charitable games of chance.

e. A complete list of all equipment, including make and model number, to be made available for use by leasing organizations.

f. Proof of approved zoning for the use of the building as a leased bingo hall facility; provided that the director of the department of finance may consider an application for a bingo lessor’s license concurrently with consideration of the zoning status by the city planning commission, the council, or the department of safety and permits.

g. The applicant shall provide a copy of its most recent federal income tax return.

(2) Bingo lessors shall provide a sufficient number of flashboards and monitors to ensure that all players may observe monitors and flashboards from available seating.

(3) There shall be available at least one camera from which players may observe bingo balls removed from the blower and one camera from which at least one winning card shall be displayed for each bingo game of the session.

(4) Bingo lessors who obtain a license must lease the authorized premises to a licensed organization for the conduct of games of chance within 90 days of the issuance of the lessor’s license. Failure to comply shall be grounds for the suspension or revocation of the bingo lessor’s license.

(5) Bingo lessor licenses shall remain at all times the property of the city. Licenses shall not be transferable and shall have no other value other than for their intended use.

(6) A bingo lessor’s license which has already been issued may be renewed for a subsequent year by the timely submission within 15 days after the end of the current permit year of the required renewal fee and a renewal application in a form prescribed by the department of finance.

(Code 1956, § 14-90)

laws.title: License and administrative fees
laws.content:
(a) A license and administrative fee shall accompany each license application under this division according to the following schedule:

(1) Bingo lessor’s license . . . . . . . . . . . . $1,000.00

(2) Renewal fee . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . 1,000.00

The bingo lessor’s license fee shall be reduced by the amount paid by the applicant for city planning commission processing fees.

(b) Applications for new licenses shall be subject to the following pro rata license and administrative fees:

(1) Applications received between July 1 and December 31, full annual fee.

(2) Applications received between January 1 and June 30, one-half the annual fee.

(c) A bingo lessor’s license is valid from July 1 to June 30 of each year and payment is due by July 1 for the current year.

(Code 1956, § 14-91)

laws.title: License to be displayed
laws.content:
Any license issued to a bingo lessor shall be conspicuously displayed at the location where licensed games of chance are held.

(Code 1956, § 14-92(b))

laws.title: Schedule to be displayed
laws.content:
A schedule containing the name of each organization licensed under this division, its license number, and the day of the week and the beginning and ending hours of the organization’s games shall be maintained and displayed at every leased bingo facility.

(Code 1956, § 14-92(c))

laws.title: Revocation of license—Grounds, authorized
laws.content:
(a) Any person who shall make any false statement in any application for a license under this division, or shall fail to keep such books and records and shall fully and truly record all transactions connected with the holding, operating or conducting of games of chance under any such license, or shall falsify or make any false entry in any books or records so far as they relate to any transaction connected with the holding, operating and conducting of any game of chance under any such license, or shall fail to submit in a timely manner any reports required under the provisions of this article, or conduct any game of chance not authorized by this article, or shall violate any of the provisions of this article, or any term of such license, shall in addition to suffering any other penalties which may be imposed by law, forfeit his current license upon a determination to revoke the same, and shall be ineligible to apply for a license under this division for one year after the date of such revocation.

(b) No license shall be issued to any applicant for the use of the same physical location or premises whereon the license of the previous licensee has been revoked for six months after the date of such revocation.

(c) Notwithstanding any provision of this section to the contrary, a violation of this article committed during the term of a previous license shall also constitute cause or grounds for revocation of a current license held under this division.

(Code 1956, § 14-94)

laws.title: Prohibited acts and grounds for denial, suspension or revocation of bingo lessor’s license
laws.content:
(a) No bingo lessor, member, employee, proprietor or agent of any such lessor or the spouse of any of the above, shall accept any form of com-

$\S 42-326$

NEW ORLEANS CODE

pensation, either directly or indirectly, derived from the operation of games of chance on the leased premises, except for those items of expense pertaining to rent and cleanup as authorized by this article and those funds derived from the sale of concessions by the lessor.

(b) Bingo lessors and members of bingo lessors, their spouses or immediate families, employees or agents, shall not act as chairpersons or operators; prepare or file any game reports or quarterly reports; or assist in the counting or reconciliation of moneys obtained from the operation of any games of chance for any organization which leases premises for the conduct of games of chance from the bingo lessor. This section does not preclude any member of a bingo lessor from performing any of these functions in connection with that bingo lessor’s own games; nor does it preclude any bona fide active member of any organization from assisting in the conduct of that organization’s games of chance in any manner not specifically prohibited by this article.

(c) Bingo lessors shall not offer their premises for lease or rental for any time period less than four hours for the conduct of games of chance, nor shall they permit the conduct of any games of chance on their premises prior to or after the times stated on the license of any organization leasing the premises.

(d) Bingo lessors, their agents or any of their members, shall not sell any material, equipment or supplies for the operation of any licensed game of chance, nor shall they allow the sale or storage for sale of such material on the premises leased for the conduct of games of chance. Lessors may allow the storage on their premises of gaming supplies owned by the lessor or by the organizations conducting games of chance therein.

(e) No video poker machines shall be permitted on the premises.

(f) No bingo lessor shall allow the holding, operating, or conducting of any game of chance by any organization which does not hold a valid license for the conduct of charitable games of chance issued by the city and the state.

(g) Violations of any of the regulations in this section and sections 42-293, 42-294, 42-327 and 42-328 by a bingo lessor shall be grounds for the denial, suspension or revocation of the bingo lessor’s license. Violations of any of the regulations in this section and sections 42-293, 42-294, 42-327 and 42-328 by a bingo lessor shall be grounds for the denial, suspension or revocation of the bingo lessor’s license to conduct games of chance.

(Code 1956, § 14-92(a), (d)–(i))

laws.title: Improper compensation
laws.content:
It shall be unlawful for the applicant or any member or employee of the applicant to receive any compensation, commission, payment, or any other thing of value in connection with the purchase or lease of a leased bingo hall facility licensed in accordance with this article. It shall be unlawful for any person to pay any fee, commission, compensation, or to give anything of value to a bingo lessor or to any agent, member or employee of a bingo lessor in connection with the sale or lease of property to a bingo lessor. In addition to any criminal penalties which may be imposed for a violation of this section, a violation of this section shall constitute grounds for suspension or revocation of a bingo lessor’s license.

(Code 1956, § 14-92(k))

laws.title: Right of entry

Each bingo lessor shall allow the department of finance, or its designated agents, to have access to any premises where a game of chance is being conducted and to any book record, or document relating to such conduct.

Approval of endorsement resolution
laws.content:
Any endorsement resolution introduced before the city council shall include the terms and conditions of the enterprise zone program as established under state law with respect to the hiring of qualified employees and shall establish compliance with and verification of those terms and conditions by the mayor’s office of economic development or its successor as a requirement for the city sales tax exemption effected through the issuance of sales tax rebates under the program.

laws.title: Failure to comply
laws.content:
The sales tax rebate application shall be rejected if the applicant fails to comply with established procedures for the filing of the sales tax rebate application or is determined by the mayor's office of business and development and the department of law to be materially out of compliance with the terms and conditions of the contract executed under section 46-88. The department of finance shall not issue a sales tax rebate until all of the business documents are in compliance with such terms and conditions. A rejected application shall be returned to the applicant with a statement of the reasons for its rejection. The application may be resubmitted at any time subject to remediation of the stated deficiencies. The mayor's office of economic development is further empowered to terminate the contract upon noncompliance and the department of finance under authority granted in article III of chapter 150 shall seek recovery of any and all sales tax previously rebated under the contract in that event. A reduction in actual or proposed workforce due to economic conditions may be considered as a mitigating circumstance in any contract compliance review.

(Code 1956, § 2-814)

laws.title: Issuance of municipal identification cards
laws.content:
(1) The administering agency shall be the agency designated by the mayor to administer the Municipal Identification Card Program consistent with the provisions of this chapter.

(2) All city departments shall accept a municipal identification card as valid identification and as valid proof of residency in the city, unless the department or entity has reasonable grounds for determining that the card is counterfeit or altered, or that the individual presenting the card is not the individual to whom it was issued.

(3) The Municipal Identification Card Program shall provide for a system whereby a municipal identification card shall be issued to any resident who meets the application requirements set forth in this chapter and in accordance with rules promulgated by the administering agency pursuant to section 2-1000, consistent with the following:

(a) The card, shall display, at minimum, the cardholder's photograph, legal name, date of birth, date issued, expiration date, identification card number, and the seal of the city.

At the cardholder's discretion, the card may display the cardholder's address, self-designated gender or name, or disability.

(b) The card shall be designed and produced in such a manner as to deter fraud.

(c) The card shall be valid for a maximum of six years from the date of issuance for adults aged 18 and over and a maximum of three years for minors aged 10—17, or when the cardholder is no longer a resident of the city.

(4) A municipal identification card shall be available to any applicant regardless of race, color, sex, gender identity, age, religion, disability, national origin, ancestry, sexual orienta-

**Sec. 46-92. Confidentiality of municipal identification card application information.**

(1) The city shall not retain originals or copies of records and any documents provided by an applicant to prove identity or residency for a municipal identification card.

(2) The city shall not disclose information collected about applicants, and shall treat that information as confidential, to the maximum extent permitted by applicable laws.

(3) The city is prohibited from soliciting, collecting, maintaining, disseminating, or requiring that an applicant produce any information or documentation other than that required to establish that applicant's identity or residency pursuant to this chapter.

(4) The city shall provide applicants with the option to opt in for the city to retain demographic information or record of the applicant's municipal identification card for the purpose of reproducing a replacement card.

(5) The city shall provide an option for victims or survivors of domestic violence, sexual assault, or human trafficking, or individuals who are currently unhoused to designate an alternative address, and alternative methods by which individuals can establish residency notwithstanding the lack of fixed address.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 30127, § 1, 11-7-24, eff. 12-31-24)

laws.title: Municipal court judicial fund
laws.content:
The municipal court judicial fund is hereby established and shall be administered by the municipal court judges of the city. The fund shall receive payment from bond forfeitures in connection with the administration of the municipal court or in other manners provided by law. laws.content:
The clerk of the municipal court shall be appointed by the judges and shall serve at their

pleasure. He shall be amenable to their orders and instructions at all times. The clerk shall furnish a surety bond in the sum of $10,000.00, payable to the treasurer of the city. The premiums for such bond shall be paid by the city.

(Code 1956, § 40-5)

*State law reference—Similar provisions, R.S. 13:2495.*

**Sec. 50-40. Duties of clerk.**

The clerk of municipal court shall have general supervision of the deputy clerks and records of the several courts. He shall also receive and keep all papers, exhibits and affidavits, number them according to the date of their filing and enter them in a docket containing an index in the manner set forth in this section. He shall make a filing entry into the police department computer records showing the current and final disposition of all municipal court cases.

(Code 1956, § 40-6)

*State law reference—Similar provisions, R.S. 13:2495(B).*

**Sec. 50-41. Designation of acting clerk.**

When the clerk of the municipal court is absent or unable to perform his duties for any valid reason or on vacation, his chief deputy shall act in his stead. If both the clerk and his chief deputy are absent, the judges sitting en banc shall designate one of the deputies to act in their stead.

(Code 1956, § 40-7)

*State law reference—Appointment of deputies, R.S. 13:2497.*

**Sec. 50-42. Assignment of police officers; additional process servers.**

The superintendent of police shall detail police officers in each section of the municipal court to keep order and execute the orders and decrees of the judges and to make service of process and the judges of the municipal court sitting en banc may appoint additional persons to serve process of court; provided, that such process servers shall be duly sworn and a record of their appointment shall be entered upon the minutes of the court or be otherwise placed of record therein.

(Code 1956, § 40-8)

*State law reference—Police detail, R.S. 13:2499.*

**Sec. 50-43. Daily allotment of cases.**

All cases in the municipal court, except those which have been especially allotted by the judge as set forth in this chapter, shall be daily allotted as provided by the rules of the municipal court.

(Code 1956, § 40-11)

**Sec. 50-44. Rules to fix hours of sitting.**

The hours during which the four sections of the municipal court shall sit are as fixed by the rules of the municipal court.

(Code 1956, § 40-12)

*State law reference—Authorizing the adoption of rules and regulations, R.S. 13:2494.*

**Sec. 50-45. One judge may sit for or assist another.**

The judge of one section of the court may sit for the judge of another section in his place and stead or to assist as judge of another section by agreement of both judges, as provided by the rules of the municipal court.

(Code 1956, § 40-13)

*State law reference—Similar provisions, R.S. 13:2492(E).*

**Sec. 50-46. Only lawyers to appear as counsel.**

Only attorneys-at-law shall appear as counsel for any accused person.

(Code 1956, § 40-29)

*State law references—Right to counsel, C.Cr.P. art. 511 et seq.; contract for fee, R.S. 37:218.*

**Sec. 50-47. No solicitation for lawyers.**

No person shall solicit, with or without consideration, the employment of any lawyer to represent an accused in any of the municipal courts.

(Code 1956, § 40-30)

*State law references—Right to counsel, C.Cr.P. art. 511 et seq.; contract for fee, R.S. 37:218.*

**Sec. 50-48. Only lawyers to receive remuneration for service rendered accused.**

No person except an attorney-at-law shall receive any remuneration for any service rendered any accused in any municipal court in connection

laws.title: All prosecutions to be by affidavit
laws.content:
(a) All prosecutions in the municipal court and all prosecutions in the traffic court of the city shall be by affidavit or by bill of information.

(b) The superintendent of police, the deputy superintendent of police, police supervisors, assistant supervisors of police, police captains, police lieutenants, police sergeants, police desk sergeants, the city attorney, deputy city attorneys and assistant city attorneys shall have the power to take oaths and verify affidavits filed by other members of the police department. The chief of security, captains, lieutenants, sergeants, airport safety supervisors, and airport safety officer II’s of the Orleans Levee Board shall have the power to take oaths and verify affidavits filed by patrol officers or safety officers of the security department of airport safety section of the Orleans Levee Board. The director, the deputy director, bureau chiefs and environmental specialists II, III and IV of the department of health shall have the power to take oaths and verify affidavits filed by the other members of the department of health. The director, the deputy director, the secretary of the department, the chief building inspector and the zoning administrator of the department of safety and permits shall have the power to take oaths and verify affidavits filed by other members of the department of safety and permits. Housing authority project managers and housing authority administrative assistants shall have the power to take oaths and verify affidavits filed by other members of the housing authority of the city. The director, the deputy director and the chief building inspector of the

Vieux Carré Commission shall have the power to take oaths and verify affidavits filed by other members of the Vieux Carré Commission. The director and the deputy director of the historic districts and landmarks commission shall have the power to take oaths and verify affidavits filed by other members of the historic districts and landmarks commission. The director, the deputy director, and the secretary of the department of utilities shall have the power to take oaths and verify affidavits filed by other members of the department of utilities.

(c) The criminal sheriff, his chiefs, captains, lieutenants and sergeants shall have the power to take oaths and verify affidavits made by the appointed deputies of the criminal sheriff for offenses committed in their presence.

(d) The director, chief of staff, division heads, the public parking administrator, administrative analyst assistants I, II, and III, administrative service supervisors, and parking control supervisor I and II of the department of public works shall have the power to take oaths and verify affidavits made by parking control officers of the department of public works. The director, chief of staff, division heads, stormwater manager, environmental affairs administrator, inspectors, engineering intern I, engineering intern II, engineer, senior engineer, principal engineer of the department of public works shall have the power to take oaths and verify affidavits made by certified green infrastructure professional employees of the department of public works. The director, chief of staff, and division heads of the department of public works and the ground transportation bureau supervisor shall have the power to take oaths and verify affidavits made by employees of the ground transportation bureau.

(e) The superintendent of fire, assistant superintendent of fire, the secretary of fire, the city fire marshal, assistant fire marshal and senior fire prevention inspectors of the fire department shall have the power to take oaths and verify affidavits filed by other members of the fire prevention division of the fire department.

(f) The parish school board truancy center leader for each truancy center shall have the power to take oaths and verify affidavits made by truancy center social workers in connection with violations of sections relative to truancy.

laws.title: What docket to show; papers to be kept two years
laws.content:
The docket shall show the disposition made of each case, and no papers, exhibits and affidavits shall be destroyed, mutilated or otherwise disposed of until two years after the final disposition of the case by the municipal court or by the appellate court, if there has been an appeal.

(Code 1956, § 40-16)

*State law reference—Similar provisions, R.S. 44:9, 44:36.*

laws.title: Powers of judges
laws.content:
(a) The judges of the municipal court and their clerks and court reporters may administer oaths, and the judges may compel witnesses to appear and testify.

(b) The court shall possess inherently all powers necessary for exercise of its jurisdiction and the enforcement of its lawful orders including the authority to issue such writs and orders as may become necessary and the court has the power to punish for contempt, as provided in the Criminal Code of Procedure, Articles 20 through 25 as the same may from time to time be amended, which articles define contempt and prescribe the penalties therefor.

(Code 1956, § 40-17)

*State law reference—Similar provisions, R.S. 13:2500.*

laws.title: Peace bonds—Authority to issue
laws.content:
Each of the judges may require bonds to keep the peace in matters to which their jurisdiction extends, as provided by law.

(Code 1956, § 40-18)

*State law reference—Peace bonds, C.Cr.P. arts. 26—33.*

§ 50-91

NEW ORLEANS CODE

**Sec. 50-91. Same—Procedure generally.**

Any judge, in all cases in which it shall appear to him, by oath that:

(1) A breach of the peace has been committed;

(2) There is a just cause to apprehend that a breach of the peace is intended; or

(3) There is just cause to violate a law or city ordinance;

may cause the party charged with such breach of the peace or intent to breach the peace or violate some law or city ordinance to be brought before him and direct such party to give such security as the judge may deem reasonable to keep the peace of the city, and to answer to the offense, if any has been committed. In case of refusal to give such security to keep the peace the judge may inflict a fine of not less than $10.00 nor more than $300.00 or imprisonment for not exceeding 30 days, or both, at the discretion of the judge.

(Code 1956, § 40-19)

*State law reference—Peace bonds, C.Cr.P. arts. 26—33.*

**Sec. 50-92. Same—Maximum amount in case of threat of bodily harm.**

The judge may place all persons who threaten to do bodily harm to another under peace bonds, in an amount within the discretion of the judge, but in no case in excess of $2,500.00.

(Code 1956, § 40-20)

*State law reference—Peace bonds, C.Cr.P. arts. 26—33.*

**Sec. 50-93. Cash bond in lieu of other type specified.**

In any case in which the type of bond has been designated by the judge to be a personal surety bond, a bond of a personal surety owning real estate or a surety company bond, the accused shall have the right in lieu of furnishing any of such bonds to deposit with the clerk of court the amount of such bond in cash or to give a certified check drawn on a bank in the city for the amount of such bond, payable to the clerk of the municipal court.

(Code 1956, § 40-21)

*State law reference—Cash deposits, C.Cr.P. art. 324.*

**Sec. 50-94. Disposition of cash bond and cash deposited therewith.**

When a cash bond is made with the clerk of a section of the municipal court, the bond itself and the cash received shall be turned over by such clerk to the clerk of the municipal court or a deputy duly authorized by him to handle cash bonds. The clerk of the municipal court, or the deputy authorized by him to handle such bonds shall, no later than the next business day following the date on which such cash is received by him, deposit it in a checking account carried with a bank in the city, denominated "Bank Account, Municipal Court of New Orleans." Checks for withdrawals shall be signed by the clerk of the municipal court and countersigned by the judge of the section having jurisdiction of the case.

(Code 1956, § 40-22)

*State law reference—Cash deposits, C.Cr.P. art. 324.*

**Sec. 50-95. Refund of cash bond.**

Cash bond shall only be refunded to the remitter of the cash bond, or to a person who produces the original receipt. The refund check must be made payable to the remitter of the cash bond.

(Code 1956, § 40-23; M.C.S., Ord. No. 27888, § 1, 10-4-18)

*State law reference—Cash deposits, C.Cr.P. art. 324.*

**Sec. 50-96. Record of cash bonds; appropriations.**

(a) The clerk of the municipal court shall keep a complete record of all cash bonds, which shall consist primarily of a daily cash book, showing all receipts and disbursements, with a special card or ledger sheet for each cash bond and a control account, which will show from day to day the total amount of cash on deposit in the checking account, check book, stubs, bank statement and cancelled checks.

(b) The city shall appropriate sufficient moneys to cover all expenses for the operation of such system, including bank charges.

(Code 1956, § 40-24)

*State law reference—Cash deposits, C.Cr.P. art. 324.*

**Sec. 50-97. Receipt for cash bond.**

A receipt shall be given every accused for every cash or certified check bond furnished which shall show the date and number of the affidavit, the amount and nature of such bond and the date on which it was received.

(Code 1956, § 40-25)

*State law reference—Cash deposits, C.Cr.P. art. 324.*

**Sec. 50-98. Forfeiture of bond; domicile deemed at last address.**

The domicile of the accused for all intents and purposes shall be the last address furnished by him. Should the accused fail to appear for trial after having been notified at that address, according to law, any cash bail bond or certified check given as a bond, as set forth in this article may be decreed forfeited by the judge having jurisdiction, without further notice, and the notice of such forfeiture shall be given the treasurer of the city. Decrees of forfeiture shall be entered on the record and spread on the minutes of the court.

(Code 1956, § 40-26)

*State law reference—Cash deposits, C.Cr.P. art. 324.*

**Sec. 50-99. Remittance of forfeited cash bond to municipal court judicial fund.**

After the expiration of two days after the entrance of a decree of forfeiture of a cash bond, the clerk of the municipal court shall remit the amount of the forfeited bond to the municipal court judicial fund and this remittance must be made not later than the fourth business day after the judgment of forfeiture has been entered.

(Code 1956, § 40-27)

*State law reference—Cash deposits, C.Cr.P. art. 324.*

**Sec. 50-100. Disposition when accused fails to collect cash bond.**

If an accused has failed to collect a cash bond made by him for a period of one year following the date of the final disposition of his case, the amount of such bond shall be remitted to the municipal court judicial fund.

(Code 1956, § 40-28)

*State law reference—Cash deposits, C.Cr.P. art. 324.*

**Sec. 50-101. Procedure for obtaining refund.**

No remittitur, refund or return shall be made or approved by the city or the department of finance thereof, of any money paid to the city arising from a bail bond forfeiture in the criminal district court for the parish, or in the municipal court of the city, unless the following procedure has been complied with:

(1) That proper proof has been submitted to the department of finance, on a form furnished by the department of finance, that the defendant who was the subject of the bail bond forfeiture has been returned to the custody of the criminal sheriff of the parish prison, or to the police department of the city, whichever is applicable; and in addition;

(2) That the governor of the state or his properly designated representative has issued a lawful pardon to the claimant and surety involved remitting the forfeiture of the bail bond theretofore forfeited;

(3) That the claimant has filed his application for remittitur within a year of the judgment of forfeiture;

(4) That applicant’s claim for bail bond remittitur is accompanied by a fee of $5.00, to be made payable to the city to cover administrative costs of processing the claim;

(5) That the surety involved has not collected all or any part of the forfeiture involved from any third party under any contract of indemnification between such surety and such third party. Applicant shall further state whether any fee has been charged in connection with the furnishing of the bond and the amount thereof;

(6) Upon the proper completion of the above requirements under oath, the applicant shall be entitled to the remittitur and refund request; provided, that where the applicant has had all or part of the bail bond forfeited repaid to him by a third

laws.title: Imposition, collection, and disposition of fines
laws.content:
(a) The power to impose a fine or penalty upon conviction in municipal court belongs exclusively to the municipal court judges.

(b) No fine shall be imposed by a municipal court judge without first conducting an assessment of the defendant’s ability to pay. Any fines imposed, unless otherwise required by law, shall be commensurate with the findings of such assessment.

(c) Where a defendant is found to be indigent, non-financial alternative sanctions shall be considered. If the court determines a fine or restitution to be the appropriate and adequate penalty for a crime, it may not thereafter imprison a person solely because he or she lacks the resources to pay it.

(d) All fines, penalties, or forfeitures imposed by the judges of the municipal court shall be collected by them or their clerk and by them paid daily to the city treasurer. No person, except the judge or his clerk, shall be allowed to receive any payment of a fine or penalty or give a receipt therefor.

(Code 1956, § 40-34; M.C.S., Ord. No. 28217, § 1, 10-17-19)

State law reference—Fines imposed remitted to city treasurer, R.S. 13:2501.

laws.title: Remission of fines

(Code 1956, § 40-36)  
*State law reference—Fines imposed remitted to city treasurer, R.S. 13:2501.*

**Sec. 50-107. Suspension of sentence; effect of subsequent conviction.**

Upon trial and conviction before the municipal court, the judge in his discretion may after the imposition of a sentence suspend all or any part of such sentence and the judge may, even after the sentence has begun to run, change, modify or cancel the unserved time or remit the fine, or part thereof, if he believes the defendant is entitled to such change, modification or cancellation. If during the period for which a sentence has been suspended, the defendant is found guilty of another offense in the same or another section of the municipal court, the judge who has tried him on the second offense may reinstate the sentence which was suspended in the first instance in addition to the imposing of the sentence for the second offense.  
(Code 1956, § 40-37)  
*State law reference—Similar provisions, C.Cr.P. art. 894, R.S. 13:2519.*

**ARTICLE IV. APPEALS**

**Sec. 50-141. To criminal district court.**

All appeals from the municipal court involving municipal ordinances shall be to the criminal district court for the parish, on the law and the facts, and shall be tried upon the records made and the evidence offered in the municipal court by the judge to whom the appeal shall be allotted, as provided by law. Such appeals shall be returnable to the criminal district court within not less than 15 days and no more than 30 days

unless an extension be granted by the criminal district court. If state law is at issue, an application to the 4th Circuit Court of Appeal is the proper remedy.  
(Code 1956, § 40-38)  
*State law reference—Similar provisions, R.S. 13:2498.*

**Sec. 50-142. Extension of time to complete record.**

The appellant shall obtain any and all extensions of time from the criminal district court when for any reason the record is not completed within the appeal period. The failure of the appellant to obtain such an extension shall operate as a dismissal of the appeal.  
(Code 1956, § 40-39)  
*State law reference—Extension of time for appeal, R.S. 13:2498(C).*

**Sec. 50-143. Payment of cost of record prerequisite to appeal.**

Any person against whom judgment has been rendered in any proceeding in the municipal court and who desires to appeal therefrom to the criminal court for the parish or to the supreme court of this state shall pay to the clerk of the municipal court contemporaneously with the filing of the motion of appeal the sum of $100.00, in cash, to defray the cost of preparing the record and transcribing the evidence. The motion of appeal shall not be signed by the judge until due proof shall have been furnished him of the payment of these costs. In addition to the $100.00 deposit required in this section the appellant shall pay to the clerk of the municipal court $2.00 per page for each page in the record and transcript.  
(Code 1956, § 40-40)

**Sec. 50-144. Bill for costs and effect of failure to pay within five days.**

The appellant or his attorney shall be sent a notice through the United States mail by the clerk of the municipal court to the effect that the record has been completed and enclosing a bill for the amount of cost due. The failure of the defendant to pay these costs within five judicial days from the mailing of such notice and bill
