laws.title: Civil remedies
laws.content:
Affirmative action ordered under this section may include but is not limited to:

(1) Hiring, reinstatement, or upgrading of employees with or without back pay. Interim earnings or amounts earnable with reasonable diligence by the person or persons discriminated against shall operate to reduce the back pay otherwise allowable.

(2) Admission or restoration of individuals to union membership, admission to or participation in a guidance program, apprenticeship training program, on-the-job training program, or other occupational training or retraining program, and the utilization of objective criteria in the admission of individuals to such programs.

(3) Admission of individuals to a place of public accommodation, resort, or amusement.

(4) The extension to all individuals of the full and equal enjoyment of the advantages, facilities, privileges, and services of the respondent.

(5) Reporting as to the manner of compliance.

(6) Posting notices in conspicuous places in the respondent’s place of business in a form prescribed by the commission.

(7) Sale, exchange, lease, rental, assignment, or sublease of immovable property to an individual.

(8) Payment to the complainant of damages for injury caused by an unlawful practice, including compensation for humiliation and embarrassment, expenses incurred by the complainant in obtaining alternative housing accommodations, and other costs actually incurred by the complainant as a direct result of such unlawful practice.

(9) The commission may publish or cause to be published the names of persons who have been determined to have engaged in an unlawful practice.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 19,278, § 1, 6-17-99)

laws.title: Judicial review and enforcement
laws.content:
(a) At any time after the filing of a complaint alleging an unlawful discriminatory practice under this chapter, if the commission determines that the respondent is doing or procuring to be done any act tending to render ineffectual any order the commission has entered or may thereafter enter in such proceeding, the commission may authorize the department of law to file a complaint for enforcement of the commission’s order. The proceeding for enforcement of a commission order shall be initiated by filing a complaint in the Civil District Court of the Parish of Orleans. Copies of the complaint shall be served upon all parties of record. Within 30 days after the filing of the complaint by the commission, or within such further time as the court may allow, the commission shall transmit to the court the original or a certified copy of the entire record upon which the order is based, including a transcript of testimony, which need not be printed. By stipulation of all parties to the proceeding, the record may be shortened.

(b) The findings of fact of the commission shall be conclusive unless manifestly erroneous in view of the probative and substantive evidence on the whole record. The court may grant such temporary relief or restraining order as it deems just and may enter an order enforcing, modifying, and enforcing as modified, or setting aside in whole or in part the order of the commission, or remanding the case to the commission for further proceedings.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 19,278, § 1, 6-17-99)

laws.title: Exclusions
laws.content:
Nothing in this article shall be construed to:

(1) Restrict an employer’s right to require that an employee meet bona fide job-related qualifications of employment.

(2) Authorize or require employers to establish affirmative action quotas based on sexual orientation or gender identification.

(3) Apply to any business, trade or occupation employing fewer than eight employees, or to any unit in a residential structure containing not more than four units, if the owner maintains and occupies one of such units as his residence.

(4) Apply to any religious corporations, religious entity, religious association, or religious organization, or any religious nonprofit corporation, religious organization or religious group, including religious charitable organizations, with respect to the employment of individuals, or with respect to the employment policies, practices, and procedures established by any such religious corporation, religious entity, religious association, or religious society.

(5) Make lawful any act that violates the state criminal code.

(6) The provisions of this article shall not be read to limit or affect in any way rights and privileges existing under state or federal law, and the city explicitly disavows its rights to any period of exclusive jurisdiction over filed charges which may exist under state or federal law, including but not limited to U.S.C., Section 2000(e) et seq.

(7) Notwithstanding anything herein expressed to the contrary, nothing in this article shall be deemed or construed to authorize or encourage the promotion of any sexual orientation or gender identification in any public or private educational institution or school, or to require the teaching in any public or private educational institution of sexual orientation or gender identification. It is the intent of this chapter to assure the rights of the citizens of this city and all persons, particularly with respect to the securing of housing and employment; this article does not have for its purpose the establishment of any public policy regarding the acceptability or nonacceptability of any sexual practice.

(8) Nothing in this chapter shall prohibit an employer from prohibiting cross-dressing in the workplace or while an employee is acting in the course and scope of his or her employment. For purposes of this section, a person shall be deemed to be acting in the course and scope of his or her employment if he or she would be deemed to be in the scope and course of his employment for the purpose of determining eligibility for worker’s compensation. For purposes of this section, “cross-dressing” shall mean the wearing of clothing, cosmetics, footwear and/or other accouterments generally deemed or perceived as inappropriate to the gender that was one’s biological or legal gender at birth and/or generally deemed or perceived as more appropriate to the gender that was not one’s biological or legal gender at birth. “Cross-dressing” shall be deemed not to include the regular wearing of clothing, cosmetics, footwear and/or other accouterments which is appropriate to the gender other than his or her biological or legal gender at birth with which an employee or applicant identifies if the employee or applicant provides the employer with the written statement of a licensed doctor or other health care professional certifying that the employee or applicant presents the characteristics of gender identification disorder or another similar status or condition and that the employee or applicant intends prospectively to attire and conduct himself or herself for the foreseeable future in the employee’s employment and workplace or workplaces in the manner appropriate for persons of the gender with which he or she identifies.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 19,278, § 1, 6-17-99)

laws.title: Interference, coercion, or intimidation
laws.content:
(a) It shall be an unlawful practice for a person or for two or more persons to conspire:

(1) To coerce, intimidate, threaten, or interfere with any person in the exercise or enjoyment of, or on account of his having exercised or enjoyed, or on account of his having aided or encouraged any other person in the exercise or enjoyment of, any right granted or protected by this chapter.

(2) To publish, circulate, display, post or mail, either directly or indirectly, any written or printed, or electronic computer based communication, notice or advertisement which evidences an intent to violate directly or indirectly any of the provisions of this chapter.

(3) To aid, abet, incite, counsel or coerce the doing of any act therein declared to be unlawful or to prevent any person from complying with this section or any rule, regulation or order issued pursuant to this chapter.

(4) To retaliate or discriminate in any manner against a person because he has opposed a practice declared unlawful by this chapter, or because he has made a charge, filed a complaint, testified, assisted, or participated in any manner in any investigation, proceeding, or hearing under this chapter.

(5) To obstruct or prevent a person from complying with the provisions of this chapter or any order issued thereunder.

(b) Any person who shall willfully resist, prevent, impede or interfere with the commission or any of its agents or representatives in the performance of duty under this chapter, or shall willfully violate an order of the commission or any of its members or representatives in the performance of duty under this chapter, shall be guilty of a misdemeanor and shall be punished by imprisonment for not more than six months, or by a fine of not more than $500.00, or by both such imprisonment and such fine; provided that procedure for the review of the order shall not be deemed to be such willful conduct.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 19,278, § 1, 6-17-99)

laws.title: Enforcement and penalties
laws.content:
(a) Any violations of articles IV through VI shall, prior to the initiation of a prosecution in municipal court, be reported and processed in the manner specified within this chapter. If this chapter has no enforcement provisions, or they are ruled unconstitutional, then any violators of articles IV through VI shall be punishable in the same manner as specified in the municipal criminal code, and more particularly by sections 54-1 through 54-26 and 54-61, but in no event shall the minimum penalty for any violation of articles IV through VI be less than that specified in section 54-26 of the municipal criminal code.

(b) Unless it is expressly provided otherwise elsewhere in a particular section of this chapter, any person who does anything prohibited or fails to do anything required by this chapter shall be guilty of a misdemeanor and, upon conviction thereof, shall be sentenced to a term of imprisonment not to exceed six months, or to a fine not to exceed $500.00, or to both such imprisonment and such fine.

(c) Unless required to do so by applicable law or by the court, the city attorney shall not prosecute an offense under this section during the pendency under this chapter of civil proceedings concerning the same complainant and respondent and the same grievance before the human relations commission.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 19,278, § 1, 6-17-99)

laws.title: Unlawful practices; housing
laws.content:
(a) Subject to the provisions of subsection (b) of this section and section 86-27, exceptions, within the City of New Orleans, the prohibitions set forth in section 86-28 shall apply to:

(1) Dwellings owned or operated by the federal government, this state, or by any political subdivision of this state.

(2) Dwellings financed in whole or in part with the aid of loans, advances, grants, or contributions made by:

a. This state or any political subdivision of this state.

b. The federal government under agreements entered into after November 20, 1962, unless payment due thereon has been made in full prior to April 11, 1968.

(3) Dwellings provided in whole or in part by loans insured, guaranteed, or otherwise secured by the credit of the federal government under agreements entered into after November 20, 1962, unless payment thereon has been made in full prior to

April 11, 1968; provided that nothing contained in paragraphs (2) and (3) of this subsection shall be applicable to dwellings solely by virtue of the fact that they are subject to mortgages held by an institution insured by the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation.

(4) Dwellings provided by the development or the redevelopment of real property purchased, rented, or otherwise obtained from a state or local public agency receiving federal financial assistance for slum clearance or urban renewal with respect to such real property under loan or grant contracts entered into after November 20, 1962.

(5) All other dwellings except as exempted by subsection (b) of this section.

(b) Nothing in section 86-28, discrimination in sale or rental of housing and other prohibited practices, except paragraph (a)(3) thereof, shall apply to any of the following dwellings:

(1) Any single-family house sold or rented by an owner, provided that such private individual owner does not own more than three such single-family houses at any one time; provided further, that in the case of the sale of any such single-family house by a private individual owner not residing in such house at the time of such sale or who was not the most recent resident of such house prior to such sale, the exemption granted by this paragraph shall apply only with respect to one such sale within any twenty-four-month period; provided further, that such bona fide private individual owner does not own any interest in, nor is there owned or reserved on his behalf, under any express or voluntary agreement, title to or any right to all or a portion of the proceeds from the sale or rental of more than three such single-family houses at any one time; provided further that the sale or rental of any such single-family house shall be excepted from the application of this provision only if such house is sold or rented without the use in any manner of the

laws.title: Exceptions
laws.content:

laws.title: Discrimination in sale or rental of housing and other prohibited practices
laws.content:
(a) As made applicable by section 86-29, unlawful practices-housing, and except as exempted by subsection (b) thereof and 86-27, exceptions, it is unlawful:

(1) To refuse to sell or rent after the making of a bona fide offer, or to refuse to negotiate for the sale or rental of, or otherwise make unavailable or deny, a dwelling to any person because of race, creed, national origin or ancestry, color, religion, gender or sex, sexual orientation, gender identification, marital status, age, physical condition or disability.

(2) To discriminate against any person in the terms, conditions, or privileges of sale or rental of a dwelling, or in the provision of services or facilities in connection therewith, because of race, creed, national origin or ancestry, color, religion, gender or sex, sexual orientation, gender identification, marital status, age, physical condition or disability.

(3) To make, print, or publish, or cause to be made, printed, or published any notice, statement, or advertisement, with respect to the sale or rental of a dwelling that indicates any preference, limitation, or discrimination based on race, creed, national origin or ancestry, color, religion, gender or sex, sexual orientation, gender identification, marital status, age, physical condition or disability, or an intention to make any such preference, limitation, or discrimination.

(4) To represent to any person because of race, creed, national origin or ancestry, color, religion, gender or sex, sexual orientation, gender identification, marital status, age, physical condition or disability that any dwelling is not available for inspection, sale, or rental when such dwelling is in fact so available.

(5) For profit, to induce or attempt to induce any person to sell or rent any dwelling by representations regarding the entry or prospective entry into the neighborhood of a person or persons of a particular race, creed, national origin or ancestry, color, religion, gender or sex, sexual orientation, gender identification, marital status, age, physical condition or disability.

(6) a. To discriminate in the sale or rental, or to otherwise make unavailable or deny, a dwelling to any buyer or renter because of a handicap of:

    1. That buyer or renter;

    2. A person residing in or intending to reside in that dwelling after it is so sold, rented, or made available; or

    3. Any person associated with that buyer or renter.

b. To discriminate against any person in the terms, conditions, or privileges of sale or rental of a dwelling, or in the provision of services or facilities in connection with such dwelling, because of a handicap of:

    1. That person;

    2. A person residing in or intending to reside in that dwelling after it is so sold, rented, or made available; or

    3. Any person associated with that person.

c. For purposes of this paragraph, discrimination includes:

    1. A refusal to permit, at the expense of the handicapped person, reasonable modifications of existing premises occupied or to be occupied by such person if such modifications may be necessary to afford such person full enjoyment of the premises except that, in the case of a rental, the landlord may, where it is reasonable to do so, condition permission for a modification on the renter agreeing to restore the interior of the prem-

Prohibition of sexual harassment
laws.content:
It is unlawful to harass a person because of that person's sex. Sexual harassment is a form of discrimination under Title VII of the U.S. Civil Rights Act of 1964, as amended and the Louisiana Employment Discrimination Law, LA Rev. Stat. § 23:332 et seq. All persons have a right to work in an environment free form sexual harassment. The City of New Orleans prohibits harassment of any person by any municipal officer, agent, elected official, employee, municipal agency or department on the basis of sex or gender. While in the course and scope of employment, all municipal officers, agents, employees, elected officials, municipal agencies and departments are prohibited from sexually harassing any person, regardless of any employment relationship.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 27795, § 1, 6-7-18)

laws.title: Definitions and examples
laws.content:
(1) "Sexual harassment" is unwelcome sexual advances, requests for sexual favors, and other verbal or physical conduct of a sexual nature when:

a. Submission to such conduct is made either explicitly or implicitly or as a condition of an individual's employment;

b. Submission to or rejection of such conduct by an individual is used as the basis for employment decisions affecting the individual; or

c. Such conduct has the purpose or effect of unreasonably interfering with an individual's work performance or creating an intimidating, hostile, or offensive work environment. For purposes of this section, an intimidating, hostile, or offensive work environment exists when sexual harassment is so pervasive or severe that it creates an intimidating, offensive workplace and alters the conditions of employment.
§ 86-41

NEW ORLEANS CODE

(2) Examples of conduct and descriptions of behavior that may constitute sexual harassment include, but are not limited to:

a. **Verbal**: Sexual innuendos, suggestive comments, insults, humor and jokes about sex, anatomy or gender specific traits, sexual propositions, threats, repeated requests for dates, statements about other employees that are of a sexual nature, or quid pro quo offers wherein an employee is in a management or supervisory role and states or implies that an employee must consent to unwelcome sexual advances in exchange for some economic benefits such as promotions, merits, job offers, or job retention. Quid pro quo sexual harassment also occurs when rejection of sexual advances would result in adverse decisions affecting an employee’s job status (e.g., demotion, termination, denial of employment).

b. **Non-verbal**: Suggestive or insulting sounds (“catcalls” or “kissing” noises), leering, obscene gestures, and sexually suggestive body gestures.

c. **Visual**: Posters, signs, pin-ups or slogans of a sexual nature, viewing pornographic materials or websites.

d. **Physical**: Touching, unwelcome hugging or kissing, pinching, brushing the body, any coerced sexual act or actual assault;

e. **Text/electronic**: Electronically sending messages with sexual content, including pictures and video, the use of sexually explicit language, harassment, cyber stalking and threats via all forms of electronic communication (e-mail, text/picture/video messages, intranet/on-line postings, blogs, instant messages and social network websites).

(3) Although severe and overt forms of sexual harassment may be readily apparent, some sexual harassment is subtle and varies depending on interpretation and perception. Review of sexual harassment allegations are subject to the standard of what offends a “reasonable person.”

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 27795, § 1, 6-7-18)

**Sec. 86-42. Initiation procedures.**

(1) Employees, whether classified or unclassified, may report to his/her respective department’s human resources manager and/or appointing authority any allegations or complaints of sexual harassment. Reporting a harassment complaint or discussing a complaint with the human resources manager and/or appointing authority will result in an investigation. If the accused harasser is the human resources manager or the appointing authority for a given agency, the complaint shall be submitted to the asst. CAO of the personnel division. If the accused harasser is an elected official that is governed by this Code, the complaint shall be submitted to the New Orleans Inspector General.

(2) A sexual harassment complaint may be an oral complaint initially but must be followed by a sexual harassment or discrimination complaint form. The complaint should include the date(s) the incident(s) occurred, name(s) of the individual(s) involved, name(s) of witness(es), and a detailed description of the incident(s).

(3) When the employee completes the sexual harassment or discrimination complaint form, a human resources manager and/or appointing authority must sign the form. Only signatures from human resources manager and/or appointing authorities are to be entered on the sexual harassment or discrimination complaint form in the space designated for this purpose. In the event that the accused harasser is the human resources manager or the appointing authority for a given agency, the complaint should be signed by the asst. CAO of the personnel division.

(4) After an employee has signed the sexual harassment or discrimination complaint form, the original should be sent to the personnel division, chief administrative office. The sexual harassment or discrimination complaint form will become part of the complaining employee’s personnel file located in that department and the civil service department employee record.

(5) Employees also have the right to file a complaint with the equal employment opportunity commission (EEOC), the human relations com-
HUMAN RELATIONS

§ 86-44

mission or to pursue other legal action, in addition to their rights under this policy. The EEOC provides employees 300 days to file an official complaint.

(6) A supervisor, manager, or employee who ignores a request to cease harassing behavior or who engages in perpetuating sexual harassment in the agency, shall face disciplinary action. (M.C.S., Ord. No. 27795, § 1, 6-7-18)

laws.title: Resolution procedures
laws.content:
(1) If the investigation substantiates the complaint of harassment, the appointing authority shall make a determination regarding the appropriate resolution, including disciplinary action. Before making the decision to impose disciplinary action, the appointing authority shall ensure that the harasser has been given the opportunity to review the results of the investigation, has received an explanation of the evidence obtained, and been given an opportunity to provide the appointing authority a response regarding the findings. The appointing authority shall take the alleged harasser’s response into account before taking final action in determining if harassment occurred and in the resolution of the complaint.

(2) In addition to any disciplinary action taken, substantiated complaints shall be noted in the harasser’s official personnel file. If the harasser

Supp. No. 84

CD86:31
§ 86-44

NEW ORLEANS CODE

continues on as an employee, the disciplinary action shall be taken into consideration during the harasser's performance evaluation.

(3) If during the course of the investigation, the investigator determines that the allegation or complaint of sexual harassment was reported to either the human resources manager or appointing authority, and that individual failed to promptly report the allegation or complaint, then disciplinary action may be initiated against the human resources manager or appointing authority. A substantiated finding of failure to report an allegation or complaint of sexual harassment and resulting disciplinary action shall also be made a part of the human resources manager or appointing authority's official personnel file. (M.C.S., Ord. No. 27795, § 1, 6-7-18)

laws.title: Discipline
laws.content: In addition to any other discipline that may be applicable, including but not limited to the rules of the civil service commission, any person who violates sections 86-40, 86-43, or 86-46 as provided herein, may be subject to a fine of up to $500.00 per offense. Each violation may constitute a separate offense. Any discipline imposed by the city shall be separate and apart from any penalty imposed by any fines or penalties imposed by a court of law or a state or federal agency. (M.C.S., Ord. No. 27795, § 1, 6-7-18)

laws.title: Retaliation
laws.content: Retaliation against an employee who brings a complaint of harassment, reports an allegation of sexual harassment on behalf of another, or participates in an investigation of a harassment complaint is prohibited and may result in disciplinary action. Similarly, allegations or complaints of sexual harassment that have been determined to be fabricated, knowingly false, or otherwise baseless shall require the appointing authority to impose disciplinary action against the complainant found to have filed the improper complaint, as well as any other employees that participated in the false allegation or complaint. (M.C.S., Ord. No. 27795, § 1, 6-7-18)

laws.title: Sexual harassment training
laws.content:
(1) Each public employee shall receive a minimum of one hour of education and training on preventing sexual harassment during each full calendar year of his/her public employment or term of office.

(2) Appointing authorities or their designees shall make use of standardized education and training materials developed by the department of state civil service; additional materials may be approved by the CAO. The education or training required may be received in person or via the Internet.

(3) Appointing authorities or their designees shall require supervisors to receive additional education and training.

(4) Each public servant shall be notified of the mandatory training requirement. Appointing authorities or their designees shall be responsible for maintaining records of the compliance of each public servant in the agency with the mandatory training requirement. (M.C.S., Ord. No. 27795, § 1, 6-7-18)

laws.title: Ending domestic partnerships; notice of termination
laws.content:
(a) A domestic partnership ends when:

(1) The partners no longer meet one or more of the qualifications for domestic partnership;

(2) One partner sends the other a written notice that he or she has ended the partnership; or

(3) One of the partners dies.

(b) When a domestic partnership ends, the partners must execute a notice of termination naming the partners and stating that the partnership has ended (hereinafter notice of termination). The notice of termination must be dated and signed under penalty of perjury by at least one of the partners. The notice of termination must be notarized and filed with the clerk of council.

If that partner has died, the surviving partner must give the notice of termination to those third parties whom she or he knows were given a copy of the declaration by the deceased party in order to qualify for a benefit or right. laws.title: Definitions
laws.content:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this chapter, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning.

*City* shall mean the City of New Orleans, a political subdivision of the State of Louisiana.

*City of New Orleans Research and Technology Advisory Committee (NORTAC)* means the committee which will make recommendations to NOBC for the administration of this policy. This committee is responsible for making recommendations to NOBC for matters relating to intellectual properties, including requirements for disclosures relating to intellectual property which must be made to the city. This committee will consist of the chief administrative officer of the City of New Orleans, the executive director of the New Orleans Building Corporation, the director of the City of New Orleans Mosquito and Termite Control Board, the city attorney, and one or more directors of intellectual properties from local universities appointed by the mayor.

*City-supported invention* shall mean an invention created in whole or in part with city funds, on city time, or with city materials.

*Creator* shall mean a city employee who creates a work or invention.

*Development expenses* shall mean all moneys paid for goods and services to protect, develop, and/or enhance the marketability or any other aspect of an invention, including, but not limited to, patent filing fees, costs incurred in securing or protecting patent rights, marketing expenses, patent maintenance fees, consulting fees, prosecution expenses, expenses incurred in dealing with equity interests, travel, attorneys’ fees and research costs. Not included as developmental expenses are salaries and general operating expenses of city administrative personnel.

*Employee* means all full-time and part-time employees of the city, including all civil service and appointed employees.

*Gross revenue* shall mean:

(1) Proceeds from the exploitation or manufacture, sale, lease, transfer, or other conveyance of an invention by an owner thereof, and

(2) License fees, option fees, running royalties, and equity interests paid by a licensee for right to exploit an invention, except that equity interests, or any portion thereof, shall not be considered "gross revenue" unless and until the equity interests, or any portion thereof, are sold.

*Intellectual property* means any and all inventions, copyrightable works, and trademarks.

*Invention* means any discovery, invention, process, method, composition of matter, machine, article of manufacture, know-how, design, model, technological development, biological material, strain, variety, culture of any organism, or any improvement of these items.

*Net income* shall mean gross revenues less all development expenses for a work or invention and its improvements and/or production.

*New Orleans Building Corporation (NOBC)* means the public benefit corporation incorporated in the State of Louisiana to plan, develop, operate, manage and promote real and intellectual property owned by the city or NOBC. NOBC will be the managing agency to work with the creators of intellectual properties and the city to promote the development of intellectual properties by the employees and contractors of the city. Any or all rights to intellectual properties in which the city asserts its interest or acquires any interests to

Supp. No. 18

CD88:3
§ 88-2

NEW ORLEANS CODE

manufacture, distribute, license, assign, or otherwise use or transfer the intellectual property can be assigned to NOBC. NOBC and its subsidiaries will adhere to this policy in the distribution of proceeds from intellectual property. NOBC is authorized to and shall be responsible for publishing any and all forms or other documents required by this policy.

*Work* means any work of authorship protectable under copyright law.  
(Ord. No. 20,098, § 1, 4-5-01)

**Sec. 88-3. Applicability.**

(a) This policy applies to all employees. Employees receiving proceeds pursuant to this policy shall continue to do so after termination of employment. Upon the employee’s death, proceeds will revert to the employee’s heirs or legatees. If this substitution results in additional responsibility or expense to either the city or the employee’s heirs or legatees, adjustments of financial distributions will be agreed upon by both parties by mutual consent.

(b) The city may require any persons or businesses doing business with the city to adhere to this policy.  
(Ord. No. 20,098, § 1, 4-5-01)

**Sec. 88-4. Condition of employment.**

This policy, as amended from time to time, shall become a part of the conditions of employment of every employee, whether such employee was employed before or after its adoption.  
(Ord. No. 20,098, § 1, 4-5-01)

**Sec. 88-5. Existing intellectual property.**

This policy shall be applied to intellectual property created prior to the date of its adoption and to intellectual property created after the date of adoption.  
(Ord. No. 20,098, § 1, 4-5-01)

**Sec. 88-6. Disclosure.**

Every employee or person to whom this policy applies shall disclose to the city all city-supported inventions created by the employee or person.  
(Ord. No. 20,098, § 1, 4-5-01)

**Sec. 88-7. Relationships between employees and the city regarding business transactions.**

Employees are required to receive written permission from the city or NOBC or its subsidiaries before soliciting or participating in any business relating to any intellectual property subject to this policy. Each employee’s prospective interest or relationship to the business involved will be subject to review for compliance with the city code of ethics.  
(Ord. No. 20,098, § 1, 4-5-01)

**ARTICLE II. OWNERSHIP OF INVENTIONS AND COPYRIGHTABLE WORKS**

**Sec. 88-8. Inventions.**

Because significant city resources could lead to inventions, the city has an important interest in coordinating the activities of employees in this area. In recognition of this interest, and of the interests of the employees, the city will administer its rights to inventions in the manner described below.  
(Ord. No. 20,098, § 1, 4-5-01)

**Sec. 88-9. City of New Orleans’ rights to inventions.**

An invention shall be assigned to city when it is a city-supported invention or when it is created by a person or business and the person or business agrees in writing to the application of this policy. In return, the creator shall share in the proceeds therefrom as described in section 88-17, subject to prior commitments to outside sponsoring agencies when applicable.  
(Ord. No. 20,098, § 1, 4-5-01)

**Sec. 88-10. Transfer of city’s rights to inventions.**

The city, after consultation with the creator, may in its discretion and upon such terms as it deems fit, cause any rights that the city may have in an invention to be transferred to the creator, in exchange for the city’s income rights as set out in section 88-16 below. The city shall, in such case,

Supp. No. 18

CD88:4
INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY

§ 88-18

execute all documents necessary to enable the creator to undertake protective measures and to make arrangements for the development and commercial exploitation of the invention.  
(Ord. No. 20,098, § 1, 4-5-01)

**Sec. 88-11. Assignment of city’s patent rights.**

The city may choose to assign its patent rights to NOBC or its subsidiaries for development, commercialization or negotiation for sale of the patent. NOBC and its subsidiaries will adhere to this policy in the distribution of proceeds.  
(Ord. No. 20,098, § 1, 4-5-01)

**Sec. 88-12. Copyrights.**

Works that are protectable by copyright belong, under copyright law, to an employer if they are created by an employee within the scope of his or her employment or are otherwise deemed works made for hire under copyright law. Some specific types of works that may be protectable by copyright are books, poems, plays, songs, catalogs, photographs, computer programs, advertisements, labels, movies, maps, drawing, sculptures, prints and art reproductions, game boards and rules, and recordings.  
(Ord. No. 20,098, § 1, 4-5-01)

**Sec. 88-13. City’s ownership rights in copyrightable works.**

Every work or part thereof that is created by an employee within the scope of his or her employment, or that is otherwise deemed a work made for hire under copyright law, or that is created by any person who agrees to the application of this policy is owned by the city.  
(Ord. No. 20,098, § 1, 4-5-01)

**Sec. 88-14. Transfer of city’s rights to copyrightable works.**

The city may, after consultation with the creator, entirely in its discretion and upon such terms as it deems fit, cause its rights with respect to any copyrightable work to be transferred or licensed to anyone as permitted by law.  
(Ord. No. 20,098, § 1, 4-5-01)

**Sec. 88-15. Trademarks.**

Trademarks adopted and used by the city in connection with its activities, services and products shall be the exclusive property of the city.  
(Ord. No. 20,098, § 1, 4-5-01)

**Sec. 88-16. Inventions transferred by the city.**

In every case in which the city transfers any right in an invention to the creator, the creator may secure whatever legal protection may be available. The city shall execute all documents necessary to enable the creator to proceed. Where the city transfers its rights in accordance with this policy, unless some other distribution is agreed to with the creator, the city shall be entitled to 15 percent of net income in excess of $10,000.00 derived from the exploitation of the transferred rights. The city’s share of the net income shall be distributed as set forth in section 88-17.  
(Ord. No. 20,098, § 1, 4-5-01)

**Sec. 88-17. Distribution of net income from inventions and copyrightable works.**

With regard to any invention or copyrightable work owned by the city, net income less any foreseeable development expenses the city deems necessary will be distributed as follows:

Fifty percent to the city, to be shared equally between the City of New Orleans General Fund and the NOBC or its subsidiaries (if applicable); and 50 percent to the individual creator(s).  
(Ord. No. 20,098, § 1, 4-5-01)

**Sec. 88-18. Timing of distributions.**

Distributions of income will be made quarterly on or before May 1, July 1, October 1, and January 1 of each year, to allow the city to account for all applicable licensing and related expenses. In instances where funds are held because of foreseeable development expenses or where expenses exceed revenue, the creators will be sent an accounting indicating the amounts received for the current three-month period and

Supp. No. 75

CD88:5
§ 88-18

NEW ORLEANS CODE

the amount of the anticipated expense or deficit. Once expenses are known with certainty, any excess withholding will be distributed. Income earned before the enactment of this policy will be paid on a quarterly basis at a rate of not less than 20 percent of the total amount due.

(Ord. No. 20,098, § 1, 4-5-01)

**Sec. 88-19. Method of payments.**

Payments of the amounts allocated to the creator(s) must be made to the creator(s) individually and cannot be assigned by the creator(s) to other parties or entities. The only exception will be that after the creator’s death, upon appropriate notification by the personal representative of the creator’s estate, and with court approval, if necessary, payment will be made to the creator’s heirs or legatees. An IRS Form 1099 or other appropriate form will be issued to the creator(s) for their share of revenues. The city will not advise individuals on the tax consequences of these payments. In the event there are multiple creators for an invention or work, the creators’ share will be divided equally among all creators. If the creators agree among themselves to a different division, the city or NOBC or its subsidiaries must be notified in writing at least one month prior to the date of the first income distribution as to the agreed-upon division of income.

(Ord. No. 20,098, § 1, 4-5-01)

**Sec. 88-20. Independent efforts.**

Any royalty(ies) accruing to the city, generated by any endeavor, including but not limited to those generated by manufacturers, distributors, or in-house sales, will be shared pursuant to a negotiated agreement approved either by the employee’s appointing authority and the NOBC director or the chief administrative officer. Prior to soliciting business through outside royalty agreements, a city employee must obtain approval to do so from the chief administrative officer.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 26738, § 1, 12-1-15)

**Sec. 88-21. Assignment/development.**

Inventions, copyrights, trademarks, and/or outside marketing opportunities may either be developed, manufactured, and distributed within the city or offered to and managed for development through outside corporate partners or other organizations or entities better suited for the manufacturing/distribution process. Decisions relative to outside assignment shall be made collaboratively by the employee’s appointing authority and the NOBC director or the chief administrative officer, and the developer/distributor of the product or process.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 26738, § 1, 12-1-15)

**Sec. 88-22. Royalty sharing.**

Royalties generated by any works, copyrights, trademarks, licensing, manufacturing, distribution, direct or indirect sales, and/or equity agreements between manufactures and the city will be shared between/among the parties involved. The NOBC director or the chief administrative officer, the appointing authority, city employee(s) involved, and any other involved parties will collaborate to confect an agreement detailing the sharing of royalties.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 26738, § 1, 12-1-15)

laws.title: Concealed handgun permit
laws.content:
(a) The superintendent of police shall have the authority to grant to an individual a concealed handgun permit that shall be valid within the boundaries of the city and shall be subject to any restrictive stipulations in the permit. The issuance of a concealed handgun permit shall not be unreasonably withheld.

(b) The superintendent of police shall determine who is entitled to receive a concealed handgun permit and may promulgate and adopt, in addition to the requirements of this section, reasonable standards and regulations with respect to the issuance and use of such permits. Such standards and regulations shall not be in conflict with this section or with R.S. 40:1379, 40:1379.3 or other applicable state law.

(c) Prior to approval of the issuance of a concealed handgun permit, the superintendent of police shall conduct a criminal record check in accordance with the standards and regulations promulgated by the superintendent and which shall include fingerprinting of an applicant and processing of such fingerprints through the Federal Bureau of Investigation.

(d) The superintendent of police shall charge and collect a nonrefundable permit application fee of $50.00 from each person upon submission of an application for a concealed handgun permit.

(e) Upon approval of an individual’s application and prior to the issuance of a concealed handgun permit, the applicant shall:

(1) Pay a permit issuance fee of $75.00;

(2) Deliver to the superintendent of police satisfactory proof of the issuance of a policy of comprehensive liability insurance providing coverage for the city and the police department with an aggregate limit of liability of not less than $500,000.00 per occurrence; which policy of insurance shall be maintained by the permittee in full force and effect during the validity of the concealed handgun permit or any renewal thereof; and

(3) Execute and deliver to the superintendent of police an agreement, in a form approved by the superintendent, to indemnify and hold harmless the city and the police department from any and all liability to any person, entity or property whatsoever resulting from the issuance of such permit or from any negligent or intentional act involving any handgun carried by the permittee.

(f) The superintendent of police shall not authorize issuance of a concealed handgun permit to any person who has been convicted of a felony under the laws of the United States, the State of Louisiana or any other state or country, regardless of the present status of such conviction nor to any person for any reason listed as automatic disqualifiers in the police department concealed handgun permit standards and regulations.

(g) Concealed handgun permits shall only be valid for a period of one year from the date of issuance.

(h) Concealed handgun permits may be renewed on a yearly basis upon approval by the superintendent of police in accordance with the requirements of this section. An additional fee of $75.00 shall be charged and collected upon approval and renewal of a concealed handgun permit. Any application submitted within 30 days of the expiration of the term of a concealed handgun permit shall be considered an application for renewal of such permit; however, such renewal shall be valid only from the date of its issuance for a period of one year thereafter; the permit shall expire on the applicant’s date of birth.

(i) The superintendent of police shall, at his discretion, have the authority to revoke any concealed handgun permit. Cancellation of any liability policy issued pursuant to the requirements of this section shall automatically serve to revoke the concealed handgun permit of the individual required to maintain such policy in full force and effect.

laws.title: Use of riot control agents
laws.content:
(a) For purposes of this section, "riot control agent" means tear gas and other chemical compounds intended to disable individuals temporarily by causing irritation to the eyes, mouth, throat, lungs, or skin.

(b) It shall be unlawful for any employee of the New Orleans Police Department, or any other law enforcement officer operating within the City of New Orleans, to use or dispense a riot control agent against any person for any purpose, except in circumstances where its use is reasonably necessary to prevent threat of imminent loss of life or serious bodily injury, or to dislodge a barricaded violent criminal suspect.

(c) Any law enforcement agency dispensing a riot control agent in accordance with section 90-40(b) shall clearly and audibly announce the impending use of the riot control agent and provide adequate opportunity to retreat prior to deployment. (M.C.S., Ord. No. 28499, § 1, 9-17-20)

laws.title: Minimum requirements of the crime laboratory and evidence division
laws.content:
(a) The City of New Orleans shall maintain a fully operational crime laboratory within Orleans Parish, which includes, without limitation, the following units, each of which shall maintain appropriate industry accreditation and meet applicable Federal Bureau of Investigation Quality Assurance Standards:

a. Advanced crime scene investigation;

b. DNA testing and databasing and

c. Firearms and toolmarks.

(b) The department of police shall use best efforts to extract DNA from firearm casings wherever possible, including through swabbing and, if appropriate, soaking technology.

(c) The crime laboratory shall maintain separate credentials as a forensic science testing and calibration laboratory. (M.C.S., Ord. No. 28953, § 1, 3-10-22)

Editor’s note—M.C.S., Ord. No. 28953, § 2, states: The accreditation requirements imposed herein shall be satisfied no later than December 31, 2025.

laws.title: Sexual assault collection kit testing
laws.content:
(a) The department of police and partner agencies shall track all sexual assault collection kits ("kits") received, including any backlog of kits never submitted for testing or analysis, and test all kits with probative value.

(b) On the first Friday of every third month (March, June, September, and December), the department of police shall submit to the clerk of council a report documenting the following, to appear on the council’s next regular meeting agenda:

a. The number of kits processed, including testing and analysis, since the prior quarterly report;

b. The number of new kits received since the prior quarterly report;

c. The total number of backlogged kits in the police department's possession that have yet to be tested or analyzed;

d. The number reported under subsection 90-42(c) in the prior quarterly report; and

e. The percent increase or decrease in the backlog since the prior quarterly report.

(c) By March 1 annually, the superintendent of police shall certify in a communication to the clerk of council that the department of police has fulfilled all other reporting requirements, including La. R.S. 15:624, regarding sexual assault collection kits and related offenses. This certification shall include a copy of all such reports submitted during the preceding year.

(d) DNA profiles of sexual assault victims shall not be entered into criminal databases, including as defined in La. R.S. 15:603.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 28953, § 1, 3-10-22)

laws.title: Staffing and operations of public integrity bureau and internal affairs
laws.content:
(a) The New Orleans Police Department (NOPD) shall ensure that a sufficient number of well-trained staff and necessary resources are assigned and available to the public integrity bureau (PIB) to complete and review thorough and timely misconduct investigations of personnel, which shall occur in accordance with requirements of applicable law.

(1) To be considered timely, all administrative investigations conducted by PIB shall be completed within the time limitations mandated by state law, as provided in La. R.S. 40:2531.

(2) Where an allegation is sustained, NOPD shall have a reasonable time to determine and impose the appropriate discipline, except in documented extenuating circumstances.

(3) All administrative investigations — defined to include assignment, investigation, review, and final approval — shall be subject to appropriate interruption and tolling periods as necessary to conduct a concurrent criminal investigation as provided by law.

(b) NOPD shall designate an office outside of PIB and the PIB director, whom NOPD officers may file complaint allegations in reference to those officers staffing PIB.

(c) Officers newly promoted to the rank of sergeant and/or lieutenant shall, within a reasonable time frame, serve a rotation in PIB.

(d) NOPD shall provide opportunities for officers to rotate into PIB on a voluntary basis, as well as opportunities for those serving within PIB to rotate into other offices within NOPD.

(e) The NOPD shall promulgate rules and regulations implementing the requirements of this section, including, without limitation, policies providing a "reasonable time" for purposes of determining and imposing discipline, and policies providing for the rotation of supervisory officers within PIB.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 29132, § 1, 8-4-22)

Editor’s note—M.C.S., Ord. No. 29132, § 1, adopted August 4, 2022, set out provisions intended for use as § 90-42. To prevent duplication of section numbers, and at the editor’s discretion, these provisions have been included as § 90-43.

laws.title: Prohibited disclosure of crime- and accident-scene images and video footage
laws.content:
(a) No member of the police department nor any person acting on the city’s behalf may share or disclose photographs or video footage depicting a crime or accident victim in cases involving death or serious bodily injury, unless the image or footage of the victim is obscured or redacted or the disclosure is expressly authorized by this section.

(b) The city may disclose unredacted images or footage of crime or accident victims:

(1) To other law-enforcement agencies;

(2) Under circumstances reasonably related to the investigation of the incident or the apprehension of the perpetrator;

(3) For internal law-enforcement training purposes;

(4) At the request of the victim or, if the victim is deceased, the victim's family;

(5) In connection with a court proceeding; or

(6) As required by the Public Records Law or other applicable law.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 30476, § 1, 10-9-25)

Secs. 90-45—90-85. Reserved.

laws.title: Deputizing persons not members of police force
laws.content:
(a) The superintendent of police of the city may deputize and issue warrant of deputization, without pay, to persons not members of the police force of the city, such as private security guards and governmental employees, to exercise limited police power in accordance with the standards and regulations as set forth by the superintendent of police.

(b) The superintendent of police, in reviewing the licensing requirements regarding private security guards, shall utilize all available crime information networks, including the Louisiana Automated Computerized Criminal Histories (LACCH) system, to check the background of each applicant.

(Code 1956, § 49-15; M.C.S., Ord. No. 18,700, § 1, 4-16-98; M.C.S., Ord. No. 28882, § 1, 12-16-21)

laws.title: Convicted felons not to be deputized
laws.content:
The superintendent of police shall not appoint or deputize any person who has been convicted of a felony under the laws of the United States, the state or any other state or country.

(Code 1956, § 49-16)

laws.title: Deputized persons not entitled to public employee benefits
laws.content:
Deputized persons who are not governmental employees shall not be entitled to public employee benefits for such services and shall not be paid from public funds when exercising such powers with respect to privately owned property or places. Governmental employees exercising such powers in the course and scope of their governmental employment shall be entitled only to the compensation and benefits of their governmental employment.

(Code 1956, § 49-17; M.C.S., Ord. No. 28882, § 1, 12-16-21)

laws.title: Rules to govern exercise of powers of deputized person
laws.content:
The superintendent of police shall prescribe the rules and regulations governing the exercise of police powers by persons so deputized and may suspend or cancel their deputization at his discretion.

(Code 1956, § 49-18)

laws.title: Annual license fee for deputized persons
laws.content:
The superintendent of police shall charge and collect a license fee of $50.00 from each person applying to be deputized in accordance with the provisions of section 90-86 upon receipt of the application and shall charge and collect beginning on or before February 11, 1980, and each succeeding year thereafter, an annual renewal license fee of $50.00 from each such deputized person. A deputized person who fails to pay his annual renewal license fee on or before February 11, 1980, and each succeeding year thereafter shall be charged a delinquent fee of $10.00 in addition to the annual license fee. A deputized person transferring his license from one company to another during a calendar year shall be charged a transfer license fee of $10.00. Exceptions for payment of these fees will be employees of federal, state and city government and retired police officers.

(Code 1956, § 49-19)

laws.title: Payment of police officers for secondary employment or private details
laws.content:
(a) Definitions. The following terms, when used in this article, shall have the meanings assigned in this section unless the context clearly indicates otherwise. (1) Secondary employment means security or police-related work performed for compensation by an NOPD officer or employee during his or her off-duty hours. Formerly known as "paid details," or simply "details." (2) Time-based jobs means those secondary employment opportunities that require a person, place, or thing to be secured for a known or estimated duration or period of time. This includes but is not necessarily limited to facility or area security jobs, such as retail, neighborhood patrol, race route security, and special events. (3) Major special events shall include any event held at the Ernest N. Morial Convention Center, Fair Grounds Race Course, Mahalia Jackson Theater, New Orleans Arena, Saenger Theater, Superdome, and UNO Lakefront Arena with an expected attendance of at least 2,000 persons. This shall not limit the authority of the city council or any other authorized entity to declare special events for the purpose of police secondary employment. (4) A. Holiday premium means a flat rate paid in addition to an officer's hourly rate of pay for time-based secondary work and to be effective on specified holidays and days of officer high demand. Officers will earn the hourly holiday premium for all hours of every continuous shift that begins on a specified holiday, even if the shift carries over past midnight. Shifts that begin before midnight the day before a specified holiday and carry over past midnight into the holiday will not be eligible for the holiday premium. This premium applies to all officers regardless of rank, and does not incur any administrative fee for the customer. B. Specified holidays are: i. New Year's Day. ii. Martin Luther King's Birthday. iii. Mardi Gras. iv. Good Friday. v. Memorial Day. vi. Juneteenth. vii. Independence Day. viii. Labor Day. ix. Veterans Day. x. Thanksgiving Day. xi. Christmas Day. C. Days of officer high demand are: i. Lundi Gras. ii. Friday after Thanksgiving. iii. Christmas Eve. iv. New Year's Eve. (b) Fee and officer pay schedule for time-based jobs. laws.title: Use of funds collected

All fees charged for services pursuant to section 90-121 hereinabove shall be payable to the City of New Orleans and shall be collected by the department of finance and deposited, pursuant to City Code Section 70-415.245, into the police secondary employment fund and used to fund operations of the office of police secondary employment.

laws.title: Same—Restrictions
laws.content:
Research reports or copies of records may be withheld from the public when the original records are being held by the police department as evidence in the investigation or prosecution of a criminal charge until after such original records have been used in open court or the criminal charge or investigation has been finally disposed of. Further, research reports or copies of records may be withheld from the public to protect from disclosure information obtained from the Federal Bureau of Investigation and designated by such bureau as "confidential.

(Code 1956, § 49-23.2; M.C.S., Ord. No. 27465, § 1, 7-27-17)

laws.title: Same—Official agencies exempt from payment of fees; copies for victim's relative
laws.content:
(a) Official agencies of the city, state and federal government shall be furnished such copies and research reports as they may request without payment of fees set forth in section 90-123; provided, however, that such agency is legally entitled thereto, and that making such information available to the particular agency does not violate good criminal investigation practice or procedure.

(b) In the case of a violent crime such as, but not limited to, purse snatching, burglary, armed robbery, rape or homicide, the victim, or in the case of homicide the victim's closest relative, may request one copy of the police report without payment of fees outlined in section 90-123. In no case shall this privilege be extended to furnishing to the victim more than one free copy of the police report, neither shall this privilege be extended to any representative of the victim, except as stated above in the case of homicide.

(Code 1956, § 49-23.3)

laws.title: Same—Monthly report and remittance

The department of police shall submit a monthly report to the director of the department of finance, showing all fees collected pursuant to the provisions of section 90-123, and all monies shown as collected in such monthly report shall

laws.title: Use of force
laws.content:
(a) The department shall maintain a force investigation team within the public integrity bureau that conducts investigations of certain uses of force by police officers as required by this division or the department’s rules and regulations. The department shall provide in-service training when an employee is initially assigned to the force investigation team and thereafter provide annual in-service training to all force investigation team employees.

(b) "Use of force" is any physical effort to compel compliance by an unwilling subject above unresisted handcuffing including, but is not limited to, pointing a firearm at a person. A "serious use of force" includes the use of lethal force; a critical firearm discharge; use of force resulting in serious physical injury or hospitalization; neck holds; use of force that causes or results in a loss of consciousness; canine bites; an application or series of applications of a Taser longer than 15 seconds; and any strike, blow, kick, Taser application, or similar use of force against a handcuffed individual.

(c) The department shall establish and maintain policies governing the use of force by its officers and outlining responsibilities for conducting investigations of uses of force in accordance with this section.

(1) The policies shall, at a minimum, define the terms "use of force" and "serious use of force" consistent with this section; identify different levels of uses of force; require the police officer who uses force to notify the officer’s supervisor of the use of force; and require the police officer who uses force to prepare and submit a written force statement describing the use of force.

(2) The force investigation team shall investigate serious uses of force; uses of force indicating apparent criminal conduct by a department police officer; uses of

Supp. No. 114

CD90:11
$\S$ 90-153

NEW ORLEANS CODE

force by a department police officer with a rank higher than sergeant; all incidents during which an individual has died while in, or as an apparent result of being in, the custody of department personnel; and uses of force as assigned by the superintendent, the superintendent’s designee, or the public integrity bureau. The policies shall require that supervisors suspend a use of force investigation and notify the public integrity bureau upon the discovery of any evidence indicating apparent criminal conduct by a department employee.

(3) The force investigation team shall respond to the scene of a serious use of force incident, secure evidence, and conduct interviews, including interviews of department officers, victims, and witnesses. The team shall review the use of force reports and submit a criminal investigation report and administrative investigation report to a designated employee of the public integrity bureau.

(4) The department’s homicide section shall not investigate any lethal use of force by a police officer.

(d) The department shall maintain a use of force review board composed of senior department personnel to review all serious uses of force and any investigation conducted by the force investigation team. The department shall maintain policies that define the procedures of the board. All reviews by the board shall conform to all applicable department rules and regulations.

(1) Members of the board shall include, but are not limited to, three members equivalent to the rank of deputy superintendent, one of which must be the deputy superintendent over the investigating bureau or his designee, and the commander of the academy or his designee. The superintendent may assign a proxy for board members equal to the rank of the member being replaced.

(2) The use of force review board shall:

(i) Review all serious use of force investigations to ensure the reports are complete and the report findings are supported by a preponderance of the evidence;

(ii) Order additional investigations as it deems necessary;

(iii) Determine whether a use of force violates department policy or implicates any issues with police training, equipment, or tactics

(iv) Document its findings in writing; and

(v) Refer all policy violations for disciplinary action and refer all other issues to the proper unit or division within the department for resolution.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 30523, § 1, 11-13-25)

laws.title: Crisis intervention
laws.content:
(a) The department shall maintain a crisis intervention team of department employees who are specially trained to manage persons experiencing a mental health crisis. Certified team members may be incorporated into any unit in the department.

(b) The department shall provide in-service training when an employee is initially assigned to the crisis intervention team and thereafter provide annual in-service training to all crisis intervention team employees. Crisis intervention training shall include appropriate techniques for response to an incident in which a person is experiencing a mental health or behavioral crisis, including for example, intense feelings of personal distress, obvious changes in functioning, or catastrophic life events.

(c) The department shall ensure that crisis intervention training is available to all police officers.

(d) The department shall establish and maintain a crisis intervention policy that comports with best practices.

(e) The department shall collect data on crisis intervention team responses in accordance with its crisis intervention policy, and publicly report the collected data, aggregated as necessary to protect privacy.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 30523, § 1, 11-13-25)

laws.title: Sexual assault response
Domestic violence response
laws.content:
(a) The department shall maintain policies governing incidents of domestic violence that reflect the provisions of this section and prioritize victim safety and protection.

(b) The department shall track and publicly report the disposition of domestic violence investigations and outcomes of domestic violence cases when the data is made available by the relevant criminal justice agency.

(c) The department shall provide in-service training when an employee is initially assigned to the domestic violence unit and thereafter provide annual in-service training to all domestic violence unit employees. The in-service training for the domestic violence unit shall include, but is not limited to, the following:

(1) Advanced, skills-based instruction in evidence collection;

(2) Victim assistance; and

(3) Interview training incorporating role-playing or other problem-based learning techniques.

(d) The department shall provide all police officers not assigned to the domestic violence unit with annual in-service training on domestic violence response.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 30523, § 1, 11-13-25)

laws.title: Community- and problem-oriented policing
laws.content:
(a) The department shall promulgate rules and regulations for the implementation of community- and problem-oriented policing strategies that reflect the provisions of this section.

(b) The department shall provide both initial and annual in-service training on community policing and problem-oriented policing to all police officers.

(c) The department shall meet regularly with the communities it serves and shall establish partnerships with community members to promote cooperation, mutual respect, and trust.

(d) The department shall assess the effectiveness of the partnerships and strategies required by this section on a regular basis and publicly report its findings.

(e) Every three years the department shall conduct or commission a comprehensive community survey regarding the community’s experiences with and perceptions of the department. The department shall publish the findings of the survey.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 30523, § 1, 11-13-25)

laws.title: Officer assistance program
laws.content:
(a) The department shall establish and maintain an officer assistance program to provide a centralized and comprehensive range of mental health services, which shall comport with best practices and current professional standards, including: readily accessible confidential counseling services with both direct and indirect referrals; critical incident debriefings and crisis counseling; peer counseling; and stress management training.

(b) The officer assistance program shall:

(1) Have mental health professionals on staff;

(2) Provide comprehensive mental health and support services to department employees and their families; and

(3) Offer services to assist employees and their families in managing stress associated with traumatic incidents.

(c) The department shall ensure that use of officer assistance program services is confidential and private to the maximum extent practicable.

(d) The department shall promote awareness and encourage employees to use officer assistance program services.

(e) The department shall maintain an electronic early intervention system, or an equivalent process to support officers with effective supervision and to help supervisors and managers identify employees in need of guidance, counseling, support, or intervention.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 30523, § 1, 11-13-25)

Supp. No. 114

CD90:14

laws.title: Body worn cameras
laws.content:
(a) The department shall establish and maintain policies regarding body worn cameras that comply with the provisions of this section.

(b) All department police officers assigned to district patrol functions shall use body worn cameras, or similar technology when responding to a call for service.

(c) The department shall ensure its police officers are sufficiently trained before issuing the officer a body worn camera. The department shall train and require its officers to activate the body worn camera when doing so will:

(1) Enhance safety and public trust;

(2) Document the relevant statements and events of an incident;

(3) Preserve evidence;

(4) Allow for self-critique and evaluation during officer training; or

(5) Promote constitutional policing.

(d) The body worn camera policy shall include provisions regarding supervisory review of, and retention of and access to body worn camera recordings.

(e) No department employee shall use a body worn camera in a manner that would infringe on a citizen’s reasonable expectation of privacy, when avoidable.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 30523, § 1, 11-13-25)

laws.title: Secondary employment
laws.content:
(a) There shall be an office of police secondary employment that is independent of the police department and has the sole authority to arrange and coordinate off-duty secondary law enforcement employment by department employees. The office shall maintain a fully auditable payment process and perform all administrative functions related to off-duty secondary law enforcement employment by department employees.

(b) The department shall notify employees of the proper process for working secondary law enforcement employment and any applicable rules regarding secondary employment including possible penalties for violation.

(c) Any department employee working secondary employment shall have the same responsibility to carry appropriate departmental equipment (e.g., police radios) and document activities in the same manner as if the employee were on regular duty, including completing incident, arrest, and use of force reports, and reporting allegations or observations of misconduct.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 30523, § 1, 11-13-25)

laws.title: Transparency
laws.content:
(a) The department shall post all rules, regulations, and policies on its website; provided that if, in the superintendent’s opinion, publication of a specific rule, regulation, or policy comprises a security risk, the department may withhold the rule, regulation, or policy from public review.

(b) The department shall collect and maintain all data and records necessary to facilitate and ensure transparency and public access to information related to departmental decision-making and activities, as permitted by law.

(c) The department shall publish open data sets on its website, including calls for service, body-worn camera metadata, investigatory stops, uses of force, and misconduct complaints.

(d) The department shall maintain a policy facilitating the prompt, proactive release of critical incident video recordings, as permitted by law.

(e) The department shall hold regular organizational meetings using data to track management topics including supervision, misconduct, uses of force, internal audits, and other facets of risk management. The department shall publicly post on its website the data used in these meetings.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 30523, § 1, 11-13-25)

laws.title: Data collection and auditing
Training academy
laws.content:
(a) The department shall have a training academy that is led by a director or post-certified academy commander and which shall staff, at a minimum, an academic director with substantial experience supporting academic institutions or large-scale training programs; and a curriculum development specialist.

(b) Each academy instructor shall possess demonstrable experience and, where applicable, all necessary certifications in the subjects assigned to teach and training on lesson-plan development, methods of instruction, and adult learning theory and techniques in advance of being assigned to teach at the academy. Full-time and adjunct instructors shall attend at least 40 hours of professional development programs annually.

(c) The department shall prepare and publish a complete, written schedule of courses and accompanying calendar in advance of each new recruiting class that includes the start date of the recruit class and the dates and times of the courses. All changes to the schedule shall be

Supp. No. 114

CD90:16
LAW ENFORCEMENT

§ 90-165

documented and approved in writing by the deputy superintendent or the major responsible for the academy.

(d) The academy shall prepare an annual master training plan that covers recruit and in-service training and provides the total number of academy instructional hours for recruits and the minimum number of hours for each course to be offered.

(e) All police officers shall receive annual in-service training.

(f) The department shall ensure that the academy’s courses incorporate the following topics whenever appropriate: de-escalation of force, procedural justice, peer intervention, community policing, and constitutional policing.

(g) All department records regarding an employee’s completion of academy courses, class attendance, grades, and internal department training shall be kept in a single, centralized database that is readily accessible for internal review and auditing.

(h) All lesson plans and course materials shall be stored in a secure electronic database that is readily accessible for internal review and auditing.

(i) The academy shall maintain a field training officer program to provide direct field experience to recruits.

(1) No more than one recruit shall be assigned to a field training officer except for limited periods of time when fewer field training officers are available due to a major public event, emergency, or other extenuating circumstances.

(2) The department shall ensure a recruit can provide confidential feedback on the recruit’s field training officer and the field training program.

(j) The department shall ensure the academy has adequate training resources, including, but is not limited to, the following:

(1) Body worn cameras, or equivalent technology, for all recruits engaged in practical skills training;

(2) A computer terminal available for use by each recruit;

(3) Adequate physical space for all recruits without exceeding maximum occupancy rules; and

(4) Dedicated space for instructors to work, prepare lesson plans, and grade tests.

(k) The department shall ensure the academy maintains a written recruit manual that is reviewed annually and updated as needed. At a minimum, the recruit manual shall contain:

(1) The disciplinary process for both academic and conduct violations; and

(2) Professional standards for recruits, including, for example, no phone use in the classroom, appropriate attire, on-time arrival, attendance.

**Sec. 94-37. City records declared public property.**

All city records as defined in section 94-36 of this article are hereby declared to be property of the city. No city official or employee has, by virtue of his position, any personal or property right to such records even though he may have developed or compiled them. The unauthorized destruction, removal from files, or use of such records is prohibited.

**Sec. 94-38. Transfer of permanently valuable records.**

Active records shall be maintained by the issuing department, agency, board, or commission in storage space provided by the agency for the legally mandated period of three years. Records that are older than three years shall be disposed of according to retention schedules prepared and maintained by the city archives or as may be ordered by the state archivist. Disposition of records not included on the retention schedules shall be determined by the responsible agency head in consultation with the city archives staff. Those records deemed to be of permanent value shall be transferred to the city archives for archival retention and preservation. Records deemed not to be of permanent value are to be destroyed or otherwise disposed of within the limits outlined in section 94-37 of this article. Nothing in this section shall be interpreted as overriding the provisions of the Louisiana Public Records Law.

(Code 1956, § 34-21)

**Sec. 94-39. City archives to preserve permanent records.**

All materials referred to in section 94-37, along with any additional materials transferred perma-

nently to the city archives by the provisions of sections 94-38, 94-40 and 94-41, shall be arranged, described, catalogued, and preserved by the city archives staff according to the standards of the archival profession. The city archives shall provide housing under archival conditions for records in its possession in such manner that those records, unless their use is restricted by law or regulation, are open to the public for research purposes. In no circumstances shall any city records be transferred to private individuals, to public or private collections, historical societies or museums, or to public or private colleges or universities.

(Code 1956, § 34-20)

**Sec. 94-40. Two copies of printed material to be filed.**

At least two copies of all printed publications issued by or prepared for any department shall be filed with the city archives at the time of publication or distribution.

(Code 1956, § 34-22)

**Sec. 94-41. Removal of materials from the city archives.**

Upon transfer of material to the city archives in accordance with adopted retention schedules or through other means, the custody of such materials shall thereupon vest in the city archives. No material once relinquished to the city archives may be removed from its jurisdiction except by special authority and consent of the city archives staff. When such removals are authorized, a reliable official must sign a receipt and assume the responsibility for the safe return of such borrowed material.

(Code 1956, § 34-24)
