The mobile home park shall conform to the following requirements:

(1) The park site must be properly graded in accordance with the building code to insure proper drainage and complete freedom from standing pools of water.

(2) Individual mobile home sites shall meet the requirements of the comprehensive zoning ordinance and shall be assigned a designated address.

(3) All mobile home sites shall abut upon a park roadway.

(4) All mobile home sites shall abut upon a park roadway. All entrance driveways at the property line of a mobile home park or court shall not exceed 25 feet in width. The paving shall be in accordance with the following specifications: Eight inches reinforced concrete with strength of 3,000 pounds, 28 days. All service alleys, roadways, and walkways within the park or court shall not be less than 25 feet in width to provide adequate circulation for vehicles, and shall be paved in accordance with the following specifications: Six inches compacted shell with one-and-one-half-inch bituminous base course and one-inch bituminous wearing surface; or six inches reinforced concrete with strength of 3,000 pounds, 28 days; and with proper expansion and contraction joints. The interior surfaces shall be constructed of moisture resistant material which will permit frequent washings and cleaning and disinfecting, as necessary, without excessive deterioration.

b. Each service building as well as its approaches shall be brightly illuminated at all times.

c. All rooms within a service building shall be well ventilated and all openings shall be effectively screened.

laws.title: Water supply
laws.content:
(a) There shall be provided in each mobile home park an accessible, adequate, safe and potable supply of water, capable of furnishing a minimum of 125 gallons of water per day per mobile home site. Where a public water supply of such quality is available that source shall be used exclusively. No independent water supplies shall be developed or used unless, upon petition by the applicant, the department of health shall, after investigation and hearing find and determine that the proposed source and the works for the production, transmission and distribution of such supply shall produce water meeting minimum standards, and shall grant special permission for the development and use of such independent water supply.

(b) Water service shall be provided for all individual mobile home sites and for all service buildings. The mobile home park shall provide running water service of a pressure of not less than 40 pounds per square inch at all outlets during peak hours (8:00 a.m.—9:00 p.m.) and 60 pounds per square inch thereafter. Facilities and fittings for water service for direct use by mobile homes shall be so located and constructed that they will not be damaged in the movement of the mobile homes and other vehicles having access to the mobile home park.

(c) It shall be unlawful for any person to make any connection between a water distribution system of a mobile home park and any nonpotable, questionable, or unapproved water supply.

laws.title: Sewage disposal
laws.content:
(a) Every mobile home park shall be provided with an adequate and suitable sewage collection system. Such sewage collection system shall meet the minimum standards provided for sewage collection systems as established by the sewerage and water board and the department of health, and the sanitary code of the state.

(b) The sewage collection system shall discharge into a public sewer where one is available.

(c) If no public sewer is available to which the mobile home park sewage collection system can be connected a sewage treatment plant or septic tank and drain field shall be provided. The design of such sewage treatment plant or other facility shall be based on the ultimate maximum capacity of the mobile home park. Sewage treatment plant effluents shall not be discharged into any drainage facility of the sewerage and water board. The sewage treatment plant or other sewage disposal facility shall be constructed in such a location and manner it will not create a nuisance or health hazard to the park or to the owners or occupants of any adjacent property. A permit to install a septic tank or other sewage disposal system shall be secured from the department of health.

(d) Each mobile home site shall be provided with a sewer connection of at least four-inch pipe. The connection shall have suitable fittings so that a watertight connection can be made between the mobile home drain and shall be trapped in such a manner as to maintain it in an odor-free and safe condition.

This population of youth is known as the "adult waiver population".

(f) The provisions of this section shall not be construed to revoke or infringe on the authority or discretion afforded to the Orleans Parish Criminal District Court, Orleans Parish Juvenile Court, and the Orleans Parish District Attorney under the Louisiana Children's Code.

**Sec. 102-39. Intentional inducement or aid of others prohibited.**

It shall be unlawful for any person to intentionally possess, buy, sell or otherwise transfer any type of model glue for the purpose of inducing or aiding any other person to violate the provisions of sections 102-37 and 102-38.

(Code 1956, § 18-18)

**Sec. 102-40. Sale to minors prohibited.**

It shall be unlawful for any person to sell any type of model glue to a minor for any reason whatsoever.

(Code 1956, § 18-19)

**Sec. 102-41. Sales by wholesalers.**

It shall be unlawful for any wholesaler of merchandise to sell or transfer any quantity of model glue to any person whatsoever, who is not, or does not represent, a recognized bona fide retail dealer in merchandise customarily handling such product in the ordinary course of his or its business at a fixed location. If any such prohibited sale is made by any wholesaler, it shall constitute prima facie evidence of an intent to violate the provisions of this article.

(Code 1956, § 18-20)

**Sec. 102-42. Sale limited to bona fide retailers; limitation on quantity to be sold.**

(a) It shall be unlawful for any person to engage in the retail sale of model glue unless such person is a recognized bona fide retail dealer (at a fixed location) in merchandise, customarily handling such product in the ordinary course of his business.

(b) It shall be unlawful for any bona fide recognized retail dealer, as defined in subsection (a) of this section, to sell more than one tube, or other minimum sized container, of model glue to any one customer within any 24-hour period; provided, that the provisions of this subsection do not apply to the sale of model glue together with a hobby or model kit.

(c) It shall be unlawful for any bona fide recognized retail dealer to keep, maintain or prominently display in his business establishment any stock or supply of model glue in such manner or place as to make the same accessible to customers, or other members of the public, without actually receiving the same directly from the retailer, or his bona fide authorized representative.

(Code 1956, § 18-21)

**Sec. 102-43. Penalties.**

(a) Any person found guilty of violating sections 102-39, 102-40, 102-41, or 102-42 shall be punished by a mandatory fine of $100.00 and by mandatory imprisonment for 90 days for each such offense.

(b) Any person found guilty of violating the provisions of any other section of this article shall be punished by a fine of not more than $100.00, or imprisonment for not more than 90 days, or by both such fine and imprisonment for each such offense.

For the purposes of this article and notwithstanding anything in La. R.S. 40:1021 to the contrary, drug paraphernalia shall not include any device or equipment used exclusively, intended for use exclusively, or designed exclusively for personal use of marijuana.

(Code 1956, § 18-28; M.C.S., Ord. No. 28745, § 1, 8-5-21, eff. 9-15-21)

Cross reference—Definitions generally, § 1-2.

State law reference—Prohibited act, R.S. 40:1033.

laws.title: Determination
laws.content:
In determining whether an object is drug paraphernalia, a court or other authority shall consider, in addition to all other legally relevant factors, the following:

(1) Statements by an owner or by anyone in control of the object concerning its use.

(2) The proximity of the object in time and space to a direct violation of the Uniform Controlled Dangerous Substances Law.

(3) The proximity of the object to a controlled substance.

Supp. No. 97

CD102:9
$\S$ 102-112

NEW ORLEANS CODE

(4) The existence of any residue of controlled substances on the object.

(5) Direct or circumstantial evidence of the intent of an owner or of anyone in control of the object to deliver it to persons whom he knows or should reasonably know intend to use the object to facilitate a violation of the Uniform Controlled Dangerous Substances Law; the innocence of an owner or of anyone in control of the object as to a direct violation of the Uniform Controlled Dangerous Substances Law shall not prevent a finding that the object is intended for use or designed for use as drug paraphernalia.

(6) Instructions, oral or written, provided with the object concerning its use.

(7) Descriptive materials accompanying the object which explain or depict its use.

(8) National and local advertising concerning its use.

(9) The manner in which the object is displayed for sale.

(10) Direct or circumstantial evidence of the ratio of sales of the object to the total sales of the business enterprise.

(11) Expert testimony concerning its use.

(Code 1956, § 18-29)

laws.title: Prohibited acts
laws.content:
(a) It is unlawful for any person, knowing the drug-related nature of the object, to sell, lend, rent, lease, give, exchange or otherwise distribute to any person any drug paraphernalia.

(b) It is unlawful for any person, knowing the drug-related nature of the object, to display drug paraphernalia.

(c) It is unlawful for any person to use or to possess with intent to use any drug paraphernalia, to plant, propagate, cultivate, grow, harvest, manufacture, compound, convert, produce, prepare, test, analyze, pack, repack, store, contain, conceal, inject, ingest, inhale or otherwise introduce into the human body a controlled substance in violation of this article.

(d) The term *knowing* as used in this section means knowledge of the drug-related nature of the object.

(Code 1956, § 18-30)

laws.title: Contraband; condemnation proceedings
laws.content:
(a) In addition to any other penalties imposed by this Code, all instruments, devices and objects which are seized after the effective date of the ordinance from which this section was derived, on condemnation as being distributed or possessed in violation of this article, may be destroyed by the authorities making the seizure, but only after compliance with the following procedure:

(1) Within 90 days after any such seizure is made, the city attorney shall institute condemnation proceedings by petition, a copy of which shall be served upon the owner of the seized items if known. If the owner is unknown, notice of the proceedings shall be published once a week for two weeks in the official journal.

(2) The petition shall allege that the seized items were distributed or possessed in violation of this article.

(b) Judgment by default shall be entered by the court 15 days of the filing of the petition, and the court shall order the seized items to be destroyed. Otherwise, the case shall proceed as other civil cases in such court. If the prosecution proves by a preponderance of the evidence that the seized items were distributed or possessed in violation of the law, the court shall order the seized items to be destroyed.

(Code 1956, § 18-31)

laws.title: Exceptions
laws.content:
(a) Nothing contained in this article shall be construed to prohibit the sale of hypodermic syringes or needles by licensed pharmacists or drug prevention and/or AIDS education programs as approved by the department of health and/or the state department of health and hospitals.

(b) Notwithstanding any other provision of law, the provisions of this division shall not apply to the manufacture, sale, distribution, or

Supp. No. 97

CD102:10
OFFENSES AND MISCELLANEOUS PROVISIONS

§ 102-201

advertisement of any product or object designed and sold primarily for scientific research, industrial, veterinary, or agricultural purposes, or for bona fide medical or clinical use.

(c) It shall be an affirmative defense that the person to whom the drug related object or advertisement or notice was distributed had a prescription from a licensed medical practitioner or psychiatrist for marijuana or the controlled substance for which the object is primarily intended to be used. It is also an affirmative defense that the drug related object was designed or marketed as useful primarily for veterinary or agricultural purposes.

(d) Notwithstanding any other provision of law, the provisions of this division shall not apply to a needle exchange program that has been expressly approved by the council. The council may, by resolution, approve the operation of such programs.

(e) Nothing in this article shall be construed to prohibit the use, possession, or sale of drug testing strips or other testing equipment designed to identify or analyze the presence, effectiveness, or purity of controlled substances.

(Code 1956, § 18-32; M.C.S., Ord. No. 27630, § 1, 12-14-17; M.C.S., Ord. No. 28671, § 1, 5-6-21; M.C.S., Ord. No. 29475, § 1, 5-25-23)

Secs. 102-116—102-199. Reserved.

laws.title: Chronic nuisances prohibited
laws.content:
(a) It shall be unlawful for any person to permit property under his ownership, control, or management to operate a chronic nuisance property.

(b) Any person found to be in violation of subpart (a) of this section shall not be permitted to possess an occupational license to conduct any business on a property found to be a chronic nuisance property for a period of up to two years, depending on the severity of the violation.

(c) The provisions of this article and the prohibitions in this section shall not apply to residential properties, apartment complexes, or any other property used exclusively for residential purposes.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 29323, § 1, 2-2-23)

laws.title: Enforcement
Emergency closure
laws.content:
Nothing in this chapter prohibits the city from taking any emergency action for the summary closure of such property when it is necessary to

Supp. No. 104

§ 102-205

avoid an immediate threat to public welfare and safety. The city may take summary action to close the property without complying with the notification provisions of section 102-203, but shall provide such notice as is reasonable under the circumstances and shall immediately take all appropriate steps to obtain judicial ratification of the closure.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 29323, § 1, 2-2-23)

laws.title: Chronic nuisance property judgments to run with the land
laws.content:
(a) A judgment declaring the existence of a chronic nuisance property, if recorded, shall constitute a charge on the immovable property that shall be effective against third parties who acquire an interest in any immovable so encumbered, subjecting them to the prohibitions contained in section 102-202 so long as they remain in effect.

(b) The city attorney shall take all appropriate steps to ensure that a judgment declaring the existence of a chronic nuisance property is effective against third parties, including through the filing of a notice of lis pendens and by recordation of any judgment rendered in connection with this article.

(c) Nothing herein shall prohibit the city from releasing an immovable from an encumbrance created pursuant to this section when there is good cause to believe that the nuisance conditions giving rise to the underlying action are not reasonably likely to continue.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 29323, § 1, 2-2-23)

laws.title: Reporting
laws.content:
(a) The city attorney shall transmit reports to the council for the first meetings in February and August of each year outlining properties referred by the superintendent to the city attorney that shall include:

(1) A narrative from the superintendent as to why each property constitutes a chronic nuisance property as defined in section 102-201;

(2) A copy of the original notice sent by the superintendent to the person in charge of a given property as required in section 102-203;

(3) The dates, times, and New Orleans Police Department item numbers for each qualifying nuisance activity for a given property;

(4) A copy of the agreed upon abatement plan between the person in charge of the property and the superintendent;

(5) A status update for each property including any abatement that has occurred at the site and the status of court proceedings; and

(6) Any penalties levied against a property by the city or civil district court, if applicable.

(7) Demographic information regarding the owners of the property and/or business.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 29323, § 1, 2-2-23)

laws.title: Trespass in Woldenberg Riverfront Park
laws.content:
(a) It shall be unlawful for any person to commit the crime of trespass in Woldenberg Riverfront Park.

(b) The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this section, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this subsection, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning.

(1) Premises of Woldenberg Riverfront Park is defined as the area bounded by the Mississippi River, including structures, docks or wharves built over the river, the enclosed portion of the Aquarium of the Americas at Number 1 Canal Street on the downtown side of Canal Street, the Mississippi River side of the Public Belt railroad tracks running parallel to the Mississippi River and including the area known as the moonwalk to the southwest edge of the Governor Nicholls Street wharf from the Public Belt Railroad tracks to the Mississippi River.

(2) Trespass in Woldenberg Riverfront Park is the intentional, unauthorized entry upon the premises of Woldenberg Riverfront Park or remaining upon the premises of Woldenberg Riverfront Park by a person when he knows his entry or remaining upon the premises is unauthorized or under circumstances where he reasonably should know his entry or remaining upon the premises is unauthorized.

(c) The premises of Woldenberg Riverfront Park shall be posted in areas of ingress and egress with signs indicating at what hours of the day or night that entry to or remaining upon the premises is prohibited without authorization.

(Code 1956, § 43-11.1; M.C.S., Ord. No. 18,551, § 1, 12-4-97; Ord. No. 20,795, § 1, 7-11-02)

laws.title: Bicycle speed limit in Audubon Park; lights
laws.content:
(a) It shall be unlawful for any person to operate a bicycle at a speed in excess of ten miles per hour in that portion of Audubon Park bounded by Magazine Street, Exposition Blvd., St. Charles Avenue and Walnut Street.

(b) All bicycles operating in the abovementioned area shall possess a working light when used in either pre-sunrise or post-sunset periods.

(Code 1956, § 42-116)

laws.title: Use of private watercraft prohibited in City Park
laws.content:
It shall be unlawful for any person to use or operate a privately owned watercraft within the boundaries of City Park, without first having applied for and obtained a permit from the general manager of New Orleans City Park Improvement Association.

(Code 1956, § 42-115)

Cross reference—Boat and water safety, § 170-51 et seq.

laws.title: Duties
laws.content:
The department of parks and parkways shall:

(1) Administer, control and manage all parks, except those otherwise provided for by applicable state laws.

(2) Cultivate, place, maintain and remove trees, shrubs, flowers, grass and other plants on public grounds.

(3) Embellish parks, parkways, highways and other public grounds.

(4) Designate the portions of parks and other areas under its control for the activities under the direction of the department of recreation.

(5) Have custody, control, operation and administration of John P. Brechtel Memorial Park, including the authority to operate such concessions therein, by lease or otherwise, as the department may deem appropriate and desirable, as well as the authority to assess and collect reasonable fees for the privilege of fishing in the lagoon of such park.

(Code 1956, § 43-9)

Charter reference—Similar provisions, § 5-901.

*Editor’s note—Pursuant to a Home Rule Charter amendment whereby the parkway and park commission has become the department of parks and parkways, the title of this division has been changed accordingly, and references within this division to the parkway and park commission have been changed to department of parks and parkways.

Charter reference—Department of parks and parkways, § 4-1701.

Cross references—Boards, committees and commissions, § 2-86 et seq.; notice to owner of property by director of the department of parks and parkways to cut or remove weeds, trash, etc., § 66-312 et seq.

laws.title: Enforcement and citation powers
laws.content:
In connection with the duties of the department of parks and parkways, the superintendent of police is hereby authorized to grant enforcement and citation powers, in accordance with section 4-502(2) of the charter, to those department of parks and parkways employees designated to him, in writing, by the director of the department of parks and parkways, for the purpose of obtaining compliance with all city ordinances as they relate to those golf courses maintained by the department of parks and parkway. Such powers, which may be granted by the superintendent of police, shall be in addition to the normal enforcement and citation powers of the police department.

(Code 1956, § 43-9.1)

laws.title: Designation of types of plants, etc., for parks, etc
laws.content:
The department of parks and parkways shall designate the type of tree, shrub or plant for all parkways, parks, highways, public squares or public places under its jurisdiction.

(Code 1956, § 43-10)

laws.title: Fee waivers
laws.content:
(a) Notwithstanding anything in the Code to the contrary, the director of the department of parks and parkways shall have the exclusive authority, at the request of an event sponsor, to waive any fee imposed by the department for the
PARKS AND RECREATION

§ 106-102

use of any park or public space under its jurisdiction for special events lasting not more than one day sponsored by:

1. a non-profit organization in good standing with the Louisiana Secretary of State;

2. any organization exempt from taxation under Section 501 of the Internal Revenue Code; or

3. an educational institution.

(b) To qualify for a usage fee waiver, the event must, in the director’s discretion, promote a valid educational, charitable, social, cultural benefit to the City of New Orleans, which must be evidenced by an attestation of a representative of the sponsoring organization on forms prepared by the director.

(c) No sponsoring organization may receive more than one fee waiver pursuant to this section per calendar year.

(d) For an event that satisfies the criteria set forth in this section and is open to the general public, the director may waive up to 100 percent of the usage fee in accordance with policies and procedures established by the department.

(e) For an event that satisfies the criteria set forth in this section and is not open to the general public, the director may waive up to 50 percent of the usage fee in accordance with policies and procedures established by the department.

(f) No entrance or admission fees may be charged in connection with any event granted a fee waiver under this section.

(g) Any fee waiver authorized by this section shall not include any direct costs to the city.

(h) Any fee waiver granted pursuant to this section shall not include any required security or damage deposits imposed. The sponsoring organization shall be responsible to the city for damage resulting from or occurring during the event.

(i) The department of parks and parkways shall compile and maintain as a public record a database of all fee waivers granted pursuant to this section. The database shall contain the sponsoring entity, a description of the event and its public purpose, the date of the event and the amount of the waiver.

(j) Denial of a fee waiver requested pursuant to this section shall not be appealable to the council.

(k) Events consisting primarily of film or television production shall not be eligible for a fee waiver under this section.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 29825, § 2, 3-7-24)

laws.title: Compensation, conflict of interest
laws.content:
The commissioners of the Audubon Park Commission shall receive no compensation for their services. No commissioner or any officer or employee of the commission shall be interested, directly or indirectly, in any contract or in the losses or profits of any contract for labor, sup-

*Cross reference—Boards, committees and commissions, § 2-86 et seq.

plies, material or construction made by the commission, while members of the commission, nor for six months after the termination of their office or the completion of the work, under the penalty of dismissal and the absolute nullity of any such contract.

(Code 1956, § 43-50)

**Sec. 106-103. Secretary and employees.**

The Audubon Park Commission may select a secretary and fix his salary at a reasonable sum and likewise employ such other agents and employees as may be required for the discharge of its functions.

(Code 1956, § 43-52)

**Sec. 106-104. Surveying work in park.**

The director of the department of streets shall do, or have done, such surveying work upon Audubon Park and furnish levels, lines, grades and similar data, relative thereto as may be from time to time requested of him by the Audubon Park Commission.

(Code 1956, § 43-53)

**Sec. 106-105. Control of Audubon Park.**

The Audubon Park Commission is vested with the control and management of the park in the city known as the "Audubon Park."

(Code 1956, § 43-54)

**Sec. 106-106. Duties.**

The Audubon Park Commission shall take charge and supervision of the park and preserve and improve it for public recreation and use as a place of public resort and pleasure and the commission shall have full charge of the control and management, repair, maintenance, development and improvement of such park.

(Code 1956, § 43-55)

**Sec. 106-106.1. Audubon commission; powers, duties and functions.**

Pursuant to section 5-802 of the Home Rule Charter, the powers, duties, functions, administration, and operation of the Audubon Commission shall be to administer, operate, maintain and post the hours of operation of facilities administered by the commission, including Audubon Park, the Aquarium of the Americas, Woldenberg Riverfront Park, the Species Survival Center, the Louisiana Nature Center, the Moonwalk, and other educational, cultural and recreational facilities, and to perform such other duties as are provided by applicable law, subject to the provisions of the city’s master plan, its land use regulations, and its permitting authority.

The commission shall not accept, assume, or exercise any power or function which relates to taxation or the police power or which imposes a financial obligation on the city derived from any state law unless approved by ordinance of the council.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 18,752, § 1, 6-4-98)

**Sec. 106-107. Rules.**

The Audubon Park Commission shall make rules fixing its own meetings and procedure.

(Code 1956, § 43-56)

**Secs. 106-108—106-130. Reserved.**

laws.title: Department of Recreation*
laws.content:
**Sec. 106-131. Composition.**

The department of recreation shall consist of a director, deputy director and departmental secretary appointed by the mayor, and a staff selected by the director from the civil service register.

(Code 1956, § 43-12; M.C.S., Ord. No. 18,452, § 2, 10-1-97)

**Sec. 106-132. Duties of director.**

The director of the department of recreation shall be the executive officer of the department of recreation and shall be responsible for all activities of the department including the management and operation of all recreational facilities

*Charter reference—Department of Recreation, § 4-1001.

Cross reference—Departments, § 2-431 et seq.

Supp. No. 108

CD106:8
PARKS AND RECREATION

§ 106-138

placed under his jurisdiction, including outdoor and indoor facilities. He shall be responsible for developing cooperative planning with all public and private agencies dealing with recreational functions which are not included under the jurisdiction of the department.

(Code 1956, § 43-13)

**Sec. 106-133. Rules and regulations.**

The department of recreation may establish such divisions or bureaus and make such rules and regulations as may be necessary for the effective and economical administration of the department. The director of the department of recreation shall draw up rules and regulations governing the use and enjoyment of the facilities under the jurisdiction of the department and provide penalties for their violation. These rules and regulations shall be promptly presented to the council for approval and, if adopted by the council, they shall have the force of law and shall be binding on all concerned.

(Code 1956, § 43-14)

**Sec. 106-134. General duties.**

The department of recreation shall be responsible for developing a well-rounded program of public recreation which will serve all people and which is to be available for people of all ages; it shall administer all funds appropriated or made available to it for recreational purposes in the city; and, it shall cooperate with federal, state and local public and private agencies having recreational functions, including schools and such parks as do not come under the jurisdiction of the parkway and park commission or some other department or commission.

(Code 1956, § 43-15)

**Sec. 106-135. Certain future programs.**

The department of recreation is the city department responsible for the administration and operation of all new developments in the recreational field that may hereafter be created and for the operation and organization of which city funds may be appropriated, including playgrounds, playfields, community centers, gymnasia, teenage and neighborhood centers,

parks or other facilities and programs, and all such developments shall be cleared through this department and placed under its jurisdiction.

(Code 1956, § 43-16)

**Sec. 106-136. Commission to carry on functions of certain former organizations.**

The New Orleans Recreation Development Commission (formerly the New Orleans Recreation Department) shall operate the recreational programs formerly carried on by the Junior Sports Association Commission, the Supervisor of Lawrence Square, the Public Bath Commission, the Teen-Age Clubs, including the installation on South Norman C Francis Parkway near Perdido Street, and the former recreational activities of the former office of the commissioner of public property and shall exercise all powers, duties and responsibilities heretofore granted to such agencies. The New Orleans Recreation Development Commission shall likewise operate the playground recreational program formerly carried on by the playground and community service commission.

(Code 1956, § 43-17; M.C.S., Ord. No. 28571, § 2, 12-17-20, eff. 1-1-21)

**Sec. 106-137. Certain playgrounds.**

The department of recreation may govern, manage and direct the playgrounds on St. Roch Avenue, on Annunciation Square or Park, in Burke Square or Park, and in Soraparu Park, lay out and regulate them, install such apparatus as may be required for the pleasure and enjoyment of children, pass rules and regulations for the government of such playgrounds not inconsistent with law and city ordinances and generally to do all things in regard to such public playgrounds, the ornamentation and beautifying of them and the installation of the necessary appurtenances for the health, pleasure, instruction and enjoyment of children.

(Code 1956, § 43-18)

**Sec. 106-138. Hours for use of playgrounds and public parks.**

(a) Except for organized activities authorized or permitted by the department of recreation, it shall be unlawful for any person to loiter, idle,

Supp. No. 108

CD106:9
§ 106-138

NEW ORLEANS CODE

wander, stroll or play in or upon the public playgrounds under the supervision of the department between the hours of 10:30 p.m. and 6:00 a.m.

(b) Upon the written request of the proper authorities of parochial and public schools of the parish and upon the written request of the officers of social and fraternal organizations of the parish, the director of the department of recreation may suspend the curfew previously described when said schools shall use the playgrounds for athletic activities for the benefit or entertainment of its students, or when such fraternal or social organizations of the parish shall use the playgrounds for athletic activities for the benefit or entertainment of the people of the parish.

(c) Except for organized activities authorized or permitted by the department of recreation or the parkway and park commission, it shall be unlawful for any person to be on, in or upon a public playground of the city or a public park of the city which is under the supervision of the parkway and park commission between the hours of 10:30 p.m. and 6:00 a.m.; provided further, however, that between sunset and sunrise, it shall be unlawful for any person to be on, in or upon a public park under the supervision of the parkway and park commission which has no lights or facilities.

(Code 1956, § 43-14.1)

laws.title: Cooperation with other departments
laws.content:
The department of recreation shall cooperate with and make use of the services of such other city departments as may have services to render in connection with the department of recreation’s program such as the departments of police,

finance, health and sanitation, and others and shall depend upon them for appropriate services. But the department of recreation may expend funds appropriated to it for the purpose of employing operational personnel and such maintenance as may be necessary to supplement the services of the department of property management.

(Code 1956, § 43-20)

laws.title: Officials not to have interest in contracts
laws.content:
The director, members of the advisory committee and employees of the department of recreation or any of them shall not directly or indirectly in any way have a beneficial interest in any contract or work of any kind whatsoever connected with the activities of the department. Any violation of this section shall be punished as is provided by law for public contract fraud. Additionally, any one convicted of this offense shall be dismissed from the department.

(Code 1956, § 43-21)

Secs. 106-142—106-165. Reserved.

laws.title: Fishing in parks without permission or during closed season prohibited
laws.content:
It shall be unlawful for any person to kill, take, snare, pursue, catch or have in possession any fish within the limits of the city parks without the authority of the board of commissioners of such parks or during the closed season, as fixed by such boards.

(Code 1956, § 43-41)

laws.title: Possession of seines, nets, etc., in parks
laws.content:
It shall be unlawful for any person to have in his possession or to carry within the limits of the city parks without the authority of the boards of

Supp. No. 108

§ 106-171

commissioners of such parks, or during the closed season as fixed by such boards, any fish nets, cast nets, seines, fishing lines or poles. (Code 1956, § 43-42)

**Sec. 106-168. Baseball, football and racquettes—Prohibited in parks.**

The playing of baseball, football and racquettes and the practicing of such games on the neutral grounds or parks of the city is hereby prohibited except as permitted by sections 106-169 and 106-170. (Code 1956, § 43-43)

**Sec. 106-169. Same—Exception for City and Audubon Parks.**

The provisions of section 106-168 shall not apply to public playgrounds and parts of the City and Audubon Parks set aside for such purposes. (Code 1956, § 43-44)

**Sec. 106-170. Permit required for game or meeting in Lafayette Square.**

It shall be unlawful to hold or conduct any baseball game, football game, game of skill or games of any kind or public meeting of any kind in Lafayette Square without first obtaining a written permit from the parkway and park commission. (Code 1956, § 43-45)

**Sec. 106-171. Rentals charged for use of centers, gymnasiums and pools.**

The following schedule of rentals and charges to be paid for the use of centers, gymnasiums and pools is hereby established:

(1) Rental for basketball or volleyball:

a. College or University:

Practice (per hour): $25.00.

Game: $100.00.

b. All other:

Practice (per hour): $10.00.

Game: $30.00.

b. For each additional hour or portion thereof: $100.00.

c. Cleanup deposit: $100.00.

(3) Pool rentals:

a. For the first four hours or portion thereof: $350.00.

b. For each additional hour or portion thereof: $100.00.

c. Cleanup deposit: $100.00.

d. Life guards, per hour: $8.00.

e. Police officers, per hour: $15.00.

The certified lifeguards shall be provided by the department of recreation; the lessee shall, in addition to the fees imposed elsewhere in this section, pay to the department of recreation the full hourly pay rate for each lifeguard provided by the department. At least four or more lifeguards must be present.

(4) In all cases, in addition to the charges herein provided, the director of the department of recreation may fix appropriate charges for the use of extra facilities or extra equipment, such as spotlights, floodlights, sound systems or similar equipment, and designate at the expense of the person renting the center the number of police and other personnel for the operations of such equipment and property security for the event.

(5) The director of the department of recreation is charged with the responsibility of ensuring that any private function for which a gymnasium, pool or center is rented does not unduly conflict with public recreation programs; and he may reject any and all applicants for events which may cause an unreasonable risk to life and property or the safety and usefulness of the facility to be rented.

(6) Lessees of the facility shall be responsible to the city for damage to any gymnasium,

pool or center resulting from or occurring during the lessee's use thereof and shall, in addition, deposit in cash, certified check or money order in the sum of $100.00, refundable, to cover any damage resulting to a gymnasium, pool or center during the lessee's use thereof.

(Code 1956, § 43-1)

It shall be unlawful for any person or animal to use the Coliseum Square Fountain for purposes of bathing or otherwise submerging themselves therein.

(4) Playgrounds. For all playgrounds, the rental charge shall be $20.00 for the first two-hour period or portion thereof and $10.00 per hour for each subsequent hour or portion thereof.

(5) Refund policy. In all cases, there shall be no refund of charges. If an event is cancelled as a result of unsatisfactory weather conditions, the department of recreation may, when feasible and appropriate, allow the lessee of the playground or stadium to use that facility on another date which shall be to the satisfaction of the department.

(6) Damage deposit. The lessee of the playground or stadium shall be responsible to the city for damage to any playground or facility resulting from or occurring during the lessee's use thereof. The director of the department of recreation may require the posting of an appropriate damage deposit by an organization to ensure compliance with this provision.

(7) Security personnel. Any organization reserving a stadium or playground operated by the department of recreation for any event shall be responsible for providing adequate security personnel to ensure the safety of any persons at the event. The number of security personnel shall be established by the director of the department of recreation for any event on facilities operated by the department.

(Code 1956, § 43-2)

laws.title: Registration fees for programs provided by the recreation department
laws.content:
The recreation department is hereby authorized to charge registration fees for instruction in amounts not to exceed the following rates except

Supp. No. 108

CD106:12
PARKS AND RECREATION

§ 106-178

for those applicants who are at or below the income level of poverty as established by federal eligibility guidelines shall be exempted:

c. Nursery school course, per nursery: $150.00.

d. Single introductory lesson: $3.00.

(2) Summer day camps: $10.00 per child ages five to 12 years of age.

(Code 1956, § 43-2.1; M.C.S., Ord. No. 18,706, § 1, 5-7-98)

laws.title: Instructional fees for courses; for rental of costumes and admission to theatre
laws.content:
The department of recreation is hereby authorized to charge the following fees and/or admission charges:

(1) For various instructional courses offered by the department, such as ceramics, yoga, painting, dance, piano, arts and crafts, etc., a sum not to exceed $50.00 per course.

(2) For rental of department of recreation costumes, a rental fee set by the director of the department, dependent upon the cost of construction of the costume.

(Code 1956, § 43-3)

laws.title: Fees for use of swimming and tennis facilities
laws.content:
(a) Fees for the use of swimming pools operated by the department of recreation shall be as follows:

(1) Treme Pool:

Adults: $1.00.

Children (15 or under): $0.50.

(2) Gert Town Pool:

Adults: $1.00.

laws.title: Payment of deposits, rentals and fees; school board exempt
laws.content:
(a) Payments of deposits, rentals and fees for services or the use of facilities and equipment shall be made in cash, certified check or money order.

(b) The parish school board shall be exempt from paying the fees set forth in sections 106-171, 106-173, 106-175 and 106-176.

(Code 1956, § 43-3.2)

laws.title: Playground surfacing
laws.content:
(a) Compliance standards. The city must comply with the guidelines of the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission, the Americans with Disabilities Act, and the Louisiana Administrative Code for the Department of Health and Hospitals.

(b) Playground surfacing. The U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission guidelines state that appropriate surfaces for public playgrounds are either loose-fill or unitary. [U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission: Public Playground Safety Handbook (April 2008)]

Supp. No. 108

CD106:13
§ 106-178

NEW ORLEANS CODE

(c) [Appropriate surfacing defined.] A national consensus of advocates and manufactures [manufacturers] defines appropriate surfacing as "any material tested to ASTM F1292 (including unitary surfaces and engineered wood fiber): [Playground Surfacing: U.S. Standards and Practice (January 2001)]

(d) [ADA compliance.] The Americans with Disabilities Act provides that ground surfaces along accessible routes, clear floor or ground spaces, and maneuvering spaces within play areas must comply with ADAAG 4.5.1 (Ground or Floor Surfaces-General) and the ASTM F 1951-99 Standard Specification for Determination of Accessibility of Surface Systems Under and Around Playground Equipment: [ADA, Section 15.6.7.]

(e) [Playground equipment.] State regulation requires that "all pieces of playground equipment with play surfaces 4 feet or higher from the ground shall have an appropriate energy absorptive surface such as wood chips at a depth of 8-10 inches or rubber mats manufactured for such use meeting ASTM Standard F-355, under the fall zone of the equipment." [Louisiana Administrative Code for the Department of Health and Hospitals, title 51: part XXI, chapter 5]

(f) [Compliance required.] Any organization committed to building playground surface materials and/or donating playground surface materials for use on property owned by the city shall comply with the guidelines of the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission, the Americans with Disabilities Act, the Louisiana Administrative Code for the Department of Health and Hospitals, and with the provisions of this section. (M.C.S., Ord. No. 23263, § 1, 10-2-08)

laws.title: Facility fee waivers
laws.content:
(a) Notwithstanding anything in the Code to the contrary, the chief executive officer of the New Orleans Recreation Development Commission shall have the exclusive authority, at the request of the event sponsor, to waive any facility usage fee, including those fees imposed pursuant to section 2-1102(A)(1), section 2-1102(A)(4), section 106-171, or section 106-173, for special events lasting not more than one day that are sponsored by:

1. a non-profit organization in good standing with the Louisiana Secretary of State;

2. any organization exempt from taxation under Section 501 of the Internal Revenue Code; or

3. an educational institution.

(b) To qualify for a facility usage fee waiver, the event must, in the chief executive officer's discretion, promote a valid educational, charitable, social, cultural benefit to the City of New Orleans, which must be evidenced by an attestation of a representative of the sponsoring organization on forms prepared by the chief executive officer.

(c) No sponsoring organization may receive more than one fee waiver pursuant to this section per calendar year.

(d) For an event that satisfies the criteria set forth in this section and is open to the general public, the chief executive officer may waive up to 100 percent of the facility usage fee in accordance with policies and procedures established by the department.

(e) For an event that satisfies the criteria set forth in this section and is not open to the general public, the chief executive officer may waive up to 50 percent of the facility usage fee in accordance with policies and procedures established by the department.

(f) No entrance or admission fees may be charged in connection with any event granted a fee waiver under this section.

(g) Any fee waiver authorized by this section shall not include any direct costs to the city.

(h) Any fee waiver granted pursuant to this section shall not include any required security or damage deposits imposed pursuant to section 106-171 or 106-173. The sponsoring organization shall be responsible to the city for damage to any gymnasium, pool, or center resulting from or occurring during the event. The New Orleans Recreation Development Commission shall compile and maintain as a public record a database

Supp. No. 108

CD106:14
PARKS AND RECREATION

§ 106-212

of all fee waivers granted pursuant to this section. The database shall contain the sponsoring entity, a description of the event and its public purpose, the date of the event and the amount of the waiver.

(i) Denial of a fee waiver requested pursuant to this section shall not be appealable to the council.

(j) Sporting events are not eligible for a fee waiver under this section.

(k) Events consisting primarily of film or television production shall not be eligible for a fee waiver under this section.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 29825, § 3, 3-7-24)

Secs. 106-180—106-210. Reserved.

laws.title: Protection of trees and vegetation on city property
laws.content:
(a) Only arborists with prior written approval from the department may perform work on city trees.

(b) No person is permitted to remove, cut, disturb, or interfere in any way with any city tree without prior written approval from the department.

(c) Vehicles and heavy equipment are prohibited from working within the CRZ of a city tree or on city vegetation without prior written approval from the department.

(d) No equipment or vehicles may be cleaned, repaired, or stored on any city property within the CRZ of a city tree or on city vegetation.

(e) Excavation and fill greater than two inches in depth within the CRZ of a city tree is prohibited.

(f) Placement of decorations, string lights, wires, ropes, signs, posters, barricades, or other fixtures on city trees is prohibited unless prior written approval is received from the department.

(g) Placement of any sign, stationary or mobile, streamer, poster, bill, or other advertisement anywhere on city property, neutral ground, park, place, triangle, or sidewalk is prohibited unless prior written approval is received from the department.

(h) The attachment or installation of any electrical wire, cable, utilities, insulator, or any device to any city tree is prohibited.

(i) Injury to city trees, including the misuse or removal of any device placed to protect any tree, is prohibited.

(j) Placement of building materials, debris, or any other material within the CRZ of a city tree or on city vegetation is prohibited.

(k) Dumping of grass clippings, tree trimmings, rocks or refuse of any nature on city property is prohibited.

(l) Paving or placing of gravel or other such material under a city tree canopy or within four feet of the trunk, whichever is greater, is prohibited.

(m) Dumping, pouring, or spilling of oil, concrete mix, salt or salt water or other substances upon any city tree, or within its CRZ, is prohibited.

(n) Any person who injures, damages, or destroys any city tree or city vegetation shall promptly notify the department of such fact and that person shall, within such reasonable time as specified by the department, repair or replace such damaged city tree or city vegetation to the satisfaction of the department, in addition to any applicable penalties outlined herein.

(o) The use of any chemicals, insecticides, or oils, or the application of whitewash or paint to any city tree or city vegetation is prohibited.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 30255, § 1, 3-27-25)

laws.title: Tree protection near construction work
laws.content:
(a) Any construction work that occurs within the CRZ of a city tree requires the presence of an arborist to ensure that correct arboreal practices are followed.

(b) Prior to the commencement of construction, and with the prior written approval of the department, an arborist must identify each city tree that will require trimming to clear for construction.

(c) Cutting, trimming, removing, spraying, treating, or planting any city tree or city vegetation without prior written approval by the department is prohibited.

Supp. No. 112

CD106:16
PARKS AND RECREATION

§ 106-214

(d) The contractor shall be responsible for damage to all city trees and city vegetation and shall be liable to the city, for either compensation or tree replacement, as determined by the department.

(e) When an approved construction plan specifies for the removal of city trees or city vegetation, the owner, contractor, or agency authorizing the work shall compensate the city prior to beginning construction.

(f) If it is found that city trees or vegetation must be removed to complete a project and the department agrees to the removal, the trees or vegetation shall be transplanted to adjacent city property if possible and shall meet all additional department planting specifications, including one year of watering. If it is not possible to transplant the plant materials the city shall be compensated for the city trees or city vegetation.

(1) Compensation may include replacement planting on the city portion of the construction site or on nearby city property. The minimum rate of replacement shall be one caliper inch of replacement tree for each inch of DBH as assigned by the project survey or department.

(2) If it is not possible to plant a replacement tree on the city property portion of the construction site or on nearby city property, the city may accept a monetary amount equal to the replacement cost of the tree based upon current market conditions and the DBH, condition, and height of the tree to be removed.

(g) Installation of tree protection fencing is required around all city trees prior to construction and shall stay in place for the duration of construction.

(1) Tree protection fencing shall include a wood or chain link barricade at least five feet high along the CRZ and shall avoid damaging trees and plant materials unless an alternative tree protection method is approved in writing from the department.

(2) The removal of tree protection fencing during construction is prohibited.

(3) The contractor or property owner shall contact the department for an inspection of the tree protection fencing prior to the commencement of any site work, including demolition or clearing.

(4) Tree protection fencing shall carry durable signs designating the area as "Tree protection zone. No entry unless authorized by the Department of Parks and Parkways". Such signs shall be spaced around the perimeter of all tree protection zones with a maximum spacing of 25 feet. Signs shall be a minimum eight inches by ten inches in size and shall be firmly affixed to the tree protection fence.

(h) Signs, barricades, equipment, or materials shall not be attached to city trees or plant materials. "Overhead Clearance" signs may be loosely attached using a rope or chain when approved by the department.

(i) If a route for machinery is required through a grove of city trees, the department may allow a temporary pathway through the grove. Such a pathway shall be as narrow as practical, temporarily covered with eight inches of wood chips and a layer of plywood and enclosed by protective fencing on both sides.

(j) When construction work is taking place within the CRZ of a city tree, including sidewalk, drainage work, utility work, or planting, all work shall be completed without the use of heavy equipment and must receive prior approval from the department.

(1) Use of an air spade, hand-digging, or similar technology may be required to reveal the roots for preventative pruning by an arborist under the supervision of department.

(2) Alternative means for utility installation, such as tunnelling and boring, may be required where deemed necessary by the department.

(3) Alternative paving methods such as sidewalk bridging, flexible paving, ADA compliant gravel, and other technologies may be required as deemed appropriate by the department.

Supp. No. 112

CD106:17
§ 106-214

NEW ORLEANS CODE

(k) The department may order additional tree protection measures if site conditions warrant them.

(l) Each city tree shall be irrigated at least two times per week for the period of April through October over the duration of the project.

(m) Trenching within the CRZ of any city tree is prohibited. If work within the area within the CRZ cannot be avoided, the department may grant permission for the work and shall require the use of boring or air spade equipment to tunnel beneath the CRZ. The minimum depth for boring is 30 inches and tunneling shall be located as far from the trunk as possible.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 30255, § 1, 3-27-25)

laws.title: Bond of contractors
laws.content:
Contractors and others doing work on a neutral ground, either for excavations or other projects shall, at the director’s written request, give bond to the department to guarantee the payment of all costs for repairing any settlement or other damage or deterioration that shall take place in such neutral ground as a result of the project undertaken by them.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 30255, § 1, 3-27-25)

laws.title: Public utilities
laws.content:
(a) Public utility companies shall submit, subject to approval by the department, an annual trim plan by January 31 of each year to the department.

(b) Utility contractors shall abide by the requirements set forth in the Louisiana Revised Statutes Chapter 24: Horticulture, and the Louisiana Administrative Code 7: XXIX.117 (H).

(c) Only utility arborists shall execute the removal of trees or portions of trees along utility rights-of-way.

(d) Except for trees being removed, utility arborists shall not use climbing irons except in locations where other practical means of tree trimming are not available or as provided by the Louisiana Administrative Code.

(e) Utility arborists shall carry insurance as provided by the Louisiana Administrative Code.

(f) Utility arborists shall prominently display their license during all work.

(g) Treatment recommendations and pruning practices shall meet the standards outlined in the latest edition of the International Society of Arboriculture Certification Manual and Best Management Practices?Utility Pruning of Trees.

(h) In an emergency, public utility companies may perform minimum pruning or digging measures without a permit only to a degree necessary to restore or to avoid the loss of service or to abate imminent endangerment to human life in accordance with the provisions herein. The department shall be notified of the emergency work in a timely manner.

(2) Any emergency work must be subsequently brought up to appropriate standards to the greatest extent possible, as determined by the department. Such remedial work shall commence as soon as possible.

(i) When the department undertakes the removal or trimming of trees for the benefit of a utility company, the department may charge the utility company at rates to be determined by the department.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 30255, § 1, 3-27-25)

laws.title: Written permission required
laws.content:
(a) No tree, shrub or plant shall be planted on city property by any person without the prior written permission of the department.

(b) Any tree, shrub or plant planted in any city property may be removed by the department at the expense of the responsible party.

Supp. No. 112

CD106:18
PARKS AND RECREATION

§ 106-219

(c) Each tree, plant, shrub, or other vegetation planted on city property shall become the property of the city.

(d) No tree shall be removed from city property without the prior written permission of the department.

(e) No tree located on city property shall be cut, pruned, or treated without the prior written permission of the department.

(f) Written permission must be attained for the temporary use of city property under the jurisdiction of the department, including but not limited to neutral grounds, rights-of-way, and parks.

(g) The department shall keep a record of all permitted city tree maintenance, removals, and plantings. These records shall be made available to the public.

laws.title: Maintenance
laws.content:
All permitted planting on city property must meet maintenance standards as set forth by the department.

(a) The permittee shall be responsible for the maintenance, repair, and replacement of all landscape materials that are installed as part of a permit. Maintenance includes, but is not limited to: mulching, weeding, irrigating, fertilizing, pruning, and replacement of dead or dying plants.

(b) All plant materials and planted areas must be tended to and maintained in a healthy growing condition and kept free of refuse and debris. Plant materials that exhibit evidence of pests, disease, or damage must be appropriately treated and dead plants must be replaced.

(c) Care shall be taken to protect all trees and landscape materials while performing routine maintenance operations such as grass cutting and trenching.

(d) Tree topping is prohibited.

(e) The department may require that the permittee allow the city to treat trees or shrubs suffering from transmittable diseases or infestation of pests. If the disease or pests warrant drastic action to curb the spread to healthy trees or shrubs, or if the tree represents a public hazard, on the advice of the department, the permittee may be required to allow the city, or its agent, to treat or remove the tree.

(f) Clear sight lines must be maintained at a minimum height of six feet for a minimum distance of 25 feet from all intersections.

(g) Watering shall be sufficient to maintain vigorous and healthy plant growth and shall occur a minimum of two times per week during the months of March through October and one time per week during the remainder of the year. (M.C.S., Ord. No. 30255, § 1, 3-27-25)

laws.title: Request for pruning
laws.content:
Requests may be made to the department in writing for the cutting, pruning, or removal of a city tree adjoining, adjacent to, or abutting private property.

(a) If it is found that a city tree substantially causes loss, damage, or deprivation of the lawful use of such property, then the department may cut, prune, or remove such tree.

(b) Requests for the cutting, pruning, or removal of a city tree performed at the applicant's expense, rather than by the department, shall receive prior written permission.

Supp. No. 112

CD106:19
§ 106-219

NEW ORLEANS CODE

(c) All such requests for cutting, pruning, or removal of city trees shall be completed by arborists, pursuant to the following provisions:

(1) Such requests shall provide the department at least ten working days advance notice of the date and time contemplated for such work.

(2) No cutting, pruning, or removal of a city tree shall be done without written permission from the department.

(3) In no instance shall a city tree be cut, pruned, or removed contrary to the expressed stipulations of the department, nor shall work commence prior to receiving written permission from the department.

(4) The department further reserves the right and authority to inspect the work in progress and to require such work comply with standards for arboricultural work as well as all applicable ordinances and policy decisions of the department.

(d) No party shall be permitted to personally cut, trim, or remove any city tree adjoining, adjacent to, or abutting their property without prior written permission from the department.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 30255, § 1, 3-27-25)

laws.title: Enforcement
laws.content:
(a) Any person or entity who violates this article shall be subject to penalties in accordance with section 1-13 of this Code. Each day that such violation exists shall constitute a separate and distinct offense.

(b) The department shall issue a stop work order when work is being done in violation of this article, without approval, or if determined by the department to be hazardous.

(c) Willful destruction of city trees shall render the party responsible liable for the actual cost of repair or replacement. The responsible party shall bear the cost of repairing the damaged tree, to be determined by the department. The responsible party shall replace the damaged tree(s) with a specimen(s) of equal size and caliper, as approved by the department, including a one-year watering contract and a five-year warranty. If in kind replacement is not possible, the difference in cost shall be met through additional financial penalties that match the monetary value of the destroyed tree or with the planting of additional city trees.

(d) If a person or entity who causes damage to a city tree or other plant on city property fails or refuses to repair or replace the damaged or destroyed trees or other vegetation within a reasonable time, the department shall perform the necessary repair or replacement and the cost of this work shall be recovered from the person or entity responsible for the damage or destruction.

(e) The department may require the person or entity responsible for damage to a city tree hire an arborist to perform remediation work including, but not limited to: root pruning, termite treatment, mulching, irrigation, vertical mulching, radial aeration, mycorrhizal fungal inoculate, or growth regulation.

(f) In addition to any fine or penalty imposed by this article, the city may seek all available relief in a court of competent jurisdiction to enjoin any violation.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 30255, § 1, 3-27-25)

laws.title: Department not to be interfered with
laws.content:
No person shall prevent, delay, or interfere with the department in the planting, pruning, spraying, or removal of a city tree or city vegetation, or in the removal of stone, cement, or other substances about the trunk of a city tree.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 30255, § 1, 3-27-25)

Supp. No. 112

CD106:20
PARKS AND RECREATION

§ 106-296

Secs. 106-222—106-260. Reserved.

laws.title: French Quarter Festivals, Inc.'s, use of Jackson Square
laws.content:
Jackson Square was once known as Public Square, with countless community celebrations held there. Even more credence was given to this location as a place of the public when in 1839 some 30-odd "stall-keepers-fruit merchants" were given permission to do business. The French Quarter Festival began in 1984 as a means of attracting locals back to the Vieux Carré after the extensive street and sidewalk repairs done in preparation for the World's Fair. This festival now attracts more than 760,000 people annually, and with the significant proof of the boost it has

*Cross references—Restrictions regarding certain entertainment in the Vieux Carré and Jackson Square, § 30-1451 et seq.; certain restrictions for sales in the central business district and Jackson Square for mayoralty permits, § 34-216 et seq.; peddlers, solicitors and itinerant vendors, ch. 110; certain restrictions for sale of artifacts by mayoralty permit holders in certain areas, § 110-76 et seq.; certain restrictions on sales by artists holding mayoralty permits in Jackson Square and the central business districts, § 110-121 et seq.; restrictions on sales of flowers by mayoralty permit holders in Jackson Square and the central business district, § 110-151 et seq.; restrictions on sales of food by mayoralty permit holders in Jackson Square and the central business district, § 110-186 et seq.; certain restrictions regarding soliciting in the central business district and Vieux Carré, § 110-221 et seq.; restrictions on sales by transient vendors in Jackson Square and Vieux Carré, § 110-256 et seq.; streets, sidewalks and other public places, ch. 146.

given to the economy by generating over $251,000,000.00 in economic impact, as well as being the stimulus for other events such as "Satchmo SummerFest" and "Christmas New Orleans Style," the French Quarter Festivals, Inc., shall be permitted to use Jackson Square for all of the activities planned for their annual festivals as provided herein. (Code 1956, § 43-57.1; M.C.S., Ord. No. 26949, § 1, 6-9-16)

laws.title: Cabildo, transferred to curators of state museum
laws.content: The Cabildo fronting on Jackson Square in the city has been transferred to the board of curators of the state museum and dedicated in perpetuity for museum purposes; provided, however, that such dedication shall lapse if the curators shall fail to discharge the duties imposed on them by law. (Code 1956, § 43-58)

laws.title: Assignment of supreme court room to historical society
laws.content:
The supreme court room in the Cabildo, with the Chartres Street front, shall be assigned to the exclusive use of the Louisiana Historical Society so long as it performs the objects and purposes for which it was created by Act No. 6 of 1860, and Act No. 108, extra session of 1877. But should the Louisiana Historical Society cease to exist, the use of the supreme court room shall be determined by the board of curators of the state museum. (Code 1956, § 43-59)

Secs. 106-265—106-295. Reserved.

laws.title: Prohibition of certain activities
laws.content:
It shall be unlawful for any person to engage in any of the activities hereinbelow listed while

†Cross reference—Streets, sidewalks and other public places, ch. 146.

Supp. No. 112

CD106:21
§ 106-296

NEW ORLEANS CODE

within confines of that portion of Joe W. Brown Park leased to Louisiana Nature and Science Center, Incorporated so long as the Louisiana Nature and Science Center, Incorporated actively continues those purposes for which the property was leased. Those activities which shall be unlawful unless specifically approved by the director of the Louisiana Nature Center are:

(1) The possession, destruction, injury, defacement, removal or disturbance in any manner of any building, sign, fence, gate, equipment, monument, marker, or other structure, or of any animal or plant and direct or indirect products thereof, including but not limited to logs, stumps, flowers, branches, leaves, cones or other fruit, egg, nest or nesting site except as otherwise provided in this section.

(2) Possession of rifles, shotguns, pistols, bows and arrows, pellet guns, BB guns, slingshots, saws, knives, hatchets, and other such weapons which might be used to harm wildlife or plants.

(3) Littering.

(4) Smoking on grounds and along trails except as allowed in designated areas and in street.

(5) Swimming, bathing or boating in any water retaining areas on the Louisiana Nature and Science Center, Incorporated grounds.

(6) Picnicking, defined as the consumption of food or drink brought onto the grounds of the Louisiana Nature and Science Center unrelated to any function or activity sponsored by the Louisiana Nature and Science Center.

(7) Fishing, crawfishing, trapping, the removal of any type of plant or animal materials, living or dead.

(8) The bringing of dogs, horses, cats, and other animals onto Louisiana Nature and Science Center grounds even when under constraints of a leash, etc. They shall be allowed in constraint along Park Road and within ten feet of curb on either side while in passage from Joe Brown Park to Lake Forest Boulevard. Persons with constrained pets in passage between the park and Lake Forest must not loiter on Louisiana Nature and Science Center property. Seeing-eye dogs used to guide visually impaired persons and dogs specially trained to assist handicapped persons with other impairments to ambulation are excluded from this regulation.

(9) The use of bicycles, skateboards, tricycles, and any other such vehicles, as well as motorbikes, motorcycles, go-carts, and other motorized vehicles on Louisiana Nature and Science Center boardwalk, trails or ground other than roads. Wheelchairs and baby carriages are allowed on trails. Bikes, motorbikes and motorcycles are allowed to be locked up at the designated area of the boardwalk near the Exhibits Building, but must be walked to this area while on the boardwalk.

(10) Leaving trails, walkways, structures and other areas as marked and designated for use by the public by Louisiana Nature Center personnel. Leaving such areas may be permitted under the guidance of Louisiana Nature Center personnel. Leaving such designated areas without the above-mentioned guidance or permission is considered trespassing.

(11) Disturbing the peace, as defined in section 54-403, while on the Louisiana Nature Center ground.

(12) Any assemblies of people on the Louisiana Nature Center grounds for non-nature-study activities, including but not limited to private parties, speeches, or playing or making music.

(13) Soliciting visitors on the Louisiana Nature Center grounds.

(14) Presence of any individual on Louisiana Nature Center property from one-half hour after sunset until one-half hour before sunrise, except for Louisiana Nature Center staff members, persons

Supp. No. 112

CD106:22
PARKS AND RECREATION

§ 106-300

attending Louisiana Nature Center programs, persons assisting Louisiana Nature Center staff, and security persons.

(15) The use of sound-producing electronic or mechanical devices such as radios, tape players, or musical instruments on Louisiana Nature Center property in a way that might disturb wildlife or interfere with another person's enjoyment.

(16) Feeding of animals.

(17) Releasing any animal or placing plant materials on Louisiana Nature Center property.

(18) Picking of berries or other fruit or any edible or nonedible parts of plants.

(19) Climbing trees, pulling on branches, hanging from branches, and any other activities potentially harmful to trees, shrubs, or other plants, including building treehouses, forts, or placing steps upon tree limbs and trunks.

(20) Disturbance of wildlife feeding areas, nesting boxes or nesting animals. People wishing to set up photographic equipment to record nesting birds or other animals, or birds or other animals at feeding areas, shall obtain permission from the staff.

(21) Cars and other motor vehicles parked or operated in areas not designated for that purpose. Vehicles parked in nondesignated parking spaces are subject to tow-away.

(22) The flying of kites and model aircraft over Louisiana Nature Center property.

(23) Camping and the setting of fires.

(24) Possession of tools and/or markers or other instruments which could be used in a manner destructive to Louisiana Nature Center property, equipment or facilities.

(Code 1956, § 43-63)

laws.title: Warning signs
laws.content:
Signs shall be erected at each entrance to the grounds of the Louisiana Nature Center which shall cite the prohibitions enumerated in section 106-296. Such signs shall conform with all parks and parkway commission and the department of streets standards relative to placement, size, materials and erection as are considered applicable by those agencies.

(Code 1956, § 43-64)

Secs. 106-298, 106-299. Reserved.

laws.title: Hours of operation
laws.content:
City Park shall be open to the public daily from one-half hour before official sunrise to one-half hour after official sunset, at which time all persons must vacate City Park premises. Harrison and Filmore will remain open through City Park. The areas to be vacated are bounded by Wisner, Marconi and up to, but not including, Harrison and City Park Avenues and public areas from Harrison to Robert E. Lee.

(a) Overnight parking, walking, sleeping, and camping by individuals or groups is prohibited within the confines of City Park except upon special written permission obtained from City Park management.

(b) Any person found one-half hour after official sunset in areas other than those outlined herein for occupancy one-half hour after official sunset or without special written permission shall be considered to be disturbing the peace by their presence in such areas and shall be presumed to be doing damage to the grass, foliage, and other property of City Park.

(c) Exceptions to (b) above include special events extending beyond hours such as football games in the stadium, the softball complex, or at New Orleans Museum of Art (NOMA), or activities being held at Christian Brothers School, or any other recognized City Park facility as specified by City Park management. Persons attending such events are required to vacate City Park premises within 30

Supp. No. 112

CD106:23
§ 106-300

NEW ORLEANS CODE

minutes of the end of any such event. Employees and patrons of Morning Call Coffee Stand, open 24 hours per day, seven days per week and located in the Casino Building on Dreyfous Avenue, are also excepted from (b) above while traveling to or from the facility and while found within the facility.

(d) Golfers are permitted in the immediate vicinity of the Golf Club House if waiting for an early morning tee-off assignment.

(e) Boy and Girl Scouts of America may use Scout Island or other areas designated by City Park management provided they are under the direct supervision of adult Scout leaders and upon prior reservation.

(f) When Tad Gormley Stadium and the Marconi Meadow area are not scheduled for other events, groups with proper bedding facilities in portable trailers, campers or mobile dwellings may be permitted, upon proper application to City Park management, to occupy such enclosed areas overnight. Such groups must (1) comply with Group Rules relative to sanitation, (2) post liability insurance as outlined by the City Park Chief Executive Officer, and (3) provide sanitary, water, and electric facilities at the users' expense. Such groups are required to notify the City Park Superintendent of Police of the number of participants in their group and the date of their arrival and departure.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 22166, § 1, 3-16-06; M.C.S., Ord. No. 25940, § 1, 7-10-14)

laws.title: Prohibition of certain activities
laws.content:
It shall be unlawful for any person to engage in any of the activities herein below listed while within the confines of City Park. Those activities which shall be unlawful unless specifically approved by the director of the park are:

(a) No individuals or groups will be permitted to purchase or sell any food, drinks or novelties within the confines of the park,

unless approved in writing by park management in accordance with its contractual arrangements with various concessionaires.

(b) There shall be no trapping, hunting, discharging of firearms, or other noisemaking devices whatsoever in the park.

(c) It is prohibited to injure, molest, or kill any bird or animal in the park.

(d) No dog or other animal will be allowed to roam at large in the park. Orleans Parish leash laws for dogs must be adhered to except in designated dog parks or "off-leash" areas. The area known as City Bark is such an "off-leash" area and is generally bounded by Zachary Taylor Drive, Diagonal Drive, and Magnolia Drive within the boundaries of City Park.

(e) It is unlawful to throw into the lake, lagoons, fountains and basins any rock, trash or any other object whatsoever.

(f) It is prohibited to play any game of chance, or to have possession of any game of chance, within the park.

(g) It is prohibited to climb or get upon any tree, statue, fountain, fence, gateway, or railing within the park, or to use any structure within the park for other than the purpose for which it is intended, and in accordance with the regulations applying thereto.

(h) It is prohibited to deface, injure, move or remove any sign, notice or label place by park management within the park, to write upon, deface, defile or otherwise injure any building, fence, fountain, seat, statue, gateway, wall, or other structure within the park.

(i) It is prohibited to lie down upon, or to sleep upon, or overturn or damage any seat, bench, bridge, railing, or floor within the park.

(j) No boisterous, indecent, or vulgar language will be tolerated, nor any public nuisance shall be permitted.

Supp. No. 112
