**Sec. 114-77. Annual report; plan year.**

The board of trustees shall prepare and submit annually, on a calendar year basis, a report to the council showing the fiscal transactions of the system for the preceding year, the amounts of accumulated cash and securities in the various funds of the system and the last balance sheet showing the financial condition of the system.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 26460, § 2, 6-18-15)

**Sec. 114-78. Exclusive benefit.**

A. The trustees shall act solely and exclusively in the interests of members and their annuitants and beneficiaries; the assets comprising the trust, from time to time, shall be applied to payment of retirement allowances and other benefits hereunder and to discharge the reasonable and necessary expenses of the system.

B. Except as otherwise provided in this article, no trustee or employee of the board shall have any direct interest in the gains or profits of any investment made by the trust, nor shall any trustee, when acting as such, receive any pay or other compensation, direct or indirect, for his services. No trustee or employee of the board shall, directly or indirectly, for himself, or as an agent, in any manner use funds of the trust, except to make current and necessary payments authorized by the trustees.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 26460, § 2, 6-18-15)

**Sec. 114-79. Amendment.**

The city council shall possess the continuing power to amend this article, but no such amendment shall be adopted that reduces the then accrued benefit of any member, beneficiary or annuitant.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 26460, § 2, 6-18-15)

**Sec. 114-80. Termination.**

The city council shall possess the power to terminate the system, in whole or in part, or to permanently discontinue contributions hereto. In either event, the rights and benefits of affected members and their beneficiaries and annuitants accrued as of the date of such termination or discontinuance shall be nonforfeitable, the affected portion of the trust shall be allocated to fund such rights and benefits, and any excess remaining after such rights and benefits have been fully funded shall be returned to the applicable employer.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 26460, § 2, 6-18-15)

**Sec. 114-81. Punishment for fraud, etc.**

Whoever with the intent to deceive shall make any statement or report, give any notice required under this article that is untrue or falsify or permit to be falsified any record of the system in an attempt to defraud the system as a result of such act shall be guilty of a misdemeanor.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 26460, § 2, 6-18-15)

**Sec. 114-82. No assignment; domestic relations orders.**

A. The right of any person to an allowance or other benefit or accrual hereunder, including the return of member contributions, shall not be assigned or subject to execution, pledge, mortgage, garnishment or attachment; any attempt to assign, execute, pledge, mortgage, garnish or attach any such right, allowance, benefit accrual or return shall be void and of no effect.

B. If the interest of a member hereunder is community property subject to division in accordance with R.S. 9:2801B:

1. Any such division shall be evidenced by a court order reasonably acceptable to the trustees.

2. No benefit shall be payable pursuant to such order until the member’s retirement date.

3. The trustees shall adopt procedures for the division and payment of benefits to the member’s spouse pursuant to any such order.

4. The system and the trustees shall have no liability for any payment made prior to the receipt and acceptance of any such order.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 26460, § 2, 6-18-15)

laws.title: Manner of payment
laws.content:
Any amount payable hereunder, whether on account of retirement, disability or otherwise, shall be paid by means of electronic funds transfer from the system to an account designated by a member, annuitant, beneficiary or other person for such purpose, unless such member, annuitant, beneficiary or person establishes to the satisfaction of the trustees that such method of payment would result in substantial hardship or unintended expense.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 26460, § 2, 6-18-15)

Secs. 114-84—114-92. Reserved.

laws.title: Members
laws.content:
Membership of the system shall be determined as follows:

A. Eligible employees. Subject to the limitations set forth herein, any person who is or becomes an eligible employee shall be a member of the system as a condition of his employment.

B. Appointed or elected officials. Membership in the system shall be optional for officials who are appointed or elected for a fixed term. Such officials may become members with respect to such term by making written application for membership within 90 days after taking office. Any such election shall be effective with respect to a single term and shall be separately made (or a prior election affirmatively continued) with respect to each fixed term.

C. Change in status. If an active member ceases to be an eligible employee for any reason, he shall cease to be an active member hereunder; if he again becomes an eligible employee, his active membership shall then resume.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 26460, § 2, 6-18-15)

laws.title: Membership of parochial and judicial employees
laws.content:
Employees and officials of a judicial or parochial office of the Parish of Orleans who are otherwise eligible within the meaning of section 114-57 may apply for membership in the system, provided:

A. The trustees have approved such judicial or parochial office as an employer hereunder, and such office has agreed to contribute its respective employer contributions.

B. No such official or employee is required to be covered by another pension or system established under the laws of this state.

C. As a condition of such application, each official or employee shall consent to the deduction of member contributions from his contribution compensation.

The trustees shall adopt such additional procedures for membership as they deem necessary or appropriate.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 26460, § 2, 6-18-15)

Secs. 114-95—114-103. Reserved.

laws.title: Procedures for determination of service
laws.content:
A. The trustees shall determine and verify a member’s member contributions and creditable service by examination of his personnel and payroll records or by examination of records maintained by his employer. The trustees may require a member to provide proof of employment, service in the armed forces, base compensation and such other matters as the trustees deem relevant with respect to any credit to be made or purchased hereunder. The decision of the trustees as to such matters shall be final and binding.

Supp. No. 73

B. The board of trustees may adopt rules and procedures for the crediting and purchase of service hereunder, not inconsistent with the provisions of this division.

C. The trustees shall adopt equivalences to be applied with respect to the purchase of service not inconsistent with the provisions of this division, but in no case shall more than one year of service be credited for all service rendered within a single calendar year; there shall be no duplication of creditable service for any period of service, including military service.

D. In no event shall the trustees allow the purchase of creditable service hereunder for any period of more than one year during which an employee is absent continuously without pay, except for leave to perform service in the armed forces.

E. If a member who has separated from service and received a refund of his member account is later reemployed, he shall be permitted to purchase creditable service for such prior period of employment, provided he is then an active member.

F. Periods of creditable service for eligible part-time employment shall be prorated.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 26460, § 2, 6-18-15)

laws.title: Determination of creditable service
laws.content:
Creditable service shall equal the sum of:

A. Service while an active member during which member contributions have been made, but excluding any such service with respect to which a refund of such contributions has occurred.

B. An additional period, credited at the election of each active member, at the rate of one month for each 21 days of accumulated sick leave or annual leave.

C. Other service purchased or credited in accordance with the provisions of this division.

D. Service rendered prior to the establishment of the system, as verified by the trustees and purchased by or credited to a member.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 26460, § 2, 6-18-15)

laws.title: Service in the armed forces while an employee
laws.content:
If an active member enters into service with the armed forces and returns to covered employment not later than six months after his discharge from service in the armed forces, or such service constitutes qualified military service, he shall receive membership service for such period, provided that he was honorably discharged and pays member contributions and interest due with respect to such period.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 26460, § 2, 6-18-15)

laws.title: Service in armed forces before employment
laws.content:
A. An active member shall be entitled to purchase creditable service for active duty service in the armed forces before employment by his employer hereunder, excluding the National Guard or reserve service, provided that he was honorably discharged.

B. An active member shall be entitled to purchase additional creditable service for service in the National Guard or Reserve Forces of the United States before employment by his employer hereunder, provided that:

1. He was honorably discharged.

2. Creditable service for full-time active duty service is longer than five consecutive days and shall be based on one day of creditable service for one day of such service.

3. Creditable service for duty which is not full-time active duty shall be determined as one day of service for each drill point, provided that a member’s military employer provides written certification of the number of drill points earned and the time during which such points were earned.

§ 114-111

4. The term "active duty" shall mean full-time active military service under written military orders, which totals five or more consecutive days of service.

5. One year of creditable service shall be credited for each 252 drill points, which may be nonconsecutive.

C. A maximum of four years of creditable service shall be purchasable hereunder.

D. An active member shall be credited with at least five years of creditable service before any purchase hereunder.

E. A member who purchases creditable service hereunder shall not receive a benefit from any other retirement system of the State of Louisiana or its political subdivisions for such service.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 26460, § 2, 6-18-15)

laws.title: Credit for eligible part-time employment
laws.content:
An active member who is credited with at least five years of creditable service shall be entitled to purchase not more than four years of creditable service for eligible part-time employment with respect to services he rendered before 1989, subject to the following:

A. Such employment shall be continuous and shall immediately precede or follow not less than one year of other creditable service.

B. Additional service shall not be purchased for any period of contemporaneous full-time and eligible or ineligible part-time employment.

C. The number of months of creditable service purchased hereunder shall be calculated as the product of (1) the quotient obtained by dividing the number of hours worked each month during the period of eligible or ineligible part-time employment by the number of hours worked each month during a period of corresponding full-time employment, multiplied by (2) the number of months of eligible or ineligible part-time employment subject to purchase hereunder.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 26460, § 2, 6-18-15)

laws.title: Credit for transient or emergency service
laws.content:
An active member who is credited with not less than five years of creditable service may purchase a maximum of 90 days of creditable service for service rendered to the city in a transient or emergency appointment, provided that:

A. Such service shall otherwise constitute full-time employment.

B. Such service shall be consecutive with and immediately precede other creditable service hereunder.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 26460, § 2, 6-18-15)

laws.title: Credit for dual employment
laws.content:
An active member who, under the provisions of R.S. 11:3843, now repealed, was previously denied membership in the system, may purchase creditable service for any period he would otherwise be an eligible employee hereunder. Such purchase shall be made in accordance with the terms and conditions prescribed by the trustees in accordance with section 114-113 hereof.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 26460, § 2, 6-18-15)

laws.title: Credit for elected officials
laws.content:
An appointed or elected official with respect to a fixed term who first elects not to become an active member hereunder and thereafter, with respect to a subsequent fixed term, elects active membership hereunder, shall not be entitled to receive credit for service rendered before such election of active membership, unless:

A. He shall then have completed three years of active membership in the system; and

B. He shall have paid to the system the equivalent of his accumulated employee and employer contributions, with interest thereon.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 26460, § 2, 6-18-15)

Supp. No. 73

laws.title: Administrative error
laws.content:
A. If an eligible employee determines that he is not an active member, he shall immediately notify the personnel officer of his employer.

B. If an eligible employee is not an active member on account of administrative error by his employer:

1. He may purchase creditable service otherwise permitted hereunder, provided that the personnel officer of his employer shall certify to the trustees his dates of employment, his base and contribution compensation, whether such employment is full-time employment or eligible part-time employment, whether such employment is performed in a permanent, provisional, transient or emergency status, and the reason such employee was not timely enrolled in the system.

2. His employer shall pay to the system an amount equal to employer contributions due with respect to any period of creditable service purchased hereunder, including interest.

C. If an eligible employee believes that he is not enrolled in the system on account of his employer’s bad faith, willful misconduct or gross negligence, such employee shall provide notice to the trustees, and he shall be entitled to purchase creditable service otherwise permitted hereunder. The trustees shall determine whether interest due with respect to such contributions shall be paid by the employee, the employer or a combination thereof, based upon the relative fault of the employer and employee. In making such determination, the trustees shall consider:

1. The education or sophistication of the employee;

2. The length of time during which the employee was not an active member;

3. Whether the employee knew, or should have known, that he was not an active member;

4. Whether the employee inquired as to why he was not an active member or making member contributions, including a request to join the system; and

5. Such other factors as the trustee may deem relevant.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 26460, § 2, 6-18-15)

laws.title: Procedures for purchase of creditable service
laws.content:
A. Creditable service shall be purchased by payment of a single-sum, or over such longer period as the trustees deem appropriate, from time to time; provided that a member shall be permitted to purchase creditable service for any period of qualified military service periodically, over a period of not less than five years.

B. As a condition of the purchase of creditable service hereunder and except as provided in section 114-112 hereof, a member shall be required to pay to the system actuarial interest accrued on any member contributions required hereunder, at the rate determined by the trustees, except that interest with respect to the purchase of service in the armed forces shall not exceed four percent.

C. Contribution compensation for purposes of the purchase of creditable service hereunder shall be the rate of such compensation in effect at the time or immediately preceding the date or dates on which such service was rendered, or, with respect to military service before employment by an employer hereunder, the rate of such compensation in effect at the time such employment commenced.

D. The board may, but shall not be required, to accept a rollover from a member in consideration of the purchase of creditable service hereunder, provided that such rollover satisfies all of the following conditions:

1. The proceeds of such rollover shall be attributable to a period of participation in the system, another qualified governmental plan within the meaning of Tax Code Section 401(a), an eligible governmental plan within the meaning of Tax Code

Supp. No. 73

Section 457(b) or a tax deferred annuity within the meaning of Tax Code Section 403(b).

2. The amount of any rollover shall not exceed the amount necessary to purchase creditable service hereunder.

3. No portion of the proceeds of the rollover shall consist of after-tax contributions.

4. Any rollover shall be made in the form of a direct transfer from a trustee or custodian of a plan, account or annuity to the system.

5. As a condition of a rollover hereunder, the board may request such documents as it deems necessary; the board may adopt such additional procedures or require such additional certifications as it deems necessary or appropriate.

laws.title: Transfers of credits and funds
laws.content:
A. The transfer of credits and funds between the system and the retirement system maintained by the sewerage and water board shall be allowed in accordance with the following reciprocal agreement:

1. A member of either system, not yet retired, who is transferring from employment covered by one system to employment covered by the other system, may transfer his service credits and be given credit in the system to which he transfers for all his creditable service in the previous system, provided he meets the eligibility requirements specified in R.S. 33:4076.1 and R.S. 11:141—11:143, where the latter statute does not conflict with R.S. 11:3822, and provided all of the reserves necessary to fund his prior service and membership credit plus all allowable interest on these reserves are transferred from the sending system to the system to which he is being transferred.

2. The amount to be transferred hereunder shall be calculated as of the date of the transfer based upon the GASB No. 5 value of the member’s accumulated benefits,

using seven percent annual interest, a five percent annual salary scale, and the remaining actuarial assumptions in use by the sending system for purposes of determining GASB No. 5 liability at the time of transfer. Such amount shall not include a reserve for future cost-of-living benefits. The salary history and benefit structure of the member under the sending system shall be used in this calculation.

3. If a member withdrew his contributions from either system and wishes to receive credit for all past service in either system, he shall repay all contributions withdrawn, plus allowable interest thereon, to the system from which he transferred, after which such past service credits shall be transferred to his current system in accordance with the rules of the system from which he withdrew; thereafter, such service credit and funds shall be transferred in accordance with the provisions of subsections (1) and (2) of this section.

4. No membership service credits, that is service as an employee rendered after the date of the establishment of the system from which the employee is transferring, shall be allowed under this agreement for those periods where there are no employee contributions, unless the transferring employee pays for such uncontributed periods the amount that would have been contributed for such periods plus all allowable interest thereon, after which such service credit and funds can be transferred in accordance with the provisions of subsections (1) and (2) hereof.

5. This agreement shall be effective as of October 17, 1988. This agreement can be modified or amended only with consent of both pension boards together with ratification by the city council (for the city) and sewerage and water board (for the sewerage and water board). Any modification or amendment of this agreement shall not affect in any way the rights of any employee who has previously effected a trans-

fer under this agreement or who has initiated an application for transfer under the provisions of this agreement.

6. If the board or the pension committee of the retirement system of the sewerage and water board (hereinafter "pension committee") seeks to terminate this agreement, the party seeking termination shall follow the following provisions:

i. If the board wishes to terminate, it shall:

a. Provide the pension committee 30 days written notice before it meets to consider such action;

b. After proper notice has been given, the trustees shall meet to discuss and vote on resolution to terminate;

c. If such vote is affirmative, the trustees shall provide the pension committee written notice of not less than 30 days that it intends to seek approval from the city council to terminate the agreement; and

d. If the city council grants the trustees the authority to terminate this agreement, such termination shall not become effective until after the trustees provide the pension committee with 90 days written notice of termination.

ii. If the pension committee wishes to terminate, it shall:

a. Provide the trustees 30 days written notice before it meets to consider such action;

b. After proper notice has been given, the pension committee shall meet to discuss and vote on resolution to terminate;

c. If such vote is affirmative, the pension committee shall provide the trustees a written notice of not less than 30 days, that it intends to seek approval

from the sewerage and water board trustees to terminate the agreement; and

d. If the sewerage and water board grants the pension committee the authority to terminate this agreement, such termination shall not become effective until after the pension committee provides the trustees with a 90-day written notice of termination.

Termination shall not affect in any way the rights of any employee who has previously effected a transfer under this agreement or who has initiated an application for transfer under this agreement. Transfers of credits and funds to the system from the sewerage and water board retirement system shall not be permitted unless a reciprocity agreement is in effect.

B. Transfers of credits and funds between the system and state, municipal or parochial retirement systems in the state, other than the sewerage and water board retirement system, shall be permitted in accordance with applicable state law, including R.S. 11:141 et seq. (M.C.S., Ord. No. 26460, § 2, 6-18-15)

Secs. 114-115—114-123. Reserved.

laws.title: Eligibility for normal retirement
Determination of pensionable compensation
laws.content:
A member’s pensionable compensation shall be determined in accordance with the following:

A. If a member separates from service and is later reemployed, his periods of service before and after reemployment may be aggregated for purposes of determining his pensionable compensation.

B. In no event shall a member’s pensionable compensation for any calendar year exceed the limit then permitted under Tax Code Section 401(a)(17), as the same may be adjusted from time to time. Any change in such limit occurring during a calendar year shall be deemed effective as of the first day of such year. If pensionable compensation is determined with reference to a period of less than 12 months, the limit hereunder shall be prorated by multiplying the dollar limit then in effect by a fraction, the numerator of which is the number of months in such period and the denominator of which is 12.

C. In no event shall the annualized pensionable compensation of any member taken into account hereunder be less than such member’s compensation permitted to be taken into account under this section, or its equivalent, as of July 1, 1993, provided he was a member of the system as of such date.

D. A member’s consecutive months of pensionable compensation shall include the furlough period beginning August 1, 2010, and ending December 31, 2010, provided that member contributions and employer contributions are made with respect to such period. Base compensation attributable to such period shall be a member’s regular rate of base compensation then in effect but determined without adjustment for such furlough.

E. For members who commenced employment after January 1, 2018, in no event shall a member’s pensionable compensation for any calendar year exceed $100,000.00, adjusted for inflation as determined by the trustees from time to time.

F. For members who commenced employment after January 1, 2018 and are employed on and after January 1, 2021, notwithstanding any provision herein to the contrary, in no event shall such member’s pensionable compensation for any calendar year exceed $150,000.00, as the trustees may adjust for inflation from time to time.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 26460, § 2, 6-18-15; M.C.S., Ord. No. 27607, § 1, 12-1-17; M.C.S., Ord. No. 28530, § 2, 10-15-20; M.C.S., Ord. No. 29248, § 1, 11-3-22)

**Sec. 114-127. Amount of retirement allowance.**

A. For each active member who commenced employment before January 1, 2018, the amount of such member’s retirement allowance, expressed in the form of a member annuity, shall equal the sum of: (A) 2.5% of such member’s pensionable compensation multiplied by such member’s creditable service not in excess of 25 years, and (B) 4% of such member’s pensionable compensation multiplied by such member’s creditable service in excess of 25 years. For this purpose, creditable service with respect to which a member has received a refund shall be disregarded, unless such member has repaid an equivalent amount as determined by the trustees.

B. For each active member who commenced employment after January 1, 2018, the amount of such member’s retirement allowance, expressed in the form of a member annuity, shall equal 1.9% of such member’s pensionable compensation multiplied by such member’s creditable service.

C. For members who commenced employment after January 1, 2018 and are employed on and after January 1, 2021, notwithstanding any provision herein to the contrary, the amount of such member’s retirement allowance, expressed in the form of a member annuity, shall equal 2.5% of such member’s pensionable compensation multiplied by such member’s creditable service. For this purpose, creditable service for which a member has received a refund shall be disregarded, unless such member has repaid an equivalent amount as determined by the trustees. (M.C.S., Ord. No. 26460, § 2, 6-18-15; M.C.S., Ord. No. 27607, § 1, 12-1-17; M.C.S., Ord. No. 28530, § 3, 10-15-20)

**Sec. 114-128. Reduction for early payment.**

If a member’s retirement allowance commences before he attains age 62, such allowance shall be reduced by three percent for each year by which his retirement date precedes his attainment of such age, provided that no reduction shall be required:

A. If the member has at least 30 years of creditable service as of his retirement date; or

B. If the member’s age and creditable service total at least 80 points as of his separation date. This provision is not applicable for any member who commences employment after January 1, 2018.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 26460, § 2, 6-18-15; M.C.S., Ord. No. 27607, § 1, 12-1-17)

**Sec. 114-129. Late retirement.**

A member shall be entitled to designate a late retirement date, which may be later than the date or dates determined in accordance with section 114-125 hereof, but shall not be later than April 1st of the calendar year following the later of (A) the year in which the member attains age 70½, or (B) the member’s separation date.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 26460, § 2, 6-18-15)

**Sec. 114-130. Form of retirement allowance.**

A. A member shall designate the form in which his retirement allowance shall be paid from among the following optional forms of payment, each of which shall be the actuarial equivalent of the other, as follows:

1. “Option One,” which shall be an annuity that provides equal monthly payments for the life of a member; provided that if the member shall die before the actuarial value of his member account has been paid, the remainder shall be paid to his beneficiary in the form of a single-sum.

2. “Option Two,” which shall be an annuity providing equal monthly payments for the life of the member and the same amount for the life of his annuitant; provided that (i) if the member’s annuitant predeceases the member, an annuity determined in accordance with subsection 1 hereof shall thereafter be paid to such surviving member and, if the member dies before the actuarial value of his member account has been distributed, any remainder shall be distributed to the member’s beneficiary, (ii) if the member predeceases his annuitant and the annuitant dies before the actuarial value of the member account has been

distributed, any remainder shall be distributed to the annuitant's beneficiary, and (iii) if the member's annuitant is not his surviving spouse, any survivor benefit payable hereunder shall not exceed the maximum percentage permitted under Tax Code Section 401(a)(9).

3. "Option Three," which shall be an annuity providing equal monthly payments for the life of the member and one-half of such amount for the life of his annuitant; provided that (i) if the member's annuitant predeceases the member, an annuity determined in accordance with subsection 1 hereof shall thereafter be paid to such surviving member; and, if the member dies before the actuarial value of his member account has been distributed, any remainder shall be distributed to the member's beneficiary, (ii) if the member predeceases his annuitant and the annuitant dies before the actuarial value of the member account has been distributed, any remainder shall be distributed to the annuitant's beneficiary, and (iii) if the member's annuitant is not his surviving spouse, the survivor benefit payable hereunder shall not exceed the maximum percentage permitted under Tax Code Section 401(a)(9).

4. "Option Four," which shall refer to such other form of payment as the trustees may, from time to time, designate, subject to such limitations, terms and conditions as the trustees deem necessary and appropriate.

B. If the trustees determine that monthly payment of an annuity is or becomes impracticable on account of its amount, the trustees may direct that such monthly payments be aggregated and paid on an annual, semi-annual or quarterly basis.

C. Any amount payable in the form of a single-sum to a beneficiary hereunder shall be paid not later than the last day of the calendar year that contains the fifth anniversary of the date of the member's death.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 26460, § 2, 6-18-15)

laws.title: Minimum retirement allowance
laws.content:
Notwithstanding any provision of this article to the contrary, in no case shall the value of the member annuity for a member who is credited with at least ten years of creditable service for full-time employment be less than $300.00 each month.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 26460, § 2, 6-18-15)

laws.title: Maximum retirement allowance
laws.content:
In no case shall the amount of a member annuity hereunder, determined as of a member's retirement date, exceed his annualized pensionable compensation as of such date, except that the foregoing limitation shall not apply:

A. To any member whose accrued benefits hereunder were in excess of such amount as of May 7, 1978.

B. To any distribution made from a member's DROP account.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 26460, § 2, 6-18-15)

laws.title: Reemployment; suspension of retirement allowance
laws.content:
If a member retires and receives a retirement allowance hereunder, the payment of such allowance shall be suspended if the member is reemployed by the employer. In such event, payment of his retirement allowance shall again commence after the member again separates from service; such member's periods of creditable service and pensionable compensation shall be recalculated taking into account service and compensation before and after his reemployment.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 26460, § 2, 6-18-15)

laws.title: Tax Code limitation
laws.content:
The value of a member's annualized retirement allowance, when expressed in the form of an annual benefit as defined herein, shall not exceed the maximum permissible amount. If the value of a member's annual benefit would exceed such amount, the value of such benefit shall be reduced to the maximum permissible amount.

Supp. No. 102

§ 114-134

NEW ORLEANS CODE

For this purpose, a member’s “maximum permissible amount” shall be the dollar limit set forth in Tax Code Section 415(b)(1)(A), as the same may be indexed from time to time under Tax Code Section 415(d), and subject to adjustment as provided herein.

A. A member’s “annual benefit” shall be the actuarial equivalent of a member’s retirement allowance, determined as a single life annuity payable under a plan to which members do not contribute and to which rollover contributions are not made. Such equivalent shall be determined using (1) an interest rate equal to the greater of 5.5%, the rate otherwise specified herein or the rate that provides a benefit of not more than 105% of the benefit derived from the interest rate specified in Tax Code Section 417(e)(3), and (2) the mortality table specified in Tax Code Section 417(e). The value of such annual benefit shall further be determined as follows:

1. The value of such benefit shall not include any after-tax member contributions, which contributions, if any, shall be separately subject to the limitations imposed under Tax Code Section 415(c).

2. The value of such benefit shall include the value of any amount paid by a member to purchase creditable service hereunder, except that:

   i. Amounts paid for service with the armed forces as contemplated under Tax Code Section 414(n) shall not be included;

   ii. Any amount transferred from another qualified governmental plan or governmental Tax Code Section 457(b) plan shall not be included; and

   iii. Reserved.

3. The value of such benefit shall not include any amount attributable to the transfer of service credit hereunder.

B. If a member retires before he attains age 62, such member’s maximum permissible amount shall be reduced to equal an annual benefit commencing as of such member’s retirement date that is the actuarial equivalent of such amount payable at age 62, determined using (1) an interest rate equal to the greater of five percent or the rate otherwise specified herein, and (2) the mortality table determined in accordance with Tax Code Section 417(e). Notwithstanding the foregoing, such adjustment shall not apply to any benefit payable on account of the death or disability of a member.

C. If a member retires after he attains age 65, such member’s maximum permissible Amount shall be actuarially adjusted to reflect such delayed retirement using (1) an interest rate equal to the lesser of five percent or the rate otherwise specified herein, and (2) the mortality table required under Tax Code Section 417(e).

D. If a member is credited with less than ten years of participation in the system, the Maximum Permissible Amount determined hereunder shall be reduced by $1/10$ for each year of such participation less than ten.

E. Notwithstanding the foregoing, in no event shall the retirement allowance of a member be reduced as provided herein if he is a qualified member. For this purpose, a “qualified member” is a member who commenced participation hereunder prior to January 1, 1990.

F. The limitations set forth herein shall not apply to any member if (1) his or her retirement benefit hereunder, including any retirement benefit paid from any other tax-qualified retirement plan maintained by the city or another participating employer hereunder, does not exceed $10,000.00 each year, and (2) no such employer has at any time maintained a defined contribution plan in which such member participated.

§ 114-136

G. If the maximum permissible amount increases after a member separates from service, the amount of any limitation imposed hereunder shall thereafter take into account such increase.

H. If a member retires before January 1, 2007, then notwithstanding any provision herein to the contrary:

1. The value of such member’s annual benefit shall not include any amount attributable to the transfer of service or benefits hereunder.

2. Member contributions made in the form of after-tax contributions shall be subject to the limitations on contributions applicable to defined contribution plans imposed under Code Section 415.

3. If such member’s retirement allowance includes a rollover hereto, the value of such rollover shall be included in the determination of such member’s annual benefit by applying reasonable actuarial assumptions.

4. If such member retires after the attainment of age 65, the maximum permissible amount shall be determined without regard to subsection C hereof.

5. If such member retires before attainment of age 62, the adjustment set forth in subsection B hereof shall not apply.

6. If a member’s retirement allowance is payable in a form other than a single life annuity, such allowance shall be expressed as the actuarial equivalent of a single life annuity.

I. The terms of this section are to be interpreted and construed in accordance with the provisions of Tax Code Section 415(b) and the regulations promulgated thereunder, the terms of which are incorporated herein by this reference.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 26460, § 2, 6-18-15; M.C.S., Ord. No. 27607, § 1, 12-1-17)

laws.title: Additional payments
laws.content:
A. The board may be authorized to retain trust earnings or gains in excess of an average three and one-half percent, which amount may be applied to provide one or more cost-of-living increases or bonuses for members who have retired, in an annual amount not to exceed three percent of each such member’s initial retirement allowance multiplied by each year of such member’s retirement, provided that the system’s actuarial funded ratio is at least 65 percent. Such benefit, if any, may be awarded and paid when funds are available from this source as provided herein, and in the manner and at the time or times determined in the discretion of the trustees.

B. Notwithstanding subsection A, the board may be authorized to provide a cost-of-living increase or bonus to help adjust for actual changes in members’ cost of living if the city appropriates sufficient funds to fully prefund the increase or bonus described in this subsection in the year the benefit is provided.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 26460, § 2, 6-18-15; M.C.S., Ord. No. 27607, § 1, 12-1-17; M.C.S., Ord. No. 29248, § 1, 11-3-22)

laws.title: Direct rollovers
laws.content:
A member, his spouse or, effective as of January 1, 2008, his annuitant or other beneficiary, may direct the trustees to roll over any eligible distribution hereunder, subject to the following:

A. Rollover shall be made to the plan, account or annuity designated by the member or other distributee. In the case of a member, such plan, account or annuity may be an individual retirement account described in Tax Code Section 408(a), an individual retirement annuity described in Tax Code Section 408(b), an annuity plan described in Tax Code Section 403(a), a qualified trust described in Tax Code Section 401(a), or an eligible governmental plan described in Tax Code Section 457(b). In the case of a rollover made for the benefit of a beneficiary or annuitant or a member’s
§ 114-136

NEW ORLEANS CODE

spouse, an eligible retirement plan shall be an individual retirement account or individual retirement annuity.

B. No amount shall be eligible for rollover hereunder if it is one of a series of substantially equal periodic payments made not less frequently than annually for the life or life expectancy of the distributee or the joint lives or joint life expectancies of a member and his annuitant or beneficiary, or for a specified period of ten years or more or a required minimum distribution under Tax Code Section 401(a)(9).

C. A direct rollover hereunder shall not be required with respect to amounts of less than $200.00.

D. The trustees shall furnish to each member, annuitant or beneficiary eligible to direct a rollover hereunder a notice containing the information described in Tax Code Section 402(f), which notice shall be furnished within a reasonable time prior to a distribution eligible for rollover hereunder.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 26460, § 2, 6-18-15)

laws.title: Early or voluntary retirement
laws.content:
A. A member shall be eligible for early or voluntary retirement as provided herein if all of the following conditions are satisfied:

1. Such member's retirement date is no earlier than October 19, 2020 and no later than December 31, 2020.

2. Such member separates from service no later than the designated retirement date and such member does not return to eligible full-time employment.

3. Such member irrevocably waives participation in DROP.

4. Such member purchases creditable service by the conversion of all accumulated sick leave.

5. Such member agrees to the waiver of certain claims in the form and at the time prescribed by the trustees.

B. A member who elects early retirement shall further satisfy the following:

1. Such member shall be credited with at least 15 years of creditable service as the member's designated retirement date, including creditable service purchased by the conversion of annual or sick leave; and

2. Such member shall have accumulated at least 70 points as of the designated retirement date, determined as the sum of the member's attained age and creditable service as of such date.

C. A member who elects voluntary retirement shall further be eligible for normal retirement (as defined in section 114-125) as of the member's designated retirement date.

D. The retirement allowance of a member who satisfies the conditions set forth herein and timely elects early retirement shall not be subject to reduction for early payment under section 114-128, regardless of the age of such member.

E. A member who satisfies the conditions set forth herein and timely elects voluntary retirement shall receive:

1. A 1% increase in the base amount of the annual retirement allowance payable as of such member's retirement date, to be prorated and paid monthly, such increase (a) to be made annually commencing as of January 1, 2022 and (b) to be made during the life of the member and any annuitant.

2. A payment in the amount of $50.00 for each full year of employment, but not less than $1,000.00, which amount shall be paid (a) annually during the ten-year period commencing as of January 1, 2022 and (b) to such member's beneficiary, beneficiaries or annuitant if such member dies prior to the payment of all such amounts.

Supp. No. 102

CD114:24
PERSONNEL

§ 114-147

F. A member who satisfies the conditions for voluntary retirement hereunder but has not yet attained age 62 may elect either early or voluntary retirement; there shall be no duplication of benefits hereunder.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 28530, § 4, 10-15-20)

Secs. 114-138—114-144. Reserved.

laws.title: DROP election
laws.content:
A. Members who commenced employment after January 1, 2018 and members with less than ten years of active service as of January 1, 2018 may elect to participate in DROP in accordance with subsection B herein, but the DROP period for each such member shall not exceed three years measured from the date on which his DROP period commenced.

B. Subject to the limitation in subsection A herein, a member who is otherwise eligible for normal retirement in accordance with section 114-125 hereof may elect to participate in DROP. Any such election shall be made on forms prescribed by the trustees and shall be subject to the following terms and conditions:

1. Such member shall designate the date on which his DROP period will commence, which shall not be earlier than 30 days after the date on which his DROP election is received and accepted by the trustees.

2. Such member shall designate his DROP period, which shall not exceed five years, or three years for those employees in the groups designated in subsection A herein, measured from the date on which his DROP period commenced and which period shall terminate earlier in the event a member separates from service before the end of the designated period.

3. Such member shall designate the form in which his retirement allowance shall be paid in accordance with section 114-131 hereof.

4. Unless otherwise permitted by the trustees, any such member may elect to participate in DROP only once; a member may revoke his DROP election or reduce the duration of his DROP period at any time prior to the date on which he receives a distribution of all or a portion of the amount credited to his DROP account, at which time such member’s election shall be deemed irrevocable.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 26460, § 2, 6-18-15; M.C.S., Ord. No. 27607, § 1, 12-1-17)

laws.title: DROP retirement
laws.content:
Upon the effective date of a member’s DROP election:

A. He shall cease to be an active member of the system.

B. The amount of his retirement allowance shall be determined, based upon such member’s pensionable compensation and creditable service as of his retirement date, but excluding any service reciprocally recognized under R.S. 11:142.

C. During such member’s DROP period, his DROP account shall be credited with the amount of his monthly retirement allowance determined in accordance with subsection B hereof and interest at the rate determined in accordance with section 114-147 hereof.

D. At the end of such member’s DROP period, the balance then credited to his DROP account shall be distributed in accordance with section 114-148 hereof.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 26460, § 2, 6-18-15)

laws.title: DROP interest
laws.content:
A member’s DROP account shall be credited with interest at the rate determined annually by the trustees. Such interest shall be credited annually as of the last day of each calendar year. Interest shall be credited hereunder for the period commencing as of the date on which a member’s DROP account is established and ending

Supp. No. 102

CD114:24.1
§ 114-147

NEW ORLEANS CODE

as of the earlier of (A) the end of such member's DROP period, or (B) such member's separation date.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 26460, § 2, 6-18-15)

laws.title: Distributions from DROP account
laws.content:
A. When a member separates from service, whether during his DROP period, at the conclusion thereof or thereafter, the balance then credited to his DROP account shall be distributed to him in the form of a (1) single-sum payment, (2) substantially equal installment payments over a period designated by such member, not in excess of 119 monthly payments, or (3) in such other manner as then may be permitted by the trustees. His monthly retirement allowance shall thereafter be paid to him.

B. If a member becomes disabled during his DROP period and he separates from service on account of such disability, he shall receive the balance then credited to his DROP account in the form of a single-sum payment or in such other manner as then may be permitted by the trustees. His retirement allowance shall thereafter be paid to him.

C. If a member dies during his DROP period, his beneficiary shall receive the amount then credited to his DROP account in the form of a single-sum payment, and the member's annuitant, if any, shall receive any survivor benefit payable in accordance with the terms of the member's retirement allowance in effect during the DROP period.

D. If a member dies during an installment payment period, the remaining payments shall be made to his beneficiary, at the time or times such amounts would have been paid to the deceased member, and the member's annuitant, if any, shall receive any survivor benefit payable in accordance with the terms of the member's retirement allowance in effect during the DROP period.

Supp. No. 102

CD114:24.2
PERSONNEL

§ 114-162

E. Any single-sum payment hereunder shall be made as soon as practicable following a member’s retirement or disability; in the event of a member’s death, in no event shall such payment be made later than the last day of the calendar year that includes the fifth anniversary of the member’s date of death.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 26460, § 2, 6-18-15)

laws.title: Continuation of employment
laws.content:
If a member continues his employment after the end of his DROP period, payment of his monthly retirement allowance shall be suspended and credits to his DROP account shall cease. He may again become an active member, provided he is then an eligible employee and his employer agrees to pay to the system the actuarial cost of such resumption of membership. Any amount accrued after the end of the member’s DROP period shall be paid as a supplement to his original retirement allowance, which shall not be recomputed. Such member’s retirement allowance shall again commence as of his separation date, without liability for any payments suspended hereunder.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 26460, § 2, 6-18-15)

laws.title: Fees and expenses
laws.content:
A member’s DROP account shall not be subject to any fees or charges.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 26460, § 2, 6-18-15)

Secs. 114-151—114-159. Reserved.

laws.title: Separation from service before retirement; refunds
laws.content:
A. A member who separates from service before January 1, 2002, and is then credited with not less than ten years of creditable service shall be entitled to (1) retain his member account in the system and receive a retirement allowance commencing not earlier than his age 60 determined in accordance with division 5 hereof, or (2) receive a single-sum distribution of his member account.

B. A member who separates from service on or after January 1, 2002, and is then credited with not less than five years of creditable service shall be entitled to (1) retain his member account in the system and receive a retirement allowance in accordance with division 5 hereof, or (2) receive a single-sum distribution of his member account. For this purpose, the interest of such member in his retirement allowance shall be deemed vested and non-forfeitable upon (1) an earlier date that may be determined hereunder, or (2) when he is credited with at least five years of creditable service and has attained age 65.

C. A member who separates from service and is not then credited with five years of creditable service shall receive a distribution of his member account in the form of a single-sum payment. If such member has not directed the distribution of his member account during the five-year period following his separation, the trustees shall distribute such amount in the form of a single-sum payment in lieu of any benefit or allowance otherwise payable hereunder. In such event, if the member fails to provide distribution instructions to the trustees and the balance of his member account is more than $1,000.00, the trustees shall rollover such balance to an individual retirement account designated and established by them for the benefit of such member.

D. A member who is inducted into the armed forces and thereafter provides extended military service may request a withdrawal of his member account, which shall be paid in the form of a single-sum distribution.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 26460, § 2, 6-18-15)

laws.title: Repayment permitted
laws.content:
If a member separates from service, receives a distribution of his member account and again becomes an active member hereunder, he may repay the full amount of such distribution, together with interest thereon as determined by the trustees, and his prior creditable service shall be restored.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 26460, § 2, 6-18-15)

laws.title: Gross misconduct
laws.content:
Notwithstanding any provision of the system to the contrary, if a member involuntarily separates

Supp. No. 73

CD114:25
§ 114-162

NEW ORLEANS CODE

from service on account of his gross misconduct, as determined by the trustees, he shall receive a single-sum distribution of his member account, in lieu of any benefit or allowance payable hereunder. For this purpose, the term "gross misconduct" shall mean a member's dishonesty, wrongdoing, or a violation of law. For this purpose, no act shall be deemed gross misconduct hereunder unless the trustees shall determine it is an intentional act or it is an act of wanton disregard.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 26460, § 2, 6-18-15)

Secs. 114-163—114-171. Reserved.

laws.title: Ordinary disability retirement
laws.content:
A. A member may apply to the trustees for retirement on account of his ordinary disability, provided that:

1. He is credited with not less than ten years of creditable service at the time of his disability;

2. He has exhausted all remedies available under applicable law, including but not limited to the Americans With Disabilities Act; and

3. The trustees have determined that he is disabled.

The trustees shall process such application as soon as practicable following its receipt and acceptance, but not later than 90 days after receipt of all information necessary to process such application.

B. Upon a member's retirement on account of his ordinary disability, he shall receive, in lieu of any benefit or allowance otherwise payable hereunder:

1. A retirement allowance in accordance with division 5 hereof, if he is otherwise eligible; or

2. An "ordinary disability retirement allowance" equal to 75 percent of the amount determined (i) as if such member continued as an active member hereunder until he attained age 65, and (ii) using his pensionable compensation determined as of the date of his disability. Such amount shall be paid in equal monthly payments during the life of such member, with no death or survivor benefit payable to any person.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 26460, § 2, 6-18-15)

laws.title: Accidental disability retirement
laws.content:
A. A member may apply to the trustees for retirement on account of his accidental disability, provided that:

1. He has exhausted all remedies available under applicable law, including but not limited to the Americans With Disabilities Act; and

2. The trustees shall have determined that he is disabled and that such disability is an accidental disability.

The trustees shall process such application as soon as practicable following its receipt and acceptance, but not later than 90 days after receipt of all information necessary to process such application.

B. Upon a member's retirement on account of accidental disability, he shall receive, in lieu of any benefit or allowance otherwise payable from the system:

1. A retirement allowance in accordance with division 5 hereof, if he is otherwise eligible; or

2. An annual allowance, an "accidental disability retirement allowance," equal to 65 percent of his pensionable earnings determined as of the year preceding the year in which such disability occurs. Such allowance shall be paid in equal monthly payments during the life of such member, with no death or survivor benefit payable to any person.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 26460, § 2, 6-18-15)

laws.title: Member account refund
laws.content:
If a member dies before he has received the balance of his member account, whether in the

Supp. No. 73

CD114:26
PERSONNEL

§ 114-177

form of an accidental disability retirement allowance or an ordinary disability retirement allowance, his beneficiary shall be paid the balance of such account in the form of a single-sum, which payment shall be made not later than the last day of the calendar year that includes the fifth anniversary of the member’s date of death.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 26460, § 2, 6-18-15)

**Sec. 114-175. Reexamination; return to active membership.**

A. Once each year during the first five years following the commencement of an ordinary or accidental disability retirement allowance hereunder, and once each three years thereafter until a disabled member attains age 60, he shall be required to establish that he remains disabled in accordance with the rules and procedures established by the trustees. If he shall refuse reexamination, his accidental or ordinary disability retirement allowance shall be suspended and, upon the expiration of six months, such allowance shall be revoked.

B. If, upon reexamination, a member is able to pursue gainful employment, his accidental or ordinary disability retirement allowance shall be discontinued upon his restoration to his former position or a substantially similar position with his employer.

C. If a member receiving an ordinary or accidental disability retirement allowance again resumes employment with his employer, his allowance shall cease and he shall again be an active member of the system. Periods of creditable service before and after such disability shall be aggregated for purposes of determining his retirement benefit, provided that the period of such accidental or ordinary disability retirement shall not be taken into account.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 26460, § 2, 6-18-15)

**Sec. 114-176. Income certification.**

A. A member receiving an accidental or ordinary disability retirement allowance shall furnish to the trustees not later than May 1st of each year a notarized statement that includes all earnings from employment during the preceding year. Failure to provide such statement may, in the discretion of the trustees, result in the suspension or discontinuance of an allowance hereunder.

B. If the trustees determine that a member receiving an accidental or ordinary disability retirement allowance is engaged in gainful employment, the earnings or compensation with respect to which are greater than the difference between his accidental or ordinary disability retirement allowance hereunder and his pensionable compensation, such allowance shall be reduced in the amount necessary to ensure that the sum of such allowance and his earnings do not exceed his pensionable compensation. Such determination shall be made and allowances shall be adjusted hereunder on an annual basis; provided, however, that any benefit payable from the system shall not be less than the actuarial equivalent of his member account, determined as of the date of his disability.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 26460, § 2, 6-18-15)

**Sec. 114-177. Offset of accidental or ordinary disability retirement allowances.**

If a member receives an accidental or ordinary disability allowance and also receives workers’ compensation benefits, Social Security benefits or compensatory benefits under similar laws:

A. Any benefit or allowance payable hereunder on account of such disability shall be offset by the amount of workers’ compensation or similar benefits representing income replacement, excluding any amount that is allocable to such member’s medical expenses.

B. Notwithstanding any offset permitted hereunder, any benefit payable from the system shall not be less than the actuarial equivalent of his member account, determined as of the date of his disability.

C. As a condition of the receipt of benefits hereunder, each member shall certify to the trustees the existence and disposition of any Social Security or workers’ compensation claim, at such time or times and in such manner as the trustees shall prescribe. A member’s failure to provide such

Supp. No. 73

CD114:27
§ 114-177

NEW ORLEANS CODE

information may result in the suspension of any accidental or ordinary disability allowance otherwise payable hereunder.

D. The trustees shall possess the authority to administer any offset or reduction described herein. The decision of the trustees as to the amount and time of any offset shall be final and binding.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 26460, § 2, 6-18-15)

laws.title: Maximum allowance
laws.content:
In no case shall the amount of an accidental disability allowance or ordinary disability allowance hereunder, expressed in the form of a member annuity and determined as of the date of a member’s disability, exceed his annualized pensionable compensation as of such date.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 26460, § 2, 6-18-15)

Secs. 114-179—114-186. Reserved.

laws.title: Beneficiaries and annuitants
Death while an active member
laws.content:
A. If an active member dies before his retirement, his beneficiary shall be paid the balance of his member account in the form of a single-sum.

B. If an active member is credited with not less than three years of creditable service as of the date of his death, then in addition to any amount payable under subsection A hereof, his beneficiary shall receive a single-sum equal to the lesser of:

1. His base compensation, determined with respect to the calendar year preceding the year in which his date of death occurred; or

2. The sum of (a) 25 percent of his base compensation determined with respect to the calendar year preceding the year in which his date of death occurred, and (b) five percent of such base compensation for each year of creditable service in excess of one.

Supp. No. 73

CD114:28
PERSONNEL

§ 114-193

C. If an active member, as of the date of his death (1) has attained age 55 and is credited with not less than ten years of creditable service or is credited with not less than 20 years of creditable service without regard to his age, disregarding any purchase of military service except qualified military service, and (2) such deceased member’s sole primary beneficiary is his surviving spouse, then such spouse may elect to receive a monthly annuity commencing as of the member’s date of death and ending when such spouse attains the earliest age of eligibility for Social Security widow/widower benefits. The benefit provided hereunder shall be in lieu of any other benefit from the system.

D. If an active member is otherwise eligible for retirement as of the date of his death, and such deceased member is survived by his spouse, then in lieu of any benefit hereunder, such spouse shall receive the survivor’s portion of the Option 2 annuity, determined as if the member had retired immediately before his date of death.

E. Any benefit payable hereunder shall be determined without regard to any military service purchased by the deceased member.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 26460, § 2, 6-18-15)

laws.title: Death after separation from service
laws.content:
If a member dies after his separation from service and:

A. Such member is not then eligible to receive a retirement allowance, the balance of his member account, if any, shall be distributed to his beneficiary in the form of a single-sum payment.

B. Such member is then otherwise eligible for retirement and survived by a spouse, then in lieu of any benefit otherwise payable hereunder, his spouse shall receive the survivor’s portion of the Option 2 annuity, determined as if such member had retired immediately before his death.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 26460, § 2, 6-18-15)

laws.title: Death after retirement
laws.content:
If a member dies after his retirement, his beneficiary or annuitant, as the case may be, shall receive the refund, payment, or survivor benefit, if any, determined in accordance with sections 114-131 or 114-148 hereof, based upon the form of payment in effect as of the date of the member’s death.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 26460, § 2, 6-18-15)

laws.title: Time of payment
laws.content:
A. Any benefit or refund payable on account of a member’s death in the form of a single-sum shall be paid as soon as practicable following the date of the member’s death, but in no event later than five years following the last day of the calendar year in which such date of death occurs.

B. Any benefit payable on account of a member’s death in the form of an annuity shall commence as soon as practicable after the date of the member’s death, but in no event later than one year after such death.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 26460, § 2, 6-18-15)

laws.title: Qualified military service
laws.content:
If a member dies while performing qualified military service and his date of death is on or after January 1, 2007, for purposes of any death or survivor benefit hereunder, other than benefit accruals with respect to the period of such service, such member shall be deemed to have resumed his employment with the employer and then died immediately thereafter.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 26460, § 2, 6-18-15)

laws.title: Offset for workers’ compensation or social security
laws.content:
If a member’s spouse or other beneficiary receives a benefit under section 114-188 and also receives workers’ compensation benefits, Social Security benefits or compensatory benefits under a similar laws:

A. Any such benefit or allowance payable on account of an accidental death shall be offset by the amount of workers’ compensation or similar benefits representing

CD114:29
§ 114-193

NEW ORLEANS CODE

income replacement, excluding any amount that is allocable to such member's medical expenses.

B. Notwithstanding any offset permitted hereunder, any benefit payable from the system shall not be less than the actuarial equivalent of his member account, determined as of the date of his disability.

C. The trustees shall possess the authority to administer any offset or reduction described herein. The decision of the trustees as to the amount and time of any offset shall be final and binding.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 26460, § 2, 6-18-15)

Secs. 114-194—114-200. Reserved.

laws.title: System to maintain three accounts
laws.content:
The system shall, for the benefit of each member, maintain three individual accounts for bookkeeping purposes:

A. A member account to which (1) member contributions and interest thereon shall be allocated, including any amount paid by such member for the purchase of creditable service in accordance with division 4 hereof, (2) any withdrawals or refunds or distributions made on account of his separation from service or death shall be charged, and (3) any transfer from the pension accumulation account on account of a member's repayment of his member account balance shall be made.

B. A pension accumulation account to or from which (1) employer contributions attributable to such member, income and gain thereon shall be credited, (2) any gift or similar amount shall be credited, (3) any single-sum death benefit shall be charged, (4) an amount equal to interest accrued with respect to a member account and interest accrued on the mean amount of the reserves in the annuity reserve account shall be charged, and (5) a transfer to a member's member account shall be made on account of his repayment of his member account.

C. An annuity reserve account, which (1) shall be credited with the balance of the member's member account and pension accumulation account as of his retirement, and (2) shall be charged with such member's retirement allowance or other benefit payable hereunder.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 26460, § 2, 6-18-15)

laws.title: Member account interest
laws.content:
Interest shall be credited to each member account as of each December 31st, at the rate determined by the trustees from time to time. Such crediting shall cease upon the earlier of (A) the date on which no amount is credited to such account, (B) a member's death or retirement date or other commencement of benefits hereunder, or (C) five years after his separation from service, if such member is credited with less than five years of creditable service as of his separation date.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 26460, § 2, 6-18-15)

laws.title: Member contributions
laws.content:
A. Each active member shall contribute to the system member contributions in an amount equal four percent of his contribution compensation; beginning January 1, 2012, and ending December 31, 2012, such contributions shall equal five percent of contribution compensation; beginning January 1, 2013, and thereafter, such contributions shall equal six percent of contribution compensation.

B. Each active member's employer shall automatically deduct such contributions from his contribution compensation on a pay period basis, and each such member shall be deemed to have consented to such deduction, without the necessity of further action. Payment of any amount, allowance, withdrawal or other benefit hereunder shall be deemed to constitute a discharge and release of any claim or demand related to such deduction.

C. Each employer shall remit member contributions to the system at the time or times designated by the trustees, but no less frequently than monthly.

Supp. No. 73

CD114:30
PERSONNEL

§ 114-206

D. Member contributions hereunder are intended to be "pick-up contributions" and shall be made and administered in the manner prescribed under Tax Code Section 414(h)(2).

E. Member contributions hereunder shall be deemed part of a member's compensation for purposes of determining whether such compensation is less than the minimum amount required by law to be provided. Payment of a member's compensation due for any period, reduced as provided herein, shall be deemed to discharge and acquit the city and his employer with respect to services rendered by such member during such period, except as to any prospective claim for benefits or payments hereunder.

F. The trustees shall adopt such procedures as may be necessary for the collection and remission of member contributions hereunder.  
(M.C.S., Ord. No. 26460, § 2, 6-18-15)

laws.title: Employer contributions
laws.content:
A. The city or other employer of each active member shall contribute to the system.

B. Each year, the system's actuarial report shall include the amount actuarially necessary, when aggregated with member contributions, to provide for the payment of benefits accrued hereunder. Such amount shall be determined in accordance with generally accepted actuarial principles, consistent with the actuarial standards of practice, as promulgated from time to time by the actuarial standards board, and the statements of the governmental accounting standards board as they relate to the disclosure, accounting, and funding of pension plans, as the same may be amended, superseded or replaced from time to time.

C. The trustees shall annually review the system's actuarial valuation and determine the amount of the annual contribution necessary and appropriate hereunder.

D. Contributions hereunder shall ordinarily be expressed as a uniform percentage of each active member's contribution compensation.

E. During the city's annual budgeting process, the board may be authorized to request an addition to the annual required contribution rate (ARC) to specifically fund cost-of-living increases or bonuses. The funding shall come in the form of an increase in the city or other employer contribution rate. The increase shall be no more than one-half of one percent of the system's actuarial valuation.  
(M.C.S., Ord. No. 26460, § 2, 6-18-15; M.C.S., Ord. No. 29248, § 1, 11-3-22)

laws.title: Custodian
laws.content:
The director of the department of finance shall be deemed the custodian of the funds comprising the system, from time to time. Unless the trustees have authorized electronic or other means of payment, all payments from such funds, other than benefits and payments shall be made only upon presentment of a regular voucher signed by two persons designated by the trustees. A duly attested copy of a resolution designating the persons authorized to sign such vouchers shall be filed with the director of the department of finance, from time to time, as authority for making payments hereunder. No voucher shall be drawn unless it shall have been previously authorized by the trustees.  
(M.C.S., Ord. No. 26460, § 2, 6-18-15)

laws.title: Management of funds
laws.content:
A. The trustees shall be and act as the trustees of the funds comprising the system, from time to time, including amounts credited to the accounts established hereunder. In such capacity, the trustees shall possess the discretionary authority to invest and reinvest such funds. When exercising such authority, the trustees shall (1) exercise judgment and care under the circumstances then prevailing, which a reasonable individual of ordinary prudence, discretion and intelligence would exercise in the management of like enterprises, and (2) act solely in the interests of members and their annuitants and beneficiaries for the purposes of providing benefits and paying administrative costs hereunder.

B. The trustees shall possess all powers ancillary to or necessary for such purpose, including without limitation:

1. The power to appoint one or more sub-custodians to hold all or a portion of the funds constituting the system, from time to time, including the apportionment of funds among such sub-custodians and the removal thereof;

2. The power to adopt and modify, from time to time, an investment policy or determine other investment goals and objectives;

3. The power to designate or remove investment managers and to monitor and evaluate the performance thereof;

4. The power to employ one or more experts or other persons to assist in the performance of their duties and obligations hereunder; and

5. The power to delegate to one or more officers or employees of the system the authority to authorize and direct routine disbursements and payments from the system, subject to such controls and limitations as the trustees deem necessary or advisable.

C. The trustees may enter into agreements with one or more investment managers, in their discretion. The trustees shall determine the portion of the funds then comprising the system allocable to any such manager and shall possess the authority to increase or decrease the amount of such funds, in their discretion. Any investment manager appointed hereunder shall be charged with the management of the funds so allocated in accordance with the investment policy adopted by the trustees. An investment manager appointed hereunder shall not have physical custody of the funds of the system, including those funds allocated to such manager for investment purposes hereunder and shall have no responsibility for the administration and operation of the system, the safekeeping of the funds comprising the system or the management and investment of the portion of the system not otherwise allocated to such manager hereunder.

D. Any financial consultant employed by the trustees hereunder may advise the trustees as to the selection and removal of investment managers, the terms and conditions of any investment policy adopted hereunder, and such other matters as the trustees deem necessary or appropriate.

E. For the purpose of satisfying the cash requirements of the system, including the payment of allowances, benefits and other amounts hereunder, not more than ten percent of the assets comprising the system may be held uninvested in cash or cash equivalents. For this purpose, any amount allocated to an investment manager that is held in cash or cash equivalents pending investment shall not be taken into account.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 26460, § 2, 6-18-15)

laws.title: Employee rights
laws.content:
(a) Subject to the terms of this article, employees shall have the right to:

(1) Organize, form, join, assist, participate in, and pay dues or contributions to a union;

(2) Bargain collectively through an exclusive bargaining representative of their own choosing and to receive fair representation from a union; and

(3) Engage in other concerted activities for the purpose of collective bargaining or other mutual aid and protection insofar as such activity is not inconsistent with this article.

(b) Employees shall also have the right to refrain from any or all such activities described above.

No city employee or any other person acting on behalf of the city, an exclusive bargaining agent, or a union or labor organization may interfere with the exercise of an employee’s rights under this article or commit any form of retaliation arising from the exercise of any rights granted here under this article.

laws.title: Rights accompanying exclusive representation
laws.content:
Any employee labor organization recognized as the exclusive bargaining agent for employees in an appropriate bargaining unit has the following rights:

(a) To speak on behalf of all members of the bargaining unit and be responsible for representing the interests of all members of the bargaining unit without discrimination and without regard to employee labor organization membership.

(b) To meet at reasonable times and places to engage in good faith collective bargaining on matters that, under this article, may be the subject of collective bargaining, in an effort to reach an agreement with the city.

(c) To meet with bargaining unit employees on city premises in non-secure areas during times when the employees are on break or in a non-duty status. Any other employee labor organization that has submitted a petition and established a valid question concerning representation of the bargaining unit is also permitted to meet with bargaining unit employees with the same limitations. An exclusive bargaining agent and the city is permitted to negotiate regarding greater access to employees by the exclusive bargaining agent as a provision of a collective bargaining agreement.

(d) To receive a quarterly list of all covered bargaining unit employees, to receive a monthly list of all new covered bargaining unit employees hired during the previous month, and to be permitted to schedule presentations as needed to the new covered bargaining unit employees hired during the previous month. The city shall invite each exclusive bargaining agent to any formal presentation to the new covered bargaining unit employees corresponding to each exclusive bargaining agent.

(e) To communicate with employees regarding collective bargaining, the administration of collective bargaining agreements, investigation of grievances, other workplace-related complaints and issues, and internal union matters involving the governance or business of the exclusive bargaining agent via city communications systems, including but not limited to, city-issued email addresses and/or phone numbers.

(f) To be represented at any formal discussion between one or more representatives of the city and one or more employees in the bargaining unit or their representatives concerning (1) any matter that is within the scope of collective bargaining as set forth in section 114-400; or (2) any examination of bargaining unit employees by a representative of the city in connection with an investigation if the employee reasonably believes that the examination involves matters covered by any
