**Sec. 114-414. Non-interference and neutrality.**

Neither the city nor any exclusive bargaining agent shall refuse to negotiate in good faith with respect to matters within the scope of collective bargaining defined in section 114-400.

(a) The city and its agents shall not:

(1) Interfere with, restrain, or coerce employees with regard to the exercise of rights granted by this article;

(2) Dominate or interfere in the administration of any employee labor organization;

(3) Deter or discourage employees or applicants for city positions from becoming or remaining members of an employee labor organization, or from authorizing dues deductions, or voting to authorize union representation, or exercising any of their rights under this article;

(4) Encourage or discourage membership in any employee labor organization, committee, or association including by discrimination in hiring, tenure, or other terms and conditions of employment, provided that use of city property and time for meetings and the city's communication system for employee labor organization business, as may be permitted by this article or a collective bargaining agreement, shall not be deemed encouragement prohibited by this section;

(5) Discharge, retaliate, or discriminate against any employee because the employee has filed an affidavit, petition, or complaint or given any information or testimony under this article or because the employee has formed, joined, or chosen to be represented by any exclusive bargaining agent;

(6) Deny the rights accompanying certification as the exclusive bargaining agent as conferred by this article;

(7) Refuse to bargain collectively with the exclusive bargaining agent as provided in this article;

(8) Refuse to participate in good faith in any agreed-upon impasse resolution procedures or those set forth in this article;

(9) Refuse to reduce a collective bargaining agreement to writing and sign such agreement provided all conditions for an enforceable agreement, as set forth in this article, have been met; or

(10) Enforce any rule or regulation which is plainly in direct conflict with any applicable collective bargaining agreement if the agreement was in effect before the date the rule or regulation was prescribed.

(b) No employee labor organization or its agents shall:

(1) Interfere with, restrain, or coerce any employee with respect to rights granted in this article or with respect to selecting an exclusive representative;

(2) Fail to represent an employee who is in a bargaining unit exclusively

laws.title: Fees for applications
laws.content:
(a) The city planning commission or any other agency designated by the city council shall collect in advance application fees according to the following schedule:

(1) For all subdivisions, there shall be a base filing fee of $200.00 plus $25.00 per lot for each lot proposed.

a. Any subdivision proposing the dedication of a street or portion thereof shall pay a minimum filing fee of $500.00.

b. Applications submitting subdivisions under Policy E of subdivision regulations shall pay a minimum filing fee of $350.00.

c. The applicant shall bear the cost of advertising and the cost of certified mailing for a subdivision requiring a public hearing.

d. A $300.00 site plan review fee shall be required for any subdivision wherein site plans are required as part of the application procedure. This fee is in addition to any other applicable processing fees mentioned above.

e. Applicants requesting reapproval or recertification of proposals previously approved or certified by the city planning commission shall be required to pay an additional $100.00 fee.

f. Applicants requesting reconsideration of proposals previously acted upon by the planning commission are required to pay an additional $200.00 fee.

g. All applicants appealing the planning commission's action on any subdivision to the city council are required to pay a fee of $300.00 for processing the appeal.

(2) The party or parties proposing an amendment to the comprehensive zoning law of the city shall remit the applicable fee to the city planning commission before any action shall be taken on the request, in accordance with the comprehensive zoning law.

a. The party or parties proposing an amendment shall be required to pay all advertising costs incurred in the processing of their application in addition to the applicable fee, regardless of the final disposition of the proposed change. Under no condition shall a fee or any part thereof be refunded after advertising commences or, in the case of administrative amendments, after such requests have been properly filed.

3. All properties between 25,000 and 74,999 square feet shall be $3,000.00.

4. All properties over 75,000 square feet shall be $4,000.00.

i. Dwelling, established two-family;

ii. Dwelling, established multi-family; and

(i) The Secretary of Louisiana Department of Transportation and development shall serve as a member of the regional planning commission.

(j) Members shall serve without compensation. However, members, when duly authorized by the Commission, may attend planning conferences or meetings or planning institutes or hearings upon pending planning legislation, and the commission may, by resolution, pay the reasonable traveling expenses incident to such attendance. When so directed and authorized by the regional planning commission, members thereof who hold no elected or other appointed office may be paid a per diem of $50.00 each for attendance at regular or specially called meetings of the full commission or the executive committee thereof in no event to exceed two such meetings per month, i.e. in no event is payment of a total per diem per such member to exceed $100.00 per month, payable out of the funds of the regional planning commission.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 25366, § 1, 6-20-13; M.C.S., Ord. No. 27292, § 1, 2-9-17)

laws.title: Terms of office
laws.content:
(a) Of the members hereof first appointed, those not holding any other elected or appointed public offices shall hold office as follows: one shall hold office for one year, one for a term of two years, one for a term of three years, one for a term of four years, one for a term of five years and the sixth member shall hold office for a term of six years.

(b) Members of the regional planning commission who may hold other public offices, appointed or elected, including the Secretary of the Louisiana Department of Transportation and Development shall serve terms co-existent with their terms of their other public office.

(c) The successors of the regional planning commission members first appointed who do not hold any other appointed or elected public office shall be appointed for a term of five years from and after the expiration of the terms of their predecessors in office.

(d) If a vacancy occurs other than for expiration of term, the same shall be filled by appointment for the unexpired term. Such appointment shall be made by the original appointing authority.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 25366, § 1, 6-20-13; M.C.S., Ord. No. 27292, § 1, 2-9-17)

laws.title: Removal of commission members
laws.content:
The governing bodies of Jefferson Parish, Plaquemines Parish, St. Bernard Parish, St. Charles Parish, St. John the Baptist Parish, St. Tammany Parish or Tangipahoa Parish may remove their respectively appointed members of the commission, after public hearing, for inefficiency, neglect of duty or malfeasance in office. The Mayor of the City of New Orleans may remove any of the members of the commission appointed by him, after public hearing, for inefficiency, neglect of duty or malfeasance in office.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 25366, § 1, 6-20-13; M.C.S., Ord. No. 27292, § 1, 2-9-17)

laws.title: Article I. In General
laws.content:

laws.title: Railroad trains and streetcars prohibited from blocking the streets
laws.content:
It shall be unlawful for the directing officer or the operator of a railroad train or streetcar to direct its operation or to operate it in such a manner as to prevent the use of any street for purposes of travel by vehicles or pedestrians as follows:

(1) For a period longer than five minutes by a stopped train or a switching operation.

(2) For a period longer than ten minutes by any movement other than in subsection (1) of this section.

(3) For a period longer than ten minutes cumulatively of any one hour period between the hours of 7:30 a.m. to 9:30 a.m. and 4:00 p.m. to 6:00 p.m. of any day except Saturdays, Sundays and legal holidays observed by either federal, state and city laws.

(Code 1956, § 38-134)

laws.title: Receiving, discharging passengers
laws.content:
It shall be unlawful for any streetcar or bus to stop within an intersection or on a crosswalk for the purpose of receiving or discharging passengers.

(Code 1956, § 38-134)

laws.title: Display of signs
laws.content:
There shall be posted in every streetcar and ferry boat cabin in the city a notice conspicuously placed and sufficiently large to be easily read by the passengers stating the acts which are prohibited and the officers of corporations or persons operating such streetcars or ferry boats shall post such notice and maintain it under the penalty herein provided.

(Code 1956, § 60-16)

laws.title: Spitting on streetcars or ferry boats prohibited
laws.content:
It shall be unlawful for any person to spit on the floor or platform of streetcars in the city or the cabin of any ferry boat operating on the river.

(Code 1956, § 60-15)

laws.title: Repair of streets disturbed by railroad reconstruction
laws.content:
The director of the department of streets shall require all street railroads immediately to place in good repair and condition all streets which have been disturbed by the railroads in their reconstruction work.

(Code 1956, § 60-1)

*State law reference—Pavement and repair of streets, R.S. 45:323.*

laws.title: Use of flat wheels on cars prohibited
laws.content:
All streetcar lines or railroads are hereby prohibited from using flat wheels upon their cars.

(Code 1956, § 60-7)

laws.title: Smoking prohibited on public transit vehicles
laws.content:
Smoking on any public transit vehicle is prohibited. Any driver of a public transit vehicle who permits such an offense shall be equally guilty of that offense under this section. Any violation of this section shall constitute a misdemeanor.

(Code 1956, §§ 60-17, 60-20)

laws.title: Playing of audio, video equipment on public transit vehicles prohibited
laws.content:
Playing of radio receivers, or other audio or video equipment, except when used with an earphone attachment audible only to the person using the attachment, on any public transit vehicle is prohibited. Any driver of a public

§ 122-9

NEW ORLEANS CODE

transit vehicle who permits such an offense shall be equally guilty of that offense under this section. Any violation of this section shall constitute a misdemeanor.

(Code 1956, §§ 60-18, 60-21)

Cross references—Noise, § 66-136 et seq.; traffic and vehicles, ch. 154.

laws.title: Consumption of food and beverages on public transit vehicles prohibited
laws.content:
Consumption of foodstuffs or beverages on any public transit vehicle, other than chartered transit service, is prohibited. It is unlawful for any driver of a public transit vehicle to permit such an offense. No metal or glass containers of any type, for the purpose of transporting, containing, or serving foodstuffs and/or beverages, shall be allowed on chartered transit vehicles. Nothing in this section shall be construed as to prevent a driver of any transit vehicle from consuming foodstuffs and/or beverages, while the transit vehicle is parked at the end of the transit line, and not in motion.

(Code 1956, § 60-22)

Cross reference—Food regulations, § 82-36 et seq.

laws.title: Concessions for handicapped passengers
laws.content:
Passengers on any wheelchair lift-equipped public transit vehicle shall, when requested by the driver of that public transit vehicle, relinquish their seats above the vehicle’s wheelchair lock mechanism to enable the driver to secure a handicapped passenger’s wheelchair to the floor of the vehicle. Passenger aids on special elderly and handicapped transit service vehicles shall relinquish their seats to accommodate elderly or handicapped passengers, at the request of the driver of the transit vehicle. Any violation of this section shall constitute a misdemeanor.

(Code 1956, § 60-23)

Cross reference—Vehicles for hire, ch. 162.

laws.title: Impeding public transit operations prohibited
laws.content:
It shall be unlawful for any person to impede public transit operations by creating a public nuisance; cause a distraction to the driver of any

public transit vehicle, making it unsafe for the driver to operate the vehicle; damage transit property; or abuse the public transit vehicle driver or passengers. Any violation of this section shall constitute a misdemeanor.

(Code 1956, § 60-24)

laws.title: Legal fares and the payment thereof required
laws.content:
It shall be unlawful for any passenger boarding any public transit vehicle to fail to pay or avoid the payment of the required fare or to use or offer for passage on any public transit vehicle any fraudulent transfer, ticket, pass, or payment token, or interfere with the collection of fares. Any driver of a public transit vehicle who permits such an offense shall be equally guilty of that offense under this section. Any violation of this section shall constitute a misdemeanor.

(Code 1956, § 60-25)

laws.title: Sale, barter, counterfeiting, or exchanging of transfer tickets prohibited
laws.content:
(a) It shall be unlawful for any person to sell, barter, counterfeit, or exchange for any consider-

CD122:4
PUBLIC TRANSIT VEHICLES

§ 122-16

ation whatsoever, any transfer ticket, pass, payment token, or other instrument issued by any public transit agency, giving or purporting to give the holder of such transfer ticket or other instrument the right to ride or transfer, without payment of additional fare, from one transit vehicle to another transit vehicle.

(b) It shall be unlawful for any person to give away any transfer ticket, pass, or other such instrument to another person, for the purpose of enabling, or with the intent to enable the latter to use or offer for passage on any transit vehicle, or for any person not lawfully entitled thereto who shall receive any such transfer ticket, pass, or other instrument to use, attempt to use or offer it for passage on any public transit vehicle.

(c) The provisions of this section shall not relate to or in any way or manner affect the issuing and giving of transfer tickets, passes, or other such instruments by the duly authorized agents or employees of the agency operating public transit services to passengers lawfully entitled thereto.

(Code 1956, § 60-26)

laws.title: Enforcement of violations of sections 122-8 through 122-14 and 122-16
laws.content:
The provisions of section 102-1, relative to the issuance of juvenile warning citations may be applicable for violations of sections 122-8 through 122-14 and section 122-16.

(Code 1956, § 60-26.1; M.C.S., Ord. No. 23665, § 1, 8-7-09)

laws.title: Ferry terminals—Prohibited activities
laws.content:
It shall be unlawful for any person to engage in any of the activities herein below listed while within the confines of the ferry terminals located at Canal Street, Jackson Avenue, or in Algiers. Those activities which shall be unlawful, unless specifically approved by the executive director of the Crescent City Connection Division of the Louisiana Department of Transportation and Development are:

(a) Offenses.

(1) The destruction, injury, defacement, removal or disturbance in any man-

ner of any building, sign, fence, gate, equipment, monument, marker, or other structure.

(2) Littering, as defined in section 138-2.

(3) Smoking, as defined in section 122-8, except as permitted in designated areas.

(4) The use of bicycles, skateboards, tricycles, and any other such vehicles, as well as motorbikes, go-carts, and other motorized vehicles in any of the ferry terminals or passenger walkways. Wheelchairs and baby carriages are permitted.

(5) Disturbing the peace, as defined in section 54-403, while on ferry terminal property.

(6) Solicitation, as defined in section 54-411.

(7) Possession of tools and/or markers or other instruments used in a manner causing destruction to property, equipment or facilities of the ferry terminals.

(b) Penalties. A violation of this section is punishable by municipal court, as follows:

(1) Any person who violates any subsections of (a) of this section shall be punished by a fine of not less than $50.00 or more than $500.00.

(2) Any person who violates subsections (a)(4) or (a)(7) shall surrender the item (vehicle, tool and/or marker) to the New Orleans Police Department or the Crescent City Connection Police Department to be used as evidence against the person found in possession of the item.

(3) In addition to the above penalties, the court may, in its discretion, order imprisonment for not more than three months for any offense of subsection (a)(1), (a)(4), (a)(5), or (a)(7) of this section.

(c) Warning signs. Signs shall be erected at each entrance to the ferry terminals lo-

Supp. No. 49

CD122:5
§ 122-16

NEW ORLEANS CODE

cated at Canal Street, Jackson Avenue, and in Algiers citing the prohibitions enumerated in this section.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 23665, § 1, 8-7-09)

Secs. 122-17—122-50. Reserved.

laws.title: Certain buses prohibited in Vieux Carre
laws.content:
(a) It shall be unlawful for any person to operate a bus having an overall length longer than 31 feet on any street in the Vieux Carre, except as provided for in the rules and regulations promulgated under section 162-942(d). Those buses with an overall length in excess of 20 feet and not greater than 31 feet shall use the streets of the Vieux Carre as provided for in section 162-942(d) of the City Code.

(b) For the purposes of this section, a bus shall be defined as any motor vehicle, excluding limousines, having an overall length in excess of 20 feet used for the purpose of transportation of passengers.

(c) For the purposes of this section, Vieux Carre shall mean the area within the lake side of Decatur Street, the downriver side of Esplanade Avenue, the river side of North Rampart Street and the downriver side of Canal Street. Therefore, all buses, regardless of the overall length, shall be permitted to use Decatur Street, North Rampart Street and Canal Street.

(Code 1956, § 38-142.1; M.C.S., Ord. No. 17,823, § 2, 10-17-96)

Cross reference—Specific street regulations, § 154-601 et seq.

laws.title: Operating at idle
laws.content:
The operator of a bus shall not allow buses to operate at idle on the streets of the city for a period longer than 20 minutes, except for situations beyond the operator's control and as otherwise provided for in chapter 162 and section 162-942.

(Code 1956, § 38-143)

laws.title: Operating at idle in the Garden District
laws.content:
The operator of a bus shall not allow buses to operate at idle on the streets of the Garden District, which is bounded by St. Charles Avenue, Jackson Avenue, Louisiana Avenue and Magazine Street, for a period longer than ten minutes, except for situations beyond the operator's control.

(Code 1956, § 38-143.1)

laws.title: Standing trains on streets, etc., prohibited
laws.content:
The standing upon any public street or street crossing of any locomotive, engine, car or train of cars, within the city limits, or the obstructing of street crossings in any manner whatsoever by any of them, except so far as may be done while in motion, or the parking or assembling of cars, the making up of trains, the switching of cars, the cleaning of cars, the loading and unloading of cars, the watering of locomotives, the blowing out of locomotives and the doing of any and all kinds of yard work in any public street, public avenue or public alley (whether in the roadway, neutral ground or sidewalk thereof) or in any other public place in the city is hereby prohibited. The provisions of this section shall not be construed to apply to the necessary and proper handling of

*State law reference—Railroads, generally, R.S. 45:321 et seq.

PUBLIC TRANSIT VEHICLES

§ 122-88

cars on industrial switch tracks operated for service to particular industries under ordinances of the city.

(Code 1956, § 53-1)

State law reference—Railroads not to obstruct highways, R.S. 45:324.

laws.title: Provisions of drainage under tracks
laws.content:
(a) The director of the department of public works shall compel all diesel and street railroad companies within the rate limits of the city to establish a system of drainage under their tracks so as to eliminate the stagnating of water caused by the construction of tracks having no underground outlet for water.

(b) Any diesel or street railroad company failing to comply and to carry out the provisions of this section after due notice from the director of the department of public works to the satisfaction of such officials shall be liable to a fine of not less than $10.00 nor more than $100.00 or to imprisonment for not less than ten days nor more than 90 days or both, in the discretion of the court having proper jurisdiction.

(Code 1956, § 53-3; M.C.S., Ord. No. 21480, § 2, 4-1-04)

State law references—Railroads not to impede drainage, R.S. 45:324; duty to relieve obstruction to natural drainage, R.S. 45:451 et seq.

laws.title: Removal of timbers, etc
laws.content:
The different railroads throughout the city shall be required upon being notified by the director of the department of streets to cause to be removed, within 48 hours from the service of notice, all timbers or stringers of any description used in the construction of railroads and which may be declared by the director of the department of streets to be obstructions to a free and uninterrupted drainage. Such timbers or stringers shall in every case be replaced by iron bars or plates or by any material suitable for the purpose, under the direction of the director of the department of streets. Upon failure or neglect of any company to remove obstructions of the kind herein specified and within the time specified, the director of the department of streets shall have them removed as

§ 122-93

soon as practicable thereafter at the risk and expense of the company.

(Code 1956, § 53-4)

State law references—Railroads not to impede drainage, R.S. 45:324; duty to relieve obstruction to natural drainage, R.S. 45:451 et seq.

laws.title: Construction and repair of streets, bridges or culverts
laws.content:
(a) The construction or repair of all bridges or culverts over which railroad tracks are laid shall be performed and carried on to completion under the direction of the director of the department of streets and in accordance with specifications to be prepared or approved by the department of streets and kept on file in the office of the department.

(b) The director of the department of streets shall require that the construction and maintenance of city streets between or immediately adjacent to the rails of any railroad be in accordance with the provisions of R.S. 45:323. The director shall prepare typical plans and specifications of general applicability to the construction and maintenance of streets between railroad tracks and adjacent thereto in street areas set forth in R.S. 45:323 and he is authorized to modify such typical plans and specifications as may be necessary in unusual installations.

(c) Should the owner or operator of a railroad or street car or the grantee of a railroad switch track privilege fail to start repair of any roadway deficiency between or adjacent to his tracks in area specified herein as soon as practicable and not more than 30 days after notice thereof has been brought to his attention by the director of the department of streets or his agent, or fail to complete such correction in not more than 60 days after the notice, the director shall correct such deficiency or cause such to be corrected and the cost of such correction shall be borne by the owner of such tracks or by the grantee of the switch track franchise; provided, that the 30-day period and/or the 60-day period herein above specified may be extended by the director of the department of streets because of extenuating circumstances such as nonavailability of material, equipment or skilled manpower or other conditions beyond the

reasonable control of the persons or legal entity required to repair the designated deficiency.

(Code 1956, § 53-5)

laws.title: New tracks or changes not to be laid without getting lines and levels from city
laws.content:
It shall be unlawful for any railroad company running its tracks within the limits of the city to lay down new tracks or lower or raise the grade of any track without first procuring lines and levels from the director of the department of streets for the proper construction of such track. In case of any violations of the provisions of this section the director shall cause such track to be immediately conformed to the proper grade or level of the streets or levees upon which it is laid and in case the railroad company should refuse or neglect so to do when notified the director shall execute the provisions of this section and use such means as may be necessary for such purpose.

(Code 1956, § 53-6)

laws.title: Placing torpedoes, etc., on track prohibited
laws.content:
It shall be unlawful for any person to place on any railroad track of a passenger or freight railway

CD122:7
§ 122-93

NEW ORLEANS CODE

within the city any torpedo, cartridge or explosive material, with malicious intent to injure or frighten passengers or other citizens.  
(Code 1956, § 53-7)

**Sec. 122-94. Obstruction of tracks or other interference with railroad.**

It shall not be lawful for any person to place any obstruction on the track of any railroad located or running in or through the city or unnecessarily to interfere with or obstruct the free passage of any car or to endanger the safety of any car or any person in any car running in or through the city.  
(Code 1956, § 53-8)

**Sec. 122-95. Exception for fire department.**

The provisions of section 122-94 shall not in any way conflict with the privileges and right-of-way granted to fire engines, hook and ladder trucks, wagons carrying Babcock fire extinguishers and other vehicles belonging to the fire department.  
(Code 1956, § 53-9)

**Sec. 122-96. Children not to swing on outside of cars in motion.**

It shall be unlawful for the parents or guardians of any minor child to allow such child to hang or swing on the outside of any car of any railroad within the limits of the city while it is in use or motion upon such road.  
(Code 1956, § 53-10)

**Sec. 122-97. Companies and their employees to enforce sections.**

The companies owning the railroads and their employees shall enforce the provisions of sections 122-94 to 122-96.  
(Code 1956, § 53-11)

**Sec. 122-98. Stopping near tracks.**

No person shall bring any automobile, auto truck, motorcycle or other motor-driven vehicle, animal-drawn vehicle, bicycle or any horse or other beast of burden to a stop at any place upon any track of any steam railroad in the city or within ten feet of the nearest rail of any railroad crossing in the city.  
(Code 1956, § 53-36)

**Sec. 122-99. Owners not to cause chauffeurs to violate law.**

No owner of any automobile, auto truck, motorcycle or other motor-driven vehicle, animal-drawn vehicle, bicycle or any horse or other beast of burden shall knowingly cause or permit the chauffeur or driver thereof to violate any of the provisions of section 122-98.  
(Code 1956, § 53-37)

**Sec. 122-100. Applicability to police and fire departments and ambulances.**

The provisions of sections 122-98 and 122-99 shall not apply to any member of the police or fire departments of the city when in the discharge of duty, nor to any owner or driver of any ambulance actually engaged in ambulance service.  
(Code 1956, § 53-38)

**Secs. 122-101–122-130. Reserved.**

laws.title: Switch Tracks
laws.content:
**Sec. 122-131. Nonliability of city.**

The city shall not be liable or responsible for any damages resulting from any disturbance or obstacle in the use or location of switch tracks from any cause whatsoever. The city shall be indemnified by the grantee of any such switch track for any personal or property damage to itself or others, or to the public which may result from the negligent use, location or unsafe condition of such utilities or the operation thereof.  
(Code 1956, § 53-25)

**Sec. 122-132. Responsibility of officers, etc.**

When a railroad or other corporation is found violating the provisions of this division, all of the officers or responsible managers or superintendents thereof shall be guilty of such violation.  
(Code 1956, § 53-27)

CD122:8
PUBLIC TRANSIT VEHICLES

§ 122-140

**Sec. 122-133. Exclusion.**

The provisions of this division shall not apply to switch tracks connecting with the tracks of the Public Belt Railroad Commission of the city, when by the terms of the grant such switch tracks are to become the property of the city, and a part of the Public Belt Railroad Commission System.

(Code 1956, § 53-12)

*Charter reference—Public Belt Railroad Commission, §§ 5-201 and 5-202.*

*Constitutional law reference—The Public Belt Railroad System, see La. Const., art. XIV, section 26.*

**Sec. 122-134. Special ordinance required.**

It shall be unlawful for any railroad or other person to establish, construct, maintain or operate a switch track in any public place in the city without permission from the council, upon proper application by special ordinance, fixing the duration of the privilege granted, the consideration therefor and the terms of payment.

(Code 1956, § 53-13)

**Sec. 122-135. Application for special ordinance.**

Application for permission required by this division shall be made in writing to the council and shall be accompanied by blueprints, in quadruplicate, showing the proposed location of the track, section measurements, and other similar details and also all existing tracks, if any, and by whom claimed and to what railroad they are connected. Such measurements shall be made along the centerline between rails from the point of frog to the property line. One of the blueprints shall be kept by the director of the department of public works, one by the sewerage and water board, and one by the clerk of the council.

(Code 1956, § 53-14; M.C.S., Ord. No. 21480, § 2, 4-1-04)

**Sec. 122-136. Approval of plans.**

Plans and specifications for the construction of new switch tracks or relaying of existing switch tracks in public places in the city shall be approved by the department of public works and the sewerage and water board.

(Code 1956, § 53-15; M.C.S., Ord. No. 21480, § 2, 4-1-04)

**Sec. 122-137. Bond required of grantee.**

Every grantee of a switch track privilege shall furnish a good and solvent surety bond, in solido, in favor of the city satisfactory to the director of the department of public works in a sum equal to the aggregate of the annual payments during the term of the privilege, but in no event to be less than $500.00 or to exceed the sum of $3,000.00 and whenever the grantee shares the privilege with other parties a good solvent surety bond, in solido, must be furnished by the grantees including all the principals in the privilege granted and such bond shall guarantee the faithful performance of all the obligations of the grantees of such privilege set forth in the ordinance granting the privilege and especially those obligations defined by the provisions of this division.

(Code 1956, § 53-16; M.C.S., Ord. No. 21480, § 2, 4-1-04)

**Sec. 122-138. Restoration of sidewalks, etc., disturbed in construction.**

All sidewalks, pavements and other public property torn up or disturbed in constructing, relaying or removing switch tracks shall be restored to their original good condition by the grantees of the switch track who shall likewise conform in all respects to the provisions of all other ordinances relative to the manner of making and restoring cuts in roadways and sidewalks pavements, especially the provisions of sections 146-436 through 146-459.

(Code 1956, § 53-17)

**Sec. 122-139. Fee for privilege.**

When the length of switch track is 300 feet or less in length the fee shall be $100.00 per annum per 100 feet or fraction thereof. When such switch track is more than 300 feet in length, the fee shall be at the rate of $50.00 per 100 feet or fraction thereof for all trackage in excess of 300 feet in length.

(Code 1956, § 53-18)

**Sec. 122-140. Evidence of payment of fee.**

The director of the department of public works shall file with the local freight agent of the railroad serving a switch track evidence that the

Supp. No. 29

NEW ORLEANS CODE

grantee of a switch track privilege has paid the annual fee required therefor. No railroad shall move railroad freight cars on any switch track located in public places without first having received a notice from the director that the annual fee as stipulated in section 122-139 has been paid by the grantee of the switch track privilege.

(Code 1956, § 53-19; M.C.S., Ord. No. 21480, § 2, 4-1-04)

**Sec. 122-141. Unlawful to switch car without evidence of payment of fee.**

The moving of a railroad freight car or cars on a switch track by any railroad without first having obtained a certificate of evidence of payment of the switch track fee shall constitute a violation of this division, and each car so moved shall be considered a separate and distinct violation and punishable as such.

(Code 1956, § 53-20)

**Sec. 122-142. Remedies in case of default of payment of fee.**

If any payment of the switch track fee is not made at the date fixed by the ordinance granting the permission for a switch track, then all subsequent installments accruing under the terms thereof shall immediately, without demand or putting in default, become payable or, at the option of the director of the department of public works, such ordinance may be terminated and cancelled by a written notice to that effect addressed to the grantee. Such cancellation shall not release any indebtedness accruing prior to the date thereof or as long as the grantee remains and makes use of such utility under such ordinance or the bond given under this division.

(Code 1956, § 53-21; M.C.S., Ord. No. 21480, § 2, 4-1-04)

**Sec. 122-143. Maintenance required of grantee.**

Every grantee of a switch track privilege shall, during the term of the privilege, maintain in good order and condition all portions of water, sewerage and drainage systems which lie beneath or in close proximity to the track maintained or operated by the grantee. The grantee shall likewise,

during the term of the privilege, maintain in good order and condition all pavements between the rails of the switch track and for a distance of 18 inches on the outside of the rails.

(Code 1956, § 53-22)

**Sec. 122-144. Relocation of tracks.**

Permission to establish, construct, maintain or operate a switch track shall be granted under the express condition that such switch track, or any part thereof, shall be subject to prompt removal or relocation within 90 days at the pleasure of the city and at the expense of the grantee whenever the city or other governmental body therein shall find it necessary to request such removal or relocation for the purpose of the execution of public works or other franchises or permits of whatsoever nature or for any necessary public purpose on the site so occupied. The city shall not be liable for damages or reimbursements of any kind resulting from any such requested removal, adjustment or change or from any disturbance or obstacle of any nature, whether temporary or permanent, in the use or location of any such switch track or any part thereof from any cause whatsoever. The cost of all necessary changes of locations of such utilities, such as catchbasins, manholes, fire hydrants, water mains, sewer and drainage lines, gas mains, electric conduits, electric and telephone poles and similar installations or shifting thereof or relocation or removal of such utilities or any part thereof found to be necessary by the city shall be at the expense of the grantee. The grantee shall perform the entire work of relocation or removal of the switch track, or any part thereof, in connection therewith within a reasonable time not to exceed 90 days after notice thereof from the city or it shall be done at the grantee’s expense. The determination of such necessity shall remain wholly discretionary with the council. Should a change of location or removal within a period of time shorter than 90 days be so deemed necessary by reason of public danger or peril then such switch track, or any part thereof, shall be removed or shifted at the grantee’s expense in the earliest time possible or in default thereof the grantee shall suffer the removal or shifting at his expense or cost.

(Code 1956, § 53-23)

§ 122-180

**Sec. 122-145. Privilege nontransferable, etc.**

The grantee of a switch track shall not exercise such privilege except in connection with his own business. He shall not lease such utilities or grant the right to use them to any other person and no charge shall be made to the city for using such utilities for public purposes. Switch track privileges shall be inalienable and not transferable. But a grantee may subrogate another to all rights and liabilities with respect to the privilege granted upon specific written notice to the director of the department of public works, giving the name and address of the person to whom the subrogation is made and securing the consent of the council.

(Code 1956, § 53-24; M.C.S., Ord. No. 21480, § 2, 4-1-04)

**Sec. 122-146. Removal of track on expiration of privilege.**

The grantee shall notify the council, in writing, 60 days prior to the expiration of the term of any switch track privilege granted under the provisions of this division if the grantee desires to renew the privilege. If the application for renewal of the utility privilege is not received by the council by the time stated the director of the department of public works shall notify the grantee to remove the switch track from the public place and to restore the location to a condition satisfactory to the city within 30 days from such notice and if the grantee shall fail to do so the city engineer shall have such switch track removed from the public place and restore the location in question to a satisfactory condition. The cost of such removal and restoration shall be borne by the grantee.

(Code 1956, § 53-26; M.C.S., Ord. No. 21480, § 2, 4-1-04)

**Secs. 122-147—122-175. Reserved.**

**ARTICLE IV. STREETCARS***

**Sec. 122-176. Fenders, guards required.**

Every person controlling, operating or owning any street railroad in the city shall equip and

*Cross reference—Streets, sidewalks and other public places, ch. 146.

provide every car used on such street railroad with fenders of steel and of the basket kind or any other device that might prove superior, which shall be substantially attached to the front end thereof so as to guard passengers and pedestrians from being injured or thrown under the wheels in case of a collision or other accident. The style or kind of fender or guard shall be approved by the council.

(Code 1956, § 60-3)

State law reference—Fenders, requirement, R.S. 45:691.

**Sec. 122-177. Operation without fenders.**

No person operating and using any street railroad car in the city shall allow or in any way permit it to be used on any street railroad in the city without first equipping and providing it with fenders as prescribed in section 122-176.

(Code 1956, §§ 60-4, 60-5)

**Sec. 122-178. Ventilation of cars.**

It shall be unlawful for any street railroad company to run any car on the streets of the city unless it is provided with proper ventilators affording a ventilation of at least four square feet.

(Code 1956, § 60-8)

**Sec. 122-179. Cars to be cleaned daily.**

Any person operating street passenger railway cars within the limits of the city shall cause each car in use on such street railway to be thoroughly cleansed inside with disinfectants at least once a day.

(Code 1956, § 60-9)

**Sec. 122-180. Department of health to enforce; inspections.**

The department of health shall enforce the provisions of section 122-179 and prosecute all persons charged with violating them and to that end its officers, members, agents, employees, inspectors and appointees shall have the right to enter any premise or place or any car, conveyance or other vehicle in the city for the purpose of inspection for violation hereof.

(Code 1956, § 60-12)

**Sec. 122-181. Responsibility for violations.**

(a) When an association of individuals is charged with the violation of any of the provisions of section 122-179, each individual of such association of individuals or, if a foreign association of individuals, the local agent or person locally in charge thereof, shall be deemed to represent such association of individuals for the purpose of enforcing such sections and shall be held responsible and punishable for each violation thereof.

Such proof shall consist of the identification card number and the name of the issuing entity. If the person, offering the part for sale cannot produce such photographic identification, the purchaser shall take a thumbprint of the person offering the part for sale. The original thumbprint shall be taken for the receipt of sale retained by the purchaser. The original thumbprint and the record of required information, relative to the person offering the part for sale, shall be made available to the superintendent of police upon demand.

laws.title: Records required
laws.content:
(a) Every secondhand dealer except those contained in division 2 of this article shall be required to maintain a book or ledger setting forth each purchase of secondhand or used merchandise when the value of any single piece of merchandise or article received shall be $25.00 or more, for each single transaction. The price at which a piece of merchandise is offered for sale by a secondhand dealer shall be considered prima facie evidence of the value of the piece of merchandise. Each ledger entry shall be entered at the time of each transaction and shall contain an accurate description in the English language of the merchandise or article received including serial numbers of such objects, if distinguishable, along with the amount paid therefor.

(b) The name, address, sex, race, height, weight, and driver’s license number of the person selling or delivering such merchandise or articles to the dealer shall be obtained and included with each ledger entry. Records of each purchase shall be preserved for a period of at least three years.

(c) Every person, licensed under the provisions of this article, shall make out and deliver to the superintendent of police, every day before the hour of 12:00 noon, a legible and correct copy of the entries in the book during the previous day. The name given by the person making a sale shall be furnished the superintendent of police when they specially request it.

(Code 1956, § 44-6; Ord. No. 20,096, § 1, 4-5-01)

*State law reference*—Similar provisions, R.S. 37:1864, 37:1866.

*Cross references*—Sales and use tax, § 150-441 et seq.; occupational license tax, § 150-951 et seq.

laws.title: (b) Exclusions. This section shall not apply to any of the following
laws.content:
(1) Secondhand furniture merchants.

(2) Pawnbrokers.

(3) Secondhand car dealers or merchants in connection with automobile and motor vehicle sales agencies but not carried on and conducted in conjunction with a junk yard.

(4) Persons engaged in the business of selling new automobile tires or batteries or other equipment taking in part payment used articles of the same kind and thereafter selling or disposing of the same.

(5) Secondhand oil well supply and equipment dealers not conducting or carrying on their business in connection with a junk yard.

(6) Secondhand clothing merchants.

(7) Any person who buys or sells junk acquired in the conduct of any business other than that of a junk dealer.

(8) Those transfers of junk by a junk dealer when the payment for the junk is by check issued to the company represented as being the owner of the junk.

(9) Junk purchased or received from another junk dealer who has recorded, reported, and held the material as required. The purchase or receipt shall also be exempt from further holding or reporting provided that the selling party gives the buyer written assurance of this fact. The seller shall be held responsible for any failure to report or hold.

(c) Junk dealer records.

(1) Every junk dealer is required to keep a written record of all purchases or acquisitions of junk, which shall contain all of the following:

(i) The name, address, and phone number of the seller;

(ii) The place and date of each purchase or acquisition;

(iii) A description of the item or items of junk purchased or acquired, including the item type and quantity or weight, and identification number, if visible;

(iv) A photocopy of the occupational license of the seller, a photocopy of the driver’s license or state-issued identification card of the seller and the vehicle license plate number including the state of issue of any motor vehicle used in transporting the junk to the junk dealer’s place of business; and

(v) If the person from whom the material is obtained does not possess a valid government-issued photo identification that matches the appearance of the person, the purchaser, collector or dealer shall take and maintain, in a manner that cross references to the written record, a photograph of the face of the person, along with a reasonably accurate record of the person’s height and weight.

(vi) If the junk dealer is unable to obtain the information required by this subsection from the person from whom the material is to be obtained, the junk dealer shall not complete the transaction.

(2) Every junk dealer selling junk is required to keep a written record of all sales, which shall contain all of the following:

(i) The name, address, phone number parish of occupational license, and occupational license number of the purchaser;

(ii) The place and date of each sale; and

(iii) A description of the item or items of junk sold, including the item type and quantity or weight, and identification number, if visible.

(d) Inspection of records. The information contained in the written record shall be submitted by the purchaser, collector of, or dealer to the New Orleans Police Department, in a manner prescribed by the superintendent of police. Every junk dealer shall, during normal business hours, allow periodic inspection of any premises maintained and any junk thereon for the purpose of determining compliance with the recordkeeping requirements of this section, and shall during those hours produce its records of transfers and all property purchased incident to those transactions which is in the possession of the junk dealer for inspection by any of the following persons:

(1) Any officer holding a warrant authorizing him or her to search for personal property;

(2) Any person appointed by the sheriff of any parish or appointed by the head of the police department of any city;

(3) Any officer holding a court order directing him or her to examine the records or property;

(4) The director of the department of public works, or his designee; or.

(5) The director of the department of safety and permits, or his designee.

§ 130-39

(e) Records; preservation. Every junk dealer shall preserve the written record required by this section for at least three years after making the final entry of any transfer of junk or scrap metals and alloys as defined in this section.

(f) Violations; offenses; punishment.

(1) Any junk dealer who fails in any respect to keep the written record required by this section, or to set out in that written record any matter required by this section to be set out therein, is guilty of a misdemeanor.

(2) Any junk dealer who makes, or causes to be made, any false or fictitious statement in any written report required by this section is guilty of a misdemeanor.

(3) Any junk dealer who transfers junk without an Occupational License shall be guilty of a misdemeanor.

(4) Any junk dealer who refuses, upon demand, to exhibit the written record required by this section, or who destroys that record within three years after making the final entry of any purchase or sale of junk therein, is guilty of a misdemeanor.

(5) Any knowing and willful violation of this section shall be punishable by a fine of five hundred dollars ($500), or by imprisonment for up to six (6) months, or by both fine and imprisonment.

For a second offense, in addition to any other sentence imposed pursuant to this paragraph, the court may order the defendant to stop engaging in business as a junk dealer for a period not to exceed 30 days.

(g) Property suspected of being stolen; peace officer placement of hold on property; rights, duties and liabilities of junk dealer; costs.

(1) The junk dealer shall not sell, transfer or otherwise dispose of any brass or copper for a minimum of seven days after the date on which it is obtained. In the event that the junk dealer is notified by an electric utility of the theft of copper or aluminum, then the material must be retained for an additional 30 days. The junk dealer shall not sell, transfer or otherwise dispose of any storm drainage materials or utility manhole covers and frames for a minimum of seven days after the date on which it is obtained. In the event that the junk dealer is notified by the sewerage and water board, the city, or any utility of the theft of storm drainage materials or utility manhole covers and frames, then the material must be retained for an additional 30 days. Whenever any peace officer has probable cause to believe that property in the possession of a junk dealer is stolen, in lieu of seizing the property, the peace officer, at his or her option, may place a hold on the property for a period not to exceed 90 days. When a peace officer places a hold on the property, the peace officer shall give the junk dealer a written notice at the time the hold is placed, describing the item or items to be held plus the case number. During that period the junk dealer shall not release or dispose of the property, except pursuant to a court order or upon receipt of a written authorization signed by any peace officer who is a member of the law enforcement agency of which the peace officer placing the hold on the property is a member. Except as specifically set forth in this section, a junk dealer shall not be subject to civil liability for compliance with this section.

(2) Whenever property that is in the possession of a junk dealer is subject to a hold and the property is required by a peace officer in a criminal investigation, the junk dealer, upon reasonable notice, shall produce the property at reasonable times and places or may deliver the property to any peace officer upon the request of any peace officer who is a member of the law enforcement agency of which the peace officer placing the hold on the property is a member.

(3) Whenever property that is in the possession of a junk dealer is subject to a hold and the property is no longer required for the purpose of criminal investigation, the law enforcement agency that placed the hold on the property shall undertake the following:

(i) With respect to the property being held, if the law enforcement agency has no knowledge of the property on hold being reported as stolen, the property shall be released upon written notice to the junk dealer. The notice shall be provided in a timely fashion.

(ii) If the law enforcement agency has knowledge that the property has been reported stolen, the law enforcement agency shall notify the person who reported the stolen property of the name and address of the junk dealer holding the property and authorize the release of the property to that person. The law enforcement agency that placed the property on hold shall release the hold after 60 days has elapsed following the delivery of the notice to the person who reported the property stolen.

(iii) If a victim seeks to recover property that is subject to a hold, the junk dealer shall advise the victim of the name and badge number of the peace officer who placed the hold on the property and the name of the law enforcement agency of which the officer is a member. If the property is not required to be held pursuant to a criminal prosecution the hold shall be released.

(iv) Upon conviction of any person for the theft of property placed on hold pursuant to this section, the court shall order the defendant to pay the junk dealer reasonable costs for storage of the property.

(h) Refillable stainless steel or aluminum alloy beer kegs; indicia of ownership.

(1) Except as provided in subsection (2), no junk dealer may purchase or receive refillable stainless steel or aluminum alloy beer kegs marked with an indicia of ownership from any person or entity other than the indicated owner. For purposes of this section, "indicia of ownership" means words, symbols, or registered trademarks printed, stamped, etched, attached, or otherwise displayed on the exterior surface of the beer keg that reasonably identifies the owner.

(2) If the seller is not the indicated owner, a junk dealer may purchase or receive refillable stainless steel or aluminum alloy beer kegs only if the seller or transferor provides a receipt from the indicated owner verifying the seller's current ownership or a document indicating that the seller or transferor is authorized by the indicated owner to sell or transfer the beer kegs. Copies of these documents shall be maintained by the junk dealer as part of the written record of the transaction.

(i) Materials marked or engraved as owned by city government or other political subdivision.

(1) A junk dealer shall not purchase any storm drain materials or utility manhole covers and frames that are marked with the name and/or initials of a political subdivision or otherwise identified as the property of a political subdivision. The junk dealer shall immediately notify NOPD of any such attempted sale.

laws.title: Permit required
laws.content:
Any person engaging in business as a secondhand motor vehicle body parts dealer shall annually apply to the director of the department of finance for a permit on a form provided by the department. The application shall include the complete name and address of the place of business; the name, address, social security number and birth date of the owners, proprietors, partners or principal incorporators owning ten percent or more of the business, and a sworn statement with fingerprints as required by the department of police showing that the applicant or any of the parties listed on the application has not been convicted of either a felony under the laws of the United States or any state or of a local misdemeanor that is related to the applicant’s business within the previous five years. The department of police shall provide to the director of the department of finance all available information regarding any charges or arrests it may possess regarding the applicant. The findings of any such charge, arrest or conviction, or the filing of false or incomplete information shall be sufficient cause for the denial of this permit. This permit shall be valid for one calendar year. Upon approval of the application by the department of finance and payment of the permit fee as provided by section 30-1281 et seq., a permit shall be issued to the applicant. The director of the department of finance shall immediately

revoke the permit for any false, incomplete or inaccurate information provided the city. The applicant may not apply or reapply for a permit for at least one year from said revocation.

(Ord. No. 20,096, § 1, 4-5-01)

**Sec. 130-53. Denial, hearing.**

If the department of finance denies the issuance of a secondhand motor vehicle body parts dealer permit it shall give written notice to the applicant at the business address listed on the application. The applicant may then file with the department of finance a written request for a hearing to appeal the denial. This request shall be filed by the applicant within five working days from the date that the applicant received the notice of denial. The hearing shall be held before the director of the department of finance or his designated representative.

(Ord. No. 20,096, § 1, 4-5-01)

**Sec. 130-54. Regulations.**

In addition to the provisions of this article, the following regulations shall apply to secondhand motor vehicle body parts dealers:

(1) It shall be unlawful for any owner, keeper, agent or person representing any such owner or proprietor of any secondhand motor vehicle body parts dealer or store to buy, pawn, pledge or exchange any article from any minor under the age of 18 years, from a person appearing to be intoxicated, from a person known to be a notorious thief or from a person known to have been convicted of larceny or burglary.

(2) It shall be unlawful for any secondhand motor vehicle body parts dealer to buy from a seller any motor vehicle body part between the hours of 7:00 p.m. and 7:00 a.m. daily.

(Ord. No. 20,096, § 1, 4-5-01)

**Sec. 130-55. Retention of purchases.**

It shall be unlawful for the permittee to sell, exchange, barter, remove from their place of business or permit to be redeemed, any motor vehicle body parts that have been brought, exchanged, pledged, or deposited by, to or with them from a seller for a period of 30 days from the date of purchase. This provision shall not apply regarding the purchase from a licensed motor vehicle body parts dealer or through a public auction of motor vehicles or parts.

(Ord. No. 20,096, § 1, 4-5-01)

**Sec. 130-56. Reports.**

(a) It shall be the duty of every licensed secondhand motor vehicle body parts dealer to make out a report which itemizes each item of motor vehicle body parts either bought, bartered, sold or otherwise acquired from a seller.

(b) Such reporting form shall be on carbonless duplicating paper with one original and two copies. The superintendent of police shall describe the manner and detail of such reports and make them available to each permittee. These reports shall include, but not be limited to, the following items of information:

(1) Consecutively numbered forms.

(2) Date of transaction.

(3) Time of transaction.

(4) Name of permittee’s clerk or agent.

(5) Name of seller.

(6) Race, sex, height, weight, hair color and eye color of seller.

(7) Address and phone number of seller.

(8) Seller’s birth date.

(9) Seller’s Social Security number.

(10) Signature of seller.

(11) Dollar amount of transaction.

(12) A complete and accurate description of each item received by the permittee including:

a. The type of vehicle, model year, manufacturer,

b. Description of vehicle part, including color, identification number, and any other identifying features.

(13) A declaration signed by the permittee that the seller has produced valid photographic identification issued by

either the state, another state or by the United States military which bears a likeness of the seller.

(14) Seller’s identification card number and issuing entity.

(15) A declaration of ownership stating that the seller is in rightful possession of the items being offered to the permittee.

(16) The permittee shall cause to be made a right thumbprint of the seller.

(17) The permittee shall cause to be made on each motor vehicle part included on the reporting form, a permanently affixed indelible number, which shall be the individual voucher number on the reporting form provided by the department of police. The permittee shall make available to the department of police or any authorized city employee any motor vehicle parts and forms requested during normal business hours for inspection to determine that the procedures are being met.

laws.title: Penalties
laws.content:
The penalty for knowingly reporting false information on this report or incomplete information or the intentional failure to report transactions or not following the procedures or regulations as required by this division shall count as one offense for each instance or for each motor vehicle body part included, when more than one motor vehicle body part is transferred in the same transaction.

First offense—A minimum fine of $250.00 and a maximum fine of $500.00, and up to six months imprisonment, and the revocation of the permit to operate as a secondhand dealer for a one-year period.

Second offense—A minimum fine of $500.00 and up to six months imprisonment, and the revocation of the permit to operate as a secondhand dealer for a two-year period.

Third offense and any additional offenses—A minimum fine of $500.00 and a minimum of one month imprisonment with up to six months imprisonment and the revocation of the permit to operate as a secondhand dealer for a minimum three-year period.

(Ord. No. 20,096, § 1, 4-5-01)

laws.title: Buy-sell agreements; pawn transactions in general
laws.content:
Items that are usually sold as a set are considered a single item and must be included in the same pawn transaction, and a pledge item together with items that are accessories to the pledged item are considered a single item and must be included in the same transaction. A separate pawn transaction retains its separate character when it is renewed, unless the parties agree otherwise. The purchase of property for the purpose of selling it back at a stipulated price (sometimes called “buy-sell agreement”) shall be deemed a pawn transaction for the purpose of this article.

(Code 1956, § 44-5.1)

laws.content:

(Code 1956, § 46-7.1)

laws.title: Compliance with law
laws.content:
Pawnbrokers shall comply with all requirements imposed by this Code, city ordinance and all requirements of applicable state law including but not limited to the provisions of Title 37 of the Louisiana Revised Statutes and particularly the provisions of R.S. 37:1791 relative to the maximum rate of interest for pawn transactions.

(Code 1956, § 44-5.2)

laws.title: Records to be kept, entries required
laws.content:
(a) Every pawnbroker shall maintain a permanent record of all transactions of things pledged on the pawnshop premises. This record, which may be maintained electronically, shall be kept for a period of two years. Entries shall be made in the English language and all of the following shall be included:

(1) The pledgor’s name and address.

(2) The pledgor’s sex, race, and approximate height.

(3) The pledgor’s date of birth.

(4) The distinctive number from the pledgor’s state driver’s license, driver’s license from another state, international driver’s license, passport, military identification, or identification issued by a government agency or the United States Postal Service.

(5) A clear and accurate description of the pledged things, including model and serial numbers if indicated on the things.

(6) The date of the original pawn transaction.

(7) The maturity date of the original pawn transaction.

(b) For complying with the provisions of this section the pawnbroker shall be entitled to the service charge set forth in R.S. 37:1799.

(c) Such book shall be available for inspection on demand of the superintendent of police or any office or person acting under his authority along with the articles of property therein mentioned.

(Code 1956, § 44-7)

State law reference—Similar provisions, R.S. 37:1796.

**ARTICLE IV. JUNKYARDS***

**Sec. 130-136. Use of public places prohibited.**

It shall be unlawful for any person to wreck, dismantle or store, for commercial purposes, any motor-driven vehicle, automobile, automobile truck, or iron or steel junk, on the public sidewalks, streets and other public places of the city.

(Code 1956, § 44-1)

**Sec. 130-137. Enclosure.**

No person shall store or offer for sale any iron and steel junk or wreckage of motor-driven vehicles, or automobiles or any automobile truck on any open lot or parcel of ground that is not properly enclosed on all boundary lines with a proper, suitable and substantial fence not less than seven feet nor more than ten feet high, and properly screening such enclosed area from public view; provided, that the fence is kept in a constant state of good repair and no sign or other advertising matter is placed upon such fence.

(Code 1956, § 44-2)

*Cross references—Businesses, ch. 30; junk and abandoned vehicles, § 66-101 et seq.; sales and use tax, § 150-441 et seq.; occupational license tax, § 150-951 et seq.*

**Sec. 130-138. Location restrictions.**

No junkyard or any establishment for the storing, processing, purchase or sale of scrap iron, paper, rags, bottles or any other junk or salvage materials, shall be located or operated upon a plot of ground facing upon a U.S. Highway, or within 500 feet thereof, and within 100 yards of any school, either public or private, elementary or high, college, university, convent, seminary, playground, asylum or orphanage.

(Code 1956, § 44-3)

*State law reference—Limitations of junkyards, R.S. 48:461.9.*

**Sec. 130-139. Requirements for disposing of motor vehicles with gasoline tanks.**

(a) *Compliance required.* Persons, firms, and/or corporations operating a junkyard, and every customer, whether a person, firm or corporation, that sells or trades with a junkyard shall comply with this section for disposing of motor vehicles with gasoline tanks.

(b) *Definitions.* The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this section, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:

*Junkyard* means and includes scrap metal dealers, salvage companies, landfill operations, junkyard or junk car operators, or any other such entity that handles motor vehicles.

*Motor vehicle* means every device by which persons or things may be transported upon a public street, highway or bridge or off-road area, which device is self-propelled by any motor using any fuel or electricity.

(c) *Acceptance of motor vehicle with gasoline tank.* All motor vehicles shall be accepted by junkyards with a gasoline tank in its normal and usual configuration, allowing for changes due to ruin or damage. Customers with motor vehicles shall not be required to remove the gasoline tank from the vehicle or modify the tank or open the tank in any manner. No customer shall be required to remove a gasoline tank or its contents from a motor vehicle offered for scrap metal or salvage purposes

as a condition of acceptance by the junkyard, any act by a junkyard inconsistent with the provisions of this section is a violation of this Code.

(d) *Legal disposition of gasoline tank.* A junkyard shall not accept any motor vehicle for junk or salvage that does not have a gasoline tank with the vehicle unless the customer disposing of same provides written evidence that the gasoline tank was previously legally disposed of or sold. A copy of this written evidence shall be maintained under the name, address, and social security number of the customer for a period of not less than three years after the vehicle is acquired by the junkyard. A false claim that a motor vehicle’s gasoline tank was legally disposed of is a violation of this section.

(e) *Records to be made available.* The records of evidence of legal disposition of gasoline tanks shall be made available to the department of sanitation, its agents or assigns, for inspection and copy upon request at no charge, the department of sanitation shall monitor compliance with this section.

(f) *Acceptance of motor vehicle gasoline tanks.* A junkyard that accepts detached motor vehicle gasoline tanks brought in for scrap metal or salvage purposes shall not require any modification of the gasoline tank as a condition of acceptance.

(g) *Environmental regulations.* A junkyard’s disposal and handling of motor vehicle gasoline tanks shall be in accordance with all federal, state and local environmental regulations.

(h) *Penalties for violation.* The first violation of this section shall be a misdemeanor and shall be punishable by a fine of not less than $200.00 nor more than $500.00 or six months imprisonment. A second violation of this section within a six-month period shall be punishable by a fine of not less than $500.00 or not less than six months imprisonment or both.

Every antique dealer, as defined in this chapter, is subject to the provisions of this chapter.  
(M.C.S., Ord. No. 19,114, § 2, 2-18-99)

laws.title: Due date for reports following holidays
laws.content:
If any report required by this chapter would have to be filed on any legal holiday, such report shall be due on the next business day following such holiday between the hours of 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.  
(M.C.S., Ord. No. 19,114, § 2, 2-18-99)

laws.title: Police to furnish blank report forms
laws.content:
The proper blank forms for the reports required by this chapter shall be furnished at the office of the superintendent of police, on application.  
(M.C.S., Ord. No. 19,114, § 2, 2-18-99)

laws.title: Prohibited acquisitions from certain classes of persons
laws.content:
It shall be unlawful for any antique dealer, owner, keeper, or agent of any antique shop, to buy, exchange, or otherwise acquire any article covered by this part from any minor under the age of 18 years, from a person appearing to be intoxicated, from a person known to be a notorious thief, or from a person known to have been convicted of larceny or burglary.  
(M.C.S., Ord. No. 19,114, § 2, 2-18-99; Ord. No. 19,710, § 1, 6-15-00)

laws.title: Duty to notify police when article tendered is believed stolen
laws.content:
If any article covered by this part is tendered for sale, exchange, or consignment to an antique dealer, owner, keeper, or agent of any antique shop, and such person has good reason to believe that such article was stolen, the antique dealer, owner, keeper, or agent of any antique shop shall immediately notify the police department.  
(M.C.S., Ord. No. 19,114, § 2, 2-18-99; Ord. No. 19,710, § 1, 6-15-00)

laws.title: Retention of acquisitions
laws.content:
It shall be unlawful for an antique dealer to sell, exchange, barter, or remove from their place of business any cemetery artifact that has been bought, exchanged, deposited on a consignment basis, or otherwise deposited with them by any transferor for a period of 30 days from the date of the antique dealer’s acquisition.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 19,114, § 2, 2-18-99; Ord. No. 19,710, § 1, 6-15-00)

laws.title: Records required
laws.content:
Every antique dealer shall be required to maintain a record, setting forth each purchase or acquisition, whether on a consignment basis or otherwise, of any object which meets the definition of a cemetery artifact, when the value of any single piece of such merchandise or article received shall be $25.00 or more for each single transaction. The price at which a piece of such merchandise is offered for sale or at auction by an antique dealer shall be considered prima facie evidence of the value of the piece of such merchandise. Each cemetery artifact purchased, acquired on a consignment basis, or otherwise acquired shall be recorded at the time of each transaction and such record shall contain an accurate detailed description in the English language of the merchandise or article received as set forth in section 131-39 (b)(13) herein along with the amount paid therefor or, in the case of acquisition by consignment or otherwise, the value of the article, as estimated by the antique dealer. This record shall be kept for a minimum period of three years. Copies of the report set forth in section 131-39 hereinbelow will satisfy the records requirement.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 19,114, § 2, 2-18-99; Ord. No. 19,710, § 1, 6-15-00)

laws.title: Reports required
laws.content:
(a) Every antique dealer shall be required to deliver an originally signed report to the superintendent of police, or his designee, on a form provided by the police department, within 24 hours of any transaction involving cemetery artifacts. This report shall be filled out in its entirety. One copy shall be given to the seller/transferor and another copy shall be retained by the antique dealer on the business premises for a period of at least three years and shall be made available to federal, state, and local law enforcement and regulatory agencies upon request.

(b) These reports shall include, but not be limited to, the following items of information:

(1) Consecutively numbered forms.

(2) Date of transaction.

(3) Time of transaction.

(4) Name of antique dealer’s clerk or agent handling the transaction.

(5) Name of seller/transferor.

(6) Race, sex, height, weight, hair color and eye color of seller/transferor.

(7) Address and phone number of seller/transferor.

(8) Seller’s/transferor’s birth date.

(9) Seller’s/transferor’s social security number.

(10) Name, address and telephone number of seller’s/transferor’s employer, if available.

(11) Signature of seller/transferor.

(12) Dollar amount of transaction or, in the case of acquisition on a consignment basis, value of article as estimated by the antique dealer.

(13) A complete and accurate description of each item received by the antique dealer, including:

a. The type of article, e.g, statue, brick, signage, plaque, urn, pot, bench, chair, cross, vase, gate, fence, or any portion thereof;

laws.title: Prohibited practices
laws.content:
An antique dealer shall not:

(1) Accept cemetery artifacts from any natural person under the age of 18.

(3) Falsify, obliterate, remove from the records, or fail to include in the report required in this chapter any accounts relating to the antique dealer’s transactions involving objects which the antique dealer knew or should have known were cemetery artifacts as defined in this chapter.

laws.title: Penalties
laws.content:

laws.content:
The provisions of this chapter regarding accessory signs shall not apply to any accessory sign which has an area less than 40 square feet; provided that the sign is not a detached sign the erection of which would require a building permit.

(Code 1956, § 3A-6(a))

laws.title: Chapter provisions complementary
laws.content:
The requirements to do or not do anything imposed by this chapter shall be in addition to any other requirements imposed by this Code or any other applicable law, except that where any other law provides a more restrictive requirement on the same subject matter, the more restrictive requirement shall supersede the less restrictive requirement of this chapter.

(Code 1956, § 3A-8)

laws.title: Enforcement agency designated
laws.content:
The director of the department of safety and permits or his departmental or agencies representative(s) is hereby designated as the primary enforcement agency to administer and enforce the terms and conditions of this chapter and all other provisions of laws relating to signs and shall, in such administration and enforcement, coordinate his efforts with the New Orleans

*Cross reference—Administration, ch. 2.

Police Department or any duly authorized law enforcement officer or code enforcement officer(s) or all other persons having enforcement powers or responsibilities.

(Code 1956, § 3A-2(a); M.C.S., Ord. No. 21877, § 1, 3-17-05)

laws.title: Enforcement responsibility
laws.content:
The duties of the department of safety and permits shall include not only the issuance of permits as required by this chapter, or by other applicable law. The department of safety and permits, New Orleans Police Department or other duly authorized law enforcement or code enforcement officer(s) have the responsibility of ensuring that all signs comply with this chapter [and] any other applicable law, and that all signs for which a permit is required do in fact have a permit. These departments and agencies shall make such inspections as may be necessary and initiate appropriate action to bring about compliance with this chapter and other applicable law if such inspection discloses any instance of noncompliance. These departments or agencies shall investigate thoroughly any complaints of alleged violations of municipal laws governing signs. The enforcement agency may locate the persons in violation by calling the number advertised as a method of investigation.

(Code 1956, § 3A-2(b); M.C.S., Ord. No. 21877, § 1, 3-17-05)

laws.title: Powers of enforcement
laws.content:
The department of safety and permits and the New Orleans Police Department or any duly authorized law enforcement or code enforcement officers or other persons having enforcement powers or responsibilities shall have the power and authority to administer and enforce the conditions of this chapter and all other laws relating to signs. Included among such powers are the following specific powers:

(1) Every sign for which a permit is required may be subject to the inspection and approval of the department. When deemed advisable by the department, a sign may be inspected at the point of manufacture if such point is within or adjacent to the city limits.
