(2) Upon presentation of proper identification to the owner, agent, or tenant in charge of such property, the departments, agencies or their representative(s) may enter, for the purposes of inspecting and investigating signs or sign structures, any building, structure, or other premises or property between the hours of 8:00 a.m. to 10:00 p.m., Sunday through Saturdays, and in the case of business, during the hours of operation of the business provided, however, that in cases of emergency where extreme hazards are known to exist to persons, loss of life, or severe property damage, and where the owner, agent or tenant in charge of the property is not available after the departmental or agencies representative(s) have made a good faith effort to locate same, the departmental or agencies representative(s) may enter the aforementioned structures and premises at any time upon presentation of proper identification to any other person on the premises. Whenever the departmental or agencies representative(s) shall enter upon private property, under any circumstances, for the purpose of inspecting and/or investigating signs or sign structures, which charge, shall be notified of his presence and shown his proper and official credentials. The departmental or agencies representative(s), when on private property, shall observe the establishment’s rules and regulations concerning safety, internal security and fire protection. In a case where permission to enter is denied, entry shall be accomplished only pursuant to a warrant obtained as otherwise provided by law.

(3) Upon notice and issuance of a stop-work order from the director of the department of safety and permits, work on any sign that is being conducted in a manner contrary to the provisions of this chapter or other applicable law or is being conducted in a dangerous or unsafe manner shall be immediately stopped. Such notice and order shall be in writing and shall be given to the owner of the property, or to his agent, or to the person doing the work, and shall state the conditions under which work may be resumed. Where an emergency exists, written notice shall not be required to be given by the departmental or agencies representative(s).

(4) Following the issuance of a stop-work order, the department or agencies representative(s) shall initiate proceedings to revoke any permit issued for the work covered by such stop work order, unless the cause of the stop work order is resolved to the departmental or agencies representatives) satisfaction.

(5) The departmental or agencies representative(s) shall have, and is hereby granted, the power and authority to revoke any and all permits authorized by this chapter for violation of the terms and provisions of this chapter; and all other applicable provisions of law, provided that, the departmental or agencies representatives) shall conduct a hearing prior to the revocation of any permit authorized under this chapter to determine the facts incident to the pending revocation. The person whose permit is under consideration shall be given at least 15 calendar days’ written notice of the hearing and shall be permitted to present relevant facts and legal arguments regarding the pending revocation. Following such, the department or agency representative shall consider the merits of the case and shall present a written opinion prior to any action. However, that if in the opinion of the department the health, safety, or welfare of the citizens of the city is endangered by any violation of this chapter, the department of safety and permits or agency representatives may immediately revoke any or all permits authorized by this chapter and shall conduct the necessary hearing as soon as possible thereafter, but in no case later than three business days after the effec-

**Sec. 134-39. Violations and penalties.**

Any person who shall violate any provision of this chapter shall be guilty of a misdemeanor and shall, upon conviction thereof, be punished by a fine of not less than $500.00 for each violation. Each day in which any violation shall occur shall constitute a separate offense. In addition, the city attorney is hereby authorized to take all actions, both legal and equitable, necessary to assure compliance with this chapter.

(Code 1956, § 3A-2(d); M.C.S., Ord. No. 21877, § 1, 3-17-05)

**Sec. 134-40. Appeals.**

Any person wishing to appeal a decision of the department of safety and permits or agencies representative(s) on the grounds that the decision misconstrues or wrongly interprets this chapter or other applicable law may, within 30 days after the decision, appeal the same to the appropriate board, as hereinafter provided. Where the decision from which an appeal is taken is based upon the Comprehensive Zoning Ordinance or a similar land use law, appeal shall be the board of zoning adjustments; when the decision from which an appeal is taken is based upon laws or regulation, including this chapter, pertaining to the design, construction, alteration, demolition, or structural aspects of buildings and/or signs, appeal shall be to the board of building standards and appeals. An appeal timely taken to the improper board shall be transferred to the proper board; and in doubtful cases, or when neither board appears to be the proper board, the mayor, pursuant to section 4-105 of the Charter, shall assign the appeal for decision by whichever board appears more appropriate. Appeals from the decision of a board shall be as otherwise provided by law, and from the decision of the board of zoning adjustments, and/or board of building standards and appeals shall be, pursuant to its rules and regulation, to the civil district court; provided that the appealing party shall give notice of appeal in writing to the department of safety and permits or agencies, representative(s) no less than ten calendar days following the decision appealed from and provided further that the appealing party shall comply with the department of safety and permits’ or agencies representative(s)’ decision pending appeal unless the department or agency representative(s) shall direct otherwise or unless otherwise expressly provided by law.

(Code 1956, § 3A-2(e); M.C.S., Ord. No. 21877, § 1, 3-17-05)

**Sec. 134-41. Sign companies.**

(a) *Registration required.* Any person who engages as a business in the erection, placement, leasing or permitting of others to use signs shall first obtain a registration from the department of safety and permits to do so.

(b) *Registration fee.* Any person required to obtain a registration under the terms of this section shall pay an annual registration fee of $400.00.

(c) *Address and agent for service of process.* Any business which is required to obtain a registration under the terms of this section shall at all times maintain an office within the city, the current address of which shall be recorded with the department, or shall appoint and file a record with the department representative and agent within the city for service of process.

(Code 1956, § 3A-4)

**Sec. 134-42. Sign maintenance and removal.**

(a) *Maintenance.* All signs shall be kept in good repair, and unless of galvanized or noncorroding metal or treated with appropriate wood preservative, shall be thoroughly painted as often as is necessary consistent with good maintenance. All braces, bolts, clips, supporting frames and fastenings shall be free from deterioration, termite infestation, rot, or loosening. All signs shall be able to withstand safely at all

times the wind pressures specified in any applicable law. In case any sign is not so maintained, the department shall give written notice to the owner or lessee thereof to so maintain the sign, or to remove the sign.

(b) Unsafe signs. Should any sign, in the opinion of the department, become insecure or in danger of falling or otherwise unsafe, the departmental representative shall give written notice of the condition of the sign to the person owning, leasing, or responsible for the sign. Such person so notified shall correct the unsafe condition of the sign in a manner to be approved by the department in conformity with the provisions of this chapter or other applicable law.

(c) Unlawful signs. In case any sign shall be installed, erected, constructed or maintained in violation of any of the terms of this chapter or other applicable law, the department shall give written notice to the owner, lessee, or person responsible for such sign ordering such owner, lessee or person to alter the sign so as to comply with the law, or to remove the sign.

(d) Removal of signs. Any written notice to alter or to remove a sign shall be given by the department by certified mail or written notice served personally upon the owner, lessee, or person responsible for the sign, or the owner’s agent. If such order is not complied with within 15 calendar days, the department shall initiate proceedings under this chapter to revoke the permit and remove the sign at the expense of the owner, lessee, or person responsible therefor.

(e) Hazardous signs. If the department determines that any sign is causing an extraordinary and immediate hazard to safety or if the owner or person having custody of a sign cannot be determined, or if the department after diligent effort has been unable to give the notice required by the other subsections herein, and if no other provision of law authorizes the city to cause the sign to be immediately removed, then the director shall cause a notice to be affixed to the sign in a prominent place, bearing the date of its posting, which notice shall instruct the person having custody or control of the sign to remove it immediately and shall identify the department as the city agency to be contacted. The notice

shall set forth the text of this subsection in full. If the sign has not been removed by 7:30 a.m. of the third calendar day after the posting of the notice, the department shall cause it to be removed and thereafter disposed of in the manner provided by section 134-122(b).

(Code 1956, § 3A-5)

laws.title: Existing signs
laws.content:
(a) After the date of passage of the ordinance from which this chapter was derived, all signs legally existing shall receive, upon application, operating permits according to a phased schedule to be determined by the department of safety and permits so as to require the permitting of the signs on or before certain dates in each of the municipal districts or in each of the wards of the city. For the purposes of this section, a private nonprofit organization is defined as an organization which possesses tax exempt status under section 501C of the Internal Revenue Code or is organized as a nonprofit corporation under the laws of any of the states of the United States of America.

laws.title: Electrical signs

Fees are hereby levied and imposed on advertising signage and all other signage constructed, erected, created, or leased in the city:

**Sec. 134-122. Placement of signs that are temporary in nature.**

The following temporary signage, when not prohibited by any other provision of law, may be placed on the public right-of-way. The following exceptions are inclusive, no other temporary signage shall be permitted:

(1) Political signs may be placed on the public right-of-way 48 hours prior to an election. Such signs shall be removed 48 hours after the closing of the polls for an election.

(2) Real estate signage advertising an open house. Such signs are limited to 48 hours prior to the open house and shall be removed upon completion of the open house.

(3) The placement of signs for garage, moving, or rummage sales, provided that such signs are not displayed for more than a total of 48 hours.

(4) The placement of signs relative to movie filming locations provided that such signs are not displayed for more than a total of 48 hours.

(5) The placement of signs notifying the community of official neighborhood or community meetings, provided that such signs are not displayed for more than five days prior to said meeting, and are removed upon completion of said meeting.

(6) The placement of signs notifying the community of lost and/or found pets/animals, provided that such signs are not displayed for more than ten days.

**Sec. 134-123. Signs resembling official signs.**

No sign shall be constructed which resembles any official marker erected by the city, state or any governmental agency or which by reason of position, shape or color would conflict with the proper functioning of any traffic sign, signal, or switch, or which, by its shape or color would conflict with or be confused with emergency vehicle lights, especially blinking lights. Use of words such as "stop," "look," "danger," or any other word, phrase, symbol or character in such a manner as to interfere with, mislead, or confuse traffic is prohibited.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 24452, § 1, 6-2-11)

No permit for a sign extending beyond private property onto a public street, public sidewalk, or

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 24452, § 1, 6-2-11)

**Sec. 134-125. Signs obscuring or interfering with view.**

Signs may not be located or illuminated in such a manner as to obscure or otherwise interfere with the effectiveness of an official traffic sign, signal, or device, or so as to obstruct or interfere with the view of a driver of approaching, merging, or intersecting traffic, or so as to prevent any traveler on any street from obtaining a clear view of approaching vehicles for a distance of 250 feet along the street.

**Sec. 134-126. Shielding of lighted signs, interference with drivers of motor vehicles.**

Signs containing lights which are not effectively shielded as to prevent beams or rays of light from being directed at any portion of the traveled roadways from which the sign is primarily viewed and which are of such intensity or brilliance as to cause glare or to impair the vision of the driver of any motor vehicle, or which otherwise interfere with any driver’s operation of a motion vehicle are prohibited.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 24452, § 1, 6-2-11)

**Sec. 134-127. Removal of signs or awnings obstructing view.**

The director of the department of public works shall, whenever any sign or awning in his/her opinion obstructs the view of any street, in any manner, shall give not more than five days’ notice to its proprietor for removal, or for the reduction of the size of the sign or awning. **Sec. 134-128. Advertisements on streets, telegraph poles, etc., prohibited.**

(a) It shall be unlawful for any person or entity to post or paint advertisements of any kind on any street, sidewalk, public buildings, utility poles, light standards, street signs, parking meters, trees located in public right-of-way or traffic signal standards.

Any signage seized by the city under this chapter that may be recyclable, shall be provided to the city sanctioned recycling program. If the signage is unrecyclable, or deemed to be unrecyclable by the city sanctioned recycling program, conventional disposal is permitted.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 24452, § 1, 6-2-11)

laws.title: Exceptions, ten year's exception for existing structures
laws.content:
It shall be lawful for any person to construct, use or maintain any billboard, signboard, display sign or any other advertising display of any nature whatsoever within the areas described in sections 134-167 and 134-168 when such billboard, signboard, display sign or other advertising display falls within one of the following specified categories.

(1) One sign not exceeding 15 square feet in overall measurements shall be permitted on any lot offering such lot for lease or sale;

(2) Wherever any advertising structure had actually been constructed and was in existence prior to October 16, 1953, such billboards, signboards, display signs or any other advertising structure may be used and maintained only for a period of ten years from October 16, 1953 and at the expiration of this ten-year period all such billboards, signboards, display signs or any other advertising display must be completely removed from their locations; it being understood, however, that the owner or operator of any such billboards, signboards, display signs or any other advertising displays that were in existence prior to October 16, 1953, may continue to repair or remodel, illuminate, redesign and relocate such billboards, signboards, display signs or any other advertising displays provided that such changes shall not enlarge the overall square foot area of the advertising copy and shall in no wise be deemed to affect the ten-year amortization period set out herein.

laws.title: Responsibility for solid waste disposal
laws.content: The city shall be responsible for providing adequate solid waste management and disposal facilities. This responsibility may be delegated to a private operator through an operating permit issued by the department of safety and permits. (Code 1956, § 28-38)

laws.title: Dump closing
laws.content:
All persons operating land disposal sites which are dumps shall convert them to sanitary landfills no later than December 31, 1977, or close them. The sites shall be closed in accordance with the following criteria:

(1) Access to the site shall be restricted by a fence or other appropriate and effective means.

(2) Information signs shall be placed at the entrance to the site on roads leading to the site stating that it is closed, the penalty for dumping at the site, the location and hours of operation of the alternate approved site and the name of the operating agency.

(3) A responsible person shall be assigned to supervise the closing procedures on a full-time basis during the closing operations.

(4) Burning of solid waste shall be prohibited except upon the approval by the fire prevention division and state air control commission.

(5) The site shall be closed to incoming solid waste as soon as the alternate site is in operation.

(6) Steps shall be taken, where potential water pollution exists, to prevent its continuance by diverting surface waters around the site, removing wastes from the water table, or by other means approved by the department.

(7) Upon completion, the closed site shall be covered with two feet of earth compacted

**Sec. 138-4. Permits required for solid waste management facilities or systems.**

(a) After December 31, 1977, no solid waste management facility or system shall be operated, maintained, constructed, expanded or modified without an appropriate and currently valid operating permit issued by the department of safety and permits. Such permits shall be annually renewable.

(b) Temporary operating permits may be issued to existing solid waste management facilities or systems, upon submission of a compliance schedule to correct deficiencies. An operating permit shall be issued by the department of safety and permits when the facility meets all standards for operations. Failure to correct deficiencies within the compliance schedule shall result in revocation of the temporary operating permit and initiation of formal enforcement procedures.

(c) The department of safety and permits shall issue operating permits only in conformity with the provisions of this article, approval of appropriate state agencies, and upon payment of a permit fee of $500.00.

(a) All vehicles engaged in transporting commercial, contractors' household garbage, garden trimmings, manufacturing or trade refuse, residential or business trash, or other debris or waste products shall be provided with permits from the director of the department of sanitation authorizing the use of such vehicles for such purpose. Owners and/or operators of vehicles engaged in transporting waste products shall pay a permit fee of $15.00 and provide certification that the disposal of such refuse shall be in a manner and at places approved by the director.

Private passenger cars and station wagons are hereby exempt from the provisions of this section.

Proof of service within the city shall be determined by the presentation to the department of sanitation by the permit seeking individual of existing contracts with city-based concerns, or the presentation to the department of sanitation of a notarized statement confirming operations within the city.

laws.title: Carts to be provided
laws.content:
The city's service provider shall provide to each eligible and occupied service location a roll cart container for storage of garbage and trash in a sanitary manner. Roll cart containers shall remain the property of the city at all times and are not to be removed from the associated service location.

A roll cart is a plastic, wheeled refuse receptacle having a tight-fitting, attached lid, carrying identification of the city, with a designated serial number/barcode and whose design, construction and capacity shall be approved by the city. The city's designated service provider will supply each eligible and occupied service location with one roll cart. Locations in the French Quarter or the Downtown Development District will be issued 35-gallon carts. Locations outside the French Quarter or the Downtown Development District will receive 96-gallon carts.

Eligible residents and small business owners who live or operate within the boundaries of the French Quarter, the Downtown Development District, or Frenchmen Street between Esplanade Avenue and Dauphine Street, may request an exemption from the use of a roll cart. Exemptions will be granted to residents who are elderly, disabled, or handicapped, or if the infrastructure does not permit storage of the roll cart off the public right-of-way. Exemptions will be granted provided that a written request, including the resident's name, address, apartment number, telephone number, email address (optional), and the number of units in the building or small business, is submitted to the department of sanitation. Additionally, the request must include a copy of a current sewerage and water board bill for the unit, the name and address of the property owner, if different from the resident, and the reason for the request. Upon approval, the resident will be notified and the cart at the specified service location will be removed.

Residents and small businesses that receive an exemption from the use of a roll cart are required to place their solid waste in 0.8 mil or greater, black, garbage bags. White trash bags, grocery bags, paper bags, and cardboard boxes are not acceptable for collection of solid waste. Roll carts are mandatory for all residents who do not have an approved exemption request on file with the department of sanitation. Any resident or small business owner who is in violation of the provisions of this section may be cited and fined for littering.

Only the city's representative shall be authorized to remove any city-owned solid waste cart from its assigned service location. It shall be unlawful for any other person to willfully damage or destroy any garbage cart, or to remove any garbage cart from the address to which it is assigned. Each eligible service location is entitled to one replacement roll cart if the initial cart is stolen. Any further replacements must be purchased from the city's service provider.

(Code 1956, § 28-17; M.C.S., Ord. No. 22601, § 1, 4-19-07; M.C.S., Ord. No. 27886, § 1, 10-4-18; M.C.S., Ord. No. 28541, § 1, 11-5-20)

laws.title: Carts to be covered
laws.content:
The roll cart container shall be stored with the attached lid closed at all times, except during the placement or removal of contents.

(Code 1956, § 28-7; M.C.S., Ord. No. 22601, § 1, 4-19-07; M.C.S., Ord. No. 27886, § 1, 10-4-18)

laws.title: Days of collection; placement and removal of garbage carts
laws.content:
(a) Except as otherwise designated by the director, the automated or semi-automated solid waste collection system shall be the method used for household and small business solid waste collection services provided by the city.

(1) The director of the department of sanitation shall designate when the collection of trash and garbage shall be made in various areas of the city.

(2) All locations outside the French Quarter, the Downtown Development District, and Frenchmen Street between Esplanade Avenue and Dauphine Street, that receive curbside collection of solid waste shall place their solid waste curbside for collection prior to 5:00 a.m. on the day designated for collection, but not prior to 4:00 p.m. of the day prior to the designated collection day for collection between the hours of 5:00 a.m. and 8:00 p.m. All carts shall be removed from the curb or service alley as promptly as possible, but no later than 8:00 p.m. on the day of collection.

a. The director of the department of sanitation shall have the authority to approve early collections during the months of June through September when excessive heat is a risk to the health and safety of workers. Between the months of June and September, collections may occur between the hours of 4:00 a.m. and 8:00 p.m.

(3) All locations within the boundaries of the French Quarter, the Downtown Development District, or Frenchmen Street between Esplanade and Dauphine Street, that receive curbside collection of solid waste shall place their solid waste curbside for collection prior to 4:00 a.m. for collection between the hours of 4:00 a.m. and 8:00 a.m. All carts shall be removed from the curb as promptly as possible, but no later than 9:00 a.m. after the morning collection. Properties within the

Supp. No. 109

area bounded by the downtown side of Canal Street, the rear property line of the properties fronting on the lakeside of Dauphine Street, the rear property line of the properties fronting on the downtown side of Dumaine Street, and the Mississippi River, the Downtown Development District, or Frenchmen Street between Esplanade Avenue and Dauphine Street, that receive twice-per-day collection, shall place their solid waste curbside for the second collection no earlier than 3:30 p.m. for collection between the hours of 4:00 p.m. and 6:00 p.m. All carts shall be removed from the curb as promptly as possible after collection. All carts shall be removed from the curb between the hours of 9:00 a.m. and 3:30 p.m.

(4) Solid waste from commercial businesses within the boundaries of the French Quarter, the Downtown Development District, or Frenchmen Street between Esplanade Avenue and Dauphine Street, shall be properly contained in garbage receptacles with tight-fitting lids or placed in fastened 3.0-mil or greater thick, black, plastic bags. White trash bags, grocery bags, paper bags, and cardboard boxes are not acceptable for collection of solid waste.

(5) All commercial businesses within the boundaries of the French Quarter, the Downtown Development District, or Frenchmen Street between Esplanade Avenue and Dauphine Street, shall make arrangements with their private collection contractors to increase the frequency of collections during special events if significant increases in their volumes of solid waste are anticipated.

(6) Any person 60 years of age or older shall be allowed to place carts with trash and garbage, bagged yard waste, or bundles of tree limbs at the curb adjacent to his or her residence outside of the items listed in section 138-42(a)(2) and 138-42(a)(3). Any person 60 years of age or older who receives written notification of a violation of this provision shall provide proof of residence and proof of age in order to be exempt from the penalties imposed by section 138-37.

(7) Service locations receiving curbside collection shall place roll carts at the curb in front of the service location on the designated collection days in such a manner that it allows for the safe and efficient operation of the collection vehicle and does not interfere with pedestrian or vehicular traffic. Roll carts shall be placed so that they open toward the street or alley. It shall be unlawful to permit carts to remain adjacent to the curb, except on regular collection days. Carts shall be stored, between collection days, on the service location’s private property so as to not interfere with pedestrian or vehicular traffic along sidewalks, streets, and other rights-of-way.

(b) All contract haulers collecting or transporting refuse within the boundaries of the French Quarter, the Downtown Development District, or Frenchmen Street between Esplanade Avenue and Dauphine Street, shall complete all work between the hours of 4:00 a.m. and 8:00 a.m. Commercial haulers that provide twice per day collection within the boundaries of the French Quarter, the Downtown Development District, or Frenchmen Street between Esplanade Avenue and Dauphine Street, shall complete all night work between the hours of 4:00 p.m. and 6:00 p.m.

(c) It shall constitute presumptive evidence that the occupant and/or owner of the establishment whose address corresponds to the serial number or barcode on the roll cart in which such garbage is held, or on the garbage itself, specifically authorized and/or directed the placement of the garbage out at a time other than authorized above. This presumption shall be applicable when such garbage is found adjacent to, or in the vicinity of the building of the party or parties whose address corresponds with the roll cart in which such garbage is found, or on the contents found in the cart.

Disposal of yard waste, tree branches, shrubbery

Yard waste, tree branches, and shrubbery shall not be placed in roll carts and shall be collected in accordance with section 138-43.

laws.title: Waste collection: commercial facilities, private contractors or businesses and multi-unit residential structures
laws.content:
(a) The following locations are not eligible for service from the city and are responsible for contracting for private collection and disposal of solid waste:

(1) Hotels.

(2) Bars.

(3) Restaurants.

(4) Any location containing five or more units.

§ 138-48

(5) Any location within the French Quarter or Downtown Development District that generates more than 35 gallons of solid waste at each regular collection.

(6) Any location outside of the French Quarter and Downtown Development District that generates more than 96 gallons of solid waste at each regular collection.

(7) Unoccupied properties.

Locations not eligible for city service shall comply with the provisions of section 138-58.

(b) Any owner of a small business or residential property being repaired or constructed by private contractors shall be responsible for the removal and disposal of all bulky waste and construction and reconstruction debris generated from such work. No such waste or debris shall be placed curbside for collection by the city’s service providers or placed on the neutral grounds.

(c) The city shall require any location not eligible for service pursuant to this section to provide evidence of a valid and current contract for the private collection and disposal of solid waste prior to the issuance of any occupational permit at that location, or any renewal thereof. A copy of the foregoing contract shall be kept on the premises at all times and made available to rangers from the department of sanitation upon request.

laws.title: Maximum collections for one service location
laws.content:
Outside the French Quarter and Downtown Development District, not more than 96 gallons of solid waste per service location shall be removed at each regular collection. Within the French Quarter and Downtown Development District, not more than 35 gallons of solid waste per service location shall be removed at each regular collection. Bulky waste shall be collected in accordance with section 138-43.

laws.title: Improperly prepared refuse not collected; improper carts taken as trash
laws.content:
Only city-owned roll carts shall be used for the collection of household and small commercial business waste. Only garbage and trash placed in the roll cart will be collected. Garbage or trash deposited into unauthorized containers and cans, or bagged garbage (not yard waste) separate from the roll cart will not be collected, unless a properly authorized exemption has been granted. Only bags containing yard waste will be collected. The director of the department of sanitation may refuse to collect garbage or trash whenever such refuse is not contained in a city-owned roll cart or the residence or business has not been granted a properly authorized exemption. Any other trash or garbage cart shall be collected as trash after notice has been given to the occupant or agent that such cart is not authorized and is unfit for use.

(Code 1956, § 28-12; M.C.S., Ord. No. 22601, § 1, 4-19-07)

laws.title: Prohibited disposal methods
laws.content:
(a) No solid waste shall be disposed of except by sanitary landfill, incineration, recycling process, or other method approved by the department of safety and permits.

(b) No solid waste shall be disposed of by being placed:

(1) In an area subject to frequent and periodic flooding unless drainage provisions approved by the department of safety and permits are installed.

(2) Within 500 feet of any habitation or place of business that is served by a public water supply or within 1,000 feet of any habitation or place of business that is served by an individual water supply well located on the premises. This prohibition is not intended to prohibit the servicing of a disposal facility with a public water supply.

(3) On any public highway, street, road, alley, or the right-of-way thereof.

Supp. No. 93

CD138:11
§ 138-48

NEW ORLEANS CODE

(4) Within the boundaries of any airport property whether such airport be for public, private or limited use.

(5) Within two miles of the closest point of any runway at any airport licensed by the state or any airport operated by the federal government which is or may be used by turbo-jet aircraft; or within one mile of any aircraft runway used only by piston-engine-type aircraft, unless it has been determined by the Federal Aviation Administration that the proposed facility poses no safety hazard to aircraft in the vicinity.

(6) In any area other than the above defined areas that in the opinion of the department of safety and permits would result in damage to the environment.

(c) The prohibitions contained in subsections (a) and (b) of this section shall not be construed as applicable to solid waste placed for collection in accordance with this article.

(Code 1956, § 28-42(1)—(3))

laws.title: Burning prohibited
laws.content:
No burning of solid waste shall be permitted at any landfill site.

(Code 1956, § 28-42(4))

laws.title: Hazardous wastes
laws.content:
The disposal of toxic or hazardous waste which may create a condition harmful to the environment, shall, at the owner's expense, be rendered safe and sanitary prior to delivery to the waste disposal facility.

(Code 1956, § 28-42(5))

laws.title: Infectious wastes
laws.content:
Infectious waste shall be properly incinerated or processed by an alternate method which has been approved by the department of safety and permits. No raw infectious waste shall be deposited in any sanitary landfill or dump or recycling facility.

(Code 1956, §§ 28-15, 28-42(6))

laws.title: Construction on filled sites
laws.content:
The construction of buildings, sewage or gas or water supply mains, parking lots, or paved areas on or through completed portions of sites filled with solid waste is prohibited unless specifically approved by the department of safety and permits.

(Code 1956, §§ 28-15, 28-42(7))

State law references—Infectious waste disposal, R.S. 30:2180 et seq.; office of solid and hazardous wastes, R.S. 36:238(D).

laws.title: Certain refuse not acceptable for collection
laws.content:
Contractors' refuse and manufacturing or trade refuse is not acceptable for municipal collection.

(Code 1956, § 28-13)

laws.title: Removal of flammable materials
laws.content:
The producers of such waste materials as celluloid trimmings, motion picture films, rags or other materials soaked with gasoline, kerosene or other flammable materials shall place such materials in metal containers with tight covers and remove them for disposal as instructed by the director of the department of sanitation.

(Code 1956, § 28-16)

laws.title: Disposal of explosives
laws.content:
It shall be unlawful to dispose of unexploded ammunition, gunpowder, fireworks and other forms of explosives by putting the same in garbage or trash containers placed out for collection.

(Code 1956, § 28-16.1)

laws.title: Disposal of unusable television picture tubes
laws.content:
It shall be unlawful for any person to dispose of or to put out on a public street or walkway any television picture tube. Such tube shall be devacuumized by a licensed television technician who shall dispose of same at a city refuse disposal facility.

laws.title: Sanitation charges; collection
laws.content:
(a) The fees for the collection and disposal of refuse, garbage, trash and other sanitation services shall be as follows for services rendered during the periods indicated below:

(1) Each residential unit, including each residential unit in multi-residential structures, per month: $24.00.

(2) Business, professional or service office and institution, per month, per unit: $24.00.

(3) Commercial, industrial and manufacturing establishment, per month, per unit: $48.00.

(b) The service fees imposed pursuant to section (a) above shall be mandatory, shall be due and owed by the sewerage and water board account holder, and shall be collected from the sewerage and water board account holder, provided:

(1) That funds of the sewerage and water board may not be used for any purpose except for the operation and maintenance of the sewerage, water and drainage systems.

(2) That no part of the cost of the procedure of including the sanitation service charge on the water and/or sewerage bills of the sewerage and water board shall be incurred by the sewerage and water board, and, accordingly, any fees owed to the sewerage and water board pursuant to a Cooperative Endeavor Agreement (hereinafter "CEA") between the City of New Orleans and the sewerage and water board shall be deducted from all sanitation collections received and collected by the sewerage and water board and that such deductions, which are subject to audit by the department of finance, shall be made monthly when the net proceeds are delivered to the city.

(3) That the sewerage and water board is relieved of any and all responsibility of the collection of the sanitation service charges if the sewerage and water board account holder fails to pay the service charges at the time the water and/or sewerage bills are paid and that all methods of enforcing such collection shall be the responsibility of the city. However, if there is a CEA between the city and the sewerage and water board pursuant to La. R.S. 33:4169.1, the sewerage and water board, at the direction of the city, shall terminate the supply of water to any premises or person delinquent in the payment of sanitation service charges in conformity with La. R.S. 33:4169.1 and the CEA. Prior to the suspension of water supply as the result of a delinquency in payment of sanitation services charges, notice of such suspension shall be mailed to the address of the premises where service will be suspended.

(4) That the collection of such sanitation service charges shall not impair or affect, in any manner or form, the authority of the sewerage and water board to collect its water bills, and its bills for sewerage service as set forth by the procedure adopted by the sewerage and water board.

(5) That the city may contract with a private attorney, law firm or collection agency for legal and other services related to the collection of the sanitation service charges and any penalties attendant thereto.

(6) That all complaints made to the sewerage and water board regarding the collection of sanitation service charges shall be referred to the proper representative of the city, unless otherwise provided by the Cooperative Endeavor Agreement.

(7) Where a charge has been made for sanitation service and no water and sewerage charges are billed by the sewerage and water board during the billing period, the person paying the sanitation service charge under this section may make a claim for refund by filing a sworn application for refund with the department of finance. Those units being serviced with water by the sewerage and water board and those receiving free water from the

laws.title: Operation of landfills and dumps
laws.content:
(a) All dumps and landfills within the city shall be operated as sanitary landfills in accordance with the comprehensive zoning ordinance.

(b) All sanitary landfill operators shall post a performance bond in the amount of $5,000.00 or other approved security in an amount consistent with the scope of the operation with the department of safety and permits.

(c) All plans and applications for a permit to construct and operate a sanitary landfill shall be signed by a professional engineer registered in the state.

(d) The department of safety and permits, following a review of the facility plans, shall impose such revisions as necessary, including provisos, in connection with the issuance of a permit for construction and/or operation to ensure compliance with the provisions of this article.

(Code 1956, § 28-44)

laws.title: Site requirements for sanitary landfills
laws.content:
The sanitary landfill site location shall:

(1) Be easily accessible by collection vehicles, automobiles, and, where applicable, transfer vehicles.

(2) Safeguard against water pollution originating from the disposal of solid waste.

(3) Have an adequate quantity of acceptable cover material available. The cover material shall not contain organic matter conducive to the harborage and/or breeding of vectors.

(4) Conform with the provisions of the comprehensive zoning ordinance.

(Code 1956, § 28-45)

laws.title: Engineering plans for landfills
laws.content:
Engineering plans for landfill facilities shall include the following information:

(1) Topographic maps. The designs of the sanitary landfill shall include one or
§ 138-99

NEW ORLEANS CODE

more topographic maps at a scale of not over 200 feet to the inch with one-foot contour intervals. These maps shall indicate features such as: Fill area; any borrow area; access roads; grades for proper drainage of each lift required and a typical cross-section of a lift; special drainage devices if necessary; fencing; equipment shelter; existing and proposed utilities; employee facilities; and all other pertinent information to clearly indicate the orderly development, operations and completion of the sanitary landfill.

(2) *Hydrological survey.* A hydrological survey of the proposed site shall be provided if required by the department of safety and permits. Where feasible, the department may accept available information from government sources.

(3) *Other maps and photographs.* A map or aerial photograph of the area showing land use and zoning within one-quarter mile of the solid waste disposal site shall be provided. The photographs or maps shall be of sufficient scale to show all homes, industrial buildings, wells, watercourses, dry runs, roads, and other significant details.

(4) *Reports.* A report shall accompany the plans indicating but not limited to the following:

a. The area to be served by the proposed site.

b. Anticipated type, annual quantity and source of solid waste, expressed in tons.

c. Anticipated life of site.

d. Geological formations and groundwater elevations to a depth of at least ten feet below proposed excavations and lowest elevation of the site. Such data shall be obtained by soil borings or other appropriate means.

e. Soil maps, interpretive guide sheets, and a report supporting the suitability of the site for such an operation.

f. Source and characteristics of cover material.

g. Type and amount of equipment to be provided at the site for excavating, earth moving, spreading, compaction, and other needs.

h. The names and addresses of persons responsible for actual operation and maintenance of the site and intended operating procedures.

(Code 1956, § 28-46)

laws.title: Operational features for sanitary landfill sites; minimum standards
laws.content:
The disposal site shall be provided with operation features and appurtenances necessary to maintain a clean and orderly operation. The following minimum features shall be required:

(1) Operational plans to direct and control the site shall be provided.

(2) An all-weather access road to the site shall be provided. A special area with a stabilized roadway shall be provided within the site for wet weather operations.

(3) The site shall be equipped with signs indicating the name of the operating authority, traffic flow, hours of operation, and charges for disposal.

(4) Records of the amount of solid waste received measured in cubic yards shall be maintained. Quantitative records shall be forwarded to the department of safety and permits upon request.

(5) Suitable dust control methods such as approved chemicals, oils, or water sprays shall be available on the site.

(6) Blowing paper and other light materials shall be controlled by providing a portable fence near completed cells.

(7) Fire protection and firefighting facilities adequate to ensure the safety of employees and provisions to deal with accidental burning of solid waste within the site shall be available on the site.

(8) Emergency first aid equipment to provide adequate treatment of accidents, especially those associated with hazardous wastes shall be provided.

(9) Telephone or radio communications shall be provided at the waste disposal site.

(10) A trained equipment operator shall be present during operating hours.

(Code 1956, § 28-47)

laws.title: Equipment requirements for sanitary landfills
laws.content:
(a) Adequate numbers, types and sizes of equipment sufficient for spreading, covering and compacting operations shall be provided on the sanitary landfill site.

(b) Sufficient reserve equipment, or arrangements to provide alternate equipment within 24 hours following equipment breakdown, shall be provided by the operators of the sanitary landfill.

(c) Suitable shelter and sanitary facilities shall be provided for personnel. Provisions for permanent or temporary shelter of adequate size, safe drinking water, sanitary handwashing and toilet facilities, electricity, heating facilities, and proper screens, shall constitute compliance with this section.

(d) The working area of the site shall be equipped with a water line of no less than six inches diameter to provide an adequate supply of water under pressure to control fires. A stockpile of cover material shall be maintained on the site to control fires. Fire extinguishers in working order shall be kept on equipment and in all buildings.

(e) This section shall not be construed to repeal, restrict or limit any requirements of the city’s building code or fire prevention code.

(Code 1956, § 28-48)

laws.title: Landfill operations
laws.content:
(a) At the time of design approval or at any time groundwater contamination is suspected, the department of safety and permits shall have the option to require the installation of monitoring wells and may specify the number, location and depth of monitoring wells in addition to the frequency of samples to be taken, and the analyses to be run.

(b) Sanitary landfills shall provide for the management of surface runoff from the site to meet established water quality standards of the receiving waters.

(c) Any leachate emanating from a landfill shall be collected and treated if it is a potential source of water pollution.

(d) The grade of the completed refuse cells and lifts in addition to the final cover shall drain the surface runoff water to prevent uncontrolled ponding.

(e) All completed portions of sanitary landfills which have received final cover shall be planted with grass or acceptable cover vegetation to minimize infiltration, erosion and dust.

(f) All sanitary landfills where gas generated by decomposition of wastes cannot readily be dispersed into the atmosphere shall be provided with a gas control system.

(g) All solid waste, except materials such as abandoned vehicles, white goods and certain hazardous wastes, as specified by the department of safety and permits shall be compacted to form cells.

(h) Pesticides used to control rodents, flies and other insects shall be approved by the department of safety and permits.

(Code 1956, § 28-49)

laws.title: Special waste handling
laws.content:
(a) Disposal of waste sludges and liquids shall be with special consideration of air and water pollution and health and safety of landfill employees. Appropriate provisions shall be made for handling these waste materials in a landfill, only where alternate disposal methods are not

Supp. No. 86

CD138:19
§ 138-103

NEW ORLEANS CODE

available and when such disposal does not violate laws and regulations. The approval of the safety and permits department shall be required.

(b) If abandoned vehicles are brought to the site, they may be stored temporarily in a separate area, provided arrangements have been made for biweekly removal to an automobile shredding, or compacting plant. If such arrangement has not been made all abandoned automobiles, white goods and similar materials shall be compacted before being placed in the fill area to minimize voids.

(c) Upon the occurrence of natural disasters, in which large accumulations of debris are created, such as trees and buildings that have been destroyed, the debris may be transported to an area remote from habitation, and burned, in accordance with the regulations of the fire prevention division of the fire department and the state air control commission.

(Code 1956, § 28-50)

laws.title: Milled solid waste
laws.content:
The department of safety and permits may waive daily soil cover requirements for sanitary landfill operations utilizing a milling facility. The department of safety and permits may grant operating permits for such facilities contingent upon the following conditions:

(1) Seventy percent of all milled refuse, dry weight, shall be capable of passing through a four-inch screen.

(2) Waste shall be spread to a smooth contour and compacted promptly after placement and left undisturbed to prevent odors. Wind blowing of milled refuse and paper shall be controlled.

(3) All solid waste storage areas in the milling facility shall be maintained and cleaned at the end of each day’s operations, or during continuous operation, each 24 hours, to prevent fly, rodent or other vector problems. All milling equipment shall be maintained to control spillage and to achieve the required milled product quality.

(4) An operational plan shall include provision for removal and proper disposal of wastes within 24 hours should the mill facility break down or operational quality be diminished. The operational plan shall include provision for a stock pile of emergency soil cover material and a plan to convert the operation to a sanitary landfill.

(5) Upon completion of the site, it shall be closed, covered with a final 18-inch thick soil cover, and shall be seeded or planted with grass or suitable cover vegetation to minimize erosion.

(6) The department of safety and permits may require daily cover of milled solid waste if health and environmental considerations so warrant.

(Code 1956, § 28-51)

laws.title: Spillage of dirt, garbage, or trash from transport or collection vehicle
laws.content:
(a) It shall be unlawful for any person to operate any vehicle or other mobile equipment being used for the hauling of earth, waste materials, garbage, trash, or other loose materials, in such manner as to cause or permit the spillages, dropping or casting of any portion thereof upon the streets, sidewalks, or public ways, or in any other manner which would create a nuisance.

(b) It shall be unlawful for any person to operate or cause to be operated any vehicle or other mobile equipment being used for the hauling of garbage, or trash, unless such garbage or trash is completely covered by a securely fastened tarpaulin, or other similar covering, and unless the tailgate of such vehicle is secured in such manner as to prevent spillage of any portion of the garbage or trash being transported upon the streets, sidewalks, or other public ways.

(c) Any person convicted of violating any of the provisions of this section shall be subject to a fine of $100.00 or in lieu thereof, shall be subject to community service work at the discretion of the courts.

laws.title: Permits required for road races
laws.content:
(a) A road race shall be defined as a contest or event involving joggers, runners, walkers or other participants to determine the relative speed or comparative mileage of the contestants or participants.

(b) No road race shall occupy, march or proceed along any public street except in accordance with a permit received from the superintendent of police.

(c) The following regulations shall apply:

(1) The organization on whose behalf a road race is being conducted must receive a permit from the superintendent of police to use the streets of the city.

(2) Such permit shall be issued only after the superintendent of police has notified the traffic engineer, to verify that issuance of such permit will not unreasonably disrupt traffic or present a safety hazard, and has notified the director of the department of health (or his designee) to verify that emergency medical service coverage, as specified in this section, has been obtained. The superintendent of police shall also notify the clerk of council upon receipt of all requests for such permits.

(3) A completed permit application form for road races five kilometers or less in length shall be submitted no later than 45 days before the scheduled race date. For road races over five kilometers, a completed permit application form shall be submitted no later than 90 days before the scheduled race date, and any supplemental documentation required by the city shall be submitted no later than 30 days before the scheduled race date.

(4) Each application for such permit shall include:

a. The name, address, and telephone number of the organization on whose behalf the event is being conducted;

b. The name of the organization’s contact person for information;

c. The name of the event;

d. The scheduled date;

e. The distance;

f. The number of projected participants;

g. The number of participants in each of the previous three years or, unless event is being conducted for the first time;

h. The starting time;

i. The estimated ending time;

j. The times of use of the public streets or other public property to be used as a staging or finishing area; and

k. A sketch of the exact route of the event.

Each request shall also include letters of approval and/or rental agreements, as may be required, for any public or private

Supp. No. 99

CD146:9
§ 146-3

NEW ORLEANS CODE

property that will be used as a part of the road race route, as well as adequate proof of insurance and proof that emergency medical service coverage shall be provided.

(5) The emergency medical services provided shall be comparable to those provided by the city. Documentation shall be provided to the director of the department of health or his designee to verify coverage, qualifications and current status of services provided. On the day of the race, the coverage documented must be in place one hour prior to the event and continue for at least one hour after the race concludes. A minimum of one staffed ambulance vehicle for every two miles of designated race course will be required. Qualifications required shall meet the requirements of certification, licensure and permits as delineated in chapter 62, article II pertaining to emergency medical service providers and technicians.

(6) Police approval or denial shall be given at least 21 days prior to the scheduled date of the road race.

(7) An applicant shall provide reasonable notice of a road race no later than 14 days before any race. The form, manner, and timing of the required notice shall be at the discretion of the city, but must be reasonably gauged to advise residents in affected neighborhoods of race-related road closures.

(d) The superintendent of police is authorized to collect a road race permit fee from all persons having met the criteria and having received approval for such permit, as set forth in this section, according to the following schedule. These fees shall be nonrefundable and shall not be waived. For purposes of this section, the term "nonprofit" shall mean an organization that is exempt from federal income tax under Section 501(c) of the Internal Revenue Code, is a Louisiana nonprofit corporation in good standing with an Employer Identification Number issued by the Internal Revenue Service, or is a school operated by the Orleans Parish School Board or Recovery School District.

(1) For road races that are sponsored by a nonprofit . . . $50.25

(2) For all other road races . . . $100.25

All road race permit fees shall be transmitted to the chief of treasury of the department of finance. The chief of treasury shall remit $0.25 of all such sums collected for account of the police pension fund to the board of trustees, police pension fund of the city.

(e) No such permit shall be issued for any road race on a primary, special, or general election day. This section shall not apply to the time period allotted for early voting as designated by the Louisiana Secretary of State, effective April 1, 2019.

(Code 1956, § 38-124; M.C.S., Ord. No. 27266, § 1, 1-26-17; M.C.S., Ord. No. 27945, § 1, 12-20-18; M.C.S., Ord. No. 28127, § 1, 6-6-19)

laws.title: Permits required for distribution of advertising brochures, leaflets, etc
laws.content:
Any person, corporation or partnership desiring to use the city streets, sidewalks or public rights-of-way to distribute product samples, advertising brochures, leaflets, pamphlets, or commercial literature of any type whatsoever shall first apply to and receive a permit from the department of finance pursuant to section 110-222.

(Code 1956, § 46-6(a))

laws.title: Enforcement of sections 146-314, 146-453, 146-584, 146-585
laws.content:
(a) It shall be illegal for any person to violate any provisions of sections 146-314, 146-453, 146-584, or 146-585.

(b) In accordance with the provisions of this section, the department of public works and the department of safety and permits shall have the

CD146:10

§ 146-8

authority to enforce the provisions of the sections referred to within this section in accordance with the following procedure:

(1) Notification shall be provided to the person found to be in violation of these sections in the form of a formal notice of violation posted on the object or structure which violates this Code.

(2) Such notice shall provide 24-hours to the responsible party to remove, correct, or mitigate the violation to the satisfaction of the department of public works and the department of safety and permits.

(3) If the violation is not removed, corrected, or mitigated within 24-hours, the city may remove or cause to be removed any materials, structures, objects, or other articles that it deems necessary to correct the violations as noticed.

i. The city may assess any reasonable costs associated with the removal of such materials, structures, objects, or other articles against the responsible party.

ii. Any materials, structures, objects, or other articles of value so removed shall be stored in a secure location by the city for a period of not less than 30-days, after which time the items shall become property of the City of New Orleans and shall be disposed of in accordance with city policy. Storage fees shall be assessed at a rate of $100.00 per day.

iii. Any materials, structures, objects, or other articles of no value, or debris which may be created by demolition or destruction of such items shall be disposed of as required by law.

(c) Any such materials, structures, objects, or other matter that has been removed in accordance with the provisions of this section may be immediately deposited into any public garbage, trash, or other disposal area. Following such action, the city may also impose a lien on the property holdings of the person having received notice of such violation, and who has failed to correct the violation named therein within the time specified therein, or may attach a fee to the property tax assessment due by such person. Any such lien or attachment shall be equal in value to the city’s cost of enforcement in accordance with the provisions of this section.

(Code 1956, § 61-115; M.C.S., Ord. No. 26036, § 1, 9-4-14; M.C.S., Ord. No. 27426, § 1, 6-15-17)

laws.title: Enforcement of sections 146-491 through 146-575
laws.content:
In accordance with the provisions of this section, the department of public works and the department of safety and permits shall have authority to prescribe penalties as provided herein for violations of these sections in accordance with the procedures outlined in chapter 6, article II of this Code.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 27625, § 2, 12-14-17; eff. 10-1-17)

laws.title: Neighborhood street closure notice required
laws.content:
No person shall obstruct or cause to be obstructed any public right-of-way for any purpose whatsoever unless authorized pursuant to this code and permitted to do so by the department of public works, as prescribed in section 146-583. If such obstruction is the closure of a public right-of-way that prohibits the passage of vehicular traffic, the permit applicant shall provide notice to the neighborhood in accordance with this section.

(a) Once permitted, but prior to closing the public right-of-way, the applicant shall distribute a neighborhood street closure notice approved by the department. Failure to distribute this notice may result in suspension or revocation of the permit, fines or fees, and any other enforcement action permissible by law.

(b) The neighborhood street closure notice must include the applicant’s contact information, including first and last name, email address and telephone number; the dates and times during which the public right-of-way will be closed; the municipal addresses on the right-of-way closed to vehicular traffic; and a brief description of the project or reason for closure.

(c) The applicant shall ensure that the neighborhood street closure notice is provided by hand delivery, or secured to a door, mailbox, fence, or front porch of each business, residence, or institution immediately adjacent to and within one

additional block in each direction of the right-of-way to be closed, at least 72 hours in advance of the commencement of the closure. The notice shall not be placed in mailboxes.

(d) Nothing herein shall be construed to exempt municipal or other governmental or quasi-governmental agencies from the neighborhood street closure notice requirements herein, even if no city permit is required for the right-of-way closure. In the event of an emergency requiring the closure of a public right-of-way by a municipal or other governmental or quasi-governmental agency, for example, to repair a break in a water main or sinkhole, such agency shall provide the notice described herein as early as reasonably possible.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 30159, § 1, 11-21-24)

Secs. 146-38—146-70. Reserved.

laws.title: Permits to cover gutters
laws.content:
For the purpose of facilitating commerce, the director of the department of streets may issue permits for the covering of gutters on such streets as may be sufficiently wide to warrant it, on plans and specifications approved by the director.

(Code 1956, § 61-75)

laws.title: Permeable paving
laws.content:
The department of public works shall ensure that any public works project involving the permanent installation of paving on public property, including without limitation parking lanes, sidewalks, parking lots, and pedestrian

pathways, shall utilize porous or permeable paving materials, except on surfaces where, in the discretion of the director of public works, the installation of porous or permeable paving would contravene established safety and engineering best practices, or otherwise violate applicable law.

laws.title: City help
laws.content:
On all approved subdivision developments where streets are to be offered for dedication and original paving is to be constructed the city shall assist financially in the manner set forth in this division.

(Code 1956, § 61-8)

laws.title: Major streets
laws.content:
On all streets in a subdivision that are designated as major streets and are so designated on the adopted major street plan of the city, assistance in an amount not to exceed 50 percent of the total cost of subsurface drainage and paving exclusive of the costs of house drain connections, sidewalks and driveways, shall be provided.

(Code 1956, § 61-9)

laws.title: Streets requiring heavy duty paving
laws.content:
On all streets in subdivisions that the director of the department of streets may designate as requiring heavy duty paving necessitated by its future use as a bus route or other purposes that require heavy duty paving, an amount not to exceed 20 percent of the total cost, exclusive of the costs of subsurface drainage, house drain connections, sidewalks and driveways, shall be provided.

(Code 1956, § 61-10)

laws.title: Other streets
laws.content:
(a) On all other streets in a subdivision the city shall provide no financial assistance except as provided in subsection (b) of this section.

(Code 1956, § 61-11)

laws.title: Title to one foot strip next to street
laws.content: The city will obtain title in fee simple to a strip of ground one foot wide separating the street to be dedicated from the adjoining tract of ground not to be subdivided concurrently with the subdivision. (Code 1956, § 61-12)

laws.title: Reimbursement of city
laws.content: Final approval shall be denied any subdivision plan for the adjoining unsubdivided tract until such time as the developer of such tract reimburses the city for its 50 percent expenditure for street improvements previously installed on the contiguous street, less a depreciation factor of five percent of initial cost per year for each year that the street improvements have been installed. The time of the depreciation to the street improvements shall start on the date of their acceptance by the director of the department of streets and shall be computed on the basis of the lesser year. (Code 1956, § 61-13)

laws.title: Dedication of one foot strip
laws.content: When the provisions of section 146-102 have been satisfactorily complied with the one foot strip referred to in section 146-101 shall be automatically dedicated for street purposes. (Code 1956, § 61-14)

laws.title: Repaving dedicated streets in subdivisions
laws.content: On all streets in a subdivision that are dedicated and require repaving the city shall bear those costs that the prevailing policy requires it to pay on any street in the city that requires repaving. (Code 1956, § 61-15)

laws.title: Nondedicated streets
laws.content: On any street in a subdivision that is not dedicated or is not to be offered for dedication the city shall provide no financial assistance. (Code 1956, § 61-16)

laws.title: Source of funds
laws.content: The funds required to provide financial assistance shall be those funds provided in the city capital budget shown as "Subdivision Development Participation" and any other funds that may from time to time be appropriated in the capital budget for this purpose. (Code 1956, § 61-17)

laws.title: Charter provisions remain in effect
laws.content: All other requirements of section 7-102(1) of the city charter shall remain in full force and effect. (Code 1956, § 61-18)

laws.title: Nonrefundable permit application fees
laws.content:
For all permits issued by the department of public works for Mardi Gras, dumpsters, vendor zones, street closures, driveway and/or curb cuts, oversize vehicles, construction zones and for all other permits as designated by the director of the department, a permit application fee of $40.00 will be charged, except as provided in section 146-583. Application fees shall be nonrefundable and shall not be waived. (Ord. No. 20,002, § 1, 1-18-01; M.C.S., Ord. No. 23818, § 10, 12-1-09; M.C.S., Ord. No. 27266, § 1, 1-26-17)

laws.title: Driveways and sidewalks not to be installed without permit
laws.content:
No person or public body shall remove a curb; install a driveway or sidewalk abutting his or its property in the city, without first having obtained a permit from the director of the department of public works. Application for such permit shall be in a form and manner designated by the director of public works, and shall include the name and address of the applicant and the dimensions and location of such driveway or sidewalk being altered or installed. Such form shall include the name and address of the person or public body desiring to install a driveway and/or sidewalk and the dimensions and location. For purposes of this division, a driveway is defined as every way or place, located within the street right-of-way, which provides a means of vehicular travel between the street roadway and property abutting such street. Sidewalk means the portion of the street between the curblines, or the lateral lines of the street and the adjacent property lines, intended for the use of pedestrians. In no event shall any drainage mechanism on the public right-of-way be paved. Failure to secure a permit as provided herein is deemed a nuisance, and violations shall be subject to the procedures for administrative adjudications provided in Chapter 6, Article II of the Code.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 27415, § 1, 6-15-17; M.C.S., Ord. No. 27715, § 1, 4-5-18)

laws.title: Permit granted only to owner of property
laws.content:
The permit required by section 146-141 shall be granted only to the owner of the real property in front of which the proposed driveway or

sidewalk is to be constructed and maintained, upon the application of such owner or his authorized agent.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 27415, § 1, 6-15-17)

laws.title: Application fee
laws.content:
The director of the department of public works shall exact from the applicant, prior to issuance of a permit for the installation of a driveway or sidewalk, an application fee of $100.00.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 27415, § 1, 6-15-17)

laws.title: Improper installation
laws.content:
Any sidewalk or driveway installed in deviation of the approved permit shall be removed and restored to the approved specifications at the cost of the property owner. Any driveway installed without a permit shall be removed at the cost of the property owner unless retention is expressly authorized by the director of the department of public works. Sidewalks installed without a permit shall be removed at the cost of the property owner unless retention is expressly authorized by the director of the department of public works.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 27415, § 1, 6-15-17)

laws.title: Director to designate number, location and design
laws.content:
The director shall designate the number, location, spacing, width, length, radius and other details of all driveways in accordance with the provisions hereinafter set forth and in compliance with the regulations provided in the Comprehensive Zoning Ordinance relative to driveways and site accessibility. He shall ensure reasonable access to the property to be served by the driveway and he shall likewise ensure safety and convenience of the public in its use of sidewalks and roadways. He shall not issue a permit for a driveway unless the off-street parking area to be served by the driveway is adequate to accommodate the parked vehicle or vehicles without encroachment of the parked vehicle upon the street area including the sidewalk thereof. When the short dimension of an individual off-street parking space abuts the driveway, no permit will be issued unless the depth of such

laws.title: Number and location of driveways
laws.content:
(a) Except as provided in this division or elsewhere in this section, each use parcel of property which abuts any public street or highway, where vehicular access is not otherwise denied, shall be entitled to one driveway provided a vehicle can be accommodated legally within such use parcel. Not more than two driveways shall be permitted for each use parcel which abuts on any street for a distance of 120 feet or less. Each driveway will provide access to not more than two off-street parking spaces which abut such driveway. Access to three or more off-street parking spaces per driveway will be by means of a lane, isle or interior roadway connecting to the driveway. Driveways abutting any use parcel shall be separated by a minimum distance of four feet between curb returns to provide necessary pedestrian refuge and driveway delineation. No driveway shall encroach upon the sidewalk areas formed by the corner radius and the extension of property lines at the corner of an intersecting street.

(b) Exemptions from the strict application of the provisions of this section and any provisions contained in the Comprehensive Zoning Ordinance may be granted by the director of the department of public works when it is determined that circumstances require wider curb cuts for turning efficiency and/or safety. In considering exemptions requested under this paragraph, the director shall consider the potential traffic safety and operational problems involved, alternatives to allowing curb cuts, and the hardship which may result to applicant if the curb cut is denied.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 27415, § 1, 6-15-17; M.C.S., Ord. No. 27715, § 3, 4-5-18; M.C.S., Ord. No. 29087, § 1, 7-7-22)

laws.title: Design of driveways
laws.content:
Driveways for one-lane operation shall not exceed 12 feet in width and driveways for two-lane operation shall not exceed 24 feet in width measured at the property line. Radius of driveway curbs shall be as prescribed by the director of the department of public works. Such radius shall not be greater than 12 feet nor less than four feet. Where rollover curbs are installed there shall be a minimum flare of three feet of widening between the curb and property line on each side of the driveway. Grades of driveway and sidewalk shall be mutually compatible to provide uninterrupted sidewalk grade for safe pedestrian movement.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 27415, § 1, 6-15-17)

laws.title: Sidewalk area where lip curbs exist; installation of full width sidewalk
laws.content: Where lip curbs exist in front of property that is used or may be used for commercial or industrial purposes, that part of the sidewalk area beyond the limits of a driveway, between the street edge of a paved sidewalk and the back of the lip curb, shall be clearly delineated by being free of concrete and other surfacing materials. When the owner of such commercial or industrial property wishes to install a full width sidewalk where lip curb exists, permission to do so must first be obtained from the director of the department of public works.

laws.title: Details of construction
laws.content:
The details of driveway construction shall conform with the latest edition of the department of public works standard drawings and specifications. The director of the department of public works shall designate whether the proposed driveway is to be standard or heavy duty and also, when lip curbs exist, whether the proposed

**Sec. 146-150. Thickness and strength of cement.**

All standard driveways shall be six inches, and all heavy duty driveways shall be eight inches in thickness. Driveways shall be formed of Portland cement concrete which shall have a compressive strength of 4,000 pounds per square inch in 28 days and contain a minimum of $5\frac{1}{2}$ bags of cement to a cubic yard. Where a reinforced concrete roadway pavement is adjacent to the driveway the steel reinforcement may be omitted in the driveway.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 27415, § 1, 6-15-17)

**Sec. 146-151. Reserved.**

**Sec. 146-152. Unused permit void.**

A permit becomes invalid unless the work authorized by the permit is commenced within 180 days after its issuance, or if the work authorized on the permit is suspended or abandoned for a period of 180 days after the time the work is commenced. The director is authorized to grant, in writing, one or more extensions of time, for periods not more than 180 days each. The extension shall be requested in writing and justifiable cause demonstrated prior to the expiration of the permit.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 27415, § 1, 6-15-17; M.C.S., Ord. No. 27715, § 4, 4-5-18)

**Sec. 146-153. Restoration of sidewalk when use of driveway discontinued.**

The owner of the property abutting any driveway whose use has been abandoned or discontinued shall be obligated to restore, in accordance with city specifications, the portion of the sidewalk and curb that was altered or changed in consequence of the construction of the driveway.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 27415, § 1, 6-15-17)

**Sec. 146-154. Enforcement of sections 146-141 through 146-153.**

(a) The director of the department of public works and the director of the department of safety and permits shall have the authority to enforce permitting requirements and technical standards set forth in sections 146-141 through 146-153 and the standards of the latest edition of the department of public works standard drawings and specifications.

(b) The provisions of these sections are subject to administrative adjudication pursuant to Chapter 6 of this Code. Driveways and other improvements within the right-of-way regulated pursuant to sections 146-141 through 146-153 are considered extensions of the adjacent property served by such improvements.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 27715, § 5, 4-5-18)

**Secs. 146-155—146-185. Reserved.**
