laws.title: Streets, Sidewalks and Other Public Places
laws.content:
§ 146-186

(b) Any person desiring to obtain a permit to install or modify a sidewalk or driveway shall make application to the director of the department of public works in accordance with sections 146-141 thru 146-144.

(c) Prior to issuing a permit, the director of the department of public works shall review the application for such a permit to assure compliance with rules, regulations and policies governing construction of driveways.

(1) In order to avoid negative impact to adjacent trees and assure compliance with department of parks and parkways rules, regulations, and policies, the director of the department of parks and parkways shall also review the application and recommend approval or disapproval of the issuance of such permit.

(2) Approval of all applications shall include any stipulations the director of the department of public works or the director of the department of parks and parkways determine must be met, by the property owner, prior to or during the course of, installation or modification of a sidewalk or driveway.

(d) An application for such a permit shall include, but not be limited to, a plan diagram, including existing trees within 50 feet of the proposed work site, and construction details, including materials to be used.

(e) If a sidewalk or driveway is installed or modified for property fronting on Canal Street in the area bounded by Claiborne Avenue and City Park Avenue without the property owner first obtaining the required permit, or complying with the application as granted by the director of the department of public works the property owner shall be responsible for any corrective action determined to be necessary.

(1) The director of the department of public works shall notify the property owner in writing by certified mail of such noncompliance or failure to obtain a permit. Upon receiving such notification, the property owner will have 15 days from the date of receipt of notification to take corrective action as set forth by the director of the department of public works in the written notification.

(2) The property owner shall incur all expenses for such corrective action including, but not limited to, removal of such sidewalk or driveway.

(3) If the property owner does not comply with the written notification from the director of the department of public works for corrective action, such corrective action shall be taken by the department of public works or its agent with the property owner incurring the cost for such corrective action.

(f) Additionally, the property owner shall be responsible for any damage or destruction caused to any public trees in accordance with the department of parks and parkways rules and regulations. The property owner shall be notified by the director of the department of parks and parkways, in writing by certified mail, of any corrective action the property owner is required to take relative to damage or destruction to any public trees as a result of sidewalk or driveway modifications or installations. Upon receiving such notification, the property owner shall have 15 days from the date of receipt of notification to take corrective action, as set forth by the director of the department of parks and parkways in the written notification. The property owner shall incur all expenses for such corrective action. If the property owner does not comply with the written notification from the director of the department of parks and parkways for corrective action, the director of the department of parks and parkways shall notify the director of the department of public works requesting that such corrective action be taken by the department of public works or its agents. The property owner shall incur the cost for such corrective action.

(g) If the property owner does not successfully complete the corrective action as required by the director of the department of public works or the director of the department of parks and parkways, requiring the department of public works or its agent to complete such corrective action, the city attorney shall be authorized to

When part of a block is without curbing, guttering or counter curbing or where they require removal in the judgment of the director of the department of public works, the required new curbing, guttering and counter curbing shall be constructed of such material as is generally used in such block.  
(M.C.S., Ord. No. 27414, § 1, 6-15-17)

**Sec. 146-189. Materials used in wings in intersections.**

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 27414, § 1, 6-15-17)

**Sec. 146-190. Property owners responsible for certain sidewalk defects.**

In the case of existing facilities, when the installation of a sidewalk/banquette is in the interest of public safety, or when a property owner creates or causes a defect in an existing sidewalk/banquette, the director of the department of public works may pave or repave such sidewalk/banquette. Upon the determination by a hearing officer, pursuant to Chapter 6, Article II of this Code, that a property owner created or caused a sidewalk defect adjacent to their property, the director of the department of public works shall issue a statement of costs against the property owner for the cost of such work as provided in section 6-38. (M.C.S., Ord. No. 27414, § 1, 6-15-17)

**Sec. 146-191, 146-192. Reserved.**

**Sec. 146-193. Minimum sidewalk treatment within the downtown development district.**

(a) All new sidewalks or banquettes or repaved sidewalks or banquettes immediately adjacent to property located within the downtown development district which is defined as that area bounded by the uptown side of Iberville Street, the river side of South Claiborne Avenue, the downtown side of the Pontchartrain Expressway and the river, shall be paved, repaved or constructed in accordance with all specifications including permitted materials, typical plans and section details, an official sidewalks designation map, and catalogue of streets as set forth herein. The department of public works and the clerk of council shall maintain as a public record, available for public inspection, a map and detailed plans, which delineate the type of treatment for each sidewalk, located within the downtown development district and Vieux Carré. Such details, plans, and map shall be referred to as "on file" for the purposes of this section and section 146-194.

(1) Category "A" streets shall be paved, repaved or constructed with Boral Red brick pavers and Boral Savannah Brown brick pavers as borders, or approved equivalent pattern and construction as per the latest edition of the department of public works standard drawings and specifications for construction in the downtown development district.

(2) Category "B" streets shall be paved, repaved or constructed in concrete, pattern and construction as per the latest edition of the department of public works standard drawings and specifications for construction in the downtown development district.

(3) Canal Street from the Mississippi River to Claiborne Avenue shall be designated as category "C" street. All sidewalks on Canal Street shall be constructed, maintained and restored in accordance with plans and specifications as outlined in the Canal St. Improvement Project (City Project # 01-DD-26840), dated November, 2004, or any subsequent plans and specifications. The department of public works and the clerk of council shall maintain as a public record, available for public inspection, detailed plans and specifications for the type of treatment for Canal Street sidewalks.

(4) Category "D" streets shall be considered specialty thoroughfares including Poydras St. from the River to S. Claiborne Ave, and Tulane Ave. from S. Rampart to S. Claiborne Ave. The category "D" streets

Streets not identified as category A, B, C, or D are exempt from the provisions of this section. Details for the aforementioned sidewalk treatment are to be found in the latest edition of the department of public works standard drawings and specifications.

(b) Exceptions:

(1) A category "B" street may be permitted to use materials, plans, and specifications permitted under category "A" under the following conditions:

a. The project site is currently brick and replacement will be in kind.

b. The existing sidewalks are predominantly brick and the project site will increase the total area of brick sidewalk along an existing block face.

c. Sidewalks currently constructed using historic Pennsylvania blue-stone may be repaired or replaced in kind so long as the entire block consists of similar materials.

(2) In cases where a single block face is treated with at least 50 percent of a particular material, the property owner or developer must match the most prevalent material on the block. The calculation will be the percentage of the project site to total block face as measured in linear feet.

(3) The prevailing determination of permitted materials shall be the effort to establish consistency and uniformity of a single block with regards to material, color, and pattern.

(4) Changes or modifications with regards to permitted materials, plans, and specifications may be authorized by the director of the department of public works after consultation with the president of the downtown development district and the district councilmember.

(c) All roadway curbs within the downtown development district will be either stone curbs or vertical concrete curbs as per details found in the latest edition of the department of public works standard drawings and specifications. In the warehouse district where granite and slate roadway curbs exist in sections of two linear feet or more, they shall be reset in place.

(d) No person shall remove an existing sidewalk or install a new sidewalk, or make any cut for any purpose whatsoever in any sidewalk pavement, in the downtown development district without first having obtained a permit from the department of public works. Application for such a permit shall be made on a printed form, which the director of the department of public works shall furnish for this purpose. Such form shall include the name, address, phone, and email address of the person desiring to install a sidewalk, the project location, the dimensions and site plans of such sidewalk. The application form, site plan, and sample of materials must be submitted to the downtown development district prior to a permit being issued. The permit required by this section shall be granted only to the owner of the real property adjacent to which the proposed sidewalk is to be constructed and maintained upon the application of such owner or his authorized agent. The property owner shall be held liable for construction work performed in the public right-of-way without the appropriate permit from the department of public works. The director of the department of public works is authorized to issue a "stop work" order for sidewalk construction being performed in violation of this section. All existing granite and slate curbs shall be retained by the city for reuse within historic districts.

(e) Any person desiring to obtain a permit to install or modify a sidewalk shall submit an application to the director of public works for approval in accordance with sections 146-141 thru 146-144.

(f) Any property owner in the downtown development district shall contact in writing the utility companies (Sewerage and Water Board, Entergy, AT&T, and Cox) prior to the demolition of old sidewalks or installation of new sidewalks and adjustment of any manholes, catch basins, metal frames and covers, etc. The purpose is to obtain any information regarding proposed new utilities or revisions to existing utilities. Such notification must be given by the property owner at least 90 days prior to the planned activities to permit coordination of work efforts.

(g) When a city agency, utility company or property owner has to make repairs within a sidewalk or banquette paved in any material other than concrete, then the replacement must be made in kind, that is, the replaced materials shall be the same color, size, pattern, and textures as the materials removed and must match the existing pattern.

(h) When a property owner, city agency or utility company has to make repairs under an existing concrete sidewalk or banquette and 35 percent or more of that concrete area measured by total area square feet within a property owner's portion of sidewalk or banquette has to be removed to perform the utility construction or repair, the property owner, city agency or utility company performing the work is responsible for replacing the entire sidewalk or banquette within the property owner's portion according to the minimum standards set forth in this section. When repairs to an existing concrete sidewalk are less than 35 percent of a property owner's portion of a sidewalk or banquette area, then the replacement shall be made in kind to match the existing pattern. When the agency, utility company, or property owner must make repairs to a concrete sidewalk then the replacement area must extend to the nearest expansion joint on all fours sides of the location of repair.

(i) Streets with sidewalks in excess of nine feet wide may be planted with street trees, pattern and construction as per the latest edition of the department of public works standard drawings and specifications for construction in the downtown development district. No person shall remove or plant sidewalk street trees within the boundaries of the downtown development district without first obtaining a permit from the department of parks and parkways. Such form shall include the name, address, phone, and email address of the person desiring to install trees, the project location, the site plan, and proposed trees species. The application form and site plan must be submitted to the downtown development district and the department of parks and parkways, prior to a permit being issued. The permit required by this section shall be granted only to the owner of the real property adjacent to which the proposed project location or to his authorized agent.

(1) All trees shall be a minimum of two to two and one-half inch caliper in size taken six inches from the top of the root ball with a minimum tree height of 12 feet.

(2) Street trees shall be planted in a manner suitable for pedestrian traffic including a minimum clear width of four feet of sidewalk. If the walking area is next to a wall, fence or other continuous vertical barrier, there should be five feet clear width, with six feet clear width preferred. The department of public works may direct the department of parks and parkways to require a clear width of six to eight feet or more if, in the determination of department of public works, the street has or is expected to have a high volume of pedestrian traffic.

(3) The minimum tree well size is four feet by four feet. Regardless of treatment, the tree well may not be included in the required clear width of sidewalk. Ground cover and/or stationary raised planters may be permitted on sidewalks within the downtown development district in lieu of tree grates upon written approval of the department of public works in

consultation with the downtown development district. Deviations relative to the size of the minimum tree well may be granted by the director of department of public works in consultation with the downtown development district.

(4) Street trees will be located and planted as per the latest edition of the department of public works standard drawings and specifications unless the proposed trees conflict with the existing utilities under the sidewalk or banquette where the trees are being proposed. Prior approval of all tree placements must be obtained from the department of parks and parkways, in consultation with the planning advisory committee. See details on street tree planting for location and spacing between trees in the latest edition of the department of public works standard drawings and specifications for construction in the downtown development district.

(j) The removal, relocation, destruction, or abuse in any manner of a street tree is prohibited on any parcel of land unless a variance, special exception, or approval has been obtained in writing from both the department of parks and parkways and the downtown development district. For any trees affected as a result of pending development, the permit holder must make all efforts to preserve protected trees or provide an appropriate mitigation or replacement plan in advance.

(k) Property owners, or any person, firm or corporation shall have responsibility for maintaining sidewalks in clean, good and safe condition and not causing any defects or hazards within their portion of sidewalk or banquette abutting said property.

(l) The sidewalk, all tree grates, manholes, detectable warnings, and all other appurtenances must comply with ADA, AASHTO and Federal Highway Administration requirements. Specifically, a minimum four foot clear pedestrian zone must be maintained. If the walking area is next to a wall, fence or other continuous vertical barrier, there should be five feet clear pedestrian zone, with a six foot clear pedestrian zone preferred. Between the face of the curb and any signpost, utility pole, fire hydrant or other vertical obstruction, there should be an 18 inch clear zone. All other grades, cross slopes, transitions, clearances should comply with the published standards. Save ADA, AASHTO, and Federal Highway Administration requirements, deviations relative to this section may be granted by the director of department of public works in consultation with the downtown development district.

(m) The director of department of public works is authorized at his discretion, to approve the installation of sidewalks constructed with other paving materials on a case-by-case basis, after consultation with the downtown development district, the city planning commission, and the district council member of the area.

laws.title: Identification required
laws.content:
On or after January 1, 1991, no owner, lessee or operator of a newsbox or newsstand shall cause or permit his newsbox or newsstand to be placed or remain on public property for any period of time during which the newsbox or newsstand does not have permanently displayed on one of its visible surfaces the name and address of the owner, lessee or operator thereof.

(Code 1956, § 40B-2(a))

laws.title: Abandonment prohibited
laws.content:
No owner, lessee or operator shall cause or permit his abandoned, litterprone or illegally fixed newsbox or newsstand to remain on any public or private property within the city. No owner, lessee or operator shall cause or permit his newsbox or newsstand to become abandoned, litterprone or illegally fixed. Nothing in this section, however, shall prohibit the storage of any newsbox or newsstand that is not being used for the vending, distribution or circulation of printed matter in a lawful place of storage on private property with the consent of the owner of such property.

(Code 1956, § 40B-2(b))

laws.title: Issuance of notice
laws.content:
The enforcement agency, whenever it commences enforcement activity in a survey zone, shall make every reasonable effort to ensure that the notice authorized by this section is affixed to every abandoned, litterprone or illegally fixed newsbox and newsstand within the survey zone. If any newsbox or newsstand in a particular zone is impounded pursuant to this section, the enforcement agency shall make every reasonable effort within one month of the first such impoundment to impound all other newsboxes or newsstands in the same survey zone that can lawfully be impounded.

(Code 1956, § 40B-3(b))

laws.title: Contents, effect of notice
laws.content:
Upon determining an appropriate survey zone, the enforcement agency shall affix to each abandoned, litterprone and/or illegally fixed newsbox or newsstand found therein a notice declaring that the newsbox or newsstand has been found to be in violation of this article and must be removed by the owner, lessee or operator within seven calendar days of the date the notice is affixed in default of which the newsbox or newsstand will be removed and impounded by the enforcement agency and disposed of in the manner provided for the disposition of signs in section 134-122(b). The notice shall state that the owner, lessee or operator may request a hearing on whether or not the newsbox or newsstand is in violation and should be removed and impounded by filing a written request in the principal office of the enforcement

agency not later than 4:00 p.m. on the fourth day following affixment of the notice.  
(Code 1956, § 40B-3(c))

**Sec. 146-243. Removal after notice.**

No owner, lessee or operator of a newsbox or newsstand shall cause or permit his newsbox or newsstand to remain on any public or private property for any period longer than seven calendar days after the notice authorized by section 146-242 is first affixed to a visible surface of the newsbox or newsstand. However, if a written application for a hearing is properly filed pursuant to section 146-242, the running of the seven calendar days shall be interrupted and shall begin to run anew on the day the applicant for the hearing receives a copy of the written findings of the enforcement agency pursuant to section 146-246.  
(Code 1956, § 40B-2(c))

**Sec. 146-244. Removal, etc., of notice.**

No person other than an officer or agent of the city shall remove or efface or obscure any notice affixed pursuant to section 146-241.  
(Code 1956, § 40B-2(d))

**Sec. 146-245. Impoundment authorized.**

If the owner, lessee or operator fails to remove a newsbox or newsstand to which a notice has been affixed and has failed to file a written request for a hearing within the time stated in the notice, the enforcement agency may remove and impound the newsbox or newsstand and cause it thereafter to be disposed of in the manner providing for disposition of signs in section 134-122(b).  
(Code 1956, § 40B-3(d))

**Sec. 146-246. Hearing.**

If an owner, lessee or operator requests a hearing, the enforcement agency shall set the time and date thereof and notify the applicant in writing of the hearing at least one calendar week in advance of the hearing. Whenever such a hearing is timely requested, no removal or impoundment shall be done until after the hearing is concluded. Upon conclusion of the hearing, if the applicant shows that the newsbox or news-

stand was not in violation of this article or that the violation has been cured, the enforcement agency shall issue a written finding directing that the notice be removed from the newsbox or newsstand. If the applicant fails to make such a showing, the enforcement agency shall issue and serve its written finding of violation upon the applicant. If the violation is not cured within seven calendar days from the date the applicant receives a copy of the written findings, the employees or agents of the agency shall remove and impound the newsbox or newsstand.  
(Code 1956, § 40B-3(e))

**Secs. 146-247—146-274. Reserved.**

laws.title: Generally
laws.content:
**Sec. 146-275. Street use privileges, permits and franchises.**

Notwithstanding any other provision of this chapter, a special franchise ordinance of the council adopted under chapter 16 of the home rule charter, shall be required for any physical plant or installations in, over, or under the streets or other public places of the city which will be so extensive or will have so much capacity that they will be suitable for use for public utility and/or telecommunications public carrier purposes, whether by those directly serving consumers or those transmitting or relaying commodities, services, or telecommunications to or from consumers and/or third parties who serve consumers. This section shall not apply to any permittee granted a street use permit prior to the effective date of the ordinance from which this section was derived. An ordinance adopted under this section shall comply with all requirements of chapter 16 of the home rule charter and the federal and state constitutions.

laws.title: Permission of council required
laws.content:
It shall be unlawful for any person to construct or maintain or operate any structure or service on, above or beneath the public streets and other public places within the city without permission of the council in accordance with the regulations provided in this article. Providers of wireline telecommunications services, as that term is defined in section 30-45 of this Code, shall be governed by sections 30-43 through 30-57 of this Code.

(Code 1956, § 61-50.1; M.C.S., Ord. No. 17,560, § 3, 6-6-96)

laws.title: Granting of permission; rates
laws.content:
(a) The permission required by this article shall be granted only by ordinance and shall specify the purpose of the privilege, the streets and other public places affected, the duration of the privilege and the consideration therefor in accordance with the following schedule of rates:

(1) Passageways, conveyors and similar structures above public streets and alleys. For one-story passageways, conveyors and similar structures bridging an area above a public street or alley, the annual fee shall be equal to 24 percent of the average assessed value per square foot of the connected or adjoining land multiplied by the total number of square feet of horizontal public street or alley space covered by the outside dimensions of the superimposed structure. One-half of such fee shall be added for each additional floor. The minimum fee shall be $600.00 per annum for one-story structures and $300.00 per annum for each additional floor.

(2) Loading platforms and occupation of public streets and alleys. For loading platforms or occupation of public streets and alleys, the fee shall be equal to 48 percent of the average assessed value per square foot of the adjoining or connected land multiplied by the total number of square feet of public street or alley area occupied including ramps and steps. The minimum fee shall be $300.00 per annum.

(3) Underground vaults, elevators and storage tanks. For underground vaults, underground elevators and underground storage tanks, the annual fee shall be $200.00 for each structure. For storage tanks, the fee shall include accompanying service piping up to 100 feet in length. Piping in excess of 100 feet shall be charged for in accordance with the appropriate schedule below.

(4) Underground pipes and conduits. An annual charge of $50.00 for the first 100 feet or less in length and $30.00 for each additional 100 feet or fraction thereof for pipes and conduits up to six inches in diameter. For pipes and conduits over six inches in diameter, the fee shall be twice the above fee.

(5) Overhead wires. An annual charge of $50.00 for the first 100 feet or less in length and $30.00 for each additional 100 feet or fraction thereof.

(6) Underground wells. An annual charge of $600.00 for each well and accompanying service piping, up to 100 feet in length. Piping in excess of 100 feet in length shall be charged at the rate of $50.00 per 100 feet or fraction thereof.

(b) The assessed value used in this section shall mean the valuation for assessment purposes as listed in the assessment rolls in the several municipal districts in and for the parish for the current year in which the privilege is granted or renewed.

(c) No fee required by this section shall be required from any nonprofit educational or charitable institution for the privilege of constructing, maintaining or operating an overhead or underground structure across or beneath any public street or alley where such structure is used primarily for the safe passage of pedestrians in connection with the operation of such institutions. A surety bond shall be provided by such an institution to guarantee the removal of the structure upon expiration of the privilege.

(Code 1956, § 61-50.2)

laws.title: Payments for privilege; default
laws.content:
All payments required by this article shall be made annually in advance. If any payment is not made on or before the dates fixed by the privilege ordinance, then all subsequent payments accruing under the terms thereof shall immediately, without demand or putting in default, become payable, or, such ordinance may be terminated or cancelled by the council, which cancellation shall not release any indebtedness accruing prior to the date thereof or as long as such grantee remains and makes use of such privilege.

(Code 1956, § 61-50.3)

laws.title: Rights of grantee
laws.content:
The grantee of a privilege under this article shall not exercise such privilege except in connection with his own business nor shall he lease or grant the right to use the same to any person for rent or hire. Privileges shall be inalienable and not transferable; provided, that the grantee may subrogate to another all his rights and liabilities with respect to the privilege granted to him, upon specific written notice to the director of the department of public works, giving the name and address of the person to whom the subrogation is made and upon securing the consent of the council by ordinance.

laws.title: Construction of service, etc., liability for costs; manner of making and restoring cuts in sidewalks, etc
laws.content:
The structure or service to be built under the privilege granted under this article shall be constructed in accordance with all applicable regulations and laws in effect. The cost of rearrangement of existing utilities or structures made necessary by the construction, operation or removal of the structure or service under the privilege granted shall be borne by the grantee. Likewise, any damages to existing utilities or structures occasioned by the construction, maintenance or operation of the structure or service under the privilege granted shall be borne by the grantee. All sidewalks, pavements and other properties torn up or disturbed in constructing, operating, maintaining or removing the structure or service under the privilege granted shall be restored to their original good condition, including removal of any markings, satisfactory to the director of the department of public works. The grantee shall likewise conform in all respects to the provisions of all ordinances and regulations relative to the manner of making and restoring cuts in sidewalks and roadway pavements, especially the provisions of sections 146-436 et seq.

(Code 1956, § 61-50.6; Ord. No. 21,148, § 2, 6-19-03)

laws.title: Removal or relocation of structure or service
laws.content:
Permission shall be granted under this article under the express condition that such structure or service shall be subject to prompt removal or relocation within 60 days at the pleasure of the city after notice thereon from the city and at the expense of the grantee whenever the city shall request such removal or relocation for the purpose of the execution of public works or other franchises or permits of whatever nature, or for any public purpose on the site so occupied. Should a change of location or renewal within a period of time shorter than 60 days be so deemed necessary by reason of public danger or peril, then such structure or service or any part thereof shall be removed or shifted at the grantee’s expense in the earliest time possible, or in default thereof such

Should the grantee abandon the structure or service under the privilege granted, or should the same be partially destroyed so as not to be of any further use, the grantee shall remove the structure or service from public property and restore any existing utilities or structures to their original good condition. **Sec. 146-283. Surety bond.**

The grantee of any privilege shall furnish a good and solvent surety bond, in solido, in favor of the city, satisfactory to the director of the department of public works, in a sum equal to the aggregate of the annual payment during the term of the privilege but in no event to be less than $500.00 or more than $ 3,000.00 to guarantee the faithful performance of all the obligations of the grantee of such privilege set forth in the ordinance granting the privilege and this article. (Code 1956, § 61-50.8; M.C.S., Ord. No. 21480, § 3, 4-1-04)

**Sec. 146-284. Scope of division.**

This article shall not be applicable to marquees and similar structures, except when the floor area of any such marquee or similar structure has the same general use or occupancy as the building to which it is attached, or to hoods, sunshades, vertical fins, ornaments, cornices, vents and exterior doors, all if not in violation of any law or ordinance; nor shall it be applicable to those utilities, public or private, which enjoy rights under existing franchises or legislation, especially the rights conferred upon the sewerage and water board by Legislative Act 6 of 1899, as amended; nor shall it be applicable to the granting of switch track privileges which are provided by section 122-131 et seq.; nor shall it be applicable to the granting of temporary revocable permits for the use of public streets, which permits are regulated under the provisions of sections 146-311—146-313 and 146-315—146-319.

(Code 1956, § 61-50.9)

**Sec. 146-285. Penalty.**

Any person violating any of the provisions of this article shall be subject to a fine of not more than $25.00 or imprisonment for not more than 30 days, or both, for each violation at the discretion of the court having jurisdiction. Each day’s violation or failure to comply with the provisions of this article shall constitute a separate offense thereunder.

(Code 1956, § 61-50.10)

**Secs. 146-286—146-310. Reserved.**

**Sec. 146-312. Reserved.**

**Sec. 146-313. Permits for temporary bus service.**

Permits for the operation of temporary bus service on certain streets where such service is not already provided and is not in conflict with existing permits or franchises shall be issued in accordance with the regulations of this division.

(Code 1956, § 61-50.17)

laws.title: Application; approval and issuance of permit
laws.content:
All applications for the installation of facilities for temporary services shall be submitted by letter to the director of the department of public works, describing the service and facilities to be installed and enclosing four copies of a sketch showing the location of the facilities with respect to property lines and street and sidewalk lines. Prior to the issuance of such temporary permits, the director of the department of public works
§ 146-316

shall obtain the approval of interested city agencies. After such approval has been obtained, the director shall, at his discretion, issue a permit authorizing the use of the public streets and other public places for the installation of the necessary facilities.

(Code 1956, § 61-50.12; M.C.S., Ord. No. 21480, § 3, 4-1-04)

**Sec. 146-317. Construction of service, etc.; liability for costs; manner of making and restoring cuts in sidewalks, etc.**

The structures to be built or the service to be furnished under the privilege granted under this division shall be constructed in accordance with all applicable laws and regulations. The cost of rearrangement of existing utilities or structures made necessary by the construction operation or removal of the structure or service under the privilege so granted shall be borne by the grantee. Any damages to existing utilities or structures occasioned by the construction, maintenance or operation of the structure or service under the privilege granted shall be born by the grantee. All sidewalks, pavements and other properties torn up or disturbed in constructing, operating, maintaining or removing the structure or service under the privilege granted shall be restored to their original good condition satisfactory to the director of the department of streets. The grantee shall likewise conform in all respects to all ordinances and regulations relative to the manner of making and restoring cuts in sidewalk and roadway pavements, especially the provisions of sections 146-436—146-443 and 146-445—146-455.

(Code 1956, § 61-50.13)

**Sec. 146-318. Removal or relocation of structures, etc.**

Permits required by this division shall be granted under the express condition that such structure or service shall be subject to prompt removal or relocation within 90 days at the pleasure of the city, after notice thereon from the city and at the expense of the grantee whenever the city shall request such removal or relocation for the purpose of the execution of public works or other franchises or permits of whatever nature, or for any public purpose on the site so occupied. Should a change of location or removal within a period of time shorter than 90 days be necessary by reason of public danger or peril, then such structure or service or any part thereof shall be removed or shifted by the grantee at his or its expense without delay, or in default thereof, the city may undertake such removal of shifting at the grantee’s expense. Should the grantee abandon the structure or service under the privilege granted, or should the same be partially destroyed so as not to be of any further use, the grantee shall remove the structure or service from public property and restore any existing utilities or structures to their original good condition, or in default thereof, the city may undertake such removal at grantee’s expense.

(Code 1956, § 61-50.14)

**Sec. 146-319. Grantee to save city harmless.**

The grantee of any temporary revocable permit under this division shall agree to save the city harmless from any damages to property or injuries to persons resulting from the installation, operation, maintenance, removal or shifting of the service or structure.

(Code 1956, § 61-50.15)

**Secs. 146-320—146-350. Reserved.**

**Sec. 146-351. Constructing conduit, etc., without permit a misdemeanor.**

Any person constructing any conduit, duct, manhole or other appurtenance or operating any electrical wire or other electrical conductor in any conduit, duct, manhole or other appurtenance without a permit from the council shall be guilty of a misdemeanor. Each conduit, duct, manhole or other appurtenance constructed on each street and each wire or other electrical conductor, used or operated in each conduit on each street shall constitute a separate offense. No punishment for one violation of this section shall bar or prevent prosecution for another violation.

(Code 1956, § 61-72)

The application for a permit required by section 146-363 shall be accompanied by full, general and detailed plans, showing the route, capacity and dimensions, alterations and changes of such conduits, ducts, manholes and other appurtenances, the size of the conduits proposed to be used and the depth of them as proposed to be

(Code 1956, § 61-56)

**Sec. 146-353. Approval of council.**

The council shall, after at least five days’ notice to the applicant, consider all applications, statements, plans and details presented for the construction of underground conduits, ducts, manholes and other appurtenances for the use and operation of electrical wires and other electrical conductors and examine into the space available for such conduits, ducts, manholes and other appurtenances under or in the streets, alleys or other public places of the city and shall decide upon, amend and approve or prepare such plans, details and constructions, conduits, ducts, manholes, materials and conditions as in its opinion the public interest seems to demand. The city shall pass upon the application, statements, plans and details presented to it in accordance with this section within 30 days from the filing thereof with the clerk of the council.

(Code 1956, § 61-57)

**Sec. 146-354. Joint construction; apportionment of cost.**

When more than one application statement or plan is presented coincidentally to the council for conduits, ducts or manholes under or in any street, alley or public place, the council may compel such applicants to build and maintain joint conduits in which all the electrical wires or other electrical conductors of like tension owned or operated by such applicants shall be placed and, in case the construction thereof involves a joint outlay and there is a disagreement among the interested parties, the council shall apportion the expense of the construction and maintenance of such conduits, ducts, manholes and appurtenances as may be jointly constructed by two or more applicants. Any applicant who fails to accept such apportionment, in writing, within five days after the apportionment of cost shall be made by

the council or by the arbitrators as hereinafter set forth, shall be excluded from all right or privilege to obtain under this article conduit, duct or manhole facilities in the streets, alleys or public places of the city and no conduit, duct or manhole permit shall be issued to applicants directed to use joint conduits, ducts and manholes until all applicants directed to use such joint conduits, ducts and manholes shall have filed with the clerk of the council a written acceptance of the apportionment of cost made by the council or by the arbitrators under this division. But if such applicant should be dissatisfied with the apportionment made by the council, the matter shall be submitted to arbitration, the applicant to appoint one arbitrator, the mayor another arbitrator and these two arbitrators to select a third.

(Code 1956, § 61-58)

**Sec. 146-355. Bond required of applicants.**

No permit for construction, use or operation of any conduits, ducts, manholes and other appurtenances for the use and operation of electrical wires and other electrical conductors shall be issued by the council except upon the party or parties applying for the same filing with the mayor a penal bond in the sum of $10,000.00, with two or more good and sufficient securities, or with one bond and trust company engaged in the business of furnishing bonds, approved by the mayor, conditioned that the conduits, ducts, manholes and other appurtenances shall be constructed in strict accordance with the plans approved by the council, that the city shall be held harmless from all suits for damages that may arise from the construction of such conduits, ducts, manholes and other appurtenances and that such person shall maintain such conduits, ducts, manholes and other appurtenances at all times in good order and condition, shall make all changes and alterations therein as the council may from time to time direct to the satisfaction of the director of the departments of public works and under the supervision of the director and shall comply with all ordinances and laws concerning conduits, ducts, manholes and other appurtenances or concerning the disturbance and repair of the streets, alleys and other public places of the city. Such bond shall be renewed

(Code 1956, $\S$ 61-59; M.C.S., Ord. No. 21480, $\S$ 3, 4-1-04)

**Sec. 146-356. Construction work to follow plans; required maintenance.**

All conduits, ducts, manholes and other appurtenances for the use or operation of electrical wires and other electrical conductors shall be constructed and maintained in strict accordance with such plans and specifications as shall be approved by the council and all construction work shall be done under the supervision of the director of the department of public works and to the satisfaction of the director. Any failure on the part of any person using or operating any conduit, duct, manhole or other appurtenance within ten days from the date of the written notice from the director to do such work as deemed necessary for proper maintenance shall constitute a breach of the bond provided for under section 146-355 and shall operate a forfeiture of all rights and privileges under this section.

(Code 1956, $\S$ 61-60; M.C.S., Ord. No. 21480, $\S$ 3, 4-1-04)

**Sec. 146-357. Work subject to supervision.**

The work of removal and replacement of the pavements in any street, avenue, highway or public place in and through which the wires of any company shall be laid shall be subject to the control and supervision of the director of the department of streets. Excavations in any and all of the unpaved streets, avenues, highways or public places shall also be subject to like control and supervision.

(Code 1956, $\S$ 61-61)

**Sec. 146-358. Construction not to impede traffic materially.**

The method employed in laying conductors shall be such that it will at no time be necessary to remove so much of the pavement or to make such excavations as to materially impede traffic

or passage upon sidewalks or streets during the operation of laying or repairing such conductors, except when in crossing streets transversely, where it shall be permitted to remove the pavement in the nearest straight line from corner to corner.

(Code 1956, $\S$ 61-62)

**Sec. 146-359. Where overhead wires prohibited.**

No person owning or using electric wires, tubes, cables or other electrical conductors strung on poles or fixtures or attached to buildings or other structures in the city shall permit them to remain above the surface of any street, alley or public place of the city in the section of the city herein-after described, with the exception of trolley wires used by street railway companies, wires or conductors placed inside of posts or brackets used in connecting lamps or signal boxes on streets with underground conductors and such poles as may be necessary to support trolley wires, such section of the city being defined as follows:

Beginning at the intersection of the northern property line of Howard Avenue and the western property line of South Front Street; thence in a westerly direction along the northern property line of Howard Avenue to the northern property line of Lee Circle; thence in a counterclockwise direction along the northern property line of Lee Circle to the northern property line of Howard Avenue; thence in a westerly direction along the northern property line of Howard Avenue to the western property line of Loyola Avenue; thence in a northerly direction along the western property line of Loyola Avenue to the southern property line of Poydras Street; thence continuing in a northerly direction along the same line across Loyola Avenue to the intersection of the eastern property line of Loyola Avenue and the northern property line of Perdido Street; thence in a northerly direction along the eastern property line of Loyola Avenue to the southern property line of Tulane Avenue; thence continuing in a northerly direction across Tulane Avenue to the intersection of the eastern property line of Elk Place and the northern property line of Tulane Avenue; thence in a northerly direction along the eastern property line of Elk Place to the

laws.title: Placing of wires throughout city in underground conduits authorized
laws.content:
Any person owning, using or operating electrical wires or other electrical conductors under proper authority along or across any street, alley or public place in the city strung on poles or attached to buildings or other structures in the city may construct, alter and repair underground conduits and place his electrical wires and other electrical conductors therein and may construct, alter and repair such ducts, manholes and other appurtenances as may be required for placing such electrical wires and other electrical conductors underground and to operate and use them. laws.content:
The city, through the director of the department of public works, may at any time inspect, superintend and control the construction, use and operation of conduits, ducts and manholes for the use and operation of electrical wires and other electrical conductors and the city reserves the right from time to time to order any alterations or changes to be made in the construction, material or manner of maintaining the same or in the location in the streets and all such changes and alterations shall be made by the person owning the conduit without expense to the city. laws.title: Costs entailed by future construction of sewer system
laws.content: If the city or any company should construct a system of sewerage, it shall pay all the costs occasioned by the displacement or alteration of any portion of the conduits laid by any person to make room for any sewer pipe. (Code 1956, § 61-67)

Each pole and other fixture on each street, alley or public place of the city for each day it is permitted to remain shall constitute a separate offense. No punishment for one violation of this section shall bar or prevent another prosecution. (Code 1956, § 61-70)

laws.title: Permitting overhead wires to remain in underground sections a misdemeanor

Each wire or other electrical conductor on each street, alley or public place shall constitute a separate offense for each day that such wires, tubes and cables are permitted to remain. No punishment for one violation of this section shall bar or prevent prosecution for another violation. (Code 1956, § 61-71)

laws.title: Blanket permit
laws.content:
Where cuts are made by a public utility company operating under a franchise or indeterminate permit issued by the city or where the utility is operated by a governmental agency, the director of the department of public works may issue a blanket permit to any such utility. Such blanket permit shall be issued for a period of no more than one year and may be renewed on an annual basis. Such utility shall provide a one-time, nonrefundable blanket permit application fee of $10,000.00. Such utility shall also be required to provide an annual deposit of $50,000.00; but any remaining deposit balance shall offset the following year’s required deposit. The recipient of a blanket permit shall be liable for the cost of any work required to restore the cut area to the same or better condition. Failure of the utility to pay the bill within 30 days of presentation or failure to otherwise conform to the requirements of this division shall constitute cause for forfeiture of their deposit or revocation of privileges extended under blanket permit. laws.title: Emergency cuts
laws.content:
Nothing in this division shall be construed to prevent the making of such cuts as may be necessary for the preservation of life or property or for the location of emergency trouble in a conduit, cable, pipe or appurtenances for making emergency repairs, provided that the person making such cut or repair shall otherwise comply with the provisions of this division.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 26646, § 1, 11-5-15)

laws.title: Permit to be carried on job; if not, police to stop work
laws.content:
Workmen engaged in making a cut in a street shall have in their possession the permit issued by the director of the department of public works and shall show said permit upon request by NOPD or DPW, or their authorized designee. Violators of this section shall immediately stop further work, safely secure the work site according to section 146-453 and be subject to a fine not to exceed $300.00 per day in accordance with section 1-13 until a permit is obtained. The foregoing shall not apply to blanket permittees, or contractors for blanket permittees engaged on an annual basis.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 26646, § 1, 11-5-15)

laws.title: Pavement cuts
laws.content:
Existing pavement shall be cut and removed in a manner that does not damage the base of the roadway that is to remain in place, for a distance of at least 12 inches beyond the width of the trench on each side of the trench and at each end thereof, unless otherwise approved by the director of the department of public works or his designee.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 26646, § 1, 11-5-15)

laws.title: Limitation of damage
laws.content:
The director of the department of public works may prohibit the use of heavy pavement breakers when their use endangers existing structures or other property. The permit holder accepts full responsibility for any such damage that may be caused by his operations. Tunneling will not be permitted except as stated in section 146-437(a), however, the director of the department of public works may require boring or other methods to prevent cutting of the pavement.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 26646, § 1, 11-5-15)

laws.title: Filling of cut on paved and asphalt surfaced streets
laws.content:
As soon as practical following the installation of the subsurface structure or structures, all trenches and pits on all paved and asphalt surfaced streets shall be carefully refilled in accordance with the standards and specifications established by the director of the department of

Supp. No. 74

CD146:34
STREETS, SIDEWALKS AND OTHER PUBLIC PLACES

§ 146-450

public works. The backfill may be inspected by the director of the department of public works prior to repaving and, if the director determines that the refill is not satisfactory, he shall have the right to order the permittee to remove all of the filled material from the excavation and to have same refilled at the expense of the permittee. If such person fails to remove the unsatisfactory fill, the entire deposit shall be forfeited. Whenever caving occurs in the sidewall of any excavation, the pavement above such caving shall be removed and in no case shall any void or cavity be restored by side or lateral filling or tamping.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 26646, § 1, 11-5-15)

laws.title: Restoration of pavements
laws.content:
(1) In the restoration of pavements, all work and materials used must meet the standards and specifications of the department of public works.

(2) Age of roadway shall be determined in accordance with official records of department of public works and the city.

(3) Pavement edges shall have vertical faces and be neatly aligned with the center and ends of the trench.

(4) Sections of sidewalks scored into stones shall be removed to the nearest score line or joint. Unscored sidewalks and driveways shall be repaved with straight edges parallel to the trench.

(5) Unstable pavement shall be removed over cave-ins, areas of contiguous subsidence, overbreaks and small floating sections and is to be treated in the same manner as the main trench.

(6) Cutouts outside of the trench lines must be normal or parallel to the trench line.

(7) Permit holder shall be required to repair existing pavement damage caused by the failing of his underground structure or structures.

(8) The director of the department of public works or his designee shall have the authority to consider debilitating conditions such as cracking, differential settlement, especially in the vicinity of trees not related to underground utilities and other conditions that might contribute to aging a street before a usual life has been achieved in determining the requirements and dimensions for

restoration and may increase the size of the replacement section required in order to safely and adequately restore the roadway.

(9) If corner sidewalk cuts or restoration work extends into an area where curb ramps that are compliant with the requirements of the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) are required, then ADA-compliant curb ramps shall be installed on that corner, except as directed by the director of the department of public works or his designee.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 26646, § 1, 11-5-15)

laws.title: Restoration of temporary surfaced streets
laws.content:
In the case of streets with gravel, shell or other temporary surfacing, all trenches shall be backfilled as required by section 146-447. Upon the subgrade shall be placed at least eight inches of compacted material of the same type as previously existed.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 26646, § 1, 11-5-15)

laws.title: Restoration of concrete streets
laws.content:
In the case of concrete pavement roadway, the following shall be required when restoring all cuts regardless of size:

(1) The concrete on a finished concrete roadway or pavement foundation shall have a compressive strength of at least 4,500 pounds per square inch at 72 hours. Concrete sidewalks shall have a compressive strength of at least 3,000 pounds per square inch at 28 days.

(2) On streets with a concrete base or full-depth concrete paving, dowelling in the existing concrete pavement shall be employed.

(3) The pavement must be restored by replacement of the full concrete panel(s) in which the cut or part of the cut is made, unless otherwise directed or approved by the director of the department of public works or his designee. A panel is defined as a homogenous section bound by full original construction joints on each side.

Supp. No. 74

CD146:35
§ 146-450

NEW ORLEANS CODE

(4) If the extent of the cut(s) and subsequent pavement restoration is 75 percent or more of the pavement surface area of the street block in which the cut was made, the entire street block from intersection to intersection shall be repaved, unless otherwise directed by the director of the department of public works. For purposes of this determination, the restoration of one or more separate cuts made within a 12-month period shall be considered as one combined restoration effort.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 26646, § 1, 11-5-15)

laws.title: Same materials required for pavement restoration
laws.content:
All roadway construction shall be restored with the same materials unless approved by the director of department of public works.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 26646, § 1, 11-5-15)

laws.title: Identification tag required for restoration
laws.content:
All permanent asphalt, concrete and brick street repairs shall be identified with a tag placed a minimum of one per 50 feet of trench resurfacing. In the case of small cuts, one tag in the center shall be required. The permit holder shall obtain said tag from the department of public works. The tag shall be color coded, in accordance with department of public works specifications and include year of the repair. Each tag shall be embedded at zero grade tolerance or slightly below in the new surface. Failure to permit holder to mark pavement cuts may result in forfeiture of guarantee compliance deposit, and the permit holder shall be subject to a fine not exceeding $300.00 per day in accordance with section 1-13. The director of the department of public works may direct that an alternative system be used in lieu of the identification tag for the tracking of restoration work.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 26646, § 1, 11-5-15)

laws.title: Provisions for public safety and traffic movement
laws.content:
(a) Safety provisions required. It shall be the duty and responsibility of each person to whom a permit is issued pursuant to this division to provide all measures necessary to ensure safety of the public. Types and placement of barriers, warning signs, lights, etc., shall meet with the approval of the director of the department of public works. Warning lights shall be flares, electrical markers, or flashers used to indicate a hazard to traffic from sunset of each day to sunrise of the next day. Electrical markers or flashers shall emit light at sufficient intensity and frequency to be visible at a reasonable distance of safety. Reflectors or reflecting material may be used to supplement, but not replace light sources.

(b) Traffic provisions required. In the exercise of the privileges granted by such permit, the permit holders shall take appropriate measures to assure that traffic conditions as near normal as possible shall be maintained at all times so as to minimize inconvenience to the occupants of the adjoining property and to the general public. When traffic conditions permit, the director of the department of public works may permit the closing of streets and alleys to all traffic for a period of time prescribed by him, if in his opinion it is necessary. Warning signs shall be placed far enough in advance of the construction operations to alert traffic within a public street, and cones or other approved devices shall be placed to channel traffic in accordance with instructions of the director of the department of public works. Fire hydrants, fire stations, fire escapes, driveways and any other vital equipment as designated by the director shall not be blocked or interfered with in connection with the work required for the approved cut. The permit holder shall maintain safe crossings for vehicular traffic at all street intersections unless exception is made by the director of the department of public works and the permit holder shall maintain safe crossings for pedestrians at intervals of not more than 300 feet. Subject to the foregoing exception, the work shall be so arranged that at least one-half of the street shall be open for traffic at all times.

(c) Notification required. The approval of the director of the department of public works shall require that the holder give notification of work and street impairment to the police, fire and other city departments, as specified by the director, and to the general public if the director deems it necessary.

(d) Violations. Any person found violating the provisions of this section shall be subject to any and all of the provisions of section 146-5. (M.C.S., Ord. No. 26646, § 1, 11-5-15)

laws.title: Marking of utility pavement cuts
laws.content:
(a) When cuts in the public rights-of-way are made by or for a public utility company operating under a franchise or a utility operated by government agency, such utility shall be required to tag all repairs in accordance with the standards and specifications established by the department of public works. All permanent asphalt, concrete and brick street repairs shall be identified with a tag placed a minimum of one per 50 feet of trench resurfacing. In the case of small cuts, one tag in the center of the repair shall be required. The tag shall be a one-piece constructed item and color coded in accordance with department of public works specifications. Each tag shall include the name, initial or logo of the utility that owns or operates the line, conduit or utility and the year of the repair. Each tag shall be imbedded at zero grade tolerance or slightly below in the new surface. The department of public works shall annually provide each utility with standards and specifications for the tags. These standards will include, but not be limited to, color codes, initial codes and tag design specifications.

(b) Failure of the utility to mark pavement cuts shall constitute cause for revocation of privileges extended under section 146-439, blanket permit. Such utility shall be subject to a fine not exceeding $300.00 per day in accordance with section 1-13.

(c) The director of the department of public works may direct that an alternative system be used in lieu of the identification tag for the marking of utility pavement cuts. (M.C.S., Ord. No. 26646, § 1, 11-5-15)

laws.title: Restoration of asphalt roadways
laws.content:
In addition to the full-depth restoration of any cut, the street’s wearing surface to a depth of at least 2½ inches shall be removed and replaced on the entire street block, as measured from beginning of intersection to the beginning of intersection, as part of the required pavement restoration, unless otherwise approved by director of the department of public works, if:

(a) The roadway is under five years old and the cut and subsequent pavement restoration runs for more than 100 linear feet along the length of the block or covers 25 percent or more of the total pavement surface area of the block; or

(b) The cut and subsequent pavement restoration runs for more than 150 linear feet along the length of the block or covers 50 percent or more of the total pavement surface area of the block, regardless of the age of the pavement.

For purposes of this determination, the restoration of one or more separate cuts made within a 12-month period shall be considered as one combined restoration effort. (M.C.S., Ord. No. 26646, § 1, 11-5-15)

laws.title: Notice to director when restoration completed
laws.content: Every person to whom a permit has been granted to make a cut in a pavement or earth roadway shall, upon completion of the backfilling and the planking or temporary restoration of the pavement or earth roadway as prescribed in this article, notify the director of the department of public works to that effect so that the work may be inspected to determine whether or not it has been satisfactorily executed. (M.C.S., Ord. No. 26646, § 1, 11-5-15)

laws.title: Failure to restore cut in pavements
laws.content: All cuts in pavements as well as pavements to be relaid and earth roadways shall be permanently restored within the time fixed in the permit or the entire deposit shall be forfeited. (M.C.S., Ord. No. 26646, § 1, 11-5-15)

laws.title: Return of deposit
laws.content:
The permittee shall be responsible for the maintenance of concrete or other hard surface

Supp. No. 83

CD146:37

NEW ORLEANS CODE

replaced if the cause of the defect is due to the work performed by the permittee or his representative; such responsibility shall extend for a period of five years on a concrete base street and for a period of one year on asphalt or other hard surfaced street without a concrete base. No deposit shall be refunded on any above designed street until the expiration of the prescribed maintenance period in each instance. Subject to the foregoing and when all cuts have been permanently restored to the satisfaction of the director of the department of public works, he shall return 90 percent of the deposit prescribed in section 146-438 and the remaining ten percent shall be retained by the city to defray the expense of necessary inspection. In the case of a blanket permit and subject to the foregoing and when all cuts have been permanently restored to the satisfaction of the director of the department of public works, he shall return the deposit prescribed in section 146-439.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 26646, § 1, 11-5-15)

laws.title: Forfeiture of deposit
laws.content:
In the case of failure to comply with any of the provisions of this division the entire deposit required by this division shall be forfeited to the city to be employed by the director of the department of public works in carrying out the intent and purpose of this division.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 26646, § 1, 11-5-15)

laws.title: Enforcement
laws.content:
Any designated employee of the departments of health, police, public works and safety and permits shall enforce the provisions of this division.

(Ord. No. 21,148, § 3, 6-19-03)

laws.title: Bond required
laws.content:
In addition to any other bonds or fees required in this chapter, any person conducting work, such as excavation or demolition, that would require the marking of utility systems on any roadway, pavement, sidewalk, banquette or any public right-of-way located within the city shall furnish a good and solvent surety bond, in solido, in favor of the department of public works, satisfactory to the director of the department of public works at $500.00 for each block face or each 300 feet, up to a maximum of $5,000.00 to guarantee the faithful performance of all obligations of that person, set forth in this division or promulgated by the department of public works. The bond requirements set forth herein shall not apply to any governmental agencies.

(Ord. No. 21,148, § 3, 6-19-03)

laws.title: Removal of markings
laws.content:
Any person making any marking for any purpose whatsoever on any roadway, pavement, sidewalk, banquette or any public right-of-way located within the city shall make only such a mark using only temporary paints allowed by the department of public works. The removal of such markings shall be the responsibility of any entity, whether public or private, conducting work, such as excavation or demolition, that would require permission from the director of public works; and such entity shall be responsible for removal of any markings on any roadway, pavement, sidewalk, banquette or any public right-of-way within five working days of the completion of the project for which the marks were made. Upon the expiration of the five working days from the time of completion for which street markings were made, if the person who requested the markings to be made has not removed the same as required herein, the department of public works, and the downtown develop-

ment district within its geographical area, are hereby authorized to remove the markings without further notice.

(Ord. No. 21,148, § 3, 6-19-03)

**Sec. 146-464. Penalties.**

(a) Whoever fails to adhere to the standards promulgated by the department of public works regarding the painting of street markings, who does anything otherwise prohibited, or fails to do anything required by this chapter, shall be fined up to $500.00 per violation. The markings on each block face or each 300 feet shall be considered one violation.

(b) In addition to any other fines or penalties provided herein, and regardless of any hearing thereon, after notice to the person having made the marking and after removal of the marking by the department of public works or the downtown development district, the bond required in section 146-462 is to be forfeited.

(Ord. No. 21,148, § 3, 6-19-03)

**Sec. 146-465. Administrative hearing.**

Violations of this chapter may be adjudicated by the administrative adjudication bureau of public housing and environmental violations. Said hearing shall be conducted by a hearing officer of the administrative adjudication bureau of public housing and environmental violations, and shall be subject to the provisions of chapter 6 of this Code.

(Ord. No. 21,148, § 3, 6-19-03)

**Sec. 146-492. Same—Exceptions.**

The provisions of section 146-491 shall not apply to existing balconies of dwelling houses nor to marquees or awnings to protect show windows if no sign or advertisement appears thereon.

(Code 1956, § 61-112)

**Sec. 146-493. Obstruction of public rights-of-way, public places prohibited.**

(a) It is the intent of this section to maintain public streets, sidewalks, and other areas in the city in a clean, accessible and safe condition.

(b) It shall be unlawful for any person, natural or juridical, to deposit, encumber, obstruct, or cause to be obstructed any street, gutter, sidewalk, public space parallel to any sidewalk, entrance or window of any building, or any other public place or right-of-way (hereafter rights-of-way), by depositing, storing or placing any article whatsoever that prevents or impedes the free and proper use of the rights-of-way. This includes but is not limited to:

(1) The erection or placement of any tent, item of household furniture not intended for outdoor use, or other semi-permanent structure unless otherwise properly permitted. Removal of the aforementioned items shall be enforced by the director of the department of health or his/her designee and shall be subject to procedures specified in the New Orleans Health Department Regulations Governing Public Place/Right-of Way Obstructions, approved by the council on Thursday, June 17, 2015.

(2) Unsecured bicycles, electric-assisted bicycles, motorized bicycles, motor-driven cycles, mobility aids, electric scooters, and other similar devices whose placement prevents the free and proper use as stated herein, may be immediately removed from the rights-of-way and stored accordingly. This subsection shall be
§ 146-493

NEW ORLEANS CODE

enforced by the director of the department of public works or his/her authorized designee.

i. For the purposes of this section, the definitions of bicycles, electric-assisted bicycles, motorized bicycles, motor-driven cycles, mobility aids, and electric scooters shall be as provided in section 154-2 of this Code.

(3) Permanent obstructions of any nature unless lawfully authorized by the City of New Orleans shall be prohibited.

(c) This section shall not be construed to prohibit or prevent the use of small-scale, portable outdoor equipment at a permitted event.

(Code 1956, § 61-114; M.C.S., Ord. No. 26011, § 1, 9-4-14; M.C.S., Ord. No. 27849, § 1, 9-6-18; M.C.S., Ord. No. 29169, § 1, 10-6-22)

Cross reference—Parking of bicycles and similar devices, § 154-1421.

laws.title: Obstruction of sidewalks
laws.content:
(a) It shall be unlawful for any person to obstruct or cause to be obstructed any public space parallel to any sidewalk including linear streets, public rights-of-way, public alleys or any entrance or window of any building so as to prevent the free and proper use thereof.

(b) If any person by performance of any outdoor act or activities causes a crowd to gather, and if the crowd makes passage by pedestrians inordinately difficult or conducts activities which impede access to the public rights-of-way the department of police shall have the authority to order such person(s) to cease performance of their act or activities. The person(s) to whom such an order is given must obey the order immediately or be subject to arrest for violation of this section and shall be prohibited from the following:

(1) Unauthorized installation or placement of sports athletic equipment or apparatus designed for temporary mobile or fixed stationary use including:

a. Basketball goal equipment;

b. Sports athletic training equipment.

(2) Unauthorized construction or assembly of sports special event or athletic event apparatus or other equipment which impedes or obstructs the public rights-of-way including amateur or homemade devices created for athletic purposes.

(c) The provisions of this section shall not apply to a person or persons engaged in watching a parade.

(d) The provisions of this section shall not apply to permitted, legal, sidewalk uses authorized pursuant to division 4 of this chapter.

(e) Jackson Square clear lanes.

(1) All artists, street entertainers, street vendors and other persons utilizing the Chartres Street, St. Ann Street and St. Peter Street malls surrounding Jackson Square under a permit from the city, hereinafter all referred to as "performers or vendors" shall endeavor to maintain "clear lanes" to facilitate pedestrian access to and around Jackson Square, as set forth below.

(2) No performer or vendor shall conduct his performing or vending activity in the clear lanes around Jackson Square.

(3) Performers and vendors shall encourage pedestrians who stop to view their performing and vending activities not to block the clear lanes established herein, and they shall cooperate with the effort of the department of police to maintain such clear lanes for pedestrian access in and around Jackson Square.

(4) The clear lanes areas shall be the following:

a. Chartres Street Mall. The clear lanes shall be from the facades of the Cabildo, St. Louis Cathedral and Presbytere to a line 20 feet out from those facades.

b. St. Ann Street Mall. The clear lanes shall be from the facades of the Pontalba building to a line 12 feet out from the downtown curb of the street.
