c. St. Peter Street Mall. The clear lanes shall be from the facade of the Pontalba Building to a line 12 feet out from the uptown curb of the street.

(f) A commercial use with street frontage located within the Central Business District, as defined by the Comprehensive Zoning Ordinance, may display and/or place one detachable, freestanding, portable accessory sign, per business location, subject to compliance with division 4 of this article.

(Code 1956, § 61-114.1; M.C.S., Ord. No. 20850, § 1, 8-22-02; M.C.S., Ord. No. 21867, § 1, 3-3-05; M.C.S., Ord. No. 23508, § 1, 5-7-09; M.C.S., Ord. No. 27625, § 3, 12-14-17; eff. 10-1-17)

laws.title: Persons using sidewalks, etc., in business to display sign
laws.content:
All persons doing business in the city on the public streets, sidewalks or other public property or on private property in the prosecution of work by which the public streets or sidewalks might be disturbed or a part of the street, sidewalks or public place encumbered with material shall exhibit a substantial sign painted black with their name and address in white letters not less than nine inches high and sufficiently wide to be conspicuous and discernible by the general public.

(Code 1956, § 61-117)

Supp. No. 102

CD146:40.1

laws.title: Building materials—Removal by contractor, builder, owner required
laws.content:
No contractor, builder or owner who may, in the raising or repairing of any building, deposit stone, brick, mortar, debris or similar material upon the street or sidewalk, shall fail to remove it after having been notified so to do by the director of the department of streets.

(Code 1956, § 61-118)

laws.title: Same—Removal and disposal of obstructions by city employees
laws.content:
The obstructions referred to in section 146-496, when the owner is in default, and any such obstructions for which no owner or claimant can be found, shall be removed by employees of the department of streets to any street requiring repairs where such material can be used for filling purposes, otherwise the same shall be deposited in any public garbage, trash or other disposal area.

(Code 1956, § 61-119)

laws.title: Uncovered manholes to have iron railings around them
laws.content:
All persons owning or operating manholes in the streets or public places of the city shall surround such manholes, whenever and for the length of time that they may be uncovered, with iron railings at least three feet high.

(Code 1956, § 61-120)

laws.title: Removal of debris from manholes
laws.content:
Every person causing manholes to be cleaned shall be obligated to have carts at the manholes to receive at once all excavations taken from them and no refuse taken from them shall be allowed to remain upon the public streets. The surroundings of the openings of such manholes shall be thoroughly cleaned after they shall have been closed.

(Code 1956, § 61-121)

laws.title: Unloading goods on streets, etc
laws.content:
It shall be unlawful for any person to encumber or obstruct any of the streets, gutters, public roads, public grounds, public squares, public places or promenades, banquets or sidewalks of the city by depositing in or on them any box, bale, hogshead, barrel or other goods, wares or merchandise or article whatsoever, except for the necessary time of loading or unloading such articles. No merchandise shall be packed or unpacked on any sidewalk.

(Code 1956, § 61-122)

laws.title: Gutters not to be obstructed
laws.content:
No person shall impede or obstruct the flow of water in any gutter, canal, pipe or other conduit used for draining within the limits of the city. Utility companies and private contractors or developers must remove in a timely manner any debris, concrete, roofing material, etc., related to any project they may be working on, from any storm drains and lateral lines throughout the city.

Anyone who violates this provision shall be subject to a $500.00 fine and/or up to six months in jail.

(Code 1956, § 61-123; Ord. No. 20,853, § 1, 8-22-02)

laws.title: Obstruction of street maintenance
laws.content:
It shall be unlawful for any person to interfere with or obstruct the maintenance and repair of any portion of any street in the city. It shall likewise be unlawful for the owner or his agent to obstruct any street where notice of street work is posted within the block and also unlawful to refuse to move from the repair area any object of personal property, such as motor vehicle or other item, when requested to do so by employees of the department of streets for the purpose of facilitating repair or maintenance of any portion of the street. Any object and/or vehicle impeding street repair or maintenance may be moved from such areas by employees of the department of streets to nearby areas or as otherwise provided by law. When any vehicle bearing a current state

license plate is moved, it shall be relocated in a legal parking space and, if relocated in other than the same block, notice of such relocation shall be filed with the department of police and shall include the license number, make, color and body type of the vehicle, and the address from which the vehicle was relocated. laws.title: Permit required
laws.content:
Use of any sidewalk or other public space for the extension of a licensed business shall be unlawful without a sidewalk use permit issued pursuant to this division. (M.C.S., Ord. No. 27625, § 4, 12-14-17; eff. 10-1-17)

laws.title: Permit requirements
laws.content:
(a) No person or business shall establish, operate, or continue to operate a sidewalk café on any public street or sidewalk unless such person or business obtains a valid sidewalk use permit pursuant to this division.

(b) No person or business shall place a display or A-frame sign on any public street or sidewalk unless such person or business obtains a valid sidewalk use permit pursuant to this division.

(c) Sidewalk use permits shall be issued only to validly licensed businesses that wish to provide sidewalk cafés on the sidewalk adjacent to their businesses for use by the general public, or that wish to place A-frame signage or limited displays of merchandise on the sidewalk in conjunction with the licensed business establishment.

(d) The eligibility for such permits shall be determined by the temporary use standards of the Comprehensive Zoning Ordinance and/or the applicable standards of the zoning district in which the subject property is situated.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 27625, § 4, 12-14-17; eff. 10-1-17)

laws.title: Authority to issue permit
laws.content:
The director of the department of safety and permits shall authorize sidewalk use permits only for validly licensed businesses that fully comply with the requirements of this division and the Comprehensive Zoning Ordinance. Such permits shall be issued only after consultation with and the positive recommendation of the director of the department of public works. A sidewalk use permit is a privilege, not a right, and may be revoked, suspended, or not renewed based on non-compliance with the requirements of the Comprehensive Zoning Ordinance or the requirements of this division.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 27625, § 4, 12-14-17; eff. 10-1-17)

laws.title: Standards and criteria for application review
laws.content:
(a) The following standards and criteria shall be used in reviewing the application and design drawings to determine if the proposed location is suitable and will not obstruct free and proper use of the public right-of-way.

(1) The sidewalk shall be of sufficient width to accommodate the proposed sidewalk use while maintaining a clear path of travel that is:

a. At least four feet in width on sidewalks of eight to ten feet in width.

b. At least six feet in width on sidewalks greater than ten feet in width.

c. In areas of congested pedestrian activity, the reviewing agencies are authorized to require a wider pedestrian path to ensure the free and proper use of the right-of-way by pedestrians.

(2) A clearance of ten feet shall be maintained between any element of a sidewalk use and a fire hydrant, or fire department sprinkler/standpipe connection.

(3) A clearance of ten feet shall be maintained between any element of a sidewalk use and a public transit pole or CPNC stand.

(4) Sidewalk uses are restricted to the area immediately adjacent to the business being served and may not project in front of neighboring businesses or vacant lots.

(5) Sidewalk uses shall not be located within the corner area of a public right-of-way, which is that area between the curb and the lines created by extending the property lines of the adjacent property being served and the curb.

(6) Tables, chairs, umbrellas and any other objects provided with the sidewalk café shall be of sufficient quality, design, materials, and workmanship to ensure the safety and convenience of users, and to enhance the visual and aesthetic quality of the urban environment.

a. Umbrellas, and other decorative elements shall be fire retardant, pressure-treated, or manufactured of fire resistant material and not interfere with the free and proper use of the sidewalk.

b. Within local control historic districts, the jurisdictional agency may provide standards or guidelines that shall be applied to determine the visual and aesthetic the suitability of proposed elements of the sidewalk café.

(7) Commercial uses seeking approval of an A-frame sign or display devices shall be limited as follows:

a. Commercial uses shall be permitted no more than one A-frame sign per street frontage occupied by the commercial use.

b. Commercial uses shall be permitted no more than two display devices per street frontage occupied by the commercial use.

c. A-frame signs and display devices shall be prohibited in the area bounded by the Mississippi River, the uptown side of Esplanade Avenue, the riverside of N. Rampart Street, and the downtown side of Iberville Street, except that these items may be authorized on N. Rampart Street subject to approval of the Vieux Carré Commission.

(8) The sidewalk use shall be permitted no closer than 18 inches from the edge of the roadway, unless otherwise approved by the director of the department of public works.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 27625, § 4, 12-14-17; eff. 10-1-17)

CD146:44

laws.title: Permit issuance
Permit renewal
laws.content:
The sidewalk use permit shall be valid one year from the date of issuance. Renewal permits shall be issued in the same manner as initial permits, and requires:

(a) Providing the department an updated copy of any of the documents required by section 146-535;

(b) Providing a revised or updated site plan, if changes to an approved plan are requested; and

(c) Proof of payment of all applicable taxes and fees as required by law.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 27625, § 4, 12-14-17; eff. 10-1-17)

laws.title: Permit display required
laws.content:
(a) The sidewalk use permit shall be conspicuously displayed on the exterior wall or window of the main entrance of the licensed establishment of which the approved use is accessory.

(b) The approved sidewalk use plan shall be posted in the same location and manner as a city issued occupational license and/or alcoholic beverage license.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 27625, § 4, 12-14-17; eff. 10-1-17)

laws.title: Operational limitations, generally
laws.content:
(a) The arrangement and number of tables or other approved items authorized by the sidewalk use permit shall not be modified or altered without the approval of the director of the department of safety and permits.

(b) All furniture and fixtures shall reflect the approved site plan and may not be substantially changed, altered, added to or reduced without the approval of the director of the department of safety and permits.

(c) No portion or element of an approved site plan may be secured through bolting or otherwise fastening any table, chair, bench, fixture, or other device to a public sidewalk, post, sign, tree, or similar feature.

(d) The permittee shall keep the portion of the sidewalk not approved for commercial use pursuant to a sidewalk use permit free of obstruction(s) at all times.

(e) The sidewalk area adjacent to a commercial establishment that is issued a sidewalk use permit shall be maintained in a neat and orderly appearance at all times and the area

shall be cleared of debris or litter on a periodic basis during the day and again at the close of business each day.

(f) A-frame signs and displays are only permitted to occupy the right-of-way while the validly licensed business is open to the public. All components shall be removed from the right-of-way at the close of each business day.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 27625, § 4, 12-14-17; eff. 10-1-17)

laws.title: Operational limitations, sidewalk cafés specifically
laws.content:
(a) The capacity of an approved sidewalk café shall not exceed the approved seating capacity indicated on the approved site plan and as stated on the permit placard.

(b) Tables and chairs associated with an approved sidewalk café shall be structurally sound and maintained in a manner ready for access and use by patrons.

(c) Sidewalk café permittees shall wash the sidewalk daily and at the close of business or, if open 24-hours, at the close of the sidewalk café element of the business.

(d) No live entertainment, speakers, or other sources of amplified sound shall be permissible on or adjacent to the approved sidewalk café.

(e) Carts, receptacles for waste or dirty dishes, and cooking appliances shall not be placed or stored on any portion of the sidewalk.

(f) Tables, chairs, and any other components of the approved sidewalk use shall be neatly stacked and organized at the end of each business day, at the hour indicated by this division, in a manner which will result in minimal intrusion into the public right-of-way.

(g) All property/building ingress and egress where a sidewalk café exists must remain unobstructed (including queuing lines) for clear, barrier-free pedestrian passage, consistent with the fire department regulations and ANSI standards for barrier-free access.

(h) Hours of operation:

(1) Seating within the sidewalk café shall not begin before 8:00 a.m.

(2) Unless otherwise provided in this section, seating within the sidewalk café shall end no later than 10:00 p.m.

(3) In the area bounded by the Mississippi River, the Pontchartrain Expressway, South Claiborne Avenue, and Canal Street (inclusive of uses which front on both sides of Canal Street), seating within the sidewalk café shall end no later than 12:00 a.m.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 27625, § 4, 12-14-17; eff. 10-1-17)

laws.title: Conditions and restrictions
laws.content:
(a) Sidewalk use permits are subject to modification, suspension or revocation by the City of New Orleans at any time during the period of validity if the city requires the subject sidewalk area cleared for street, sidewalk, or utility repair or other public purposes.

(b) Sidewalk use permits are non-transferable and may not be assigned or granted to any other person or business which may occupy the location to which a permit has been issued.

(c) The permittee accepts the prevailing site conditions with regard to ambiance, including, but not limited to, loading and passenger zones, loading zones, automobile traffic, exhaust fumes, noise, and pedestrian traffic.

(d) Sidewalk use permits shall be automatically suspended for periods 2-hours before, during, and 2-hours after a carnival parade for business locations on parade routes.

(e) The director of safety and permits may suspend sidewalk use permits without prior notice in the event of permitted special events where crowd control is likely to be necessary.

(f) The departments of police and fire and any other emergency response agency may require immediate removal or relocation of all or part of the sidewalk use in emergency situations.

(g) The City of New Orleans, its officers, agents, or any private utility company operating pursuant to a franchise granted by the city council, their officers, agents, or employees shall not be responsible for sidewalk use components relocated during emergencies.

(h) Issuance of a sidewalk use permit does not grant, convey, or infer any vested right to the use of the sidewalk area by the permittee nor does it constitute a deed, grant of easement, or servitude by the city. The city retains the right to revoke or deny the issuance or renewal of a sidewalk use permit for noncompliance with the provisions of this division, the City Code, or the comprehensive zoning ordinance.

(i) Sidewalks shall not be painted, modified, or altered in any way without prior written approval of the director of the department of public works.

(j) The city and/or its agents may schedule general cleaning and maintenance operations. If such work is scheduled, the city and/or it agents shall give notification of its scheduled cleaning times in advance of such operations to all sidewalk use permittees. Each permittee in the affected area shall remove all portions of the sidewalk café operations so that they do not inhibit the scheduled sidewalk cleaning, repair, and/or maintenance operations.

(k) Permittee is wholly responsible for the proper maintenance and use of any permitted sidewalk use, and shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless the city from all actions, claims, costs, damages and expense to which the city may be subject by reason of any injury or alleged injury to any person or property resulting or alleged to result from such sidewalk use. The owner shall pay all sums so recovered against the city in any suit on account of such alleged injuries to which the city may be made a party, together with all such costs, damages and expenses as may be suffered by the city, all in a manner as to hold the city harmless from all such actions or claims.

laws.title: Fees
laws.content:
(a) Upon initial submission of an application for a sidewalk use permit, a non-refundable application fee of $50.00 shall be remitted to the department of safety and permits.

(b) Fees for new issuance or renewal of sidewalk use permits shall be assessed in accordance with the following schedule, which shall be sufficient to administer and enforce the regulations of this program and to compensate the city for use of public property:

(2) Display devices: $200.00 per approved device.

Claiborne Avenue, Pontchartrain Expressway, St. Charles Avenue, Broadway Street, Maple Street, S. Carrollton Avenue, Oak Street, to the Mississippi River, inclusive of both sides of bounding streets: $350.00 per table (up to four seats), $100.00 per seat for tables seating more than four persons.

b. In all other areas: $200.00 per table (up to four seats), $75.00 per seat for tables seating more than four persons.

(c) Sidewalk use permit fees shall be payable at the time of permit issuance or renewal and are non-refundable in the event of suspension, revocation, or surrender of the sidewalk use permit during the term of validity.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 27625, § 4, 12-14-17; eff. 10-1-17)

laws.title: Penalties

Any violation of this division and/or the correlating provisions in the comprehensive zoning ordinance may subject a violator to any remedy,

**Sec. 146-545. Denial, revocation, or suspension of permits.**

(a) The director of the department of safety and permits may deny an application for a sidewalk use permit if, in the investigation of the application it is determined:

(1) That the proposed sidewalk use does not or cannot meet the standards of this division; or,

(2) That the proposed sidewalk use does not or cannot meet the standards of the comprehensive zoning ordinance; or,

(3) Upon recommendation of denial from the director of the department of public works that the location is unsuitable for commercial use on the public right-of-way due to pedestrian congestion, traffic, existing obstructions on the sidewalk, or any other reason that would result in an unsafe or substandard condition.

(b) The director of the department of safety and permits may administratively suspend a sidewalk use permit for a period not to exceed 30-days, for failure to abide by and maintain compliance with the standards of this division, the comprehensive zoning ordinance relative to operation of the licensed use, or revocation of any license or permit required by any other agency or entity for the legal operation of the licensed use.

(1) Operation of a sidewalk use during the period of such administrative suspension shall constitute a separate offence of this division and shall be grounds for revocation.

(c) Penalties for non-compliance with the provisions of this division may result in fines, suspension of the sidewalk use permit for a period not to exceed 180-days, or revocation of the sidewalk use permit.

(1) Hearings shall be conducted in accordance with the provisions of chapter 6, article II of this Code.

(2) In the case of revocation, a business entity shall be ineligible to receive another sidewalk use permit for a period of two years from the date of such revocation.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 27625, § 4, 12-14-17; eff. 10-1-17)

[Subdivision II. Public Transit Shelters]*

**Sec. 146-546. Regulations applicable to public transit shelters.**

Sidewalk use permit requirements and standards provided in sections 146-531 through 146-545 of this division shall apply to the installation and maintenance of public transit shelters placed on public rights of way for the general use and welfare of the public. Public transit shelters shall be temporary structures that are typically located at the curb adjacent to a street or in a median, designed with a shelter, which may be designed to include a sign and/or lighting, for the purpose of providing a covered waiting area for passengers boarding or alighting public transit vehicles.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 27764, § 1, 5-3-18)

**Sec. 146-547. Insurance requirements for public transit shelters.**

(a) Proof of commercial general liability insurance with limits of not less than $500,000.00 per occurrence/$ 1,000,000.00 aggregate combined

laws.title: Supplemental design standards for public transit shelters
laws.content:
(a) Public transit shelters shall only be installed at or within 20 feet of a designated transit stop.

(b) Public transit shelters shall be designed and installed in full compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act and all applicable local, state, and/or federal design standard requirements.

(c) Commercial general advertising signage may be included as part of an approved public transit shelter when the proposed location is:

(1) Adjacent to any non-residentially zoned property as provided on the official zoning map of the city.

(2) Within the right-of-way of a primary arterial street, as classified by the Louisiana Department of Transportation and Development.

(3) Additional shelter locations where general commercial advertising signage is allowed may be permitted by motion of the council

(4) Commercial general advertising signage may not exceed 23 square feet in area;

however, only one side of a double-faced sign shall be included in the computation of sign area.

(d) The design of public transit shelters is subject to the review and approval of the design advisory committee of the city planning commission.

(1) The design advisory committee is authorized to approve one or more standard designs of public transit shelter, allowing any sidewalk use permit application proposing such standard design to bypass design advisory committee review.

(2) Such approval shall be provided in writing and/or by issuance of stamped, approved plans.

(e) Within full control local historic districts, including the Vieux Carré, the staff of the jurisdictional historic commission shall review the design of public transit shelters to be located within such districts.

(1) The staff of the jurisdictional historic commission is authorized to approve one or more standard designs of public transit shelter, allowing any sidewalk use permit application proposing such standard design to bypass staff review.

(2) Such approval shall be provided in writing and/or by issuance of stamped, approved plans.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 27764, § 1, 5-3-18)

laws.title: Permit validity
laws.content:
A sidewalk use permit for a public transit shelter is valid as long as all structural elements are maintained in a safe and structurally sound condition life of the structure; a new permit shall be required for permanent removal or replacement of structure. Removal and/or replacement of a damaged shelter structure is not required, except as otherwise provided by law.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 27764, § 1, 5-3-18)

laws.title: Permit number required
laws.content:
Every sign or other advertising structure shall display the sidewalk use permit number and the voltage of any electrical apparatus used in connection with the public transit shelter, either painted on the structure or by application of a sticker, approved by the department of safety and permits, applied to the structure.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 27764, § 1, 5-3-18)

laws.title: Operational limitations, public transit shelters specifically
laws.content:
(a) The installation authorized by the sidewalk use permit shall not be modified or altered without the approval of the director of the department of safety and permits.

(b) Installation of the public transit shelter shall reflect the approved site plan and may not be substantially changed, altered, enlarged or reduced without the approval of the director of the department of safety and permits.

(c) The public transit shelter may be secured to the public right-of-way through bolting or otherwise fastening the structure to the city sidewalk, subject to approval of the department of public works, as long as it remains temporary in nature. If a new foundation or sidewalk is required for installation, such work shall be included on the plans and shall be constructed in accordance with the standards of the department of public works.

(d) The permittee shall keep the portion of the sidewalk not approved for use pursuant to a sidewalk use permit free of obstruction(s) at all times.

(e) Permittee shall in consultation with the department of sanitation, shall submit to the department of safety and permits a trash and litter abatement plan for the timely collection of refuse in a manner that prevents overflow of refuse unto the ground.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 27764, § 1, 5-3-18)

laws.title: Fees, public transit shelters specifically
laws.content:
(a) Upon initial submission of an application for a sidewalk use permit, a non-refundable application fee of $50.00 shall be remitted to the department of safety and permits.

(b) A permit fee of $250.00 shall be assessed for issuance of sidewalk use permits, which shall be sufficient to administer and enforce the regulations of this program and to compensate the city for use of public property.

(c) Sidewalk use permit fees shall be payable at the time of permit issuance and are non-refundable in the event of suspension, revocation, or surrender of the sidewalk use permit during the term of validity.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 27764, § 1, 5-3-18)

laws.title: Removal of public transit shelters
laws.content:
(a) Permittees are solely responsible for removal of any public transit shelter installed within the right-of-way upon cessation of transit service to the location.

(b) Permittees are solely responsible for the removal of any public transit shelter in the event the permittee will no longer maintain or service the public transit shelter in accordance with the standards of this chapter.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 27764, § 1, 5-3-18)

laws.title: Faithful performance bond required

(a) The permittee shall furnish to the City of New Orleans proof of the posting of a faithful performance bond in favor of the City of New Orleans, with good and sufficient surety approved by the City of New Orleans, in the penal sum of $250,000.00, conditioned that the permittee shall

laws.title: Operating permit required
laws.content:
Use of any right-of-way for installation, operation, or maintenance of an electric vehicle charger shall be unlawful without an operating permit issued pursuant to this division.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 27545, § 1, 9-28-17, eff. 10-1-17)

laws.title: Operating permit requirements
laws.content:
(a) For purposes of enforcing this division, operating permits shall be considered an extension of a dwelling on publicly owned property and any violation of this division shall be attributable to the owner of such adjacent dwelling.

(b) Operating permits shall only be issued as accessory and subordinate uses to dwellings.

Supp. No. 113

CD146:51
$\S$ 146-563

NEW ORLEANS CODE

(c) Operating permit eligibility shall be limited to the owner or occupant of a dwelling that does not and cannot provide off-street parking on the lot on which the dwelling is situated, in a manner compliant with the Comprehensive Zoning Ordinance.

(d) Electric vehicle chargers shall be monitored and controlled by the permittee at all times and may only be utilized for private, non-commercial use. Fees, gratuities, or other remuneration may not be received by the permittee for use of the charger.

(e) All improvements associated with the installation, operation, and maintenance of electric vehicle chargers shall be compliant with the adopted construction codes of the City of New Orleans, and certified as compliant by the director of safety and permits.

(f) Cords shall be retractable or have a place to hang the connector and cord sufficiently above the pedestrian surface. Any cords connecting the charger to a vehicle shall be configured so that they do not cross a driveway, sidewalk, or passenger unloading area.

(g) Issuance of an operating permit for installation, operation, and maintenance of an electric vehicle charger on the right-of-way does not create a private or reserved parking space for the permittee on the right-of-way. A sign shall be affixed to the electric vehicle charger indicating that the presence of the charger does not constitute a private or reserved parking space, the dimensions and text of which shall be determined by the director of safety and permits.

(h) The electric vehicle charger shall be removed by and at the expense of the permittee or owner of the associated real property if the owner or permittee no longer owns or resides at the associated dwelling or upon non-renewal or cancellation of the operating permit. If a subsequent owner or renter of the property is desirous of taking possession of the electric vehicle charger for usage purposes, however, he/she must apply for a permit before expiration of the permit.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 27545, § 1, 9-28-17, eff. 10-1-17)

laws.title: Authority to issue permit
laws.content:
The director of the department of safety and permits shall authorize operating permits only for residential uses that fully comply with the requirements of this division. Such permits shall be issued only after consultation with and the positive recommendation of the director of the department of public works. An operating permit is a privilege, not a right, and may be revoked, suspended, or not renewed based on non-compliance with the requirements of this division.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 27545, § 1, 9-28-17, eff. 10-1-17)

laws.title: Application, documents and requirements
laws.content:
(a) Any natural person seeking an operation permit for the installation, operation, and/or maintenance of an electric vehicle charger in the right-of-way shall file a written application with the director of safety and permits on a form to be provided for that purpose.

(b) In addition to the application form, the following documents shall be submitted for review for an application to be considered complete:

1. A plan shall be submitted on $8\frac{1}{2}" \times 11"$ paper or in digital format. This plan does not need to be to scale, but shall show exact length and width dimensions of entire right-of-way abutting the subject property. This plan shall include the location and size of the EV charger (including the stored cord), as well as all existing encumbrances on and underneath the public way including, but not limited to, driveways, parking meters, fire hydrants, bike racks, light poles, water, sewer, drain, and other utility lines, underground streetlight conduit and traffic signal conduit, and trees. A written narrative may accompany the plan.

2. Photographs depicting the proposed site where the electric vehicle charger will be installed and the relationship between the proposed electric vehicle charger and the surrounding public right-of-way.

Supp. No. 113

CD146:52

laws.title: Streets, Sidewalks and Other Public Places
laws.content:
§ 146-567

3. If the applicant is not the owner of the adjacent real property or their designee, written authorization of the property owner shall be required as part of the application.

4. A permittee shall maintain an insurance policy that covers any risk for any injury or damage resulting from the installation, operation, and/or maintenance of the electric vehicle charger, and the property owner shall agree to indemnify and hold the city harmless from any claims arising from the installation, operation, and/or maintenance of the electric vehicle charger to the extent permitted by law.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 27545, § 1, 9-28-17, eff. 10-1-17)

laws.title: Standards and criteria for application review
laws.content:
(a) The following standards and criteria shall be used in reviewing the application and design drawings to determine if the proposed location is suitable and will not obstruct free and proper use of the public right-of-way.

1. The right-of-way width shall be of sufficient width to accommodate the proposed electric vehicle charger while maintaining a clear path of travel that is:

   a. At least four feet in width on sidewalks of eight to ten feet in width.

   b. At least six feet in width on sidewalks greater than ten feet in width.

   c. In areas of congested pedestrian activity, the reviewing agencies are authorized to require a wider pedestrian path to ensure the free and proper use of the right-of-way by pedestrians.

2. A clearance of at least 15 feet shall be maintained between any electric vehicle charger and a fire hydrant, or fire department sprinkler/standpipe connection.

3. A clearance of at least 20 feet shall be maintained between any electric vehicle charger and an intersection or crosswalk.

4. A clearance of at least three feet shall be maintained between any electric vehicle charger and a driveway or other curb cut.

5. A clearance of at least ten feet shall be maintained between any electric vehicle charger and a public transit pole or CPNC stand.

6. Locations of electric vehicle chargers are restricted to the area immediately adjacent to the dwelling being served and may not project in front of neighboring properties or vacant lots.

7. The location shall avoid interference with vehicular sight lines at street corners or driveways and minimize the removal of vegetation.

8. The electric vehicle charger shall be installed no closer than 18" from the edge of the roadway, unless otherwise approved by the director of the department of public works.

9. Verification that the property has no outstanding taxes or property liens.

10. In local control historic districts, the historic district landmarks commission staff shall have approval jurisdiction over the design of electric vehicle chargers.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 27545, § 1, 9-28-17, eff. 10-1-17)

laws.title: Permit issuance
Permit renewal
laws.content:
The operating permit shall be valid one year from the date of issuance. Renewal permits shall be issued in the same manner as initial permits, and requires:

(a) Providing the department an updated copy of any of the documents required by section 146-565;

(b) Providing a revised or updated site plan, if changes to an approved plan are requested; and

(c) Proof of payment of all applicable taxes and fees as required by law.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 27545, § 1, 9-28-17, eff. 10-1-17)

laws.title: Approved equipment
laws.content:
(a) Equipment shall be certified to current standards by a nationally recognized testing laboratory (such as UL or ETL) and listed and approved for electric vehicle use.

(b) Equipment shall comply with Society of Automotive Engineers (SAE) J1772-2009 standards, or a comparable standard as determined by the director of safety and permits, including safety features between the electric vehicle charger and the electric vehicle. These safety features include, but are not limited to:

(1) Ground fault circuit interrupter(s).

(2) Proximity detection and signaling.

(3) Power may only be supplied from the electric vehicle charger after the device has determined a proper and safe connection between the electric vehicle charger and the electric vehicle.

(c) Types of electric vehicle charger authorized:

(1) Level 1 Chargers with a power level of 110 to 120 VAC and up to 20 Amps.

(2) Level 2 Chargers with a power level of 208 to 240 VAC and up to 100 Amps.

(3) Level 3 Chargers and Fast DC Chargers with a capacity of up to 150kW.

(4) The director of the department of safety and permits may authorize an electric vehicle charger not described in paragraphs (1) through (3) above provided that the director creates a memo detailing why the approved electric vehicle charger substantively complies with the standards of this section and does not pose a danger to public health and safety.

(d) Power shall, under no circumstance, be provided to an electric vehicle parked on the right-of-way via extension cord that is run from a dwelling across a sidewalk and to the right-of-way. Such configuration constitutes a public nuisance and is in violation of the city’s adopted construction codes.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 27545, § 1, 9-28-17, eff. 10-1-17; M.C.S., Ord. No. 30377, § 1, 6-26-25)

laws.title: Authorized and prohibited locations
laws.content:
(a) Electric vehicle chargers shall be permitted only in conjunction with a permitted residential use in a legally occupied dwelling.

(b) No property or parcel may have more than one electric vehicle charger installed in the right-of-way adjacent to such property or parcel.

(c) Installation, operation, and/or maintenance of electric vehicle chargers within the right-of-way shall be prohibited in the Vieux Carré, as defined in Chapter 166 of this Code.

laws.title: Conditions and restrictions
laws.content:
(a) Operating permits are subject to modification, suspension or revocation by the City of New Orleans at any time during the period of validity if the city requires the subject right-of-way area cleared for street, sidewalk, or utility repair or other public purposes.

(b) Operating permits are non-transferrable and may not be assigned or granted to any other person or business which may occupy the dwelling to which a permit has been issued. A subsequent owner or renter of a property with an electric vehicle charger may submit a permit application before expiration of the permit. The requirement to remove the electric vehicle charger will be postponed while the new permit application is reviewed. Upon approval of such application, a transfer fee will be assessed in addition to any permit fees which may be due.

(c) The permittee accepts the prevailing site conditions including, but not limited to, loading and passenger zones, loading zones, obstructions within the right-of-way, active residential permit parking zone restrictions and permitting requirements, street cleaning parking restrictions, and automobile traffic.

(d) Operating permits shall be automatically suspended for periods two hours before and two hours after a carnival parade for locations on parade routes.

(e) The director of safety and permits may suspend operating permits without prior notice in the event of permitted special events where crowd control is likely to be necessary.

(f) The departments of police and fire and any other emergency response agency may require immediate removal, deactivation, or relocation of the electric vehicle charger in emergency situations.

(g) The City of New Orleans, its officers, agents, or any private utility company operating pursuant to a franchise granted by the city council, their officers, agents, or employees shall not be responsible for electric vehicle charger components relocated during emergencies.

(h) Issuance of an operating permit does not grant, convey, or infer any vested right to the use of the right-of-way by the permittee nor does it constitute a deed, grant of easement, or servitude by the city. The city retains the right to deny the issuance or renewal of an operating permit for noncompliance with the provisions of this division, the City Code, or the comprehensive zoning ordinance.

(i) No area of the right-of-way shall be painted, modified, or altered in any way without prior written approval of the director of the department of public works. No part of the right-of-way shall be obstructed, blocked, or otherwise reserved for a permittee’s use of the approved electric vehicle charger. The public right-of-way shall remain available for parking of the general public at all times when the location is not legally occupied by the permittee’s vehicle.

(j) The city and/or its agents may schedule general cleaning and maintenance operations. If such work is scheduled, the city and/or it agents shall give notification of its scheduled cleaning times in advance of such operations to permittees if the city expects such cleaning or maintenance will effect the permitted electric vehicle charger. Each permittee in the affected area shall remove, or cause to be removed, electric vehicle chargers so that they do not inhibit the scheduled cleaning, repair, and/or maintenance operations.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 27545, § 1, 9-28-17, eff. 10-1-17)

laws.title: Penalties
laws.content:
Any violation of this division may subject a violator to any remedy, legal or equitable, available to the city. laws.title: Carrying away earth from streets, etc
laws.content:
No person shall, without the consent of the director of the department of streets, carry away or cause to be carried away any earth from any street, square, public square, public walk or commons.

(Code 1956, § 61-124)

laws.title: Throwing glass, etc., on streets
laws.content:
(a) It shall be unlawful for any person to drop, place, throw and suffer to remain or to be dropped, placed or thrown upon any highway, street, lane, square or other public place in the city any broken glass, crockery, scrap iron, nails, tacks, wire or such other substance as shall cause the streets and highways of the city to become dangerous to vehicles making use of them.

(b) Any person failing to comply with the provisions of this section shall be fined in a sum not exceeding $25.00 or imprisoned for 30 days.

(Code 1956, § 61-125)

laws.title: Street paving not to be damaged by heavy vehicles, etc
laws.content:
It shall be unlawful for any person to drive, push or haul any vehicle, tractor, truck, road-grading machine, roller or other heavy object on any hard surface street paving in such a manner as to cut or cause indentations to appear in such hard surface street paving or otherwise to injure or damage such paving.

(Code 1956, § 61-126)

laws.title: Liability of officers of corporation
laws.content:
When any agent, or employee of any corporation shall be responsible for the injury to any hard surface street paving in the manner set forth in section 146-578, the president, vice-president, secretary or other responsible managing officer of such corporation shall, likewise, be held liable for the violation of such section.

(Code 1956, § 61-127)

laws.title: Discharge of liquids, etc., into streets
laws.content:
(a) It shall be unlawful to discharge any liquid or other material into or upon a street or open gutter in the city, other than the natural runoff of rain water or the discharge of clear water from drinking fountains or swimming pools, except under extenuating circumstances and in a manner approved by the director of the department of streets.

(b) Whenever it is brought to the attention of the director of the department of streets that an unlawful discharge of liquid is being made, he shall notify the owner and/or the occupant of the property from which the discharge of liquid flows that a violation of this section exists and the owner and/or occupant shall, within 30 days after the receipt of a notice from the director, correct the violation by an applicable measure indicated below:

(1) If wastewater is being discharged, a direct connection should be made to drainage canals, existing subsurface drainage, or subsurface drainage should be installed to tie into existing subsurface drainage.

(2) If discharge is not wastewater, a connection should be made to sanitary sewers in accordance with the requirements of the sewerage and water board.

(3) A method of disposal approved by the director of the department of streets and the sewerage and water board shall be used if disposal cannot be accomplished by the application of subsections (1) or (2) of this section.

(Code 1956, § 61-128)

**Sec. 146-581. Mixing cement, etc., on asphalt streets prohibited.**

It shall be unlawful for any person to use asphalt streets for the mixing of cement and other matter in the preparation of concrete or to use such pavements for slacking lime or mixing mortar. Persons who are compelled to prepare cement, slack lime or mix mortar on asphalt streets shall be equipped with proper boards and cement boxes to protect the asphalt pavements from any injury in the preparation of such concrete or other material.

(Code 1956, § 61-129)

**Sec. 146-582. Placing of fill on a lot or site.**

(a) It shall be unlawful to terrace, grade or place fill on any lot or site, or part thereof, in such a manner so as to adversely alter the present natural drainage pattern of the area. Requirements for lot or site grading and filling are on file in the office of the department of streets and are obtainable from the department. The department of streets shall approve the method used to terrace, grade or fill lots in order to assure that water will effectively drain from such lot or site and from the adjacent area. Whenever it is brought to the attention of the director of the department of streets that the provisions of this section are being violated, he shall notify the owner that the terracing, grading or filling being placed in place does not meet its requirements. The owner is to within 60 days after receipt of notice from the director of the department of streets grade or fill the lot or site in such a manner so as to be in compliance with the requirements of the department of streets. Should the owner of the property fail to comply with the notice sent concerning violation of this section, the director of the department of streets shall direct the maintenance division of the department of streets to properly grade and fill the lot or site in order to comply with the requirements of the department. The cost of all labor, equipment, and materials, including additional fill if needed shall be charged to the property owner.

(b) Upon completion of the work the director of the department of streets shall issue a bill against the property owner for the cost of such work which shall be due in cash within ten days after presentation of the bill.

(c) Whenever any property owner shall fail to pay the bill due by him within ten days after presentation thereof, the director of the department of streets, through the director of the department of finance, shall then record in the mortgage office within 60 days from the date of default on the part of the property owner, a copy of such bill in order that it may operate as a lien and privilege against the property affected thereby.

(d) Any retaining walls installed pursuant to the provisions of this section shall be constructed of concrete. Requests for approval of the use of material other than concrete shall be reviewed and approved or disapproved by the city council after consultation with appropriate city departments concerning the structural integrity of the alternate material.

(e) It shall be unlawful to terrace, grade or place fill on any lot or site, or part thereof, in such a manner so as to allow the runoff to drain on to adjacent property.

(Code 1956, § 61-130)

**Sec. 146-583. Permit for private use of street.**

The temporary closure of streets for noncommercial purposes by individuals or organizations shall be allowed only after obtaining written approval from the district councilmember and issuance of a special permit by the director of the department of public works, who is authorized to impose conditions upon the issuance thereof. These fees shall be nonrefundable and shall not

laws.title: Permit required for placement of trash containers, dumpsters, etc., in the public right-of-way
laws.content:
The placement of trash containers, receptacles, other similar containers, and dumpsters, hereafter referred to as dumpsters for purposes of this section, in the public right-of-way by contractors, builders, owners, or others requiring the temporary use of curb space to facilitate work conducted by them in the immediate vicinity shall be allowed only after the issuance of a permit by the department of public works. The city is authorized to impose conditions on the issuance of any permit issued pursuant to this section. If the curb space to be utilized, or any portion thereof, is regulated by parking meters, then the space designated for dumpster placement and fees relative thereto shall be as provided in section 154-1090, and fees for all other spaces shall be $10.00 per day. The city shall collect from the applicant for such permit an application fee in the amount of $40.00. The permit issued by the department of public works shall be valid for a period not to exceed 45 days, and may be renewed for additional 45-day periods provided that the contractor, builder, owner, or other applicant makes a request for renewal at least five working days prior to the expiration of the effective permit.

(Code 1956, § 61-131.1; Ord. No. 20,001, § 1, 1-18-01; M.C.S., Ord. No. 23818, § 14, 12-1-09; M.C.S., Ord. No. 26263, § 1, 2-26-15)

laws.title: Mandatory safety and identifying markings and permits to appear on all trash containers, dumpsters, etc., placed in the public right-of-way
laws.content:
All trash containers, receptacles, other similar containers, or dumpsters, hereafter referred to as dumpsters for purposes of this section, that are placed in the public right-of-way shall bear the name, address, and phone number of the owner or party assuming liability for said dumpster and this identification shall be permanently affixed to each side of the dumpster, shall appear in legible characters that are of a color directly contrasting that of the dumpster, and be of a height not less than two inches. Any permit issued pursuant to section 146-584 shall also be clearly displayed. Dumpsters shall also bear no less than two "Type 2" safety markers, permanently affixed, upon each upper corner at each end. For purposes of this section, "Type 2" markers are those consisting of either three yellow reflectors, each with a minimum dimension of approximately three inches, that are arranged either vertically or horizontally, or an all-yellow reflective panel with dimensions no less than six inches by 12 inches.

(Code 1956, § 61-133; M.C.S., Ord. No. 26263, § 1, 2-26-15)

laws.title: Permit required
laws.content:
Use of any public parking spaces or the parking lane for the extension of a licensed business shall be unlawful without a parklet permit issued pursuant to this division.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 29064, § 1, 6-23-22)

laws.title: Permit requirements
laws.content:
(a) No person or business shall establish, operate, or continue to operate a parklet on any parking lane or public parking space unless a valid parklet permit is obtained pursuant to this division.

(b) Parklet permits shall be issued only to validly licensed businesses that wish to provide additional customer space on the public parking space adjacent to their businesses for use by business patrons. Such additional customer space may include additional seating.

(c) The eligibility for such permits shall be determined by the standards in this division and the Comprehensive Zoning Ordinance, including its use standards and standards applicable to the zoning district in which the subject property is situated.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 29064, § 1, 6-23-22)

laws.title: Authority to issue permit
laws.content:
The director of the department of safety and permits shall authorize parklet permits only for validly licensed businesses that fully comply with the requirements of this division and the Comprehensive Zoning Ordinance. Such permits shall be issued only after consultation with and the positive recommendation of the director of the department of public works, who shall consider whether a parklet would impose an unreasonable impact on pedestrian congestion, traffic congestion, nearby business activity, available on-street parking, and public safety. A parklet permit is a privilege, not a right, and may be revoked, suspended, or not renewed based on non-compliance with the requirements of the Comprehensive Zoning Ordinance and/or the requirements of this division.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 29064, § 1, 6-23-22)

laws.title: Application, documents, and requirements
laws.content:
(a) Any business or person seeking a parklet permit shall file a written application with the department of safety and permits on a form to be provided for that purpose.

(b) In addition to the application form, the following documents shall be submitted for review in order for an application to be considered complete:

(1) A site plan on 8.5-inch by 11-inch paper or in digital format, which shows:

    a. the exact location of the planned parklet, including the street address of the adjacent property, and dimensions from fixed reference points in the public right-of-way;

    b. all design elements, including table spacing, any utilities in the area, and all relevant right-of-way dimensions;

    c. any existing designated curb uses in the area, including whether the area is regulated by parking meters; and

    d. the layout of any existing sidewalk café, including the permit number for such sidewalk café.

(2) Photographs depicting the proposed site where the parklet will be implemented and the relationship between the proposed parklet and the surrounding public right-of-way.

(3) Images, renderings, or photographs of the furniture and fixtures to be utilized as part of the requested parklet.

(4) Proof of commercial general liability insurance with limits of not less than $1,000,000.00 per occurrence/ $1,000,000.00 aggregate combined single limit for bodily injury, personal injury, and property damage liability. The operator of the parklet, which shall be the same as the operator of the adjacent business, shall obtain, maintain, and provide proof of general liability cover-

age, with the city listed as an additional named insured via endorsement (additional insured — designated person or organization), Form CG 20 26 04 13 or similar endorsement(s) providing equivalent coverage). The City of New Orleans must be shown by name in the schedule of the endorsement and included in the definition of "Who Is an Insured." The insurance policy must be reviewed by the city risk manager or law department for compliance with this section. The applicant shall provide for 30 days prior written notice to the department of safety and permits if coverage is substantially changed, cancelled, or not renewed.

(5) A hold-harmless and/or indemnity agreement from the operator to the city on a form to be prepared by the city.

(6) Engineering plan showing all details of structural and dimensional elements of the proposed parklet. These plans must be stamped by a Louisiana licensed professional engineer.

(7) A maintenance and operations plan for the parklet and adjacent area on a form developed by the department of public works.

(8) A hurricane preparedness plan outlining plans in the event of an approaching tropical storm threat consistent with the following:

    a. For parklets without a roof structure:

        1. A plan to remove the parklet from the right-of-way; or

        2. A plan to secure the parklet in place, including engineering plans stamped by a Louisiana licensed professional engineer specifying the parklet structure will remain securely in place without bolting or otherwise fastening the parklet to the street, curb, or sidewalk.

b. For parklets with a roof structure:

1. A plan to remove the parklet from the right-of-way;

2. A plan to demount the roof structure of the parklet and secure the rest of the parklet structure in place, including engineering plans stamped by a Louisiana licensed professional engineer specifying the parklet structure will remain securely in place without bolting or otherwise fastening the parklet to the street, curb, or sidewalk; or

laws.title: Standards and criteria for application review
laws.content:
(a) Location criteria.

(1) Parklets may only be placed in parking lanes. They shall not be placed in travel lanes.

(2) Parklets must be placed a minimum of 15 feet from water hydrants; 20 feet from stop signs, crosswalks, and corners; and three feet from driveways.

(3) Parklets shall not be placed in bus stop or bus zone areas.

(4) Parklets shall not be placed in cab stand or hack stand areas.

(5) Parklets shall not be placed in fire lanes.

(6) Parklets shall not be placed in handicapped parking zones.

(7) Parklets are only allowed on streets with a speed limit of 30 miles per hour or less.

(8) Parklet areas will be limited to the property frontage of the requesting business unless the adjacent property owner provides written consent of the parklet extending to their property frontage.

(9) Every location will be assessed for feasibility on a case-by-case basis. Road geometry, parking restrictions, and other necessary usages on the block or impacts from losing curb space shall be considered.

(10) Parklets are not permitted on streets within the City of New Orleans that are under the jurisdiction of another public entity or that are privately owned without written approval from that entity.

(11) Parklets are not permitted within one foot of any utility access point in the public right-of-way.

(12) The number of parklets permitted per block face shall be limited in accordance with the temporary use standards of the comprehensive zoning ordinance.

(13) Notwithstanding any other provisions herein, no parklet shall be permitted within the boundaries of the Vieux Carré, which for the purposes of this subsection shall be bounded by and include the downtown side of Canal Street, the river side of North Rampart Street, the uptown side of Esplanade Avenue, and the Mississippi River.

(14) Notwithstanding any other provisions herein, no parklet shall be permitted on Magazine Street from its intersection with Washington Avenue (uptown side) to its intersection with Louisiana Avenue (downtown side).

(15) A parklet and a sidewalk café may be permitted at the same location if not otherwise prohibited by law.

(b) Safety and material criteria.

(1) No portion or element of an approved site plan may be secured through bolting or otherwise fastening any table, chair,

Supp. No. 108

CD146:64.2

laws.title: Streets, Sidewalks and Other Public Places
laws.content:
§ 146-593

bench, fixture, or other device to a public sidewalk, street, curb, post, sign, tree, or similar feature.

(2) Care must be taken to ensure adequate sight lines for vehicles on the street and near driveways, intersections, and crosswalks.

(3) Sidewalk access must be maintained at all times.

(4) No portion or element of an approved site plan shall obstruct drainage or prevent drainage from falling or flowing across sidewalks or roadways.

(5) The seating area and any transition from the sidewalk or curb shall be ADA compliant.

(6) Parklet decking shall be designed to support a minimum live load of 60 pounds per square foot after accounting for furniture weight.

(7) Parklets shall maintain a minimum 18 inch buffer between seating and the vehicular travel lane. The buffer shall be at least 32 inches in height, as measured from the road grade. Any portion of this buffer that exceeds 42 inches in height shall be visually transparent to maintain sight lines.

(8) Parklets shall include wheel stops offset two feet from either end of the parklet structure and offset one foot from the curb to maintain drainage. Wheel stops shall not be secured through bolting or otherwise damaging the roadway to secure.

(9) Parklets shall include a retroreflective element on the leading edge adjacent to approaching traffic.

(c) Design specifications and review.

(1) The design advisory committee will adopt a standard template for the visual and aesthetic aspects of proposed elements of the parklet.

(2) If a proposed parklet uses the standard template for the visual and aesthetic aspects of proposed elements, no further design review will be required.

(3) If a proposed parklet will not use the standard template for the visual and aesthetic aspects of proposed elements, the parklet design shall be reviewed by the design advisory committee, whose approval shall be required prior to permitting. All design advisory committee meetings are public meetings, and all agendas will be publicly noticed according to applicable law.

(d) Other criteria.

(1) Tables, chairs, umbrellas, and any other objects provided with the parklet shall be of sufficient quality, design, materials, and workmanship to ensure the safety and convenience of users, and to enhance the visual and aesthetic quality of the urban environment.

a. Umbrellas, and other decorative elements shall be fire retardant, pressure-treated, or manufactured of fire-resistant material and shall not interfere with the free and proper use of the sidewalk.

(2) No tents may be placed in a parklet.

(3) Glass construction elements or materials are prohibited.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 29064, § 1, 6-23-22; M.C.S., Ord. No. 29862, § 1, 3-21-24)

laws.title: Permit issuance
Permit renewal
laws.content:
The parklet permit shall be valid one year from the date of issuance. Renewal permits shall be issued in the same manner as initial permits, and shall require:

(a) Providing the department with an updated copy of any of the documents listed in section 146-591(b);

(b) Providing a revised or updated site plan if changes to an approved plan are requested; and

(c) Proof of payment of all applicable taxes and fees as required by law.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 29064, § 1, 6-23-22)

laws.title: Permit display required
laws.content:
(a) The parklet permit shall be conspicuously displayed on the parklet structure and the exterior wall or window of the main entrance of the licensed establishment with which the parklet is associated.

(b) The approved parklet plan shall be posted in the same location and manner as a city issued occupational license and/or alcoholic beverage license.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 29064, § 1, 6-23-22; M.C.S., Ord. No. 29862, § 1, 3-21-24)

laws.title: Operational limitations, generally
laws.content:
(a) The arrangement and number of tables or other approved items authorized by the parklet permit shall not be modified or altered without the approval of the director of the department of safety and permits.

(b) All furniture and fixtures shall match the approved site plan and may not be substantially changed, altered, added to or reduced without the approval of the director of the department of safety and permits.

(c) No portion or element of an approved site plan may be secured through bolting or otherwise fastening any table, chair, bench, fixture, or other device to a public sidewalk, street, curb, post, sign, tree, or similar feature.

(d) The permittee shall keep any portion of the public right-of-way not approved for parklet use, pursuant to a parklet permit, free of obstruction(s) at all times.

(e) The parklet area shall be maintained with a neat and orderly appearance at all times and the area shall be cleared of debris or litter on a periodic basis during the day and again at the close of business each day.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 29064, § 1, 6-23-22)

laws.title: Operational limitations
laws.content:
(a) The capacity of an approved parklet shall not exceed the approved seating capacity indicated on the approved site plan and as stated on the permit placard.

(b) Tables and chairs associated with an approved parklet shall be structurally sound and maintained in a manner ready for access and use by patrons.

Supp. No. 108

CD146:64.4

laws.title: Streets, Sidewalks and Other Public Places
laws.content:
§ 146-598

(c) The parklet permittee shall sweep and remove trash from the parklet area throughout the day and at the close of business of the parklet.

(d) No live entertainment, speakers, or other sources of amplified sound shall be permissible on or adjacent to the approved parklet.

(e) Carts, receptacles for waste or dirty dishes, and cooking appliances shall not be placed or stored on any portion of the public right-of-way or parklet.

(f) Tables, chairs, and any other components of the approved parklet shall be neatly stacked and organized at the end of each business day, no later than 10:30 p.m. pursuant to this section, in a manner which will result in minimal intrusion into the public right-of-way.

(g) All property ingress and egress where a parklet exists must remain unobstructed (including queuing lines) for clear, barrier-free pedestrian passage, consistent with the fire department regulations and ANSI standards for barrier-free access.

(h) Hours of operation:

(1) Seating within the parklet shall not begin before 8:00 a.m.

(2) Food or beverage service shall not provided within the parklet after 10:00 p.m.

(3) The parklet permittee shall not use the parklet for business purposes outside of these hours.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 29064, § 1, 6-23-22)

laws.title: Conditions and restrictions
laws.content:
(a) Parklet permits are subject to modification, suspension, or revocation by the City of New Orleans at any time during the period of validity if the city requires the subject area cleared for street, sidewalk, utility repair, other public purposes, or in the case of an emergency.

(b) Parklet permits are non-transferrable and may not be assigned or granted to any other person or business that may occupy the location to which a parklet permit has been issued.

(c) The permittee accepts the prevailing site conditions, including, but not limited to, loading and passenger zones, bus stop or bus zones, cab stands or hack stands, fire lanes, handicapped parking zones, vehicle traffic, exhaust fumes, noise, and pedestrian traffic.

(d) Parades and street closures:

(1) Parklet permits shall be automatically suspended for a period of one week prior to the carnival parade season and remain suspended until after the final carnival parade of the carnival season for business locations on designated parade routes. If a permittee fails to remove the elements of the parklet one week prior to carnival parade season, the director of the department of public works and/or sanitation shall remove and dispose of the parklet elements.

(2) Parklet permits shall be automatically suspended for periods before, during, and after moving or stationary street closures unless the special event permit associated with the street closure includes the parklet. If a permittee fails to remove the elements of the parklet, prior to the moving or stationary street closure, the director of the department of public works and/or sanitation shall remove and dispose of the parklet elements.

(3) Parklet permits shall be automatically suspended in a Clean Zone as created by ordinance of the city council for a special event, unless the Clean Zone ordinance includes the parklet. If a permittee fails to remove the elements of the parklet, prior to the moving or stationary street closure, the director of the department of public works and/or sanitation shall remove and dispose of the parklet elements.

(e) The director of safety and permits may suspend parklet permits without prior notice in the event of permitted special events where crowd control is likely to be necessary.

Supp. No. 108

CD146:64.5
§ 146-598

NEW ORLEANS CODE

(f) The departments of police and fire, or any other emergency response agency, may require immediate removal or relocation of all or part of the parklet in emergency situations.

(g) The City of New Orleans, its officers, agents, or any private utility company operating pursuant to a franchise granted by the city council and their officers, agents, or employees, shall not be responsible for parklet components relocated during emergencies.

(h) Issuance of a parklet permit does not grant, convey, or infer any vested right to the use of the public right-of-way area by the permittee nor does it constitute a deed, grant of easement, or servitude by the city. The city retains the right to revoke or deny the issuance or renewal of a parklet permit for noncompliance with the provisions of this division, the City Code, or the Comprehensive Zoning Ordinance.

(i) The public right-of-way shall not be painted, modified, or altered in any way without prior written approval of the director of the department of public works.

(j) The city and/or its agents may schedule general cleaning and maintenance operations. If such work is scheduled, the city and/or its agents shall give notification of its scheduled cleaning times in advance of such operations to all parklet permittees. Each permittee in the affected area shall remove all portions of the parklet so that they do not inhibit the scheduled cleaning, repair, and/or maintenance operations.

(k) Permittee is wholly responsible for the proper maintenance and use of any permitted parklet use, and shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless the city from all actions, claims, costs, damages, and expense to which the city may be subject by reason of any injury or alleged injury to any person or property resulting or alleged to result from such parklet use. The owner shall pay all sums so recovered against the city in any suit on account of such alleged injuries to which the city may be made a party, together with all such costs, damages and expenses as may be suffered by the city, all in a manner as to hold the city harmless from all such actions or claims.

(l) The permittee is wholly responsible for repairs and alterations to parklets as needed. (M.C.S., Ord. No. 29064, § 1, 6-23-22)

laws.title: Fees
laws.content:
(a) Upon initial submission of an application for a parklet permit, a non-refundable application fee of $250.00 shall be remitted to the department of safety and permits.

(b) Fees for new issuance or renewal of parklet permits shall be assessed in accordance with the following schedule, which shall be sufficient to administer and enforce the regulations of this program and to compensate the city for use of public property:

(1) Initial issuance fee per below:

a. Parklet issuance fee of $400.00.

b. Parklet right-of-way usage fee: Through December 31, 2024, the parklet right-of-way usage fee shall be waived for any establishment seeking its initial parklet permit. This waiver shall not apply to any establishment seeking a renewal of its parklet permit.

1. Metered locations in the area bounded by the Mississippi River, Calliope Street, Earhart Boulevard, S. Claiborne Avenue, Canal Street, N. Rampart Street, Joseph Guillaume Place, St. Claude Avenue, and Franklin Avenue, inclusive of both sides of bounding streets: $31.50 per square foot.

2. Unmetered locations in the area bounded by the Mississippi River, Calliope Street, Earhart Boulevard, S. Claiborne Avenue, Canal Street, N. Rampart Street, Joseph Guillaume Place, St. Claude Avenue, and Franklin Avenue, inclusive of both sides of bounding streets: $21.00 per square foot.

laws.content:
