(b) It shall be unlawful for any person to operate or cause to be operated any vehicle or other mobile equipment being used for the hauling of garbage, or trash, unless such garbage or trash is completely covered by a securely fastened tarpaulin, or other similar covering, and unless the tailgate of such vehicle is secured in such manner as to prevent spillage of any portion of the garbage or trash being transported upon the streets, sidewalks, or other public ways.

(Code 1956, § 38-140)

*State law references—Loads on vehicles; care required thereto, R.S. 32:383.*

laws.title: Operation on flooded or closed streets
laws.content:
(a) It shall be unlawful for any person to operate any motor vehicle or boat on the streets, roads, highways or bridges which are flooded or inundated within this city either (i) in excess of a speed of five miles per hour or (ii) in such a manner as to cause water, waves or wakes to damage property alongside of or adjacent to such streets, roads, highways or bridges at any speed.

(b) No person shall in any way tamper with, move, damage or destroy any barricades, signs or signals placed upon any streets, roads, highways or bridges within the city by any department of the city government or any other governmental agency in connection with any such street, road, highway or bridge being flooded or inundated, nor shall any person disobey the instructions, signals, warnings or markings of any warning sign, signal, city employee, or barricade so placed on any such street, road, highway or bridge which is flooded or inundated, unless at the time having been expressly so directed by a police officer of the state or city.

(c) It shall be unlawful for any person to operate any motor vehicle on the streets, roadways, highways, or bridges within the city when signage, signals, warnings, or markings are in place that indicate or designate that such street, roadway, highway, or bridge is closed. Such signage, signals, warnings, or markings are intended to notify and warn such operators of an impaired or flooded street, roadway, highway, or bridge, and that passage thereon is prohibited.

(d) Any person may file an affidavit with the Traffic Court of New Orleans complaining of a violation of this section in accordance with City Code section 154-142 and R.S. 13:2512.

(Code 1956, § 38-144; M.C.S., Ord. No. 20,904, § 1, 10-17-02; M.C.S., Ord. No. 28186, § 1, 9-5-19)

laws.title: Motor vehicles operating in bicycle lanes
laws.content:
(a) No person shall operate a motor vehicle in a bicycle lane except as follows:

(1) To prepare for a turn within a distance of 200 feet from the intersection.

(2) To enter or leave the roadway onto an alley, private road, or driveway.

(3) To enter or leave a parking space when parking is permitted adjacent to the bicycle lane.

(b) Any person operating a motor vehicle upon a bicycle lane in accordance with subsection (a) of this section shall yield the right-of-way to all bicycles and electric mobility aids within the bicycle lane.

(c) This section shall not prohibit the use of a motorized bicycle in a bicycle lane when the operator travels at no speed greater than what is reasonable or prudent, has due regard for visibility, traffic conditions, and the condition of the roadway surface of the bicycle lane and in a manner which does not endanger the safety of bicyclists.

(d) In case of an emergency, the driver of a motor vehicle may lawfully operate the vehicle in a bicycle lane in accordance with the normal standards of prudent conduct to protect the

Supp. No. 89

CD154:44.2
TRAFFIC AND VEHICLES

§ 154-406

driver and others from harm. When the emergency ends, the motor vehicle shall not be operated in the bicycle lane.

(e) Any person found in violation of this section shall be fined not less than $300.00, nor more than $500.00.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 27363, § 1, 4-20-17; M.C.S., Ord. No. 28047, § 1, 3-28-19)

**Sec. 154-406. Limitations on passing bicycles.**

The operator of a motor vehicle, when overtaking and passing a bicycle proceeding in the same direction on the roadway, shall exercise due care while the motor vehicle is passing the bicycle

Supp. No. 89

CD154:44.2.1

TRAFFIC AND VEHICLES

§ 154-437

and shall leave a safe distance between the motor vehicle and the bicycle of not less than three feet and shall maintain such clearance until safely past the overtaken bicycle. An operator of a motor vehicle may pass a bicycle traveling in the same direction in a no-passing zone only when it is safe to do so.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 27363, § 1, 4-20-17)

**Sec. 154-407. Harassment of bicyclists prohibited.**

It shall be unlawful to harass, taunt, or maliciously throw objects at or in the direction of any person riding a bicycle.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 27363, § 1, 4-20-17)

**Secs. 154-408—154-435. Reserved.**

laws.title: Turning and Stopping Rules
laws.content:
**Sec. 154-436. Required position and method of turning at intersections.**

The driver of a vehicle intending to turn at any intersection shall proceed as follows:

(1) *Right turns.* Both the approach for a right turn and a right turn shall be made as close as practicable to the right-hand curb or the edge of the roadway.

(2) *Left turns on two-way roadways.* At any intersection where traffic is permitted to move in both directions on each roadway entering the intersection, an approach for a left turn shall be made in that portion of the right half of the roadway nearest the centerline thereof and by passing to the right of such centerline where it enters the intersection and after entering the intersection, the left turn shall be made so as to leave the intersection to the right of the centerline of the roadway being entered. Whenever practicable, the left turn shall be made in that portion of the intersection to the left of the center of the intersection.

(3) *Left turns on other than two-way roadways.* At any intersection where traf-

fic is restricted to one direction on one or more of the roadways, the driver of a vehicle intending to turn left at any such intersection shall approach the intersection in the extreme left-hand lane lawfully available to traffic moving in the direction of travel of such vehicle and after entering the intersection the left turn shall be made so as to leave the intersection in the safest lane lawfully available to traffic moving in such direction upon the roadway being entered.

For the purpose of this section, each roadway of a boulevard shall be considered as an independent one-way street.

(Code 1956, § 38-75)

*State law reference—Required position and method of turning at intersections, R.S. 32:101.*

**Sec. 154-437. Position, signal for change of direction, starting and stopping.**

(a) No person shall turn a vehicle at an intersection, unless the vehicle is in proper position upon the roadway as required in section 154-436 or turn a vehicle to enter a private roadway or road or to otherwise turn a vehicle from a direct course or move right or left upon a roadway unless and until such movement can be made with reasonable safety, or without interfering with the right-of-way of the vehicles traveling lawfully in their proper lanes on the same street, or on intersecting streets.

(b) A signal of intention to turn right or left from the roadway shall be given continuously during not less than the last 100 feet travelled by the vehicle before turning.

(c) No person shall stop or suddenly decrease the speed of a vehicle without first giving the signal provided by law to the driver of any vehicle immediately to the rear when there is an opportunity to give such signal.

(Code 1956, § 38-76)

*State law reference—Turning movements and required signals, R.S. 32:104.*

§ 154-438

NEW ORLEANS CODE

laws.title: Improper starting or backing
laws.content:
(a) No person shall start a vehicle which is stopped, standing or parked unless and until such movement can be made with reasonable safety, or without interfering with the right-of-way of other vehicles travelling lawfully in adjacent or intersecting lanes of traffic.

(b) The driver of a vehicle shall not back it unless such movement can be made with reasonable safety or without interfering with the right-of-way of other vehicles travelling lawfully on the same street or intersecting streets, nor for a distance of over 60 feet, nor at a speed in excess of ten miles per hour.

(Code 1956, § 38-77)

*State law references—Moving parked vehicles, R.S. 32:103; limitations on backing, R.S. 32:281.*

laws.title: Signals by hand or arm or signal device
laws.content:
Any stop or turn signal when required in this division shall be given either by means of the hand and arm or by a signal lamp or mechanical device of the type as approved by the director of the state department of highways, but when a vehicle is so constructed or loaded that a hand and arm signal would not be visible both to the front and rear of such vehicle then such signal must be given by a lamp or signal device.

(Code 1956, § 38-78)

*State law reference—Signals by hand or arm or signal device, R.S. 32:105.*

laws.title: Method of giving hand and arm signals
laws.content:
(a) All signals required to be given by hand and arm shall be given from the left side of the vehicle in the following manner, and such signals shall indicate as follows:

(1) *Left turn.* Hand and arm extended horizontally, with the hand open and the back of the hand to the rear.

(2) *Right turn.* Hand and arm extended upward at an angle of 95 degrees from shoulder or elbow, with the hand open and the back of the hand to the rear. A bicyclist may also extend the right hand and arm horizontally with the hand open and back of the hand to the rear.

(3) *Stop, decrease speed or start.* Hand and arm extended downward at an angle of 45 degrees from shoulder or elbow, with the hand open and the back of hand to the rear.

(4) *Pulling from curb or side of highway.* The same as for left turn.

(b) A bicyclist is not required to continuously give the signals required by subsection (a) of this section if the hand or arm is needed to control the bicycle.

(Code 1956, § 38-79; M.C.S., Ord. No. 27365, § 4, 4-20-17)

*State law reference—Methods of giving hand and arm signals, R.S. 32:106.*

laws.title: Authority to place and obedience to turning markers
laws.content:
The city traffic engineer is hereby authorized to place markers, buttons or signs within or adjacent to intersections indicating the course to be travelled by vehicles turning at intersections and such course to be travelled as so indicated may conform to or be other than as prescribed by ordinance. When authorized markers, buttons or other indications are placed within an intersection indicating the course to be travelled by vehicles executing such turns, no driver of a vehicle shall disobey such indications.

(Code 1956, § 38-80)

laws.title: Authority to place restricted turn signs, obedience
laws.content:
(a) The city traffic engineer may determine those locations at which drivers of vehicles shall not make a right, left or "U" turn and shall place proper signs at such locations. The making of turns may be prohibited between certain hours of any day and permitted at other hours, in which event, such hours shall be plainly indicated on the signs or they may be removed when such turns are permitted.

Supp. No. 80

CD154:44.4
TRAFFIC AND VEHICLES

§ 154-483

(b) Whenever authorized signs are erected indicating that no right, left or "U" turn is permitted, no driver of a vehicle shall disobey the directions of any such sign.

(Code 1956, § 38-81)

laws.title: Limitations on turning around; use of storage lanes while turning
laws.content:
(a) The driver of any vehicle shall not turn such vehicle so as to proceed in the opposite direction upon any through street or upon any street in a business district other than a boulevard and shall not, upon any other street, so turn a vehicle unless such movement can be made in safety and without interfering with the right-of-way of approaching traffic either in opposing lanes or intersecting lanes of traffic.

(b) No vehicle shall be turned so as to proceed in the opposite direction upon any curve or upon the approach to or near the crest of a grade where such vehicle cannot be seen by the driver of any other vehicle approaching from either direction within 300 feet.

(c) At those intersections having storage lanes for turning movements, it shall be unlawful for the driver of any vehicle to turn any place other than through such storage lanes.

(Code 1956, § 38-82)

State law reference—Turning on curve or crest of grade prohibited, R.S. 32:102.

Secs. 154-444—154-480. Reserved.

laws.title: Vehicle obedience to yield signs
laws.content:
The driver or operator of a vehicle approaching a yield sign shall slow down to a speed reasonable for the existing conditions, or shall stop if necessary before entering the crosswalk on the near side of the intersection, or if there is no crosswalk, at a clearly marked stop line, but if none, then at a point nearest the intersecting roadway where the driver has a view of approaching traffic on the intersecting roadway. Having stopped or slowed in this manner, the driver shall yield the right-of-way to any pedestrian legally crossing the roadway on which he is driving, and to any vehicle in the intersection or approaching on another highway so closely as to constitute an immediate hazard.

(Code 1956, § 38-98)

State law reference—Stop signs and yield signs, R.S. 32:123.

laws.title: Vehicles entitled to right-of-way on certain intersecting streets
laws.content:
(a) Upon entering or crossing a boulevard from any street on which no traffic control sign or signal is erected, the driver of a vehicle or operator of a streetcar shall proceed cautiously, yielding to vehicles which are within the intersection or approaching so closely as to constitute an immediate hazard.

(b) The driver of a vehicle approaching an intersection shall yield the right-of-way to a vehicle which has entered the intersection from a different highway.

(c) When two vehicles enter an intersection from different highways at approximately the same time, the driver of the vehicle on the left shall yield the right-of-way to the vehicle on the right.

(d) The right-of-way rules declared in subsections (b) and (c) of this section are modified at through streets and otherwise as stated in this chapter.

(Code 1956, § 38-99)

State law reference—Vehicles approaching or entering intersection, R.S. 32:121.

laws.title: Vehicle emerging from an alley or private driveway to yield right-of-way
laws.content:
The driver of a vehicle emerging from any alley, driveway or building shall stop such vehicle immediately prior to driving onto a sidewalk or the sidewalk area extending across any alleyway, yielding the right-of-way to any pedestrian, and

Supp. No. 104

CD154:45
§ 154-483

NEW ORLEANS CODE

upon entering the roadway shall yield the right-of-way to all vehicles approaching on such roadway.

(Code 1956, § 38-100)

*State law reference—Similar provisions, R.S. 32:124.*

laws.title: Stop when traffic obstructed
laws.content:
No driver of a vehicle or operator of a streetcar shall enter an intersection or a crosswalk unless there is sufficient space on the other side of the intersection or crosswalk to accommodate the vehicle he is operating without obstructing the passage of other vehicles or pedestrians, notwithstanding any traffic control signal indication to proceed.

(Code 1956, § 38-101)

*State law reference—Stopping, standing or parking prohibited in specified areas, R.S. 32:143(3).*

laws.title: Overtaking and passing school bus
laws.content:
(a) The driver of a vehicle, upon meeting or overtaking from either direction, any school bus which has stopped on the roadway for the purpose of receiving or discharging any school children shall stop the vehicle before reaching such school bus, when there is in operation on such school bus a visual signal denoting same, and such driver shall not proceed until such school bus resumes motion or is signalled by the school bus driver to proceed, or the visual signals are no longer actuated.

(b) The driver of a vehicle upon a highway with separate roadways need not stop upon meeting or passing a school bus which is on a different roadway or when upon a controlled access highway and the school bus is stopped in a loading zone which is a part of or adjacent to such highway and where pedestrians are not permitted to cross the roadway.

(c) It shall be a violation of this section for any school bus driver to stop such bus for the purpose of receiving or discharging passengers without first actuating a visual signal denoting same.

(Code 1956, § 38-102)

*State law reference—Similar provisions, R.S. 32:80.*

laws.title: Obedience to signal indicating approach of railroad train
laws.content:
(a) Whenever any person driving a vehicle approaches a railroad grade crossing under any of the circumstances stated in this section, the driver of such vehicle shall stop not less than 15 feet from the nearest rail of such railroad and shall not proceed until he can do so safely. The foregoing requirements shall apply when:

(1) A clearly visible electrical or mechanical signal device gives warning of the immediate approach of a railroad train;

(2) A crossing gate is lowered or a human flagman gives or continues to give a signal of the approach or passage of a railroad train;

(3) A railroad train approaching within approximately 1,500 feet of the highway crossing emits a signal audible from such distance and such railroad train by reason of its speed or nearness to such crossing is an immediate hazard; or

(4) An approaching railroad train is plainly visible and is in hazardous proximity of such crossing.

(b) No person shall drive any vehicle through, around or under any crossing gate or barrier at a railroad grade crossing while such gate or barrier is closed or is being opened or closed.

(Code 1956, § 38-103)

*State law reference—Similar provisions, R.S. 32:171.*

laws.title: Operation of vehicles and streetcars on approach of authorized emergency vehicle
laws.content:
(a) Upon the immediate approach of an authorized emergency vehicle giving audible or visible signals, or in the case of a police vehicle, with an audible signal only:

(1) The driver of every other vehicle shall yield the right-of-way and shall immediately drive to a position parallel to, and as close as possible to, the right-hand edge or curb of the roadway clear of any intersection and shall stop and remain

Supp. No. 104

CD154:46

§ 154-535

in such position until the authorized emergency vehicle has passed, except when otherwise directed by a police officer; and

(2) The operator of every streetcar shall immediately stop such streetcar clear of any intersection and keep it in such a position until the authorized emergency vehicle has passed except when otherwise directed by a police officer.

(b) This section shall not operate to relieve the driver of an authorized emergency vehicle from the duty to drive with due regard for safety of all persons using the highway.

(Code 1956, § 38-22)

State law reference—Similar provisions, R.S. 32:125.

Secs. 154-488—154-530. Reserved.

laws.title: General limit
laws.content:
It shall be unlawful for the driver of any vehicle to exceed a speed limit of 25 miles per hour upon the streets of the city, except as provided in this article on through streets or upon boulevards or upon those streets or parts designated in section 154-533.

(Code 1956, § 38-73(a))

laws.title: Thirty, 35 mph speed zones
laws.content:
It shall be unlawful for the driver of any vehicle to exceed a speed limit of 30 miles per hour upon any through street designated in schedule II, section 154-1193, or for the driver of any vehicle to exceed a speed limit of 35 miles per hour upon any boulevard of the city except upon the streets or parts of streets designated in section 154-533.

(Code 1956, § 38-73(b))

laws.title: When not operative
laws.content:
The speed limits set out in sections 154-531 and 154-532 shall not be operative where otherwise posted by the traffic engineering division of the city and set out in schedule III, section 154-1194. Such speed limits shall also

not be operative on all urban extensions and state maintained highways within the city, where they shall be the same as the speeds posted and designated by the state department of highways.

(Code 1956, § 38-73(c))

laws.title: School zones
laws.content:
(a) Within the limits of all school zones where authorized signs designating them as school zones are posted at the entrance and exit of the school zone, and within 100 feet upon every designated approach to and within those intersections designated as "School Crossings" and where authorized signs designating such "School Crossings" are posted, it shall be unlawful for the driver of any vehicle to exceed a speed limit of 20 miles per hour one hour before and one hour after the beginning of a school day and one hour before and one hour after the end of a school day.

(b) When and where so designated by a traffic engineer, motorists shall be given proper warning by flashing beacons or other appropriate systems that the speed limit described in subsection (a) is being enforced.

(c) A traffic engineer shall ensure operability of all authorized flashing beacons erected as described in subsection (b), including that such beacons flash during the hours required by this section. If such flashing beacons are inoperable, or do not flash as intended, violations of this section shall not be enforced.

(d) This regulation shall only apply on school days during the specified time periods when children are in school.

(Code 1956, § 38-73(d); M.C.S., Ord. No. 24948, § 1, 7-12-12; M.C.S., Ord. No. 29369, § 1, 3-9-23; M.C.S., Ord. No. 30250, § 1, 3-13-25)

laws.title: Playground zones
laws.content:
The city traffic engineer shall erect caution signs in the vicinity of all playgrounds; he shall also mark whatever crosswalks in playground zones that he may deem necessary. Notwithstanding any other speed regulations of this article, no person shall drive a vehicle, while in a playground zone, at a speed greater than is reasonable and prudent under the conditions and having regard

Supp. No. 112

CD154:47
§ 154-535

NEW ORLEANS CODE

to the actual and potential hazards then existing. In every event, speed shall be so controlled as may be necessary to avoid colliding with any person, vehicle or other conveyance upon or entering a roadway.

(Code 1956, § 38-73(e))

**Sec. 154-536. Alleys.**

It shall be unlawful for the driver of any vehicle to exceed the speed of ten miles per hour in all public alleys.

(Code 1956, § 38-73(g))

**Sec. 154-537. Parks.**

It shall be unlawful for the driver of any vehicle to exceed the speed of 20 miles per hour on any roadway within the boundaries of any park in the city unless otherwise posted.

(Code 1956, § 38-73(i))

**Sec. 154-538. Lake Forest Boulevard.**

It shall be unlawful for the drivers of any vehicle to exceed a speed limit of 20 miles per hour upon Lake Forest Boulevard from Read Boulevard to Deer Park.

(Code 1956, § 38-73(l))

**Sec. 154-539. Minimum speed regulations—Generally.**

No person shall drive a motor vehicle at such a speed as to impede the normal and reasonable movement of traffic except when reduced speed is necessary for safe operation or in compliance with law. Where feasible and necessary the city traffic engineer may determine minimum speed limits applicable to certain streets, or portions of streets and such limits shall be binding on all drivers on such streets when signs are posted specifying such minimum speed limits.

(Code 1956, § 38-73(f))

**Sec. 154-540. Same—U.S. Highway 90 Business, hours.**

(a) It shall be unlawful for the driver of any vehicle to drive slower than 25 miles per hour on that section of U.S. Highway 90 Business (Greater New Orleans Mississippi River Bridge) between Camp Street and the West Bank Toll Plaza.

(b) This minimum speed limit shall apply only between the hours of 6:30 a.m. and 8:30 a.m. for east-bound traffic and only between the hours of 4:30 p.m. and 6:30 p.m. for west-bound traffic, excluding Saturdays and Sundays and those holidays which are specified elsewhere in this Code.

(Code 1956, § 38-73(j))

**Sec. 154-541. Trucks, tractors or trailers—Generally.**

It shall be unlawful for the driver of any truck, tractor or trailer, whose combined weight of body and load exceeds five tons, to exceed a speed limit of 15 miles per hour upon any undivided street or upon any divided street which has only one moving lane of traffic on each side of the median, provided that said 15 mile per hour speed limit shall not apply to any truck route designation in section 154-1561, nor shall it apply to any street over which regularly scheduled transit passenger service is provided, nor to any street on which prima facie speed limits exist in accordance with section 154-1194, schedule III, nor to any state and federal highway, nor to the driver of any vehicle on an emergency call involving public safety and welfare.

(Code 1956, § 38-73(h))

**Sec. 154-542. Same—Lake Forest Boulevard.**

It shall be unlawful for the drivers of any bus, truck, tractor or trailer, whose combined weight of body and load exceeds five tons, to exceed a speed limit of 20 miles per hour upon Lake Forest Boulevard, from Read Boulevard to Bullard Avenue.

(Code 1956, § 38-73(k))

**Sec. 154-543. Same—Berkley Drive.**

It shall be unlawful for the drivers of any bus, truck, tractor or trailer to exceed 20 miles per hour on that section of Berkley Drive between Kabel Drive and Simpson Place.

(Code 1956, § 38-73(m))

Supp. No. 112

CD154:48
TRAFFIC AND VEHICLES

§ 154-601

**Sec. 154-544. Prohibiting the use of radar detection units on certain city streets.**

(a) It shall be unlawful for any person to operate any device or mechanism to detect the emission of radio microwaves which are employed by police to measure the speed of motor vehicles for law enforcement purposes upon Louisiana Avenue between Tchoupitoulas Street and South Claiborne Avenue.

(b) It is unlawful to use such device or mechanism commonly known as "fuzz busters" upon any such motor vehicle on Louisiana Avenue between Tchoupitoulas Street and South Claiborne Avenue.

(c) The provisions of this section shall not apply to any receiver of radio waves utilized for lawful purposes to receive any signal from a frequency lawfully licensed by any state or federal agency.

(Code 1956, § 38-73.1)

*State law references—Power of local municipal authorities, R.S. 32:41; powers of local parish authorities, R.S. 32:42.*

**Sec. 154-545. Regulation of speed by traffic signals.**

The city traffic engineer may regulate the timing of traffic signals on any street so as to permit the movement of traffic in an orderly and safe manner at speeds slightly at variance from the speeds otherwise applicable on the streets or intersections and may erect appropriate signs giving notice thereof.

(Code 1956, § 38-74)

**Sec. 154-546. Maximum speed regulation; Warbler Street.**

It shall be unlawful for the driver of any vehicle to exceed a speed limit of 20 miles per hour upon Warbler Street.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 19,149, § 1, 3-31-99)

**Sec. 154-547. Neighborhood slow zones.**

(a) The city traffic engineer may establish neighborhood slow zones in which it shall be unlawful for the driver of any vehicle to exceed the speed limits posted by the traffic engineering division of the city and set out in schedule XII, section 154-1203.

(b) The traffic engineering division of the city shall erect signage at all entry points to a neighborhood slow zone with the zone’s posted speed limit.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 28495, § 1, 9-17-20)

**Secs. 154-548—154-600. Reserved.**

**ARTICLE VII. SPECIFIC STREET REGULATIONS***

**Sec. 154-601. Authority to designate one-way streets and alleys.**

(a) Whenever any law of the city designates any one-way street or alley, the city traffic engineer shall place and maintain signs giving notice thereof, and no such regulations shall be effective unless such signs are in place. Signs indicating the direction of lawful traffic movements shall be placed at every intersection where movement of traffic in the opposite direction is prohibited.

(b) The city traffic engineer is hereby authorized to, on the basis of engineering studies, and after notifying the superintendent of police, designate any street or portion thereof upon which vehicular traffic shall proceed in one direction during one period and the opposite direction during another period of the day, and shall place and maintain appropriate markings, signs, barriers or other devices as is necessary to give notice thereof. The city traffic engineer, after notifying the superintendent of police, may erect signs temporarily designating lanes to be used by traffic moving in a particular direction, regardless of the centerline of the roadway. It shall be unlawful for any person to operate any vehicle in violation of such markings, signs, barriers or other devices so placed in accordance with this section.

(Code 1956, § 38-93)

laws.title: Access to Canal Boulevard
laws.content:
Whenever the Orleans Levee Board Police finds it necessary to close the entrance to Lakeshore Drive at Canal Boulevard due to traffic congestion, the levee board police is hereby authorized to limit access to Canal Boulevard between Robert E. Lee Boulevard and Lakeshore Drive to local residents and to New Orleans Public Service buses by either placing a barricade which leaves one lane open for local traffic or by stationing an officer at this intersection to control said traffic.

(Code 1956, § 38-96.1)

laws.title: Vehicles and streetcars to stop at stop signs
laws.content:
When stop signs are erected at or near the entrance of any intersection, every driver of a vehicle and every operator of a streetcar shall stop such vehicle or streetcar before entering the crosswalk on the near side at a clearly marked stop line, but if none, then at the point nearest the intersecting roadway where the driver or operator has a view of approaching traffic on the intersecting roadway before entering the intersection. After having stopped, the driver or operator shall yield the right-of-way to all vehicles which have entered the intersection from another highway, or which are approaching so closely on such highway as to constitute an immediate hazard.

(Code 1956, § 38-97)

State law reference—Similar provisions, R.S. 32:123.

laws.title: Operation of miniature vehicles in Vieux Carre prohibited
laws.content:
(a) It shall be unlawful to rent or lease to operate in the Vieux Carre of the city any vehicle which is considered to be a "minivehicle" under the provisions of this section.

(b) A minivehicle for the purpose of this section is defined as follows:

(1) Any three- or four-wheeled vehicle which is or may be powered by gasoline, diesel or electric motor which has been constructed on a scale smaller than the size of the vehicle as originally manufactured and of which it is a miniature reproduction capable of transporting passengers;

(2) Any vehicles, having three or more wheels, bearing a seat, saddle or bench which is propelled or may be propelled by any variety of electromechanical or internal combustion powered means, excluding public utility vehicles and three- or more wheeled vehicles operated by ice cream vendors.

(c) For the purpose of this section, the Vieux Carre is that area bounded by Iberville Street, North Rampart Street, Esplanade Avenue and the Mississippi River.

(d) Whoever violates this section shall be guilty of a misdemeanor and shall be fined no more than $100.00, or imprisoned for not more than 30 days.

(Code 1956, § 38-114.1; M.C.S., Ord. No. 24115, § 1, 9-2-10)

laws.title: Vieux Carre malls
laws.content:
The portions of Royal and Bourbon Streets listed in this section shall be closed to vehicular traffic in accordance with the following provisions:

(1) *Royal Street Mall.* Royal Street shall be closed to vehicular traffic from the northern curb of Bienville Street to the southern curb of Orleans Street between the hours of 11:00 a.m. and 4:00 p.m. weekdays and 11:00 a.m. and 7:00 p.m. on Saturdays and Sundays.

(2) *Bourbon Street Mall.*

a. Bourbon Street, from the northern curb of Iberville Street to the southern curb of St. Ann Street, shall be closed to all vehicular traffic except delivery, freight, and service vehicles, as defined in this chapter, and taxicabs, as provided for in subsection c., during the hours commencing at 8:00 p.m. and continuing until 11:00 a.m. of each day, with the exception of New Year’s Day, Mardi Gras, and all other occasions declared by resolution of the city council. At those times, all vehicular traffic shall be prohibited at all hours of each day or as otherwise provided by resolution of the city council.

b. During the hours commencing at 6:00 a.m. and continuing until 4:00 p.m. of each day, delivery, freight, and service vehicles, as defined in this chapter, shall be permitted to exclusively park within the areas designated by appropriate signage erected and/or installed by the department of streets, consisting of the riverside curbs of the Bourbon Street Mall, as defined hereinabove. During these hours, all other vehicles shall be prohibited from parking or stopping in the Bourbon Street Mall.

c. Taxicabs that are either picking up or dropping off passengers in the 300 block of Bourbon Street will be permitted to enter the Bourbon Street Mall from 6:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.

(Code 1956, § 38-144.1; M.C.S., Ord. No. 17,161, § 1, 8-17-95)

Secs. 154-609—154-650. Reserved.

laws.title: Same—Powers, duties
Civil nature of parking and stopping violations
laws.content:
The civil regulation of parking and stopping (hereinafter sometimes referred to as "parking") shall be governed by this article. Any parking violation prohibited in this article shall be a civil violation only and no criminal penalty will be imposed for its commission. For purposes of this article, a parking violation is the violation of any provision of this article providing for or regulating the parking or stopping of a vehicle. Nothing contained in this article shall be construed to repeal, restrict or amend any other section of this chapter which other section shall continue to remain and remain in full force and effect as if this article had not been adopted.

(Code 1956, § 38-286)

laws.title: Parking citation forms
laws.content:
(a) The parking citation shall be the notice of violation for purposes of this article.

(b) The parking citation shall contain information concerning the nature, date, time, location of the alleged violation, the state vehicle license plate number, and make of car. In those cases where a license plate is not visible and/or legible, either the vehicle identification number or the

Supp. No. 45

§ 154-688

brake inspection tag number shall be in lieu of the state vehicle plate number. In the case of livery vehicles the certificates of public necessity and convenience number (CPNC) shall be in lieu of the state vehicle license plate number. In the case of overparking in a space regulated by a multispace pay station or single/double space parking meter, the parking citation shall contain the number of the meter at which the vehicle is overparked. The parking citation shall also contain information advising the person charged of the manner and time in which he may contest the violation charged in the notice. The parking citation shall also provide that a failure to timely answer or appear before a hearing examiner shall be considered a prima facie admission of the violation set forth in the parking citation, in which event the hearing examiner may assess the appropriate fine or fines and all penalties incidental thereto.

(Code 1956, § 38-286.4; M.C.S., Ord. No. 22035, § 2, 8-4-05)

**Sec. 154-688. Service of parking citations.**

(a) A parking citation shall be served personally upon the operator of a vehicle who is present at the time of service. If the operator is not so served, or is not present, the parking citation shall be served upon the registered owner of the vehicle by affixing the parking citation to the vehicle in a conspicuous place thereon. The original parking citation shall be signed by the issuing officer who shall affirm the truth of the facts set forth therein. An operator of a vehicle who is not the owner thereof, but who uses or operates the vehicle with permission of the owner, express or implied, shall be considered the agent of the owner to receive a parking citation required to be served upon the operator or registered owner of a vehicle in accordance with the provisions of this section.

(b) If the registered owner or operator of a vehicle drives the vehicle away from or in any manner leaves the site of the violation while the issuing officer is preparing the parking citation, or refuses service of the parking citation and drives away from or in any manner leaves the site of the

violation, this fact shall be duly noted on the original and all copies of the parking citation. This original and all copies of a parking citation shall constitute a business record of the city and shall constitute prima facie evidence that the parking citation was issued and that an attempt at service thereof was made in accordance with the provisions of this section.

(Code 1956, § 38-286.5)

laws.title: Citation as legal demand and prima facie evidence
laws.content:
The original parking citation or any true copy thereof shall constitute an ordinary business record of the city and prima facie evidence of the facts contained therein.

(Code 1956, § 38-286.7)

laws.title: Responsibility of owner and operator
laws.content:
(a) Except as provided in subsection (b) of this section, the owner and the operator, when not the same, shall be solidarily liable to the city for parking violations, unless the owner can prove that the vehicle was operated without his consent, express or implied. An owner who pays any parking fine, costs, or administrative fees pursuant to this article shall have the right to recover the same from the operator.

(b) An owner of a vehicle who is engaged in the business of renting or leasing vehicles under written rental or leasing agreements (“lessor”) shall not be liable for parking fines and penalties imposed by a local authority on the lessor of such rented or leased vehicles, if within 30 days after receiving written notice of the parking violation, the lessor provides, in affidavit form, the true name, address and driver’s license number and state of issuance of the person in possession of the vehicle (“lessee”) at the time of the issuance of the citation, or provides a true copy of the lease or rental agreement.

(c) A lessor who fails to comply with the foregoing provisions shall be treated as any other owner and shall be solidarily liable with the operator.

(d) If any owner of a motor vehicle receives a notice of violation for a period during which the illegally parked vehicle was reported to any police department as having been stolen, it shall be a valid defense to any charge of a parking violation that the motor vehicle has been reported to the police as stolen prior to the time the violation occurred and had not been recovered by such time. (Code 1956, § 38-286.8)

laws.title: Failure to answer parking citation, additional delinquent penalties
laws.content: If the owner, his agent or the operator fails to appear on or prior to the administrative hearing date, there shall be assessed additional delinquent penalties, as listed in section 154-699. (Code 1956, § 38-286.10)

laws.title: Notice of hearing
laws.content: The parking citation shall provide information as to the time and place of a hearing. Whenever a person charged with a parking violation denies liability with explanation, the parking administration bureau shall advise such person, personally or by U.S. mail postage prepaid, of the date of which he must appear to answer the charge at a hearing. The form and content of such hearing shall be prescribed by the chief administrative officer, and shall contain a warning to advise the person that failure to appear on the date designated, or on any subsequent date, to which the hearing is adjourned, shall be deemed an admission of liability. (Code 1956, § 38-286.11)

laws.title: Adjudication by mail
laws.content:
(a) In cases where a person charged with a parking violation shows good cause for not attending a hearing, either personally or through a representative, the hearing officer may permit the matter to be adjudicated by mail which adjudication shall be made within 60 days of the date of the citation. Letters, memoranda, affidavits, photographs or other documentary materials shall be admissible as evidence for the purposes of adjudications by mail. The hearing officer may exclude from consideration any material which is not relevant to the adjudication of the alleged violation. Failure of the person charged to proceed with an adjudication by mail after requesting and receiving permission to adjudicate by mail shall constitute an admission by the person charged of liability of the parking violation and shall subject the person who requested the adjudication by mail to the appropriate fines and costs assessed by the parking adjudication bureau.

(b) If a hearing examiner determines that an adjudication cannot proceed by mail, the parking adjudication bureau shall advise the person charged by first class mail that he must appear to answer the charge at a hearing. (Code 1956, § 38-286.12)

laws.title: Failure to appear at hearing, consequences
laws.content:
Failure to appear at a hearing other than the original hearing when required to appear shall constitute an admission of liability of the parking violation and shall subject the person charged with the violation herein to the appropriate fines and costs assessed by the parking adjudication bureau acting through a hearing examiner.

(Code 1956, § 38-286.14)

Rehearing.** (a) There shall be a review board within the parking adjudication bureau which shall consist of three hearing examiners, but in no event shall the hearing examiner whose decision is being reviewed be included in the panel determining such rehearing. (b) A request for rehearing following an original responsible disposition rendered by any hearing examiner shall be received within 30 days of such a disposition. After making such a request for a rehearing, and prior to the scheduling of the rehearing, the person shall be obligated to post a cash bond in the amount of the fines and/or fees for which the hearing examiner rendered a responsible disposition. If the original responsible disposition is reversed by the review board such bond shall be returned to the depositor. (c) A request for a rehearing shall not be accepted until such a cash bond has been deposited with the city. Any bond posted shall equal the amount due on the date the bond is received. (d) The review board shall have the power to review the fact and the law and shall have the power to affirm or reverse any original responsible deposition for error of fact or law. (Code 1956, § 38-286.16) **Sec. 154-701. Judicial review.** The decision of the review board shall be the final decision by the city. Any person aggrieved by any decision may file a petition for judicial review in the civil district court of the parish, within 30 days after the date of entry of the decision, pursuant to the provisions of R.S. 49:964. (Code 1956, § 38-286.17) **Sec. 154-702. Method of notice.** Any notice permitted or required to be given under this article shall be considered given when mailed by United States mail, postage prepaid, to the operator, if known, or to the registered owner at the address appearing on the registry of the office of motor vehicles of the department of safety and corrections, or to a lessee at the address provided by the lessor, or in the case of an out of state owner or operator, to such address as may be shown at the appropriate registration office. laws.title: Immobilization for unpaid parking fines and penalties; impoundment; procedure for release; hearing
laws.content:
(a) A vehicle against which three or more parking citations have been issued shall be immediately immobilized, or towed and impounded, or both, by any police officer or other person duly authorized where, for at least three parking citations issued to that vehicle, the vehicle owner:

(1) Having admitted liability for a parking offense, has failed to pay the fines and penalties assessed by the parking adjudication bureau; or,

(2) Having been found liable for the parking offense, has failed to pay the fines and penalties assessed by the parking adjudication bureau; or

(3) Has failed to contest or pay the fines/penalties and tow fee for a tow-related citation for which a ROR bond was posted.

(b) Such vehicle shall be surrendered or released only to the duly registered owner of such vehicle or his agent thereof upon:

(1) Payment of all outstanding fines and penalties assessed by the parking adjudication bureau recorded against such vehicle plus any towing, immobilization or storage fees; or

(2) Such person depositing a cash or surety bond in the amount of all outstanding fines and penalties assessed by the parking adjudication bureau recorded against such vehicle plus any towing, immobilization or storage fees.

(c) If a vehicle has been immobilized by means of a "self releasing boot" for unpaid parking fines and penalties as provided in subsection (a), the motorist will be allowed to remove the boot immediately upon payment of all outstanding fines and penalties due the city. The motorist must pay the balance of all unpaid parking fines along with the boot fee prior to receiving a code to unlock the boot. Any motorist who may need or desires assistance with removal of the "self releasing boot" may contact the immobilization office of the department of public works for assistance or to have the immobilization device removed.

Should the motorist choose to remove the boot, after receipt of the code to unlock the boot, the motorist will have 24 hours (excluding weekends and holidays) to return the boot to the immobilization office of the department of streets. If the boot has not been returned within 24 hours, the vehicle owner will be assessed a fine of $25.00 per day up to a maximum fine of $500.00.

(d) If the person whose vehicle has been immobilized or impounded deposits a bond as provided in subsection (b)(2), such person shall be issued a notice to appear for a hearing. The scope of the hearing provided under this section shall be limited to the determination as to whether the vehicle immobilized or booted belongs to the owner or his agent who failed to appear at a hearing when required to do so or, having admitted liability for a parking offense, has failed to pay the fines and penalties assessed by the parking adjudication bureau, or, having been found liable for the parking offense has failed to pay the fines and penalties assessed by the parking adjudication bureau. Any person whose vehicle has been impounded or immobilized under the provisions of this section and desires an

expedited hearing shall be afforded a hearing within three business days of his written request therefor.

(e) If a vehicle is immobilized for unpaid parking fines and penalties as provided in subsection (a), an immobilization fee as set forth in section 154-777 shall be assessed. If such fee is deposited in the form of a cash bond and the responsible person is found not liable for all parking fines and penalties for which his vehicle was immobilized, such bond will be returned to the depositor or his agent.

(f) If the vehicle impounded has not been reclaimed within 24 hours of the time of impoundment, the department of police shall notify the vehicle’s last owner of record (as determined by the license tags thereof) of the place of impoundment of the vehicle.

(g) If a person whose vehicle has been impounded or immobilized deposits a bond as provided in subsection (b)(2), such a bond will be subject to forfeiture if he fails to pay fines and/or penalties assessed by the parking adjudication bureau within six months after assessment.

laws.title: Damaging or removal of immobilization devices prohibited
laws.content:
It shall be unlawful and an offense for any person to release, deface, injure, tamper with, break, destroy, remove or impair the usefulness of or cause any person to release, deface, injure, tamper with, break, destroy, remove or impair the usefulness of any immobilization device which has been attached to a vehicle in accordance with the provisions of this chapter, with the exception of the authorized removal of a "self releasing boot" as provided in section 154-778.

(Code 1956, § 38-276; M.C.S., Ord. No. 23144, § 1, 7-10-08)

laws.title: Removal of immobilized vehicles prohibited
laws.content:
It shall be unlawful and an offense for any person to move or cause any person to move any vehicle, wherever immobilized, which has an immobilization device attached to it in accordance with the provisions of this chapter, with the exception of the authorized removal of a "self releasing boot" as provided in section 154-778.

(Code 1956, § 38-276.1; M.C.S., Ord. No. 23144, § 1, 7-10-08)

laws.title: Fines and fees imposed on vehicles involved in certain criminal offenses
laws.content:
All fines and fees assessed pursuant to this division, or otherwise imposed pursuant to section 162-1016 of this Code, shall be waived in circumstances where the immobilization, towing, or impoundment of a vehicle occurs as a result of any of the following crimes delineated in the Louisiana Criminal Code, as amended: R.S. 14:64 (armed robbery); R.S. 14:64.1 (first-degree robbery); R.S. 14:64.2 (carjacking); R.S. 14:64.4 (second-degree robbery); R.S. 14:67 (theft); R.S. 14:67.26 (theft of a motor vehicle); R.S. 14:68 (unauthorized use of a movable); or R.S. 14:69(B) (illegal possession of stolen things); and the Code of the City of New Orleans: section 54-186 (theft); section 54-187 (unauthorized use of movables); or section 54-188 (illegal possession of stolen things). A person seeking a waiver under this Section shall present evidence that the alleged crime was timely reported to the New Orleans Police Department or other appropriate law enforcement agency. The perpetrator or alleged perpetrator of a crime delineated in this section shall not be entitled to any abatement of fines or fees.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 28948, § 2, 2-17-22)

Secs. 154-782—154-810. Reserved.

laws.title: Abandoned vehicles—Sale or use
laws.content:
(a) The department of police or the department of streets shall retain custody and possession of all unclaimed motor vehicles for a period

(b) Vehicles the City chooses to use for City use must be retained a minimum of six months. An official request identifying the vehicle by VIN, make, and model, along with its intended use must be delivered to the Department of Public Works by the Superintendent of Police or the Chief Administrative Officer.

laws.title: Storage fee after sale
laws.content:
(a) Within six days after the consummation of the sale of unclaimed vehicles, the purchasers shall remove such vehicles from the police department's property or the department of public works' property, or shall be subject to storage fees as set forth in section 154-777.

(b) For the purpose of this section, the six-day period shall commence at 8:00 a.m. on the day after the consummation of the sale, and the storage fee shall commence at 4:00 p.m. on the sixth calendar day thereafter provided the sixth day does not fall on a Sunday or a holiday, in which case the storage fee shall not commence until the next legal day following.

(c) For the purpose of this section, the storage fee shall be imposed for any fraction of a day in excess of six days.

laws.title: Liability for storage fees
laws.content:

(Code 1956, § 38-301; M.C.S., Ord. No. 24313, § 1, 2-17-11)

laws.title: Sale to city employee prohibited

laws.title: Record of charges and sales

The department of police and the department of public works shall keep a complete record of all monies collected by it for storage and towing charges with details as to the date, the amount, and the name of the person making such payment, and shall also keep a true and correct record of all unclaimed or unidentified vehicles sold at public auction by virtue of this division. Such record shall be, at all times, open to public inspection.

(Code 1956, § 38-302; M.C.S., Ord. No. 23427, § 1, 3-19-09; M.C.S., Ord. No. 24315, § 1, 2-17-11)

laws.title: Penalty for false or fraudulent bidding

Any person, directly or through a third person, found guilty of furnishing false information or submitting one or more bids on vehicles sold at public auction by the city who does not have the funds to purchase such vehicle or made such bid for the purpose of delaying or disrupting such sales, shall be guilty of a misdemeanor and sentenced to serve no more than 90 days in jail, or fined $100.00, or both; provided further that each separate bid found to be false or fraudulent shall constitute a separate offense.

(Code 1956, § 38-303; M.C.S., Ord. No. 24316, § 1, 2-17-11)

laws.content:

laws.title: Lights on parked vehicles
laws.content:
(a) Whenever a vehicle is lawfully parked upon a street or highway during the hours between a half hour after sunset and a half hour

before sunrise and if there is sufficient light to reveal any person or object within a distance of 1,000 feet upon such street or highway, no lights need be displayed upon such parked vehicle.

(b) Whenever a vehicle is parked or stopped upon a roadway or shoulder adjacent thereto, whether attended or unattended, during the hours between a half hour after sunset and a half hour before sunrise and there is not sufficient light to reveal any person or object within a distance of 1,000 feet upon such highway, such vehicle so parked or stopped shall be equipped with one or more lamps meeting the following requirements:

laws.title: Parking in a loading zone, freight only, or freight zone
laws.content:
(a) No person shall stop or park a vehicle for any purpose or period of time, other than for the expeditious loading and unloading of merchandise, or necessary equipment, in any place signed as a loading, freight only, or freight zone (hereafter, loading zone). No vehicle shall remain in a loading zone when not actively loading or unloading unless the vehicle meets the definition of a delivery vehicle; and any vehicle that utilizes a loading zone shall do so for the primary purpose of transporting and delivering merchandise or necessary equipment.

(b) If a vehicle meets the definition of a delivery vehicle, it will be allowed to remain in the loading zone for 45 minutes. Taxicabs, when actually engaged in the transportation of merchandise, not passengers, will be allowed 25 minutes for the completion of the loading or unloading. This allotted time shall be used to complete the delivery of merchandise.

(c) Loading zones may be used for the expeditious receiving or discharging of passengers when such stopping does not interfere with a vehicle waiting to enter, entering or using such zones for the loading or unloading of merchandise. Freight handling and service truck zones shall be used as loading zones, freight only, or freight zones when loading or unloading merchandise or as a service zone when performing repair of service work.

(d) If a non-delivery vehicle is being utilized to deliver musical equipment in connection with a musical performance, the vehicle can utilize a loading zone with prior city authorization.

(1) City authorization shall be in the form of a "musician loading/unloading parking permit", and the permit shall be issued to a location only if the business is permitted by the CZO to have live music on-site. Permits will be issued at the request of the business to the department of safety and permits.

a. The "musician loading/unloading parking permit" shall provide the business' name and address, the location of the loading zone that is authorized for use, and permit number.

b. The permit shall be displayed on the windshield of the vehicle utilizing the loading zone during the loading and unloading of musical equipment.

c. The vehicle can utilize the loading zone for up to one hour before and after the scheduled musical performance, but in no event shall any such vehicle remain in a loading zone for more than 15 minutes.

(2) Each approved business location shall be issued two "musician loading/unloading parking permits". "Musician loading/unloading parking permits" are non-transferable and shall become void if the business location ceases musical performances.

(Code 1956, § 38-286.22; M.C.S., Ord. No. 28091, § 1, 5-23-19)

laws.title: Parking in a service zone
laws.content:
(a) No person shall stop or park a vehicle for any purpose or period of time, other than for the expeditious completion of repair or service work in any place signed as a service zone. No vehicle shall use a service zone unless it meets the definition of a service or equipment vehicle.

(b) If a vehicle meets the definition of a service vehicle, it will be allowed to remain in a service zone for a maximum of one hour.

(c) If a vehicle meets the definition of an equipment vehicle, it will be allowed to remain in the service zone until the repair work is completed.

(d) At the discretion of the parking administrator, service zones may be in effect on a limited basis as indicated by signs.

(e) A service zone may be used for the expeditious receiving or discharging of passengers when such stopping does not interfere with a vehicle waiting to enter, entering or using such zone for the performance of repair or service work.

(Code 1956, § 38-286.23)

laws.title: Designation of emergency ambulance parking zones
laws.content:
(a) The parking division may, upon request, install signs for emergency ambulance parking zones at hospitals. These zones shall be occupied by emergency treatment vehicles. The vehicles shall be designed with the equipment necessary to care for patients requiring nonambulatory transport. These vehicles shall have either public or commercial license plates, as well as the name and/or emblem of the department or company providing such service.

(b) Vehicles designed for nonambulatory transport will be allowed to remain in such zone for the period of time necessary to attend to the details of the patient's treatment and/or admission to the hospital.

(Code 1956, § 38-286.25)

laws.title: Parking of buses, livery vehicles and taxicabs
laws.content:
(a) The driver of a sightseeing bus, livery vehicle or taxicab shall not park upon any street during the hours of 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. in the central business district at any place other than a bus stand, a livery stand or a taxicab stand, respectively, except that these provisions shall not prevent the driver of any such vehicle from temporarily parking in accordance with other parking regulations at any place for the purpose of and while actually engaged in loading or unloading passengers. It shall be unlawful for the driver of any taxicab to park in any designated taxicab stand for a period of more than one hour. It shall be unlawful for the operator of any bus to park in any designated bus stand for a period of more than one-half hour.

(b) It shall be lawful for the driver of any taxicab to park in any metered space upon any street during the hours of 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. in the central business district and Vieux Carré, defined for the purposes of this section as the area from the Mississippi River to Claiborne Avenue and from Howard Avenue to Esplanade Avenue. Upon entering such parking space, the driver shall immediately make a payment for the use of the space by depositing the specified amount of legal tender of the United States or by

No taxicab shall park within 60 feet of any hotel taxi stand or zone when the legal parking spaces are metered spaces. **Sec. 154-873. Restricted use of veterinary parking zones.**

No person shall stop or park a vehicle in a veterinary parking zone for any purpose or period of time, other than the time required for the emergency treatment of any animal within the veterinary hospital or clinic. Such allowed parking time shall not exceed 30 minutes.

(Code 1956, § 38-286.27)

**Sec. 154-874. Restricted areas of parking spaces for registered individuals with disabilities.**

(a) No person shall stop or park a vehicle in an appropriately signed parking space for persons with disabilities except those vehicles bearing (i) a handicapped license plate, a disabled veteran license plate, handicapped parking card issued by the state, or parking card bearing the international symbol of accessibility prominently displayed on the dashboard of the driver's side of the vehicle issued pursuant to R.S. 47:463.4 or 467.463.4.1, or; (ii) a vehicle registered in another state and bearing that state's official designation for the handicapped, or; (iii) removable windshield placards, temporary removable windshield placards and special license plates which have been issued by issuing authorities of other countries, for the purpose of identifying vehicles permitted to utilize parking spaces reserved for persons with disabilities for any person with disabilities who is temporarily in this state and

who is not required to obtain Louisiana license plates. This will include appropriately signed parking spaces on any street, publicly owned and operated parking facilities, public facilities or public facilities for accommodation, and privately owned parking facilities subject to the provisions of the Americans with Disabilities Act. For the purpose of this section, a "public facility" and "public facility for accommodation" shall also include parking spaces belonging to privately owned parking areas covered by the Americans with Disabilities Act.

(b) Any person who uses any appropriately signed parking spaces for persons with disabilities shall be in violation of this section if the vehicle was not used for the transportation of the person for whom the license plate or parking card specified in paragraph (a) of this section was issued.

(c) When a motor vehicle bearing plates or displaying a hang tag issued to a mobility-impaired person or person with disabilities is being operated for the transport of the mobility-impaired person or person with disabilities, the motor vehicle may be parked for up to a maximum of three hours without payment, regardless of meter fares otherwise applicable to the parking space. This provision shall apply except where ordinances or police regulations prohibit parking on a highway for the purpose of creating a fire lane or where the ordinances or police regulations provide for the accommodation of heavy traffic during morning, afternoon, or evening hours or where the motor vehicle is parked in such a manner as to clearly be a traffic hazard.

(d) This section may be enforced by any person, duly authorized by the director of public works or the superintendent of police.

(e) Any person who violates the provisions of this section shall be fined $500.00. In addition to such fine, the offender shall be required to pay all court costs plus all towing fees and storage costs, if any.

(Code 1956, § 38-286.28; M.C.S., Ord. No. 18,534, § 1, 11-25-97; M.C.S., Ord. No. 21876, § 1, 3-17-05; M.C.S., Ord. No. 26070, § 1, 10-2-14)

Such facilities may include, but are not limited to, permitted truck stops, truck wash facilities, RTA storage facilities, vehicle repair facilities, or similar uses.

(e) It shall be unlawful for any commercial bus to stop, stand, or park, even momentarily, on St. Charles Avenue between Jackson Avenue and Louisiana Avenue except when necessary to avoid conflict with other traffic, in compliance with a law enforcement officer's direction, or in compliance with a law enforcement officer's direction, or in compliance with a traffic control sign or device. It shall be a violation of this section for any commercial bus to stop in a bus loading area when not actively engaged in passenger loading and unloading. Passenger loading and unloading shall not exceed the time indicated on the signs.

(f) Enforcement.

Furthermore, when an individual found to be in violation of these provisions refuses a request by a duly authorized person to move the vehicle found in violation, the officer shall be authorized to have such vehicle towed or booted.

(2) The citation shall contain information concerning the nature, date, time, and location of the alleged violation, the state vehicle license plate number, and the make of vehicle. The citation shall also contain information advising the person charged of the manner and the time in which he may contest the violation charged in the citation. The citation shall also provide that a failure to timely answer or appear before a court of competent jurisdiction shall be considered a prima facie admission of the violation set forth in the citation, in which the court may assess the appropriate fine or fines and all penalties incidental thereto.

laws.title: Storage and transportation of hazardous materials
laws.content:
(a) [Purpose.] The purpose of this section is to prohibit and/or restrict the transportation by roadway, storage, and use of certain hazardous materials as defined by the United States Department of Transportation within the city limits of New Orleans.

(b) Definitions—Generally. The following definitions have been abstracted in order to aid and clarify wording used throughout this section:

*Alley.* A narrow street; especially a thoroughfare through the middle of a block giving access to the rear of lots or buildings.

*Assembly.* A building used, in whole or in part, for the gathering together of persons for such purposes as deliberation, worship, entertainment, amusement, or awaiting transportation.

*Avenue.* The principal walk or driveway to a house situated off a main road. A broad passageway bordered by trees. An often-broad street or road.

*Institution.* A building in which persons are harbored to receive medical, charitable, or other care or treatment, or in which persons are held or detained by reasons of public or civic duty, or for correctional purposes.

*Parking lot.* An area used for the parking of motor vehicles (public or parking area).

*Pressure vessel.* When used in connection with liquefied petroleum gases shall mean any tank or vessel in which liquefied petroleum gases are stored or transported or in which liquefied petroleum gases are placed for utilization through a liquefied petroleum gas system.

*Residential.* A detached part of whole of a building occupied exclusively as a family dwelling place and the usual accessory occupancies.

*Street.* A thoroughfare, especially in a city, town, or village that is wider than an alley or lane and that usually includes sidewalks. The part of a street reserved for vehicles. A thoroughfare with abutting property.
TRAFFIC AND VEHICLES

§ 154.925.1

Tanker, containerized vehicle and container. Any vehicle other than railroad tank cars and boats, with cargo tank mounted thereon or built as an integral part thereof, used for the transportation of hazardous material/flammable liquids. Tank vehicles include self-propelled vehicles, full trailers and semitrailers without motor power and with wheels carrying either part or all of the load.

(c) Classes of hazardous material. The following definitions have been abstracted from the Code of Federal Regulations, Title 49—Transportation, and shall apply to the eight classes of hazardous material as defined by the United States Department of Transportation mentioned herewith:

Class I.

Class A explosive. Detonating or otherwise of maximum hazard. The nine of (sic) class A explosives are defined in section 173.53.

Class B explosive. In general, functions by rapid combustion rather than detonation and includes some explosive devices such as special fireworks, flash powders, etc. Flammable hazard. (Section 173.88)

Class C explosive. Certain types of manufactured articles containing class A or class B explosives, or both, as components but in restricted quantities, and certain types of fireworks. Minimum hazard. (Section 173.100)

Blasting agent. A material designed for blasting which has been tested in accordance with section 173.114a(b) and found to be so insensitive that there is very little probability of accidental initiation to explosion or of transition from deflagration to detonation. (Section 173.144a(a))

Class II.

Flammable gas. Any compressed gas meeting the requirements for lower flammability limit, flammability limit range, flame projection, or flame propagation criterial gas specified in section 173.300(b).

Nonflammable gas. Any compressed gas other than a flammable compressed gas.

Poison A—Extremely dangerous poisons. Poisonous gases or liquids of such nature that a very small amount of the gas, or vapor of the liquid, mixed with air, is dangerous to life. (Section 173.326)

Class III.

Combustible liquid. Any liquid having a flash point above 100 degrees Fahrenheit and below 200 degrees Fahrenheit as determined by tests listed in section 173.115(d). Exceptions are found in section 173.115(b).

Flammable liquid. Any liquid having a flash point below 100 degrees Fahrenheit as determined by tests listed in section 173.115(d). For exceptions see section 173.115(a).

Class IV.

Flammable solid. Any solid material, other than an explosive, which is liable to cause fires through friction, retained heat from manufacturing or processing, or which can be ignited readily and when ignited burns so vigorously and persistently as to create a serious transportation hazard. (Section 173.150)

Class V.

Organic peroxide. An organic compound containing the bivalent-0-0 structure and which may be considered a derivative of hydrogen peroxide where one or more of the hydrogen atoms have been replaced by organic radicals must be classed as an organic peroxide unless—(See Section 173.151(a) for details).

Oxidizer. A substance such as chlorate, permanganate, inorganic peroxide, or a nitrate, that yields oxygen readily to stimulate the combustion of organic matter. (See Section 173.151)

Class VI.

Poison A—Extremely dangerous poisons. Poisonous gases or liquids of such nature

Supp. No. 95

CD154:72.1
§ 154.925.1

NEW ORLEANS CODE

that a very small amount of the gas, or vapor of the liquid, mixed with air, is dangerous to life. (Section 173.326)

**Poison B—Less dangerous poisons.** Substances, liquids, solids (including pastes and semisolids), other than class A or irritating materials, which are known to be so toxic to man as to afford a hazard to health during transportation; or which, in the absence of adequate data on human toxicity, are presumed to be toxic to man. (Section 173.343)

**Irritating material.** A liquid or solid substance, which upon contact with fire or when exposed to air gives off dangerous or intensely irritating fumes, but not including any poisonous material, Class A.

**Class VII.**

**Radioactive material.** Any material, or combination of materials, that spontaneously emits ionizing radiation, and having a specific activity greater than 0.002 microcuries per gram. (Section 173.389) Note: See Section 173.389(a) through (1) for details.

**Class VIII.**

**Corrosive material.** Any liquid or solid that causes visible destruction of human skin tissue or a liquid that has a severe corrosion rate on steel. (See Section 173.240(a) and (b) for details).

(d) Regulations governing transportation, storage and use of hazardous material. It shall be unlawful for any tank motor vehicle or containerized motor carrier to park in any residential zoning district. It shall be unlawful for any tank motor vehicle or containerized motor carrier to be left unattended on any street, highway, from necessary absence from a vehicle or the vehicle is in connection with delivery of materials, except during the actual discharge of any liquid, bulk, gas, or those eight hazardous materials as defined by the United States Department of Transportation. A representative or responsible person shall be present with the vehicle. This provision shall not prevent stops for meals during the day or night, provided that streets or parking area is well lighted at the point of parking.

(1) No tank motor vehicle, containerized motor carrier or pressure vessel containing any of the eight classes of hazardous material as defined by the United States Department of Transportation shall be parked out of doors at any point longer than one hour.

(2) No tank motor vehicle, containerized motor carrier or pressure vessel containing any of the eight classes of hazardous material as defined by the United States Department of Transportation shall at any time be parked within 100 feet of any building used for assembly, institutional, or residential occupancy.

(3) No tank motor vehicle, containerized motor carrier or pressure vessel containing any of the eight classes of hazardous material as defined by the United States Department of Transportation shall be parked or garaged in any area not specifically zoned and approved by the New Orleans City Council, Department of Public Works, Fire Department, Police Department, and hazardous material personnel.

(4) All roadway vehicles shall use only established and designated authorized routes within the city limits. No carrier shall enter or drive in a residential zoning district except on an established and designated authorized route.

(5) Parking lots as defined by this section shall mean parking areas.

(6) Carriers shall adequately maintain vehicles to provide maximum safety and efficiency level for travel.

(7) Carriers shall provide notice to the fire department and police department whenever a hazardous material is released into the atmosphere, when there is an accident of any kind, or a potential problem which may bring about problems throughout the area.

(8) Carriers shall provide prior and advance notice to the fire department and police department whenever explosives are transported or stored throughout the city.

(9) Carriers will reduce speed in areas of hazardous roadway or congested areas when carrying any of the eight classes of hazardous material as defined by the United States Department of Transportation within the corporate limits of the city and 2,000 feet beyond in either direction.

(10) Carriers containing any of the eight classes of hazardous material as defined by the United States Department of Transportation shall be properly marked when traveling through, stored in, or involved within the city limits.

(11) The cost [of] cleanup, restoration, and any other cost incurred by the government relative to any of the eight classes of hazardous material as defined by the United States Department of Transportation within the city limits, and which are brought about by accidents or any other malfunction of the carrier vessel, shall be borne by the applicable carrier.

(12) The responsible company which owns or operates any vehicle or container which must be repaired, towed, altered, removed or stored in order to correct a situation which is deemed unsafe or is in violation of this section by the police department, fire department, or the public works department, shall be required to reimburse the city for the cost of said action.

laws.title: Parking or stopping prohibited at all times; license plate and brake tag requirements
laws.content:
(a) No person shall stop or park a motor vehicle on any street, sidewalk or neutral ground unless the motor vehicle is visibly equipped with a current, valid license plate or temporary registration from the state or a foreign state.

(b) No person shall stop or park a motor vehicle on any street, sidewalk, neutral ground, or any other public place if the motor vehicle is equipped with a license plate which is mutilated, defaced, damaged, or obscured in such a manner that the letters, numerals, and expiration dates are not legible.

(c) If a motor vehicle bears a license plate from the state, no person shall stop or park the motor vehicle on any street, sidewalk or neutral ground, unless the vehicle displays a current safety inspection certificate (brake tag) issued by a municipality or parish of the state or by the state or its agents. The lack of a safety inspection certificate (brake tag) on a motor vehicle equipped with a current, valid, temporary registration from the state shall not constitute a violation of this section.

(d) Self-propelled motor cranes, bulldozers, tractors, and similar equipment used for construction are exempt from the provisions of this section.

(e) Any ticket, summons, citation, or affidavit issued pursuant to this section shall be dismissed by the parking adjudication bureau if the owner of the vehicle submits to the parking adjudication bureau a valid motor vehicle registration for the vehicle to which the ticket, summons, citation, or affidavit was issued indicating that there existed a valid license plate or temporary registration as of the date of issuance of the ticket, summons, citation or affidavit, that the license plate or temporary registration was reported stolen and a police item number obtained, and that application for a new temporary registration or license plate has been submitted to the appropriate licensing authority, and if applicable, a valid receipt for a safety inspection sticker indicating that the vehicle possessed a current inspection sticker on the date of the issuance of the ticket, summons, citation, or affidavit.

(f) Any ticket, summons, citation, or affidavit issued pursuant to this section shall be dismissed by the parking adjudication bureau if the owner of the vehicle submits to the parking adjudication bureau adequate proof indicating that the vehicle to which the ticket, summons, citation or affidavit was issued was parked on the street within the boundaries of the property line (extended to the street) of the residence of the owner of the vehicle and on the same side of the street as the residence of the owner of the vehicle.

(g) For the purposes of this section, a vehicle is "equipped with" or "displays" a license plate, temporary registration, or safety inspection certificate (brake tag) only if the license plate, temporary registration, or safety inspection certificate is readily visible to a person standing outside the vehicle and only if the placement of the license plate, temporary registration, or inspection certificate complies with all applicable requirements of law.

(h) Nothing contained in this section shall be construed to authorize or permit parking or stopping on any street, sidewalk, neutral ground, or other public place if such parking or stopping is otherwise prohibited by law or ordinance.

(i) No person shall be fined or punished for a first offense violation of this section and no person shall be fined or punished for a second or subsequent violation of this section unless a period of at least 30 days shall have passed between receipt of the citation for a first offense and receipt of a citation for a second or subsequent violation of this section.

**Sec. 154-983. Restriction on stopping by buses.**
