laws.title: Illegal parking upon neutral ground, public playground, pedestrian mall or Lafitte Greenway
laws.content:
(a) No person shall stop or park a vehicle or other conveyance, except when necessary to avoid conflict with other traffic or in compliance with the law or directions of a police officer or traffic control device, at any of the following places:

(1) Upon a neutral ground other than those designated and operated as parking facilities.

(2) Upon any area of city-owned property formally dedicated, recognized and maintained as a playground by the city recreation department, not specifically designated for parking and interfering with the designed purpose of the playground.

(3) Upon any area of city-owned property formally dedicated or recognized and maintained as a pedestrian mall, not specifically designated for parking and interfering with the designed purpose of the pedestrian mall.

(b) No person shall move a vehicle not lawfully under his control into any such prohibited area or away from a curb such distance as is prohibited.

(c) No person shall park or leave standing any vehicle or other conveyance, whether attended or unattended, upon the Lafitte Greenway, the 2.6-mile trail and green corridor spanning from the intersection of North Alexander and St. Louis Streets to Basin Street and Lafitte Avenue.

(Code 1956, §§ 38-239.1, 38-286.48; M.C.S., Ord. No. 27429, § 1, 6-15-17)

laws.title: Parking prohibited on sidewalks in Vieux Carré area
laws.content:

(b) Stopping, standing or parking within the 300 block of Exchange Place shall be permitted only for delivery vehicles for a short-term period not greater than 30 minutes and only while such vehicles are being used for the loading or unloading of merchandise. A violation of the prohibition against stopping, standing or parking within the 300 block of Exchange Place for other vehicles shall carry the same penalty as that for other violations of this section.

(Code 1956, §§ 38-239.3, 38-286.49; M.C.S., Ord. No. 23426, § 1, 3-19-09)

**Sec. 154-1037. Parking of vehicles equipped with living accommodations prohibited during certain hours.**

(a) No person shall park a vehicle which is equipped with living accommodations with an overall length in excess of 22 feet on any street between the hours of 7:00 p.m. and 7:00 a.m. Any citations issued under this section and resulting administrative proceedings shall be dismissed upon receipt of written notification from the vehicle’s owner or lessee and verification by the parking division of the department of public works that the vehicle was legally registered or leased to an individual who resides in the same block in which the vehicle was parked when the citation was issued for apparent violation of this section.

(3) Lavatories.

(4) Mattresses.

(7) Refrigerators.

The city traffic engineer may determine when parking may be permitted upon the left-hand side of any such one-way roadway and erect signs giving notice thereof.

laws.title: Installation of single/double parking meters, multispace pay stations, or OPS
laws.content:
Single/double-space parking meters shall be placed upon the curb, sidewalk or neutral ground alongside of or next to individual parking places to be determined and designated by the director of the department of public works. Each single/ double parking meter shall so set as to show or display a signal that the metered space alongside of it is or is not in use.

Multispace pay stations shall be installed upon the curb or adjacent sidewalk in city blocks where metered spaces are to be regulated, in such specific locations as determined and designated by the director of the department of public works.

OPS shall have installations that vary with service type. For pay-by-phone parking, signage shall be installed at two locations within each half block, in a manner and of sufficient size such that the pay-by-phone access phone number, SMS short code and/or payment URL and unique location number are visible and readable by drivers from any vantage point within the half block. Additionally, where multispace or single/ double-space parking meters are present, decals denoting the pay-by-phone phone number, SMS short code and/or payment URL and unique location number shall be installed on both street and sidewalk facing sides. (M.C.S., Ord. No; 23215, § 1, 9-11-08)

laws.title: Single/double-space parking meter, multispace pay station or OPS operation
laws.content:
(a) Each single/double-space parking meter or multispace pay station shall be so set as to display a signal to indicate the parking time allowed upon the payment for use of the space by depositing the specified amount of legal tender of the United States or by using a credit card, debit card, smart card or token; as acceptable to the particular regulating device, in such single/double- space parking meter or multispace pay station, as the case may be, for the part of the street upon which the single/double-space parking meter or multispace pay station is placed.

(b) Each single/double-space parking meter or multispace pay station shall be so arranged that upon the expiration of such parking limit, it will indicate at what time the lawful parking period expires.

(c) The OPS shall indicate to the customer by voice, text message, email, web or other online means the parking time allowed for the selected location upon payment for use of the space. Payment for OPS transactions shall be made by credit card, debit card, prepaid account or other electronic payment mechanism.

(d) The OPS shall provide data for enforcement in real time, via wired or wireless networks, such that parking operations staff may identify separately those locations that are currently paid by OPS means and those that are not. (M.C.S., Ord. No. 23215, § 1, 9-11-08)

Claiborne Avenue to N. Claiborne Avenue to Elysian Fields to the River, including both sides of all streets listed, where the charge shall be $70.00, or $35.00 for an event sponsored by a nonprofit, per diem, in addition to the $45.00 fixed fee. Temporary use is defined as the time period posted on the single/double-space parking meter, multispace pay stations, or OPS. Temporary use of curb space controlled by

single/double space parking meters or multi-space pay stations or OPS shall not permit a user to disregard other regulations posted in the area. For purposes of this section, the term "nonprofit" shall mean an organization that is exempt from federal income tax under Section 501(c) of the Internal Revenue Code, is a Louisiana nonprofit corporation in good standing with an Employer Identification Number issued by the Internal Revenue Service, or is a school operated by the Orleans Parish School Board or Recovery School District. These fees shall be nonrefundable and shall not be waived.

Upon receipt of an application and payment for such rentals the department of public works, or its representative, will appropriately display notice of such rental. In the case of a space(s) regulated by a multispace pay station, single/double space parking meters or OPS, the department of public works, or its representative, will appropriately display a notice of such rental on the physical barriers used to indicate the space(s) being rented. If the department of public works determines that the single/double space parking meter(s) or the multispace pay station(s), or installed OPS signs will hamper the work to be performed by the user or the possibility of damage to the single/double space parking meter, multi-space pay station or OPS signs exists, then the department of public works, or its representative will remove the applicable single/double space parking meter(s), multispace pay station(s) and OPS signage and install "no parking" signs to indicate the space(s) have been rented. For this service a fee of $305.00 will be imposed, in addition to the per diem rates.

Acceptance of an application for the use of curb space occupied by single/double-space parking meters, multispace pay stations or OPS signage shall be limited to a maximum of 90 days. If this period is not sufficient, the user must request renewal of the application at least five working days before the expiration date of the original application. If an extension is requested within less than five working days of the expiration of the original application, a new application must be initiated, and payment of the fixed fees of $45.00 and $305.00 will be required.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 23215, § 1, 9-11-08; M.C.S., Ord. No. 23428, § 1, 3-19-09; M.C.S., Ord. No. 23818, § 1, 12-1-09; M.C.S., Ord. No. 26786, § 1, 2-4-16; M.C.S., Ord. No. 27266, § 1, 1-26-17)

laws.title: Duty to make payment prerequisite to use of space
laws.content:
When any vehicle is parked in any legal parking space which is a metered space, the owner, operator, manager or driver of such vehicle shall, upon entering such parking space, immediately make the specified payment in the single/double-space parking meter or multispace pay station, or by use of an OPS, as is applicable, by using either legal tender of the United States or by using a credit card, debit card, smart card or token, prepaid account or other electronic means as is acceptable to the particular device being used to regulate such parking space. Upon making such payment, the metered space regulated by the device to which payment was made may be used by such vehicle during the parking limit provided, for the part of the street in which the parking space is located.

(a) Any field representative of a department of city government when engaged in official business who displays a valid field representative parking permit on the inside of the vehicle on the right side of the rear windshield (rear windshield of the passenger side), or whose vehicle license plate is registered as a valid field representative in the OPS, while parking in any metered zone described below, shall not be required to deposit a coin or be charged via OPS for the use of the parking space for that period of time during which he is actually on official duty; provided, however, that no such vehicle shall be parked in the same space for more than four consecutive hours. **Sec. 154-1093. Use by mobility-impaired/disabilities.**

When a motor vehicle bearing a plate or displaying a hang tag or a special parking card issued to a mobility-impaired person or person with disabilities in conformance with state regulations is being operated for the transport of the mobility-impaired person or person with disabilities, the motor vehicle may be parked for a period of up to a maximum of three hours without payment, regardless of meter fares otherwise applicable to the parking space. This provision shall apply except as restricted or prohibited by ordinance, or where parking is prohibited by ordinance or police on a roadway for the purpose of creating a fire lane or for the accommodation of heavy traffic during morning, afternoon, or evening hours or where the motor vehicle is parked in such a manner as to clearly be a traffic hazard.

The city shall recognize hang tags, special parking cards, or other removable windshield placards and special license plates which have been issued by authorities of other states and countries for the purpose of identifying vehicles transporting a mobility-impaired person or person with disabilities. Additionally, special registration of the vehicle license shall be recognized in the OPS.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 23215, § 1, 9-11-08; M.C.S., Ord. No. 26070, § 2, 10-2-14)

**Sec. 154-1094. Direction of parking.**

Any vehicle parked in any parking space regulated by a single/double-space parking meter shall be parked with the bumper of such vehicle alongside of or next to the single/double-space parking meter alongside of or adjacent to the parking space in parallel parking spaces, and with the center and front of the vehicle directed at the single/double space parking meter in diagonal parking spaces.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 23215, § 1, 9-11-08)

**Sec. 154-1095. Marking of spaces to be observed.**

The director of the department of public works may cause to be placed lines or marks on the curb or on the street to designate the physical limits of a metered space. Each vehicle parked in any metered space so demarcated shall park within the lines or markings so established. No person shall park any vehicle across any such line or mark or park a vehicle in such a way that it shall not be within the area so designated by such lines or markings, except in the event a vehicle may be longer than the space allotted, and in such case, the driver of any vehicle occupying more than one space or any part of an additional space shall make a payment for each metered space, or any portion of a metered space, being occupied, and such driver shall be deemed to be in violation of any one of the single/double space parking meters whose space is occupied shows a violation.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 23215, § 1, 9-11-08)

**Sec. 154-1096. Use of proceeds.**

The payment made by depositing the specified amount of legal tender of the United States or by using an OPS, a credit card, debit card, smart card or token as is acceptable to the particular regulating device as provided in this division are hereby levied as policy regulations and inspection fees to cover the cost of inspection and regulation involved in inspection, installation, operation, control and use of the parking spaces and single/double space parking meters, multi-space pay stations and OPS described herein, and involved in checking and regulating the

laws.title: Residential Permit Parking Program
laws.content:
**Sec. 154-1136. Definitions.** The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this division, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning: *Motor vehicle* means an auto, truck, motorcycle or other motor-driven form of transportation with a gross weight of less than 6,000 pounds. *Primarily residential* means 50 percent of the ground level space is residential property. *Resident* means an individual(s) domiciled and living in a residential property. For purposes of this definition domiciled means (1) a fixed residence in a residential permit parking zone, (2) which is the resident’s primary and habitual residence (whereby the resident lives the majority of the year) and (3) the resident has the intention to remain there permanently or indefinitely. *Resident motor vehicle* means a registered motor vehicle owned or leased by a resident of the residential permit parking area and registered at his or her address within the residential parking permit area. *Residential area* means the contiguous or nearly contiguous area containing public streets and highways or parts thereof, the zoning of which is residential as provided in the Comprehensive Zoning Ordinance. *Residential permit parking zone* means a residential area designated as herein provided where resident motor vehicles displaying a valid permit as described herein shall be exempt from parking time restrictions established pursuant to this division. *Residential property* means a building or portion thereof, designed or used exclusively for residential occupancy, but not including trailers, hotels, motels, motor lodges, dormitories, boarding and lodging homes, or time share buildings. *Residential property owner* means the individual(s) that have at least a 51 percent ownership interest in a residential property as reflected on the property tax records for real property address. The residential property owner may or may not be a resident. *Special area* means a primarily residential contiguous or nearly contiguous area containing public streets and highways or parts thereof that necessitates specific parking regulations to accommodate the residents therein. *Special permit parking zone* means a special area ordained by the city council upon the recommendation of the director of the department of public works or their designee that provides specific permit requirements and applicable permit fees that supersede these specific requirements as provided herein. (Code 1956, § 38-313; M.C.S., Ord. No. 26477, § 1, 7-9-15) Cross reference—Definitions generally, § 1-2. **Sec. 154-1137. Penalties for violation.** (a) Any person parking a motor vehicle not displaying a valid permit in a residential permit parking zone for a period exceeding the time limitation established shall be subjected to a fine, as set forth in section 154-699. laws.title: Eligibility requirements
laws.content:
(a) A residential area shall be deemed eligible for residential permit parking if, based on objective criteria established by the parking administrator, parking therein is impacted by commuter vehicles.

(b) In determining whether an area identified as eligible for residential permit parking or special permit parking zone shall be appropriately designated, the parking administrator shall take into consideration the following factors:

(1) The extent of the desire and need of the residents for appropriate designations and their willingness to bear the administrative costs in connection therewith.

(2) Proximity of the neighborhood to major parking attractors including employment centers, retail stores, restaurants, universities, hospitals and tourist attractions.

(3) Proximity of the neighborhood to transit service.

(4) Scarcity of convenient off-street parking for residents.

(5) The extent to which motor vehicles registered to persons residing in the residential area cannot be accommodated by the number of available off-street parking spaces.

(6) Substantial use of neighborhood curb space by commuters and other nonresidents for parking. Substantial use is defined as 25 percent or more of non-resident vehicles in the area under consideration during peak parking space usage times.

(7) Traffic, noise and safety problems caused by vehicles cruising for parking.

(Code 1956, § 38-314; M.C.S., Ord. No. 26477, § 1, 7-9-15)

laws.title: Implementation; application for permit
laws.content:
(a) Once a residential permit parking zone or special permit parking zone has been approved by the city council, implementation on a particular street shall be contingent on the following criteria:

(1) The street is primarily residential.

(2) A majority of the households signed a petition seeking resident or special parking status for their block.

(3) At least 75 percent of the legal on-street parking spaces must be occupied during the period proposed for parking restrictions, as determined by the parking administrator.

Supp. No. 73

CD154:84.1
§ 154-1141

NEW ORLEANS CODE

(b) The chief traffic engineer or his designee shall install parking signs on the streets designated as the residential permit parking zone or special parking zone. The signs shall indicate the times, locations and conditions under which parking shall be by permit only.

(c) The application fee pursuant to section 146-108 shall apply for both residential permit parking zone applications and special permit parking zone applications.

(d) For residential permit parking zones, a permit for parking shall be issued only to residents within a designated residential permit parking zone upon application and payment of the applicable fee. A person is eligible to apply for a residential parking permit if they are a resident within a designated residential permit parking area and do not have adequate off-street parking available at their property, as determined by the parking administrator. Eligibility for a residential parking permit is ultimately at the discretion of the parking administrator. No more than one permit shall be issued to each vehicle for which application is made.

(e) For residential permit parking zones, each application for a permit or renewal of a permit shall contain information sufficient to identify the applicant, provide proof of residency, identify the location of the resident’s real property address or residence within the residential parking permit area, and identify the license number and provide proof of current registration of the resident motor vehicle for which the permit would be issued. The owner or operator of any motor vehicle applying for a residential parking permit shall have a valid state motor vehicle license except when the car is titled in a company’s name and assigned to the resident for personal use. A letter from the company (on company stationery) must be presented identifying the resident, residential permit parking address, make and model and license plate number of the car along with the motor vehicle registration.

(f) For residential permit parking zones, a resident shall provide proof of residency in the residential permit parking zone on a block designated for implementation at the time application is made. Adequate proof of residency may include:

the resident’s tax bill providing a “homestead exemption” for the municipal address of the eligible property or an executed, current lease or other agreement for the municipal address of the eligible property.

(g) For residential permit parking zones, the application for a permit shall contain the name of the owner or operator of the motor vehicle; residential address, the make, model, registration and plate numbers of the motor vehicle; and the applicant’s driver’s license number. The motor vehicle registration and the driver’s license of the applicant must be presented at the time of making such application in order to verify the contents thereof. The owner or operator of any motor vehicle applying for a residential parking permit shall have a valid state motor vehicle license.

(h) For special permit parking zones, the applicable permits, application and evaluation criteria, and permit fee shall be dictated by council ordinance, as provided herein.

(Code 1956, § 38-316; M.C.S., Ord. No. 26477, § 1, 7-9-15)

laws.title: Permit fee
laws.content:
(a) The parking administrator is authorized to establish by order an annual residential permit parking fee for each residential parking zone to cover the administrative costs of permits issued pursuant to this section. The annual fee for each such permit shall be $30.00, unless otherwise provided herein. Upon presentation of adequate proof, persons 65 years of age or older who otherwise qualify for the permit shall pay a permit fee of not more than $20.00.

(b) The annual fee special parking zone shall be as fixed by the council, but in no event shall the fee be less than $30.00, except persons 65 years of age or older who otherwise qualify for the permit, said fee shall be no less than $20.00.

(Code 1956, § 38-321; M.C.S., Ord. No. 26477, § 1, 7-9-15)

laws.title: Use of permit
laws.content:
(a) Use notwithstanding any provisions of this chapter to the contrary, the holder of a residential or special parking permit shall be permitted to

Supp. No. 73

CD154:84.2
TRAFFIC AND VEHICLES

§ 154-1146

stand or park a motor vehicle for which a permit has been issued in the residential or special permit parking zone designated on the permit without being subject to the limitations imposed on vehicles lacking the permit, provided however that parking is permitted. While a vehicle for which a residential or special parking decal has been issued is so parked, such permit decal shall be displayed so as to be clearly visible through the windshield of the vehicle.

(b) A residential or special parking permit shall not authorize the holder thereof to stand or park a motor vehicle in such places or during such times as the stopping, standing, or parking of motor vehicles is prohibited or set aside for specified types of vehicles, and shall not exempt the holder from the observance of any traffic regulation other than the parking limit.

(c) A residential or special parking permit shall not guarantee or reserve to the holder thereof an on-street parking space within the designated permit parking area.

(Code 1956, § 38-317; M.C.S., Ord. No. 26477, § 1, 7-9-15)

laws.title: Exemption
laws.content:
Service vehicles parked in residential or special parking zones while making service calls to residential dwellings within the zone shall be exempt from holding a residential parking zone permit and exempt from the posted time limits. Such service vehicles shall display in the windshield on the passenger side of the vehicle a work slip showing the name and address of the residence being serviced.

(Code 1956, § 38-318; M.C.S., Ord. No. 26477, § 1, 7-9-15)

laws.title: Eligibility of temporary residents
laws.content:
(a) Temporary residents. Temporary residents of a residential or special permit parking zone whose motor vehicles are registered in another state may apply for a temporary visitor’s permit valid for the duration of the 30-day reciprocity period allowed under state law. Applicants must present a valid driver’s license and motor vehicle registration from their home state, as well as a rental or lease agreement, utility bill receipt, or some other adequate proof of residence in the designated residential permit parking zone. The fee for issuance of such permit shall be $15.00 and may be, within 30 days, applied towards a resident sticker valid for the balance of a twelve-month period from the date of issuance when the registration of the vehicle is matched to the local address in the residential or special parking zone.

(b) Student residents. Students of local universities who temporarily reside, semester-by-semester, on a block designated as part a residential or special permit parking zone shall be allowed to apply for a semester-long residential parking permit for each semester attended. Such permit shall be issued only after such individual presents a valid student identification card, current vehicle registration, license plate number and operator’s license as well as a rental agreement or utility bill showing the applicant as a bona fide resident of the address in question for the semester. The permit fee for shall be $20.00 per semester for each permit issued. No more than one permit per vehicle shall be issued. Students are not eligible to receive a visitor permit.

(Code 1956, § 38-319; Ord. No. 20,004, § 1, 1-18-01; M.C.S., Ord. No. 26477, § 1, 7-9-15)

laws.title: Visitor and non-resident permits
laws.content:
(a) Annual residential parking visitor permit.

(1) In a residential permit parking zone where parking spaces for visitors are not set aside on-street, the holder of a permanent valid residential parking permit or a resident without a vehicle who would otherwise qualify for a residential parking permit, may apply for one annual residential parking visitor’s permit.

(2) The annual residential parking visitor permit shall identify the resident’s permanent permit number, as applicable, and zone, and shall be signed by the permit-holder host attesting that the temporary pass shall be used by a bona fide visitor.

(3) The fee for issuance of such permit shall be in accordance with section 154-1142.

Supp. No. 73

CD154:84.3
§ 154-1146

NEW ORLEANS CODE

(4) Such permit shall not be duplicated, but may be transferrable to different visitors at the discretion of the permit-holder host.

(b) Daily visitor permit.

(1) In parking zones where parking spaces for visitors are not set aside on-street, the holder of a valid annual residential parking permit or valid student permit or residential property owner subject to restrictions contained herein, may apply for a daily visitor’s permit, which shall not be transferable.

(2) The daily visitor permit shall identify the permanent residential permit number, as applicable, and zone, and shall be signed by the permit-holder host or residential property owner attesting that the temporary permit shall be used by a bona fide visitor.

(3) Each daily visitor permit shall be $4.00 per pass. Upon presentation of adequate proof, persons 65 years of age or older who otherwise qualify for the permit shall pay a fee of $2.00 for each permit issued. An application fee shall not be charged for issuance of a daily visitor permit.

(4) No single residential parking permit or valid student permit holder shall be permitted to be issued or possess more than one daily visitor permit at any one time. A waiver of this limitation may be granted by the parking administrator subject to approval by the director of public works or their designee.

(c) Residential property owner permit.

(1) The parking administrator is authorized to issue an annual non-transferrable property owner permit to a residential property owner that is not a resident provided that they provide proof that they have at least a 51 percent ownership interest in a residential property as reflected on the property tax records for a real property address, current vehicle registration, license plate number and valid driver’s license.

(2) The fee for issuance of such permit shall be in accordance with section 154-1142.

(3) No single real property address shall be permitted to be issued or possess more than one residential property owner permit. A waiver of this limitation may be granted by the parking administrator subject to approval by the director of public works or their designee.

(4) The holder of a residential property owner permit shall not be authorized to apply for a daily visitor permit.

(Code 1956, § 38-322; M.C.S., Ord. No. 23818, § 2, 12-1-09; M.C.S., Ord. No. 26477, § 1, 7-9-15)

laws.title: Misrepresentation by applicant; illegal use of transfer of permit
laws.content:
(a) It shall constitute a violation of this division for any person to falsely represent himself as eligible for a residential or special parking permit or to furnish any false information in an application to the parking administrator in order to obtain a residential or special parking permit.

(b) No person other than the permittee named thereon shall use a residential or special parking permit or display it on a vehicle operated or parked, and any such use or display by a person other than the permittee shall constitute a violation of this section by the permittee and by the person who so used or displayed such parking permit.

(Code 1956, § 38-323; M.C.S., Ord. No. 26477, § 1, 7-9-15)

laws.title: Penalties for misrepresentation, illegal use
laws.content:
(a) The parking administrator is authorized to revoke the residential or special parking permit of any permittee found to be in violation of section 154-1147 and upon written notification thereof the permittee shall surrender such permit to the parking administrator.

(b) Any person who shall violate any provision of section 154-1147 shall, upon conviction, be subject to punishment by a fine of not more than $500.00.

(Code 1956, § 38-324; M.C.S., Ord. No. 26477, § 1, 7-9-15)

laws.title: Parking penalties
laws.content:
Any person parking a motor vehicle not displaying a valid residential or special parking permit that has been issued in accordance with the provisions of this article, and who parks such vehicle in a residential or special permit parking zone where signs are erected giving notice thereof for more than a maximum of two hours cumulatively anywhere within the boundaries of the zone and at any time during the posted hours of operation of the zone, shall be subject to receipt of a notice of violation and imposition of monetary fine, in accordance with the provisions of this chapter. Any vehicle parked in a residential or special permit parking zone in violation of any provision of this chapter requiring immediate removal and impoundment, or which is found to be causing a severe hazard to traffic or public safety, shall be subject to such action without regard to display of valid residential or special parking zone permit.

(Code 1956, § 38-325; M.C.S., Ord. No. 26477, § 1, 7-9-15)

laws.title: General requirements
laws.content:
(a) Every vehicle operated in this parish shall comply with all equipment requirements of state law and involving vehicles traveling on state highways, and particularly requirements of Title 32, known as the Louisiana Highway Regulatory Act, relative to driver responsibility for maintaining on the vehicle adequate headlights, backup lights, stop lights, braking equipment, taillamps, reflectors, electric turn signals, horns, windshield wipers, mirrors, safety glass, tires, fuel tank caps, fenders, mud guards, and all other equipment required by state law at the time and in the manner provided for by such statutes, in addition to requirements now imposed by this chapter.

(b) All trucks, tractors, or trailers used to haul oversized vehicles and overlength loads between dusk and dawn are to be equipped with portable lights and barricades. These lights are to be red or amber in color and are to be placed on the truck, tractor, or trailer, or on the overlength load, in a position which will enable it to be seen from any direction. They should also be equipped with portable barricades containing fixtures for the attachment of portable lights. These lights or barricades are to be used in case of a breakdown or in time of trouble.

(c) Every school bus operated in the parish shall be equipped with an exterior convex mirror at least $7\frac{1}{2}$ inches in diameter mounted on either the left or right front fender in such a manner that the seated driver may observe, through its use, areas to the immediate front and side of the bus when direct observation is not possible.

(d) Should there be any conflict between the requirements of state law and the equipment standards set forth in this chapter, state law will govern.

(Code 1956, § 38-166)

*State law reference—Equipment of vehicles, R.S. 32:301 et seq.*

laws.title: Trailers and towed vehicles
laws.content:
(a) When one vehicle is towed by another, the drawbar or other connection shall be of sufficient strength to pull all weight towed thereby, and such drawbar or such connection shall not exceed 15 feet from one vehicle to the other except the connection between any two vehicles transporting poles, pipes, machinery, or other objects of structure or nature which cannot be readily dismembered.

(b) When one vehicle is towed by another and the connection between them consists of a chain, rope or cable, there shall be displayed upon such connection a red flag or cloth not less than 12 inches square; from sunset to sunrise, this signal shall be a red light, plainly visible under ordinary atmospheric conditions for a distance of at least 500 feet.

(Code 1956, § 38-171)

laws.title: Unauthorized vehicle equipment prohibited
laws.content:
(a) No person shall operate any vehicle in the parish which shall display, have attached to it, or use any equipment prohibited by state law and particularly the Louisiana Highway Regulatory Act.

(b) It shall be a violation for any vehicle, except authorized emergency vehicles, to display a blinking red light, visible from the front of the vehicle, while such vehicle is in operation.

(c) It shall be a violation for any vehicle, except authorized vehicles of the New Orleans Police Department and Department of Public Works vehicles operating under the direction of the New Orleans Police Department to display a blinking blue light, visible from the front of the vehicle, while such vehicle is in operation.

(Code 1956, § 38-167; M.C.S., Ord. No. 27621, § 1, 12-14-17)

laws.title: Headlight requirements
laws.content:
Every vehicle upon a street or highway within this city at any time between sunset and sunrise and at any other time when, due to insufficient light or unfavorable atmospheric conditions, persons and vehicles on the highway are not clearly discernible at a distance of 500 feet ahead shall display lighted lamps and illuminating devices as required by state law and this chapter

laws.title: Child passenger restraint system
laws.content:
(a) Any driver who transports a child or children under the age of five years in a motor vehicle which is equipped with safety belts at the time of manufacture or assembly or is currently equipped with safety belts shall have the child properly secured in accordance with the manufacturer's instructions in a child passenger restraint system which meets the applicable federal motor vehicles safety standards in effect on the effective date of the ordinance from which this section was derived, except as provided in subsections (c), (d) and (e) of this section.

(b) The terms "motor vehicles" as used in this section shall not mean the following: bicycles; farm tractor; motorcycle or motor-driven cycle; truck of manufacturer's rating carrying capacity of over 2,000 pounds; ambulance or other emergency vehicle; school bus as defined in R.S. 32:1(62)(a) and (b); church bus, private bus or recreational vehicle which has a passenger capacity of over ten persons; or commercial truck, van or taxi.

(c) If such child is three to five years of age, securing the child in a lap belt or safety belt in a rear seat shall be sufficient to meet the requirements of this section. If there are no rear seats, a child passenger restraint system shall be used.

(d) Where the number of children under the age of five in the motor vehicle exceeds the number of child passenger restraint systems and seat belts available in the motor vehicle, the unrestrained children shall be seated in a rear seat.

(e) The provisions of this section shall not apply when one of the following conditions exists:

(1) The motor vehicle is being used as an ambulance or other emergency vehicle.

(2) An emergency exists which threatens the life of any person operating a motor vehicle to whom this section otherwise would apply or the life of any child who otherwise would be required to be restrained under this section.

(3) Any child who would otherwise be required to be restrained under this section who is physically unable because of medical reasons to use a child passenger safety system or safety belt.

(f) In no event shall failure to wear a child passenger safety seat system be considered as comparative negligence, nor shall such failure be admissible as evidence in the trail of any civil action with regard to negligence, nor shall such failure be considered a moving violation.

(g) Any operator of a motor vehicle stopped for a violation of this section and against whom enforcement action has been taken shall not be guilty of a subsequent violation of this section until 24 hours have elapsed from the date and time of the violation as indicated on the traffic ticket.

(Code 1956, § 38-162.3)

State law reference—Similar provisions, R.S. 32:295.

laws.title: Penalties
laws.content:
All vehicles registered in the parish shall be inspected at 12-month intervals, and any vehicle presented for inspection with an inspection certificate which had been issued in excess of three months previously shall be delinquent and subject to a delinquency fee according to the following schedule:
Months Fees
From 1.1 to 3 months $ 2.00
From 3.1 to 6 months 4.00
From 6.1 to 9 months 6.00
From 9.1 to 12 months 8.00
From 12 and over 10.00
(Code 1956, § 38-161.6) Secs. 154-1257—154-1295. Reserved.

laws.title: Vehicle inspection required
laws.content:
(a) No person shall operate a vehicle owned by a resident of this state upon the streets of the City of New Orleans unless it bears a current safety inspection certificate (brake tag) from the municipality where the vehicle is registered, or if such municipality does not require such safety inspection certificate, then from the state. All vehicles registered in the City of New Orleans shall be presented to the department of public works or an authorized inspection station at least once every other year, except as may be otherwise provided in this section. Such an inspection shall be performed within 60 days after the month the vehicle was acquired or newly registered in the State of Louisiana after being transferred from another state.

(b) Vehicles with a gross vehicle weight rating of 10,000 pounds or less are eligible for a two-year inspection certificate only if the vehicle age is ten years or less. For purposes of this article, the term "vehicle age" shall be determined based on the vehicle's model year, and a "year" shall be measured through the last day of that respective calendar year (for example, a vehicle with a model year of 2000 shall have a vehicle age of one year as of January 1, 2001).

Supp. No. 96

CD154:115
§ 154-1303

NEW ORLEANS CODE

(c) Vehicles with a gross vehicle weight rating of 10,001 pounds or greater shall be presented to the department of public works or an authorized inspection station on an annual basis and shall not be entitled to a two-year inspection certificate.

(d) The annual inspection period shall begin on January 1 of each year; the reinspection month shall be determined by the month and year indicated on each particular vehicle’s previous inspection certificate.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 26599, § 1, 10-1-15; M.C.S., Ord. No. 27962, § 1, 12-20-18; M.C.S., Ord. No. 28640, § 1, 3-25-21)

laws.title: Vehicles exempt from inspection
laws.content:
The following categories of vehicles are exempt from inspection under this chapter:

(a) Farm tractors, self-propelled farm equipment, rubber-tired farm wagons and carts, drawn rubber-tired farm equipment, and implements of animal husbandry which are designed primarily for field use and which are operated or moved only incidentally on the streets or highways of the city or state, and which are used for farm purposes only.

(b) Motor vehicles which are 25 years old or older and which are used primarily for exhibition in shows, parades, tours, and other special uses and not for general transportation and which are registered and licensed as antique as provided in R.S. 32:707(L) of the Louisiana Revised Statutes.

(c) Single-axle two-wheel trailers, tandem trailers, and all boat trailers unless these trailers are used in commerce and are subject to Code of Federal Regulations (49 CFR 396.17).

(d) Commercial vehicles with an apportioned plate provided that the vehicle has complied with the requirements of Code of Federal Regulations (49 CFR 396.17).

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 26599, § 1, 10-1-15; M.C.S., Ord. No. 27962, § 1, 12-20-18)

laws.title: Motor vehicle inspection standards
laws.content:
(a) The director of public works is authorized to promulgate administrative rules and regulations for the inspection of motor vehicles to further the purpose and intent of this article. Rules and regulations so promulgated shall supersede and take precedence over standards of the Louisiana Department of Public Safety and Corrections.

(b) In the absence of administrative rules and regulations established by the director of public works, motor vehicle inspections within the City of New Orleans will be conducted in compliance with the standards promulgated by the Secretary of the Louisiana Department of Public Safety and Corrections, unless such standards conflict with the provisions of this article, in which case this article shall govern.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 26599, § 1, 10-1-15; M.C.S., Ord. No. 28640, § 1, 3-25-21)

laws.title: Issuance of certificate
laws.content:
(a) Upon determining that a vehicle is equipped with functioning safety devices, as required by the laws of the city and state, and is adequately covered by liability insurance as required by state law, and upon collection of fees for such inspection as set forth in section 154-1307 of this chapter, the department of public works shall attach or cause to be attached an inspection certificate to the lower left side of the windshield of such vehicle. Inspection certificates shall expire on the last day of the month indicated on the face of the certificate.

(b) Vehicles which fail to pass inspection shall be issued a card showing the mechanical faults or indicating that proof of liability insurance as required by law has not been provided. A period of not more than 30 days shall be allowed in which to make necessary repairs or to provide proof of liability insurance as required by law, and such rejection card shall be a substitute for the inspection certificate during such period. Vehicles that pose a specific road safety hazard are restricted to driving no more than 20 miles within a 30-day period in order to make necessary repairs.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 26599, § 1, 10-1-15; M.C.S., Ord. No. 27962, § 1, 12-20-18; M.C.S., Ord. No. 28640, § 1, 3-25-21)

CD154:116

§ 154-1308

laws.title: Fees
laws.content:
(a) Inspection stickers:

(1) The fees to be paid by the owner or operator of a vehicle for an annual inspection certificate under this chapter shall be as follows:

i. Commercial vehicles shall pay a fee of $60.00.

ii. All other vehicles shall pay a fee of $25.00.

(2) The department of public works shall collect from the operator of permitted satellite inspection stations the following amount per annual inspection certificate issued:

i. All inspection certificates for commercial vehicles, as defined in this chapter: $20.00.

ii. Inspection certificates for all other vehicles: $12.50.

(b) Late fees shall be assessed at a rate of $2.00 per month beginning on the first day of the calendar month following expiration, or 60 days after the month the vehicle is acquired or newly registered in the state of Louisiana after being transferred from another state. Late fees shall not exceed the price of an annual inspection certificate.

(c) All fees for inspection certificates and late fees shall be collected by an approved inspector and remitted to the department to be deposited into the general fund of the city. Payment for late fees shall be submitted no more than 15 days after being collected.

(d) For inspection certificates providing two years of validity as set forth in this chapter; the fee for such certificates shall be equivalent to the fee required for two annual inspections.

(e) Fees for satellite inspection stations:

(1) Permitted satellite inspection stations shall remit an annual fee of $25.00 to the department of public works plus an annual fee of $5.00 for each inspector named on the permit application.

(2) If additional inspectors are added subsequent to the new or renewal application, the satellite inspection station shall remit the $5.00 fee when that inspector is submitted to the department of public works for approval

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 26599, § 1, 10-1-15; M.C.S., Ord. No. 27962, § 1, 12-20-18; M.C.S., Ord. No. 28640, § 1, 3-25-21; M.C.S., Ord. No. 29874, § 1, 3-21-24)

laws.title: Motor vehicle inspection stations, generally
laws.content:
(a) Motor vehicle inspection stations shall conduct vehicle inspections throughout the calendar year.

(b) Inspection stations shall display signage as proscribed by the director providing information including, but not limited to, hours of motor vehicle inspections, types of vehicle inspections performed, and standards for inspections.

(c) Restrooms must be available within the facility for use of customers.

(d) All motor vehicle inspections must be conducted on the premises of the approved inspection station and must be conducted on a hard surface (concrete or asphalt). Notwithstanding any law, rule or administrative policy to the contrary, inspection stations are not required to reserve a service bay or stall for the exclusive purpose of conducting motor vehicle inspections.

(e) For inspecting vehicles with a gross weight rating below 10,001 pounds, inspection stations must have available space to conduct a 20 mile per hour road test approved by the department of public works. Alternatively, a properly installed and calibrated brake testing machine may be utilized in lieu of the road test. For inspecting commercial vehicles, as defined in this chapter, stations shall meet all standards outlined in Title 55 of the Louisiana Administrative Code.

(f) Inspection stations are required to maintain telephone service to the place of business and ensure that the telephone number is published in the local telephone directory and is made available on the internet.

Supp. No. 108

CD154:117
§ 154-1308

NEW ORLEANS CODE

(g) The following equipment shall be present at all inspection stations at all times during inspection hours:

(1) Windshield scraper (for removal of expired certificates).

(2) Standard single hole punch.

(3) Tire depth gauge.

(4) Measuring tape at least six feet in length.

(5) Flashlight.

(6) Tint meter (two-piece type).

(7) Adjustable mirror.

(8) Numerical stamps, numbered 1 through 12, and an "X" stamp, 1" size, and a black indelible ink stamp pad.

(9) The motor vehicle inspection bureau may require additional or alternate equipment for the proper operation of a satellite inspection station in the interest of ensuring public safety. Any additional or alternate equipment requirements will be provided to inspection stations in writing after which the station will have 30 days to obtain such equipment.

(h) The following equipment shall be present at all satellite inspection stations performing inspections on vehicles with a gross vehicle weight rating in excess of 10,001 pounds:

(1) Mechanic's creeper.

(2) Soapstone marker.

(3) Floor jack or lift or two jack stands, required only for stations which will perform inspections on school buses.

(4) Two wheel chocks

(5) Brake chamber tool

(6) A current Federal Motor Carrier Safety regulation handbook (updated within one calendar year) as prescribed by the U.S. Department of Transportation, Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration Regulations, 49 CFR Parts 40, 303, 325, 350-399.

(i) Inspection stations shall give priority to customers seeking motor vehicle inspections.

(j) Inspection stations may inspect vehicles for good condition and proper adjustment during rain if the conditions are safe and the vehicle can be accurately inspected.

(k) Inspection stations shall offer certificates of inspection which are valid for both one year and two year periods. The owner of the vehicle shall have the option of purchasing a one year or a two year certificate, if such vehicle is eligible for a two-year certificate under this chapter.

(l) Inspection stations shall maintain an inventory of certificates of inspection adequate to satisfy the needs of the public, subject to the determination and standards of the department of public works.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 26599, § 1, 10-1-15; M.C.S., Ord. No. 27962, § 1, 12-20-18; M.C.S., Ord. No. 28640, § 1, 3-25-21)

laws.title: Satellite inspection stations, specifically
laws.content:
(a) For the purpose of making inspections and issuing official inspection certificates, as provided within this article, the director of the department of public works may issue permits for and furnish instructions to satellite inspection stations for the inspection of vehicles as required by this chapter.

(b) Application for a satellite inspection station permit shall be made upon an official form provided by the director for that purpose, and may be granted when the director is satisfied that the station is properly equipped, has adequately trained personnel to perform such inspections, and that inspections will be conducted in accordance with the laws of the city and state.

(c) The director shall supervise and cause inspections to be made of such satellite inspection stations and shall suspend and/or revoke and require surrender of any permit issued to a station which is not properly equipped or where inspections are not properly conducted.

(d) The director shall suspend and/or revoke and require surrender of any permit issued to a station when such station issues an inspection certificate in violation of this article, the Code of the City of New Orleans, or state law.

Supp. No. 108

CD154:118
TRAFFIC AND VEHICLES

§ 154-1310

(e) Satellite inspection stations permits shall not be assigned, transferred, or used at any location other than therein designated and every permit shall be posted in a conspicuous place at the location designated.

(f) Satellite inspection station operators are responsible for the safekeeping of motor vehicle inspection certificates purchased for use by that station from the department of public works. If inspection certificates are lost, stolen, destroyed, or otherwise rendered unusable, no refund of fees or replacement certificates shall be issued by the director.

(g) Qualification for satellite inspection stations:

(1) Any business seeking approval as a satellite inspection station must guarantee inspections will be conducted in accordance with this article for a minimum of 40 hours per week.

i. Subject to the determination of the director of public works, approval of a satellite inspection station may be conditioned upon a guarantee of operation on specific days or during specific times to ensure adequate service to the public.

(2) Satellite inspection stations shall only be approved at locations operating under the use classification of "gas station," "motor vehicle service and repair, major," "motor vehicle service and repair," or "car wash" with permanent structures and sewerage and water board approved drainage in compliance with the standards of the Comprehensive Zoning Ordinance.

(3) Businesses applying for approval as a satellite inspection station must have been in operation for a minimum of 90 days at the time of application, as evidenced by the business's occupational license issued by the department of finance.

(4) Satellite inspection stations are required to submit and maintain a surety bond for the amount of $5,000.00 to provide for any damages which may occur to private vehicles during inspection due to negligence on the part of the satellite inspection station or its employees.

(5) Satellite inspection stations shall have a minimum of two approved motor vehicle inspectors on staff and registered with the department of public works, with at least one approved motor vehicle inspector on duty during all inspection hours to perform motor vehicle inspections.

(6) Permitted satellite inspection stations shall inspect and issue inspection certificates to the owner or operator of private motor vehicles in accordance with the fees outlined in section 154-1307(a)(1) of this chapter.

(h) Satellite stations are required to record each inspection performed, along with all inspection certificate serial numbers and late fees collected, in the format required and frequency specified by the department of public works. (M.C.S., Ord. No. 26599, § 1, 10-1-15; M.C.S., Ord. No. 27962, § 1, 12-20-18; M.C.S., Ord. No. 28640, § 1, 3-25-21)

laws.title: Approved motor vehicle inspectors
laws.content:
(a) All personnel employed by the satellite inspection station for the purpose of conducting motor vehicle inspections shall be approved and licensed by the department of public works.

(b) No person shall be approved as a motor vehicle inspector that has not completed motor vehicle inspection training approved by the Louisiana Department of Public Safety. Evidence of completion shall be submitted to the department of public works. Any inspector that has been unlicensed for a year or more must be retrained before inspecting any vehicle.

(c) Persons performing inspections on commercial vehicles, as defined in this chapter, shall be a current ASE (Automotive Service Excellence) Certified Diesel Mechanic or have an

equivalent accreditation. Proof shall be provided to the department each time an inspector's application is submitted for review.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 26599, § 1, 10-1-15; M.C.S., Ord. No. 27962, § 1, 12-20-18; M.C.S., Ord. No. 28640, § 1, 3-25-21)

**Sec. 154-1311. Fleet inspection stations.**

(a) Any person, corporation, partnership, or other business entity owning or holding leases for more than ten motor vehicles registered in New Orleans and operating at least one vehicle repair and maintenance shop, may, upon request, have one or more of his vehicle repair and maintenance shops designated as fleet inspection stations for the purpose of inspecting and certifying those motor vehicles which are owned or leased by him.

(b) Such fleet inspection stations are required to maintain compliance with all applicable provisions of sections 154-1308, 154-1309, and 154-1310.

(c) Permitted fleet inspection stations shall remit an annual fee of $25.00 to the department of public works plus an annual fee of $5.00 for each inspector named on the permit application.

(1) If additional inspectors are added subsequent to the new or renewal application, the fleet inspection station shall remit the $5.00 fee when that inspector is submitted to the department of public works for approval.

(d) The department of public works shall collect from the operator of permitted fleet inspection stations the full amount of inspection certificates as provided in section 154-1307(a)(1).

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 26599, § 1, 10-1-15; M.C.S., Ord. No. 28640, § 1, 3-25-21)

**Sec. 154-1312. Misrepresentation and false certificates.**

(a) No person shall, in any manner, represent any place or business as a satellite or fleet inspection station unless such station is operating pursuant to a valid permit issued by the department of public works.

(b) No person other than an approved motor vehicle inspector shall issue an inspection certificate on behalf of the department of public works or a permitted satellite or fleet inspection station.

(c) No person shall use, possess, display or cause to be displayed upon any vehicle any inspection certificate knowing same to be fictitious, fraudulent, issued to a vehicle other than the one to which it was recorded, or issued without an complete inspection having been made.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 26599, § 1, 10-1-15; M.C.S., Ord. No. 27962, § 1, 12-20-18; M.C.S., Ord. No. 28640, § 1, 3-25-21)

Secs. 154-1313—154-1400. Reserved.

**ARTICLE XII. BICYCLES**

**Sec. 154-1401. Purpose and effect of regulations.**

The purpose of this article is to facilitate the recovery of lost and stolen bicycles through a system of identification numbers and also to govern the rental and use of bicycles.

(Code 1956, § 38-190; M.C.S., Ord. No. 27900, § 1, 10-18-18; M.C.S., Ord. No. 29169, § 2, 10-6-22)

**Sec. 154-1402. Responsibility of parent or guardian.**

No parent of a child or tutor or curator of a minor or incompetent person shall authorize or knowingly permit any such child, minor or incompetent person to violate any of the provisions of this article.

(Code 1956, § 38-191)

**Sec. 154-1403. Registration permitted.**

Any person who resides in the City of New Orleans and who owns a bicycle and rides it upon a public right-of-way may register the bicycle with the department of safety and permits to receive a specific identification number for each bicycle he or she owns. The director of the department of safety and permits and his or her

Supp. No. 102

CD154:120
TRAFFIC AND VEHICLES

§ 154-1409

designee (hereafter department) is authorized to promulgate rules and regulations as may be required to carry out the purpose of this article. (Code 1956, § 38-192; M.C.S., Ord. No. 27900, § 1, 10-18-18)

**Sec. 154-1404. Registration application and fee.**

(a) Applications to register bicycles shall be made upon a form provided by the department. There shall be a $5.00 application fee for each registered bicycle.

(b) It shall be a violation of this article for any person to register a bicycle when they know or have reasonable grounds to believe that they are not the owner or authorized by the owner to possess and register the bicycle. (Code 1956, § 38-193; M.C.S., Ord. No. 27900, § 1, 10-18-18)

**Sec. 154-1405. Issuance of registration; record.**

(a) Upon the department's receipt of a proper application and fee, the department shall register the bicycle, assign it a registration number, and issue to the applicant a bicycle certificate sticker, as provided in section 154-1406.

(b) The department shall keep a record of each issued registration number, the date issued, the name and address of the person to whom a bicycle certificate sticker was issued, the manufacturer's identification number that is printed on the frame of the bicycle, if applicable, and all fees collected relative thereto.

(c) Upon the department's receipt of a written request, it shall be the duty of the department to provide the superintendent of police and/or the superintendent of fire with a copy of the record of each registration. (Code 1956, § 38-194; M.C.S., Ord. No. 27900, § 1, 10-18-18)

**Sec. 154-1406. Attachment of registration certificate.**

The department upon registering a bicycle shall issue to the applicant a bicycle certificate sticker bearing a unique city registration number, specifically assigned to the bicycle. The department shall instruct the applicant to firmly attach the bicycle certificate sticker on the frame of the bicycle in such a position that it is plainly visible. It shall be a violation of this article for any person to remove a bicycle certificate sticker from a bicycle without express permission of the owner. (Code 1956, § 38-195; M.C.S., Ord. No. 27900, § 1, 10-18-18)

**Sec. 154-1407. Inspection of bicycles.**

The department shall receive from each applicant a written and signed certification that their bicycle is in a safe, sound condition as required by law, prior to any issuance of a bicycle certificate sticker. Nothing contained herein shall preclude the department from requesting to inspect the condition of a bicycle prior to issuance if deemed necessary by the department. The department may authorize satellite inspection stations to perform bicycle inspection and issue bicycle certificate stickers on behalf of the department, subject to the rules outlined in this chapter. (Code 1956, § 38-196; M.C.S., Ord. No. 27900, § 1, 10-18-18)

**Sec. 154-1408. Transfer of ownership.**

Upon the sale or other transfer of a bicycle, the new owner may obtain a new registration as provided herein, or may continue to use the existing registration number, but should update contact information with the department. (Code 1956, § 38-197; M.C.S., Ord. No. 27900, § 1, 10-18-18)

**Sec. 154-1409. Rental of bicycles.**

Any person, natural or juridical, that offers for rent bicycles shall not rent or offer for rent any bicycle unless each bicycle is registered with the department and has received a correlating bicycle certificate sticker, which shall be prominently attached to each individual bicycle. (Code 1956, § 38-198; M.C.S., Ord. No. 27900, § 1, 10-18-18; M.C.S., Ord. No. 29169, § 2, 10-6-22)

Supp. No. 102

**Sec. 154-1410. Reserved.**

*Editor’s note—M.C.S., Ord. No. 27900, § 1, adopted Oct. 18, 2018, repealed § 154-1410, which pertained to reports of bicycle dealers, and requiring of bills of sale and derived from Code 1956, § 38-199.*

**Sec. 154-1411. Traffic laws applicable to persons riding bicycles.**

Every person riding a bicycle upon a roadway shall be granted all of the rights and shall be subject to all of the duties applicable to the driver of a vehicle by the laws of this state declaring rules of the road applicable to vehicles or by the traffic laws of the city applicable to the driver of a vehicle, except as otherwise provided in this article and except as to those provisions of law which by their nature, can have no application.

(Code 1956, § 38-200)

*State law reference—Similar provisions, R.S. 32:194.*

**Sec. 154-1412. Obedience to traffic control devices.**

Any person operating a bicycle shall obey the instructions of official traffic control signals, signs, and other traffic control devices applicable to vehicles, unless otherwise directed by a police officer. Whenever authorized signs are erected indicating that no right, left, or "U" turn is permitted, no person operating a bicycle shall disobey the direction of any such signs, except when such person dismounts from the bicycle to make any such turn, such person shall then obey the regulations applicable to pedestrians.

(Code 1956, § 38-201)

**Sec. 154-1413. Failure to stop in event of accident.**

Any person who, while riding or propelling a bicycle or other vehicle or instrument of that general character, shall run against, upon or over any person upon the public highways or the property of any person in his personal possession or use in such a manner as might do an injury or cause damage to such person or property and shall not stop at once to ascertain the extent of such injury and to render such assistance as may be needed or shall refuse to give his name and residence when asked for by the person so injured or by any other person in his behalf shall be guilty of an offense.

(Code 1956, § 38-202)

**Sec. 154-1414. One-handed steering.**

Every rider of a bicycle, tricycle or other vehicle propelled by hand or foot must keep at least one hand on the handlebars of his machine when riding it.

(Code 1956, § 38-203)

*State law reference—Similar provisions, R.S. 32:195.*

**Sec. 154-1415. Riding on roadways and bicycle paths.**

(a) Every person operating a bicycle upon a roadway shall ride as near to the right side of the roadway as practicable, exercising due care when passing a standing vehicle or one proceeding in the same direction, except under any of the following circumstances:

(1) When overtaking and passing another bicycle or vehicle proceeding in the same direction.

(2) When preparing for a left turn at an intersection or into a private road or driveway.

(3) When reasonably necessary to avoid fixed or moving objects, vehicles, bicycles, pedestrians, animals, surface hazards, or substandard width lane or any other conditions that make it unsafe to continue along the right-hand curb or edge of the roadway. For the purposes of this paragraph, a "substandard width lane" is a lane that is too narrow for a bicycle and a vehicle to travel safely side by side within the lane.

(4) When approaching a place where a right turn is authorized.

(b) Persons riding bicycles upon a roadway shall not ride more than two abreast except on paths or parts of roadways set aside for the exclusive use of bicycles.

(c) Persons riding bicycles shall be allowed to operate on the shoulder of a roadway.

§ 154-1422

(d) Any person operating a bicycle upon a roadway or a highway, where there are two or more marked traffic lanes and traffic travels in only one direction, may ride as near the left-hand curb or shoulder of that roadway as practicable when preparing for a left turn.

(Code 1956, § 38-204; M.C.S., Ord. No. 27365, § 5, 4-20-17)

State law reference—Similar provisions, R.S. 32:197.

laws.title: Riding on sidewalks
laws.content:
No person 15 or more years of age shall ride a bicycle upon any sidewalk in the city nor will bicycles be allowed on sidewalks in the business district.

(Code 1956, § 38-205)

laws.title: Speeding
laws.content:
No person shall operate a bicycle at a speed greater than is reasonable and prudent under the conditions then existing.

(Code 1956, § 38-206)

laws.title: Right-of-way at alley or driveway
laws.content:
The operator of a bicycle emerging from an alley, driveway or building shall, upon approaching a sidewalk or the sidewalk extending across any alleyway, stop and yield the right-of-way to all pedestrians approaching upon such sidewalk area and upon entering the roadway shall yield the right-of-way to all vehicles approaching on such roadway.

(Code 1956, § 38-207; M.C.S., Ord. No. 27365, § 6, 4-20-17)

laws.title: Manner of riding
laws.content:
A person propelling a bicycle shall not ride other than astride a permanent and regular seat attached thereto. No bicycle shall be used to carry more persons at one time than the number for which it is designed and equipped.

(Code 1956, § 38-208)

State law reference—Similar provisions, R.S. 32:195.

laws.title: Carrying articles
laws.content:
No person operating a bicycle shall carry any package, bundle or article which prevents the rider from keeping at least one hand upon the handlebars or which interferes with the stability of the bicycle or the rider’s vision.

(Code 1956, § 38-209)

State law reference—Similar provisions, R.S. 32:195.

laws.title: Parking of bicycles
laws.content:
No person shall deposit, place, or store a bicycle or similar device upon the right-of-way other than at or on a proper bike rack or other designated storage area. Any bicycle or similar device that is improperly deposited, placed, or stored on the right-of-way shall be deemed an encumbrance or obstruction, pursuant to section 146-493, and subject to immediate removal.

(Code 1956, § 38-210; M.C.S., Ord. No. 27849, § 1, 9-6-18; M.C.S., Ord. No. 29169, § 2, 10-6-22)

Cross reference—Obstruction of public rights-of-way, public places prohibited, § 146-493.

laws.title: Necessary bicycle equipment
laws.content:
(a) Every bicycle when in use between sunrise and sunset or when persons and vehicles on the street are not clearly discernable at a distance of 500 feet ahead shall be equipped with the following:

(1) A lamp mounted on the front that shall emit a white light visible from a distance of at least 500 feet to the front. A generator-powered lamp that emits light only when the bicycle is moving may be used to meet this requirement.

(2) A lamp mounted on the rear that shall emit either a flashing or steady red light visible from a distance of 500 feet to the rear.

(3) A red reflector mounted on the rear and a reflector on each side facing outward at a right angle to the bicycle frame that shall be visible from all distances from 100 feet to 600 feet to the rear when directly in front of lawful lower beams of head lamps on a motor vehicle.

(b) A bicycle or its operator may be equipped with lights or reflectors in addition to those required by subsection (a) of this section, except that red lamps and red reflectors shall not be

Supp. No. 102

CD154:123
§ 154-1422

NEW ORLEANS CODE

used on the front of the bicycle and white lamps and white reflectors shall not be used on the rear of the bicycle.

(c) A lamp or lamps worn by the operator of a bicycle shall comply with the requirements of subsection (a) of this section, if the lamp or lamps can be seen at the distances specified.

(d) No person shall operate a bicycle unless it is equipped with a bell or other device capable of giving a signal audible for a distance of at least 100 feet, except that a bicycle shall not be equipped with nor shall any person use upon a bicycle any siren or whistle.

(e) Every bicycle shall be equipped with a brake which will enable the operator to make the braked wheels skid on dry, level, clean pavement.

(Code 1956, § 38-211; M.C.S., Ord. No. 27365, § 7, 4-20-17)

State law reference—Similar provisions, R.S. 32:329.

laws.title: Disposition of unclaimed bicycles
laws.content:
All unclaimed, unidentified, or abandoned bicycles in the possession or custody of the department shall be held for a period of not less than 45 days. Storage fees may be assessed at a rate of up to $100.00 per day. Thereafter, such bicycles may be sold at a fair price or may be donated to a nonprofit organization or agency serving the children of the parish, as permitted by law.

(Code 1956, § 38-212; M.C.S., Ord. No. 27900, § 1, 10-18-18; M.C.S., Ord. No. 29169, § 2, 10-6-22)

laws.title: Penalties
laws.content:
Penalties for violations of this article shall be as provided in section 1-13 of the City Code.

(Code 1956, § 38-213; M.C.S., Ord. No. 27900, § 1, 10-18-18)

laws.title: Rights and duties of electric-assisted bicycles
laws.content:
Except as otherwise provided in this Article, an electric-assisted bicycle or an operator of an electric-assisted bicycle shall be afforded all the rights and privileges, and be subject to all of the duties, of a bicycle or the operator of a bicycle. An electric-assisted bicycle is a vehicle to the same extent as a bicycle.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 28180, § 2, 9-5-19)

laws.title: Insurance, licensing, and registration
laws.content:
An electric-assisted bicycle or a person operating an electric-assisted bicycle is not subject to the provisions of this Code relating to financial responsibility, driver’s licenses, registration, certificates of title, off-highway vehicles and license plates. An electric-assisted bicycle is not a motor vehicle.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 28180, § 2, 9-5-19)

laws.title: Tampering restriction
laws.content:
A person shall not tamper with or modify an electric-assisted bicycle so as to change the classification of an electric-assisted bicycle, unless they appropriately replace the manufacturer’s label indicating the classification.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 28180, § 2, 9-5-19)

laws.title: CPSC compliance
laws.content:
An electric-assisted bicycle shall comply with the equipment and manufacturing requirements for bicycles adopted by the United States Consumer Product Safety Commission (16 C.F.R. part 1512).

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 28180, § 2, 9-5-19)

laws.title: Motor disengagement
laws.content:
An electric-assisted bicycle shall operate in a manner so that the electric motor is disengaged or ceases to function when the rider stops pedaling or when the brakes are applied.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 28180, § 2, 9-5-19)

laws.title: Trail use by class 1 electric-assisted bicycles
laws.content:
A class 1 electric-assisted bicycle may be ridden on a bicycle or shared use trail where bicycles are permitted.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 28180, § 2, 9-5-19)

**Sec. 154-1432. Trail use by class 3 electric-assisted bicycles.**

A class 3 electric-assisted bicycle shall not be ridden on a bicycle or shared use trail.

**Sec. 154-1433. Age restriction.**

No person under the age of 16 may operate a class 3 electric-assisted bicycle. A person under the age of 16 may ride as a passenger on a class 3 electric-assisted bicycle that is designed to accommodate passengers.

**Sec. 154-1434. Helmet requirement.**

All operators and passengers of class 3 electric-assisted bicycles shall wear a properly fitted and fastened bicycle helmet that meets the standards provided by either the United States Consumer Product Safety Commission or the American Society for Testing and Materials, or standards subsequently established by those entities.  
(M.C.S., Ord. No. 28180, § 2, 9-5-19)

laws.title: Speedometer requirement
laws.content:
All class 3 electric-assisted bicycles must be equipped with a speedometer that displays the speed the bicycle is traveling in miles per hour. (M.C.S., Ord. No. 28180, § 2, 9-5-19)

laws.title: Riding generally
laws.content:
(a) No driver of a two- or three-wheel motorcycle or motor-driven cycle shall carry any other person on, upon or within such vehicle on any street or highway in the city, except as hereinafter provided. If any two- or three-wheeled motor vehicle is equipped with:

(1) A dual seat designed for two persons or a separate seat for a passenger and double foot rests; or

(2) A side car attachment providing a separate seat space within such sidecar attachment for each person riding therein so that such person shall be seated entirely within the body of such sidecar, then it shall be permissible for an operator who has attained the age or ages required by state law to carry a passenger.

(b) A demonstration ride by a licensed dealer or his employee is excepted from the provisions hereof.

(Code 1956, § 38-126)

laws.title: Responsibility of operator
laws.content:
The operator of any motorcycle or motor-driven cycle shall be responsible for all violations incurred by his passengers.

(Code 1956, § 38-162.1)

laws.title: Required equipment
laws.content:
(a) Rear view mirrors. All vehicles covered under this section shall be equipped with at least one mirror mounted on the vehicle in such a position so as to enable the operator to clearly view the roadway for a distance of 200 feet to the rear of his vehicle.

(b) Speedometer. All motorcycles and motor-driven cycles covered under this section shall be equipped with a properly operating speedometer.

(c) Headgear. No person shall operate or ride upon any motorcycle or any motor-driven cycle unless such person is equipped with and wearing on the head a safety helmet of the type and design manufactured for use by the operators of such vehicles, which shall be properly secured with a chin strap while the vehicle is in motion. All safety helmets shall consist of lining, padding and chin strap.

(d) Handlebars. Handlebars on motorcycles and motor-driven cycles shall not exceed 12 inches in height, measured from the upper front fork plate, and under no conditions shall the highest point exceed 15 inches above the horizontal plane at the seat of such vehicle.

(e) Brakes. All motorcycles and motor-driven cycles shall be equipped with brakes adequate to control the movement of same to stop and hold such vehicle, including two separate means of applying the brakes, one means shall be effective to apply the brakes to the front wheel and one means shall be effective to apply the brakes to the rear wheels.

(Code 1956, § 38-162)

State law reference—Required equipment, R.S. 32:190 et seq.

laws.title: Muffler and exhaust system requirements
laws.content:
(a) Every motorcycle and motor-driven cycle shall at all times be equipped with a muffler in good working order and in constant operation.

(b) No person shall use a muffler cutout, bypass or similar device upon a motorcycle or motor-driven cycle on a street of the city.

(c) No person shall modify the exhaust system of a motorcycle or motor-driven cycle in a manner which will amplify or increase the noise emitted
