laws.title: Suspension of rules
laws.content:
In its sound discretion, the council may suspend the operation of any provision of this article or modify them instanter, or may authorize temporary rates and/or changes in service or, to the extent authorized by law, or after such proceedings and upon such conditions as it finds to be just and practicable, provided that any such suspension or modification or rate or service authorization shall be consistent with the provisions of the home rule charter of the city.

(Code 1956, § 52-144)

laws.title: Archives
laws.content:
The clerk shall keep all original copies of documents filed in proceedings governed under this article in the archives of the council, filed according to their docket number, and segregated from the other records of the council. All such documents shall be available for inspection and, for a reasonable fee, copying by members of the public. The fee to be charged for certified and uncertified copies shall be equal to the fee charged for certified and uncertified copies, respectively, by the clerk of the civil district court for the parish, provided that no officer, department, agency, or board of the city shall be charged such a fee. Parties or attorneys-at-law presenting proper identification may be permitted by the clerk to charge out a single copy of any such document for three days or less, upon giving receipt therefor, provided that no less than two originals shall remain

Supp. No. 64

CD158:23
§ 158-237

NEW ORLEANS CODE

in the custody of the clerk at all times, and at least one designated original of each document shall never leave the custody of the clerk.

(Code 1956, § 52-145)

laws.title: Computation of time
laws.content:
(a) *Computing time.* In computing any period of time prescribed or allowed by this article, by order of the council, or by any applicable statute, the rules prescribed by the Louisiana Code of Civil Procedure shall be controlling.

(b) *Extensions.* Unless otherwise provided, the time for filing any pleading or document, including a prehearing order, may, but shall not necessarily, be extended by order of the president of the council or in his absence, the vice-president of the council, or in the absence of both, by any two councilmembers, upon written motion duly filed with the clerk prior to the expiration of the applicable period of time for the filing of the same, showing that there is good cause for such extension of time and that the need therefor is not caused by the inexcusable neglect, indifference or lack of diligence of the party making such motion. A copy of any such motion shall be served contemporaneously with the filing thereof upon all other parties of record to the proceeding and upon all of the recipients of service specifically designated in section 158-236.

(Code 1956, § 52-103)

laws.title: Agreements to be in writing
laws.content:
No stipulation or agreement between the parties, their attorneys or representatives, with regard to any matter involved in any proceeding before the council under this article, shall be enforced unless it shall have been reduced to writing and signed by the parties or the representatives authorized hereunder to appear for them, or unless it shall have been dictated into the record by them during the course of a hearing, or incorporated in an order bearing their written approval; and any such stipulation or agreement shall be subject to council approval or the approval of the presiding officer provided for under section 158-432.

(Code 1956, § 52-104)

laws.title: Service
laws.content:
(a) Where public notice is permitted or required by this article, by other ordinances, by statute, or by the home rule charter, such public notice shall be given in the manner prescribed by applicable law in the official journal of the council.

(b) Whenever the council or its agents are required by this article, by other ordinances, by statute, or by the home rule charter to give notice other than by publication, the clerk of council shall mail the same, by certified and registered mail, to the last known place of address of the person entitled to receive such notice. Any party shown to have received actual and timely notice of a matter through any of the above methods shall not be permitted to rely upon lack of service as a defense in or as grounds for continuance of any proceeding.

(c) A copy of any protest, reply, answer, motion or other pleading or document or other filing filed by any party in any proceeding subsequent to the institution thereof shall be mailed or otherwise delivered by the party filing the same to every other known party of record, and if the filing constitutes a first appearance shall be accompanied by a statement of cause for interest in the proceeding and, to the degree possible, the names of witnesses to be called for a public hearing, and the anticipated time of that party’s presentation. If any party has appeared in the proceeding by attorney or other representative authorized under this article to make appearances, service shall be made upon such attorney or other representative. The willful failure of any party to make such service shall be sufficient grounds for the entry of an order by the council, striking the protest, reply, answer, motion or other pleading or document or other filing from the record.

(d) A certificate by the party, attorney or representative who files a pleading, document or other filing stating that it has been served on the other parties, shall be prima facie evidence of such service. The following form of certificate will be deemed sufficient in this connection:

I hereby certify that I have this ______ day of ______________, 19/20____, served the required number of copies of the

Supp. No. 64

CD158:24
UTILEITIES

§ 158-288

foregoing pleading upon all other known parties of this proceeding, by (here state the manner of service).

Signature

(Code 1956, § 52-105)

laws.title: Conduct and decorum
laws.content:
Every party, witness, attorney or other representative and every member of the public shall comport himself in all proceedings with proper dignity, courtesy and respect for the council, the clerk, and all other parties and persons present. Disorderly conduct will not be tolerated. Attorneys and other representatives of parties shall observe and practice the standards of ethical behavior prescribed for attorneys at law by the Louisiana State Bar Association, the Louisiana Supreme Court, and the Code of Civil Procedure. Any party, witness, attorney or other representative may be excluded by the council from any hearing for such period and upon such conditions as are just for violation of this rule, or may be subject to such other just, reasonable, and lawful disciplinary action as the council may lawfully prescribe.

(Code 1956, § 52-106)

Secs. 158-242—158-285. Reserved.

laws.title: Classification
laws.content:
(a) Parties to proceedings before the council under this article are subject to classification as applicants, protestants, petitioners, complainants, respondents and intervenors. Regardless of errors in their designations of themselves in their pleadings or other filings, the council may align parties in accordance with their interest in the proceedings.

(b) The department of finance through the director of the department of finance, shall be, ex officio, a party to all matters governed under this article, in which capacity he shall represent and

shall make recommendations as to the best interests of the city as a municipal corporation, e.g., to assert the city’s interest as an energy consumer.

(c) Any party of whom a greater filing fee is not required by another provision of law shall, at the time of first appearing in or filing in any matter governed by this article, remit to the clerk, in cash or by postal money order or certified check, a filing fee equal to the filing fee for an ordinary petition in the civil district court for the parish. Failure to remit the required fee shall be cause for dismissal of the party from the matter, provided that if a party would be entitled to appear in forma pauperis before the civil district court, the party shall not be dismissed for failure to pay the filing fee. No officer, department, agency or board of the city shall be required to remit a filing fee. The council may, in its sound discretion, waive the filing fee otherwise required herein as to any party or matter governed by this article by adopting a resolution providing for such waiver.

(Code 1956, § 52-107; Ord. No. 20,259, § 1, 7-19-01; Ord. No. 20,273, § 1, 8-2-01; M.C.S., Ord. No. 21480, § 4, 4-1-04; M.C.S., Ord. No. 21536, § 1, 5-6-04)

laws.title: Parties in interest
laws.content:
Any party actually in interest may appear in any proceeding before the council under this article. All appearances shall be subject to a motion to strike upon a showing that the party has no justiciable or administratively cognizable interest in the proceeding. Unless otherwise provided by law, any public official, agency, board or department of the city, the state or any of its political subdivisions, the United States Government, and every civic, consumer, public advocacy and trade organization shall be permitted to appear in any proceeding whether as a formal intervenor or otherwise, and present any relevant and proper testimony and evidence bearing upon the issues involved in the particular proceeding.

(Code 1956, § 52-108)

laws.title: Appearances personally or by representative
laws.content:
Any party may appear in proper person and/or be represented by an attorney-at-law authorized

Supp. No. 64

CD158:25
$\S$ 158-288

NEW ORLEANS CODE

to practice law before the supreme court of the State of Louisiana. A natural person whose interest in a matter arises in the course of his business may appear on his own behalf, or through a bona fide full-time employee who is his attorney in fact. A corporation, partnership or association may appear and be represented by any bona fide officer, partner, full-time employee, or other person presenting proof of his authority so to so appear. Any person appearing in a representative capacity before the council under this article other than as an attorney-at-law shall be required, in advance, to register with the clerk of council upon an appropriate form to be supplied by the clerk.

(Code 1956, § 52-109)

Secs. 158-289—158-320. Reserved.

laws.title: Form and content of pleadings
laws.content:
(a) All pleadings or other documents filed in any proceeding shall, unless the council otherwise orders or permits, be typewritten or printed and, to the maximum extent possible, pleadings shall be filed electronically. If typewritten, the impression shall be on one side of the paper, and lines shall be double-spaced, except that long quotations, schedules of data and tariffs may be single spaced, and indented. Mimeographed, multigraphed, hectographed, photostated or planographed papers and the like will be accepted as typewritten. If printed, the paper shall be unglazed, and the printing shall be in clear type, adequately leaded.

(b) Except as otherwise ordered or permitted by the council, all papers, except exhibits, shall be cut or folded so as not to exceed a width of $8\frac{1}{2}$ inches and a length of 14 inches, and shall have inside margins not less than one inch wide. Whenever practical, all exhibits of a documentary character shall conform to such requirements of size and margin.

(c) The original copy of every pleading or other filings shall be signed in ink by the party filing the paper, or by the officer, partner, attorney or other representative who appears for such party. Pleadings shall contain the address and telephone number of the party filing the paper or, if he is represented by an attorney or other representative, the name, business address and telephone number of such attorney or other representative. A private or United States Post Office Box or drawer shall not constitute a sufficient address for the purposes of this section.

(d) All pleadings shall contain:

(1) The official docket number and/or other official designation given to the case or matter by the clerk of council.

(2) The names of the party seeking to bring about or prevent action by the council or other parties.

(3) The names of all other known parties in interest, provided that known parties in interest as used herein shall not include persons whose only known interest is as a ratepayer, unless such person is already a party of record.

(4) A concise statement of the ultimate facts relied upon by the pleader.

(5) A prayer stating the type of relief, action or order desired by the pleader.

(6) A list of witnesses who may be called in the event of an oral hearing, and the anticipated time of presentation of the case.

(7) Any other matter required by the home rule charter or by statute, ordinance or rule.

(8) A certificate of service, where service is required by any provision of law.

Supp. No. 64

CD158:26
UTILITIES

§ 158-361

(e) During the pendency of a proceeding under this article, no party of record shall engage in any ex parte written communications with regard to any matter pending, with any councilmember or designated agency of the council.

(Code 1956, § 52-111; M.C.S., Ord. No. 22930, § 2, 12-6-07)

laws.title: Incorporation by reference of council records
laws.content:
Any pleading may adopt and incorporate, by specific reference thereto, any part of any document or entry in the official files and records of the council. Testimony, exhibits, and other matters of a like nature are excepted from this section, unless with specific approval of the council and this section shall not relieve any applicant of the necessity of alleging and providing in detail, where required, such facts as the council may in its sound discretion deem necessary to the proper determination of a case.

(Code 1956, § 52-115)

Secs. 158-327—158-360. Reserved.

laws.title: Place and nature of hearings
laws.content:
(a) All official hearings conducted in any proceeding governed by this article shall be open to the public. All hearings shall be held in the city, in the council chamber, city hall, unless the council shall designate another place of hearing. A public utility regulatory hearing or franchise regulation hearing under this article may be conducted within a regular or special meeting of the council, or may, under circumstances where the hearing is limited to inquiries into fact by a referee, special master, administrative law judge, or designated agent or hearing officer of the council, be held before such officer outside of a council meeting and outside the presence of the council. If a hearing is held before the council at a meeting thereof, the president of the council shall declare for the record the time at which such hearing commences and is concluded and the times at which it shall digress from or continue utility or franchise council business. No such digression from or continuance of utility or franchise business shall occur except upon approval of a motion so to digress or to continue. The clerk shall provide for recordation, by a certified court reporter, of any hearing under this article.

(b) Whenever it is deemed desirable by the council that members of the public at large who are not parties of record should be heard on any matter under this article, or wherever such

hearing is required by the city charter or any applicable law, the council president or other presiding officer shall declare at the beginning and end of the at-large hearing the nature of such hearing, and shall declare that no part of statements made or evidence adduced at such at-large public hearing shall, in legal terms, form (and such matter shall not form) the basis of any council decision in a contested proceeding. No member of the public at large who speaks as such, and not as a party of record, shall be compelled to submit to cross-examination under an instanter subpoena.

(Code 1956, § 52-123)

laws.title: Formal exceptions
laws.content:
Formal exceptions to rulings of the presiding officer during a hearing shall be unnecessary. It shall be sufficient that the party at the time any ruling is made or sought shall make known to the presiding officer the action which he desires.

(Code 1956, § 52-127)

laws.title: Briefs
laws.content:
Briefs shall be filed only when requested or permitted by the council or by the presiding officer in a proceeding. They shall conform, as near as may

CD158:28

laws.title: Admissibility in general
laws.content:
Any evidence which would be admissible under the general statutes of the state, or under the rules of evidence governing proceedings in matters not involving a trial by jury in the courts of the state, shall be admissible before the council or its agents in matters governed by this article. Other evidence may be admitted by the council or its presiding agents if it is at all probative and relevant provided the substantive rights of all parties are protected. The rules of evidence shall be applied liberally in any proceeding to the end that all needful and proper evidence shall be conveniently, inexpensively and speedily heard while preserving the substantive rights of the parties to the proceeding.

(Code 1956, § 52-129)

laws.title: Evidence in uncontested proceedings
laws.content:
In any uncontested proceeding, the council or its presiding agents shall receive, without regard to the legal rules of admissibility, any evidence of a form and character which would ordinarily be relied upon by a prudent person in an ordinary business transaction, including, without limitation, affidavits, documents and other forms of heresay testimony deemed by him to be reliable.

(Code 1956, § 52-130)

laws.title: Prepared testimony
laws.content:
In all proceedings, with leave of or upon order of the council, or its designated presiding agents, and after service of copies upon all parties upon whom service may be required by section 158-240, at such time as may be designated by a majority of the council or its designated presiding agents, the prepared testimony of a witness upon direct examination, in either narrative or question and answer form, may or, upon order, shall be incorporated in the record as if read, or received as an exhibit, upon the witness’s being sworn and identifying the same, or upon the prefilng of the same accompanied by an affidavit incorporating the same in a statement under oath by reference. Such witness shall be subject to cross examination and the prepared testimony shall be subject to a motion to strike in whole or in parts.

(Code 1956, § 52-131)

laws.title: Limitations on number of witnesses
laws.content:
The council, or its designated presiding agent, shall have the right in any proceeding to limit the number of witnesses whose testimony is merely cumulative.

(Code 1956, § 52-132)

laws.title: Exhibits
laws.content:
(a) Form. Exhibits of documentary character shall be of such size as not unduly to encumber the files and records of the council. Wherever practicable the sheets of each exhibit shall be not more than 8½ inches by 14 inches in size and shall be numbered, and there shall be a brief statement on the first sheet of the exhibit of what the exhibit purports to show. Exhibits shall be limited to factual material relevant to the issue involved in a particular proceeding.

(b) Tender and service. The original of each exhibit offered shall be tendered to the clerk or a deputy clerk for identification; a copy shall be furnished each councilmember and/or presiding agent of the council, one copy each to the clerk and each counsel for the council, and one copy to each other party of record or his attorney or representative and every other person upon whom any filings or copies of same are required by section 158-236

CD158:29
§ 158-480

NEW ORLEANS CODE

and upon whom service is required by section 158-240. If any of the persons be not present at the time of tender, his copy shall be furnished to the clerk for later transmittal to that person.

(c) Excluded exhibits. If an exhibit has been identified, objected to and excluded, the presiding officer shall determine whether or not the party offering the exhibit withdraws the offer, and if so, permit the return of the exhibit to him. If the excluded exhibit is not withdrawn, it shall be given an exhibit number for identification, shall be endorsed by the presiding officer with his ruling, and shall be included in the record, for the purpose only of preserving the exception.

(d) After hearing. Unless specifically directed by the council, no exhibit will be permitted to be filed in any proceeding after the conclusion of the hearing.

(Code 1956, § 52-133)

laws.title: Subpoenas
laws.content:
(a) Subpoenas for the attendance of witnesses from any place in the state, or for the production of books, papers, accounts or documents at a hearing in a pending proceeding, may be issued by the council, as provided elsewhere in this Code, upon its own motion, or upon the written motion of a party showing that there is good cause for the issuance of same.

(b) Motions for subpoenas to compel that production of books, papers, accounts or documents shall be verified and shall specify as nearly as may be possible the books, papers, accounts or documents desired and the material and relevant facts to be proved by them. No such subpoena shall be issued unless the president, with the advice of the city attorney, shall determine that the matter sought is relevant, material and necessary and that the production of such books, papers, accounts or documents will not result in unnecessary harassment, imposition, or undue inconvenience or expense to the party to be required to produce the same. No subpoena shall issue for material alleged to be of a trade secret or confidential nature unless it be shown after hearing of arguments on the same that no other alternative, such as a protective order, within the meaning of the Louisiana Code of Civil Procedure, will accomplish a result consistent with the interests of all parties and the public.

(Code 1956, § 52-136)

laws.title: Form of exceptions and replies
laws.content:
Exceptions and replies shall conform as near as may be to the rules herein provided for form of pleadings. The specific exceptions shall be concisely stated. The evidence relied upon shall be pointed out with particularity, and such evidence and the argument shall be grouped under the exceptions to which they relate.

(Code 1956, § 52-137)

laws.title: Oral argument
laws.content:
Any party may request oral argument at any time prior to the final determination of any proceeding, but oral argument shall be allowed only in the sound discretion of the council or its designated presiding agent. A request for oral argument may be incorporated in the exceptions, reply to exceptions, petition for reconsideration or in a separate pleading.

(Code 1956, § 52-138)

laws.title: Form, content and service of orders
laws.content:
All orders of the council shall be in writing and shall be signed by at least four councilmembers. Abstentions shall be regarded as total nonparticipation by the abstaining councilmember, except where an abstention deadlocks the participatory vote, in which case, if after reconsideration the deadlock remains, an abstention shall be taken as a denial of the relief sought. Such findings of fact as the record justifies may be incorporated either in the body of the order or by reference to the official record. A copy of each order shall be served forthwith by the clerk upon all parties to the proceeding and upon all persons required to be served under section 158-240. All orders shall go into effect ten days after mailing thereof, unless otherwise provided.

(Code 1956, § 52-140)

laws.title: Show cause orders and complaints; contempt
laws.content:
The council, either on its own motion or upon receipt of sufficient written complaints, may, in its sound discretion, at any time after legal notice to all interested parties, cite any person operating under its jurisdiction to appear before it in a public hearing and require him or it to show cause why his or its franchise or operating authority should not be revoked, suspended or amended, or why some other action available to the council be taken, for failure to comply with any applicable statute, order or the rules, rates, regulations or general order of the council. All hearings of such proceedings shall be conducted in accordance with the provisions of this article; provided that in any proceeding wherein the public interest may be seriously and adversely affected, or service to the public discontinued, the council may issue on its own motion a restraining order for purpose of protecting the public interest until the matter may be orderly heard and a decision rendered thereon.

(Code 1956, § 52-141)

Secs. 158-513—158-545. Reserved.

laws.title: Generally
laws.content:
**Sec. 158-581. Rules and regulations.**

The chief administrative officer, pursuant to section 4-302 of the home rule charter, shall adopt, promulgate, and implement rules, regulations, and internal administrative procedures to ensure that all the provisions of this article are applied and complied with by all city officials, departments, boards, and agencies to the fullest extent practicable.

(Code 1956, § 52-74)

**Sec. 158-582. Assessment deemed legitimate operating expense.**

Payments made by any public utility or person under this article shall be considered a legitimate operating expense of the utility for rate-making or other purposes; provided, that any expense incurred by any company or person under sections 158-661 or 158-691 may be disallowed as a legitimate expense and not recoverable by such company or person if the council determines, in the course of a rate case or in other due proceedings, that such expenses were caused by the malice, imprudence, neglect, or recklessness of such company or person or the attorneys, agents, or employees thereof. In no case shall an expense attributable to the frivolous institution, frivolous prosecution or frivolous defense of litigation or other proceedings be deemed a legitimate and

recoverable expense. An institution, prosecution, or defense shall be deemed frivolous whenever it would or could not have been advised or undertaken by a prudent, ethical, reasonable and knowledgeable attorney-at-law. Similarly, no expense arising out of a special investigation or proceedings under section 158-626 or 158-661 shall be deemed a legitimate and recoverable expense of a particular utility or person if such investigation or proceeding is occasioned by or discloses unlawful or grossly negligent or reckless conduct by such utility or other person subject to this article.

(Code 1956, § 52-71)

**Sec. 158-583. Excessive charges.**

(a) On written appeal filed with the clerk of council within 30 days of the rendition or effective or due date, as the case may be, of any bill or assessment pursuant to this article, the party so charged shall be afforded an opportunity to be heard as to the reasonableness of the amount thereof.

(b) The hearing shall be conducted before the council or its designated referee. The director of the department of finance or his designee, represented, upon request of the director of the department of finance, by the department of law, shall appear at the hearing to defend the reasonableness of the bill or assessment being challenged. If the bill or assessment be found unreasonable or excessive, it shall be set aside or reduced. The council shall decide the appeal within 60 days of its filing. The pendency of an appeal under this section shall not suspend interest or penalties on any past due bill or assessment, except with respect to any bill, assessment, or portion thereof found to be excessive by the council. Any sums which have actually been paid under protest by a utility, person or corporation which are subsequently found, pursuant to this section, to have been unreasonable or excessive and therefore not to have been due, shall be refunded with legal interest within 30 days of the decision of the council. Any party aggrieved by a decision of the council under this section may appeal therefrom to the civil district court for the parish.

(Code 1956, § 52-72; M.C.S., Ord. No. 21480, § 4, 4-1-04; M.C.S., Ord. No. 21536, § 1, 5-6-04)

*Cross reference—Franchises, § 30-36 et seq.

Supp. No. 30

CD158:32

laws.title: Article not exclusive
laws.content:
Any assessment or billing under this article shall be in addition to any and all property, franchise, license and other taxes and fees and charges now or hereafter fixed, assessed or charged by law against any public utility, person, or corporation.

(Code 1956, § 52-73)

laws.title: Access to records
laws.content:
Pursuant to and subject to the terms and limitations of the Louisiana Public Records laws, any public utility or other person subject to the provisions of this article shall have the right to inspect and copy public records of the city for the purpose of verifying or investigating any cost or expense incurred by the city or its agents.

(Code 1956, § 52-75)

laws.title: Assessments upon public utilities
laws.content:
(a) A general annual assessment is hereby imposed upon each public utility serving the ultimate consumer (other than those regulated under chapter 162 and other than governmental entities or political subdivisions) within the city and subject to the authority of the council to supervise, regulate, and control rates or services, which assessment shall be equal to one-sixth of one percent of its gross receipts from rates charged the ultimate consumers in the parish during the preceding fiscal year of such utility, for the purpose of defraying the costs and expenses incurred in the ordinary and routine investigation, supervision, regulation, and control of the affairs of each such utility. From time to time, with the advice of the department of finance or the chief administrative officer as provided hereinafter, the director of the department of finance shall, subject to the approval of the council, adjust this assessment to provide a level of income sufficient to fund ordinary and routine general regulatory operations and activities of the city. In the case of a company or person commencing business in the parish during a particular calendar year which has had no receipts derived from the parish in its preceding fiscal year upon which a calculation may be based, a provisional general annual assessment shall be assessed for the calendar year in which the company or person commences doing business in the parish of one and one-half percent of the dollar sum obtained by multiplying the gross receipt of the company or person during the first 90 days of operation times the factor obtained by dividing the number of days remaining in the year beginning with the first day of operation over the total number of days in the year.

(b) No provision of this section or any other section of this division shall apply to any cable television company doing business in this parish on the effective date of the ordinance from which this article was derived.

(Code 1956, § 52-60; M.C.S., Ord. No. 21480, § 4, 4-1-04; M.C.S., Ord. No. 21536, § 1, 5-6-04)

laws.title: Payment dates; delinquency
laws.content:
All annual general assessments shall be due on March 1 of each year and shall be paid by check or postal money order to the director of the department of finance. Any public utility may elect, however, to pay the annual general assessment in quarterly payments due on or before March 31, June 30, September 30, and December 31 of each year.

(Code 1956, § 52-61)

laws.title: Penalties and interest
laws.content:
A penalty of an additional fee of ten percent of the amount due under any assessment or billing under this article shall be assessed for any late payment. Interest shall accrue on fees delinquent for more than 30 days, at the rate of legal interest established in the Civil Code of Louisiana calculated on the total of both the assessment or billing and the penalty due.

(Code 1956, § 52-62)

laws.title: Payment into general fund
laws.content:
All fees, penalties, and interest paid to the city under the provisions of this article shall be paid

Supp. No. 30

CD158:33
$\S$ 158-624

NEW ORLEANS CODE

into the general fund but shall thereafter be expended only for the purpose of funding regulatory operations and activities of the city (other than operations or activities governed by chapter 162 of this Code).

(Code 1956, $\S$ 52-63)

**Sec. 158-625. Records and adjustments.**

The chief administrative officer shall devise and implement a system of recordkeeping and accounting which will enable him to determine, and he shall determine, at the end of each calendar quarter, the actual cost to provide a reasonable level of funding for all ordinary and routine regulatory operations and activities of the city (other than those governed by chapter 162 of this Code) for the quarter just ended. The quarterly determination shall be transmitted to the director of the department of finance, who shall promptly review the same and determine whether, based on reasonable assumptions, the rate of general annual assessment then in effect will be sufficient to defray the ordinary and routine regulatory costs which it is anticipated the city will have incurred by the end of the then-current quarter or any subsequent quarter. If the director of the department of finance determines that the assessment then in effect will not be sufficient, he shall make and promulgate a rule adjusting the assessment then in effect to a sufficient level. The rule shall become effective and binding when approved by a resolution of the council after notice to and public hearing of the utilities affected thereby. The notice of the public hearing shall be advertised in the I (sic) official journal, and members of the public shall be entitled to participate therein. If a utility has elected to pay the general annual assessment on an annual basis, the adjusted assessment shall be applicable to it beginning with the calendar year following the effective date of the adjustment rule. If a utility has elected to pay the general annual assessment in quarterly installments, the adjusted assessment shall be applicable to it for the remaining quarters of the current calendar year and thereafter, and all quarterly installments for the current calendar year due subsequent to the effective date of the adjustment rule shall be increased by a percentage equal to the percentage by which the adjust-

ment rule shall have increased the previously effective rate of annual general assessment. Any such adjustment rule shall expire on the last day of the calendar year following the calendar year of its adoption; provided that nothing in this sentence shall impair the power of the council to amend by ordinance the rate of the annual general assessment established under this article.

(Code 1956, $\S$ 52-64; M.C.S., Ord. No. 21480, $\S$ 4, 4-1-04; M.C.S., Ord. No. 21536, $\S$ 1, 5-6-04)

**Sec. 158-626. Special assessments.**

Nothing in this article shall preclude or limit the exercise by the council of any right it may have, under section 4-1604 of the charter of the city or any other applicable law, to make special assessments upon a particular utility to defray costs in regulatory operations or activities (including but not limited to litigation or special investigations) which are not ordinary and routine. Nothing in this article shall preclude the assessment of fees or charges for processing or evaluating initial applications or requests for franchises, certificates, or authority to do business or provide service, made by new utilities.

(Code 1956, $\S$ 52-65)

**Sec. 158-627. Annual supplemental assessment or credit.**

On or before February 28 of each year, the director of the department of finance, under the direction of the chief administrative officer, shall compute the actual costs and expenses of the city for the preceding calendar year and, after deducting the amounts previously recovered from utilities pursuant to this article or pursuant to section 4-1301 of the Home Rule Charter shall, on or before March 15, assess a supplemental annual assessment applicable on a one-time basis to the preceding calendar year at a rate sufficient to defray all unrecovered costs and shall send to each public utility company affected thereby a statement setting forth the amount due and payable by, or the amount standing to the credit of, such public utility company. Any amount owing by any public utility company shall be paid not later than 30 days following the date such statement is received. Any such amount standing to the credit of any public utility company shall be

Supp. No. 30

CD158:34
UTILITIES

§ 158-661

applied as a credit against any succeeding payment due. The supplemental general assessment or credit made under this section attributed to any utility company or person shall be proportional to the amount originally owing to the city by that particular utility company or person under the annual general assessment imposed by section 158-621.

(Code 1956, § 52-66; M.C.S., Ord. No. 21480, § 4, 4-1-04; M.C.S., Ord. No. 21536, § 1, 5-6-04)

**Sec. 158-628. Illustrative costs.**

The costs which are intended to be defrayed by the annual general assessment and supplemental general assessment under this article include, but are not limited to, that portion of fees of experts and consultants and that portion of the compensation and expenses of the council members, the council staff, the director of the department of finance and the staff of the department of finance, the city attorney and the staff of the department of law, or any other city agency or department, which are attributable to the expenditure of time, money, or resources on ordinary and routine general regulatory operations and activities (other than those governed by chapter 162 of this Code), including the cost of retirement contributions, Social Security, worker’s compensation, annual leave, sick leave, compensation time, overtime pay, and other fringe benefits and compensation and including all equipment, services, and supply purchase expenses, overhead expenses, and all other items of maintenance and operation expenses and all other direct and indirect costs, including the costs of general and routine investigations or studies initiated by the council or director of the department of finance. Ordinary and routine regulatory operations and activities shall be deemed to include, but not be limited to, any and all reasonable exercises of the powers of supervision, regulation, and control of the rates and services of public utilities except the consideration or disposition of extraordinary matters such as rate cases.

(Code 1956, § 52-67; M.C.S., Ord. No. 21480, § 4, 4-1-04; M.C.S., Ord. No. 21536, § 1, 5-6-04)

**Sec. 158-629. Maximum and minimum assessment.**

An adjusted general annual assessment imposed upon a public utility company under this article (including any supplemental assessment under section 158-627) shall not exceed one-third of one percent of the gross receipts of the public utility company derived from rates charged the ultimate consumers in the parish in the last preceding fiscal year of such utility. In no case shall an annual assessment under this division be less than $500.00.

(Code 1956, § 52-68)

Secs. 158-630—158-660. Reserved.

**Sec. 158-661. Persons not subject to rates or service regulation.**

(a) No person who is subject to the jurisdiction of the council only with respect to safety of his operations, enforcement of franchises or permits, or the payment of permit fees for the use of the streets or public ways shall be subject to the annual general assessment provided for under this article.

(b) In the case of corporations or persons subject to the jurisdiction of the council only with respect to safety of operations, enforcement of franchises or permits, or the payment of permit fees for the use of the streets or public rights-of-way, the director of the department of finance shall ascertain from time to time, but not less than once in each year, all reasonable direct and indirect costs, actually incurred, of special investigations of the safety of the plants or operation of such persons or corporations or special investigations or proceedings to supervise their compliance with the terms of their franchises or permits or the sufficiency of the payment of their permit fees. The costs incurred in any special investigations or proceedings to supervise shall not be assessed against any company or person unless such special investigations or proceedings have been initiated by a resolution of the council or have been initiated by a pleading filed and docketed with the council and subsequently declared, by council motion or resolution, to constitute a matter of substantial public importance. The director shall for each investigation or case of

laws.title: Costs of proceedings and litigation
laws.content:
(a) Whenever such costs are not otherwise recovered under another section of this article or any other provision of law or pursuant to an award by a competent court or other forum, the director of the department of finance, upon the recommendation of the city attorney, shall assess against public utilities, persons, or corporations all costs and expenses incurred by the city in the conduct of or participation in judicial, administrative or other proceedings which directly or indirectly affect the council’s powers of supervision, regulation, and control of rates and services, the franchise and permit powers of the city, or the powers and duties of the department of finance or which directly or indirectly affect the interests of the ratepayers of the city, and/or which are otherwise related to such other matters over which the council has jurisdiction, including the costs, fees, and expenses of all services provided by consultants, engineers, attorneys, experts and such other persons whose services are deemed useful because of their having expertise in the supervision, regulation, and control of a public utility or in the enforcement of franchises or permits [or permits]. The proceedings the costs of which may be recovered under this section shall include but not be limited to proceedings which have been commenced or instituted by the city itself, or proceedings into which the city has voluntarily joined or intervened, as well as proceedings in which the city has been made a defendant or has been involuntarily joined, but shall not include proceedings instituted or intervened in by the city in which the city is dismissed or denied intervention because the city lacks standing.

(b) Costs recoverable under this section shall be assessed in equal shares against each public utility, franchisee, or permittee subject to the supervision, regulation, and control or otherwise subject to the jurisdiction of the council or the city which is or has been a party to the particular proceeding in question. A bill for the assessment shall be served by the director of the department of finance upon the assessed utility within 15 days of the receipt of the recommendation by the city attorney, and shall be due and payable on or before the 30th day following service.

(c) No assessment shall be made under this section against a litigant whose position in litigation was adverse to that of the city and whose position prevails. A party adverse to the city shall not be deemed not to have prevailed because the said party has agreed to a settlement, compromise or transaction; provided, however, that any such contract may provide for responsibility of the parties thereto for costs and attorney’s fees.

(a) Each utility shall be required to develop and file for review and approval by the council a least-cost resource plan as described by these regulations. The city council shall take such action within 12 months of the date of a complete plan filing as prescribed in section 158-767(a) through (f).

laws.title: Same—Contents of energy and demand forecasts
Same—Forecasting methods and determinants
laws.content:
(a) *Forecasting methods.* Commencing with the plan filed in 1994, utility forecasts shall be based on disaggregated end-use methods unless the utility obtains a waiver from the city council by showing that an alternative forecasting method is superior for LCP. Prior to the 1994 plan filing, forecasts which are based on any other method shall be disaggregated into estimated end-use components, and the methods for forecasting and estimating end-use components shall be fully explained and justified.

(b) *Forecasting determinants.* Each forecast of energy and demand shall identify and describe the significant determinants assumed in forecasting future peak demand and energy usage, shall specifically include a detailed description of the source of all such determinants, and shall document and fully justify the procedure by which the determinants were incorporated into the peak demand and energy usage forecasts. The determinants used in forecasting energy and demand must be consistent with and integrated into the different components of the forecast.

(c) *Data requirements.* Energy and demand forecasts shall be based on the best available data. Where reliable data are not available, estimates should be used and fully justified. The utility shall develop a data base of electricity consumption patterns by customer class and by end-use. The utility shall conduct periodic customer surveys to obtain current data on end-use appliance penetration and saturation rates and end-use electricity consumption patterns. A proposed schedule for such surveys shall be submitted with each energy and demand forecast. Each forecast shall include a detailed description of data used in making the forecast, an identification of the sources of such data, and an explanation of techniques employed for gathering, organizing, adjusting, or interpreting the data.

(d) *Econometric forecasting methods.* Where statistical or econometric methods are used in developing forecast inputs or in the forecasting process,

analyses of the reasonableness of such methods and models shall be presented, including statistical documentation and justification of each equation, variable selection, estimated coefficients, theoretical or empirical basis for functional form, and method of estimation.

(e) *Forecasting models.* Each energy and demand forecast shall include a complete description of the model or models used, including justification of model design and explanation of variables used.  
(Code 1956, § 52-353(c))

laws.title: Same—Sensitivity analyses and contingency planning
laws.content:
(a) *Sensitivity to major assumptions.* Each energy and demand forecast shall include an analysis of the sensitivity of results to the major assumptions and estimates used in preparing the forecast. The major assumptions to be tested should include end-use efficiencies and saturation rates, electricity prices, prices of competing fuels, demographic projections, economic projections, and any other major determinant of energy use or demand. Sensitivity analyses shall assess the uncertainty ranges and the consequences of uncertainty for each of the major assumptions and combination of assumptions.

(b) *Contingency planning.* Each plan must contain a series of demand forecasts which represents a reasonable range of electricity sales and demand which it may be required to serve. The contingency planning forecasts must be sufficiently different to meaningfully test the flexibility and robustness of the preferred and alternative resource plans. As a minimum, the sensitivity to alternative assumptions of demand determinants should be used to set the range of the contingency planning forecasts. If that range is insufficient to test the resource plans, a sufficient range may be selected. The contingency planning forecasts should include the following:

(1) A base case scenario, which incorporates all assumptions which the utility determines to be most likely. This case shall be used to project, among other things, revenue requirements, avoided costs, and resource blocks;

(2) A high growth scenario, to be used as a basis for developing a full array of resource options for consideration and to assess resource plan robustness;

(3) A low growth scenario, to be used as a basis for assessing the impact of lower than projected energy and demand growth on resource plan robustness.

(Code 1956, § 52-353(d))

laws.title: Existing resources
laws.content:
(a) Resource identification. The utility shall discuss and describe all existing resources, including utility demand-side resources, purchases from nonutility sources, purchases from other utilities, pooling or coordination agreements that reduce resource requirements, and owned or partially-owned generating facilities. The utility shall also discuss and describe all resources available to the system, to the extent that these resources affect the resources available to the utility. This description shall include the same information required for potential future options, as described in sections 158-774 through 158-776. The utility shall report actual historic information (including the most recent ten years), as well as a projection of future information through the life of the resource. Any predicted changes must be fully documented and justified. The information assembled must be used by the utility in evaluating existing resources and assessing future resource options.

(b) Assessment of existing transmission. The utility shall analyze the adequacy of its existing transmission system to meet loads over a minimum of the next ten years, with projections for the following ten years, to identify areas where the transmission system is not capable of carrying loads, and to identify and analyze possible solutions to the transmission problems areas. The utility shall document its analysis, including providing transmission power flow studies supporting its conclusions. The transmission analysis shall include a sufficient portion of the regional and system transmission facilities to reasonably represent utility transmission system problems and solutions.

(c) Assessments regarding future requirements. Each utility shall assess the role of existing demand-side and supply-side resources in meeting future demand requirements. Each resource shall be considered for the potential of continued use, upgrading, repowering, life extension, temporary mothballing, retirement, or other options. For those resources for which any action other than continued use appears to be cost-effective, the utility shall assess and document the cost and benefit associated with any such action, and justify why such action will or will not be taken. The utility shall report, consistent with U.S. Department of Energy Form IE-411, any planned retirements, changes in ratings, or any other expected changes in the amount or availability of existing resources.

(Code 1956, § 52-354(a))

laws.title: Potential utility demand-side resources
laws.content:
(a) Assessing resources. The utility shall assess the full technical potential of future demand-side resources as a guide for developing comprehensive demand-side programs. Demand-side resources shall be evaluated for each customer segment, and shall include technologies such as, but not limited to, insulation, weatherization, heat recovery, efficient lighting, efficient motor drives, efficient refrigeration, efficient air conditioning, high efficiency furnaces, high efficiency water heating, and efficient architectural design standards. The utility shall compile a list of all available demand-side resources and, after consultation with the working group, assess those with a reasonable probability of passing the screening test in developing demand-side programs, as described in sections 158-788 through 158-793, and a least-cost resource plan. The assessment of technical options shall consider and, where appropriate, be based upon the inventory of end-use devices and consumption patterns developed for energy and demand forecasting as described in sections 158-769 through 158-772. For purposes of these regulations, full technical potential is defined as the amount of capacity and energy that could be obtained from the direct installation and use of the most efficient equipment and technology, without regard for economic limitations or market barriers.

(b) Alternative fuels. The utility shall examine, as a demand-side resource, end-uses employing alternative fuels that are also offered by the utility,

its parent holding company, or its affiliates within the jurisdiction, on the effective date of this article. The utility shall justify its selection of resource options, in light of options involving the use of alternative fuels, by using the screening test.

(c) Increased consumption. The utility shall demonstrate that any planned demand-side resources that increase overall electricity consumption contribute to increasing the net societal value relative to options that do not increase electricity consumption.

(d) Screening. The utility shall screen all demand-side resources utilizing the screening test.

(1) Program administrative costs shall not be included in the total cost for the initial screening of the measure for programs yet to be designed. After programs are designed, program administrative costs are estimated and shall be included in subsequent screening of demand-side programs.

(2) For options utilizing alternative fuels also offered by the utility, its parent holding company, or its affiliates, costs and benefits shall also include the changes in the costs of production, gathering, transmission, distribution, storage, and consumption of such alternative fuels, as valued using economic marginal costs.

(3) Program costs include the participant’s direct cost of a demand-side resource, the utility’s direct cost of a demand-side resource, and the utility’s administrative cost for developing and implementing the demand-side resource. Participant’s costs are incremental costs and include only those costs which would not have been incurred but for participation in the program. If a program also provides other benefits, such as improved amenities or other fuel savings, a reasonable allocation of program costs shall be made.

(4) Utility estimates of these costs and benefits should, to the extent practicable, be differentiated according to seasonal, daily, and hourly cost variations. The time period for evaluation of a program’s cost-effectiveness should to the extent practicable be the same period used by the utility for evaluating electric supply-side resources.

(e) Resource elimination. Those options which fail the screening test shall be eliminated from pilot or full-scale program consideration for inclusion in the resource plans. If the utility eliminates any demand-side resources, each such option shall be identified, and the reason for rejection shall be fully explained and justified.

(Code 1956, § 52-354(b))

laws.title: Demand-side program costs
Projected effects of demand-side program designs
laws.content:
The effects on energy consumption and peak demand of each program design developed pursuant to this section shall be estimated by program.

(1) The estimates shall be based on the resource savings and market penetration data of demand-side resources, as developed pursuant to sections 158-774(a) and 158-788(c) respectively, adjusted for the interactions between demand-side resources. Interaction can reduce the energy savings attributable to specific resources, in comparison to those same resources standing alone.

(2) The estimates shall include the annual change in energy consumption and peak demand pursuant to the program for:

a. Each year of the program’s assumed operation; and

b. Each year after the program’s assumed cessation in which the demand-side resources caused to be implemented by the program are expected to remain in place.

(3) The effects of each demand-side program on the rate of use of each energy form shall also be estimated. At a minimum, where applicable, program effects on maximum annual (hourly or daily) demand, maximum seasonal demand, and average demand during any time-varying energy costing periods used by the utility (on-peak, off-peak, shoulder) shall be estimated.

**Sec. 158-792. Demand-side program screening.**

The utility shall screen all demand-side programs using the screening test to determine which shall be considered for inclusion in the development of all resource plans. Although demand-side programs are comprised of demand-side resources which individually passed the screening test, the inclusion of program administrative cost and the effect of interaction between demand-side resources on program impact may cause some programs to fail the screening test. Programs which fail should be reviewed and modified to improve their cost-effectiveness.

(Code 1956, § 52-355(e))

**Sec. 158-793. Demand-side program evaluation.**

(a) Each utility shall develop a plan to evaluate the program implementation process and impact on energy use of demand-side programs. The plan shall identify the anticipated method for evaluating the defects of each program design developed pursuant to section 158-788. The plan shall identify procedures to be employed with regard to the following aspects of the evaluation of each program:

(1) Establishment of protocols to collect basic data describing program activity, including utility actions to optimize market penetration of programs;

(2) Comparison of demand patterns of similar participant and nonparticipant groups, and/or use of customer bill analysis, engineering estimates, meter data or other methods to identify the impact before and after program participation on customer’s usage and demand patterns.

(b) The utility shall use program evaluation data gathered from previous demand-side programs implemented in the past two years to assist in the development of program designs as required in sections 158-788 through 158-792.

(Code 1956, § 52-355(f))

**Sec. 158-794. Cost recovery and incentives.**

(a) *Cost recovery.* All prudent and reasonable costs incurred by the utility in:

(1) Developing its plan;

(2) Preparing and advancing applications for resources consistent with the plans approved by the city council; and

(3) Implementing full-scale or pilot demand-side programs which have been approved by the city council as part of the utility’s action plan;

are properly includable for recovery through general rates, pursuant to the established procedures for adjusting general rates, and/or other appropriate mechanisms.

(b) *Accounting for costs.* All costs for developing a least-cost resource plan, preparing and advancing resource options, and for implementing demand-side programs must be accounted for in the utility’s books and records separately from accounts attributable to any other activities. All accounts must be maintained in such a manner as will allow these costs to be identified readily. Costs attributable to specific programs must be readily identified.

(c) *Recovery of lost contributions.* To the extent that the utility demonstrates that successful implementation of demand-side programs will decrease sales below the volumes which the city council determines would be sufficient to recover fixed costs, the city council may allow the utility to recover lost contributions resulting from implementation of demand-side programs.

(d) *Utility financial incentive mechanisms.* Based upon the utility’s pursuit of least-cost planning in the city, the city council may, among other approaches, adjust the utility’s rate of return on common equity.

(Code 1956, § 52-358)

**Sec. 158-847. If connection found to exist public water to be cut off.**

If the representatives of the sewerage and water board upon making inspection of any premises finds that a connection exists in violation of the provisions of this article, the sewerage and water board shall thereupon cease supplying with potable public water any person, political subdivision of the state or federal agency upon whose premises such connection is found to exist, unless and until such connection is disconnected so that there will be no further possibility of the commingling of the potable public water supply and any other water supply, the source of which is distinct from the potable public water supply.  
(Code 1956, § 59-21)

**Sec. 158-848. Prohibition of connections.**

It shall be unlawful for any owner, tenant, or other person directly to discharge or to allow to be discharged directly from the premises owned or occupied by such person into the subpavement pipes or drains connecting the premises owned or occupied by such person, with the conduits constructed or to be constructed for the disposal of stormwater only, anything except the runoff from the rainfall upon such premises. Nothing in this section shall be construed as prohibiting owners, tenants or other persons from discharging into the open gutters of the streets any output from their premises permitted by the department of health. The intention of this section is to exclude the output of any privy, bath, sink, factory or other source of sewage from the drainage conduits and to confine it exclusively to the sewerage system or, in other words, to keep the drains for drainage and the sewers for sewerage.  
(Code 1956, § 59-22)

**Sec. 158-849. Penalty applicable to plumbers who make connections.**

The prohibition provided in section 158-848 shall apply not alone to the owner or occupant of the premises, but alike to the plumber or other person who shall do the work of fitting and connecting the discharge of anything other than the runoff from rainfall with the subpavement drain pipes, and they may both be adjudged guilty of the same offense.  
(Code 1956, § 59-23)

Secs. 158-850—158-890. Reserved.

Pending the laying of wires and electrical conductors underground in pursuance of existing ordinances or of ordinances which may hereafter be passed by the council, the provisions of this article shall govern the erection of poles and the stringing of wires overhead.  
(Code 1956, § 21-1)

**Sec. 158-1041. Purpose.**

The purpose of this article is to create a customer bill of rights which includes an expedited process for addressing certain complaints filed against utilities providing electric and/or gas services to customers in the city.

**Sec. 158-1042. Definitions.**

The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this Article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning.

*Complaint*—A serious or good-faith difference between the customer and utility concerning the imposition of a utility charge, rule or service that would constitute a violation of the customer service regulations, and that would require an investigation, account review and/or may require corrective action by the utility, whether the complaint is written or communicated orally, e.g., the misapplication of a council-approved electric or natural gas rate schedule for service, including net metering service as approved by council resolutions R-07-132 and R-07-221:

(3) Disconnection without cause, the improper disconnection of service, lack of appropriate notification of impending disconnection, or failure to adequately notify of scheduled outages on the distribution system;

laws.title: Enumerated rights
laws.content:
Among the rights that are more fully set forth in the council-adopted customer service regulations governing the provision of utility services in New Orleans, customers shall have the following rights:

(a) The right to safe and reliable service in accordance with industry standards.

(b) For residential customers, the right to choose to pay a deposit or obtain a satisfactory credit score in lieu of a deposit on a nondiscriminatory basis. For commercial and industrial customers, the right to choose to pay a deposit or to obtain an irrevocable bank letter of credit or surety bond from a bank or surety company acceptable to the utility.

(c) The right to earn interest on any deposit at a rate ordered from time to time by the council.

(d) For residential customers, the right to have any deposit returned after 24 months if customer has paid its bills on time for the preceding 12 months or, at any time, if customer discontinues receiving service from the utility and does not have an outstanding balance with the utility.

(e) The right to have customer information, including payment history and consumption patterns, kept confidential.

(f) The right to receive written notice from the utility at least five days prior to the disconnection of service due to nonpayment. During the five-day period, customer may either make payment or request alternate payment arrangements to avoid disconnection.

(g) The right to not have service disconnected when: (1) the temperature for the day is forecast to remain at or below 40 degrees Fahrenheit or the night-time temperature is forecast to be 32 degrees Fahrenheit or lower, or (2) if the high temperature for that day is forecast to be 100 degrees F or higher, or (3) if the National Weather Service issues an Excessive heat warning (or such term that reflects a heat index of 115 degrees F or higher) for Orleans Parish for the day. $^{1}$ Once the National Weather Service issues an excessive heat warning, the utility is prohibited from reinstating normal disconnect policies for the remainder of the day, regardless of whether the excessive heat warning is subsequently lifted during the day.

(h) The right to have a special medical designation which prohibits service from being disconnected for 30 days if customer is on life support or has another life-sustaining medical treatment system which requires electricity or natural gas. Customer has the right and obligation to provide the utilities written medical certification from a licensed physician as to customer’s condition to receive this special designation.

(i) The right to not have service disconnected on a weekend, holiday, day before a holiday or Friday after 1:00 p.m.

(j) The right to have same-day service for reconnection as long as payment is re-

**Sec. 158-1052. Notice of formal complaint.**

(1) The council utilities regulatory office shall advise the affected utility whenever a formal complaint has been filed and shall provide a copy of the complaint to the director of customer service and department of regulatory affairs of the utility and the designated complaint officer within three business days of the filing of the complaint.

(2) The utility shall, by fax or other suitable means of communication, immediately, but in no event more than three business days later, written acknowledgment of the receipt of the complaint to the council utilities regulatory office, the complaint officer and the customer, which acknowledgment may also contain a written response setting forth the utility’s position with respect to the allegations contained in the complaint and/or any grounds that exist which, in the opinion of the utility, constitute the grounds for the immediate dismissal of the complaint. The utility’s response shall also include a copy of any report produced by the Utility in connection with any informal investigation of the complaint, and such other records of the utility in its dealing with the informal complaint of the customer in its informal complaint process.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 22814, § 1, 9-20-07)

**Sec. 158-1053. Complaint officer.**

(1) Formal complaints shall be heard by the complaint officer. The complaint officer shall conduct and arrange for an administrative hearing of all eligible complaints. The complaint officer shall make a finding as to whether the customer service regulations, including any of the customer’s enumerated rights, have been violated by the utility and, if necessary, recommend an appropriate remedy. However, the complaint officer shall not award any monetary damages.

(2) The complaint officer shall have the authority to resolve complaints through settlement on terms that are mutually agreeable to all parties. Such settlements are encouraged and can occur prior to and in place of a formal hearing.

(3) The complaint officer shall also have the authority to dismiss summarily, and without hearing, Complaints that are deemed frivolous, that fail to meet the definition of complaint stated in section 158-1042, or that are otherwise ineligible for administrative hearing as set forth in section 158-1057. Where eligibility for hearing is raised as an issue, the determination of whether a complaint is eligible for administrative hearing shall be made by the complaint officer and a decision on the eligibility of the complaint for hearing shall be made and issued within eight business days of notice of formal complaint issued by the council utilities regulatory office.

(4) Where appropriate, and given unusual and complex situations, the complaint officer may request technical assistance that may be provided by the council, at its discretion.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 22814, § 1, 9-20-07)

**Sec. 158-1054. Timing and notice of administrative hearing.**

Unless otherwise ordered by the complaint officer taking into account any unique or special circumstances of the customer’s ability to attend on a proposed date, formal complaints shall be heard within 20 business days of issuance of notice of complaint by the council utilities regulatory office, but in no event later than 30 business days of the issuance of notice of complaint by the council utilities regulatory office. The complaint officer shall provide written notice of the date of the hearing to the customer and the utility. The notice shall state the potential consequences of any failure to appear for the hearing. Service of such notice shall be made at least five

**Sec. 158-1056. Administrative hearing procedures.**

Customers may represent themselves or be represented by counsel or any other person of their choosing. Both the parties and the complaint officer shall have the right to question all witnesses. The complaint officer shall have the discretion to limit any line of questioning to the relevant issues in dispute and the allotted time for summaries of each party's position. The formal rules of evidence shall not apply, although the complaint officer may exclude irrelevant or unduly repetitious evidence.

**Sec. 158-1057. Restriction on administrative hearing.**

A customer may not request an administrative hearing if:

(1) The customer/applicant did not initiate a complaint that follows the procedures required for informal customer complaints as provided for in the relevant section(s) of the customer service regulations applicable to electric and gas service by Energy New Orleans, Inc. and Entergy Louisiana, LLC on or before the 90th day after the customer knew or should have known about the subject of the dispute; or

(2) The customer/applicant did not file a formal complaint requesting an administrative hearing; or

(3) The customer/applicant is disputing:

(a) The terms or denial of a deferred payment agreement voluntarily offered to the customer by the utility;

(b) The customer's financial ability to pay for utility services provided by the respective utility;

(c) A council-approved rate schedule, fuel adjustment clause, or purchased gas adjustment clause;

(d) Unlawful use of service, damage to utility equipment, unauthorized sale of utility service, or violation of law;

(e) The right of the respective utility to collect for undercharged costs or charges assessed for an unlawful use of service, or damage to utility equipment;

(f) The complaint involves utility consumption and:

(i) As part of the informal complaint process dealing with the customer's complaint, the customer's meter has been tested and has been determined to be accurate; or

(ii) The customer has refused a meter test on the basis that they, in accordance with the service regulations, may be required to bear the cost of such test if the meter is found to be accurate;

(g) Denial or discontinuance of utility service based on a danger to public health or safety;

(h) A matter subject to a court decision;

(i) The application or amount of a security deposit; or

(j) A claim for property damage made against the utility.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 22814, § 1, 9-20-07)

laws.title: Effect of complaint officer finding(s)
laws.content:
The finding(s) of the complaint officer shall be nonbinding. Following the issuance of the complaint officer’s finding(s), the parties may exercise any other rights or remedies they may have at law.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 22814, § 1, 9-20-07)

laws.title: Customer protections
laws.content:
Customers shall have the following rights related to the provision of sewer and water utility services. Prohibitions to disconnect service do not extend to suspension of service that is necessary to perform a critical repair.

(a) The right to safe and reliable water service.

(b) The right to opt-in to paying a fixed monthly rate for water services, which shall be determined by calculating the average monthly cost of the customer's service based on his recent water readings.

(c) The right to dispute any amount SWBNO asserts is owed, including the right to an investigation, arbitration and appeal, as described in this chapter.

(d) The right to not have late fees charged on the disputed amount during the bill dispute process described in this chapter.

(e) The right to receive written notice from SWBNO at least ten days, exclusive of weekends and holidays, prior to the disconnection of service due to nonpayment.

Supp. No. 110

CD159:3
§ 159-3

NEW ORLEANS CODE

During the ten day period, the customer may either make payment or request a deferred payment arrangement.

(f) The right to not have service disconnected when: (1) the temperature for the day is forecast to remain at or below 40 degrees Fahrenheit or the night-time temperature is forecast to be 32 degrees Fahrenheit or lower, (2) the high temperature for the day is forecast to be 100 degrees Fahrenheit or higher, (3) the National Weather Service issues an excessive heat warning or heat advisory for Orleans Parish for a day, or portion of a day, or (4) there is a state of emergency declared for Orleans Parish by federal, state, or local officials. If the National Weather Service issues an excessive heat warning or heat advisory, SWBNO is prohibited from disconnecting service for the entire day, even if the excessive heat warning or heat advisory is lifted during the day.

(g) The right not to have service disconnected on a weekend, federal, state, or local holiday, day before a federal, state, or local holiday, or Friday after 1:00 p.m.

(h) The right to have same-day service to restore service if the customer pays, or causes to be paid, the outstanding balance or an alternative amount agreed to by the customer and SWBNO before 4:00 p.m.

(i) The right to have a meter that is regularly maintained and accurate by SWBNO.

(j) The right to receive notice from SWBNO when there is a scheduled repair that may disrupt service to customers. SWBNO shall notify customers no later than five days, exclusive of weekends and holidays, prior to the scheduled repair.

(k) The right to have any outstanding balance due discharged upon the death of the account holder.

(l) The right not to have interest, fees, or penalties assessed on an amount in dispute while a customer.

(m) The right not to have their account referred to collections while the customer has a bill in dispute.

(n) The right not to have service disconnected while the customer has a bill in dispute.

(o) The right to receive notice in writing to the address of the account on file, to the any other contact address provided, and to any email address provided by the customer of its intent to execute a service disconnect at least 30 days prior to discontinuing service.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 30050, § 1, 9-5-24)

laws.title: Billing procedures
laws.content:
(a) Meter readings:

(1) Prior to January 1, 2025, SWBNO shall conduct meter readings no less frequently than bimonthly.

(2) After January 1, 2025, SWBNO shall conduct meter readings monthly as necessary to bill customers in accordance with the prescribed billing cycles.

(3) Beginning January 1, 2025, SWBNO shall provide customers access to a picture of the meter at the time of the reading. Such picture shall include a date and time of the meter reading as well as clear images of the numbers indicating water usage and the meter number.

(b) Monthly billing:

(1) SWBNO shall bill customers in accordance with monthly billing cycles. Should SWBNO fail to send a customer a monthly bill, after three consecutive billing cycles, SWBNO forfeits its right to collect payment for the unbilled amount.

(2) In the event a customer receives a billed amount 20 percent higher than the customer's last actual bill, SWBNO shall

Supp. No. 110

CD159:4
SEWERAGE AND WATER BOARD OF NEW ORLEANS

§ 159-5

allow the customer to enter into a deferred payment arrangement for the difference in billed amounts through which SWBNO will collect the balance due over a period not to exceed 24 billing cycles.

(c) Fixed rate billing:

(1) Included with the bills for the October billing cycle, SWBNO shall send all residential customers their fixed rate amount. Customers may opt-in to fix rate billing, by remitting payment in the amount of the fixed rate prior to the October payment due date.

(2) On all bills for residential customers beginning with the October billing cycle, SWBNO shall include the method by which the residential customer may elect to receive fixed rate bills, including via email, phone call, in person at a SWBNO customer service center, or postal service.

(3) At any time, a residential customer may opt-in to fixed rate billing by utilizing any of the methods provided by SWBNO. If a customer opts-in to fixed rate billing, SWBNO shall take all necessary steps to ensure that the customer’s bills reflect the fixed rate no later than the second billing cycle after the customer submits their request.

(d) Estimated billing:

(1) If SWBNO elects to send an estimated bill instead of an actual bill, the billed amount shall equal the average of the last three uncontested actual bill amounts.

(2) If a customer receives an estimated bill calculated in any other manner, the customer shall only owe SWBNO the average of the last three uncontested actual bill amounts, and SWBNO shall recalculate the bill to reflect the correct amount owed.

(3) Beginning January 1, 2025, SWBNO is prohibited from sending estimated bills.

(e) Third party manager. The council has the right to select a third party to oversee, supplement, manage, or otherwise participate in the billing procedures described herein. The third party shall be selected in accordance with all applicable procurement policies and laws.

(f) Bills not in compliance. If SWBNO sends a bill that is not in compliance with any provision of this section, the noncompliance is sufficient grounds for a customer to dispute the bill as provided in section 159-5.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 30050, § 1, 9-5-24)
