laws.title: Generally
laws.content:
**Sec. 162-46. Administration, enforcement generally.**

The department of public works shall be responsible for the administration and enforcement of the provisions of this chapter. The director of the department of public works shall make such administrative regulations as may be necessary to implement or administer the provisions of this chapter.

(Code 1956, §§ 12-22, 12-31; M.C.S., Ord. No. 21480, § 5, 4-1-04; M.C.S., Ord. No. 28624, § 2, 3-11-21)

There is hereby created a ground transportation bureau, which shall consist of a supervisor appointed by the director of the department of

**Sec. 162-48. Duties and responsibilities.**

(a) It shall be the duty of the department of public works, to see that all applications to own or operate taxicabs or other for hire CPNC licensed vehicles or transportation network company vehicles conform to all requirements established by this article and other articles of this chapter where applicable; and to certify that such requirements have been met; to execute all policies established; and carry out duties as may be assigned from time to time by the director of the department of public works.

laws.title: Police, municipal courts to assist
laws.content:
All officers and members of the department of police and the municipal and criminal court personnel shall assist the ground transportation bureau or enforcement agents in the necessary performance of their duty when so requested. The superintendent of police shall furnish the taxicab and for hire bureau with a monthly report of all arrests of persons engaged in the taxicab or transportation for hire business. The clerk of the municipal court shall promptly report daily in writing all convictions for violations in such court.

(Code 1956, § 12-35; M.C.S., Ord. 27992, § 3, 2-7-19)

laws.title: Owners/driver to report change of employment of driver
laws.content:
All owners/drivers of taxicabs or other for-hire vehicles shall notify the ground transportation bureau in writing of the names, addresses and driver's permit numbers of all persons permitted by them by agreement of any nature to drive any such vehicle within five working days after each such occurrence, and they shall also furnish such information in writing to the ground transportation bureau relative to the termination of every driver's employment or agreement within five working days after the termination of such employment or agreement. The date of termination of the driver shall be provided by such notice.

(Code 1956, § 12-48; M.C.S., Ord. 27992, § 3, 2-7-19)

laws.title: Designation of routes
laws.content:
The director of the department of public works may designate routes over which CPNC vehicles may operate and may prohibit the operation of certain classes of vehicles in specified areas and at specified times upon the approval of the city council.

(Code 1956, § 12-76; M.C.S., Ord. No. 21480, § 5, 4-1-04; M.C.S., Ord. No. 28624, § 2, 3-11-21)

laws.title: Unlawful use of vehicles for hire by businesses and their employees
laws.content:
(a) It shall be unlawful for any agent or employee of any entity required to have an occupation tax license pursuant to section 150-951, et seq., to direct patrons to any unlicensed and/or un-permitted vehicle for hire, or for any

Supp. No. 95

CD162:17
§ 162-53

NEW ORLEANS CODE

entity required to have an occupation tax license pursuant to section 150-951, et seq., to knowingly permit or allow any of its agents or employees to direct patrons to any unlicensed and/or un-permitted vehicle for hire.

(b) In addition, it shall be unlawful for any agent or employee of any entity required to have an occupation tax license pursuant to section 150-951, et seq., to allow a vehicle, which is not pre-arranged, to stage. For purposes of this section, stage shall mean to stop, park, or otherwise place a vehicle for hire, other than a taxicab, in the loading or curbside area of any business required to have an occupation tax license pursuant to section 150-951, et seq., when the vehicle is not engaged in a pre-arranged round trip or one-way fare. Prearrangement, as required by this subsection, shall be via a communicated contract prior to pick-up, evidenced by a properly completed trip sheet. The trip sheet shall include, but not be limited to, the guest’s name, number of passengers to be picked up, time of pick up, final destination, hotel room number, if applicable, and a valid contact phone number. Vehicle for hire operators shall make said trip sheets available for verification by employees of the pickup location, as well as all law enforcement agencies. In addition, said trip sheets shall be completed prior to arrival at the pickup location.

(c) It shall be unlawful for any agent or employee of any entity required to have an occupational tax license pursuant to [section] 150-951, et seq., to request, demand, or accept any gratuity from a for hire operator in order to procure a fare, whether pre-arranged or not.

(d) It shall be unlawful for any taxicab or for hire operator to offer a gratuity, tip, or any other compensation, in order to procure a fare, whether pre-arranged or not.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 24840, § 1, 4-19-12)

Secs. 162-54, 162-55. Reserved.

laws.title: Not provide the bureau with any material false or misleading information
laws.content:
In order to obtain or maintain a driver permit, company permit, or CPNC, the applicant, driver,

company, or CPNC holder shall not provide the bureau with any material false or misleading information. A violation of this article shall constitute cause for denial of the application or suspension or revocation of the driver permit, company permit, or CPNC. False or misleading information is considered "material" if the driver’s permit or CPNC may have been denied had an accurate response been given.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 24841, § 1, 4-19-12)

laws.title: Evidence of attempt to bribe
laws.content:
(a) In order to obtain or maintain a driver permit, company permit, or CPNC, the applicant, driver, company, or CPNC holder (or someone acting on his/her behalf) must not offer or give any gift or gratuity to any employee, representative, public servant, or member of the bureau.

(b) An applicant must immediately report to the director of the department of public works if any employee, representative, public servant, or member of the bureau makes a request or demand for any gift of gratuity.

(c) Denial of an application/revocation of a permit or CPNC. The director may deny or revoke a driver permit, company permit, or CPNC for the reasons specified in this section. If the director identifies that the applicant meets the criteria in this section, the director will deny or revoke the driver’s permit, company permit, and/or CPNC and no application fees will be refunded.

(d) Any person violating this section will be banned from reapplying for a CPNC or driver’s permit for a period of ten years.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 24842, § 1, 4-19-12; M.C.S., Ord. No. 28624, § 2, 3-11-21)

laws.title: Prohibited vehicles
laws.content:
(a) Any vehicle which has ever been issued the title class of either "salvage", "rebuilt", "junk", "total loss", "reconditioned" or any equivalent classification in any jurisdiction is not eligible for operation as a for-hire vehicle and shall not be issued a CPNC.

(b) It is the affirmative duty of the CPNC holder to ascertain that the for-hire vehicle is in compliance with this section. Any vehicle placed in operation by a CPNC holder as a for-hire vehicle in violation of this subsection is unsafe, and subject to immediate CPNC suspension and/or revocation.

(c) The director may require CPNC holders to submit a car history report at the CPNC holder’s expense.

laws.title: Driver’s permits and CPNCs are privileges
laws.content:
Driver’s permits and CPNCs are privileges and not rights. The director of public works or his designee has full discretion in determining whether a driver’s permit or CPNC shall be issued.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 24843, § 1, 4-19-12; M.C.S., Ord. No. 28624, § 2, 3-11-21)

Secs. 162-60—162-80. Reserved.

laws.title: Required
laws.content:
It shall be unlawful for any person to drive any vehicle regulated by this chapter without possessing a current driver’s permit or a duplicate thereof should the same be lost or destroyed.

(a) CPNC holders are authorized to designate an employee or employees to operate a vehicle regulated by this chapter for the sole purpose of delivering such vehicle to the bureau’s inspection station for the semi-annual mechanical inspections required pursuant to sections 162-377 and 162-379 of this Code.

(b) CPNC holders are required to notify the Bureau of the name(s) of such designee(s) and their position within the entity holding CPNCs. The bureau shall maintain a listing of those individuals authorized to deliver vehicles to the inspection station and the CPNC holder with which they are affiliated.

(Code 1956, § 12-105; M.C.S., Ord. No. 26289, § 1, 3-12-15)

laws.title: Application
laws.content:
An applicant for a driver’s permit shall submit an application to the ground transportation bureau. The applicant must comply with all of the requirements set forth for drivers as provided in this chapter.

(Code 1956, § 12-106; M.C.S., Ord. 27992, § 3, 2-7-19)

laws.title: Photographs and fingerprints
laws.content:
Each applicant for a driver’s permit shall submit photographs according to the requirements for identification established by the ground transportation bureau and shall submit to being fingerprinted.

(Code 1956, § 12-108; M.C.S., Ord. 27992, § 3, 2-7-19)

laws.title: Chauffeur’s license; letters of employment agreement
laws.content:
The application for a permit to operate a for-hire vehicle solely as a driver shall, in addition to the requirements set out in this article, be accompanied by a valid chauffeur’s license and a letter in duplicate from the employer CPNC owner or lessor for whom the applicant expects to work immediately upon the issuance of such permit. This provision shall not apply to operators of animal-drawn vehicles.

(Code 1956, § 12-109)

laws.title: Display of certificate
laws.content:
It shall be unlawful for any person to transport or offer to transport passengers for hire in any vehicle regulated by this article which does not have affixed to the windshield thereof a valid certificate of public necessity and convenience issued by the director of the department of public works unless the for-hire vehicle is used exclusively to transport passengers for weddings and funerals.

(Code 1956, § 12-69; M.C.S., Ord. No. 21480, § 5, 4-1-04; M.C.S., Ord. No. 28624, § 2, 3-11-21)

laws.title: Penalties for violation
laws.content:
The penalty for a first offense under this article shall be a fine of not less than $300.00 and may include a term of imprisonment for not more than five months. A term of imprisonment of up to 30 days may be imposed for nonpayment of the fine. For second and subsequent offenses the penalty shall be a fine of not less than $300.00 and a term of imprisonment for not less than ten days nor more than five months. An additional term of imprisonment of not more than 30 days may be imposed for nonpayment of the fine.

(Code 1956, § 12-69)

laws.title: Extended renewal period and fee
laws.content:
The renewal period for a CPNC that expired between December 31, 2019 and April 1, 2023, is extended until December 31, 2023, provided that the renewal complies with the applicable provisions or this chapter. The fee for a renewal pursuant to this section is $250.00 for reinstatement of the CPNC, plus $150.00 for each delinquent renewal year. This shall be a one-time reinstatement. Additionally, any CPNC revoked for nonrenewal between April 1, 2020 and May 1, 2023 may reissued under this section.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 23492, § 1, 4-23-09; M.C.S., Ord. No. 29567, § 1, 7-27-23, eff. 7-1-23)

Secs. 162-156—162-180. Reserved.

laws.title: Generally
laws.content:
Each person who shall make application to the director of the department of public works for a CPNC, shall meet the requirements as established by law, and shall certify that all of the requirements have been properly satisfied. No license shall be granted if the applicant fails to meet the requirements of this chapter or if the applicant provides the department of public works with false, misleading or incomplete information. Licenses issued on the basis of false, misleading or incomplete information furnished by the applicant may be revoked by the director of the department of public works.

(Code 1956, § 12-42; M.C.S., Ord. No. 21480, § 5, 4-1-04; M.C.S., Ord. No. 28624, § 2, 3-11-21)

laws.title: Age and literacy
laws.content:
Applicants for CPNCs or driver's permits must be 18 years of age and must be able to read, write and fluently speak English. In the case of a partnership or a corporation, such provisions shall be satisfied by the qualification of a principal partner or duly registered officer respectively.

(Code 1956, § 12-43; M.C.S., Ord. No. 24596, § 1, 9-22-11)

laws.title: Citizenship and residency
laws.content:
(a) Citizenship. An applicant for any CPNC license must be a citizen or permanent resident of the United States. Proof of citizenship or permanent residency shall be submitted by the applicant at the time application is made.

(b) Residency. An applicant for a CPNC must currently reside in this parish and/or in the contiguous parishes of Jefferson, St. Bernard, St. Tammany, Plaquemines, or in the noncontiguous parishes of St. Charles, St. John the Baptist, or St. James. Taxicabs
laws.content:
(a) Delinquency penalty. A certificate of public necessity and convenience (CPNC) expires on December 31 of each year and must be renewed within the month following expiration (January)

NEW ORLEANS CODE

for a fee of $150.00. A CPNC renewal that is submitted in the month of February is subject to a delinquency penalty of $75.00 in addition to the renewal fee of $150.00. A CPNC renewal that is submitted in the month of March is subject to a delinquency penalty of $75.00 in addition to the renewal fee and the February delinquency penalty. A CPNC shall not be renewed after March 31; however, the director of the department of public works (or his designee) at his discretion may make an exception for good cause shown by the CPNC holder. The request for an exception must be in writing before April 1 and if granted is subject to a delinquency penalty of $50.00 per month beginning in the month of April. This delinquency penalty shall be in addition to the fees and penalties outlined above.

(b) Revocation of certificates of public necessity and convenience (CPNC). A certificate of public necessity and convenience (CPNC) that is not renewed by March 31 is suspended. A CPNC shall be revoked if a renewal is not submitted in January, February, or March or within the extended time period granted by the director or the designee.

(c) Extension for acquiring a vehicle and fee. Compliance with the requirement that a certificate of public necessity and convenience (CPNC) holder must have a vehicle in service may be extended for a period of time by the director of the department of public works (or his designee) for good cause. The first extended time period is limited to a maximum of 90 days. Additional extensions may be granted but the aggregate of such extensions is limited to a maximum of three years. There is no fee for the first extension. Additional extensions are subject to a fee of $50.00 per month. If a vehicle is not placed in service within the extended time period granted by the director or the designee, the CPNC shall be revoked.

laws.title: Animal-drawn vehicles
laws.content:
The director of the department of public works is hereby authorized to issue no more than a total of 30 certificates of public necessity and convenience for animal-drawn vehicles. The fees charged by the department of public works for certificates of public necessity and convenience for animal-drawn vehicles are as follows:

(1) Initial license …………… $250.00

(2) Annual renewal …………… 300.00

(3) Delinquency penalty. A certificate of public necessity and convenience (CPNC) for animal drawn vehicles expires on March 31 of each year and must be renewed within the month following expiration (April) for a fee of $300.00. A CPNC renewal that is submitted in the month of May is subject to a delinquency penalty of $150.00 in addition to the renewal fee of $300.00. A CPNC renewal that is submitted in the month of June is subject to a delinquency penalty of $150.00 in addition to the renewal fee and the May delinquency penalty. A CPNC shall not be renewed after June 30; however, the director of the department of public works (or his designee) at his discretion may make an exception for good cause shown by the CPNC holder. The request for an exception must be in writing before July 1 and if granted is subject to a delinquency penalty of $50.00 per month beginning in the month of July. This delinquency penalty shall be in addition to the fees and penalties outlined above.

laws.title: Courtesy vehicles
laws.content:
(a) The director of public works is hereby authorized, subject to the conditions of this section, to issue not more than 75 courtesy vehicle certificates of public necessity and convenience. Such courtesy vehicle certificates of public necessity and convenience shall not be issued for passenger buses as defined in subsection (i) below, except as provided therein. A vehicle or operator using a courtesy vehicle certificate of public necessity and convenience shall not in any manner provide transportation for hire. All courtesy vehicle CPNC’s shall be nontransferable. Any courtesy vehicle CPNC which is refused renewal and/or revoked shall be returned to the director of public works. (b) (1) Any entity providing overnight lodging may provide courtesy vehicles for the benefit of its patrons and employees only upon application for and receipt of a courtesy vehicle CPNC, according to the schedule set forth below, provided: a. Courtesy vehicle passengers are patrons of the CPNC holder’s business, as operating under the cur- rent occupational license as disclosed in the courtesy vehicle CPNC application; b. The point of origin of any trip by a courtesy vehicle is located within Orleans Parish, except that the point of origin of any trip by a luxury sedan courtesy vehicle is located in Orleans Parish or at the New Orleans International Airport; c. The courtesy vehicle driver is an employee of the entity offering the service and is properly licensed by the director of public works; and d. Entity providing the courtesy vehicle service does not receive remuneration from any entity or source for the provisions of such service. (2) Any licensed gaming entity, as defined herein, shall not own or operate any CPNC or be granted any courtesy vehicle certificates of public necessity. For purposes of this section, “licensed gaming entity” is defined as an entity licensed to conduct gaming operations pursuant to R.S. 27:1, et seq., or chapter 10 of title 4 of the Louisiana Revised Statutes of 1950, as amended. Notwithstanding the foregoing or any other law to the contrary, the casino operator of the “official gaming establishment”, as defined in R.S. 205(26) and further described in R.S. 27:241, may obtain courtesy vehicle certificates of public necessity for the operation of a total of two courtesy limousines and one courtesy bus in the aggregate. (3) Any commercial entity not included in subsections (1) and (2) above may apply to the director of the department of public works for a waiver from the provisions of this section. The director of the department of public works shall provide the applicant with a decision, within five calendar days, as to whether or not the waiver from the provision of this section should be granted in the best interest of providing safe and reliable public transportation in the city. The director of Supp. No. 95 CD162:25 § 162-187.5 NEW ORLEANS CODE the department of public works shall provide a written report to the city council every seven calendar days, relative to the disposition of all requests for such a waiver. The city council shall approve, modify or deny, within 30 calendar days, the director of public works' decision on each waiver. (c) All courtesy vehicles operating under a courtesy vehicle CPNC issued pursuant to this section shall bear an external sign which clearly and conspicuously provides the name, address and telephone number of the entity providing the courtesy vehicle service. (d) The driver of each courtesy vehicle operating under a courtesy vehicle CPNC issued pursuant to this section shall keep a trip report, showing on the upper part the CPNC and vehicle registrations certificate number, driver's permit number, name of driver, time on duty, time off duty and the date. Such trip report shall be filled out for each engagement including the time and point of destination. All entries shall be made legibly, and the trip report shall be signed by the driver, who shall preserve them for a period of not less than 90 days. (e) All courtesy vehicle CPNCs shall be issued in accordance with the following schedule:
Entity Maximum Certificates
Hotel, motel, bed and breakfast, time-share solicitation and any other entity providing overnight lodging for the public having a capacity of 400 rooms or less One
Hotel, motel, bed and breakfast, time-share solicitation and any other entity providing overnight lodging for the public having a capacity greater than 400 rooms Two
(f) Each applicant for a courtesy vehicle CPNC must provide to the director of the department of public works proof of ownership of the vehicle to be operated as a courtesy vehicle. (g) Each applicant for a courtesy vehicle CPNC must provide to the director of the department of public works a copy of the most current occupational license held by the applicant. (h) The fees charged by the department of public works for courtesy vehicle CPNC's are as follows: (1) Initial license …………… $300.00 (2) Annual renewal …………… 300.00 (3) Delinquency penalty. A certificate of public necessity and convenience (CPNC) for courtesy vehicles expires on March 31 of each year and must be renewed within the month following expiration (April) for a fee of $300.00. A CPNC renewal that is submitted in the month of May is subject to a delinquency penalty of $150.00 in addition to the renewal fee of $300.00. A CPNC renewal that is submitted in the month of June is subject to a delinquency penalty of $150.00 in addition to the renewal fee and the May delinquency penalty. A CPNC shall not be renewed after June 30; however, the director of the department of public works (or his designee) at his discretion may make an exception for good cause shown by the CPNC holder. The request for an exception must be in writing before July 1 and if granted is subject to a delinquency penalty of $50.00 per month beginning in the month of July. This delinquency penalty shall be in addition to the fees and penalties outlined above. (4) Revocation of certificates of public necessity and convenience (CPNC). A certificate of public necessity and convenience (CPNC) that is not renewed by June 30 is suspended. A CPNC shall be revoked if a renewal is not submitted in April, May, or June, or within the extended time period granted by the director or the designee. (5) Extension for acquiring a vehicle and fee. Compliance with the requirement that a certificate of public necessity and convenience (CPNC) holder must have a vehicle in service may be extended for a period of time by the director of the department of public works (or his designee) for good cause. The first extended time period is limited to a Supp. No. 95 CD162:26 VEHICLES FOR HIRE § 162-189 maximum of 90 days. Additional extensions may be granted but the aggregate of such extensions is limited to a maximum of one year. There is no fee for the first extension. Additional extensions are subject to a fee of $50.00 per month. If a vehicle is not placed into service within the extended time period granted by the director or the designee, the CPNC shall be revoked. (i) Any passenger bus, as defined herein, being operated as a courtesy vehicle for a continuous period of six months immediately prior to the effective date of this section by the Hyatt Regency or The Radisson (formerly the Clarion) Hotels shall not be subject to the limitations contained in the provisions of subsections (a) and (e), provided that the respective entity applies for a courtesy vehicle CPNC for such vehicle under this exception within 15 days of the effective date of this section. The courtesy vehicle CPNC holder shall be bound by all other provisions of this chapter. For purposes of this section, a passenger bus is defined as any vehicle with a capacity of not less than 12 passengers and not more than 52 passengers. The passenger buses provided for in this section may only transport passengers from one point of origin to two points of destination, provided that one of the three points is the CPNC holder’s place of business listed under the current occupation license provided to the director of public works in its courtesy vehicle CPNC application and each of the designated points of destination have been filed with the director of the department of public works. (j) Any vehicle, other than a passenger bus as defined in subsection (i) being operated as a courtesy vehicle by the hotel/motel industry for a continuous period of six months immediately prior to the effective date of this section shall not be subject to the limitations of subsection (e), provided that the owner apply for a courtesy vehicle CPNC for such vehicle(s) under this exception within 15 days of the effective date of this section. If any entity receiving courtesy vehicles CPNC’s pursuant to this section exceeds the maximum number allowed by subsection (e), such entity shall not be eligible for additional courtesy vehicle CPNC. The CPNC issued pursuant to this part shall be included in the limitation contained in subsection (a) and shall be subject to all other provisions of this chapter. (k) The director of the department of public works may submit a review and further recommendations to the ground transportation committee after 90 days from the effective date of this section. laws.content:
(a) All applicants for certificates of public necessity and convenience for limousines shall serve and maintain a fidelity bond in the amount of $10,000.00, and evidence of such bond shall be provided upon application or renewal of such certificate.

(b) Stretch limousines are luxurious for-hire vehicles that meet the manufacturer’s specifications for luxury limousines designed with a capacity for six to nine passengers or less, including the driver, whereby all passengers are seated behind the driver, and no door exists at the rear of the vehicle that is designed to allow passenger entry or exit. Luxurious is considered a high-end, quality, spacious vehicle, as determined by the director. Generally, limousines may include luxury sedans, luxury Sports Utility Vehicles

(1) Luxury sedans shall mean any of the four-door-sedan-type automobiles with a seating capacity of not more than six, including the driver (e.g., - Lincoln Town Car). (3) Luxury sprinter vans shall have a seating capacity of not more than 12, including the driver (e.g., Mercedes-Benz Sprinter Van).

(4) Luxury mini-bus shall have a seating capacity of greater than 16, including the driver.

(c) The director of the department of public works shall have the administrative authority to approve the type of limousine, and the colors shall be restricted to white, black, gray or dark blue.

laws.title: Types for buses and limousines
laws.content:
A certificate of public necessity and convenience will be issued for buses, limousines or other for-hire vehicles, except taxicabs, school buses, vehicles not operated on fixed rails, vehicles upon specified routes or between fixed terminals, vehicles under one or more of the following categories:

(1) Group tours and special sightseeing. Includes general charter, group tours and special services of various types specifically identified by the terms of the CPNC (i.e., transportation for the handicapped, foreign language tours, etc.).

(2) Per capita sightseeing. Includes all services defined under subsection (1) of this section, but in addition permits sightseeing tours to be sold on an individual or per capita basis.

(3) Limousine service. Includes all vehicles defined pursuant to section 162-189 that are operating for prearranged hire pursuant to a limousine CPNC. Prearranged shall be arrangement directly with the livery service or through a third party (e.g., internet-based software application, guest service desk, or concierge desk), prior to pick-up, and evidenced by a properly completed trip sheet as provided in section 162-53. This provision shall not apply to wedding and funeral services. Limousine drivers shall be prohibited from picking up any passenger who attempts to hail a limousine from the public right-of-way. A violation of this provision shall subject the limousine driver to a fine of $500.00, and

a driver's permit shall be subject to suspension or revocation for three or more offenses.

(4) Airport contract limousines. Permits service from the airport to points within the city. The number of airport CPNC's to be issued will be determined jointly by the department of public works and the aviation board considering the number of vehicles required to provide the base level of service specified in the ground transportation contract with the aviation board. Airport CPNC's will be valid for the life of the ground transportation contract and will revert to the city upon termination of that contract.

(5) Airport delivery limousine service. Includes limousines, except airport contract limousines which may transport passengers to but not from the New Orleans International Airport.

(6) Special charter. Public service commission and Interstate Commerce Commission certified bus companies are eligible for a special charter CPNC. Holders of a special charter CPNC may lease buses to tour planners and holders of per capita sightseeing CPNC's. ICC and PSC companies licensed under this section must be in full compliance with all relevant rules, regulations and requirements contained herein.

(7) Per capita continuous loop, fixed-route sightseeing. Includes all services defined under subsections (1) and (2) of this section, but in addition permits sightseeing tours to operate on a fixed-route with a continuous loop allowing multiple stops and points of boarding and exiting.

laws.title: Accessible taxicab (AT)
laws.content:
(1) The director of public works is hereby authorized to issue nontransferable certificates of public necessity and convenience for accessible taxis (AT). The AT Certificates of Public Necessity and Convenience (CPNC) shall not be transferred, leased, sold, or donated. In the event of a sale of a company possessing an AT CPNC, the purchaser must apply for the applicable permits as set forth in this article.

(2) All accessible taxicabs must comply with guidelines set forth in the ADA (Americans with Disabilities Act).

(3) Any vehicle which has been modified or custom-built must be fully compliant with all relevant FMVSS (Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standards) requirements. The manufacturer or modifier will provide, upon request, certified engineering test reports to show compliance with FMVSS.

(4) The City of New Orleans may revoke an AT CPNC for cause. Cause for revocation of an AT CPNC includes, but is not limited to, citizen complaints, a substandard level of service, or unauthorized or excessive billing. Also, an AT CPNC may be revoked should the vehicle for which the AT CPNC was issued cease operation as an ADA compliant accessible taxicab. Furthermore, AT drivers shall grant priority to requests for service from people with disabilities, and wheelchair or mobility scooter users. Each AT driver shall maintain verifiable trip sheets documenting the response to each request for AT transportation and shall maintain said trip sheets in accordance with section 162-609(b).

(5) All AT CPNCs shall have an operating two-way radio. All AT CPNC vehicles shall be painted a distinct color as set forth by the ground transportation bureau and have ground transportation bureau approved labels on its exterior identifying the vehicle as wheelchair accessible. The model year of vehicles for which a new AT CPNC will be issued must be of the same year as the AT CPNC. No vehicle for which an AT CPNC has been issued may be operated when the model year of said vehicle is greater than eight model years old. An additional three model years may be granted for alternative fuel vehicles.

(6) All AT CPNC companies shall have 24 hour central dispatch. Such companies shall provide service to customers at any location in the City of New Orleans within 30 minutes from the customer's call for service.

(7) The fees charged by the department of public works for certificates of public necessity and convenience for AT CPNCs are as follows:

(a) Initial license: $100.00.

(b) Annual renewal: $100.00.

(c) Delinquency penalty. A certificate of public necessity and convenience (CPNC) for accessible taxicabs expires on December 31 of each year and must be renewed within the month following expiration (January) for a fee of $100.00. A CPNC renewal that is submitted in the month of February is subject to a delinquency penalty of $50.00 in addition to the renewal fee of $100.00. A CPNC renewal that is submitted in the month of March is subject to a delinquency penalty of $50.00 in addition to the renewal fee and the February delinquency penalty. A CPNC shall not be renewed after March 31; however, the director of the department of public works (or his designee) at his discretion may make an exception for good cause shown by the CPNC holder. The request for an exception must be in writing before April 1 and if granted is subject to a delinquency penalty of $50.00 per month beginning in the month of April. This delinquency penalty shall be in addition to the fees and penalties outlined above.

(d) Revocation of certificates of public necessity and convenience (CPNC). A certificate of public necessity and convenience

laws.title: AT CPNC holder and driver requirements
laws.content:
(a) AT CPNC holders and vehicle operators shall provide service to passengers with disabilities or in wheelchairs before any other passengers and shall not accept any other fare while in route to a service call by a customer who is a person with disabilities or in a wheelchair.

(b) AT CPNC holders and vehicle operators must successfully complete a department of public works approved training program for the needs of passengers in wheelchairs and other persons with disabilities. Such training shall include, but not be limited to, loading and tie-down procedures and door-to-door service. AT vehicle operators shall also be certified in First Aid and CPR.

(c) Eligibility for AT CPNC Holders.

(1) Each application shall be investigated by the bureau to determine the applicant’s eligibility pursuant to the factors listed herein. In determining whether the permit should be granted the department may consider such facts as it deems pertinent, but shall at least consider the following factors:

i. The applicant’s compliance with all applicable statutes, ordinances, and regulations. If, during the five years prior to application, an applicant has violated any statute, ordinance or regulation which would be a basis for revocation of the AT CPNC or driver’s permit, the department may, in its discretion, refuse to issue the permit.

ii. The record of the applicant regarding any other permits issued for the commercial operation of a motor vehicle for the transport of passengers in the city or elsewhere.

(2) The AT CPNC holder shall require any vehicle operator of such AT CPNC vehicle to satisfactorily complete training for operation of an accessible taxi in compliance with department requirements.

(3) No individual or entity may have any financial or beneficial interest in more than ten AT CPNCs.

(d) Minimum qualifications for AT CPNC operators.

(1) All applicants for an AT CPNC operator’s permit must have satisfactorily completed training for operation of an accessible taxi in compliance with department requirements.

(2) All applicants for AT CPNC operator’s permits must meet or exceed both the moving accident and driver violation conviction standards described below.

i. Applicants shall not have more than two moving traffic accidents, in

Supp. No. 95

CD162:33
§ 162-201

NEW ORLEANS CODE

which the applicant was at fault, within the five years preceding the date of his application for an AT CPNC operator's permit. Applicants shall not have more than one vehicle moving traffic accident within two years preceding the date of the application for an AT CPNC operator's permit. However, any moving traffic accidents within the five years immediately preceding the date of application that result in a serious injury or fatality shall disqualify an individual applicant.

ii. Applicants shall not have more than two moving traffic violation convictions within five years preceding the date of his application for an AT CPNC operator's permit. Applicants shall not have more than one moving traffic violation conviction within two years preceding the date of the application for an AT CPNC operator's permit.

(3) All applicants for an AT CPNC operator's permit must meet or exceed both the following "notice of violation" and "passenger complaint" standards.

i. Applicants shall not have more than two sustained violations of the municipal code relative to operation of a taxicab or for-hire vehicle within the five years preceding the date of the application for an AT CPNC operator's permit. Applicants shall not have more than one violation of the municipal code relative to operation of a taxicab or for-hire vehicle within the two years preceding the date of the application for an AT CPNC operator's permit. A notice of violation that is appealed at a taxicab hearing and withdrawn will not be counted.

ii. Applicants shall not have more than two passenger complaints within the five years preceding the date of the application for an AT CPNC operator's permit. Applicants shall not have more than one passenger complaint within the two years preceding the date of the application for an AT CPNC operator's permit. Passenger complaints will be counted if they are determined to be credible after investigation by department.

(e) Narcotics tests and mandatory revocation for use of narcotics. Each applicant for an AT CPNC and/or AT CPNC operator's permit shall be drug tested in the manner set forth in section 162-247 of this chapter.

laws.title: AT vehicle requirements
laws.content:
(a) The vehicle model of an AT CPNC shall be approved after a review by the Mayor's Advisory Council for Citizens with Disabilities.

(b) Any vehicle which has been modified or custom-built must be fully compliant with all applicable FMVSS requirements. The manufacturer or modifier shall provide, upon request, certified engineering test reports to demonstrate compliance with FMVSS.

(c) All AT vehicles shall be equipped with credit/debit card acceptance machines. Further, such credit/debit card acceptance machines are subject to the following regulations.

(1) The passenger shall have the ability to swipe his/her own credit or debit card.

(2) A Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard (PCI DSS) compliant Passenger Information Monitor (PIM) must be installed in all accessible taxicabs, and shall be integrated directly to the taximeter by means of a hard wire connection.

a. The PIM must communicate wirelessly to obtain approvals for credit and debit card transactions. The system shall provide communication back to the taxicab within ten seconds.

(4) AT CPNC holder shall retain all trip sheets of all drivers in a safe place for a period of three years immediately succeeding December 31st of the year to which they respectively pertain and shall make such manifests available for inspection by the Bureau upon reasonable demand. Each taxicab shall have a schedule of passenger rights, [section] 162-455, affixed to the rear of both front seats a device, approved by the bureau, which shall hold a color photocopy of the driver's permit and the passenger's rights information. (5) Logo and identification scheme. Each company shall submit to the bureau a company logo and identification scheme which shall not be the same or similar to any other and which within ten days shall be approved or rejected. The logo and identification scheme shall be affixed to the left and right front doors and any other part of the vehicle, if applicable, and shall not be less than 12 inches in height, but not greater than 24 inches in height. (6) Top lights. a. Except for vehicles that have received an exterior advertising permit for a roof-top advertising display device, all AT vehicles shall be equipped with a top light permanently affixed to the exterior roof of the taxicab. The top light shall consist of three sections. The central section shall be inscribed in plain block numbers indicating the CPNC number of the accessible taxicab to which the top light is affixed. The left and right sections shall be identical to each other and shall display the words "off duty". b. The top light, when lit, must be visible at 300 feet in normal sunlight. c. The top light shall be installed and maintained in such manner that the top light will automatically be lit when the taximeter is not activated and the top light will automatically be unlit when the taximeter is activated. Each taxicab must be equipped with a driver-operable switch that will enable the driver to manually turn on and off the top light to display "off duty". d. Prohibited items. No bumper stickers, or stickers other than those identifying markings approved by the bureau, shall be placed on the body of an AT vehicle. laws.title: Permanent disqualification for certain offenses
laws.content:
(a) Applicants for a driver’s permit, or a renewal thereof shall never have been convicted of, or plead guilty to, anywhere under the laws of this state or any other state or of the United States any aggravated offense defined in R.S. 15:541 or murder.

(b) If an applicant for a new or renewal of a driver’s permit has been arrested or charged with any offense enumerated in this section, consideration of the application shall be suspended until a conviction or dismissal is rendered. If after being charged, there is a judicial determination of no probable cause for the arrest, the suspension shall immediately cease. Upon conviction of an enumerated offense, the driver’s permit shall be revoked.

(c) An arrest for any of the offenses listed in paragraph (a) above shall be grounds for an immediate interim suspension of an existing driver’s permit. If after being charged, there is a judicial determination of no probable cause for the arrest, the suspension shall immediately cease. Upon conviction of an enumerated offense, the driver’s permit shall be revoked.

(d) Any holder of a driver’s permit or applicant for a new or renewed driver’s permit or must notify the bureau in writing of any arrest, charge, or conviction of a crime within 15 days of receiving any such arrest, charge, or conviction. If the applicant or permit holder is incarcerated during this period, they shall notify the bureau
$\S$ 162-241

NEW ORLEANS CODE

immediately upon release. Subsequently, they shall deliver to the bureau a certified copy of any order, judgment, or certificate of disposition issued by the clerk of the court within 15 days of disposition or sentencing.

(Code 1956, § 12-49; M.C.S., Ord. No. 25357, § 1, 6-20-13, eff. 6-30-13; M.C.S., Ord. No. 26596, § 1, 10-1-15; M.C.S., Ord. No. 27757, § 1, 5-3-18)

**Sec. 162-242. Prescription for certain offenses.**

(a) Applicants for a driver's permit or renewal thereof shall not have been convicted of, or plead guilty to, any felony other than those listed in section 162-241, within five years of the date of filing an application.

(b) Applicants for a driver's permit or renewal thereof shall not have been convicted of, or plead guilty to, any offense or equivalent offense of pandering, prostitution, soliciting for prostitution, or distribution of a controlled dangerous substance, as set forth in R.S. 40:961, et seq., within three years of the date of filing an application.

(c) Applicants for a driver's permit or renewal thereof shall not have been convicted of, or plead guilty to, the offense or equivalent offense of illegal possession or use of a controlled dangerous substance, as set forth in R.S. 40:961, et seq., within one year of the date of filing an application..

(d) Applicants for a driver's permit or renewal thereof shall not have been convicted of, or plead guilty to, any offense under the laws of this state or any other state or of the United States for the offense or equivalent offense of operating a vehicle while intoxicated within five years of the date of filing the application, or have more than three moving violations within a single calendar year.

(e) An applicant for a driver's permit shall not have been convicted of two or more felony offenses, in the last ten years, which stem from separate incidents.

(f) If an applicant for a new driver's permit has been arrested or charged with any offense enumerated in this section, consideration of the application shall be suspended until a conviction or dismissal is rendered. If after being charged, there is a judicial determination of no probable cause for the arrest, the suspension shall immediately cease. Upon conviction, the driver's permit shall be revoked.

(g) An arrest for any of the offenses listed in sections (a), (b), or (d) of this section shall be grounds for an immediate interim suspension or non-renewal of an existing driver's permit. If after being charged, there is a judicial determination of no probable cause for the arrest, the suspension shall immediately cease.

(1) Upon conviction for any of the offenses listed in this section the driver's permit shall be revoked.

(h) Any holder of a driver's permit or applicant for a new or renewed driver's permits must notify the bureau in writing of any arrest, charge, or conviction for any of the offenses listed in sections (a), (b), or (d) of this section within 15 days of receiving any such arrest, charge or conviction. If the applicant or permit holder is incarcerated during this period, they shall notify the bureau immediately upon release. Subsequently, they shall deliver to the bureau a certified copy of any order, judgment, or certificate of disposition issued by the clerk of the court within 15 days of disposition or sentencing.

(i) Any holder of a driver's permit or applicant for a new or renewed driver's permit or who was convicted of or plead guilty to any of the offenses listed herein whose record has been officially expunged for said offense(s) is eligible for a drivers permit.

(Code 1956, § 12-50; M.C.S., Ord. No. 24747, § 1, 2-16-12; M.C.S., Ord. No. 25356, § 1, 6-20-13, eff. 6-30-13; M.C.S., Ord. No. 26596, § 1, 10-1-15; M.C.S., Ord. No. 27757, § 1, 5-3-18)

**Sec. 162-243. Specific causes for suspension or revocation.**

(a) The director of the department of public works or a duly designated agent is hereby given authority to suspend for a period not exceeding 90 days or revoke, pursuant to the applicable

Supp. No. 95

CD162:40
VEHICLES FOR HIRE

§ 162-247

procedure, any driver's permit or CPNC for due cause whenever such party has to his discredit one of the following:

(1) Conviction in any court for violating any of the disqualifying provisions of this article;

(2) Finding by the director of the department of public works, after administrative hearings as set out hereinafter, that the holder of the permit or CPNC has failed to comply with the provisions of this chapter;

(3) A combination of convictions in any court and/or suspensions totaling five within one year;

(4) Operation of a vehicle regulated by the provisions of this article when the operator's permit is under suspension;

(5) Investigation by the supervisor of the ground transportation bureau revealing that the permit holder falsified or concealed information which would have disqualified such applicant as a recipient of a permit under this chapter.

(b) A driver's permit shall also be suspended or revoked for due cause whenever the party has to his discredit one of the following:

(1) Conviction in any court for drunken driving; or

(2) Five or more moving violation convictions of the traffic division of this Code or three or more convictions of moving violations within a period of 12 months.

(Code 1956, § 12-52; M.C.S., Ord. No. 21480, § 5, 4-1-04; M.C.S., Ord. 27992, § 3, 2-7-19; M.C.S., Ord. No. 28624, § 2, 3-11-21)

laws.title: Exception provided for honorable discharge from military
laws.content:
Where an applicant for a driver's permit or CPNC has been honorably discharged from the armed forces of the United States with a minimum of not less than one year's service, the disqualifications set forth in section 162-242 shall not apply

to the period prior to such service, but offenses or convictions occurring subsequent to such discharge shall be applicable.

(Code 1956, § 12-51)

laws.title: No addiction to intoxicating drugs
laws.content:
The applicant for a driver's permit shall not be addicted to the use of intoxicating liquors and shall not use any controlled dangerous substance as set forth in R.S. 40:961, et seq., or any combination thereof, except under the supervision of a licensed physician for medical purposes and in the manner as set forth in section 162-247(e) of this article.

(Code 1956, § 12-53; M.C.S., Ord. No. 26595, § 1, 10-1-15)

laws.title: Drug tests and mandatory revocation for positive results
laws.content:
(a) All applicants for a new or renewed driver's permit shall be required to take a drug test, at his or her expense, at a drug testing facility approved by the department of public works.

(b) The director of the department of public works may periodically require the holder of any driver's permit issued under this article to take

Supp. No. 95

CD162:41
$\S$ 162-247

NEW ORLEANS CODE

additional random drug tests to determine if such holder or driver uses any controlled dangerous substance as set forth in R.S. 40:961, et seq.

(c) Upon being involved in an accident in a vehicle for hire, the operator of the vehicle for hire at the time of the accident must submit to drug testing within 48-hours of the accident.

(d) Should any drug test prove positive for a controlled dangerous substance as set forth in R.S. 40:961, et seq., or any combination thereof, the driver's permit shall be summarily suspended pending a full revocation hearing. Proof of a positive test at such hearing shall result in a mandatory denial of an application for or renewal of a driver's permit or revocation of an existing driver's permit, unless he is able to assert an affirmative defense under section 162-247(e) below.

(e) If a person testing positive has a valid and legal prescription for the medication for which he tested positive, such person may have an affirmative defense to revocation under the following limited circumstances. The prescription must be issued by a licensed physician, in compliance with the laws of the State of Louisiana. Further, the prescription must be accompanied by a written certification from the physician that he prescribed the medication, that the physician is familiar with the person's medical history (including drug and alcohol use and other medications), that the person has not been diagnosed with any substance abuse issue, and that the prescribed drug will not adversely affect that applicant's ability to operate a motor vehicle safely. Such affirmative defense is not applicable to any person who was issued a prescription under R.S. 40:1046.

(f) If a person testing positive has a valid and legal prescription for the medication for which he tested positive, such person may have an affirmative defense to revocation under the following limited circumstances. The prescription must be issued by a licensed physician, in compliance with the laws of the State of Louisiana. Further, the prescription must be accompanied by a written certification from the physician that he prescribed the medication, that the physician is familiar with the person's medical history (including drug and alcohol use and other medica-

tions), that the person has not been diagnosed with any substance abuse issue, and that the prescribed drug will not adversely affect that applicant's ability to operate a motor vehicle safely.

(Code 1956, § 12-54; M.C.S., Ord. No. 21480, § 5, 4-1-04; M.C.S., Ord. No. 24861, § 1, 4-19-12; M.C.S., Ord. No. 25328, § 1, 6-6-13; M.C.S., Ord. No. 26432, § 1, 6-4-15; M.C.S., Ord. No. 26595, § 1, 10-1-15; M.C.S., Ord. No. 28241, § 1, 11-21-19; M.C.S., Ord. No. 28624, § 2, 3-11-21)

State law reference—Drug testing, R.S. 49:1001 et seq.

laws.title: Provisions for hearing and appeal of denial or revocation of driver's permit or CPNC
laws.content:
(a) The director of the department of public works or a duly designated agent may deny or revoke the issuance of a CPNC whenever, in the exercise of reasonable and sound discretion and after giving notice and affording the applicant or holder a hearing thereon, the director shall determine that the applicant or holder is in violation of this chapter. The director shall conduct a hearing in accordance with the provisions of R.S. 49:951 et seq.

(b) If the hearing results in the denial or revocation of a CPNC, then the party involved may thereafter appeal to the Civil District Court for the Parish of Orleans within 30 working days of the decision.

(Code 1956, § 12-56; M.C.S., Ord. No. 21480, § 5, 4-1-04; M.C.S., Ord. No. 24724, § 2, 1-5-12; M.C.S., Ord. No. 28624, § 2, 3-11-21)

State law reference—Administrative Procedure Act, R.S. 49:951 et seq.

laws.title: Suspension hearing
laws.content:
(a) The director of the department of public works or a duly designated agent shall have the authority to suspend for not more than 90 days the CPNC or driver's permit of a holder in violation of any section of this chapter, provided that the party shall be first afforded notice of a hearing at which the holder will be permitted to present a defense, the convocation of such a hearing at the ground transportation bureau, and the written reasons for the suspension by

Supp. No. 95

CD162:42
VEHICLES FOR HIRE

§ 162-283

the supervisor of the ground transportation bureau of the department of public works in the event of a decision of suspension.

(b) If the hearing results in the suspension of a CPNC or driver's permit, the party involved may appeal to the civil district court. (Code 1956, § 12-57; M.C.S., Ord. No. 21480, § 5, 4-1-04; M.C.S., Ord. 27992, § 3, 2-7-19; M.C.S., Ord. No. 28624, § 2, 3-11-21)

laws.title: One-year prohibition against application after revocation
laws.content:
No person whose CPNC or permit has been revoked, pursuant to the procedure required by this article, shall be permitted to file an application for a new permit or CPNC under this chapter within a period of 12 months after such revocation. If after such period application is made, the applicant shall have met all the requirements and qualifications provided in this chapter for original applicants. The director of the department of public works has the discretion to issue a probationary license or permit at an established fee for a period of 12 months. Such probationary license or permit shall be revocable by the director of the department of public works in the exercise of sound discretion, for any violation of the law. (Code 1956, § 12-58; M.C.S., Ord. No. 21480, § 5, 4-1-04; M.C.S., Ord. No. 28624, § 2, 3-11-21)

Secs. 162-251—162-280. Reserved.

laws.title: Liability for certificate holders
laws.content:
Persons to whom CPNC's have been issued in accordance with the provisions of this article shall be liable and answerable in damages for all injuries or damages whatsoever caused directly or indirectly by the use or operation of the CPNC holder's for-hire vehicles, whether at the time of the injury or damages such for hire passenger vehicles were being used or operated by the owner, agent, servant or employee or other persons

not agents, servants or employees of the holder, unless proof is shown that the vehicle was stolen. (Code 1956, § 12-61)

laws.title: Liability coverage required
laws.content: No for-hire vehicle subject to the provisions of this chapter shall be permitted to operate on the streets of the city by any owner and/or operator until such party shall have first provided personal injury and property damage liability coverage for each such vehicle in the manner and in the amount specified hereinafter in this article. The ground transportation bureau shall maintain a continuous check of the liability coverage of each taxicab and for-hire vehicle specified in this chapter and shall not permit any such vehicle to operate without the required coverage. (Code 1956, § 12-62; M.C.S., Ord. 27992, § 3, 2-7-19)

laws.title: Coverage by insurance policy
laws.content:
No insurance policy submitted to the ground transportation bureau to provide coverage provided by this division shall be accepted unless the same shall be written by a public insurance company authorized to do business in the state, shall be issued to such person, shall be in the amounts specified in and shall conform to all the requirements of this division, and shall not stipulate that any person who may sustain damage to their person or property resulting from such negligent operation of such vehicles, shall have their right of action on such policy as fully and to the same extent as if such policy were made and executed directly in favor of the claimant for such damages, and shall contain a clause providing ten days' notice by certified mail of expiration or cancellation to be given to the ground transportation bureau as well as to the policyholder, provided that no policy will be accepted for a shorter period than six months nor shall any policy be accepted that has an expiration date in advance of the expiration date of the CPNC applicable to the vehicle for which coverage is being provided. Such insurance written under this section may be in either an admitted company or a surplus line company certified to do business in the state, provided

Supp. No. 95

CD162:43
§ 162-283

NEW ORLEANS CODE

that if same be written in a surplus line company, such company shall have a minimum rating with A.M. Best Company of A, Class V.  
(Code 1956, § 12-63; M.C.S., Ord. 27992, § 3, 2-7-19)

**Sec. 162-284. Effectiveness of certificate.**

The certificate for any and all for-hire vehicles of an owner thereof shall be effective and operation shall be permitted thereunder only so long as the insurance requirements as to such vehicle shall remain in force as therein provided.  
(Code 1956, § 12-64)

**Sec. 162-285. Enforcement.**

The provisions of this division may be enforced by appropriate civil remedy in any court of competent jurisdiction by governmental authority or by any person having an interest affected, directly or indirectly, by any violation thereof.  
(Code 1956, § 12-65)

**Sec. 162-286. Revocation of vehicle license for failure to provide liability coverage.**

Unless the certificate of public necessity and convenience holder furnishes the ground transportation bureau with satisfactory evidence of required legal liability coverage prior to the expiration of the first seven days of the ten-days’ notice specified in this chapter, or upon the third notice of cancellation within a 12-month period, the certificate of public necessity and convenience shall be subject to revocation after a hearing held by the director of the department of public works as set forth in section 162-248.  
(Code 1956, § 12-66; M.C.S., Ord. No. 21480, § 5, 4-1-04; M.C.S., Ord. 27992, § 3, 2-7-19; M.C.S., Ord. No. 28624, § 2, 3-11-21)

**Sec. 162-287. Coverage amounts.**

Each for-hire vehicle subject to the provisions of this chapter shall be represented by a policy of liability insurance issued by an insurance company licensed to do business in the State of Louisiana. At a minimum, and in accordance with state and/or federal requirements, the policy must provide the following coverage:

(a) *Taxicabs and accessible taxicabs:* $25,000.00 to satisfy all claims for damages by reason of bodily injury to, or death of, any one person resulting from any one accident; $50,000.00 to satisfy all claims for damages by reason of body injury to, or death of, two or more persons resulting from any one accident; and $25,000.00 to satisfy all claims for damage to property resulting from any one accident, by reason of the ownership, operation, maintenance or use of such vehicle upon any street.

(b) *Non-taxicabs licensed to carry under 9 passengers:* $250,000.00 to satisfy all claims for damages by reason of bodily injury to, or death of, any one person resulting from any one accident; $500,000.00 to satisfy all claims for damages by reason of body injury to, or death of, two or more persons resulting from any one accident; and $10,000.00 to satisfy all claims for damage to property resulting from any one accident, by reason of the ownership, operation, maintenance or use of such vehicle upon any street.

(c) *Non-emergency medical transport (NEMT):* At a minimum, automobile liability insurance in the amount of $25,000.00 per person, $50,000.00 per accident, and $25,000.00 property damage is required. The liability policy shall cover any and all autos; hired autos; and non-owned autos; or scheduled autos; hired autos; and non-owned autos. In addition, general commercial liability insurance in the amount of $100,000.00 on the business entity is required.

(d) *Non-taxicabs licensed to carry 9 to 15 passengers:* $1,000,000.00 combined single limit for any combination of bodily injury, death, and property damage liability claims resulting from any one accident, by reason of the ownership, operation, maintenance, or use of such vehicle upon any street.

laws.title: Prerequisites generally
laws.content:
Upon the sale or transfer of any taxicab or for-hire vehicle, except for accessible taxicabs which cannot be transferred under any circumstances, consideration may be received by the vendor or transferor or other person or paid thereto by the vendee or transferee for the transfer of the permit governing such vehicle. The CPNC may be transferred provided that the following requirements are met:

(1) A written statement is submitted to the ground transportation bureau including the following information:

a. The name and address of the transferor;

b. The CPNC number and the date the vendor or transferor received same;

c. A description of the vehicle transferred to include make, body type and year the new vehicle was placed on the market;

d. The price for which the permit and the vehicle were transferred.

(2) Payment of to the bureau of transfer fees and non-refundable processing fees as described in [section] 162-324.

(3) The transferee shall submit an application for a CPNC to the bureau and shall meet all requirements for same in this chapter.

(4) The ground transportation bureau shall be provided a certified copy of a binding agreement to transfer the CPNC which shall be due and eligible upon demand by either the transferor or the transferee, on the condition that the qualifications of the transferee as a permit holder are approved by the bureau.

(5) The vehicle of the transferee shall have been inspected for approval and approved for issuance of a for-hire vehicle inspection certificate, and otherwise comply with all of the requirements of this chapter.

(6) Before any transfer may become effective, the transferor and the transferee shall apply to the director who shall approve the transfer upon the determination that the transferee meets the qualifications of a CPNC holder under this chapter. In determining whether a proposed transferee is qualified to obtain a CPNC, the director shall apply the same standards and requirements as a new applicant. No CPNC may be transferred if suspension or revocation proceedings are pending with the bureau.

(Code 1956, § 12-78; M.C.S, Ord. No. 16,880, § 2(b), 2-2-95; M.C.S., Ord. No. 24848, § 1, 4-19-12; M.C.S., Ord. 27992, § 3, 2-7-19)

laws.title: False statements
laws.content:
Any false statement made pursuant to the requirements for transfer by either party for the purpose of obtaining a CPNC or transferring a CPNC shall constitute a violation of this article and shall constitute cause for rejection of the application for transfer and may constitute cause for suspension or revocation of the CPNC.

(Code 1956, § 12-79)

**Sec. 162-323. Denial.**

The director of the department of public works shall not approve the transfer or reissuance of the certificate of public necessity and convenience if the vehicle fails to meet the requirements for issuance of the for-hire vehicle inspection certificate by the for-hire vehicle inspection station. Such vehicle must have satisfactorily passed inspection by the station within 15 days of the date of application for transfer of the CPNC.

(Code 1956, § 12-80; M.C.S., Ord. No. 21480, § 5, 4-1-04; M.C.S., Ord. No. 28624, § 2, 3-11-21)

**Sec. 162-324. Processing fee.**

Upon application for transfer or reissuance of a certificate under this division, the applicant shall pay a fee of $350.00 for the transfer to cover the administrative cost of transferring such certificate.

(Code 1956, § 12-81; M.C.S., Ord. No. 21480, § 5, 4-1-04; M.C.S., Ord. 27992, § 3, 2-7-19; M.C.S., Ord. No. 28241, § 1, 11-21-19)

**Secs. 162-325—162-375. Reserved.**

**ARTICLE IV. FOR-HIRE VEHICLE INSPECTIONS***

**Sec. 162-376. Required.**

The director of the department of public works shall cause each vehicle for which a certificate of public necessity and convenience has been issued to be inspected as prescribed in this article, unless otherwise provided in this chapter. The director of the department of public works shall make available a list of the items which shall be inspected when a vehicle is subject to inspection. When the vehicle has met all of the requirements of this article and of the for-hire vehicle inspection station, and the required fees have been paid by the licensee, the director of the department of public works shall issue a for-hire vehicle inspection certificate of such size, color and form as may be determined by the aforesaid director and shall cause same to be affixed to the

*Cross reference—Certificates of public necessity and convenience, § 162-151 et seq.

windshield of the vehicle. The for-hire vehicle inspection certificate shall be identified by number. If it becomes damaged or destroyed, a duplicate shall be issued by the director of the department of public works after application has been made.

(Code 1956, § 12-83; M.C.S., Ord. No. 21480, § 5, 4-1-04; M.C.S., Ord. No. 28624, § 2, 3-11-21)

**Sec. 162-377. Schedule for inspections.**

(a) Every taxicab, for-hire vehicle, or courtesy vehicle for which a CPNC has been issued pursuant to the provisions of this chapter shall be submitted to the for-hire vehicle inspection station by the CPNC holder, or their authorized designee, for mechanical inspection annually.

(b) With respect to the annual inspection requirement of section (a), above, any vehicle operating as a taxicab in or after its ninth year, as provided by section 162-613, shall be subject to an annual inspection by a mechanic certified by the National Institute for Automotive Service Excellence (ASE) or by the State of Louisiana to certify that engine and transmission meet the state or ASE standards. The vehicle must pass inspection favorably each year and submit such proof to the city.

(Code 1956, § 12-85; M.C.S., Ord. No. 17,164, § 1, 9-7-95; M.C.S., Ord. No. 26289, § 2, 3-12-15; M.C.S., Ord. No. 27148, § 1, 11-3-16, eff. 1-1-17; M.C.S., Ord. No. 27180, § 1, 11-3-16; M.C.S., Ord. No. 27980, § 1, 1-10-19)

**Sec. 162-378. Nonscheduled inspections.**

All motor vehicles operated in accordance with the provisions of this chapter engaged in transporting passengers for hire shall at all times be subject to inspection and be maintained in a condition of mechanical fitness with respect to each element of safety as is required by the laws of this state and all regulations as may be enacted by the city council. The supervisor of the ground transportation bureau of the department of public works shall have the power and authority to require inspections from time to time, other than those herein prescribed, when same through reason and sound judgment are deemed necessary.

(Code 1956, § 12-86; M.C.S., Ord. No. 21480, § 5, 4-1-04; M.C.S., Ord. 27992, § 3, 2-7-19; M.C.S., Ord. No. 28624, § 2, 3-11-21)

(a) Every taxicab and for-hire vehicle shall be submitted by the CPNC holder, or their authorized designee, for mechanical inspection as follows:

(1) Upon initial issuance of the certificate of public necessity and convenience and before placing the vehicle in service;

(1) The vehicle fails to meet the requirements of the inspection as provided in this chapter; or

laws.title: Renewal certificate required
laws.content:
It shall be unlawful for any owner or driver, as defined herein, to operate any taxicab, for-hire vehicle, or courtesy vehicle for which a permit has been issued under this article without a valid for-hire vehicle renewal certificate pasted on the windshield, as provided herein.

(Code 1956, § 12-84; M.C.S., Ord. No. 17,164, § 1, 9-7-95)

laws.title: Suspension for failure to renew certificate
laws.content:
Failure of a CPNC holder to submit a vehicle for inspection at the time required by the department of public works, pursuant to the provisions of this chapter, or whenever requested by the department of public works, and to have at all times the required for-hire vehicle renewal certificate affixed on the windshield thereof or a duplicate should same be destroyed shall, in addition to the penalties provided therefor, be subject to the suspension of a holder’s CPNC in the discretion of the director of the department of public works or a duly designated agent of the director.

(Code 1956, § 12-91; M.C.S., Ord. No. 21480, § 5, 4-1-04; M.C.S., Ord. No. 28624, § 2, 3-11-21)

laws.title: Expiration and renewal of inspection certificate
laws.content:
Each for-hire vehicle renewal certificate issued by the for-hire vehicle inspection station pursuant to the provisions of this article, unless sooner removed for cause, shall expire at the end of the month of the next scheduled inspection by the department of public works; shall be renewable on the first of such month; and shall show by numeral on the face thereof the subsequent month scheduled for its expiration and renewal.

(Code 1956, § 12-88; M.C.S., Ord. No. 21480, § 5, 4-1-04; M.C.S., Ord. No. 28624, § 2, 3-11-21)

laws.title: Expired inspection certificate
laws.content:
Unless the for-hire vehicle renewal certificate is renewed prior to ineligibility, each such certificate shall become invalid for operation on the applicable expiration date as set forth in a schedule determined by the director of the department of public works.

(Code 1956, § 12-89; M.C.S., Ord. No. 21480, § 5, 4-1-04; M.C.S., Ord. No. 28624, § 2, 3-11-21)

laws.title: Renewal of certificate

Each renewal certificate in good standing shall be renewable by the director of the department of public works semiannually provided that:

(1) The vehicle has been inspected by the for-hire vehicle inspection station and has been issued a for-hire vehicle renewal certificate by the department of public works.

laws.title: Delinquency penalty
laws.content:
There shall be a penalty of $2.00 per day of delinquency whenever a vehicle is not submitted to the department of public works during the months listed in the schedule contained in this chapter. There shall be a charge of $5.00 for each duplicate vehicle inspection certificate issued for each substituted vehicle.

laws.content:
Upon completion of the vehicular inspection, the department of public works shall, if necessary, replace any for-hire vehicle renewal certificate previously issued for such vehicle with the proper for-hire vehicle renewal certificate, which shall be affixed to the windshield of the vehicle. If any vehicle is found defective at any time, the current for-hire vehicle renewal certificate shall be removed and a new for-hire vehicle renewal certificate shall not be issued until all defects found to exist have been corrected.

laws.content:
If the liability coverage of any vehicle does not meet the requirements of this chapter at the time of its inspection and/or at any other time, the current for-hire vehicle renewal certificate shall be removed, and a new for-hire vehicle renewal certificate shall not be issued until such liability coverage shall properly meet the requirements of this article.

laws.title: Operation of unsafe vehicle prohibited
laws.content:
It shall be a violation of this article for any owner or any driver to transport or offer to transport for pay any passenger or to drive any vehicle for which a permit has been issued under this article while such vehicle is unsafe and in an unsuitable condition for such use, whether or not such vehicle bears a current for-hire vehicle renewal certificate.

(Code 1956, § 12-93)

laws.title: Safe and legal operation of vehicle
laws.content:
Every for hire passenger motor vehicle shall be operated in accordance with the laws of the state and the laws of this city and with due regard for the safety, comfort and convenience of passengers and for the safe and careful transportation of property and for the safety of the general public.

(Code 1956, § 12-119)

laws.title: Speed of vehicle
laws.content:
No for hire passenger motor vehicle shall be operated at a rate of speed greater than that established by state laws or by this Code; nor, in any event, without proper regard for the traffic surface and width of the highway and the hazards at intersections and any other conditions then existing; nor in such manner or condition as to endanger or to be likely to endanger the safety of passengers, pedestrians, vehicles or the persons and property of others.

(Code 1956, § 12-120)

laws.title: Operation of vehicle while under influence of liquor or drugs prohibited
laws.content:
It shall be unlawful for any person to drive or operate any vehicle regulated by this chapter with or without passengers while under the influence of intoxicating liquor or narcotic drugs or any barbituric acid derivative or any central nervous system stimulant, or to sell, use or to possess any such narcotic drugs or any barbituric acid derivative or central nervous system stimulant except while under treatment of a licensed physician with the medication in a prescription bottle.

(Code 1956, § 12-121)

laws.title: Driver’s good conduct
laws.content:
No person to whom a driver’s permit has been issued under the provisions of this article shall interfere with, impede, obstruct the legal operation of or intentionally damage any vehicle or its equipment authorized to operate under the provisions of this chapter; nor shall any person threaten, abuse, insult, provoke, interfere with,

impede or obstruct any passenger, prospective passenger or any other person in connection with operations under this chapter.  
(Code 1956, § 12-122)

**Sec. 162-447. Driver not to smoke.**

No driver of a for hire passenger vehicle shall smoke a cigarette, cigar or pipe, nor shall the driver possess a lighted cigarette, cigar or pipe, while the vehicle is occupied by a passenger.  
(Code 1956, § 12-126)

**Sec. 162-448. Driver's personal appearance.**

Every driver while operating a for-hire vehicle shall be neat and clean in appearance at all times.  
(Code 1956, § 12-129)

**Sec. 162-449. Taxicab driver's dress code.**

(a) In addition to the requirements provided in this chapter, every owner, and/or operator of any for-hire vehicle who possesses a CPNC and/or a valid chauffeur's license shall wear the following apparel and maintain the following grooming standards while transporting passengers for hire:

(1) Male taxi drivers shall wear long pants, shirts with collars and sleeves, and shoes. Shoes shall be clean, closed-in and worn with socks. Hair, beards and/or moustaches shall be neat, trimmed and present a groomed appearance. Chauffeur's style caps may be worn.

(2) Female taxi drivers shall wear long pants or skirts, shirts with collars and sleeves, and shoes. Shoes shall be clean, closed-in and worn with socks or stockings. Hair shall be neat, trimmed, and present a groomed appearance. Chauffeur's style caps may be worn.

(3) Taxicab and carriage drivers may wear knee-length walking style shorts with a short sleeve or a polo shirt, white socks and a leather top shoe with a rubber sole with the approval of the line or company, during seasonal periods designated by the director of the department of public works. Low cut, sleeveless shirts and tank tops shall not be worn. Cut-off jeans shall not be used. Sheer, transparent or fish net materials shall not be used for any apparel.

(b) No owner and/or operator of any for-hire vehicle who possesses a CPNC and/or valid chauffeur's license shall, while transporting passengers for hire, wear sleeveless shirts, tennis shoes, sandals, slippers, jumpsuits or coveralls/overalls.

(c) Failure to comply with the provisions of this section shall subject the owner and/or operator of the vehicle for hire to the penalties provided for in this chapter.  
(Code 1956, § 12-132; M.C.S., Ord. No. 18,747, § 1, 6-4-98; M.C.S., Ord. No. 21480, § 5, 4-1-04; M.C.S., Ord. No. 28624, § 2, 3-11-21)

**Sec. 162-450. Solicitation for prostitution, violation of law.**

(a) No driver of any for-hire vehicle licensed to operate on the streets of the city pursuant to this article shall solicit any person, either in or out of the vehicle, to transport such person to any place in the city or elsewhere in the state for the purpose of participation in prostitution, sexual lewdness or obscenity, or for the purpose of participation in the violation of any law of the state.

(b) It shall be unlawful for any driver of any vehicle licensed to operate under this chapter to permit any person to occupy or use such vehicle for the purpose of prostitution or pandering, or the violation of any other law of this state or ordinance of this city. It shall be unlawful for any driver, as mentioned in this section, to allow or permit the use of the vehicle for any of the purposes prohibited in this entire section where the driver has knowledge or reasonable cause to believe that the vehicle is to be used, or is being used for such unlawful purpose.  
(Code 1956, § 12-123)

**Sec. 162-451. Public utilities solicitation.**

No person operating a motor vehicle described in this chapter, nor their agents, servants or
