laws.title: Diversion of passenger from designated destination
laws.content:
It shall be unlawful for the operator of any for-hire vehicle governed by this article to divert or attempt to divert a passenger in any such vehicle from a legitimate destination designated by such passenger. It shall likewise be unlawful for any and all parties concerned to enter into an agreement between such operator and the owner, agent or employee of a commercial enterprise whereby any such passenger would be diverted or attempted to be diverted from the destination of the passenger to another destination of to offer, ask, give or receive any remuneration for such diversion or attempted diversion of a passenger or passengers.

(Code 1956, § 12-125)

laws.title: Lost articles in taxicabs
laws.content:
(a) Taxicab drivers are required to notify the ground transportation bureau when lost items are recovered. Such notice shall be provided by the driver within one working day of the discovery of the article and should contain the following information:

(1) Description of the article; and

(2) Location where the article was found.

(b) All such recovered articles must be deposited with the ground transportation bureau within two working days of their discovery. The driver shall receive a receipt for each article deposited with the ground transportation bureau and may claim such article six months after deposit by surrendering the receipt to the bureau. If the article has been recovered by the owner, the bureau shall provide the driver with the name and the address of such owner.

(Code 1956, § 12-127; M.C.S., Ord. 27992, § 3, 2-7-19)

laws.title: Vehicle to be kept clean
laws.content:
Every driver of a for hire passenger vehicle shall keep the interior of such vehicle clean and in a sanitary condition at all times. The exterior of each vehicle shall at all times be kept in a presentable condition.

(Code 1956, § 12-128)

laws.title: Passengers' rights notice
Powers of SPCA
laws.content:
(a) Agents nominated by the Louisiana Society for Prevention of Cruelty to Animals shall be appointed and commissioned by the mayor to serve as special police officers, and shall have the usual power of policemen and peace officers in supervising animal-drawn CPNC vehicles.

(b) Whenever any vehicle for which a CPNC is required under this article is animal-drawn, the fitness of the animal for the work and its humane treatment shall be under the supervision of the agents nominated by the Louisiana Society for Prevention of Cruelty to Animals and appointed and commissioned by the mayor as special police officers, with the powers to determine:

(1) Physical fitness of the animal and limitations on work and conditions of work;

(2) Condition and fitness of harness;

(3) Care and treatment of such animals.

(c) The special officers shall direct the inspection of such animals at least once every three months.

(Code 1956, § 12-206)

laws.title: Violation of standards
laws.content:
(a) Upon discovery of a violation of this article, the special officer may issue an order to the person or persons responsible for the violation requiring the immediate removal of the subject animal from service.

(b) No animal which has been removed from service for violation of this section shall be returned to service until the animal has been inspected by an SPCA veterinarian and approved for return.

(Code 1956, § 12-207)

**Sec. 162-498. Refusal to comply.**

Any person who refuses to comply with the order of the SPCA or who complies with such order and returns the subject animal to service before being inspected and approved by the SPCA shall be guilty of the offense of refusing to obey an order of the SPCA.

(Code 1956, § 12-208)

**Sec. 162-499. Penalty.**

The fine for all offenses under this article shall be $100.00 or 90 days in jail, or both. Upon commission of such offense, the special officer shall issue a summons to the offender.

(Code 1956, § 12-209)

**Sec. 162-500. Summons.**

A summons may be served on the offender by the person issuing the summons or by anyone authorized by the law to do so. The summons need not be served at the time of the offense. The summons shall recite the offense charged and the fine specified above. The summons shall also apprise the offender that he has ten days from the date of the issuance of the summons to pay the fine to the office of the SPCA.

(Code 1956, § 12-210)

**Sec. 162-501. Trial date.**

The summons shall further contain a trial date and recite that, if after the expiration of ten days the fine has not been paid, a copy of the summons will be forwarded to the clerk of the municipal court and a hearing will be held on the trial date.

(Code 1956, § 12-211)

**Sec. 162-502. Powers of arrest.**

The special officers shall have the power to arrest and charge the driver, as well as the owner, with any violation of this article.

(Code 1956, § 12-212)

**Secs. 162-503—162-540. Reserved.**

**DIVISION 2. OPERATING REQUIREMENTS**

**Sec. 162-541. Identifying number and current veterinary health certificate.**

(a) Each animal must have a tattooed identifying number on the inside of its lip or ear, or on the left rump.

(b) A current veterinary health certificate for each animal showing the tattoo number shall be furnished to the Louisiana SPCA office when such animal is placed in service, and no more than 12 months thereafter. The certificate will show that a veterinarian licensed in the state has given the animal a coggins test with negative results as required by state law and declares this animal to be fit for carriage service.

(Code 1956, § 12-213)

**Sec. 162-542. Health of the animal.**

No animal shall be permitted to pull any carriage unless the animal is in good health and meets at least the following requirements:

(1) All animals purchased subsequent to the effective date of the ordinance from which this section was derived shall be mules and must weigh at least 1,000 pounds.

(2) The animal has no open sores or wounds, is not lame nor has any other ailment. Any animal found to have an ailment shall not be used without the approval of a veterinarian.

(3) The hoofs of the animal must be properly shod and trimmed.

(4) The animal must be groomed daily and not have fungus, dandruff or a poor or dirty coat.

(5) The animal must have adequate flesh and muscle tones.

(Code 1956, § 12-214)

**Sec. 162-543. Animal working conditions.**

(a) No animal shall be worked under any of the following conditions, and any owner that allows such conditions to exist will be found in violation of this article:

(1) The carriage the animal is pulling is holding more than nine people, including the driver.

Supp. No. 95

CD162:56
VEHICLES FOR HIRE

§ 162-549

(2) The animal works more than seven hours in any 24-hour period with 15-minute rest periods between each trip.

(3) The animal pulling a carriage is moved at a speed faster than a slow trot.

(4) The animal is worked with equipment causing an impairment of vision other than normal blinders.

(5) The animal is subject to any condition or treatment which will impair the good health and physical condition of the animal.

(6) Between the dates of June 1 and August 31, only mules may be used in the daytime before 5:00 p.m., and total hours worked shall not exceed six hours in a 24-hour period with 30-minute rest periods between each trip.

(b) Should the director of the department of public works determine that special circumstances exist which would jeopardize the safety of the animal, such as bad weather or other environmental problems, he may order the temporary suspension of the operation of all animal-drawn vehicles until such time as the special circumstances abate.

(Code 1956, § 12-215; M.C.S., Ord. No. 21480, § 5, 4-1-04; M.C.S., Ord. No. 28624, § 2, 3-11-21)

laws.title: Harness
laws.content:
(a) No animal will be worked with a harness or bit that is not approved by the Louisiana SPCA.

(b) The harness must be oiled and cleaned so as to be soft at all times.

(c) The harness will be properly fitted and maintained and kept free of makeshift like wire, sisal rope, and rusty chain.

(Code 1956, § 12-216)

laws.title: Carriages
laws.content:
Carriages must be properly lubricated, and wheels must spin freely.

(Code 1956, § 12-217)

laws.title: Whip
laws.content:
No driver may whip an animal with more than a light touch by a light whip approved by the Louisiana SPCA.

(Code 1956, § 12-218)

laws.title: Water
laws.content:
Adequate water will be provided in the working area and stables at all times.

(Code 1956, § 12-219)

laws.title: Stalls and stables
laws.content:
(a) Ventilation will be provided for stalls with animals in hot weather.

(b) Ceilings in stalls and stables must be at least nine feet high from bedding and flooring. Future construction will provide for ceilings at least ten feet high from bedding flooring.

(c) Bedding in stalls and stables must be at least six inches deep and dry enough so as not to show wetness under the pressure of the animal’s hoofs.

(d) Foot hazards and sharp surfaces will not be permitted in any area or building where they may come in contact with the animals.

(e) Roofs must be kept free of leaks where animals are kept.

(f) Each animal must have a stall large enough for the animal to turn around.

(g) Food must be kept free of contamination.

(h) Animal areas must be treated to destroy and repel insects.

(Code 1956, § 12-220)

laws.title: Drivers to maintain stands in sanitary condition; diapering of animals required
laws.content:
(a) Driver of CPNC-licensed horse-drawn vehicles operated under this article shall maintain stands in a sanitary condition at all times. Any failure on part of such driver to conform to the

Supp. No. 112

CD162:57
§ 162-549

NEW ORLEANS CODE

requirements of this section shall be unlawful and shall subject such drivers to the penalties provided by this article.

(b) It shall be unlawful for any person, firm, corporation or other entity to utilize any animal for the purpose of pulling any CPNC-licensed vehicle on city streets unless such animal is equipped with diapering apparatus that prevents the droppings of such animal from being deposited or otherwise left on city streets. It shall be the responsibility of the driver of a CPNC-licensed animal-drawn vehicle to see that the diapering apparatus is maintained in working order. The penalty for violation of this section committed within one year as follows:

*First offense:* $50.00

*Second offense:* $100.00

*Third offense:* $200.00 and a temporary suspension of the driver’s permit for a minimum of five days. On a subsequent violation within one year from the date of the first offense the fine is $200.00 and the suspension of the driver’s permit may be a maximum of 30 days.

Each company operating vehicles [is] responsible for immediate removal of the droppings.

(Code 1956, § 12-221; M.C.S., Ord. No. 20970, § 1, 1-9-03)

laws.title: Identification
laws.content:
Each company operating carriages must identify each carriage with the name of the company prominently displayed on each side or the rear of each vehicle.

(Code 1956, § 12-222)

laws.title: Company telephone numbers
laws.content:
Each company will have its listed telephone number printed on the vehicle to assign responsibility for complaints.

(Code 1956, § 12-223)

Supp. No. 112

CD162:58

laws.title: In-lieu provision
laws.content:
In lieu of utilizing an animal drawn carriage, a holder of an animal drawn carriage CPNC may provide the same service without the use of an animal and instead use an electronic or e-carriage that adheres to all the following standards:

(1) The department of public works must certify that the vehicle is an electric carriage; and

(2) The vehicle must be powered by electricity or battery and not utilize a combustion engine and may not be gasoline powered; and

(3) The vehicle must not be able to seat over 16 passengers in addition to a driver; and

(4) The vehicle shall be no longer than 20 feet; and

(5) The vehicle must not be able to exceed a speed of 25 miles per hour; and

(6) To be certified as an electric carriage, the vehicle’s design must be inspired by a vintage horse-drawn carriage.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 30322, § 1, 4-24-25)

In addition to the other applicable provisions of this chapter, all taxicab CPNC holders and taxicab drivers shall comply with the applicable provisions of this article.

laws.title: Renewal certificate required
laws.content:
(a) No taxicab shall be operated on the streets of the city unless the owner of such vehicle has first applied for and received a CPNC qualifying a taxicab in the manner provided in this chapter; however, any person holding a CPNC issued by the city to transport passengers may transport passengers on an organized sightseeing tour into and within the city from any point beyond the boundaries of any parish contiguous to the city when such vehicle is accompanied by and under the direction of a guide holding a valid tour guide license.

(b) It shall be unlawful for any person to transport or offer to transport passengers for hire in any taxicab which does not have affixed to the windshield thereof a valid for-hire vehicle renewal certificate issued at the for-hire vehicle inspection station under the auspices of the director of the department of public works.

(Code 1956, § 12-143; M.C.S., Ord. No. 21480, § 5, 4-1-04; M.C.S., Ord. No. 28624, § 2, 3-11-21)

laws.title: Interparish operation of taxicabs
laws.content:
Taxicabs of the type subject to regulation under this chapter in the parish authorized to operate in any other parish or in any political subdivision thereof may transport passengers from such parish or subdivision thereof to a

destination within or beyond the parish. No owner or operator of such taxicab for-hire vehicle, not licensed with a certificate of public necessity and convenience, shall accept a fare or transport a passenger for hire commencing within the parish.

(Code 1956, § 12-144)

laws.title: Maintenance and appearance of vehicle
laws.content:
Each driver of a taxicab shall be fully responsible for the exterior and interior physical appearance of the taxicab. Each driver shall be required to maintain the taxicab and his or her person in a neat and clean condition at all times. Interiors of all cabs must be kept free of all debris. Dashboards must be maintained free and clear of all paraphernalia and other items not necessary for the operation of such taxicab. Each taxicab must be air conditioned and operating in a first-class condition. A sign stating that no smoking, drinking or eating are permitted in the taxicab shall be installed in the passenger portion of the vehicle. The minimum penalty for one violation of this section within a one-year period shall be $50.00. The penalty for two violations within one year of the first violation shall be a minimum $75.00 fine plus a minimum ten-day suspension from operating any for-hire vehicle. The penalty for three or more violations within a one-year period of the first violation shall be a minimum $100.00 fine plus a minimum 90-day suspension from operating any for-hire vehicle.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 20638, § 1, 4-18-02)

laws.title: Vehicle requirements
laws.content:
(a) No application for a permit to own and/or operate a taxicab under this chapter shall be approved unless the vehicle is a mini-van (having gross vehicle weight rating of 5,500 pounds or less, has a wheel base of not less than a minimum of 112 inches, or a maximum of not more than 120 inches, has a running board affixed to the passenger side of the vehicle for access and discharge of passengers, and does not seat more than six passengers including the driver), a sports utility vehicle (SUV), or a four-door sedan. Each of the foregoing vehicles must meet the following minimum specifications:

(1) Head room: Front 33 inches, rear 32 inches.

(2) Leg room: Front 40 inches, rear 35 inches.

(3) Shoulder room: Front 55 inches (taxis with bucket front seats, 15 inches per seat), rear 49 inches.

(4) Hip room: Front 51 inches (taxis with bucket front seats, 20 inches per seat), rear 51 inches.

(5) Entrance height: Front 30 inches, rear 29 inches.

(6) Tire size: 13 inches.

(7) Wheel base: 103 inches (four-door sedans only).

(8) Air conditioning: Standard system which meets manufacturer’s specifications for the specific type of vehicle.

(b) Official interior dimensions from the manufacturer must be submitted by applicant to the ground transportation bureau upon request at the time of application.

(c) No wheelchair accessible vehicle shall be approved for use as a taxicab under this chapter unless that vehicle and all necessary retrofitting have been approved by the mayor’s advisory council for citizens with disabilities.

(Code 1956, § 12-147; M.C.S., Ord. No. 16,480, 4-21-94; M.C.S., Ord. No. 22861, § 1, 10-18-07; M.C.S., Ord. No. 26589, § 1, 9-17-15; M.C.S., Ord. 27992, § 3, 2-7-19)

laws.title: Additional requirements
laws.content:
After the application for a permit to obtain a CPNC for a taxicab has been approved and before the vehicle shall be eligible for operation as a for-hire vehicle, the party shall, in addition

to other requirements of the director of the department of public works, perform the following:

(1) Supply in writing the following information relative to each vehicle to be covered by such permit:

a. The model and make of such vehicle, motor number and seating capacity;

b. Type, make and number of taximeter meeting the requirements of this chapter;

c. A certificate that the applicant is the actual sole and registered owner of the vehicle or vehicles to be used, including certificate of title number.

laws.title: Taxicab driver photo identification
laws.content:
All drivers are required to wear a photo identification containing the driver's name and the affiliated company, of a design specified by the director of the department of public works. This identification should be worn during all duty hours and should be worn so as to be plainly visible at all times.

Passenger as controller of cab

It shall be unlawful for a taxicab driver to cause a passenger to wait without the passenger's consent or to pick up additional passengers en route without the passenger's consent; except, that ride sharing is permitted in the following cases:

(1) Trips to and from New Orleans International Airport;

(2) Trips between central business district hotels and the Rivergate and the Superdome;

laws.title: Number of passengers per vehicle
laws.content: It shall be unlawful to load more passengers in a taxicab beyond the vehicle’s capacity as set forth by the vehicle’s manufacturer. Seat belts must be available for each passenger. No taxicab shall be loaded with passengers in such a manner as to obstruct the view of the driver or otherwise interfere with the safe operation of the vehicle. (Code 1956, § 12-152; M.C.S., Ord. No. 24852, § 1, 4-19-12)

laws.title: Refusal to carry passengers
laws.content: No operator of any taxicab shall refuse to take any passenger to a destination within ten miles outside of the city limits or to a municipal airport operated by the city; provided, however, that the driver shall be required to take only the class of passengers the taxicab is registered to accommodate. (Code 1956, § 12-153)

laws.title: Maximum age of taxicabs
laws.content:
A vehicle for which a CPNC is obtained may be operated as a taxicab until the vehicle is fifteen years old. For purposes of this section, the vehicle’s age shall be determined based on the vehicle’s model year, such that a vehicle with a model year of 2000 shall have a vehicle age of one year as of January 1, 2001. (M.C.S., Ord. No. 24862, § 1, 4-19-12; M.C.S., Ord. No. 26557, § 1, 8-6-15; M.C.S., Ord. No. 27180, § 2, 11-3-16; M.C.S., Ord. No. 27963, § 1, 12-20-18; M.C.S., Ord. No. 28241, § 1, 11-21-19)

laws.title: Taxicab and for-hire vehicle stands
laws.content:
(a) The director of the department of public works is hereby authorized, as a police measure, to designate the location of taxicab and other for-hire vehicle stands on the streets and other public places in the city. Such stands shall be marked by appropriate signs and shall be reserved exclusively for the parking of taxicabs or other for-hire vehicles as specified by such signs, while waiting to pick up passengers for hire.

(b) Additionally, the director of the department of public works is hereby authorized to designate the location of temporary taxicab and for-hire vehicle stands on the streets and other public places in the city for use of taxicabs and for-hire vehicles in support of large special events or other temporary activities.

i. The director of public works is authorized to assess the impact of a proposed special event or temporary activity to determine if a temporary taxicab or for-hire vehicle stand is required in support of convenience to the general public.

ii. Subject to the discretion of the director of public works or upon request of a special event or temporary activity organizer, a special event taxicab/for-hire vehicle stand permit may be issued in conjunction with other required special event permits. This permit will designate the location of the temporary stand and authorizes the assignment of public works investigator(s) to regulate the flow of for-hire vehicle traffic at that location.

iii. Subject to the discretion of the director or upon request by a special event or temporary activity organizer, additional time or personnel may be provided by the department of public works to monitor and regulate the flow of for-hire vehicle traffic a permitted special event taxicab/for-hire vehicle stand.

iv. Fees for special event taxicab/for-hire vehicle stand permits and staffing are established as follows:

a. The fee for the special event taxicab/for-hire vehicle stand permit shall be $150.00.

b. The fee for additional time (beyond the first three hours) and additional personnel shall be $30.00 per hour.

c. The director of public works is to collect all required fees at the time of permitting and shall give receipts for same. All fees collected under this section shall be deposited to the bureau of the treasury, to the account of the general fund.

**Sec. 162-652. Priority of service at taxicab stands.**

Taxicabs located in any officially designated stand shall be loaded in their order of occupancy of the stand, i.e., first-in, first-out, and only the taxicab first out may move into a passenger zone ahead of such stand for the purpose of loading; provided, however, that each prospective taxicab passenger shall have the right, unless otherwise prohibited, to approach, engage and occupy any taxicab at its location within such stand, and it shall be unlawful for the operator of any taxicab or any other person to interfere, prevent or impede the movement of a loaded taxicab from such stand. It shall likewise be unlawful for the operator of any cruising or other taxicab to usurp the priority of any stand, or to enter, stop or stand any taxicab in a passenger zone ahead of such stand, except for the purpose of and while actually engaged in the discharge of passengers. It shall also be unlawful for the operator of any taxicab who has unloaded passengers at such loading zone to accept any passenger at that time unless such taxicab is first out, in accordance with the priority established above.

(Code 1956, § 12-155)

**Sec. 162-653. Driver restrictions in stands.**

The driver of any taxicab or other for-hire vehicle parked in any stand designated for use of this type of vehicle shall remain within the limits of the stand, which shall be interpreted to be the parking strip and adjacent sidewalk between the signs designating the stands; provided that from 6:00 p.m. to 6:00 a.m. the driver of any taxicab or other for-hire vehicle parked in any stand in the restricted area, as specified in the following section, shall remain within the immedi-

ate vicinity of or in the front seat of his vehicle at all times except when it is necessary to assist passengers to board or alight from his cab.

(Code 1956, § 12-156)

**Sec. 162-654. Restricted area defined.**

It shall be unlawful for the driver of a taxicab to park at any time upon any portion other than metered zones of any street except in properly designated taxicab stands, beginning at the intersection of Canal Street and the Mississippi River; thence on Canal Street to North Rampart Street; thence on North Rampart Street to Toulouse Street; and thence on Toulouse Street and the projection thereof to its intersection with the Mississippi River.

(Code 1956, § 12-157)

**Sec. 162-655. Parking in vicinity of residence.**

Subject to the provisions of laws and regulations applicable to the parking, stopping or standing of private vehicles, no owner or driver of a taxicab shall be prohibited by the provisions of this section from parking his taxicab within the immediate vicinity of his residence of record as long as he continues to reside thereat; provided, that such vehicle is not then being used or offered for use as a taxicab; and provided further, that no taxicab shall be parked at any place or time when such parking of taxicabs is prohibited by any applicable law or regulation other than the provisions of this section.

(Code 1956, § 12-158)

**Sec. 162-656. Nonparish licensed operators.**

No owner or operator of any vehicle authorized to operate in any parish other than the parish or in any political subdivision thereof shall stop or park anywhere on the city’s streets where such stopping or parking is prohibited to any taxicab or other for-hire vehicle operating under a permit from the city, or stop or park anywhere in the city with intent to violate this Code. No such owner or operator of any such vehicle shall operate such vehicle in any manner contrary to the provisions of any law of this state or this

Supp. No. 95

§ 162-659

Code. No such owner or operator of any such vehicle at any time shall utilize taxicab stands established for the use of taxicabs authorized and licensed to operate in the parish.

(Code 1956, § 12-159)

**Sec. 162-657. Taximeter required; location.**

(a) Unless otherwise specifically provided herein, no owner or operator of any taxicab shall operate such vehicle unless it is equipped with a taximeter which shall automatically compute and register the amount of the fare on a basis of the miles traveled or the time elapsed (the fare reflecting the elapsed time if it occurs first or the mileage if it is traveled before the applicable time has elapsed). Each taximeter must show the amount of the fare on its face and shall be located in the cab in such position that the fare may be continuously seen both day and night by each and every passenger seated in the rear compartment of the vehicle. Each taximeter shall be placed in the taxicab in such a position that the flag will be visible from the street when in the for hire position. It shall be unlawful to transport passengers in a pay status in such vehicle unless such meter is in operation.

(b) Taximeters shall be either hardwired or connected via an encrypted and secured wireless connection to a passenger information monitor and dispense a receipt with the following information:

i. CPNC number;

ii. Driver ID;

iii. Trip ID;

iv. Distance of trip;

v. Date of trip;

vi. Time of trip;

vii. Fare charges;

viii. Extra charges;

ix. Total charges;

x. Taxicab company name and phone number; and

xi. The words "Ground Transportation Bureau. For compliments or concerns, please call 504-658-7176."

(c) This provisions of this section shall become effective on August 1, 2012.

(Code 1956, § 12-160; M.C.S., Ord. No. 16,880, § 2(c), 2-2-95; M.C.S., Ord. No. 24863, § 1, 4-19-12; M.C.S., Ord. No. 25818, § 1, 4-24-14; M.C.S., Ord. No. 27963, § 1, 12-20-18; M.C.S., Ord. 27992, § 3, 2-7-19)

**Sec. 162-658. Unlawful to alter taximeter.**

It shall be unlawful for any person to tamper with or alter in any manner the taximeter of such vehicle except as by the department of public works.

(Code 1956, § 12-161; M.C.S., Ord. No. 21480, § 5, 4-1-04; M.C.S., Ord. No. 28624, § 2, 3-11-21)

**Sec. 162-659. Credit/debit card acceptance machines; alternative systems.**

(a) All taxicabs shall be equipped with a bureau-approved and fully functioning credit/debit card acceptance machine. Further, such credit/debit card acceptance machines are subject to the following regulations.

(1) The passenger shall have the ability to swipe his own credit or debit card.

(2) A payment card industry data security standard (PCI DSS) compliant passenger information monitor (PIM) must be installed in all taxicabs, and shall be integrated directly to the taximeter by means of a hard wire connection.

i. The PIM must communicate wirelessly to obtain approvals for credit and debit card transactions. The system shall provide communication back to the taxicab within ten seconds.

ii. All PIMS must be bolted to the head rest or in an area approved by the bureau in the passenger compartment.

Supp. No. 112

CD162:63
§ 162-659

NEW ORLEANS CODE

iii. The system must provide a printed or digital receipt for every credit or debit card transaction. Handwritten receipts are not allowed.

(3) A GPS receiver is required for the credit/debit card system.

(4) Drivers must be able to sign into the PIM using either a unique identifying number or biometrics.

(5) No surcharge may be imposed for the use of a credit/debit card so that the total charge exceeds the legal rate of fare.

(6) No minimum charge may be imposed for the use of a credit/debit card.

(7) No service may be refused to any person desiring to use a credit/debit card.

(8) The bureau shall have unlimited online access to all information collected by the PIM.

(b) Any licensed CPNC holder may also petition the bureau for approval of any alternative credit/debit card acceptance systems. The ground transportation bureau shall adopt rules establishing evaluation criteria for approval or denial; and procedures relative thereto.

(c) If the bureau denies approval of the proposed alternative system, it shall prepare a report within 30 days of the date of the petition that states the reasons for said denial. This report shall be mailed to the petitioner.

(d) Any licensed CPNC holder whose petition is denied shall have a right to apply in writing to the city council for reversal or modification thereof. Any such appeal shall be taken within 15 days from the date the decision is mailed. The appeal shall be docketed at the next regular meeting after receipt of communication. The city council has the right to reverse, change, or modify any decision of the bureau only by a majority vote of all its members.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 24864, § 1, 4-19-12; M.C.S., Ord. No. 26027, § 1, 9-4-14; M.C.S., Ord. No. 28624, § 2, 3-11-21; M.C.S., Ord. No. 29981, § 2, 7-11-24)

laws.title: Security systems

laws.title: Trade name to be registered
laws.content:
The trade name applicable to each vehicle operated under the provisions of this article shall be registered with and approved by the ground transportation bureau. Such registration shall set forth the full name and address of the lawful owner or owners of such trade name and shall specify the color scheme of vehicles to be operated under such trade name. The owner or owners of such trade name shall furnish to the ground transportation bureau a to-scale model of the vehicle, which shall be painted in conformity with the trade name applicable and lettered as required by this chapter. Each change in color scheme or of lettering of such vehicle shall likewise be registered and a modified scale model of the vehicle shall be furnished. laws.title: Number of taxicabs required to form new line
laws.content:

(b) telephone service and must meet all the requirements of a corporation or partnership applying for a CPNC.

laws.title: Identification of vehicles

In addition, the vehicle’s registered certificate number assigned by the ground transportation bureau shall be permanently painted on the vehicle as prescribed by the ground transportation bureau. laws.title: Current record; complaints; notices
laws.content:
All taxicab line operators shall:

(1) Maintain a current record of taxicab CPNC numbers and each driver per vehicle that is on the line;

(2) Refer any and all complaints by passengers of taxicabs to the ground transportation bureau; and

laws.title: Violation; penalty
laws.content:

(Code 1956, § 12-166; M.C.S., Ord. No. 21480, § 5, 4-1-04; M.C.S., Ord. No. 28624, § 2, 3-11-21)

laws.title: Legal fares and payment thereof required
laws.content:
(a) It shall be unlawful for any person to ask, demand or collect any rates of fare other than as specified herein for use of any for hire passenger vehicle including vehicles for hire for the physically challenged, or "Disabled Friendly Taxi" (DFT), regulated by this chapter.

(b) It shall be unlawful for any passenger of any such vehicle to refuse to pay the operator thereof the legal rate charged pursuant to the provisions of this article.

(c) The department of public works shall review all ground transportation fares each consecutive odd year, and shall submit a report in a national peer city comparative analysis format to the mayor and the city council.

laws.title: Taxicab rates for airports
laws.content:
(a) Except as provided hereinafter, taxicab fare to or from the Louis Armstrong New Orleans International Airport (Moisant Field) to or from the same destination in New Orleans shall be $36.00 for one to two passengers; and for three or more passengers to or from the same destination, the taxicab fare shall be $15.00 per passenger. Meter rate shall be charged after an initial stop in cases of additional stops from the airport, and vice versa to the airport. To or from any location east of Elysian Fields boundary line the fare shall be the metered fare from such boundary to the destination or point of origin plus the fare stated above. The fare to or from the Louis Armstrong New Orleans International Airport to or from any Westbank location shall be $36.00 plus the meter rate to or from the toll plaza.

(b) The taxicab fare to or from the New Orleans Lakefront Airport to any location in an area bounded by Galvez Street, Esplanade Avenue, the Mississippi River and Jackson Avenue for one to two passengers shall be $25.00 total fare; for more than two passengers the fare shall be $10.00 per passenger.

(c) The taxicab fare to or from Alvin Calendar Field shall be the New Orleans International Airport rate to or from the toll plaza plus the Westbank meter fare, or the meter fare for the entire trip, whichever is greater. Airport tolls and other applicable charges as specified in this chapter shall be in addition to the fares specified in this section.

(d) An additional gasoline surcharge of $1.00 per completed trip shall be authorized until December 31, 2022.

(e) All taxicabs and DFTs are required to post in plain sight in the interior of the vehicle notice to passengers of a $1.00 gasoline surcharge for each completed trip subject to design specifications approved by the director of the department of public works pursuant to 162-74.

laws.content:
(a) When all passengers are members of the same group or party and originate from the same point and go to the same destination, or when the original passenger directs the driver to pick up or discharge others in the same group or party, all passengers shall be transported for the recorded meter fare, plus applicable bridge and ferriage charges, except as provided otherwise in this article.

(b) When one or more additional groups consisting of one or more passengers share the same taxicab, the fare charged shall be metered fare. The chauffeur shall rewind the meter upon the discharging of each group. Additional passengers may be picked up at the beginning of any trip or in route only if such pick up is agreeable to the initial passenger or group employing the taxicab.

No sign, device or poster, whether permanent or temporary, whether for advertising or other purposes, shall be placed or carried on or inside any vehicle regulated by this article without the approval of the director of the department of public works. However, prior approval is not required for a person licensed under this chapter to affix one sticker of not more than two inches by three inches in size to the right front wind-vent window of his certified vehicle, indicating that such owner is a member of a recognized transportation organization or association composed of persons licensed under this article.

laws.title: Director to authorize advertising
laws.content:
(a) The director of the department of public works is hereby authorized to permit the installation of advertising cards in the passenger compartment or the top or roof area of taxicabs, on the exterior or interior of general charter vehicles, and on the exterior of sightseeing vehicles, animal drawn vehicles, and pedicabs. The director shall permit such advertisement only where the conditions set forth in this article are met. Advertising wraps are expressly prohibited on for-hire motor vehicles.

(b) With respect to the general prohibition of advertising wraps provided in subsection (a), the director is authorized to permit temporary advertising wraps or signage as may be appropriate for vehicles contracted for service to the organizer of a special event as declared by the city council, mayor, or the mayor’s designee in accordance with section 162-197 of this chapter. Such temporary advertising shall be permissible only for the duration of the declared special event. Fees for such temporary advertisements shall be $25.00 per vehicle.

(c) The director of the department of public works is authorized to permit the installation of advertisement decals which promote third-party dispatch or hailing services for taxicabs, provided that such advertisements do not obstruct the CPNC numbers, CPNC holder name, or other livery as may be approved for the operation of a taxicab line. No fee shall be assessed for advertising of such third-party services on the body of the taxicab vehicle.

**Sec. 162-795. Advertisement holder required.**

All advertisements shall be enclosed only in a shatter-proof, splinter-proof card holder covered by a shatter-proof, fire resistant transparent material which shall be constructed in such a manner as to provide no safety hazard to either driver or passenger, the measurements, design and location to be determined by the director of the department of public works.

(Code 1956, § 12-196; M.C.S., Ord. No. 21480, § 5, 4-1-04; M.C.S., Ord. No. 28624, § 2, 3-11-21)

**Sec. 162-796. Holder not to interfere with passengers.**

No advertising sign, poster or advertising card holder, official notice, identification card or sticker required by any other provisions of this article, although otherwise complying with the provisions of this article, shall be placed in such a position within the vehicle as to interfere with the full use of the vehicle by passengers or with any equipment of such vehicle.

(Code 1956, § 12-197)

**Sec. 162-797. Maintenance of advertising material.**

Advertising, when placed in or on a vehicle, shall be maintained in a clean, neat and uniform manner. Soiled, torn or otherwise defaced advertisements shall be removed immediately from the advertising card holder.

(Code 1956, § 12-198)

**Sec. 162-798. Inspection of advertising posters.**

Each licensed vehicle owner who has installed an approved advertising card holder in or on the vehicle pursuant to the provisions contained herein shall submit such vehicle for inspection prior to placing such vehicle in operation. Vehicles shall be subject to inspection at all times, and such vehicles that fail to pass such inspection shall be subject to such penalties as are provided by this chapter.

(Code 1956, § 12-199)

**Sec. 162-799. Advertising holder inspection fee.**

There shall be an annual fee of $25.00 for advertising devices, payable in semiannual installments of $12.50 at the time of inspection. This fee shall be collected by the for-hire vehicle inspection station and shall be deposited with the department of finance. This fee shall not be charged for an animal-drawn vehicle advertisement.

(Code 1956, § 12-200)

**Sec. 162-800. Penalties for violation of advertising privileges.**

Failure to comply in any manner with the provisions of this division by any advertising firm, agent, owner or operator of any vehicle governed by this article, or any other person, shall subject the offender to such fines and penalties as are provided by this chapter as well as to the temporary or permanent removal of all advertising material from the vehicle of such owner or operator. The privilege to advertise in the vehicles covered by this division may be suspended or revoked by the director of the department of public works following due notice and a hearing in accordance with R.S. 49:951 et seq. at the ground transportation bureau.

(Code 1956, § 12-201; M.C.S., Ord. No. 21480, § 5, 4-1-04; M.C.S., Ord. 27992, § 3, 2-7-19; M.C.S., Ord. No. 28624, § 2, 3-11-21)

laws.title: Garden District tour bus route limitations
laws.content:
(a) Authorized zones. Except as otherwise provided by this section, no buses with a seating capacity of more than 20 passengers shall be permitted to travel on any street within the area known as the Garden District, which is bounded by St. Charles Avenue, Jackson Avenue, Louisiana Avenue and Magazine Street. Tour buses may be stopped for the purpose of receiving and discharging passengers for the Garden District at authorized zones that are marked and bear signs indicating that tour buses may stop for the purpose of receiving and discharging passengers. Tour buses may be parked while pedestrian Garden District Tours are in progress at authorized zones within nonresidential areas. The authorized zones shall be designated by the director of the department of public works.

(b) Exceptions.

(1) The bus route limitation of this section shall not be applicable to school buses transporting students in the Garden District.

(2) The director of the department of public works may authorize up to 22 buses per month having a seating capacity of more than 20 passengers to travel on Prytania Street and Washington Avenue within the Garden District for the sole purpose of receiving and discharging passengers from commercial establishments if customers were transported to the establishments by bus on a regular basis on or before July 1, 1979. A permit shall be issued by the director of the department of public works to each bus authorized to travel on Prytania Street and Washington Avenue under the provisions of this subsection. The permit shall be displayed in a conspicuous place on the bus so as to be visible to police or other law enforcement officers in accordance with regulations established by the director of the department of public works. Buses permitted under this subsection shall park only in authorized zones marked and bearing signs permitting such parking, such zones to be designated by the director of the department of public works and the director of the department of public works.

The director may revoke a permit issued to this section for repeated violations of this section.

laws.title: Vieux Carré bus limitations
laws.content:
(a) It shall be unlawful for any bus having an overall length longer than 31 feet to use any street within the Vieux Carré, except as provided for in the rules and regulations promulgated under subsection (d) of this section.

(b) Those buses with an overall length in excess of 20 feet and not greater than 31 feet may use the streets of the Vieux Carré as provided for in this section. For the purposes of this section a bus shall be defined as any road bus, tour bus or tour vehicle, excluding limousines and taxicabs.

(c) For the purposes of this section, Vieux Carré shall mean the area within the lake side of North Peters Street, the center line of Decatur Street between Conti Street and St. Philip Street, the downriver side of Esplanade Avenue, the river side of North Rampart Street and the downriver side of Canal Street. Therefore, all buses, regardless of the overall length, shall be permitted to use North Rampart Street, Canal Street, North Peters Street, and the river side of Decatur Street between Conti Street and St. Philip Street.

(d) A properly licensed CPNC bus having an overall length in excess of 20 feet and not greater than 31 feet shall be permitted to use routes in the Vieux Carré as recommended by the director of the department of public works and approved by the city council. The director of public works shall, within 135 days of the adoption of this ordinance (Ordinance Number 17,558 M.C.S., as amended by Ordinance Number 17,727 M.C.S.), promulgate such rules and regulations, in compliance with section 2-1000 of the City Code, as enacted by Ordinance Number 17,611 M.C.S., necessary to enforce the provisions of this section. Such rules and regulations shall become effective, in accordance with section 4-107(3)(d) of the Home Rule Charter, only after approval by the city council, after review and recommendation by the council’s ground transportation committee or its successor. No bus operator while loading or unloading passengers shall be permitted to idle the bus engine longer than ten minutes. Further, no bus shall be allowed to stop in one place for a period in excess of 15 minutes.

(e) A violation by a CPNC holder or its driver of any of the regulations set forth in this section shall result in a fine and/or suspension or revocation of the CPNC according to the following:

(1) First violation in any 12-month period shall result in a fine of not less than $200.00 nor more than $500.00, to be determined by a duly authorized hearing examiner following a hearing on the matter.

(2) Second violation in any 12-month period shall result in a fine of $500.00 and/or suspension of the CPNC for a minimum period of one month and a maximum period of six months, to be determined by a duly authorized hearing examiner following a hearing on the matter.

(3) Third violation in any 12-month period shall result in a fine of $500.00 and suspension of the CPNC for a minimum period of three months and a maximum

Supp. No. 95

CD162:75
§ 162-942

NEW ORLEANS CODE

period of 12 months, to be determined by a duly authorized hearing examiner following a hearing on the matter.

(4) Fourth violation in any 12-month period shall result in the revocation of the CPNC. If another violation takes place during the revocation period, an additional period of 12 months shall be added to the revocation period for each violation. Prior to such revocation, the CPNC holder shall be entitled to a hearing on the matter before a duly authorized hearing examiner.

(f) A violation by a bus driver or company who is not a CPNC holder of any of the regulations set forth in this section shall result in a fine and/or imprisonment and additional actions by the city according to the following:

(1) First violation shall result in a fine of not less than $200.00 and the department of public works' nonapproval of any CPNC application made by the offending driver or the offending company for a three-month period from the date of the violation.

(2) Second violation shall result in a fine of not less than $400.00 and imprisonment for not more than three months and the department of public works' nonapproval of any CPNC application made by the offending driver or the offending company for a six-month period from the date of the violation.

(3) Third violation shall result in a fine of not less than $500.00 and imprisonment for not less than 30 days. Thirty days or more of public service in the Vieux Carré and adjacent areas may be substituted for the days of imprisonment. Further, the department of public works shall not consider any CPNC application or issue any CPNC to the offending driver or the offending company for a period of nine months from the date of the violation.

(4) Four or more violations shall result in a fine of not less than $500.00 and imprisonment for not less than 60 days for each violation. Sixty days or more of public

service in the Vieux Carré and adjacent areas may be substituted for the days of imprisonment. Further, the department of public works shall not consider any CPNC application or issue any CPNC to the offending company for a period of 12 months from the date of the violation. Further, if more than four violations take place, an additional 12-month nonapproval period shall be added for each violation to the original period during which time no CPNC application shall be considered or issued.

(g) The director of the department of public works shall make such administrative regulations which may be necessary to implement the provisions of this section; such regulations shall become effective upon approval of the city council after review and recommendation by the council's ground transportation committee or its successor.

(Code 1956, § 12-250; M.C.S., Ord. No. 17,558, § 1, 6-6-96; M.C.S., Ord. No. 17,727, § 1, 8-15-96; M.C.S., Ord. No. 17,789, § 1, 10-3-96; M.C.S., Ord. No. 17,823, § 1, 10-17-96; M.C.S., Ord. No. 21480, § 5, 4-1-04; M.C.S., Ord. No. 25795, § 1, 4-24-14; M.C.S., Ord. No. 28624, § 2, 3-11-21)

State law reference—Authority to regulate, R.S. 45:180(F).

laws.title: Eastern New Orleans tour bus route limitations
laws.content:
Authorized zones. Except as otherwise provided by this section, no tours for compensation may be conducted in the area east of the Industrial Canal. Tours for compensation may not be conducted in that area.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 22118, § 1, 1-5-06)

laws.title: Amphibious vehicle limitations
laws.content:
Any tour bus or sightseeing bus capable of amphibious transportation shall be precluded from operating within the geographical boundaries of New Orleans City Council District "A" and New Orleans City Council District "C."

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 25794, § 1, 4-24-14)

laws.title: Prohibition on noisemakers and amplified sound in the operation of any tour or sightseeing vehicle including vehicles capable of amphibious transportation
laws.content:
The operators and employees of any tour bus or sightseeing bus including vehicles capable of amphibious transportation shall not use noisemakers, permit the use of noisemakers, or distribute noisemakers to passengers. Amplified sound, other than sounds produced for the legal operation of the vehicle, shall not be plainly audible from the public-right-of-way or private property while operating any tour bus or sightseeing bus including vehicles capable of amphibious transportation in the City of New Orleans in order to minimize the intrusion of amplified sound.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 25794, § 1, 4-24-14)

laws.title: Regulation of per capita continuous loop, fixed-route sightseeing tour vehicles
laws.content:
(a) Per capita continuous loop, fixed-route sightseeing tour vehicle stops located on city-owned streets or other city-owned property require approval by the director of public works.

(b) Signage located on city-owned streets or other city-owned property identifying the location of per capita continuous loop, fixed-route sightseeing tour vehicle stops is required, the design and placement of which requires approval by the director of public works.

(c) Stops on city-owned streets shall be for active passenger loading and unloading only and not used for staging.

(d) Per capita continuous loop sightseeing stops on city-owned streets that are co-located with regional transit authority stops are permitted, subject to the approval of the director of public works.

(e) The executive director of the regional transit authority shall be notified of the locations of the continuous loop, fixed-route sightseeing tour vehicle stops.

(f) The regional transit authority shall be notified by the department of public works of any application for a vehicle stop at the same location where an regional transit authority has a stop.

(g) The director of the department of public works is hereby authorized, as a police measure, to designate the location of continuous loop sightseeing stops on the streets and other public places in the city. Such stands shall be marked by appropriate signs and shall be reserved exclusively for the parking of taxicabs or other for-hire vehicles as specified by such signs, while waiting to pick up passengers for hire.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 27735, § 1, 4-19-18; M.C.S., Ord. No. 28624, § 2, 3-11-21; M.C.S., Ord. No. 30194, § 1, 12-19-24)

*Editor’s note—M.C.S., Ord. No. 27735, § 1, adopted April 19, 2018, set out provisions intended for use as § 162-944. At the editor’s discretion, to prevent duplication of section numbers, these provisions have been included as § 162-947.*

laws.title: Courtesy transportation declaration to be posted

(a) All courtesy transportation or courtesy vehicles in the tour industry shall be required to file a notarized declaration form annually with the ground transportation bureau of the department of public works specifying the following:

(1) Number of courtesy vehicles including the model of each vehicle.

(2) Vehicle identification number.

(3) License plate number of each courtesy vehicle.

(4) Proof of insurance of coverage.

(b) With the exception of limousines or luxury sedans, all courtesy transportation or courtesy vehicles in the tour industry shall have exterior signage (visible from a distance of 50 feet indicating the name of the owner of the vehicle (hotel, restaurant, etc.,) and that the courtesy vehicle is free of charge, courtesy, or complimentary. Failure to comply with the registration and requirements for courtesy transportation or courtesy vehicles in the tour industry shall subject the owner of the transportation or vehicles to a minimum fine of $25.00 for the first offense and $ 50.00 for subsequent offenses. If these fines are not paid within 30 days, the department of public works shall not issue a motor vehicle inspection tag to the vehicle in default.

**Secs. 162-963—162-995. Reserved.**

**ARTICLE XI. TOWING, RECOVERY AND STORAGE REGULATIONS***

**DIVISION 1. GENERALLY**

**Sec. 162-996. Definitions.**

The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:

*Accident* shall mean a situation where one or more motor vehicles have collided with any motor vehicle or object.

*City* shall mean the City of New Orleans.

*Compulsory liability insurance/security impoundment* shall mean the towing and storage of a vehicle in violation of state law requiring proof of insurance coverage to be maintained in a vehicle operated within the state.

*Consent tow* shall mean the towing of a motor vehicle upon the consent of the vehicle owner.

*Heavy-duty tow/vehicle* means any vehicle which because of its size, weight or other design characteristics, or due its position off road or submerged in water, would require its transport by towing by a heavy-duty tow truck as defined in sections 162-1020 through 162-1021.

*Motor vehicle* means every vehicle which is self-propelled, and every vehicle which is propelled by electric power obtained from overhead trolley wires, but not operated upon rails, but excluding a motorized bicycle. Motor vehicle shall also include a "low-speed vehicle" which is a four-wheeled, electric-powered vehicle with a maximum speed of not less than 20 miles per hour but not more than 25 miles per hour and is equipped

*Nonconsensual tow* shall mean the towing of a motor vehicle where the vehicle owner has not called a towing service for assistance or is unable or unwilling to do so.

*NOPD* shall mean the New Orleans Police Department.

*NOPD towing allocation list* shall mean the list of towing companies authorized to provide tow truck response and storage as maintained by the NOPD towing and recovery section.

*Police authorized tow* shall mean the nonconsensual towing of a motor vehicle upon authorization of a city police officer from a police scene at which the vehicle owner is not present, is incapable of making or declines to make arrangements for the removal of the vehicle or is in violation of state compulsory liability insurance/security law.

*Police scene or scene* shall mean a place at which an accident has taken place that is subject to police field investigation, a place at which the city has recovered a stolen vehicle, a place at which a vehicle has been abandoned in a roadway, a place where custodial arrest by police has taken place, or any place at which a vehicle is subject to removal or impoundment pursuant to law by a police officer.

*Storage lot* shall mean an automobile storage facility situated within the city.

*Recovered stolen vehicle* shall mean any vehicle which has been previously reported stolen, recovered by a police officer, and no longer has any evidentiary value.

*Tow* means pull, winch, carry, or otherwise move a vehicle or equipment other than by its own power with the use of a tow truck.

*Tow truck* means any motor vehicle equipped with a boom or booms, winches, slings, tilt beds, and/or similar equipment designed for the towing and/or recovery of vehicles and other objects which cannot operate under their own power or for some reason must be transported by means of towing.

*Towing allocation approval* means a letter issued by the NOPD which authorizes a towing company to perform towing and provide for storage of vehicles established by this article.

*Towing allocation decal* means a sticker issued by the NOPD for each tow truck to be used in the performance of towing allocation list responsibilities which certifies that such truck has been inspected and meets all vehicle, boom and winch, and accessory specifications and requirements as are mandated by law.

*Towing service business/towing company* means the business by an individual, partnership, corporation, or other entity of providing tow service which may include transportation and storage of a vehicle to a storage lot.

*Vehicle owner* shall mean the actual owner of the vehicle towed or transported or any driver of the vehicle who reasonably appears to have authority to operate the vehicle.

laws.title: Operational requirements
laws.content:
Every towing service business operating within the City of New Orleans shall comply with the following operational requirements: Each tow truck and towing service business shall possess all necessary federal, state, and city certificates, licenses and permits to operate as designated.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 28755, § 1, 8-5-21)

laws.title: Administration, enforcement
laws.content:
It shall be the duty of the NOPD, under the direction of the superintendent of police (superintendent), to implement, administer, and enforce the provisions of this article. The duties shall include, but not be limited to the following: the proper advertisement requesting applications for the towing allocation list; the evaluation of applications for the towing allocation list and determination of towing companies which qualify; the issuance of towing allocation decals;

**Sec. 162-999. NOPD towing allocation list.**

The NOPD is authorized to prescribe and promulgate rules, regulations and minimum requirements for towing service businesses to be included on a towing allocation list to provide emergency tow truck response and storage for nonconsensual tows in order to increase public safety and in conformance with R.S. 32:1711 through R.S. 32:1731. Any such rules, regulations, and requirements not already contained in this article shall be subject to the procedure for the promulgation of regulations established in section 2-1000. The towing allocation list shall include only towing businesses located within the city and ownership or contractual access to business and storage lot facilities within the city. Such authorization shall remain current for one calendar year unless terminated by an action of the NOPD. Qualification for the towing allocation system list shall be on an annual basis only. (M.C.S., Ord. No. 28755, § 1, 8-5-21)

laws.title: Application and Fees
laws.content:
**Sec. 162-1000. Application.**

Each applicant for the towing allocation list shall submit an application with the NOPD, shall meet the requirements established herein, and shall certify the same in writing. No participation shall be granted if the applicant fails to meet the requirements of this article or if the applicant provides the NOPD with false, misleading, or incomplete information. Towing allocation decals issued based on false, misleading, or incomplete information furnished by the applicant shall be revoked by the superintendent, or their designee, and towing allocation privileges shall be permanently revoked for any company found providing false, misleading, or incomplete information on their application. Applicants shall agree to release vehicles immediately upon retrieval by the owner and bill the City of New Orleans directly for fees associated with towing, recovery, and/or storage of vehicles that have been previously reported as stolen, provided that the City of New Orleans is not billed for more than 90 days of storage fees, except in instances of extenuating circumstances when agreed upon by the chief administrative officer. Under no circumstances shall an applicant require vehicle owners to provide a copy of a police report as a condition of releasing their vehicle. (M.C.S., Ord. No. 28755, § 1, 8-5-21; M.C.S., Ord. No. 29085, § 1, 7-7-22)

**Sec. 162-1001. Owners and operators**

(a) No officer, owner, partner, person, employee, or other individual with a financial interest in the licensed towing company making an application for the towing allocation list, shall have ever been convicted of a violation of any of the provisions of R.S. 32:521 pertaining to stored motor vehicles or R.S. 32:701 et seq., the Louisiana Certificate of Title Law, R.S. 14:67.26 pertaining to auto theft, R.S. 14:68.4 pertaining to unauthorized use of a motor vehicle, or R.S. 14:69 pertaining to possession of stolen property concerning anything vehicle related.

(b) Additionally, any company, which has an officer, principle or employee who has been convicted of a felony within the last ten years, or is under indictment at the time of application, shall not be considered for participation on the towing allocation list.

i. The superintendent may establish such rules and regulations as are necessary to enforce the provisions of this section including criminal history investigations of company personnel for the last ten years. (M.C.S., Ord. No. 28755, § 1, 8-5-21)

laws.title: Application fee
laws.content:
The NOPD shall charge a $20.00 processing fee for each application for the towing allocation list. This fee shall cover the inspection of the applicant's storage facility and tow truck. Additionally, there shall be a $10.00 surcharge for each towing truck inspected which shall be utilized in performance of towing allocation list duties. Such fees are due when the application is presented to the NOPD and are non-refundable regardless of the applicant's eligibility, approval/disapproval, or removal from the towing allocation list.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 28755, § 1, 8-5-21)

laws.title: Required
laws.content:
The superintendent, or their designee, shall inspect each tow truck which shall be used in the performance of towing allocation list responsibilities for conformance with the tow truck requirements established in this article. The superintendent, or their designee, shall make available all inspection requirements in advanced of an inspection.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 28755, § 1, 8-5-21)

laws.title: Re-inspections; suspension, revocation of license
laws.content:
Any towing company whose tow truck fails to meet the requirements of inspection outlined in city or state law shall have ten days to bring such vehicle into compliance with the requirements. Failure to bring the vehicle into compliance within ten calendar days of the date of the inspection failure shall result in a temporary suspension of the towing allocation privileges and removal of the towing allocation decal until compliance is reached.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 28755, § 1, 8-5-21)

laws.title: Spot inspections
laws.content:
All tow trucks operated in the performance of towing allocation responsibilities shall be subject to inspection at any time while certified under this article and shall be maintained in a state of mechanical fitness as required by city and state law. The superintendent, or their designee, shall have the authority to require periodic inspections, other than those regularly scheduled under section 162-1288, when such inspections through reason and sound judgment are deemed necessary.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 28755, § 1, 8-5-21)

laws.title: Special inspections
laws.content:
In addition to the annual inspections required, every tow truck shall be inspected by NOPD:

(a) Prior to issuance of the towing allocation decal;

(b) Whenever there is a transfer of the vehicle from one licensed towing company to another; or

Supp. No. 97

NEW ORLEANS CODE

(c) Whenever the vehicle has been involved in a crash requiring repairs.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 28755, § 1, 8-5-21)

laws.title: Inspection decal
laws.content:
(a) When the towing vehicle has met all of the requirements established in this article and paid the required fees, the superintendent, or their designee, shall issue a towing allocation decal of such size, color and form as the superintendent, or their designee may determine, and shall cause the same to be affixed to the windshield of the vehicle. The towing allocation decal shall be identified by number. If it becomes damaged or destroyed, a duplicate shall be issued by the superintendent, or their designee, after application has been made, at the same cost as the original decal.

(b) The operation of a tow truck by a towing allocation list operator which has not received a towing allocation decal shall result in their revocation from the towing allocation list.

(c) No towing allocation decal shall be issued until proof of liability coverage that meets the requirements of this article is confirmed by the city.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 28755, § 1, 8-5-21)

laws.title: Expiration and renewal of certificate
laws.content:
(a) Each tow truck certificate issued by the superintendent, or their designee, pursuant to the provisions of this article, unless removed for cause, shall expire at the end of each calendar year; shall be renewable on the first of the following calendar year; and shall show, by numeral on the face thereof, the year of its expiration.

(b) Unless the towing allocation decal/certificate is renewed prior to its expiration, each such decal/certificate shall expire on the applicable expiration date as set forth in a schedule determined and posted by the superintendent, or their designee.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 28755, § 1, 8-5-21)

laws.title: Removal of towing allocation privileges
laws.content:
Upon completion of the towing vehicle inspection, the NOPD shall, if necessary, remove from the approved list any towing allocation company operating a tow truck found defective or is not able to pass inspection at any time. The current decal shall be removed from the vehicle by the NOPD and a new towing allocation decal shall not be issued until all defects have been corrected and the towing vehicle passes inspection. Additionally, any towing company, towing vehicle or driver that violates this article or the rules set forth by the superintendent, or their designee, shall have their towing allocation privileges revoked until the case is adjudicated in court.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 28755, § 1, 8-5-21)

laws.title: Towing allocation list qualification criteria
laws.content:
Each applicant shall maintain their towing and recovery business "storage facility" in Orleans Parish. The applicant must maintain all records pertaining to calls made under the towing allocation list at the storage facility, titled for this towing, recovery, and storage business and staffed Monday through Friday 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., excluding legal holidays. The towing service must make these records available for inspection by the NOPD. A representative of the towing and recovery business shall be on call for emergencies, and an owner of a towed vehicle shall not be charged a storage fee for the days that the owner could not retrieve his or her vehicle as a result of an action or omission from which the tow business would benefit. Each applicant shall maintain all insurance coverage required by Louisiana law, including worker's compensation insurance and sufficient liability insurance to indemnify the City of New Orleans against any losses. A certificate of insurance shall be required as proof of insurance at the submission of an application or renewal. There shall be an annual fee of $20.00 paid to the City of New Orleans for the NOPD to inspect and verify that a towing business and single tow truck meet the criteria as herein established for the towing allocation list at a particular location in the city. There shall be an annual fee of $10.00 paid to the City of New

laws.title: Equipment requirements/personnel standards
laws.content:
Tow trucks and operators shall meet all City of New Orleans equipment requirements and personnel standards as follows:

(1) Each towing business shall use a unique name as designated on the state towing license, which shall be clearly distinguishable from the trade name of any other licensee.

(2) No tow truck owner shall operate or permit anyone to operate a tow truck until the following requirements are fulfilled:

a. Tow truck operators shall have valid licenses as required by state and municipal law.

b. Every operator shall be competent by reason of experience or training to safely operate the type of tow truck or tow trucks authorized by the state towing license.

c. Every operator shall possess the knowledge and ability to rig, move, pick up, and transport vehicles without causing or increasing existing damage insofar as possible.

d. Every operator shall be free from impairment of alcoholic beverages, narcotics, or dangerous drugs when operating a towing service or tow truck.

e. No tow truck company or individual shall operate a tow truck without having in his possession proof of current insurance in accordance with state law.

(3) Every owner and operator shall be familiar with the laws, rules, and regulations pertaining to tow trucks.

(4) Drivers are to wear clothing sufficient to identify the towing company and driver.

(5) Any person operating a tow truck will have the necessary experience and qualifications to operate a tow truck in the manner required by this article.

(6) All tow truck drivers will develop, for each vehicle towed or serviced, an itemized statement, bill, or invoice of the towing and storage charges incurred.

(7) Drivers must be 18 years of age or older. Only those duly licensed to drive in the State of Louisiana shall be permitted to drive and operate a tow truck. The class of operator’s license must be compatible to the equipment operated.

(8) Tow trucks shall comply with all applicable lighting and equipment requirements in accordance with state law.

(9) All tow trucks, except slide back recovery vehicles while they are transporting a vehicle on their beds, shall be equipped with at least one amber rotating or flashing beacon visible for 360 degrees at a distance of 1,000 feet under normal atmospheric conditions at night. While at the scene of an accident, recovered stolen vehicle, or disabled vehicle, or when actually towing a vehicle, a tow truck operator shall illuminate or cause to be illuminated the amber rotating or flashing beacon.

(10) All tow trucks shall be equipped with the following required equipment:

a. *Oil-absorbent material*: All tow trucks shall have at least the following: Sand, clean dirt, or a commercial oil and grease absorbent in an amount of at least 1,155 cubic inches or the equivalent of a five-gallon can of material which is carried in a weatherproof container.

b. *Electric lantern or flashlight*: All tow trucks shall have at all times, in good working condition, a battery

Supp. No. 97

CD162:83
§ 162-1013

NEW ORLEANS CODE

powered electric lantern, or two-cell flashlight in lieu of an electric lantern.

c. Fire extinguishers: Each tow truck shall be equipped with either:

1. A fire extinguisher having an Underwriters Laboratories rating of 5 B:C or more; or

2. Two fire extinguishers, each of which has an Underwriters Laboratories rating of 4 B:C or more.

d. Steering wheel clamp: A steering wheel clamp, rope, or its equivalent shall be of sufficient strength to adequately lock the steering mechanism of a towed vehicle in a straightforward position.

e. Tow sling or tow plate:

1. Every tow truck shall be equipped with a tow sling, plate, bar, or equivalent that is structurally adequate for any weight drawn. Slings or plates shall be properly and securely mounted on the tow truck without excessive slack.

2. The tow plates, slings, and tow-bars shall be securely attached to the towed vehicle by means of chains, hooks, straps, or equivalent. Attachment chains will have a capacity equal to the weight of the towed vehicle. At least two chains, hooks, straps, or equivalent shall be used.

f. Attachments:

1. Every towed vehicle shall be coupled to the tow truck with attachments of a structural strength adequate to safely tow the vehicle.

2. Attachments shall be securely attached to the towing and towed vehicle with no more slack left in the attachment than is necessary to permit proper turning.

(11) Each tow truck shall display on the door or side panel the trade name to their respective business, as registered with the NOPD. The letters are to be at least $2\frac{1}{2}$ inches in height and shall be permanently affixed to the tow truck.

(12) Capacities and specifications of towing equipment:

a. The minimum standards of each tow truck license shall be determined solely by the manufacturer’s specifications for the capabilities and capacities of the tow trucks and all towing equipment.

b. Each tow truck shall be equipped with only those winches and cranes that have been produced and constructed by a manufacturer of such equipment who carries product liability insurance, and which regularly produces winches and cranes of guaranteed quality.

1. A winch or crane will not be prohibited by this subsection if the tow truck owner possesses certification from a reputable testing laboratory, regularly engaged in the testing of such equipment or similar equipment, indicating that the capacity of the winch or crane is not less than the weight for which application has been made.

2. All costs of such testing and certification shall be borne by the tow truck owner/applicant.

(13) No tow truck shall tow another vehicle, unless the tow truck has a manufacturer’s rating of 10,000 gross vehicle weight rating (GVWR) or higher, and the tow truck has been issued the appropriate towing license plate required by the State of Louisiana. Tow trucks with a manufacturer’s rating of less than 10,000 GVWR shall not be permitted.
