(14) All tow truck components (i.e., winches, booms, cables, cable clamps, thimbles, sheaves, guides, controls, blocks, slings, chains, hooks, and hydraulic components) are to be maintained in good condition at all times. Cable fittings for hooks, slings, etc., shall be assembled by factory recommendations and specifications. All portable equipment (i.e., shovel, broom, reflectors, flashlights, fire extinguisher, etc.) shall be permanent accessories and be available on the truck at all times.

(15) It is required that the owner/operator carry on board the towing vehicle the following: Proof of all required insurance including a hazardous material policy, if applicable.

(16) Tow truck equipment specifications:

a. At no time shall any tow truck exceed its manufacturer’s gross vehicle weight rating or the manufacturer’s rated capacity for the towing assembly.

b. At no time will a tow truck attach to a vehicle which, by its size and/or weight, would make towing such vehicle an unsafe movement. That is, a tow truck and its load should never exceed the capabilities of the towing vehicle to safely accelerate, stop, or maneuver.

(17) Towing services shall determine the method and manner of removing vehicles; provided, however, that they shall exercise due care in removal operations and shall follow the lawful direction of any law enforcement officer directing the removal so as not to impede traffic or endanger the general public and property.

(18) Each tow truck authorized on the City of New Orleans towing allocation list shall display on the left front window above the brake tag the NOPD decal, recognizing their approved participation on the towing allocation list.

(19) Towing services and operators on the towing allocation list, in accordance with the provisions of this article, shall be liable and answerable for damages for all injuries or damages whatsoever caused directly or indirectly by the use or operation of the towing allocation list tow truck, whether at the time of the injury or damages such tow truck was being used or operated by the owner, agent, servant or employee or other persons not agents, servants or employees of the holder, unless proof is shown that the vehicle was stolen.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 28755, § 1, 8-5-21)

laws.title: Storage facilities
laws.content:
Storage facilities shall meet all City of New Orleans requirements as follows:

(1) Towing/storage facility business practices.

a. Storage facility business hours for purposes of inspection of records, place of business, and towing equipment shall be Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., excluding holidays.

b. When an operator is not open for business and does not have personnel present at the place of business, the operator shall post a clearly visible telephone number at the business location to advise the public how to make contact for the release of vehicles or personal property.

c. All billing invoices that are provided to the redeemer of the vehicle shall be consecutively numbered and shall contain the following information:

1. Date of service and tow truck operator’s name.

2. The name of any police agency requesting the tow, if applicable.

3. If the call for service is for a private individual, then an invoice must contain the full name, address, driver’s license

Supp. No. 97

CD162:85
§ 162-1014

NEW ORLEANS CODE

number or some form of permanent identification of the person requesting the tow.

4. Itemized fees for service; and

5. The date the vehicle was released.

d. Any invoice, bill, statement, authorization or other form utilized by a towing company, which is to be signed by the owner (or agent) of a vehicle to be towed, must be of a format approved by the NOPD. This form must clearly denote what service is being authorized by signature. That is, there will be a separate signature line which merely authorizes the towing of the vehicle and another signature line to authorize any repairs to the vehicle.

e. No repairs shall be performed upon any vehicle unless there is an explicit signed written agreement authorizing such repairs.

f. Towing companies must submit a sample copy of their invoices to the NOPD towing and recovery unit to be kept on file there. Any invoice which does not meet the criteria outlined above will be in violation of these regulations and any charges for services on an unauthorized invoice will be forfeited. Towing companies shall furnish copies of invoices required herein with their application to the towing allocation list.

g. A copy of the invoice shall be filed by invoice number at the business location and a copy of any voided invoices shall be retained in this same file.

h. The address that the towing service lists on its application shall be the business location where its business records are kept. The application shall also list the locations of all storage areas for vehicle redemption.

i. The owner of a storage facility will be required to maintain a suitable office to transact business and to accommodate the public. It shall be staffed from at least 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., Monday through Friday, except holidays, throughout the year. Such facilities must be maintained properly, be clean, be presentable at all times and shall be subject to inspection by the NOPD towing and recovery unit.

j. Towing services must make business records available for inspection upon request by law enforcement officers, which information shall be confidential and shall not be released or deemed a public record.

(2) Storage procedures:

a. All vehicles shall be handled and returned in substantially the same condition as they existed before being towed.

b. All storage facilities shall employ reasonable safeguards and procedures so that all personal belongings and contents in the vehicle are intact and returned to the vehicle's owner or agent upon release of the vehicle. Reasonable requests for the return of essential property to the owner or agent of the property prior to the release of the vehicle shall be considered and honored wherever possible.

c. All personal property left in a vehicle and not claimed prior to a towing company obtaining a permit to sell such vehicle will be handled in accordance with existing applicable civil law. Reasonable requests for the return of essential property shall be honored whenever possible.

d. Any person who shows proof of ownership or written authorization from the impounded vehicle's

Supp. No. 97

CD162:86
VEHICLES FOR HIRE

§ 162-1014

registered or legal owner may inspect and view the vehicle without charge during normal business hours.

(3) Storage facility:

a. Storage areas must be secured against unauthorized entry in such a way as to give security to the property contained therein.

b. Storage lots shall be designed to be adequate in size for the individual towing service’s need for storing vehicles. The storage facility shall be of sufficient size to accommodate a minimum of 20 stored vehicles. Shared use of a storage facility by more than one towing and recovery business is prohibited, unless authorized by the Louisiana Department of Public Safety and Corrections.

c. If a facility uses outdoor storage, fence material shall be of wood or metal design or of no less quality wire than $14\frac{1}{2}$ gauge hog wire.

    1. The fence must not be less than six feet in height.

    2. All lots shall have at least one gate of the same quality material as the fence.

    3. If such construction upon existing lot(s) is in violation of municipal zoning ordinances or other laws, the operator may file a petition for an alternate means of compliance and a proposed security plan with the NOPD towing and recovery unit.

d. If the storage is an open area, it shall be adequately lighted as described herein.

    1. Such storage area must have security with reasonable human attendance.

    2. Such open area must be paved or have a sufficiently hard or gravel surface to prevent problems in entry or exit during inclement weather.

3. A conspicuous sign shall be maintained at all times at the entrance to the impound lot and at the impound lot office stating the name of business, telephone number, after hours telephone number, and hours of operation.

4. All impound lots will be lighted during all hours of darkness.

5. The gate to the impound lot(s) shall be locked during the hours of darkness except to provide reasonable ingress and egress in connection with towing service operations.

6. All storage facilities are subject to inspection by the NOPD and must meet the applicable standards defined herein.

(4) [Minimum security requirements.] The foregoing shall be considered minimum security requirements.

a. The towing allocation list operator shall, at all times, keep the NOPD advised of the address of the storage facility furnished by it under this requirement. Each vehicle storage facility as provided herein must be approved by the NOPD. Each storage facility shall be inspected by the NOPD and shall contain a minimum of 7,200 square feet of storage area. This is inclusive of a separate and secure area where vehicles towed due to towing allocation duties are properly separately stored.

b. Nothing contained in this section shall be considered to supersede or otherwise affect applicable provisions of the zoning ordinance of the city.

c. Whenever any vehicle has been towed (other than by owner’s request)

Supp. No. 97

CD162:87
§ 162-1014

NEW ORLEANS CODE

to a storage facility where fees are charged for such storage or parking, the owner or operator of the storage facility shall, within 24 hours of the time such vehicle is towed to that storage facility, notify the NOPD towing and recovery unit that the vehicle has been towed for storage. The storage operator shall provide to the law enforcement authorities or their designees:

1. The police item number;
2. The location from which the vehicle was towed;
3. A description of the vehicle;
4. The license plate number and vehicle identification number of the vehicle;
5. The name and address of the location to which the vehicle was towed; and
6. An official report of stored vehicle card must be filed with the department of public safety, office of motor vehicles, dealer support section or its agent.

d. Each towing service shall be licensed as a separate legal entity.

e. Towing operators intending to lease or rent storage facilities from established business firms shall file such plan of lease or rent with the NOPD for approval. Such plan must include specific terms delineating the responsibility of the operator relating to compliance with these regulations and assurance that accountability is maintained.

f. Towing operators will maintain all records dealing with the towing and storage of vehicles for a minimum of five years. The NOPD shall have the right to enter and inspect all towing/storage facilities during normal working hours and these documents will be made available upon request.

g. All towing services shall maintain impoundment records which shall include the following information:

1. The date and time the call for service was received and from whom it was received, when applicable.
2. The police item number.
3. A description of the vehicle including make, model, color, vehicle identification number, and license plate number.
4. The date, time, and place at which the operator began the towing operation.
5. The date at which the impounded vehicle was released to the owner.
6. The name of the driver of the tow truck.
7. Letters of notification as required by these rules.
8. Proof of administrative costs.
9. Records of release of vehicle(s).

(5) Storage rates. All storage facility operators shall charge rates as set forth in the rules and regulations of the Louisiana Public Service Commission.

(6) Owner notification of a stored vehicle.

a. Within seven days of the time that a vehicle is placed in a storage facility, the operator of the storage facility shall notify in writing, by certified letter, return receipt requested, the last registered owner of the vehicle (at the owner's last known address) and the lien holder, should there be any.

b. The storage operator shall provide to the owner:

1. The police item number.
2. The location and name of the storage facility.
3. The vehicle identification number.

Supp. No. 97

CD162:88
VEHICLES FOR HIRE

§ 162-1015

4. The vehicle license plate number.

5. A description of the vehicle.

6. The name of the person or agency that had the vehicle towed and/or placed in storage.

7. The date that the vehicle was placed in storage.

8. The condition of the vehicle.

9. The notice of the owner's right to an administrative hearing.

10. The address to which the request for a hearing must be sent.

11. The date by which the request for a hearing must be mailed, by certified letter, return receipt requested, which shall be ten days from the date that the owner's notification is postmarked.

c. Administrative fees:

1. Towing services may charge the registered owner/lienholder those administrative costs incurred by the filing of the official report of stored vehicle card with the office of motor vehicles along with any postal charges related to the mailing of the official report of stored vehicle card or certified letters to the registered owner/lienholder.

2. All costs must be documented with receipts which shall be made available to the registered owner/lienholder upon demand. Failure to comply will result in the forfeiture of all administrative costs, towing, and storage fees.

3. At no time will administrative costs exceed $25.00 for in-state notifications and $30.00 for out-of-state notifications.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 28755, § 1, 8-5-21)

CD162:89

laws.title: NOPD towing allocation list dispatch—Accident scenes, recovered stolen vehicles, police emergencies, and compulsory liability insurance/security impoundment
laws.content:
(a) Accident scenes, police emergencies. Whenever a motor vehicle has been involved in an accident or collision within the limits of the City of New Orleans and is unable to proceed safely, or the driver is physically unable to drive the motor vehicle, the investigating officer shall request of the driver that the driver designate a towing business to tow the motor vehicle. In the event that the driver is physically unable to designate a towing business, or expresses no preference for a towing business, the towing business next on the towing allocation list maintained by the NOPD shall be dispatched to the scene of the accident to tow the motor vehicle. For any other emergency requirements for a towing service by the NOPD, this same procedure and rotation shall be followed.

(b) For towing and impoundment of vehicles as required for violation of state law regarding compulsory liability insurance/security, a separate towing allocation list for this purpose shall be utilized. The towing business next on the towing allocation list maintained by the NOPD shall be dispatched to the scene of an impoundment to tow the motor vehicle.

(c) For towing and impoundment of recovered stolen vehicles, a separate towing allocation list shall be utilized. Whenever the police locates a vehicle which has been reported stolen and the owner of the vehicle cannot be located or is unwilling or unable to remove the vehicle from the recovery location, and the vehicle no longer has any evidentiary value to the police, the towing business next on the towing allocation list maintained by the NOPD shall be dispatched to tow the vehicle.
§ 162-1015

NEW ORLEANS CODE

(d) For towing and impoundment of abandoned and nuisance motor vehicles, the NOPD shall use its allocation lists. Whenever the parking enforcement division notifies the NOPD that is cannot tow or store an abandoned or nuisance vehicle, the towing business next on a towing allocation list maintained by the NOPD shall be dispatched to tow the vehicle. The towing business shall not lose its place in the towing allocation list from which it was chosen when picking up an abandoned and nuisance motor vehicle.

(e) The NOPD shall log the following information:

(1) Police item number;

(2) Time and date of the dispatch;

(3) Description of the vehicle to be towed;

(4) Purpose of the tow request for services;

(5) Name(s) of the dispatching officer(s); and

(6) Name(s) of the towing business(es) called.

(f) If tow truck operators are unable to respond when summoned by special request or through the NOPD towing allocation list, they must immediately notify the NOPD and shall not summon a substitute. Multiple failures to respond when summoned will subject the towing service business to review and possible removal from the NOPD towing allocation list.

(g) For towing and impoundment of vehicles as required for violation of this Code regarding illegal dumping, a separate towing allocation list for this purpose shall be utilized. The towing business next on the towing allocation list maintained by the NOPD shall be dispatched to the scene of an impoundment to tow the motor vehicle.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 28755, § 1, 8-5-21)

laws.title: Schedule of fees; charge or fee increases
laws.content:
Whenever a motor vehicle has been towed through a towing service business obtained from the NOPD towing allocation list, the owner/operator of the vehicle being towed shall be responsible for the payment of fees associated with the towing and recovery, and storage, if applicable. The maximum charges or fees for emergency towing by a vehicle owner or operator using the towing allocation list, and for towing performed without the knowledge and consent of the owner or operator of a vehicle, shall be set in accordance with the mandatory tariff schedule set forth by the Louisiana Public Service Commission Schedule of Prescribed Rates and Requirements for Non-Consensual Towing and Recovery Services. Notwithstanding the foregoing, in no instance shall victims of certain crimes be responsible for the payment of fees associated with the towing, recovery, and/or storage of a stolen vehicle in accordance with section 154-705 and section 154-781 of the Code.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 28755, § 1, 8-5-21; M.C.S., Ord. No. 29085, § 1, 7-7-22)

laws.title: Response to towing allocation list, response time
laws.content:
(a) In any case where public safety considerations permit, and where the vehicle operator specifically requests that a particular licensed tow company provide for the removal, towing and/or storage of his vehicle, the vehicle operator’s request shall be honored even if the towing company requested is not a listed towing allocation operator; provided, however, where the public health, safety and welfare dictate an

Supp. No. 101

CD162:90
VEHICLES FOR HIRE

§ 162-1018

allocation operator be used, it shall be the duty  
of law enforcement officials to direct the removal  
by listed towing allocation operator.

(b) The maximum allowable response time by  
a licensed towing company requested by the  
vehicle operator, other than a listed towing

Supp. No. 101

CD162:90.1

VEHICLES FOR HIRE

§ 162-1019

allocation operator, shall be 45 minutes from notification by the vehicle owner or the law enforcement officer. Upon the expiration of such 45 minutes and the dispatching of a listed towing allocation operator, the towing allocation list operator shall have sole authority for removal of vehicles.

(c) All towing businesses must be able to respond in accordance with all traffic laws and safe driving practices to the scene within a 45-minute time period on a 24-hour, 365-day basis.

(d) Towing businesses shall ensure that all operators possess the knowledge and skills to determine the proper sizing, weight requirements, and type of equipment necessary to handle each towing assignment on a damage free basis. In those instances where a towing business representative determines that a different type of equipment is necessary, that business shall be allowed to summon its own equipment, such delivery within a time period not to exceed an additional 30 minutes. If the towing business does not possess the equipment necessary to relocate or clear an accident safely, or to handle the towing and recovery of a recovered stolen vehicle, an immediate notification to the on-scene police officer is required so that the next towing business on the towing allocation list may be officially notified to respond by the NOPD.

(e) Towing businesses designated to respond on the towing allocation list for towing and impoundment of vehicles in violation of state compulsory liability insurance/security shall respond and utilize damage-free towing equipment only.

(f) Towing businesses shall have communication equipment at their facility to provide direct contact between the tow representative and their tow wagons. Citizen band radios and pagers are not sufficient equipment for this purpose.

(g) The allocation of multiple vehicle accident scenes shall be assigned on a "one car - one tow" system. The investigating police officer shall notify the police communications dispatcher of the vehicle license numbers of those vehicles requiring towing support. The sequence of the license plates submitted shall determine the assignment of the towing business in that order of towing allocation list. The towing business shall be notified of their assigned vehicle by license plate at dispatch.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 28755, § 1, 8-5-21)

laws.title: Licensee requirements
laws.content:
(a) It shall be the duty of the driver of each tow truck that picks up wrecked or disabled vehicles for the purposes of towing the same away to clear the street or highway of all debris, parts, glass, and automotive fluids.

(b) The licensee shall be responsible and liable for any damages or losses inflicted to vehicles lifted, hauled, or transported, or subjected to any other activity performed which is the subject of the licensee's responsibilities and shall be responsible for maintaining the safety and security of contents of the vehicle in his care and custody.

(c) A vehicle removed from the scene shall be transported to its point of destination or storage by the most direct route practical.

(d) Towing companies which are also engaged in the automotive body repair service shall have clearly printed on the front of all invoices or receipts for towing services the following:

(1) A statement which informs the owner or operator of a vehicle towed pursuant to towing allocation list responsibilities that the owner or operator is under no obligation to have body repair or any other work performed on the towed vehicle by the business which towed the vehicle;

(2) The maximum daily vehicle storage charge;

(3) The right of the owner or operator to remove a vehicle upon payment of the accrued daily storage fee and towing fee.

(e) All towing companies shall be party to a reciprocal assistance agreement under which requests for assistance in the performance of allocation responsibilities shall be honored by

Supp. No. 97

CD162:91
§ 162-1019

NEW ORLEANS CODE

any other allocation list operator when feasible. Assistance by a company other than an approved towing allocation business is prohibited.

(f) Towing companies shall immediately inform the NOPD whenever a vehicle to which it has been dispatched is placarded as a carrier of hazardous material. The towing company shall not move a placarded vehicle except under the on-site supervision of department of fire officials (NOFD). However, the NOPD after consultation with NOFD officials may direct the removal of the placarded vehicle without such on-site supervision.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 28755, § 1, 8-5-21)

laws.title: Applicant qualifications
laws.content:
(a) An applicant for a heavy-duty tow truck allocation shall comply or present substantial evidence of his intention and ability to comply with the minimum qualifications herein listed. In any event, an applicant who has been determined by the superintendent, or their designee, to be eligible for heavy duty tows shall, within four days of such determination, provide the superintendent, or their designee, with copies of purchase orders for any equipment which must be purchased to meet equipment qualifications established herein. Any such equipment to be ordered must be available for service by the licensee within 90 days of a determination of heavy-duty towing allocation eligibility. Failure to meet these deadlines may result in the loss of the applicant’s eligibility. Every towing company making application shall have operated a heavy-duty tow truck service domiciled in the parish for at least two continuous years immediately prior to submission of a towing allocation application. The city council may approve the application of a towing company not domiciled in the parish to provide service to the 15th Ward (Algiers) after having received a recommendation thereon from the superintendent and upon a determination that such area would otherwise receive inadequate or delayed service.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 28755, § 1, 8-5-21)

laws.title: Equipment
laws.content:
Each applicant for heavy-duty tow truck allocation under this article shall own and have in operable condition, not less than two heavy-duty tow trucks conforming to the following specifications:

(1) Heavy-duty tow truck minimum specifications:

(a) Gross vehicle weight rating of not less than 33,000 pounds as rated by the manufacturer or certifying laboratories; normally $3\frac{1}{2}$ tons.

(b) A minimum of 102 inches from the rear of passenger cab to center of rear axle for single-axle trucks or 102 inches to the center of bogie on tandem trucks.

(c) Single or tandem rear axles equipped with dual rear wheels and tires.

(d) Five-speed manual or automatic transmission.

(e) A service brake system, air only, capable of controlling the movement of or stopping and holding the combination of vehicles under normal and adverse conditions. The air brake system shall be equipped to provide for the transfer of air from the wrecker’s brake system to that of the towed vehicle.

(f) A parking brake system separate from the service brake which shall be maintained in proper working order.

(2) Boom and winch minimum specifications (bare drums):

(a) Minimum rated boom capacity of 25 tons.

(b) Mechanical or hydraulic power winches with a total rated capacity of not less than 25 tons or as per manufacturer rating.

(c) Minimum of 200 feet of wire rope per winch at least 9/16-inch in diameter of rated breaking strength of 27,000 pounds.

Supp. No. 97

CD162:92

laws.title: (3) Required accessories
laws.content:
(a) Chain equipped with hooks at least three-eighths inch in diameter.

(b) At least 75 feet of auxiliary air lines equipped with necessary transfer fittings.

(c) Heavy-duty truck towing hitch.

(d) Flashing system with two revolving amber lights mounted on each towing vehicle, body clearance lights, reflectors and at least one work light mounted which has the capacity to light the scene of an accident under darkened or foggy conditions.

(e) One or more brooms, a shovel and 50 pounds of chemical fire extinguisher.

(f) Power up and power down winch operating from the rear of the tow truck. All winches must be operational. Electrical and hand winches shall not be used.

(g) Tow trucks must have throttle control and hydraulic, air or manual brakes on rear wheels. A front push bumper may be provided on trucks that are so designed.

(h) All tow trucks must be equipped with a two-way radio or other telecommunications device enabling communication with a base station having telephone service or with telephone service direct. Radios must be equipped with a business frequency; no citizen band radios will be permitted. Applicable F.C.C. licenses must be maintained and displayed upon request by any law enforcement agency.

(i) Lock-out tools for entry into locked vehicles or vehicles wherein occupants have no ready and suitable means of egress.

(j) Four low-pressure air recovery cushions for use in righting trailers and tractor trailers or in lieu thereof a notarized agreement between the towing allocation list operator and a firm located in the parish or within five miles of the city boundaries which provides for air recovery cushions service upon request of the towing company at a cost to the vehicle owner or operator not in excess of the maximum allowable cost stipulated in the towing allocation application.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 28755, § 1, 8-5-21)

laws.title: Transportation of vehicles from scenes
laws.content:
(a) Towing operators are required to transport the vehicle from the accident scene or the scene of a recovered stolen vehicle only to a location specified by the vehicle owner/driver or to the towing business storage facility.

(b) Subsequent relocation towing, retrieval, and/or repair of the vehicle may only be authorized through the signing of an order of repair by the owner at this storage location only. No repair orders shall be signed on the scene of an accident or stolen vehicle recovery.

(c) Towing operators transporting vehicles impounded for violation of state compulsory liability insurance shall transport these vehicles only to the designated storage facility.

(d) Towing invoices shall contain standard language that must be approved by the NOPD to clearly indicate that the approval signature for the towing of a vehicle as required by the towing allocation system does not include any authorization or involvement in any repair service decision.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 28755, § 1, 8-5-21)

laws.title: Exclusion from tow allocation program
laws.content:
(a) The NOPD may deny participation in the tow allocation program to any towing service company that fails to comply with any rule, regulation, criterion or standard imposed pursuant to this article, or for any other good cause. Participation in the tow allocation program is a privilege, not a right.

Supp. No. 97

CD162:93
§ 162-1023

NEW ORLEANS CODE

(b) The NOPD shall provide each towing service company excluded from participation in the towing allocation program with a written notice setting forth the reasons for exclusion. This notice shall be mailed to the business address identified on the most recent application on file and shall set forth the manner in which the company may request reconsideration.

(c) A towing service company excluded from participation in the tow allocation program may, within ten days of the notice of exclusion, request reconsideration by submitting a written request via certified letter to the NOPD, along with any documentation supporting the request.

(d) Within 30 days of a request for reconsideration, the superintendent, or an authorized designee, shall hold an informal, in-person hearing to discuss the applicant’s request for reconsideration. The superintendent shall notify the applicant in writing of the disposition of a request for reconsideration within ten days of this meeting.

(e) Any towing company aggrieved by a decision of the superintendent may appeal to the city council. Any such appeal shall be made in writing through the clerk of council within ten calendar days from the date of the decision.

(f) A towing service company excluded from participation under this section may apply for participation in the tow allocation program in subsequent years.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 28755, § 1, 8-5-21)

laws.title: Relationship to other laws/ regulations
laws.content:
Nothing in this article or in the NOPD towing allocation list requirements exempts any towing business or towing vehicle from any other state or federal laws or regulations dealing with towing, recovery and storage.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 28755, § 1, 8-5-21)

laws.title: Accident scene and stolen vehicle recovery scene requirements
laws.content:
Owners and/or operators of motor vehicles involved in an accident or stolen vehicle recoveries shall cause the damaged or recovered stolen vehicle to be removed from the public roadways, adjacent service lanes, or other city and state property within one hour after completion of the police investigation of the incident or accident. Any vehicle remaining in such areas will be considered as abandoned and hazardous and shall be subject to removal on the order of the NOPD. The NOPD is responsible for conducting all such follow-up after proper investigation of an accident or stolen vehicle recovery to cause such vehicle to be removed within this time limit. The NOPD reserves the right to remove a vehicle which remains in any hazardous position or obstructs the free flow of traffic through a towing service from the towing allocation list if the owner/operator’s towing service cannot respond to clear the accident scene, other hazardous condition, or stolen vehicle recovery location within a one-hour response time upon notification. Towing service businesses, whether called from the NOPD towing allocation list or by the owner/operator of the accident vehicle(s) or recovered stolen vehicle(s), shall be responsible for the clearing of all debris, including, but not limited to automotive parts and fluid from an accident or stolen vehicle recovery scene, per each vehicle assigned by the tow truck driver, other towing business employee, or the towing business assignee. The investigating police officer shall monitor the clean-up of an accident or stolen vehicle recovery scene, prohibiting the towing and removal of the vehicle until all such debris, including, but not limited to automotive parts and fluid has been cleared. If a tow truck summoned from the towing allocation list arrives at the scene and is unable to provide the necessary services, they must immediately notify the NOPD and shall not summon a substitute unless

Supp. No. 97

CD162:94
VEHICLES FOR HIRE

§ 162-1030

the other tow truck is from the same company and such delivery must be within a time period not exceeding an additional 30 minutes.  
(M.C.S., Ord. No. 28755, § 1, 8-5-21)

laws.title: Prohibited response to an accident scene, police investigation or disabled vehicle
laws.content:
Tow truck operators shall not respond to the scene of a police investigation unless called by the police or by the owner or operator of a disabled vehicle. No person, including, but not limited to, the tow truck owner, or his agent, employee or operator, shall stop at the scene of an accident, at the scene of a stolen vehicle recovery, or at or near a disabled vehicle, for the purpose of soliciting an engagement for towing service. No tow truck owner, or his agent, employee or operator shall stop at the scene of an accident, at the scene of a stolen vehicle recovery, or at or near a disabled vehicle unless he has been summoned to such scene by the owner or operator of a disabled vehicle or has been requested to perform such services by the NOPD or other police agency.  
(M.C.S., Ord. No. 28755, § 1, 8-5-21)

laws.title: Prohibited use of emergency equipment
laws.content:
Rotating or strobe beacon lights shall not be used except while at the scene of the accident/emergency or while towing a vehicle. No towing service company or tow truck operator may operate or utilize a police radio monitoring device to obtain information regarding police emergencies, recovered stolen vehicles, or vehicular accident scene for the purpose of soliciting towing service. The possession of radios and/or scanning devices which access police radio frequencies, in any vehicle or tow truck assigned to the towing business is prohibited.  
(M.C.S., Ord. No. 28755, § 1, 8-5-21)

laws.title: Removal of vehicle
laws.content:
(a) No towing service business shall tow or remove any vehicle from the scene of any accident, stolen vehicle recovery, or other towing emergency unless summoned to the scene by the owner or operator of the vehicle or the NOPD.

(b) No towing service business shall be allowed to tow or remove any vehicle from the scene of an accident, stolen vehicle recovery, or other towing emergency unless the towing service business complies with state law and this article.

(c) No towing service business shall remove any wrecked, disabled, or recovered stolen vehicle from the scene where an accident has occurred or a stolen vehicle has been recovered or attach a tow truck to such wrecked, disabled, or recovered stolen vehicle until the investigating police officers have completed their investigation. Operators may in emergency cases move a vehicle involved in an accident, if the movement is necessary to extricate a person from a wreckage or to remove an immediate hazard to life and/or property. In no event shall the movement be more than is reasonable and necessary.

(d) Tow truck operators shall not, without the express authorization of the responsible investigating agency, move any vehicle from a public highway or street, or from any public property with such vehicle is abandoned, stolen, or damaged.  
(M.C.S., Ord. No. 28755, § 1, 8-5-21)

laws.title: Repairs, alterations limited
laws.content:
No towing service business shall require the performance of repair work on a disabled, wrecked, or recovered stolen vehicle in connection with providing towing service for the vehicle. No towing service shall make repairs or alterations to a disabled, wrecked, or recovered stolen vehicle without first having been authorized by the owner of such vehicle, except for emergency alterations necessary to permit the towing of such disabled, wrecked, or recovered stolen vehicle by the towing service or its agents.  
(M.C.S., Ord. No. 28755, § 1, 8-5-21)

laws.title: Written statement of services
laws.content:
No operator shall charge for services which are not itemized and documented on an invoice and/or written statement detailing the charges for any towing services, the location to which the vehicle will be towed and/or stored, and a listing of any services to be performed in addition to the

Supp. No. 97

CD162:95
§ 162-1030

NEW ORLEANS CODE

towing services as well as the charges for these services. The tow truck driver shall not remove any disabled vehicle without signing such written statement and obtaining the signature of the customer on such statement. The only exception to this requirement is when the tow truck has been dispatched from the NOPD towing allocation list and the owner or operator/driver is not present or is incapable of making or declines to make arrangements for the removal of the vehicle. (M.C.S., Ord. No. 28755, § 1, 8-5-21)

**Sec. 162-1031. Unauthorized removal.**

No towing service shall tow or remove any vehicle to any location other than to the towing service’s approved storage facility unless authorized by the registered owner of the vehicle, the operator, or the NOPD. (M.C.S., Ord. No. 28755, § 1, 8-5-21)

laws.title: Penalties
laws.content:
**Sec. 162-1032. Termination of towing allocation privilege.**

(a) Failure to comply with the provisions of this article by a towing company approved to perform towing allocation responsibilities, unless otherwise indicated herein, shall result in the revocation of their privilege by the superintendent.

(b) If a towing allocation permit is terminated during the calendar year, the business may follow the appellate process outlined in section 162-1023. (M.C.S., Ord. No. 28755, § 1, 8-5-21)

**Sec. 162-1033. Criminal penalties for noncompliance.**

Any person who fails to comply with sections 162-1010 through 162-1016 contained in this article shall be in violation of this article, subject to prosecution in municipal court, and such person shall be fined, upon conviction, not less than $100.00 nor more than $500.00 for the first violation during a one-year period. The second violation during a one-year period shall require a fine of not less than $250.00 nor more than $500.00, and a mandatory total of 60 community service hours performed within a 30-day period collecting and picking up litter and trash on the public roads, streets, and highways, and up to six months in jail. Three or more violations during a one-year period shall require a fine of not less than $400.00 nor more than $500.00 for each violation, and a mandatory total of 90 community service hours performed within a 45-day period collecting and picking up litter and trash on the public roads, streets, and highways for each violation, and up to six months in jail for each violation. A conviction for any provision of this article shall also be grounds for removal from the NOPD towing allocation list for a period of one year from the date of such conviction. (M.C.S., Ord. No. 28755, § 1, 8-5-21)

**Sec. 162-1034. Towing zones.**

The NOPD may establish no more than four geographic zones based upon existing police district boundaries to assist in the prompt service delivery requirement. Each towing business shall be allowed to participate in the towing allocation list for accidents/police emergencies, the list for stolen vehicles, and the list for impoundment of vehicles in violation of state law regarding compulsory liability insurance/security, in one or more of these zones. The four towing zones identified by police districts are: Zone 1 (4th), Zone 2 (2nd and 6th), Zone 3 (1st, 3rd, and 8th), and Zone 4 (5th and 7th). However, should NOPD determine that four zones are not needed, it may establish separate city-wide call allocation lists for accidents/police emergencies, recovered stolen vehicles, and impoundment of vehicles in violation of state law regarding compulsory liability insurance/security. (M.C.S., Ord. No. 28755, § 1, 8-5-21)

Secs. 162-1035—162-1280. Reserved.

laws.title: Contract courtesy vehicle service
laws.content:
(a) Any CPNC holder may, within the limitations and restrictions of the CPNC held with notice to the director of the department of public works, contract with a person or entity for the provision of courtesy vehicle service. A CPNC holder contracting with a person or entity for the provision of courtesy transportation is prohibited from soliciting the general public as customers of the contracting person or entity or as users of such transportation service. A CPNC holder contracting with a person or entity for the provision of courtesy transportation shall specifically identify, in a contemporaneously maintained transportation log, produced on request of any representative of the city, the contracting party, the person, entity or groups for which such transportation service is provided and the point of origin and destination of the transportation.

(b) A CPNC holder contracting with a person or entity for the provision of courtesy transportation may only transport passengers from point of origin to one point of destination, provided that one of the two points is the place of business of the person or entity contracting for the provision of courtesy vehicle service, with the following two exceptions:

(1) The CPNC holder has filed with the director of the department of public works a written plan detailing the various points of destination. The plan may be disapproved by the director of public works. If approval is not granted within five calendar days, or if the request is denied, the applicant shall have the right to appeal to the Civil District Court for the Parish of Orleans within 30 working days of the denial; or

(2) The courtesy transportation is a charter where the passenger has the absolute discretion as to destination, route and time of departure and return.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 17,164, § 1, 9-7-95; M.C.S., Ord. No. 21480, § 5, 4-1-04; M.C.S., Ord. No. 24724, § 3, 1-5-12; M.C.S., Ord. No. 28624, § 2, 3-11-21)

laws.title: Off-street loading and unloading
laws.content:
A courtesy vehicle CPNC holder must provide off-street parking for the vehicle when not in use. Loading and unloading of passengers at the CPNC holder's place of business, stated in the current occupational license provided to the director of the department of public works in the courtesy vehicle CPNC application, shall only take place in appropriate passenger or loading zones.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 17,164, § 1, 9-7-95; M.C.S., Ord. No. 21480, § 5, 4-1-04; M.C.S., Ord. No. 28624, § 2, 3-11-21)

laws.title: Violation; penalty
laws.content:
(a) A violation by a courtesy vehicle CPNC holder or its driver of any of the regulations set forth in this article shall result in a fine and/or suspension or revocation of the CPNC according to the following:

(1) First violation shall result in a fine of not less than $50.00 nor more than $200.00, to be determined by a duly authorized hearing examiner following a hearing on the matter.

(2) Second violation shall result in a fine of not less than $250.00 nor more than $500.00, to be determined by a duly authorized hearing examiner following a hearing on the matter.

(3) Third violation shall result in an automatic suspension of the courtesy vehicle CPNC for a length of time to be determined by a duly authorized hearing examiner following a hearing on the matter.

(4) Fourth violation shall result in the revocation of the courtesy vehicle CPNC. Prior to such revocation, the CPNC holder shall be entitled to a hearing on the matter before a duly authorized hearing examiner.

laws.title: Special regulations
laws.content:
In addition to the other applicable provisions of this chapter, all holders of a pedicab certificate of public necessity and convenience (CPNC holders) and pedicab operators shall comply with the applicable provisions of this article.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 24156, § 1, 10-21-10)

laws.title: Certificate required
laws.content:
(a) No pedicab shall be operated on the streets of the city unless the owner of such vehicle has first applied for and received a certificate of public necessity and convenience (CPNC) qualifying a pedicab in the manner provided in this chapter.

(b) It shall be unlawful for any person to transport or offer to transport passengers for hire in any pedicab which does not have affixed to vehicle thereof a valid for-hire vehicle registration number issued along with a valid CPNC as set forth by the director of the ground transportation bureau.

(c) All CPNC registration numbers and/or vehicle registration plates shall remain as the property of the city.

(d) CPNCs and/or and registration plates shall not be transferred, sold or given from one owner to another including the sale of one pedicab company in its entirety to another.

(e) All unused CPNCs shall be returned to the ground transportation bureau of the department of public works.

(f) The director of the ground transportation bureau shall track all CPNCs and after the renewal period if the CPNC has not been renewed it shall be determined to be unused.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 24156, § 1, 10-21-10; M.C.S., Ord. No. 28624, § 2, 3-11-21)

laws.title: Inter-parish operation of pedicabs prohibited
laws.content:
Pedicabs of the type subject to regulation under this chapter in the Parish of Orleans shall be bound to operating within the boundaries of the Parish of Orleans and shall not accept a fare or transport passenger going to or coming from a parish outside of Orleans. Inter-parish operation is prohibited.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 24156, § 1, 10-21-10)

laws.title: Nonparish-licensed operators
laws.content:
No owner or operator of any pedicab authorized to operate in any parish other than the Parish of Orleans or in any political subdivision thereof shall stop or park anywhere on the city's streets where such stopping or parking is prohibited to any pedicab or other for-hire vehicle operating under a permit from the city, or stop or park anywhere in the city with intent to violate this Code. No such owner or operator of any such vehicle shall operate such vehicle in any manner contrary to the provisions of any law of this state or this Code. No such owner or operator of any such vehicle at any time shall transport passengers for hire within the parish of Orleans without meeting the provisions herein.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 24156, § 1, 10-21-10)

laws.title: Pedicab liability coverage
laws.content:
All pedicabs operating in the parish shall have current liability coverage for each vehicle. The liability coverage for a pedicab shall be represented by a policy of liability insurance issued by an insurance company authorized to do business in the state, either as an admitted company or a surplus line company certified to do business in the state, provided that if same is written in a surplus line company, and such policy shall provide for payment of a sum of not less than $100,000.00 to satisfy all claims for damages by reason of bodily injury to or death of any one person resulting from any one accident, and subject to such limit for one person; for payment of a sum not less than $300,000.00 to satisfy all claims for damages by reason of bodily injury to or death of two or more persons resulting from any one accident; and for payment of a sum not less than $50,000.00 to satisfy all claims for damage to property resulting from any one accident by reason of the ownership, operation, maintenance or use of such vehicle upon any street.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 24156, § 1, 10-21-10)

laws.title: Maintenance and appearance of vehicle
Traffic Laws and Waiting Areas
laws.content:
**Sec. 162-1645. Pedicab traffic laws.**

All pedicab operators must obey all the same traffic laws as described in article XII, sections 154-1401 to 154-1424, which will be enforced by the ground transportation bureau investigators, police, or any commissioned policing authority.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 24156, § 1, 10-21-10)

**Sec. 162-1646. Pedicab and for-hire vehicle waiting areas.**

Pedicabs shall be prohibited from parking on sidewalks and all street parking of pedicabs shall be in adherence to current parking laws. While waiting for a fare, the operator of a pedicab shall not restrict the free movement of

Supp. No. 95

CD162:104
VEHICLES FOR HIRE

§ 162-1651

pedestrians. All loading and unloading of passengers from a roadway must be from a curb lane. The pedicab should be as close as possible to the curb and in no circumstances more than three feet from the curb while parked and while loading and unloading a passenger.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 24156, § 1, 10-21-10)

**Sec. 162-1647. Restricted areas defined.**

(a) It shall be unlawful for any pedicab to inhabit, stand or park in neutral grounds of the city with their vehicles while waiting to obtain a passenger.

(b) It shall be unlawful for a pedicab to transport passengers on city streets with a posted speed limit which exceeds a rate of 35 miles per hour except where noted below.

(c) Pedicabs shall be permitted to transport passengers on any city thoroughfare dedicated as a bicycle lane or corridor which is clearly marked for said use irrespective of posted speed limit for motor vehicle traffic.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 24156, § 1, 10-21-10)

**Sec. 162-1648. Unlawful to alter rates.**

It shall be unlawful for any person to alter in any manner the established rates of hire for such vehicle except as by the Council of the City of New Orleans.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 24156, § 1, 10-21-10)

laws.title: Trade Names and NEW Lines
laws.content:
**Sec. 162-1649. Trade name to be registered.**

The trade name applicable to each vehicle operated under the provisions of this article shall be registered with and approved by the ground transportation bureau. Such registration shall set forth the full name and address of the lawful owner or owners of such trade name and shall specify the color scheme of vehicles to be operated under such trade name. Each change in color scheme or of lettering of such vehicle shall likewise notify and be approved by the ground transportation bureau. No new trade name or

color schemes which are identical or deceptively similar to any trade name or color scheme already registered with the ground transportation bureau shall be approved by the ground transportation bureau.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 24156, § 1, 10-21-10)

**Sec. 162-1650. Identification of vehicles.**

(a) A pedicab operated under the provisions of this article shall conform in all respects to the color scheme as set forth for the registered trade name under which it is to be operated. In addition, the vehicle’s registered certificate number assigned by the ground transportation bureau and the telephone number of the pedicab company shall be permanently affixed to the vehicle as prescribed by the bureau.

(b) The full name of the owner of each for-hire carrier vehicle operated as a pedicab and the number of the vehicle’s certificate shall be conspicuously affixed to the vehicle in letters and figures at least two inches high in a location to be determined by the bureau. Proof of the for-hire vehicle renewal certificate shall appear inside the pedicab in a manner also to be determined by the bureau in accordance to the provisions herein.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 24156, § 1, 10-21-10)

**Sec. 162-1651. Current record; complaints; notices.**

All pedicab line operators shall:

(a) Maintain a current record of pedicab CPNC numbers and each operator per vehicle that is on the line;

(b) Refer any and all complaints by passengers of pedicabs to the ground transportation bureau; and

(c) Distribute any and all notices issued by the director of the department of public works to each and all operators of the line. Such distribution shall be in written form within five days of receipt of such notice by the line owner.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 24156, § 1, 10-21-10; M.C.S., Ord. No. 28624, § 2, 3-11-21)

Supp. No. 103

**Sec. 162-1652. Violation; penalty.**

A violation by a pedicab line of any regulations set forth in this article shall result in a fine to the violator of not more than $500.00 per violation, to be determined by the director of the department of public works pursuant to a hearing in accordance with R.S. 49:951 et seq.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 24156, § 1, 10-21-10; M.C.S., Ord. No. 28624, § 2, 3-11-21)

**DIVISION 4. FARES**

**Sec. 162-1653. Legal fares and payment thereof required.**

(a) It shall be unlawful for any pedicab operator to ask, demand or collect any rates of fare other than as specified herein.

(b) It shall be unlawful for any passenger of any such vehicle to refuse to pay the operator thereof the legal rate charged pursuant to the provisions of this article.

(c) The department of public works shall review all ground transportation fares each consecutive odd year, and submit a report in a national peer city comparative analysis format to the mayor and the city council.

(d) An individual pedicab operator may, upon the collection of a fare from a passenger, accept a gratuity for the provision of transport services if the passenger deems appropriate to do so.

(e) It shall be unlawful for a pedicab operator to force payment of gratuity or to attempt to coerce, intimidate or cajole a passenger into paying a gratuity beyond that which the passenger deems appropriate.

(f) Fare rates must be posted and permanently affixed in a location on the pedicab that is visible to passengers.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 24156, § 1, 10-21-10; M.C.S., Ord. No. 28624, § 2, 3-11-21)

**Sec. 162-1654. Maximum rate per trip.**

No operator of any pedicab shall charge any passenger more than the amount allowed such operator for the trip under this chapter.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 24156, § 1, 10-21-10)

**Sec. 162-1655. Established fares.**

For distances up to and including six city blocks, each pedicab company shall set its fare schedule at a rate not to exceed $5.00 per passenger transported; each subsequent city block of transport may incur an additional fare of up to $1.00 per passenger. After having exceeded the first six city blocks, and in the event that a portion equal to roughly one-half of one city block is traveled, the operator shall be permitted to charge an additional $0.50 based upon his/her discretion.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 24156, § 1, 10-21-10)

**DIVISION 5. PUBLIC NECESSITY**

**Sec. 162-1656. Number of pedicabs.**

(a) No individual may be an owner, partner, minority holder, or otherwise associated in a manner of ownership capacity with more than one pedicab company.

(b) No one owner or company may operate with more than 15 pedicabs and no more than half of the total pedicab CPNCs issued citywide, except when authorized to operate with a temporary certificate per section 162-1665 herein.

(c) The maximum total number of pedicabs CPNCs to be issued citywide shall not exceed 65. This number may only be raised following a market analysis recommending such an increase. Any increase of pedicab CPNCs shall only be considered after completion of a petty cab market analysis report, which, upon completion, shall be transmitted as a communication to the city council public works, sanitation and environment committee.

(1) A pedicab market analysis must be initiated by the chair of the city council public works, sanitation and environment committee and the director of the ground transportation bureau, who shall transmit as a communication to the city council a joint letter documenting initiation of the analysis. Prior to submitting the letter, the parties shall consult with relevant stakeholder groups, including

Supp. No. 103

CD162:106
VEHICLES FOR HIRE

§ 162-1658

French Quarter residents, business groups, and economic development entities.

(2) Only third party entities outside of the City of New Orleans executive branch, as defined in Home Rule Charter section 4-101, are eligible to complete a pedicab market analysis.

(3) A completed market analysis shall include an examination of the geographic proliferation and impact of pedicabs, particularly in French Quarter, along with all other modes of transit. It shall also consider economic development opportunities and additional needed enforcement that would result from enhanced pedicab use in other neighborhoods, as well as broader sustainable tourism model practices applicable citywide. The study must be done in consultation with relevant stakeholder groups, including neighborhood associations, business and economic development entities, the pedicab industry, and pedicab operators.

(d) The surplus of pedicab CPNCs, which shall be defined as the difference between the number of pedicab CPNCs issued and the maximum permitted citywide, shall be maintained by the ground transportation bureau. The director of the ground transportation bureau shall use best efforts to ensure that at least 35 percent of the approved surplus pedicab CPNCs are allocated to registered disadvantaged business enterprises, consistent with Chapter 70, Article IV, Division 2 of the City Code.

(e) Any pedicab company or individual operator shall be free to operate uninhibited in all parts of the city except in those areas restricted within the provisions set forth in this article.

(f) No pedicab company shall have a favored territory or zone of operation over another pedicab company, but an owner may deploy operators as needed.

CPNCs shall not be transferred, sold or given from one owner to another. In the event of a sale of a pedicab company, and its assets, in its entirety to another, the purchaser must apply for applicable permits as set forth in this article. (M.C.S., Ord. No. 24156, § 1, 10-21-10; M.C.S., Ord. No. 28912, § 1, 1-6-22; M.C.S., Ord. No. 29345, § 1, 2-16-23)

laws.title: Application fee required
laws.content:
(a) An application for operating authority must be accompanied by an application fee of $50.00 for administrative expenses.

(b) A person who applies for multiple CPNCs on one application shall pay only one application fee.  
(M.C.S., Ord. No. 24156, § 1, 10-21-10)

laws.title: Annual licensing fee required
laws.content:
The fees charged by the department of public works for each certificate of public necessity and convenience for pedicabs are as follows:

(1) Initial license …………… $100.00  
(2) Annual renewal …………… 100.00  
(M.C.S., Ord. No. 24156, § 1, 10-21-10; M.C.S., Ord. No. 28624, § 2, 3-11-21)

laws.title: Standards for issuing and denying certificate
laws.content:
In a decision and recommendation to approve or deny an initial or renewal application for operating authority, the bureau shall consider whether:

(1) All applicable requirements of this chapter have been met;

(2) A certificate of necessity and convenience for any type of for-hire vehicle has previously been revoked;

(3) The applicant advertised, offered, or provided pedicab service before the application was approved.  
(M.C.S., Ord. No. 24156, § 1, 10-21-10)

laws.title: Appeal of application denials
laws.content:
(a) The department shall notify an applicant in writing of the denial of an application and the reason for the denial. The notice must include a statement of the applicant's right to appeal.

(b) An applicant may appeal a denial of the application to the Civil District Court for the Parish of Orleans no later than thirty (30) working days after the notice of denial is mailed to the applicant.

(c) The city council shall issue a decision on the appeal no later than 30 days after receipt of the written appeal.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 24156, § 1, 10-21-10; M.C.S., Ord. No. 24724, § 4, 1-5-12)

laws.title: Pedicab renewal application
laws.content:
(a) [Annual renewal.] An owner that maintains a fleet of pedicabs must annually apply for a renewal for each certificate of public necessity and public convenience on a form prescribed by the bureau.

(b) [Good standing.] No owner in good standing shall be denied an annual renewal.

(c) Delinquency penalty. A certificate of public necessity and convenience (CPNC) for pedicab vehicles expires on March 31 of each year and must be renewed within the month following expiration (April) for a fee of $100.00. A CPNC renewal that is submitted in the month of May is subject to a delinquency penalty of $100.00 in addition to the renewal fee of $100.00. A CPNC renewal that is submitted in the month of June is subject to a delinquency penalty of $100.00 in addition to the renewal fee and the May delinquency penalty. A CPNC shall not be renewed after June 30; however, the director of the department of public works (or his designee) at his discretion may make an exception for good cause shown by the CPNC holder. The request for an exception must be in writing before July 1 and if granted is subject to a delinquency penalty of $50.00 per month beginning in the month of July. This delinquency penalty shall be in addition to the fees and penalties outlined above.

(d) Revocation of certificates of public necessity and convenience (CPNC). A certificate of public necessity and convenience (CPNC) that is not renewed by June 30 is suspended. A CPNC shall be revoked if a renewal is not submitted in April, May, or June, or within the extended time period granted by the director or the designee.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 24156, § 1, 10-21-10; M.C.S., Ord. No. 26306, § 1, 3-26-15; M.C.S., Ord. No. 28624, § 2, 3-11-21)

laws.title: Temporary operating permits
laws.content:
During special or other events that attract a large number of visitors to the city, if a pedicab for-hire service experiences periods which demonstrably require more pedicabs than are currently registered with the city, the owner may request supplemental temporary pedicab permits by submitting a written application which shall state the reason why supplemental pedicabs are needed and identify the pedicabs to be used. Supplemental pedicabs authorized by a supplemental operating permit are temporary and:

(a) Are subject to fees for daily or weekly use which shall be set at a level of half of those levels assessed for special charter fees in subsection 162-195(2) of the Municipal Code of Ordinances.

(b) Shall be issued no sooner than noon of the day before the event; and shall be valid until no later than noon of the day after the event.

(c) Must comply with the pedicab requirements of this article.

(d) Must comply with the insurance requirements of this article.

(e) Are subject to inspection by the department of public works, who may at any time order unsafe vehicles to be removed from service.

(f) Must be operated by a New Orleans licensed pedicab company.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 24156, § 1, 10-21-10; M.C.S., Ord. No. 28624, § 2, 3-11-21)

Supp. No. 103

CD162:109
§ 162-1666

NEW ORLEANS CODE

laws.title: Operator's license application
Pedicab vehicle inspections
laws.content:
It shall be unlawful for any person to operate a pedicab without it passing an annual inspection.

(a) The holder of each pedicab vehicle grant shall annually obtain from the department of public works an inspection receipt that indicates that the pedicab vehicle has passed inspection. A copy of said receipt shall be maintained with the vehicle at all times in a manner prescribed by the bureau.

(b) Any pedicab vehicle found not to conform to the standards and tolerances provided for in this article shall not be approved by the department of public works and shall be ordered out of service. The department of public works shall make or cause to be made, at least every 12 months, inspections of pedicab vehicles to ensure their compliance with this article. The department of public works shall maintain a record of each inspection and shall provide the owner a copy of same. Once a pedicab vehicle is inspected and found to be in compliance with this article, the department of public works shall furnish an inspection receipt to the company representative undergoing the inspection. Such inspection receipt shall be maintained with the vehicle at all times in a manner prescribed by the bureau.

(c) Annually, the owner shall pay $20.00 inspection fee per pedicab vehicle.

(d) If a pedicab is involved in an accident or collision during the term of the operating authority, the owner shall notify the ground transportation bureau within five days after the accident or collision. Before operating the pedicab again under the operating authority, an owner shall have the vehicle reinspected for safety and shall send to the department of public works a sworn affidavit that the vehicle has been restored to its previous condition.

(e) All new approved pedicab companies in the year of inaction of this article shall be issued an inspection gratis by the department of public works.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 24156, § 1, 10-21-10; M.C.S., Ord. No. 28624, § 2, 3-11-21)

laws.title: Advertising authorized
laws.content:
(a) The placement of placards, signs, images, insignias or logos shall be permitted on the body of a pedicab as approved by the director of the department of public works.

(b) Advertisement images shall not obscure the visibility of the registration number or plate.

Supp. No. 103

CD162:110
VEHICLES FOR HIRE

§ 162-1699

(c) Advertisements shall be limited to exclude the following:

(1) Lewd, crass, vulgar or sexually explicit content or images.

(2) Political slogans or propaganda.

(3) Advertisements which emit their own source of illumination.

Bumper stickers shall be prohibited.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 24156, § 1, 10-21-10; M.C.S., Ord. No. 28624, § 2, 3-11-21)

**Sec. 162-1669. Disadvantaged business enterprise.**

In approving pedicab certificate of public necessity and convenience (CPNC) holders, the director of the ground transportation bureau shall be required to make every reasonable effort to ensure that a minimum 35 percent of the approved pedicab businesses are registered disadvantaged business entrepreneurs in accordance with chapter 70, article IV, division 2 of the City Code.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 24156, § 1, 10-21-10; M.C.S., Ord. No. 29345, § 2, 2-16-23)

laws.title: Pedal Carriages
laws.content:
**Sec. 162-1670. Prohibited acts.**

It shall be unlawful for any person to operate a pedal carriage or to offer to transport passengers for hire in any pedal carriage within the City of New Orleans.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 28678, § 1, 5-20-21)

**Secs. 162-1671—162-1699. Reserved.**

CD162:110.1

laws.title: TNC permit required
laws.content:
No TNCs shall operate without first having applied for and received a TNC permit in the manner provided in this article. Any person or entity found operating a TNC without a TNC permit shall be subject to a fine of no less than $500.00 for the first offense and shall be prohibited from obtaining a TNC permit for one calendar year from the date of the offense. For second or subsequent offenses violators shall be subject to the maximum fine allowed by law and shall be permanently prohibited from obtaining a TNC permit.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 26339, § 2, 4-9-15)

laws.title: Occupational license required
laws.content:
No applicant shall receive a TNC permit without first having applied for and received an occupational license from the department of revenue. The occupational license application shall include proof of registration to conduct business in the state and the name, address, and contact information of an agent for service of process within the state, and the address of an

Supp. No. 95

CD162:111
§ 162-1702

NEW ORLEANS CODE

office located within Orleans Parish. A physical office must be maintained in the parish; a P.O. Box is not sufficient.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 26339, § 2, 4-9-15)

**Sec. 162-1703. TNC permits are privileges.**

TNC permits are privileges and not rights. The director of public works or his designee has full discretion in determining whether a TNC permit shall be issued. TNC permits are not transferrable.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 26339, § 2, 4-9-15; M.C.S., Ord. No. 28624, § 2, 3-11-21)

**Sec. 162-1704. TNC permit application.**

An application for a TNC permit shall be submitted to the department of public works on forms to be furnished by the director of the department of public works, and the applicant shall furnish the following information with each application:

(1) The name and form of business under which the service will be operated;

(2) The name, phone number, mailing address, and street address (if different from the mailing address) of the applicant’s agent for service of process;

(3) Proof of current coverage of insurance as required by this article;

(4) A general description of the means and methodology used to charge passengers and the standard rates for for-hire vehicle transportation services rendered; and

(5) Any additional information as requested by the director of the department of public works for administration of this section.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 26339, § 2, 4-9-15; M.C.S., Ord. No. 28624, § 2, 3-11-21)

**Sec. 162-1705. TNC permit fees.**

The department of public works shall charge an annual TNC permit fee of $15,000.00. The TNC shall also remit quarterly payments to the department of public works in an amount equal to $0.50 per trip originating in Orleans Parish each quarter. These fees shall be assessed in addition to any other fees charged in any other provision of this chapter. Six months after the effective date of this article, the department of public works shall evaluate the fees and assessments established herein as to whether they are sufficient to offset the cost of the enforcement of this article.

(M.C.S., Ord. No. 26339, § 2, 4-9-15; M.C.S., Ord. No. 28624, § 2, 3-11-21)

**Sec. 162-1706. Reserved.**

**Sec. 162-1707. Accessibility.**

(a) TNC drivers shall comply with all applicable laws relating to accommodation of service animals.

(b) A TNC shall not impose additional charges for providing services to persons with physical disabilities because of those disabilities

(c) As of January 1, 2016, any TNC that has at least 50 vehicles operating on its TNC digital network shall provide that:

(1) No less than three percent of all TNC vehicles in its network shall comply with vehicle guidelines set forth in the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) with the average time available per week for such vehicles being reasonably within the average time available per week of all TNC vehicles on its TNC digital network;

(2) No less than three percent of the total time available per week of all TNC vehicles in its network shall be achieved by TNC vehicles that comply with vehicle guidelines set forth in the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA); or

(3) The TNC shall make its TNC digital network available to all accessible taxicab CPNC holders to allow passengers to book rides on the TNC digital network with accessible taxicabs. The TNC shall make available the same or substantially the same software TNC digital network functionality as it provides for TNC vehicles, but is not required to accept payment through the TNC digital

Supp. No. 95
